surprises.description: The company lowered the upper end of full-year comp guidance from 2.5% to 2.0%, leaving the 1.5% floor unchanged. That is weaker than the preview’s base case, which anticipated a narrower guide around 2.10–2.16% EPS and treated a comp-guide cut as a downside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management narrowed full-year guidance to comp sales growth of 1.5%-2.0% (from 1.5%-2.5%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated a guide “narrowed to ~$2.10–2.16”; its bear case anticipated “comp guide cut below 1.5%.”

surprises.description: The full-year EPS range was narrowed to $2.07–$2.11 from $2.07–$2.15, trimming the high end rather than raising the low end. The preview was watching for the low end to be raised again and expected a base-case range around $2.10–$2.16.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether the low end gets raised again”; the preview’s base case expected a guide “narrowed to ~$2.10–2.16.”

surprises.description: {N}power penetration reached the previewed 84% level, but its year-over-year increase was 2 percentage points rather than the preview’s expected 3-point increase. The level therefore matched, while the pace of penetration growth fell short.
surprises.fact_evidence: “{N}power Rewards net sales penetration rose 2 percentage points year-over-year to 84%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “{N}power penetration (84% of sales, +3pts).”

surprises.description: Natural Grocers brand penetration increased to 9.7% of sales, below the preview’s 9.8% expectation, with growth of 110 basis points rather than the expected 120 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Natural Grocers brand penetration increased 110 basis points year-over-year to 9.7% of total sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Private label (9.8%, +120bps).”

surprises.description: The company launched DoorDash delivery across all stores and plans to phase in curbside pickup, a new customer-access initiative not anticipated in the preview. The call provided no financial impact or adoption figures, so the shareholder implication is not yet clear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched a DoorDash delivery partnership across all stores in mid-July and plans to phase in curbside pickup.”

surprises.description: Management said Q4 will have one fewer selling day because stores will close for Labor Day. The preview did not identify this as a calendar headwind to the already-watched Q4 earnings trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 will have one fewer selling day due to Labor Day store closures.”

in_line: The company maintained capital expenditure guidance at $45–$50 million, as the preview reported that capex had already been cut to that range.
The long-term annual unit-growth target remained 4%–5%, matching the target highlighted in the preview.
The company opened 6 stores fiscal year-to-date, consistent with the preview’s stated FY26 target of 6–8 openings.
The $2 million business-interruption insurance recovery was already disclosed in the preview; the reported administrative-expense decline was aided by that recovery.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.55, below the preview’s $0.68 consensus estimate, even though adjusted EBITDA exceeded the preview’s estimated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income of $54 million or $0.55 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | $0.68”

surprises.description: Kodiak made some progress turning its power pipeline into a customer project, with a sub-100 MW West Texas data center leased to a hyperscaler and a limited notice to proceed. But the long-term contract was still only expected before year-end, rather than being a signed customer contract disclosed at the call.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Executed a limited notice to proceed for a sub-100 MW West Texas data center project leased to a hyperscaler,” with power supply “starting early 2027” and “a long-term contract expected before year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the key question was how much capacity had “signed, take-or-pay-style customer contracts” and described named counterparties or contract structures as a bull-case disclosure.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in above the preview’s estimated range: $217 million versus an estimate of about $205–212 million. The quarter also set a company record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA hit a company record $217 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | ~$205–212M.”

surprises.description: Kodiak raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance instead of merely reaffirming it: the low end rose from $820 million to $830 million, while the high end stayed at $860 million. The call also reported higher full-year discretionary cash flow and Compression gross-margin guidance, though the preview did not give prior full-year estimates for those two measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance, lifting adjusted EBITDA to $830-860 million, discretionary cash flow to $570-600 million, and Compression gross margin to 69-70.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the existing FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide as “$820–860M” and said “reaffirm = base case” while “a raise is the bull trigger.”

surprises.description: Power Infrastructure revenue exceeded the preview’s estimate of about $25–30 million, reaching $33 million. Its 64.5% adjusted gross margin was within the preview’s expected 60–70% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Power Infrastructure generated $33 million in revenue at a 64.5% adjusted gross margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Power Infrastructure … My Q2 '26 est. ~$25–30M” and “@ 60–70% AGM.”

surprises.description: Leverage was lower than the preview’s expected post-equity range, at 3.1x rather than roughly 3.3–3.5x. Management also said it expects leverage to peak in the mid-3s under the base plan, easing the preview’s concern about leverage approaching or exceeding 4.0x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post-May equity offering of ~$836 million, net debt was ~$2.6 billion with a record-low leverage ratio of 3.1x, expected to peak in the mid-3s under the base plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 leverage “nearer **3.3–3.5x**” and flagged a trajectory toward “4.0x+ with un-contracted power capex” as the bear case.

surprises.description: Half of 2027 large-horsepower deliveries were contracted, up from the preview’s report that more than 40% were already spoken for. That is progress, although short of the preview’s illustrative 60% level for a materially stronger booking update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Already 50% contracted on 2027 large-horsepower deliveries.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “>40% of 2027” deliveries were contracted and called an update “materially above that (say, 60%+)” a bullish datapoint.

surprises.description: Revenue was $391 million, above the preview’s $386.3 million consensus, though only slightly above the top published estimate and below the preview’s bull-case threshold of $392 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $391 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed total revenue consensus of “$386.3M,” with an alternate estimate of “$377.1M” and another of “$365.0M”; its bull scenario called for “$392M+.”

in_line: Compression Infrastructure’s 70% adjusted gross margin and 98.2% utilization were broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of roughly 69.5% margin and a highly utilized fleet; the reported margin was also within the previously stated 68.5–70.0% range. The call noted lube-oil cost headwinds but did not report a material margin shortfall.

The Baker Hughes turbine-supply arrangement was not wholly new: the preview already described a deal anchoring about 1 GW with a pathway to 1.8 GW. The call’s report of roughly 1.8 GW available by 2030 therefore did not, by itself, establish that the capacity had been contracted with end customers.
Management’s reaffirmed power returns of 15%+ were consistent with the preview’s prior expectation of greater than 15% unlevered returns.

surprises.description: Sysco’s FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $5.02–$5.12 came in above the preview’s $4.96 consensus and its expected standalone range of $4.80–$4.95, even though the guidance includes a 53rd week and buybacks remain paused.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sysco guided fiscal 2027 to adjusted EPS of approximately $5.02 to $5.12, representing 9% to 11% growth, though this includes benefit from a 53rd week.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 Adj. EPS (consensus) ~$4.96”; “A clean standalone guide is plausibly $4.80–$4.95.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS was $1.53 versus the preview’s $1.51 consensus and the roughly $1.52 implied by the high end of prior guidance. Full-year adjusted EPS of $4.61 also edged past the $4.60 high end of the prior guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sysco delivered Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.53 and full-year adjusted EPS of $4.61, both exceeding prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $1.51”; “FY26 guide: ‘high end of $4.50–$4.60’ … implied Q4 ≈ $1.52.”

surprises.description: Sysco reported a Q4 gross-margin decline rather than the improvement suggested by the preview’s discussion of Q3 margin expansion and an easing year-over-year incentive-compensation lap. Gross profit still grew, but the margin fell 17 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross margin declined 17 basis points to 18.7%, pressured by a tough prior-year strategic sourcing comparison and elevated inbound fuel costs, though gross profit still rose 3.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 gross margin expanded 31bps to 18.6% with GP +6.5%”; “Q4 is the quarter where the incentive-comp lap should ease.”

surprises.description: Sysco introduced a new AI-driven efficiency program with targeted FY2027 savings that the preview did not anticipate. The company expects about $100 million of net savings in-year, with a larger run-rate benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sysco announced a new AI-driven efficiency program targeting approximately $100 million of net in-year cost savings in fiscal 2027 (roughly $160 million on a run-rate basis), weighted to the second half and to the U.S.”

surprises.description: Sysco supplied FY2027 revenue guidance of 6%–7% growth to about $90 billion, a specific outlook not provided in the preview. The forecast includes a 53rd week and assumes roughly 2.5% USFS local case growth and 1.5%–2% inflation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 revenue is guided to grow 6% to 7% to approximately $90 billion, driven by ~2.5% USFS local case growth and inflation of ~1.5% to 2%.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue exceeded the preview’s $21.92 billion consensus, reaching more than $22 billion. The gap was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 total revenue grew 4.7% to over $22 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sales $21.92B.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged soft national-chain traffic, but Sysco reported national cases up 2.6% in Q4, matching local case growth. This was a stronger national-volume result than that concern suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “USFS total volume [was] up 2.5% (both local and national cases up 2.6%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “National chain traffic soft (−1.9% in Q3).”

surprises.description: Sysco reported that International operating margins had risen to over 4% in FY2026 from about 2% in 2022, an improvement the preview did not specifically anticipate. The segment’s double-digit adjusted operating income growth streak, by contrast, was expected to continue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The International segment posted its 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit adjusted operating income growth, up 15.7%, with operating margins more than doubling from ~2% in 2022 to over 4% in fiscal 2026.”

in_line: USFS local case growth was 2.6% in Q4, within the preview’s 2.5%–3.0% base range and above management’s 2.5% floor, though below the preview’s >3.0% bull-case threshold. The preview also anticipated recovery; the reported second-half average of 2.9% versus 0.5% in the first half is consistent with that improvement.
The International segment extended its double-digit adjusted operating income growth streak to an 11th consecutive quarter, as the preview anticipated.
The Restaurant Depot deal remains on the expected timeline: closing is still expected by Q3 FY2027 despite the FTC second request, which the preview had already noted.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.19, far below the preview’s $0.60–$0.67 consensus range. The gap was especially large despite year-over-year improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted adjusted EPS rose to $0.19 from $0.03 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | Consensus | $0.66–0.67 (a second feed shows $0.60).”

surprises.description: Dana cut full-year adjusted EPS guidance to about $2, the bottom of its prior $2–$3 range and below the preview’s roughly $2.45–$2.62 Street expectation. Management cited higher depreciation and net interest, lower China JV earnings, and unfavorable tax mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year diluted adjusted EPS guidance was cut to approximately $2 per share due to higher depreciation, higher net interest ahead of the Eaton deal, lower China JV equity earnings, and unfavorable tax mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $2.00–3.00” and “Street at ~$2.45–2.62.”

surprises.description: The 10.3% Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin missed the preview’s implied 10.6%–11.1% margin expectation, even though EBITDA dollars landed within the preview’s implied range. The margin gap was modest but fell short of a key test the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $207 million, delivering a 10.3% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~10.6–11.1% implied”; the preview also said the key metric to watch was “Adjusted EBITDA margin (target ~10.5%+).”

surprises.description: Q2 sales of $2.0 billion exceeded the preview’s $1.94 billion consensus by about 3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales reached $2.0 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $1.94B (range $1.92–1.94B).”

surprises.description: Dana raised its full-year sales outlook to about $7.75 billion, above the prior range’s $7.70 billion high end, and raised adjusted EBITDA guidance by $25 million to $825 million. That was stronger than the preview’s expectation of repeating the upper-end sales message, although $825 million remained within the old EBITDA range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance to approximately $7.75 billion in sales (up $225 million) and $825 million in adjusted EBITDA (up $25 million), driven primarily by stronger commercial vehicle demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guidance was “Sales | $7.30–7.70B” and “Adj. EBITDA | $750–850M”; the preview’s base case expected guidance to be reaffirmed with “upper end of sales” repeated.

surprises.description: Despite Q2 adjusted free cash flow of just $68 million, Dana raised full-year free cash flow guidance by $25 million to about $325 million. This is better than the preview’s concern that the annual range might be trimmed, but it leaves a substantial cash-generation burden for the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted free cash flow improved $75 million year-over-year to $68 million, and full-year free cash flow guidance was raised $25 million to approximately $325 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2–Q4 “must produce ~$495M to hit the midpoint” of the prior annual range and called FCF “the guidance line most at risk of a quiet trim.”

surprises.description: Dana restarted repurchases and plans another $200 million of buybacks before year-end, while saying repurchases can continue through the Eaton closing. The preview flagged whether the deal would restrict buybacks as an open question and cited a $300 million 2026 target; the company also accelerated its $2 billion authorization completion target from 2030 to 2029.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restarting share buybacks with a plan for an additional $200 million in repurchases before year-end 2026,” with program-to-date repurchases “just over $1 billion” toward a “$2 billion authorization targeted for completion by 2029 (accelerated from 2030).” The Eaton separation “allow[s] continued buybacks through closing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$125M done in Q1 against $300M for the year” and asked whether the agreement restricts repurchases during pendency; it described that as “an open question.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that Dana is still working to eliminate $40 million of stranded Off-Highway costs, an ongoing cost burden not identified in the preview’s discussion of the savings program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Still working to eliminate $40 million of stranded Off-Highway costs.”

surprises.description: Management provided new details on the already-expected $250 million synergy target: about $75 million in year one, cash costs to achieve below $250 million, and payback under two years. The rapid payback is encouraging, though the stated cost-to-achieve ceiling is substantial relative to the target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The combined Dana-Eaton entity targets at least $250 million in run-rate cost synergies within 24 months (about $75 million in year 1), with total cash cost to achieve under $250 million and a payback under two years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected the “$250M synergy target” to be reaffirmed and said no integration or carve-out costs had been publicly framed, raising the question of whether they had been quantified.

surprises.description: Dana described a larger 2030 combined-company opportunity than the preview had laid out: revenue of $14–$15 billion versus the $10 billion standalone target, including about $1.7 billion of aftermarket sales. This is an additional scale and aftermarket target beyond the preview’s deal discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Eaton combination raises the Dana 2030 revenue target to $14–15 billion (from $10 billion standalone), boosts aftermarket sales to approximately $1.7 billion (16% of total).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited the $5.1 billion Eaton Mobility combination and deal valuation, but did not state a higher combined-company revenue target or an aftermarket target.

surprises.description: The stated pro forma 2026 net leverage of approximately 1.4x is higher than the approximately 1.2x pro forma net leverage referenced in the preview’s deal setup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expected to maintain pro forma 2026 net leverage of approximately 1.4x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “pro forma net leverage of ~1.2x.”

surprises.description: Dana disclosed a one-time approximately $20 million union signing bonus hitting Q3, a near-term cash cost the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A one-time ~$20 million union signing bonus hits Q3.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $207 million, within the preview’s implied range of approximately $205–$215 million.
The $250 million synergy target and the Q1 2027 Eaton deal closing timeline were reaffirmed, as the preview expected.
Dana reported $54 million in year-to-date savings and remained on track for $65 million in 2026, matching the preview’s stated annual cost-savings target.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $190 million, roughly $6 million above the preview’s $184.17 million consensus. The beat was positive but modest relative to the expected quarter’s revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached approximately $190 million,” up 21% year-over-year and 9% sequentially.

surprises.description: TransMedics raised the low end of its FY26 revenue range from $727 million to $737 million, while leaving the high end at $757 million. That puts the new floor above the preview’s cited FY26 revenue consensus of $733.18 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised the low end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $737 million to $757 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (reiterated May 5, 2026): FY26 revenue $727–757M”; FY26 revenue consensus was “$733.18M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin guidance fell to 12.5%–14%, well below the roughly 16% expectation implied by the preview’s guidance for margins up to about 250 basis points below 2025’s 18.5%. Management attributed the lower outlook primarily to higher planned OCS Kidney investment; adjusted operating expenses rose 46% and adjusted R&D nearly doubled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted operating margin guidance was cut to approximately 12.5%-14%,” down from the prior “~16% expectation,” “primarily due to higher planned OCS Kidney investment.” Adjusted operating expenses “rose 46% year-over-year,” and adjusted R&D “nearly doubl[ed] to $32 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted operating margin was guided to “up to ~250 bps below 2025”; 2025 adjusted operating margin was 18.5%. The preview also asked whether “opex leverage return[s] in Q2.”

surprises.description: The preview expected CHOPS/ENHANCE Part B to be on track for an early-Q3 launch, but management now targets FDA IDE supplement approval only in late Q3 or early Q4. Meaningful heart and lung trial revenue is not expected until late Q4 and into 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Targeting FDA IDE supplement approval for CHOPS/ENHANCE Part B by late Q3 or early Q4 2026,” with meaningful heart and lung trial revenue “not expected until late Q4 2026 and into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CHOPS: IDE supplement approval and early-Q3 2026 launch on track.”

surprises.description: Although the PAD Aviation acquisition had already closed, management disclosed that its Q3 consolidation is expected to dilute both gross and operating margins, with no financial guidance yet provided. The preview flagged a need for a revenue and cost timeline but did not anticipate this stated margin dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PAD Aviation acquisition in Germany will be consolidated starting Q3 and is expected to be dilutive to both gross and operating margins, with no financial guidance yet provided.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The PAD Aviation investment closed July 6, 2026; watch for a revenue/cost timeline on the pan-European NOP.”

in_line: The preview anticipated logistics/flight growth running ahead of product or OCS growth and potentially weighing on margin. The call reported service revenue growth of 29% versus product revenue growth of 16%, consistent with that expected mix direction.

surprises.description: Precigen reported net income of $20.1 million, or $0.05 per diluted share, and operating income of $22.6 million, rather than the preview’s expected $0.01-per-share loss. The company reached profitability before Papzimeus’s first FDA-approval anniversary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “quarterly net income of $20.1 million ($0.05 per diluted share) and operating income of $22.6 million, reaching profitability before the drug's first FDA-approval anniversary.”

surprises.description: Management said quarterly revenue growth should continue, but at a mathematically diminishing rate. The preview focused on meaningful acceleration into Q2 and did not flag this qualification to the subsequent growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “expects future quarterly revenue growth to continue but at a mathematically diminishing rate.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 95%, but management said that margin should not be treated as the steady-state level: after remaining pre-launch inventory is used in Q3, margins are expected to settle in the high-80% to low-90% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin was 95%, but management guided that steady-state margins will stabilize in the high-80% to low-90% range (roughly 10% COGS) once remaining pre-launch inventory is consumed in Q3.”

surprises.description: The patient activity update showed more than 200 patients had received at least one dose and over 100 had completed treatment, while the Hub tracked well over 500 patients plus additional non-hub patients. The preview noted about 400 Hub-enrolled patients in Q1 and flagged enrollment as an issue to watch, but gave no expectation for this increase or treatment progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “More than 200 patients have received at least one dose and over 100 patients have completed treatment, with the Precigen Hub now tracking well over 500 patients plus significant additional non-hub patients.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~400 hub-enrolled patients ... as of Q1”; “Patient hub enrollment ... [was]” among the items to watch.

surprises.description: Covered lives rose by about 18 million to roughly 315 million, which management described as nearly all potential U.S. covered lives. The preview cited 297 million covered lives as of Q1 but did not forecast further expansion to near-total coverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payer coverage grew by approximately 18 million covered lives in Q2 to roughly 315 million total commercial and government lives, representing nearly all potential covered lives in the US.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~297M US covered lives as of Q1.”

in_line: Papzimeus revenue accelerated sequentially from the Q1 base, consistent with the preview’s expectation of meaningful quarter-over-quarter acceleration; the preview did not provide a Q2 revenue consensus.
Management reiterated funding operations through cash-flow breakeven by year-end 2026, as the preview said to watch for.
The seven-year exclusivity for Papzimeus was already reported before the quarter in the preview; the call specified protection through August 2032.

surprises.description: The preview noted that gas realizations were 72% of benchmark in Q1 and looked for evidence of Waha recovery. NOG reported gas realizations at 90% of Henry Hub before hedges and 123% including hedges, a stronger realized level than the preview had quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “gas realizations at 90% of Henry Hub (123% including hedges)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 realizations were 72% of benchmark” and “Confirmation that H2 infrastructure relief is real is a genuine 2027 estimate driver.”

surprises.description: Instead of the preview’s concern about possible cost inflation, production expenses per BOE were down year over year and normalized AFE costs were also lower than the 2025 average. The reported reductions were modest but favorable against the cost-risk framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “production expenses per BOE down 4% year-over-year” and “normalized AFE costs down 5% from the 2025 average.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “cash costs” as a key metric, described Uinta and Duvernay as “margin wildcards,” and listed “Cost inflation on Uinta/Duvernay” in its bear scenario.

surprises.description: The call gave a full-year adjusted EBITDA and free-cash-flow outlook at strip pricing, including potential free cash flow above $500 million. The preview expected FY guidance to be reiterated but did not provide an annual EBITDA or FCF range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance calls for $1.4 billion to over $1.5 billion of adjusted EBITDA at strip pricing” and “$375 million to over $500 million of free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance — Reiterated (production and capex).”

surprises.description: The preview flagged possible Duvernay integration drag and cost risk, while the call characterized the acquired asset as self-funding and described a long inventory and low development costs. Those favorable asset details were not included in the preview’s acquisition discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Duvernay/Parallax acquisition is “a self-funding asset with 20 years of inventory, average breakeven below $50, and cost of less than $600,000 per location.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear scenario cited “Duvernay integration drag,” and the preview identified “Cost inflation on Uinta/Duvernay” as a risk.

surprises.description: Management made a strong valuation-disconnect argument that the preview had not anticipated, putting its estimated asset value well above enterprise value and emphasizing NOG’s share-price lag versus peers.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimated assets are worth “$7 billion-plus versus a $4.6 billion enterprise value,” and said the stock was flat year-to-date while peers rose 40%–50%.

in_line: Q2 free cash flow was $159 million, within the preview’s estimated $110–165 million range.
Q2 capital expenditures were $196 million, within the preview’s pre-announced $190–200 million range.
The 2.95 million-share repurchase and approximately $243 million authorization matched figures already disclosed in the preview.
The $0.45 quarterly dividend matched the preview’s expectation that management had recommended that dividend for all of 2026.
Record gas production was already described in the preview as pre-announced, despite Permian curtailments.

surprises.description: Owlet reported Q2 revenue of $33.9 million, well above the preview’s $30.5 million anchor consensus and also above its $31.7 million alternate estimate. It was a sizable beat even though the preview’s bull scenario had allowed for revenue as high as $34 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was a record $33.9 million, up 29.9% year-over-year”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $30.5M”; “Revenue (alt.) | $31.7M”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA excluding the tariff refund was $2.9 million, above the preview’s estimated Q2 range of about $0.5–1.5 million. That also landed near the preview’s $2.0–3.0 million bull case, rather than its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA excluding the tariff refund was a record $2.9 million, a $2.4 million increase versus prior year”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$0.5–1.5M (unpublished)”; bull scenario: “Adj. EBITDA | $2.0–3.0M”

surprises.description: International revenue reached $5.7 million, up 214% year-over-year, far exceeding the preview’s expectation of 22% growth. International sell-through also grew 38%, slightly above the preview’s 37% figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International revenue grew 214% year-over-year to $5.7 million, the highest international quarter excluding last year's camera load-in, with international sell-through units up 38%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “International grew 22% with 37% sell-through”

surprises.description: Owlet received about $4 million in tariff refunds, lifting Q2 gross margin and adjusted EBITDA: reported gross margin was 64.4% and adjusted EBITDA was $6.7 million including the refund, versus 54% and $2.9 million excluding it. The preview did not anticipate this one-time benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Owlet received approximately $4 million in tariff refunds, recognizing a one-time $3.5 million benefit to COGS and $3.75 million benefit to adjusted EBITDA”; “including the refund [gross margin] reached 64.4%”; adjusted EBITDA “including the refund it was $6.7 million.”

surprises.description: Even excluding the refund, gross margin was 54%, above the preview’s estimated 51–53% range and the 50–52% full-year guide. The preview had flagged a possible margin-guide increase if Q2 stayed above 52%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin excluding the tariff refund was 54%, expanding 270 basis points year-over-year”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~51–53%”; “If Q2 holds above 52%, the FY GM guide gets raised”

surprises.description: Owlet raised its full-year gross-margin outlook to 53–55% and adjusted EBITDA outlook to $10.75–12.75 million, from 50–52% and $7–9 million, respectively. The call said the increases reflect only the one-time tariff benefits, so the higher ranges do not indicate that the refund is recurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $118-122 million while raising gross margin outlook to 53-55% and adjusted EBITDA to $10.75-12.75 million, reflecting only the one-time tariff benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Current Guide” — revenue “$118–122M,” gross margin “50–52%,” adjusted EBITDA “$7–9M”; “a reaffirm is neutral-to-fine”

surprises.description: Prime Day units fell 8% year-over-year, which the call said underperformed expectations because competitors discounted aggressively ahead of the August 10 deactivation of non-FDA-cleared vital-sign monitors. Outside Prime Day, U.S. sell-through grew 20%, with Dream Sock up 21% and Duo up 29%—below the preview’s stated +30% expectation for both products.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Owlet's Prime Day units sold declined 8% versus last year due to aggressive competitor discounting … underperforming expectations”; “Excluding Prime Day, US Q2 total sell-through units grew 20% year-over-year, with Dream Sock and Duo up 21% and 29% respectively.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said Q2 sell-through was running +30% YoY for both Duo and Dream Sock”

surprises.description: The new $25 million Wells Fargo credit facility sharply lowers Owlet’s interest-rate margin, from 7.5–8.5% to SOFR plus 2–2.25%, a reduction of at least 525 basis points. The preview did not anticipate a new facility or this financing-cost improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new $25 million Wells Fargo asset-based credit facility lowered the interest rate margin to SOFR plus 2-2.25% from 7.5-8.5%, a reduction of at least 525 basis points”

surprises.description: Cash ended Q2 at $30.9 million, below the $35.5 million reported at March 31 and below the preview’s cited $32 million bear-case threshold. The provided facts do not quantify the quarter’s cash use or explain the decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “cash at $30.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$35.5M at 3/31/26”; bear scenario: “cash <$32M”

surprises.description: Dream Sock U.S. penetration reached 36%, an improvement over the preview’s cited 34% Q1 attach rate, but short of the preview’s watch point of movement toward 40%. Subscriber count and subscription revenue were broadly in line with the preview’s stated range and threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dream Sock US penetration reaching 36%”; “130,000 paying subscribers generating $3.2 million in revenue”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “34% attach rate on U.S. Dream Sock”; “attach rate moving toward 40%”; “128–132k subs, $3.0M+ revenue”

in_line: Full-year revenue guidance of $118–122 million was reaffirmed, as the preview described a reaffirm as the expected outcome.

Paying subscribers and subscription revenue were broadly in line with the preview’s watch range: 130,000 subscribers and $3.2 million of revenue versus 128–132k subscribers and a $3.0 million-plus expectation. MRR also remained above the preview’s $1 million threshold.

surprises.description: The preview said backlog above roughly $350 million would decisively break the year-over-year decline pattern. Manufacturing backlog instead reached $421.8 million, up about 40% from $302 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Manufacturing backlog surged approximately 40% to $421.8 million from $302 million a year ago,” with lead times of about 9 weeks.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog above ~$350M with lead times extending would decisively break the YoY-decline pattern”; the preview also cited a $316M Q4 exit, down 8% year over year.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue guidance calls for mid-single-digit year-over-year growth, excluding Homes Direct. That is stronger than the preview’s base case of an in-line Q2 guide, though the acquisition is expected to add only immaterial revenue to Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company guided Q2 revenue to grow mid-single digits year-over-year,” excluding Homes Direct, which “will be additive but immaterial.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated a “modest beat with in-line Q2 guide.”

surprises.description: Sales of $710.2 million modestly exceeded the preview’s consensus range, whose high end was $709.4 million, and grew 1.3% rather than being approximately flat as previously guided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales increased 1.3% year-over-year to $710.2 million, slightly ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus was “$702.0M – $709.4M”; prior management guidance was “approximately flat YoY.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.88 landed at the very bottom of the preview’s consensus range and below its working estimate of $0.89–$0.90 and base-case range of $0.93–$1.00.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.88 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave an EPS consensus range of “$0.88 – $0.92,” said to “treat $0.89–$0.90 as the working number”; its base scenario projected “$0.93–1.00.”

surprises.description: Input-cost inflation was described as leveling off, whereas the preview expected it to be accelerating into Q1. The Q2 gross-margin outlook still includes a roughly 200-basis-point year-over-year headwind, so the more favorable news is the change in inflation trend rather than the disappearance of cost pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 adjusted gross margin guidance is “25-26%,” implying “roughly 200 basis points of year-over-year headwind” from elevated input costs, “though inflation is leveling off.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said inflation in key inputs was “accelerating into Q1” and that the headwind was “peaking this quarter.”

in_line: U.S. homes sold rose 1.8% while industry shipments declined roughly 5%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Champion would gain share against a weakening industry.
The Homes Direct acquisition closed in Q2 and matched the preview’s outline: 11 Western U.S. stores and about $70 million in annual sales, with the deal excluded from guidance.
The effective tax rate rose from 21% to about 25% after ENERGY STAR-related incentives expired, in line with the preview’s expected 3–4-point increase.
ASP growth was modest and lower-priced channel mix weighed on it, consistent with the preview’s warning that mix shifts toward lower price points could pressure ASP.
The Q2 gross-margin outlook still reflects substantial year-over-year cost pressure, consistent with the preview’s expectation of deliberate margin compression.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.54, well above the preview’s central consensus estimate of about $0.29; net income also more than doubled to $32 million. The preview cautioned that EPS estimates were unusually dispersed, including a $0.48 estimate, so the gap is smaller against the high end of the cited range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 54% to $0.54” and “net income more than doubling to $32 million from $12 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS: ~$0.29 (wide dispersion)” and “Q2 EPS marks at both $0.29 (Aug 5) and $0.48 (Jun 23).”

surprises.description: Payment Software grew 7% in constant currency, below the preview’s expectation of double-digit Q2 segment growth. Issuing and acquiring revenue nevertheless grew 33–37%, and the segment’s EBITDA margin reached 48%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Payment Software segment grew 9% (7% constant currency) to $196 million,” with “issuing and acquiring revenue growth of 33-37%” and “segment EBITDA margin reaching 48%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided the segment to double-digit growth in Q2”; the preview also said “Sub-6% cc here would undercut” the thesis.

surprises.description: Biller revenue grew only 5% and segment EBITDA declined year over year, with a terminated-partnership charge accounting for about one-third of the EBITDA contraction. The preview gave no warning of a Biller earnings contraction or this one-time charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Biller segment revenue grew only 5% to $234 million with EBITDA declining year-over-year,” pressured by comparisons and “a one-time charge from a terminated partnership representing about one-third of the EBITDA contraction.”

surprises.description: ACI said second-half revenue would be weighted 40% to Q3 and 60% to Q4, with Q3 revenue of $417–427 million and EBITDA of $90–95 million. That makes the near-term quarter dependent on renewals arriving later, whereas the preview’s bull case required license-renewal timing to land in-quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-half revenue is expected to skew 40%/60% between Q3 and Q4 due to timing of high-margin payment software license renewals,” implying “Q3 revenue of $417-427 million and EBITDA of $90-95 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “This is a lumpy revenue line and the single biggest swing factor between base and bull”; “The bull case needs license/renewal timing to land in-quarter.”

surprises.description: Net new ARR bookings were $18 million and new license/services bookings were $59 million, both down against a strong year-ago period, with more signings pushed into the second half. The preview highlighted bookings as a key metric but provided no specific Q2 forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new ARR bookings were $18 million and new license/services bookings were $59 million in Q2, both down against a strong prior-year period, with more signings weighted to the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net new ARR bookings: $12.4M in Q1 (+39%), driven primarily by Biller. Watch the segment mix.”

in_line: Revenue was $430 million, matching the preview’s approximately $430 million consensus and landing at the midpoint of the $420–440 million Q2 guide.
Adjusted EBITDA of $91 million was within the $85–95 million company guide and the preview’s $88–94 million base-case range.

ACI raised full-year guidance as expected: adjusted EBITDA guidance of $545–560 million matches the preview’s anticipated range, while revenue guidance of $1.895–1.925 billion is close to its expected roughly $1.90–1.92 billion.

Management declined to comment on media speculation about a Biller sale, consistent with the preview’s explicitly anticipated possibility of a “no comment on process specifics” response. It did not confirm a sale process, timeline, valuation, or use of proceeds.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $1.84, far above the preview’s preferred consensus range of $1.27–$1.28 (and also above its conflicting $1.42 estimate).
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS was $1.84.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I’d anchor on $1.27–$1.28” (with $1.42 identified as an unverified outlier).

surprises.description: ADM raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance by about $1 at both ends, to $5.15–$5.60. That substantially exceeded the preview’s $4.15–$4.70 company range and the $4.80 sell-side estimate, which was already above the old guidance ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ADM raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.15-$5.60,” up roughly $1.00 at both ends from $4.15-$4.70.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 EPS (sell-side): $4.80”; company guidance was “$4.15–$4.70.” The preview noted consensus was “effectively pre-baking a second guidance raise.”

surprises.description: AS&O operating profit reached $867 million, up 129% year over year, with large gains in both Crushing and Ag Services. The preview highlighted AS&O as the main swing factor but did not anticipate or provide a segment-profit estimate for a result of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AS&O segment operating profit surged 129% year-over-year to $867 million, with Crushing up ~$330 million to $363 million and Ag Services up 159% to $293 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Crush margins / biofuel policy — the whole story”; “Ag Services & Oilseeds is the delta vs the $379M year-ago segment profit.”

surprises.description: The quarter included about $100 million of net positive mark-to-market and timing impacts, but management said the first half still had a carried net negative position that would mostly reverse in Q3. That makes the Q2 timing benefit real but less complete or earlier than the preview’s discussion of a Q2 reversal might have led investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 results included approximately $100 million of net positive mark-to-market and timing impacts,” while the first half’s carried position was net negative and expected to reverse “mostly in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any Q2 reversal is a mechanical tailwind — watch how much of the beat is ‘quality’ vs timing.”

surprises.description: ADM raised its expected 2026 net benefit from the 45Z tax credit to about $250 million from roughly $150 million. The preview flagged 45Z and RVO durability for discussion but did not anticipate this $100 million increase in the expected benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its expected 2026 net benefit from the 45Z tax credit to approximately $250 million, up from prior guidance of about $150 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “45Z/RVO commentary — durability of the credit into 2027, and any RIN/LCFS pricing color.”

surprises.description: Nutrition operating profit rose to $172 million, above the preview’s $140 million bull-case marker, even though revenue fell 5%. Both Human and Animal Nutrition each grew profit by more than 50%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nutrition segment operating profit rose 51% to $172 million despite revenue declining 5% to $1.9 billion, with both Human and Animal Nutrition each up over 50% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bull … Nutrition >$140M”; the preview also called the third straight quarter of recovery a “credibility test.”

surprises.description: Instead of only a possible capex-guide increase tied to previously announced added crush capacity, ADM described a first phase of brownfield expansions at four U.S. facilities for about $100 million total, with capital intensity roughly one-quarter of greenfield builds. The low stated cost and facility-selection detail were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ADM identified 4 U.S. crush facilities (out of 10 candidates) for a first-phase brownfield expansion costing about $100 million total, with capital intensity roughly one-quarter that of greenfield builds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “After the four-plant crush expansion; 2027–29 spending shape”; “watch for a capex-guide bump.”

surprises.description: Management said it was evaluating a return to opportunistic share repurchases later in the year. The preview discussed the dividend and capex but did not flag a possible buyback resumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage was 1.6x at June 30 (targeting ~2x by year-end), and management is evaluating a return to opportunistic share repurchases later this year.”

surprises.description: Management gave a quantified long-term natural-colors opportunity: a roughly $1 billion U.S. addressable market and an $80–$100 million operating-profit target over time. The preview did not identify this opportunity or provide a comparable expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The natural colors transition represents a ~$1 billion U.S. addressable market from which ADM targets $80-$100 million in operating profit over time.”

surprises.description: ADM reported North American Q3 crush about 90% locked but Q4 only about 30% locked, adding a notable difference in near-term visibility between quarters that the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North American Q3 crush ~90% locked but Q4 only ~30% locked.”

in_line: The constructive biofuels and crush backdrop, including higher ethanol margins, aligned with the preview’s emphasis on strong crush margins and biofuel policy as key drivers.
ADM paid its 378th consecutive quarterly dividend of $256 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a $0.52-per-quarter dividend and its note about the 378th consecutive payment.

surprises.description: The preview expected a revenue-guide trim, with earnings and free cash flow held or raised. Republic instead raised the revenue range by $150 million at both ends, lifted EBITDA guidance, raised the low end of EPS guidance by $0.03, and raised both ends of its free-cash-flow range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $17.2–17.3 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $5.525–5.55 billion, adjusted EPS of $7.23–7.28, and adjusted free cash flow of $2.54–2.575 billion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The expected outcome is the WM template — trim revenue, hold/raise EBITDA, EPS and FCF.”

surprises.description: Revenue growth exceeded the preview’s consensus pace: Republic reported 4.6% growth, versus the preview’s 3.0% implied year-over-year growth. The preview also described revenue tracking to or below the low end of guidance as part of the setup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 4.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “$4.36B” and “Implied YoY +3.0%”; it also said revenue was tracking “below the low end” of full-year guidance.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.85 came in above the $1.81 consensus estimate, though it reached only the top of the preview’s broader $1.81–$1.85 base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $1.85.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adjusted EPS” consensus of “$1.81” and a base-case range of “$1.81–1.85.”

surprises.description: The consolidated EBITDA margin held at 32.1%, rather than coming in flat to slightly down as management had previously indicated. Underlying business margin expanded 90 basis points, showing stronger underlying margin performance than the cautious quarterly setup suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin maintained at 32.1%”; “core price on related revenue was 6.4%, exceeding cost inflation and driving 90 basis points of underlying margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided Q2 margins to be “somewhat flat to slightly down,” and noted that “≥32.1%” would be a clean beat.

surprises.description: Recycling commodity prices recovered more than the preview’s stabilization outlook implied: Q2 averaged $136 per ton and current prices were about $140, supporting a full-year average near $135 versus the original $115 assumption. This was also the main source of the EBITDA guidance increase, rather than primarily an operating improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recycling commodity prices averaged $136 per ton in Q2 … with current prices ~$140 supporting an implied full-year average of ~$135 per ton, up from the original $115 assumption”; the EBITDA guidance increase was driven mostly by “higher commodity prices (~$25 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said commodity prices were “stabilizing” around “~$125/ton” at the Q1 call, while the original full-year assumption was $115 per ton.

surprises.description: Republic had already closed nearly $1.2 billion of acquisitions year-to-date, exceeding the preview’s stated full-year target of more than $1.0 billion by the time of the Q2 report. Management said the closed acquisitions were already included in the raised guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Republic invested nearly $1.2 billion in acquisitions closed year-to-date (all included in guidance).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed a full-year acquisition-spend target of “~$1.0B” and said it had been raised to “>$1.0B at Q1”; it noted “>$700M deployed YTD.”

in_line: Average yield on total revenue was 3.4%, matching the preview’s 3.4% consensus estimate.

Volumes remained soft as expected: total-revenue organic volume declined 1.6%, with 1.3 percentage points attributed to prior-year event-driven landfill volumes; large-container volume improved slightly from Q1’s 2.5% decline to 2.2%.

Environmental Solutions showed sequential recovery and management reaffirmed year-over-year revenue growth and margin expansion in the second half, consistent with the preview’s expected trough and H2 recovery. Its 20.2% margin was up 100 basis points sequentially.

Management’s expected 60–70 basis points of full-year underlying margin expansion is consistent with the preview’s expectation that underlying margins would expand; the call specified that Q3 would be roughly flat and most expansion would come in Q4.
The dividend increase was already known from the preview, which stated that the dividend had been raised on July 30.

surprises.description: Arcutis raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $525–540 million, well above the preview’s $500–515 million bull-case range; the preview had identified a raise as important, but expected a smaller one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Arcutis raised full-year 2026 net revenue guidance from $480-495 million to $525-540 million, driven by first-half momentum and new commercial initiatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise to ~$500–510M is the single biggest swing factor”; the bull scenario expected guidance “Raised to $500–515M.”

surprises.description: Q2 product revenue reached $129.9 million, above both the $118.85–121.85 million consensus estimates and the preview’s ~$122–126 million whisper range. Sequential growth was 23%, also ahead of the preview’s roughly 14% QoQ credibility threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net product revenue reached $129.9 million, up 59% year-over-year and 23% sequentially over Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $118.85M” and “$121.85M”; “Working whisper: ~$122–126M”; “credibility requires roughly +14% QoQ.”

surprises.description: Arcutis reported $15 million of net income, substantially above the preview’s roughly $6 million modeled net income. The preview’s EPS estimates cannot be compared directly because the call facts do not provide actual EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company delivered $15 million in net income in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “net income ~$6M, EPS ~$0.04–0.05 diluted.”

surprises.description: ZORYVE recorded more than 280,000 prescriptions in the quarter, a record. The preview highlighted a need for prescription re-acceleration but did not anticipate or quantify a record quarterly demand level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ZORYVE achieved a record quarterly demand of more than 280,000 prescriptions across all indications and formulations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Need re-acceleration” in weekly TRx; the preview reported about 21,300 rolling four-week TRx at Q1 end but gave no Q2 prescription target.

surprises.description: The Chief Commercial Officer is leaving later this month, an unanticipated leadership change, though a 30-year industry veteran is taking over on an interim basis during a search.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chief Commercial Officer Todd Edwards is resigning effective later this month, with 30-year industry veteran Rob Lisicki stepping in as Interim CCO during a national search.”

in_line: Gross-to-net remained in the 50s, with a gradual move toward the low 50s expected by year-end, broadly matching the preview’s expectation that it was in the 50s and guided to improve.
Operating cash flow remained positive; the preview specifically flagged sustained positive OCF as an important expectation after Q1’s +$2.2 million.

The pediatric psoriasis approval for children as young as age 2, the accepted infant atopic dermatitis sNDA and its February 23, 2027 PDUFA date, and the expected Q4 2026 vitiligo and Q1 2027 HS readouts were already described in the preview.

surprises.description: Rigel raised the upper end of full-year guidance by $5 million, but the increase came entirely from contract revenue: the contract range moved from $20–30 million to approximately $30 million. Product guidance stayed at $255–265 million and excludes Vepinu, rather than the raise reflecting Vepinu sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rigel raised the upper bound of its full-year guidance by $5 million,” driven “entirely by increasing contract revenue guidance” to approximately $30 million; “Product sales guidance was maintained at $255 million to $265 million” and excludes Vepinu.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the guide might be “raised or ‘reaffirm + exclude’” Vepinu, and called “A raise incorporating VEPPANU” the most bullish possible headline.

surprises.description: Rigel gave no near-term Vepinu launch-sales guidance, reported no sales yet, and said updates would come only after Q3. Management also indicated that formal guidance around J.P. Morgan may still exclude Vepinu because there will be too little sales history.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “declined to issue any near-term guidance for the Vepinu launch, with no sales reported yet and updates expected only after the third quarter”; formal guidance around J.P. Morgan “may still exclude Vepinu due to insufficient sales history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for whether guidance was “raised or ‘reaffirm + exclude’” and described an August launch; it also identified launch-readiness and a first explicit 2H26 operating-expense framing as issues to watch.

surprises.description: Management put the second-line-and-later ESR1-mutated patient population at about 20,000 and described roughly a $1 billion opportunity, but clarified that this is the total oral-SERD market—not a Vepinu-specific peak-sales estimate. The market-size figure therefore offers commercial context but is not a Vepinu sales forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimated “approximately 20,000 patients,” corresponding to “about a $1 billion market opportunity”; the figure “represents the total addressable market opportunity for oral SERDs rather than a Vepinu-specific peak sales estimate.”

surprises.description: Management emphasized Vepinu’s differentiated profile in second-line ESR1-mutated breast cancer, citing a strong PFS treatment effect, higher response rates, and improved clinical benefit rates. The preview focused on launch readiness and did not flag this efficacy positioning as a key expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Rigel positioned Vepinu as a “market-leading, differentiated heterobifunctional protein degrader” with “strong PFS treatment effect, higher partial and overall response rates, and improved clinical benefit rates” in second-line ESR1-mutated breast cancer.

surprises.description: The call highlighted a broader Vepinu combination-study program than the preview discussed: data had already been presented for combinations with palbociclib, abemaciclib, and samuraciclib, with ribociclib and additional samuraciclib data expected soon.
surprises.fact_evidence: Pfizer is running “multiple combination studies”; data for vepdegestrant plus “palbociclib, abemaciclib, and samuraciclib” had been presented, with “ribociclib and additional samuraciclib data” anticipated in the near future.

in_line: Vepinu’s expected commercial availability in August was consistent with the preview’s expectation of an August 2026 launch; management said it should be available in the middle of the month.
The existing $255–265 million product-sales guidance was maintained, consistent with the preview’s discussion of a reaffirmed product-sales guide.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.39, far above the $0.28 consensus and the company’s $0.27–$0.32 guidance range. Revenue of $1.02 billion also edged above the preview’s $999 million–$1.002 billion consensus band.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted diluted EPS rose to $0.39 from $0.32 a year earlier” on “total revenues of $1.02 billion (up 1%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus “$0.28” and company guide “$0.27 – $0.32”; revenue consensus band “$999M–$1,002M.”

surprises.description: U.S. comps rose 2.3%, above the preview’s roughly 1.5% expectation, but traffic still fell 1.9% and trailed the industry benchmark by 1.1 percentage points. Outback had positive 1.4% comps but a steeper 2.8% traffic decline, rather than the preview’s hoped-for narrowing of the traffic gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. comparable restaurant sales grew 230 basis points in Q2, but traffic declined 190 basis points, with traffic trailing the Black Box industry benchmark by 110 basis points.” Outback comps “rose 140 basis points while traffic fell 280 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: U.S. comp sales were expected at “~+1.5%.” The preview said positive Outback comps “with traffic approaching flat” would be proof of concept, and described the base case as Outback “~flat, traffic still ‑1.5 to ‑2%.”

surprises.description: The next-quarter outlook included a loss of $0.27–$0.22 per share, with an approximately $5 million tax expense attributed to the full-year tax rate. The preview anticipated negative H2 EPS overall, but did not flag a loss this large in Q3 or the tax expense as its driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 to a loss of $0.27 to $0.22 per share,” driven by “an approximately $5 million tax expense in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the full-year guide implied “H2 adjusted EPS of roughly ‑$0.22 to ‑$0.07” and estimated Q3 FY25 at “≈ ‑$0.04.”

surprises.description: The turnaround investment burden was reduced substantially: total investments fell to $36 million from the $50 million previously planned, and productivity savings left only $6 million of net investment. The preview had framed the plan as roughly $50 million of spend against $30 million of offsets, or about $20 million net.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total turnaround investments” were cut “to $36 million from $50 million,” with “a net investment of just $6 million after $30 million in productivity savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “$50M of turnaround spend” against “~$30M of productivity offsets for a net ~$20M investment.”

surprises.description: Commodity inflation came in above the preview’s stated range: 5.7% versus a 4.5%–5.5% outlook. Despite that pressure, adjusted operating margin expanded year over year, rather than showing the softness the preview warned could weigh on Q2 margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: Commodity inflation was “5.7%”; adjusted operating margin “expanded 50 basis points to 4.0% from 3.5%,” aided by favorable labor and productivity gains.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said commodity inflation was guided at “4.5–5.5%” and noted that Q2 FY25 restaurant-level margin had fallen year over year, with Q2 seasonally lower.

surprises.description: Marketing spend is increasing by about $15 million year over year, above the preview’s stated expectation of $10 million of incremental marketing spend. The increase is partly directed to Outback, with roughly $10 million of the spend allocated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: Marketing spend is increasing “by about $15 million year-over-year,” with “~$10 million directed to Outback.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$10M of incremental marketing concentrated in the back half.”

surprises.description: Bonefish delivered unusually strong results, with comps up 8.1% and traffic up 4.5%; Fleming’s and Carrabba’s also extended their consecutive quarters of positive comps. These brand results were not anticipated in the preview, which focused its sales discussion on Outback.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bonefish was the standout brand with comp sales up 810 basis points and traffic up 450 basis points,” while Fleming’s and Carrabba’s posted their “eighth and sixth consecutive quarters of positive comps.”

in_line: The full-year adjusted EPS range was raised to $0.90–$1.00 from $0.75–$0.90, matching the preview’s base case that guidance could be nudged to “~$0.90–$1.00.”
Full-year U.S. comparable-sales guidance remained 1%–2%, the same range cited in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview expected FY2026 CAFD guidance to be reaffirmed, while Clearway cut the range from $470–510 million to $430–470 million. Management attributed the entire reduction to weak wind resource in the first half tied to the El Niño Southern Oscillation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clearway lowered its 2026 CAFD guidance to $430-470 million from the prior $470-510 million range, driven entirely by weak wind resource tied to the El Niño Southern Oscillation weather pattern in the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “buy-side expects reaffirmation”; the preview's base case also called for “Reaffirmed $470–510M.”

surprises.description: Q2 CAFD was $167 million, below the preview's roughly $190 million estimate and near the bottom of its $165–224 million seasonal range. Adjusted EBITDA, by contrast, landed within the preview's estimated $390–410 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $409 million and CAFD was $167 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “CAFD ~ $190M” and gave a seasonality range of “$165–224M”; it estimated adjusted EBITDA at “~$390–410M.”

surprises.description: Clearway reported completed long-term PPA restructurings for all three ERCOT wind projects, covering more than 600 MW, with contracts extended beyond 2040 and accretion to EBITDA and CAFD from the first month of effectiveness. This is ahead of the preview's expectation that two remaining Texas wind PPAs would close by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed long-term PPA restructurings on all three ERCOT wind projects (over 600 MW), extending contracts beyond 2040 and making them accretive to EBITDA and CAFD from the first month of effectiveness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Two remaining Texas wind PPAs were guided to close by year-end.”

surprises.description: Clearway disclosed substantially more specific growth funding visibility than the preview anticipated: about 70% of the investment needed for the top end of its 2030 target is already commercialized, with over $2 billion of identified growth for 2027–2029.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 70% of the growth investment needed to reach the top end of the 2030 target is already commercialized, with over $2 billion of identified growth lined up for the 2027-2029 completion vintages.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the 2027 and 2030 targets were “on track,” but did not identify this degree of commercialization or a lined-up growth amount for those vintages.

surprises.description: The digital infrastructure opportunity was quantified at a much larger scale than the preview's specific Wyoming and Montana examples: the co-located generation pipeline now exceeds 17 GW, with over 6 GW included in the reported pipeline and potential corporate capital upside of $400–500 million per GW.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clearway's digital infrastructure pipeline now exceeds 17 gigawatts of co-located generation under development, with over 6 GW incorporated into the reported pipeline and potential corporate capital upside of $400-500 million per gigawatt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Wyoming's first load target and Montana's 500 MW of signed PPAs and “$1B or greater” opportunity, and asked management to “quantif[y] data center capital.”

surprises.description: Although the preview highlighted equity issuance as a funding risk, management said it could defer equity issuance for the rest of 2026 and wait for the growth outlook to be reflected in the share price. The plan still includes $0.5–1 billion of external equity, so the change is in timing flexibility rather than eliminating the need.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated it has flexibility to delay equity issuances for the remainder of 2026, waiting for the growth outlook to be reflected in the stock price before issuing.” The plan includes “$0.5-1 billion of external equity (of which only $50 million is raised).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called equity funding “the underappreciated risk,” said incremental capital above the $2.5B baseline was funded “~45% corporate debt / ~55% equity issuance,” and flagged “equity funding language at a $31 share price.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a long-term commitment to bring the payout ratio below 70% and said it plans to roll forward its five-year growth targets and formalize updated capital-allocation targets at the Q3 call. The preview focused on near-term dividend growth and the existing 2030 targets, not this longer-term framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets rolling forward its 5-year growth targets into 2031 and formalizing updated capital allocation framework targets at the Q3 earnings call, while committing to lower its payout ratio below 70% long term.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $409 million was within the preview's estimated $390–410 million range.
Clearway reaffirmed its 2027 CAFD-per-share target of $2.70 or better, matching the preview's “on track” expectation.
The 2030 CAFD-per-share target remained at the top end or better of $3.10, consistent with the preview's expectation of the top end or better of $2.90–3.10.

surprises.description: Upwork cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $730–750 million from $760–790 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $225–235 million from $250–260 million. The revised EBITDA midpoint implies a 31% margin, below the preview’s expected H2 margin of about 35%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Upwork cut its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $730-750 million and adjusted EBITDA to $225-235 million (31% margin at midpoint), citing accelerating AI automation and worsening SEO headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance to be reaffirmed/revised: Revenue $760–790M; Adj. EBITDA $250–260M”; the preview also said H2 implied “~$140M in H2 on ~$390M = ~36% margin” and called H2 35% margin confirmation the valuation anchor.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $64.1 million, well above both the $56–59 million guidance range and the preview’s $57–58 million consensus estimate. Its 33.4% margin also beat the expected 30–31% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $64.1 million and a 33.4% adjusted EBITDA margin, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$56–59M,” consensus of “~$57–58M,” and an expected adjusted EBITDA margin of “30–31%.”

surprises.description: Active clients fell to 763,000 from 784,000 in Q1, so the sequential stabilization the preview said investors wanted did not appear. The preview warned that another decline without inflection language would be a negative signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active client count fell to 763,000 under pressure from AI automation, SEO changes, and a subdued labor market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Active clients (Q1: 784K)” and said “Sequential stabilization matters more than the YoY print”; it also said a “third straight quarter of decline with no inflection language is a sell.”

surprises.description: AI-related GSV grew 22% year over year, far below the preview’s expectation that growth would remain above 40%. Growth also slowed from 40% the prior quarter and 50% two quarters earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GSV from AI-related jobs grew 22% year over year to an approximately $330 million annualized run rate, decelerating from 40% growth the prior quarter and 50% two quarters ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether “AI-related GSV growth is still >40%.”

surprises.description: GSV was $966 million, just below the preview’s $970 million low-end consensus, and declined as low-value, highly automatable work eroded faster than expected. The reported decline was also slightly steeper than the preview’s expected year-over-year range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GSV declined to $966 million as low-value, highly-automatable work eroded faster than expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed GSV consensus of “~$0.97–1.00B” and implied year-over-year performance of “~flat to -3%.”

surprises.description: The preview noted that Lifted was down 6% year over year in Q1 and that enterprise/Lifted needed to show evidence of improvement. The call reported 174% GSV growth in Business Plus, 51% growth in AI strategy and consulting, 29% growth in EOR, and Lifted on track for about 25% full-year GSV growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business Plus GSV grew 174% year over year, AI strategy and consulting category grew 51%, and employer of record (EOR) solutions grew 29%, while Lifted remains on track for ~25% full-year GSV growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Enterprise / Lifted (Q1: $24.8M, -6% YoY)” and called this the “first quarter of evidence” after pipeline growth and first migrations in June.

surprises.description: Take rate reached 19.8%, above the preview’s approximate 19.5% expectation, while monetization levers grew 15% year over year. This provided a stronger offset from monetization than the preview’s cautious setup implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Take rate reached 19.8% with connects and talent subscriptions now representing 15% of total revenue, and monetization levers (dynamic pricing, connects, Business Plus) grew 15% year over year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario anticipated “take rate ~19.5%” and warned that deceleration in take-rate expansion would remove “the last revenue lever.”

surprises.description: Upwork plans to add $5–10 million of marketing spend in the back half after cost per new contract start improved 22% quarter over quarter. The preview watched for damage to go-to-market from the workforce cuts, but did not anticipate this specific spending increase or efficiency improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Upwork plans to boost marketing spend by an incremental $5-10 million in the back half after cost per new contract start improved 22% quarter over quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to confirm that “go-to-market wasn't damaged by a 24% headcount cut.”

surprises.description: The company reported a new $150 million revolving credit facility to repay its August 2026 convertible notes. The preview identified the converts as a capital-allocation issue but did not anticipate this refinancing facility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] secur[ed] a new $150 million revolving credit facility to repay August 2026 convertible notes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$361.0M converts” and said to watch “buyback pace against $256.1M remaining and only $12.9M of Q1 FCF, plus $361M of converts.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $191.7 million was near the preview’s roughly $190 million consensus and within its $189–192 million base-case range, although it came in at the high end of company guidance.
GSV per active client rose 5% year over year, matching the preview’s stated Q1 growth rate of 5% and its expectation that the metric would keep rising even as client count fell.

The restructuring savings cadence was as expected: the May restructuring is annualizing $70 million of OpEx reductions and is expected to deliver about $40 million of realized FY2026 savings, matching the preview’s figures.

surprises.description: Spero’s June 30 cash was $50.8 million, above the preview’s estimate of $46–48 million. The figure excludes the July royalty-financing proceeds, so the reported quarter-end cash was a small positive gap versus expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents were $50.8 million as of June 30, 2026,” excluding “the net proceeds from the July 2026 royalty financing.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was zero, consistent with the preview’s $0.0–0.3 million estimate; the preview also said no published consensus was available.
The $9.6 million net loss and $3.4 million R&D expense were within the preview’s respective ranges of roughly $8–10 million and $3–4 million.
Management extended the cash runway into the second half of 2029, as the preview expected.
The SP001 Phase II start remains planned for Q2 2027, matching the preview’s expected timing.
GSK expects UTEBSI to be available in the US in the second half of 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation of availability by end-2026.
The $105 million royalty financing and its non-recourse structure were already anticipated in the preview.

surprises.description: Watts raised FY2026 organic sales growth guidance to 8%–11%, well above the prior 2%–6% range and the preview’s expected buy-side range of 4%–7%. Reported sales growth guidance also rose to 14%–17% from 8%–12%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised full-year organic sales growth guidance to 8%-11%, a more than 5-point increase to the prior midpoint, and reported sales growth guidance to 14%-17%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Full-year FY2026 guidance ... organic +2% to +6%; reported sales +8% to +12%. The preview also says buy-side wants +4–7%.

surprises.description: Q2 sales substantially exceeded the preview’s expectations: organic growth was 12% versus roughly 6% consensus and a company guide of 4%–8%, while revenue was $763 million versus about $726 million expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 organic sales rose 12% to a record $763 million (up 19% reported), driven by data center growth, favorable pricing, and pull-forward demand.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: $725.8–726.0M; organic sales growth: ~+6% (guide midpoint). Company guidance for Q2: organic sales +4% to +8%.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $3.66 beat the $3.34 consensus by about 10%, also exceeding the preview’s estimated buy-side expectation of $3.45–$3.55.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS grew 18% year-over-year to $3.66.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted diluted EPS consensus: $3.34. The preview says buy-side expectations are realistically $3.45–$3.55.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin was 21%, above the 20.0%–20.6% company range and the preview’s roughly 20.3% consensus-implied level. The year-over-year decline was only 60 basis points, rather than the approximately 130-basis-point decline implied by the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted operating margin declined 60 basis points to 21%, primarily due to 70 bps of acquisition dilution and a difficult comparison against a prior-year one-time price/cost benefit.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance for Q2 ... adjusted operating margin 20.0%–20.6%; consensus implied ~20.3% and a 130 bps year-over-year decline.

surprises.description: Watts disclosed that data center sales more than tripled year over year, stronger than the preview’s baseline expectation that growth would remain around the high-double-digit range. It also quantified data center sales at 8% of first-half sales and expected a mid- to high-single-digit share for the full year.
surprises.fact_evidence: Data center sales more than tripled year-over-year and represented 8% of total sales in the first half of 2026, up from just 3% of sales in the prior full year. Full-year data center sales are now expected to reach mid- to high single digits as a percentage of company sales.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlights data center revenue growth and the “high double-digit for the year” reaffirmation, and says the Street wants a dollar figure or revenue %.

surprises.description: Watts doubled its estimated served data center market to about $2 billion, rather than the preview’s stated market of more than $1 billion.
