surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$65M implied” adjusted EBITDA consensus, a base case of “~$63–66M (~9.0%),” and said Q2 margin “Needs ~9%+” with “Sub-8.5%” threatening the full-year bridge.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS came in as a loss rather than the substantial profit expected: the company reported a $0.13 loss per share versus consensus of $0.57 in earnings per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company swung to a Q2 adjusted net loss of $2.3 million (13 cents per share) versus adjusted net income of $1 million (6 cents) in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS” consensus was “$0.57 (Zacks) / $0.59 (alt. compile).”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the midpoint of full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance instead of narrowing toward the low end or cutting it, as the preview expected in its base case. The outlook implies second-half margins above 12% and includes more than $50 million of incremental cost savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “reaffirmed the midpoint of full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance,” implying “second-half EBITDA margins above 12%” and supported by “another $50+ million in incremental cost savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said its “base case” was FY EBITDA guidance “narrowed to ~$255–275M” and its read was “a guidance narrowing to the low end (or an outright trim).”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow turned positive at $16.3 million, modestly better than the preview’s roughly breakeven base case and a sharp improvement from Q1’s cash outflow. Management also projected roughly $100 million of free cash flow in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow improved $39.7 million year-over-year to $16.3 million in Q2,” aided by refinancing and working-capital optimization; management indicated “roughly $100 million in second-half free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “FCF roughly breakeven” and said Q2 needed to show “a decisive inflection toward the ‘positive FCF for 2026’ commitment.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that guidance was updated to raise CapEx and restructuring expense, while lowering net interest expense after refinancing. The preview anticipated refinancing-related interest savings, but did not anticipate the higher spending guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guidance was updated to raise CapEx and restructuring expense while lowering net interest expense after refinancing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated “a $6M/yr cash-interest reduction from the March refinancing” and emphasized the need for “positive FCF for 2026.”

surprises.description: Management described sustained gross-margin expansion despite flat-to-lower production and expects expansion to continue in 2026 even with flat volumes. That offers a more resilient margin outlook than the preview’s concern that weak production and volume would undermine the second-half thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit margins have expanded 160 basis points over two years despite flat-to-lower production,” and management expects “continued margin expansion in 2026 even with flat volumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said industry production was “weaker into H2” and warned that negative volume/mix would mean “the H2 volume thesis is undermined.”

surprises.description: The fluid handling business reported nearly 10 mid-production conquest awards over 10 months, totaling nearly $40 million in annual sales effective this year, as competitors’ struggles create opportunities. The preview discussed awards targets overall but did not flag this specific source of share gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The fluid handling segment won nearly 10 mid-production conquest awards over 10 months totaling nearly $40 million in annual sales effective this year,” with competitors’ struggles creating share-gain opportunities.

in_line: Net new business awards were $118 million in Q2 and $246 million for the first half, consistent with the preview’s expectation of another roughly $100 million-plus quarter against the company’s greater-than-$400 million annual target.

Management’s expectation that index-based contracts will recover most commodity costs, with recovery beginning after the Q2 lag, was consistent with the preview’s expectation that commodity recoveries would start in Q3.
Lower net interest expense after refinancing was anticipated in the preview, which cited an expected $6 million annual cash-interest reduction.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $1.5 million, modestly above the preview’s roughly $1.43 million consensus estimate. The beat was small and the result remained within the preview’s $1.35–$1.50 million base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $1.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue | ~$1.43M”

surprises.description: Lucid performed 2,770 EsoGuard tests, below the preview’s 3,000–3,300 estimate and its 3,100–3,400 base-case range, although still within the company’s 2,500–3,000 target range. Volume therefore came in weaker than the preview’s expected operating level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The lab performed 2,770 EsoGuard tests in Q2 2026”; test volume remained “essentially flat within the 2,500-3,000 target range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EsoGuard tests | ~3,000–3,300”; the base case also anticipated “3,100–3,400.”

surprises.description: Despite lower-than-expected test volume, Lucid recognized about 19% of billable value, up from the 14% level cited in the preview. That was better than the preview’s base case of roughly flat recognition and landed near the high-teens level it identified as a meaningful step-up.
surprises.fact_evidence: The 2,770 tests had a “billable/pro forma value of about $7.6 million” but “only ~19% was recognized as revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Lucid recognizes only 14% of billable value”; the base case assumed “ASP recognition roughly flat.”

surprises.description: Claim outcomes were weaker than the preview’s prior benchmark: only 28% of adjudicated claims yielded an allowable amount, versus 31% paid in the preview’s cited data, and the average allowable was $1,424 rather than $1,646 per test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “65% were adjudicated with only 28% of those resulting in an allowable amount averaging $1,424 per test.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Of adjudicated claims, 31% paid at an average allowable of $1,646/test.”

surprises.description: The VA contribution was pushed out: rather than testing beginning in the “very near future,” management expects it to add test volume only after the new federal fiscal year starts October 1. The company is still working on purchase orders and building the pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The VA opportunity [is] to begin contributing to test volume only after the new federal fiscal year starting October 1,” while the company focuses on “securing purchase orders and building pipeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said testing was to begin “in the very near future” and highlighted the prospect of “First VA revenue.”

surprises.description: Concert coverage had already been announced, but the call reported concrete early uptake: three client health plans had adopted the policy, covering just under 10 million lives. The preview flagged downstream adoption as something to watch but did not set an expectation for this level of adoption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Three of Concert's client health plans have already adopted the coverage policy,” and the LBM covers “just under 10 million covered lives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for downstream plans adopting it,” without specifying a number or scale.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a broader fully diluted share count of roughly 225 million, materially above the 190.8 million GAAP shares outstanding cited in the preview. The difference includes unvested RSAs and abeyance shares, so it indicates potential dilution beyond the headline share count rather than a change in GAAP shares outstanding.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fully diluted shares including unvested RSAs and abeyance shares would total roughly 225 million, versus GAAP shares outstanding of 190.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Shares out: 190.8M” and described the share count as “190.8M now.”

in_line: Q2 cash burn was broadly in line with the preview: the quarter’s $11.3 million burn matched the cited average quarterly burn of about $11.3 million. Quarter-end cash of $33.4 million was also consistent with the preview’s roughly $45 million post-raise cash expectation less a quarter of burn.
The first Concert/LBM coverage policy itself was not new at the release: the preview said it had already been announced and was effective in July.

surprises.description: GEE Group reported $20.8 million of Q3 revenue, $1.1 million above the preview’s $19.7 million model, and the year-over-year decline was 15% rather than the modeled 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenues fell to $20.8 million for the quarter (down 15%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Q3 FY26E (my model) $19.7M” and “Y/Y -20%.”

surprises.description: Direct hire revenue substantially outperformed the preview’s modest-growth estimate: it reached $3.8 million, up 16% year over year, versus a $3.3 million estimate and 4% expected growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct hire placement revenues … grew to $3.8 million for the quarter (up 16% year-over-year and 18% sequentially).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Direct hire placement … Q3 FY26E (my model) $3.3M” and “Y/Y +4%.”

surprises.description: Contract staffing revenue also came in above the model, at $17 million versus $16.4 million expected; its 20% year-over-year decline was less severe than the preview’s 23% forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contract staffing revenues declined to $17 million for the quarter (down 20%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Contract staffing … Q3 FY26E (my model) $16.4M” and “-23%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 39.9%, 160 basis points above the preview’s 38.3% estimate. The preview expected a mix benefit from losing a low-margin account, but the reported expansion was greater than modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded significantly to 39.9% for the quarter (up 450 basis points), driven by the shift toward higher-margin direct hire revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … Q3 FY26E (my model) 38.3%”; the preview also said “GM expanded 400bps to 38.1% in Q2” and that a chunk reflected mix from losing a low-margin account.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $570,000, well above the preview’s roughly $200,000 estimate. That is a substantially stronger improvement than the expected modestly positive quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved to $570,000 for the quarter … up from negative $25,000” in the prior-year period.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … Q3 FY26E (my model) ~$200K.”

surprises.description: Quarterly net income was $566,000, versus the preview’s $150,000 estimate, and GEE reported diluted EPS of one cent despite the preview expecting EPS to remain at zero.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income of $566,000 (one cent per diluted share) for Q3 FY2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net income (cont. ops) … Q3 FY26E (my model) ~$0.15M”; the preview also said “EPS will print $0.00 in essentially every plausible scenario.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects a decision soon on the strategic-alternatives review, a more specific near-term signal than simply saying the process is ongoing. However, it did not announce a transaction or a defined timetable, which fell short of the preview’s hoped-for evidence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GEE Group has engaged Roth Capital Partners to evaluate strategic alternatives including a potential M&A transaction, describing interest as robust and expecting a decision soon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side expects either a defined timeline or an announced transaction”; the preview also said “Silence here is a negative.”

surprises.description: The company said it is suspending further acquisitions until the strategic review concludes. The preview discussed the review and a potential transaction, but did not anticipate this pause in acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Suspending further acquisitions until the review concludes.”

in_line: Cash remained near the preview’s expected level: the company reported $20.3 million, versus the model’s approximately $20.1 million. The preview also expected the balance sheet to remain debt-free.

surprises.description: MPC reported adjusted EPS of $17.73, well above the preview’s $14.52 high-end consensus estimate and its $13.50–$15.00 base case. The result was within the preview’s bull scenario, but materially exceeded the central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $8.5 billion and EPS of $17.73.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS: $14.52 (Zacks) / $13.26 (Barchart mean)” and “My base case sits at $13.50–15.00”; the bull scenario gives “$17.00–18.50.”

surprises.description: R&M margin capture was 112%, above the preview’s 95–100% base-case range and even beyond its bull-case threshold of at least 100%. This directly exceeded the preview’s key concern that capture could lag the sharp rise in cracks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “System-wide R&M margin capture reached 112% in Q2 (108% year-to-date).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case projected “capture 95–100%,” its bull case “capture ≥100%,” and warned that “capture below ~95% turns a headline ‘beat’ into a quality miss.”

surprises.description: R&M adjusted EBITDA was about $6.7 billion, roughly 16% above the preview’s $5.80 billion estimate. The segment was therefore a larger earnings contributor than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&M segment adjusted EBITDA was approximately $6.7 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “R&M adj. EBITDA: $5.80B.”

surprises.description: West Coast utilization came in at 93%, below the preview’s 96% Q2 company-guide figure, even though system utilization met the 94% target. The regional shortfall was a modest operating miss against the preview’s aggressive West Coast assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refineries ran at 94% overall utilization … West Coast at 93%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 guide table listed “Crude utilization … 94% (GC 99% / MidCon 87% / WC 96%).”

surprises.description: MPC disclosed a $3.8 billion working-capital source of cash, but said it came from timing, higher payables and inventory draws and carries an obligation to repay SPR barrels. That makes the cash contribution less clearly recurring than the preview’s broad expectation of more than $4 billion in Q2 free cash flow might suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Working capital was a $3.8 billion source of cash in Q2 from higher payables, crude exchange timing, and inventory draws, with an obligation to repay SPR barrels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 FCF likely $4B+” and highlighted the buyback pace, but did not discuss a large working-capital inflow or the SPR repayment obligation.

surprises.description: MPLX raised its 2026 growth-capital outlook by $500 million to $2.9 billion, an added spending commitment not anticipated in the preview’s capex discussion. The increase is a headwind to the capital-spending outlook, despite the stated rationale of pulling forward growth projects.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MPLX raised its 2026 growth capital outlook by $500 million to $2.9 billion, pulling forward Gulf Coast fractionation spending.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for FY26 “capex ex-MPLX $1.5B” and flagged “FY26 turnaround and capex reaffirmation ($1.35B / $1.5B ex-MPLX),” but did not anticipate higher MPLX growth capital.

surprises.description: MPLX’s 12.5% annual distribution-growth target was extended to both 2026 and 2027. The preview expected reaffirmation of the 12.5% target but did not flag a target for a second year.
surprises.fact_evidence: MPLX is “targeting 12.5% annual distribution growth in both 2026 and 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “the 12.5% distribution growth reaffirmation” as a key item to watch.

surprises.description: Renewable Diesel EBITDA rose about $277 million year over year, a substantial improvement in a segment the preview described as a rounding error at Q1 levels and relevant mainly if it turned materially negative. The strong increase was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Renewable Diesel segment adjusted EBITDA rose approximately $277 million year-over-year with utilization at 95% post-Martinez turnaround.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Renewable Diesel — $38M in Q1 is a rounding error; only matters if it turns materially negative.”

surprises.description: Management gave Q3 guidance that includes about $290 million of turnaround expenses and said the work will create a margin-capture headwind. The preview’s central Q3 debate was whether July’s record cracks were being realized; this guidance instead highlights a near-term operating drag, although it does not provide a Q3-to-date capture figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects 2.8 million bpd crude throughput at 94% utilization with approximately $290 million in turnaround expenses focused on Gulf Coast and Mid-Con conversion units, creating a capture headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market wanted “Q3 quarter-to-date margin commentary” confirming July’s record cracks were being realized, and identified Q3 discussion limited to supportive conditions as a bear tell.

surprises.description: Management described a stronger-than-historical supply disruption and said it supports an enhanced mid-cycle outlook into 2027. The preview already expected discussion of refinery closures and Russian capacity impairment, but the stated scale and extension of the outlook provide a more favorable structural signal than the preview’s baseline framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “over 9 million bpd of global refined capacity offline—about 4 million bpd above historical norms—with over 2.8 million bpd (one-third) of Russian capacity down, supporting an enhanced mid-cycle outlook into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited global refinery output cuts of “~4.5 mmb/d” and said a key call signal would be management “raising its structural mid-cycle bar.”

in_line: Overall refinery utilization was 94%, matching the preview’s Q2 guide; throughput of nearly 3 million barrels per day was also close to the 2,990 mb/d guide.
Share repurchases of $2.5 billion were at the upper end of the preview’s expected $2.0–$2.5 billion range.
MPLX’s 12.5% distribution-growth target for 2026 reaffirmed the target the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $346.2 million modestly exceeded the $341.7 million consensus estimate, while remaining within the company’s $325–355 million guidance range. The call also said the result did not include significant safe-harbor pull-forward, easing the preview’s concern that a large beat might have borrowed from later quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 19.6% year-over-year ... to $346.2 million, above the midpoint of guidance with no significant safe harbor revenue pull-forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $341.7M”; the preview also said management had stated Q2 guidance “does not include any significant one-time pull forward.”

surprises.description: SolarEdge delivered positive non-GAAP operating income and net income, slightly exceeding the published $0.04 EPS estimate and doing better than the preview’s roughly breakeven-to-negative buy-side whisper. The $10.2 million operating profit was stronger than the preview’s base-case estimate of roughly breakeven EBIT.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income of $10.2 million and non-GAAP net income of $3.6 million ($0.05 per diluted share), marking its first non-GAAP profitability since Q2 2023.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | +$0.04”; the preview said to “Treat the buy-side whisper as roughly breakeven to –$0.05, not +$0.04” and described base-case “EBIT ~breakeven ±$5M.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin reached 28.6%, above both the 23–27% company guide and the preview’s roughly 25% consensus estimate. The reported margin included a $13.3 million IEEPA tariff-refund benefit, an additional realized benefit beyond the preview’s description of a roughly $55 million refund as a timing-dependent free option.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin expanded for the sixth consecutive quarter to 28.6% ... beating guidance and including a $13.3 million benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin | ~25%” and company guidance of “23–27%”; the preview said the “IEEPA tariff refund (~$55M, CBP process underway) is excluded from guidance” and that timing of receipt was “a free option.”

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue outlook is weaker than the preview’s roughly $350 million sell-side placeholder: the $310–340 million range is below that figure throughout and implies a sequential decline. Management also described no typical Q3 pickup in the softening U.S. market, alongside European seasonality.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $310–340 million implies a sequential decline, with roughly $15 million of the drop in Europe due to seasonality and no typical Q3 pickup expected in the softening U.S. market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Q3 guidance the “single most important number,” cited a “~$350M sell-side placeholder,” and gave a base-case Q3 range of “$330–360M (flat to modestly up).”

surprises.description: Management guided Q3 non-GAAP gross margin down to 22–26%, versus Q2’s 28.6%. The preview emphasized continued margin expansion and a path toward 30%; the call attributed the near-term decline to lower volume and fixed-cost absorption, with no assumed tariff-refund benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 non-GAAP gross margin is guided to approximately 22–26%, down from Q2 largely due to lower fixed-cost absorption on reduced volume and excluding any potential IEEPA refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Non-GAAP gross margin and the 45X bridge,” noting Q1 was the “sixth consecutive quarter of expansion,” and said to watch for “a path toward 30%.”

surprises.description: The call introduced a substantial AI-factory SST development and timeline that the preview did not discuss: lab efficiency has reached 99%, with a working system targeted by year-end 2026 and volume shipments not expected until 2028. This is encouraging technical progress, but commercialization remains several years away.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AI factory SST solution demonstrated 99% efficiency in labs, with a working system targeted by end of 2026, pilot installations in 2027, and volume shipments in 2028.”

in_line: Europe was expected to carry the quarter: the preview said Nexis Q2 European production was “fully booked” and cited strong European market growth. Reported European revenue more than doubled year-over-year and rose 36% sequentially.

The preview flagged U.S. C&I allocation and structural share gains as a narrative item to watch. The call’s report of more than 50% share of recent U.S. C&I rooftop installations and installations on over 60% of Fortune 100 rooftops is consistent with that anticipated strength.

The preview expected management to reaffirm positive full-year free cash flow and noted FY capex guidance of $60–80 million. The call reaffirmed positive full-year free cash flow, reported Q2 free cash flow of $3.1 million, and maintained capex guidance of $60–80 million.

surprises.description: Same-location NOI was $5.9 million, above the preview’s $5.2–5.5 million base case, and grew 12%—faster than the 5–7% growth in the preview’s base scenario and even above its 8–10% bull case. The 12% growth also outpaced same-location revenue growth of 5.6% by roughly two times.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same location NOI grew 12% year-over-year to $5.9 million”; same-location revenue “rose 5.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was NOI of “$5.2 – 5.5M”; it said Q2 needed to show acceleration and described “same-loc NOI +5–7%” in its base scenario and “+8–10%” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the full-year guidance rather than narrowing it toward the low end, which the preview considered the more likely and more credible outcome given the required second-half run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed,” including revenue of $35–38 million, NOI of $21.5–23 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $15–16.5 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for a quiet narrowing toward the low end” and called reaffirming $35–38 million of revenue “strain[ing] credibility” given the second-half math.

surprises.description: Quarterly RevPAS reached about $225, exceeding the preview’s expected recovery range of $205–215 and reaching its highest second-quarter level in three years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RevPAS reached approximately $225 in the quarter, the highest second-quarter level in three years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 RevPAS “should recover toward the $205–215 zone.”

surprises.description: Contract parking volume growth accelerated to about 12% year over year, versus 6% growth in Q1. The preview noted Q1 growth and expected a seasonally stronger quarter, but did not anticipate this degree of acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contract parking volumes grew approximately 12% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, accelerating from 6% growth in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Contract volumes grew ~6% YoY in Q1” and said “Q2 is seasonally stronger.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a concrete pipeline of roughly $25 million in additional asset transactions, with possible closings by year-end. The preview anticipated continued asset sales but did not specify a comparable pending transaction pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is “currently negotiating approximately $25 million of additional asset transactions,” targeting a sub-3% cap rate, with “potential closings by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “more sales at those levels” and noted that the company had sold more than $30 million of assets, but gave no estimate for additional transactions under negotiation.

surprises.description: The company reported a quarter-over-quarter reduction in net debt, including payments of principal and accrued interest. The preview highlighted debt paydown as an important possible development but did not forecast a specific payment or reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company paid down “$3.7 million of principal and $0.8 million of accrued interest,” reducing net debt to $197.1 million from $200 million at Q1-end.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that disclosure of “a refinancing commitment, or a paydown materially changes the risk profile.”

surprises.description: Trailing 12-month portfolio utilization reached about 70%, its highest average quarterly level since the company took control of the portfolio in 2021. The preview did not identify a utilization expectation or flag this metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Portfolio utilization on a trailing 12-month basis reached approximately 70%, up 5 percentage points from 65% a year ago,” the highest average quarterly utilization since 2021.

in_line: Revenue was $8.9 million, within the preview’s $8.9–9.1 million base case; the preview had also warned that consensus might be too high because of asset sales.

Cumulative asset-rotation proceeds exceeding $30 million was consistent with the preview’s statement that more than $30 million of assets had already been sold and its expectation of continued sales at low cap rates.
Management’s limited comment on the take-private proposal was in line with the preview’s expectation that management would defer questions to the Special Committee.

surprises.description: Q2 net cash use was about $3.2 million, below the preview’s $5–7 million base case, and quarter-end cash and marketable securities were $11.1 million versus the preview’s base-case expectation of $7–9 million. This was closer to the preview’s bull case of burn at or below $4 million and cash of at least $10 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net cash use improved sharply to approximately $3.2 million in Q2, ending the quarter with only about $11.1 million in cash and marketable securities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (~55%): ... Burn $5–7M, cash $7–9M”; the bull case was “Burn ≤$4M, cash ≥$10M.”

surprises.description: The company introduced a Q4 2026 target to reach cash flow breakeven and begin generating cash, a more favorable outlook than the preview’s focus on reducing quarterly burn and obtaining additional funding; it gave no expectation of breakeven by Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company introduced new guidance to achieve cash flow breakeven and begin generating cash during Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 burn to fall, but said the company was “evaluating strategies to obtain additional funding” and described the base case as burn of $5–7 million.

surprises.description: FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $86–89 million rather than reaffirmed at $80–85 million, as the preview considered most likely. The new range is also above the preview’s cited $83.9 million Street estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $86-89 million ... up from the prior $80-85 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirm is the base case”; FY26 revenue was “$83.9M (Street) vs. $80–85M guided.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $21.7 million was about 7% above the $20.25 million consensus and $20.3 million model, whereas the preview’s base case was $20.0–20.7 million. Sequential growth was 13%, compared with the preview’s implied 5% sequential growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $21.7 million, up 18% year-over-year and 13% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $20.25M” consensus and “$20.3M” model; the base scenario was “$20.0–20.7M (in line),” with implied growth of “+10% YoY / +5% QoQ.”

surprises.description: The reported $7.7 million net loss was smaller than both the preview’s roughly $9 million consensus estimate and its roughly $10 million model estimate, despite the preview expecting a possible EPS miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating loss and net loss improved to $6.9 million and $7.7 million respectively.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss ~($10.0M)” in the preview’s model and “~($9.0M)” consensus; the preview modeled a modest EPS miss.

surprises.description: The company described a future reimbursement change not covered in the preview’s discussion of MAC-rate stabilization: beginning in 2027, reimbursement is to move from regional MAC pricing to a nationally published RVU framework under new Category 1 CPT codes. The preview does not establish whether this will improve or reduce payment, so the effect is uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Beginning January 1, 2027, reimbursement transitions from regional MAC pricing to a nationally published RVU framework under new Category 1 CPT codes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed that “all seven MACs now publish payment rates” and that management estimated “~75% of physician confidence had been recovered,” but did not mention a 2027 transition to national RVU pricing.

surprises.description: Operating expenses were $24.6 million, modestly above both the preview’s $24.3 million model and its roughly $23.6 million implied estimate, even though they were flat sequentially and lower year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses were $24.6 million, flat sequentially and roughly 6% lower year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Opex $24.3M” and cited “~$23.6M implied” consensus.

in_line: Gross margin was 81.9%, within the preview’s expected 81–82% range.

The CoHelix pipeline of about 55 active VAC reviews was within the preview’s expected 55–60 accounts in evaluation; its stated cadence of 10–15 completions per quarter broadly overlapped the expected 12–15.

U.S. Resell grew sequentially following reimbursement stabilization, consistent with the preview’s expected sequential build and its discussion of recovering physician confidence and more frequent ordering.

surprises.description: US Foods reported adjusted diluted EPS of $1.44, above the preview’s $1.37 estimate by about 5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS jumped 21% to $1.44.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS: $1.37.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $604 million, above the preview’s $585–595 million estimate, and margin reached 5.7% versus the preview’s roughly 5.6% estimate. The call attributed the beat in part to unusually strong fuel-surcharge recovery and vendor-management savings brought forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 10.2% to a record $604 million with margin expanding 29 basis points to a record 5.7%.” The beat was driven by “fuel surcharge recovery of about 70% (versus a typical 30-40%)” and “strategic vendor management gains pulled forward from the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$585–595M” and “Adj. EBITDA margin ~5.6%.”

surprises.description: Independent restaurant case growth reached 5.1%, above the preview’s 4.0–4.5% estimate and near the preview’s +5% bull trigger. Net new account generation was also described as the strongest in three years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Independent restaurant case growth accelerated to 5.1%, the strongest since Q4 2023 and the fifth consecutive quarter of acceleration, with net new account generation the strongest in three years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Independent rest. cases: +4.0–4.5%” and “+5%+ is the bull trigger.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the full 9–13% FY2026 adjusted EBITDA growth range rather than narrowing it toward the lower half, as the preview expected. The preview highlighted that the low end already required H2 acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year FY2026 guidance” including “9-13% adjusted EBITDA growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect the FY range to be narrowed to the lower half”; the base scenario expected the guide to be “explicitly steered to the low end.”

surprises.description: Fuel-surcharge recovery was about 70%, far above the 30–40% recovery rate the preview said was typical, and offset higher fuel costs rather than leaving the full expected fuel headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fuel surcharge recovery of about 70% (versus a typical 30-40%) that offset higher fuel costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “USFD recovers only ~30–40% of fuel increases via surcharge with a one-month lag”; the preview also said any improvement in that rate would be an EBITDA unlock.

surprises.description: Some strategic vendor-management gains expected to support the second half were pulled into Q2, which could leave less of that benefit for the H2 acceleration the preview said the full-year guide required.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Q2 EBITDA beat included “strategic vendor management gains pulled forward from the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the low end of full-year guidance required H2 EBITDA growth to accelerate and identified initiative proof points as something to watch.

surprises.description: Pronto was live in 52 markets, above the preview’s 47-market figure, and management raised its 2027 sales estimate to over $1.7 billion from $1.5 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pronto is now live in 52 markets” and “the 2027 estimate [was] raised to over $1.7 billion from a prior $1.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pronto (47 markets, $1.5B 2027 revenue target).”

surprises.description: The company repurchased $374 million of shares in Q2, a sharp step-up from the $125 million repurchased in Q1 and consistent with the preview’s bull-case possibility of buybacks reaccelerating.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $374 million of shares in Q2 (about $500 million year-to-date).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$125M in Q1” and the preview’s bull case cited “buyback re-accelerates”; it also warned that a slowdown could imply strain.

surprises.description: The seller compensation plan went live with flat year-over-year attrition, easing the preview’s concern that the transition could disrupt the sales force. The stated 2–3 year transition period was consistent with the preview’s expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new seller compensation plan went live company-wide in June with flat year-over-year attrition,” and management expects “2 to 3 years for most of the local sales force to fully transition to 100% variable pay.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Seller shift to 100% variable comp — rollout began ~June, and disruption risk is real over 2–3 years.”

surprises.description: Management reported substantial self-help savings, including more than $20 million of indirect-spend savings year-to-date and a target above $75 million this year, with over $100 million targeted in 2027. The preview flagged initiatives but did not set expectations for these savings amounts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Indirect spend savings of over $20 million year-to-date targeting more than $75 million this year and over $100 million in 2027.”

in_line: Net sales were $10.5 billion, within the preview’s $10.42–10.52 billion base-case range.
Total case volume grew 1.9%, within the preview’s estimated 1.5–2.0% range.
Net leverage ended at 2.6x, matching the preview’s stated 2.6x figure and remaining within the company’s 2–3x target range.

surprises.description: Instead of simply reaffirming the $380–390 million revenue outlook, Xeris raised the floor and narrowed guidance to $385–390 million. The upper end is unchanged, but the tighter, higher range was identified in the preview as a potential bull-case action.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised the bottom end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance and tightened the range to $385–390 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaffirm at $380–390M is the base case”; a “raise (or narrowing to $385–390M) is the bull trigger.”

surprises.description: The company fully retired its 2028 convertible notes, going beyond the preview’s mention of a June exchange of about $23 million of notes. That saves roughly $3 million in annual interest, but the associated $31 million non-cash charge is a separate, much larger-than-expected hit against the preview’s positive Q2 earnings outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fully retired its 2028 convertible notes in July via cash and equity, eliminating $34 million of debt and saving roughly $3 million in annual interest,” while “incurring a one-time non-cash GAAP charge of about $31 million in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “~$23M of convertible notes exchanged in June 2026, cutting ~$2M of annual interest”; its Q2 estimates were “$0.02” EPS consensus and approximately “$5–6M” net income in the author’s model.

surprises.description: GVOKE recovered sequentially, but missed the expected year-over-year inflection: revenue was $22.5 million versus the preview’s $23.5 million Q2’25 comparison, implying a decline rather than the expected return to YoY growth. The 10% sequential prescription growth is encouraging, but did not yet deliver that anticipated inflection in revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GVOKE rebounded to $22.5 million in net revenue, up 8% sequentially, with prescription growth of 10% versus Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A return to any YoY growth in Q2 confirms the thesis”; the preview’s Q2 estimate was “$23.5” million, compared with Q2’25 actual revenue of “23.5.”

surprises.description: The full-year SG&A increase is now expected to be about $50 million, $5 million more than the preview’s expected $45 million step-up. This means higher planned commercial and administrative spending than investors were led to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year SG&A is now expected to increase approximately $50 million versus 2025 (up $5 million from prior guidance).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided to “~$45M incremental SG&A” for FY2026.

surprises.description: Net product revenue came in below the preview’s $92.4 million model estimate, even though total revenue landed within the preview’s $91–93 million base case. The product-only result was specifically flagged as a key metric to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net product revenue of $91 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2’26E estimate was “Net product revenue … $92.4” million and said to “Watch the product-only line.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $19.3 million, slightly below the preview’s $20–23 million base estimate. It remained above the preview’s roughly $18 million caution threshold and grew strongly, so the shortfall was modest rather than a break in the profitability outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose over 50% year-over-year to $19.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$20–23M” of adjusted EBITDA and said a result “below ~$18M” would signal spending arriving faster than revenue.

surprises.description: Xeris reported securing a second U.S. patent for XP-8121 and receiving a notice of allowance for a third, an additional pipeline-protection update not anticipated in the preview. The preview focused on confirmation of the Phase 3 timeline and a fall program review.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management secured a second US patent (July 28) plus a notice of allowance for a third.”

in_line: Total Q2 revenue of $92.1 million was within the preview’s $91–93 million base case and above its cited $90.73 million consensus estimate.

Recorlev revenue of $56.8 million was close to the preview’s $56.5 million estimate and within its stated $54–57 million expected range; the reported record patient starts supported the expected growth narrative.
Gross margin of approximately 86%, up nearly 400 basis points year over year, was broadly consistent with the preview’s approximately 87% estimate and expected 400-basis-point improvement.

Keveyis revenue of $11.7 million was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of roughly $12 million per quarter, and the patent outlook through at least 2039 matched the durability discussion in the preview.

The approximately $25 million full-year R&D increase, largely for XP-8121 Phase 3, matched the preview’s expectation of about $25 million of incremental R&D. The Phase 3 start by year-end also remained in line with the expected 2026 start; the September 9 webinar supplied a specific date for the anticipated fall program review.

surprises.description: Beacon Point financing terms were stronger than the preview’s already-positive description: the notes priced 20 basis points inside Riverbend, were substantially oversubscribed, and extended amortization from two years to four. The preview noted Beacon Point’s higher rating notch, but did not anticipate these additional favorable terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Beacon Point notes priced one notch higher and 20 basis points inside Riverbend, were substantially oversubscribed, and extended amortization from 2 years to 4 years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Baa2 (Moody's) — a notch above River Bend. Cost of capital is the moat”

surprises.description: Hut eliminated its only remaining parent-recourse debt by converting $159.3 million of notes into 9.7 million shares. That reduces parent recourse debt, but the share issuance brings dilution; the preview highlighted equity issuance as a risk rather than anticipating this debt-to-equity conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company eliminated its only remaining parent recourse debt by converting $159.3 million of notes into 9.7 million shares.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bear case for a 6x-beta, $12.6B-cap name is an equity raise. Watch for any ATM refresh or shelf language.”

surprises.description: The balance-sheet cash figure was not largely available for corporate use: of approximately $7 billion in cash, $6.8 billion was restricted to project accounts, leaving only $233.6 million of unrestricted corporate cash alongside approximately $7.6 billion of total debt. This makes the corporate liquidity picture more constrained than the headline cash balance alone suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The balance sheet grew to approximately $7.6 billion of total debt and $7 billion of cash, with $6.8 billion restricted to project accounts and only $233.6 million of unrestricted corporate cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bear case for a 6x-beta, $12.6B-cap name is an equity raise. Watch for any ATM refresh or shelf language”; the preview also flagged “any framing of corporate-level liquidity needs.”

surprises.description: The development pipeline reached about 8.7 GW, roughly 300 MW above the preview’s 8.375 GW figure. That is a modest expansion, though it remained below the preview’s greater-than-9-GW bull-case marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The development pipeline grew to about 8.7 gigawatts, up approximately 300 megawatts from the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “8,375 MW development pipeline” and the bull scenario’s “pipeline >9 GW.”

in_line: Revenue was $74.9 million versus the preview’s roughly $79–80 million working consensus, but the preview explicitly made another revenue miss its base case and gave a $72–80 million base-case range.

A large GAAP loss driven by digital-asset mark-to-market was anticipated; the call reported a $177.1 million net loss, including a $138 million non-cash digital-asset loss. The call facts do not provide EPS for a direct comparison with the preview’s GAAP EPS estimate.

The second Beacon Point lease and the Riverbend and Beacon Point project financings were already disclosed in the preview; the reported 352 MW lease, approximately $9.8 billion of base-term value, and $7.5 billion total financing did not constitute new surprises.
The 9%-to-7% facility refinancing was already noted in the preview.

surprises.description: Organic revenue growth was 6.6%, well above the preview’s implied 4.5%–5% range. Reported revenue also edged past the $813.6 million consensus, reaching $816 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue grew 5.2% to a record $816 million, with organic revenue growth of 6.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $813.6M”; organic revenue growth “~4.5–5% (implied).”

surprises.description: Consumer adjusted EBITDA grew 24.2% and its margin expanded 310 basis points to 21.3%, a notably strong profitability result not anticipated in the preview’s Consumer discussion, which centered on organic growth and the effects of exiting lower-margin lines.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumer segment adjusted EBITDA margin surged 310 basis points year-over-year to 21.3% as adjusted EBITDA grew 24.2% to $77 million, driven by exiting lower-margin service lines and higher productivity.”

surprises.description: The full-year capex outlook was raised to approximately 8.5% of revenue, above the preview’s expected 7%–8% range. Management called the higher level an anomaly relative to its long-term 6%–8% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year capital expenditures guidance was raised to approximately 8.5% of revenue”; management characterized it as “an anomaly versus the long-term 6%-8% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 guidance: “Capex | 7%–8% of revenue.”

surprises.description: Business exits continued to weigh on Q2 revenue by about 1%, or roughly $6 million; without them, organic growth would have been about 80 basis points higher. The preview had highlighted the exit-related Consumer headwind but expected Q2 to benefit as the toughest Consumer comparison passed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business exits from the restructuring plan created an approximately 1% revenue drag (about $6 million in Q2), meaning organic growth would have been roughly 80 basis points higher without them.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q1 was the toughest Consumer comp” and that “Q2 must accelerate,” citing “~1% of self-inflicted headwind from exiting non-strategic, lower-margin lines” in Q1.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.59 exceeded the published $0.56 consensus, but only reached the bottom of the preview’s inferred $0.59–$0.62 functional bar rather than exceeding that higher bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS increased 13.5% to $0.59.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Published consensus was “$0.56”; the preview inferred “the functional bar is closer to $0.59–$0.62 adjusted EPS.”

surprises.description: Certification testing grew by more than 10%, primarily on volume, and management said volume contributed more than price to overall revenue growth. The preview discussed certification as an Industrial growth area but did not anticipate this strength or the volume-led mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Certification testing grew over 10% for the quarter, driven primarily by volume, with management noting volume contributed more than price to overall revenue growth.”

surprises.description: Industrial revenue grew 7.8% (7.2% organically), but its adjusted EBITDA margin slipped 10 basis points to 32.3% because of higher performance-based incentive compensation. The margin decline was a small offset to the preview’s focus on broad margin expansion, though Industrial growth remained above the preview’s roughly 7% concern threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial revenue rose 7.8% to $402 million (7.2% organic), but adjusted EBITDA margin slipped 10 basis points to 32.3% due to higher performance-based incentive compensation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Deceleration below ~7% would signal the megatrend narrative is cooling” and estimated consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin at “~26.5–27.5%.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $219 million, close to the preview’s derived estimate of approximately $220 million; the 26.8% margin was within its estimated 26.5%–27.5% range. The company also reaffirmed the approximately 27% full-year margin outlook rather than raising it, as the preview’s base case anticipated.
The company maintained its mid-single-digit full-year organic revenue growth outlook, consistent with the preview’s stated guidance.
The Eurofins Electrical & Electronics acquisition remained on track for a Q4 2026 close, and the DQS stake sale remained on track for the second half of 2026, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $76.1 million, below the preview’s $82–88 million estimate. Excluding Longridge, EBITDA was a record $48.7 million, but that did not make up the gap to the overall estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached $76.1 million”; “excluding Longridge (held for sale) it was a record $48.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA consensus is my derivation… **$82–88M**”; “Core EBITDA $82–88M” in the base scenario.

surprises.description: Longridge’s capacity factor was 85%, below the preview’s expectation of 95% or more for a normalized quarter. EBITDA still rose year over year despite the planned outage, and management said Q3 capacity was running near 100%.
surprises.fact_evidence: An “11-day planned outage” limited capacity factor to “85%,” despite Q2 adjusted EBITDA rising to $27.4 million from $23 million; Q3 capacity factor was “currently running near 100%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A clean quarter should show Long Ridge back near a 95%+ capacity factor.”

surprises.description: The Wheeling synergy target was stated as $20 million rather than the preview’s $23 million, and management said the full impact would not appear until Q3 and Q4. That is less near-term realization than the preview expected when it said to watch for the remaining $13 million to show up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Wheeling integration is roughly 80% complete with $20 million of targeted cost synergies on track,” but “full impact will not appear until Q3 and Q4 as initiatives ramp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Of the $23M targeted synergies, $10M was realized in Q1 — watch for the remaining $13M landing.”

surprises.description: The Longridge sale is expected to reduce parent-level debt service by about $25 million annually, below the preview’s roughly $30 million annual interest-savings expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: The sale is expected to eliminate “approximately $1.4 billion of total debt” and reduce “parent-level debt service by about $25 million annually.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the sale would cut parent interest by “~$30M/yr.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed more than $50 million of incremental annual EBITDA potential from new rail revenue sources, an opportunity the preview did not identify. This is potential rather than reported EBITDA, and no timing was given.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimated “in excess of $50 million of incremental annual EBITDA potential from new rail revenue sources.”

surprises.description: Jefferson’s crude ship volumes were temporarily reduced by Middle East volatility, a headwind the preview did not flag. Management expects volumes to recover in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: Jefferson’s crude ship volumes “were temporarily reduced by Middle East volatility and are expected to recover in Q3.”

surprises.description: Transtar volumes softened because US Steel overhauled its largest Gary Works blast furnace, an unanticipated operating headwind. Higher-priced Wheeling carloads offset the volume weakness and lifted blended pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Transtar volumes were softer in Q2 due to US Steel’s overhaul of its largest Gary Works blast furnace,” offset by “higher-priced Wheeling carloads driving higher blended pricing.”

in_line: Tidewater Logistics was acquired at the end of Q2 for $45 million and is expected to add about $9 million of annual EBITDA, consistent with the preview’s stated deal terms and expectation that it would contribute essentially nothing to Q2.

Repauno Phase 2 remained targeted for completion by year-end 2026 with revenue beginning in early 2027; the combined phases’ nearly 100,000-barrel-per-day capacity and roughly $80 million of annual EBITDA potential were consistent with the preview.

The three Jefferson expansion projects remained a potential opportunity of more than $50 million of incremental annual EBITDA with little to no additional capex, broadly consistent with the preview’s discussion of roughly $50 million of expansion potential still in negotiation.

surprises.description: XPEL reported Q2 revenue of $143.1 million, well above the preview’s $135.1–$135.6 million consensus and the company’s $135–$137 million guide. About $2 million was pulled forward ahead of Q3 price increases, but the reported result still substantially exceeded expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 14.7% to a record $143.1 million, exceeding company expectations, though about $2 million was pull-ahead sales ahead of Q3 price increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $135.1–135.6M”; “Company guidance | $135–137M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 44.1%, above the preview’s estimated 43.0–43.5% and its key 43.5%+ watch level. This was a stronger Q2 margin result than the preview’s base case of modest expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 44.1% in Q2 from 43.7% in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~43.0–43.5% (est.)”; “Gross margin vs. 43.5%+ (‘past highs’).”

surprises.description: EPS exceeded the preview’s $0.57–$0.61 diluted estimate range: reported EPS was $0.65 and adjusted EPS was $0.68. Both were clearly above the preview’s approximate $0.60 number to beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS was $0.65 (adjusted $0.68).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | $0.57–0.61 (mid ~$0.60)”; “Treat $0.60 as the number to beat.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow reached a record $30.8 million, much stronger than the preview’s cash-flow concern based on weak Q1 operating cash flow. The preview’s risk of another negative-FCF quarter was not necessarily avoided, given Q2 CapEx of $65.1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash flow from operations hit a record $30.8 million, while Q2 CapEx was $65.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 OCF was $7.4M against $10.3M net income, with $9.7M capex → negative FCF”; “a second consecutive negative-FCF quarter is a real risk.”

surprises.description: Q2 CapEx included a real-estate purchase and was partly financed with a new $44.8 million 10-year term loan—specific spending and financing details the preview did not identify. The preview had anticipated substantial manufacturing-program spending and FCF pressure, so the surprise is mainly the acquisition and debt financing detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 CapEx was $65.1 million including the real estate purchase, financed partly with a $44.8 million 10-year term loan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With the $110M program spending through 2H26, a second consecutive negative-FCF quarter is a real risk.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a manufacturing ramp-up drag of about $0.03 per share in Q2 and expects $0.03–$0.04 per share in Q3. That is a more concrete near-term earnings cost than the preview’s characterization of the 2026 EPS impact as minimal, though the expected mid-2027 margin benefits remain on the preview’s timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Manufacturing ramp-up costs were about $0.03 per share in Q2 and are expected to rise to $0.03-$0.04 per share in Q3, with incremental margin benefits beginning mid-2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “reaffirming or raising the 2028 targets”; “2026 EPS impact is ‘minimal’ ex-one-timers with contribution from mid-2027.”

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $137–$139 million was broadly within the preview’s expected range of about $137–$140 million, although it implies a sequential decline.
The preview anticipated another negative-FCF risk amid heavy program spending; Q2’s $65.1 million of CapEx kept cash investment substantial despite record operating cash flow.
Management expected modest gross-margin improvement after Q2, and it said margin should continue to increase modestly through the rest of the year.
The preview flagged the Middle East as a downside risk; the reported India/Middle East region declined 5%.

surprises.description: AECOM recorded a $337 million pretax charge tied mainly to a delayed P3 construction-management project, cutting EPS by $1.99, and sharply lowered its full-year guidance: EPS to $4.05 at the midpoint, adjusted EBITDA to about $950 million, and NSR to about $7.3 billion. The preview expected FY26 EPS guidance of $5.90–$6.10 and discussed a possible narrowing or reaffirmation, not a reduction of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AECOM recorded a $337 million pretax charge in Q3 2026, primarily due to a delay in delivering a large P3 design-build construction management project, reducing EPS by $1.99”; “revised its full-year guidance to approximately $7.3 billion NSR, $950 million adjusted EBITDA, and $4.05 EPS at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adjusted EPS guidance action. Guide is $5.90–$6.10”; the base case anticipated guidance “narrowed to ~$5.95–$6.10 rather than raised.”

surprises.description: The two troubled projects are expected to keep consuming cash well into FY27: management forecast roughly $500 million of cash burn across the first two quarters, with completion in Q1 and Q2. AECOM is pursuing $600–650 million in claims, but the preview did not flag these projects or this scale of future cash drain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The two troubled P3 construction management projects will drive continued cash burn totaling roughly $500 million across the first two quarters of fiscal 2027, with completion expected in Q1 and Q2 of fiscal 2027”; “AECOM is pursuing claims of $600-650 million on the two projects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance is ~$400M and the first half was roughly breakeven at best, so essentially the entire year's cash has to land in H2.”

surprises.description: Even excluding the project charge, Americas adjusted operating margin was 18%, below the preview’s expectation that the segment was already at about 20%. Management said elevated business-development activity reduced margin by about 140 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Americas segment posted a negative 16.1% adjusted operating margin due to the charge, but was 18% excluding it, with elevated business development activity reducing margin by about 140 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Americas at 20.0% is already there.”

surprises.description: Backlog and bookings were considerably stronger than the preview’s already-positive base case: backlog grew 13% year over year, and book-to-burn was 1.6x, versus the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly 1.0–1.1x and backlog growth around 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog reached an all-time high, growing 13% year-over-year, on a 1.6x book-to-burn (1.8x in the Americas) and a 1.4x year-to-date book-to-burn.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “backlog ~$26–27B, book-to-burn ~1.0–1.1x”; the preview also cited record backlog “(+8%).”

surprises.description: International’s 14.3% adjusted operating margin was a stronger result than the preview’s expectation that the segment would remain soft, even as it turned back to growth. Double-digit Australian growth, high-single-digit U.K. growth, and backlog up 28% accompanied the margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The International segment returned to growth with 4% NSR increase and a 14.3% adjusted operating margin, driven by double-digit growth in Australia and high single-digit growth in the U.K., with backlog up 28%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “International still soft but less negative”; the preview noted Q2’s “11.1% margin (flat).”

surprises.description: Project cash burn is also expected to raise FY27 interest expense by $30–35 million year over year, while near-term share buybacks will be constrained. The preview had described a potential CM sale as a catalyst for increased buyback capacity, but did not anticipate this financing pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Higher debt balances from project cash burn are expected to raise interest expense by $30-35 million year-over-year in fiscal 2027, while share buybacks will be constrained near-term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a signed CM deal could mean “proceeds against a $9.45B market cap with 1.2x net leverage” and be “materially accretive to buyback capacity.”

surprises.description: Despite the charge, AECOM raised its adjusted EBITDA margin target to 17.4% from 17%. The preview discussed margin expectations but did not anticipate this specific target increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the charge, AECOM reaffirmed its prior guidance of ~$7.65-7.7 billion NSR, $1.29 billion adjusted EBITDA, and $6.00 EPS, and raised its adjusted EBITDA margin target to 17.4% from 17%.”

surprises.description: AECOM reported roughly 30% growth in both U.S. Water and Department of War pipelines, alongside strong data-center and defense-related demand. The preview noted data-center demand but did not anticipate these quantified pipeline expansions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Key pipeline expansions include roughly 30% growth in both U.S. Water and Department of War pipelines, alongside strong data center and defense-related demand supporting the 5%-8% long-term organic growth algorithm.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “AI-sector/data-center design wins” as an offset to watch, but did not give a comparable pipeline-growth expectation.

in_line: Excluding the charge, AECOM reaffirmed its prior full-year EPS guidance of about $6.00, consistent with the preview’s expected FY26 range of $5.90–$6.10.
International returned to positive NSR growth, in line with the preview’s expectation that the segment would begin converting its growing backlog into revenue.

surprises.description: PowerFleet cut FY2027 revenue guidance to $468–473 million from $485–490 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $111–114 million from $122–125 million. Management attributed the cuts to forgoing about $17 million of South African nonstrategic revenue, with an estimated $11 million adjusted EBITDA impact that includes about $5 million in one-time costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cut full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $468-473 million from $485-490 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $111-114 million from $122-125 million,” driven by “a deliberate South African revenue reprioritization”; the company began “forgoing an estimated $17 million of nonstrategic full-year revenue,” with an “~$11 million adjusted EBITDA impact including ~$5 million of one-time costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided FY2027 to “$485–490M revenue” and “$122–125M adjusted EBITDA,” and highlighted whether those guides would be “held, raised, or quietly softened.”

surprises.description: Q1 adjusted EBITDA was well below the preview’s guidance-derived estimate, even though the preview anticipated a more back-half-weighted year. The result was $21.5 million, versus an estimated $25–26 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 total revenue was $110.8 million… with adjusted EBITDA of $21.5 million (19.4% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q1 adjusted EBITDA at “~$25–26M” based on the full-year guide and described a sequential dip from Q4 as the guided outcome.

surprises.description: The South African National Treasury deployment advanced much faster than the preview’s late-FY2027/FY2028 timing implied: more than 70,000 vehicles are already installed and near-term ARR exceeds $27 million. That is also far ahead of the roughly 10,000 assets originally expected at this stage, though the preview had noted 60,000+ assets in deployment planning.
surprises.fact_evidence: The contract “has accelerated to over $27 million in near-term ARR and 70,000+ vehicle installations,” roughly “7-9x the ~10,000 assets originally expected at this stage”; deployment is projected to reach “80,000-90,000 vehicles.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management framed contribution as “late FY2027” and “wholeheartedly in FY2028,” and described “60,000+ assets in deployment planning.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $110.8 million came in below the $115.5 million consensus estimate, although it fell within the preview’s roughly $110–115 million guidance-implied range. The miss was about 4% versus consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 total revenue was $110.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “$115.5M”; the preview also gave a “Guidance-implied range” of “~$110–115M.”

surprises.description: The company lowered full-year free cash flow guidance and moved its net loss outlook from expected net income to a loss. Both changes reversed the preview’s positive full-year cash-flow expectation and the anticipated profitability trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was cut to $20-23 million from $30-35 million, and net loss guidance moved to $6-8 million from prior net income of $4-8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified FY2027 free cash flow of “+$30–35M” as guided and flagged the “path to positive GAAP net income in H2 FY27” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: A WiFi chip compatibility issue delayed about $3.2 million of high-margin product revenue in Q1, with some Q2 revenue expected to shift to Q3. Management said it expects to recover the delayed revenue within the fiscal year, limiting the full-year impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A production constraint from a WiFi chip compatibility issue delayed approximately $3.2 million of high-margin product revenue in Q1,” with “some Q2 revenue expected to shift into Q3 but fully recaptured within the fiscal year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described product revenue as lumpy and said it could swing the total revenue line “±$3M on its own,” but did not anticipate this production constraint or timing shift.

surprises.description: Despite cutting its FY2027 guidance, management reaffirmed a stronger Q4 exit-rate outlook: about $495 million in annualized revenue and more than $130 million in adjusted EBITDA. That is a more constructive longer-term run-rate statement than the revised full-year outlook alone suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “reaffirmed an annualized Q4 fiscal 2027 exit revenue run rate of approximately $495 million (implying over $130 million adjusted EBITDA at ~27% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview centered on FY2027 guidance of “$485–490M revenue” and “$122–125M adjusted EBITDA,” and said reaffirmation of that full-year guide mattered most.

surprises.description: Product gross margin fell sharply to 21.3%, versus about 29% in the prior quarter, and management expects a recovery only in the second half. The preview noted product’s low-margin, lumpy nature but did not flag this degree of margin weakness or the timing of recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product revenue fell 6.7% year-over-year to $16.5 million with product gross margin dropping to 21.3% (from ~29% prior quarter), while management expects recovery to 31-32% in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called product revenue “Lumpy and low-margin” and discussed its potential to move quarterly revenue, without a specific gross-margin expectation.

surprises.description: The call reported a new multimillion-dollar ARR deal with a European construction leader spanning 26 countries, as well as 12 Fortune 500 on-site expansions. These specific customer wins were not part of the preview’s stated expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported “12 Fortune 500 on-site expansions, and a new multimillion-dollar ARR deal with a European construction leader across 26 countries.”

surprises.description: PowerFleet announced a new President and CFO and a Chief AI Officer appointment. The preview did not signal an executive transition or a new AI leadership role.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PowerFleet appointed Paul Lalljie as President and CFO (replacing David Wilson) and Vishal Vallabha as Chief AI Officer.”

surprises.description: Underlying sales grew 6%, above the preview’s roughly 5% Q3 expectation, showing a stronger revenue inflection than the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Underlying sales grew 6%” in Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance calls for ~5.5% reported / ~5% underlying growth”; the preview also says the base case is “in-line-to-slightly-better volumes.”

surprises.description: Adjusted segment EBITDA margin reached 28.5%, 50 basis points above the preview’s roughly 28% Q3 bar. The preview flagged input-cost and tariff pressures, but price cost exceeded inflation and margin expansion was stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted segment EBITDA margin expanded 140 basis points to 28.5%,” with “price cost exceeding inflation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 needs ~28% vs. 27.1% LY”; the preview also flags “higher input costs, restructuring, and FX” as pressures.

surprises.description: Orders grew 7%, exceeding the preview’s ≥6% confirmation threshold and its roughly 5% run-rate base case. Software & Systems orders were especially strong at 10%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Underlying orders grew 7% in Q3, with Software & Systems leading orders growth at 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says to watch for “≥6% to confirm the FY27 setup” and describes the base case as “orders ~+5%.”

surprises.description: Growth-vertical demand was notably strong: the group was up 27%, with semiconductor sales up 53% and power sales up 37%. The preview anticipated power/Ovation momentum, but did not set expectations for growth at these levels or for such strong semiconductor results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Growth verticals were up 27% overall, with semiconductor sales up 53% (orders up 70%) and power sales up 37%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlights “Power / data center / Ovation momentum” and says Ovation orders were “+74% in Q1 and +41% in Q2.”

surprises.description: The project funnel expanded to $12.4 billion and Ovation lead times now reach into Q4 2027 and 2028, indicating longer-duration demand visibility beyond the preview’s cited $11.2 billion funnel and its focus on near-term orders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The project funnel grew $1.2 billion to $12.4 billion (up 8% year-over-year), with power now at $3 billion and LNG at $2.2 billion, and Ovation lead times now extend into Q4 2027 and 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cites a “project funnel of $11.2B” and asks investors to watch orders and backlog conversion visibility into FY27.

surprises.description: Q3 free cash flow reached $1.3 billion, well above the prior-year Q3 figure cited in the preview and a strong build toward the full-year target. However, the reported cash flow benefited from an $82 million tariff refund and tax timing shifts into Q4, making the quarter’s cash strength less representative of recurring performance and shifting some cash timing into the next quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 free cash flow rose 36% to $1.3 billion at a 27.1% margin, boosted by $82 million in tariff refunds (accounted for on a cash basis and excluded from adjusted results) and tax timing shifts into Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says “FCF has to build materially in 2H to hold the guide” and cites Q3 FY25 FCF of $970M.

surprises.description: Full-year underlying sales growth guidance was raised to 3.5%, above the roughly 3% outlook the preview treated as the current baseline. The increase is a positive change to the full-year sales outlook, separate from the anticipated EPS guidance raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was raised to 5% GAAP sales growth, 3.5% underlying growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says the FY underlying growth number was approximately “3%” and identifies trimming it as a bear-case outcome.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.71 beat the $1.68 consensus and exceeded the top of the company’s $1.65–$1.70 guidance range, though it was within the preview’s $1.70–$1.73 base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 13% year-over-year to $1.71, exceeding the top of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists “Q3 FY26 Consensus” adjusted EPS of “$1.68” and company guidance of “$1.65–$1.70”; its base case is “$1.70–$1.73.”

in_line: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance of approximately $6.55 was consistent with the preview’s stated expectation of a raise to at least $6.55; the preview’s base case also allowed for $6.50–$6.58.
Software ACV grew 9% to $1.68 billion, with management confident of exiting the year above 10% growth, consistent with the preview’s reported 9% growth and target of more than 10%.
The approximately $2.2 billion shareholder-return commitment, including $1.2 billion in dividends and $1 billion in buybacks, matched the preview’s stated FY26 commitment.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $101.9M, above both the $96.04M consensus and the preview’s roughly $94M build, with DefenCath at $66.1M versus the roughly $60M pre-guided figure. The beat was therefore larger than expected and came mainly from DefenCath; Melinta’s $35.8M was within the preview’s $32–36M estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue reached $101.9 million,” including “DefenCath sales of $66.1 million”; the preview cited “Revenue $96.04M” consensus, a “~$94M” build, and DefenCath “~$60M” management guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $96.04M” consensus; “Total net revenue ~ $94M”; “DefenCath $60M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $58.7M, well above the preview’s roughly $46M estimate. The preview expected a sharp sequential decline from Q1’s $70.0M, but the reported decline was much smaller.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $58.7 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$46M — vs. $70.0M in Q1.”

surprises.description: The company raised its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $125–140M, above the preview’s expected $115–135M range. This was an improvement to the outlook even as revenue and DefenCath guidance were maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $125-140 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA guide $115–135M.”

surprises.description: July order volumes were reported as stable with larger dialysis players and in line with the post-TDAPA forecast, rather than showing a clear immediate volume collapse after the reimbursement change. The preview identified post-July usage as the central uncertainty and described its base case as too early to tell.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July DefenCath order volumes tracked in line with the post-TDAPA forecast,” with “stabilized volumes with larger players” and “expected attrition among small players.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called these “the first real data on whether dialysis operators keep using DefenCath” and said the base case was “too early to tell; management defers to Q3.”

surprises.description: CorMedix signed a multi-year supply agreement with another large dialysis organization, bringing its contracts to all five top U.S. dialysis providers. The preview highlighted customer retention risk but did not anticipate this additional contract; the pilot begins in Q3 and possible expansion is in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed a multi-year supply agreement with an additional large dialysis organization,” giving it “commercial contracts with all 5 top U.S. dialysis providers,” with “a pilot of a couple hundred clinics starting in Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: Net income and diluted EPS exceeded the preview’s estimates: $26.0M and $0.29 per share versus approximately $21.5M and $0.23 per diluted share. The result was above the preview’s cited $0.26 consensus EPS as well, despite tax expense and non-operating mark-to-market items.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $26.0 million ($0.29 diluted EPS),” including “$12.7 million in income tax expense and $4.2 million in non-operating mark-to-market items.”
