surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net income (28% tax) ~$21.5M”; “EPS ~$0.27 basic / ~$0.23 diluted”; consensus EPS “$0.26.”

surprises.description: Reported G&A benefited from a $4.2M insurance reimbursement credit, including $2.7M tied to prior-period legal fees. That one-off lowered reported expenses and means underlying G&A was higher than the headline expense level suggests, an earnings-quality caveat the preview had not identified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “G&A benefited from a $4.2 million insurance reimbursement credit (of which $2.7 million related to prior-period legal fees), artificially lowering expenses and implying a higher underlying run rate.”

surprises.description: The Q2 cash position was substantially above the preview’s stated $178.1M cash figure: the company ended the quarter with $256.7M in cash, or roughly $267M including investments. First-half operating cash flow was also $128.6M, versus $49.7M in the prior-year period.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ended Q2 2026 with $256.7 million in cash and cash equivalents (roughly $267 million combined cash and investments),” and “generated $128.6 million in operating cash flow in the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$178.1M cash” and said the current balance should be verified against the 10-Q.

surprises.description: Management identified Medicare Advantage contracting as a meaningful long-term growth avenue, although it is excluded from 2026 guidance. This was a new potential growth source not discussed in the preview, and it does not change the near-term guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medicare Advantage contracting is being pursued as a meaningful long-term growth avenue but was excluded from 2026 guidance.”

in_line: FY2026 revenue guidance of $325–345M and DefenCath revenue guidance of $175–195M were reaffirmed, as the preview expected.
Melinta portfolio revenue of $35.8M was within the preview’s estimated $32–36M range.
The ReSPECT study’s non-inferiority endpoint had already been reported before the preview, and the expected sNDA timing was H2 2026; the call’s expected Q3 2026 submission is within that window.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $60 million, below the preview’s roughly $65 million base case, and adjusted operating earnings of $0.03 per share were below its +$0.15 base-case estimate. EBITDA was within the preview’s broad $50–85 million range, but the per-share result was notably weaker than the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA…to $60 million in Q2 2026 with a 7% margin”; “Adjusted operating earnings were only $0.03 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base-case build…≈ $66M”; the base scenario estimated “Adj. EPS +$0.15” and “Adj. EBITDA ~$65M.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a substantial second-half price-and-mix benefit of $75–85 million, with about 70% from price. The preview expected a second-half recovery but had no quantified second-half benefit, and specifically highlighted that management had previously declined to quantify price realization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guides to a $75-85 million second-half benefit from better price and mix versus the first half, with roughly 70% attributable to price.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “declined to quantify the sequential price benefit” and highlighted the question of “Quantified price realization”; it expected the “2H recovery” to be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: North American second-half volumes are now expected to decline, rather than the volume recovery or reversal that formed part of the preview’s constructive bridge. The decline reflects lost Riverdale supply, a longer-than-planned Eastover outage, and tariffs curtailing imports.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North American second-half volumes will decline due to the loss of ~90,000-100,000 tons of Riverdale supply and a longer-than-planned Eastover outage…while new tariffs are curtailing planned imports from Brazil and Europe.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 bridge expected “Partial reversal” of the inventory-build volume impact, and its base case included a “~$25M volume reversal”; it also described a constructive 2H recovery as the expected framing.

surprises.description: New tariffs erased a previously expected $20 million benefit from Brazilian imports, pushing the footprint-alignment estimate back to $85 million. That reverses the preview’s expectation that tariff relief had improved the 2026 transition headwind by $20 million, mostly benefiting the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New tariffs eliminated the previously expected $20 million benefit from importing Brazilian tons, pushing the footprint alignment estimate back to the original $85 million figure from the February guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “North America footprint transition headwind –$65M to EBITDA (improved $20M on tariff relief, mostly benefiting 2H).”

surprises.description: The Eastover projects are now expected to produce $55 million in total annual benefits, modestly above the preview’s cited $50 million run-rate benefit. Management expects $30–40 million of the benefits to be realized in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Eastover strategic investments…are expected to generate $55 million of total annual benefits, with $30-40 million realized in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $50M run-rate benefit is a 2027 story.”

in_line: North American margins improved to 15% from 10% sequentially, consistent with the preview’s expectation that announced price increases would be largely realized in Q2.
The long-term targets were reaffirmed: management cited over $300 million in annual free cash flow and greater than 15% ROIC, consistent with the preview’s stated targets.
Europe remains under strategic review, with no immediate closure or sale announced; the preview had identified Europe as a key debate and flagged restructuring or capacity action as a possibility.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $30,000, well below the preview’s consensus estimate of about $70,000, though it landed at the bottom of the preview’s $30,000–$70,000 base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was just $30,000”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$70K”

surprises.description: The net loss widened to $9.1 million, worse than the preview’s expected $7.5–$8.0 million loss; operating expenses of $10 million also exceeded the preview’s watch level of $9.4 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $9.1 million”; “operating expenses of $10 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss | ~$7.5–8.0M”; “Watch for opex ≤ $9.4M”

surprises.description: The CE-mark submission slipped from the preview’s mid-2026 target to Q4 2026. Management said it chose to complete additional assay-performance and sample-stability testing first.
surprises.fact_evidence: “European CE marking submission was pushed to Q4 2026 (from midyear)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “the CE mark dossier was targeted for mid-2026”; “Due mid-2026 — confirm or slip.”

surprises.description: Sera reported more than 20 payer opportunities across more than 20 states and said it had exceeded its goal of doubling payer discussions. The preview’s stated baseline was 13 payers across 15 states, although these opportunities are discussions rather than a reported count of contracted payers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “exceeded its 2026 goal of doubling payer discussions, now engaging over 20 payer opportunities across more than 20 states”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “13 payers / 15 states baseline”; “A move to 15+ payers, or the first contracted commercial payer, would be the genuine narrative unlock.”

surprises.description: A July-published PRIME subgroup analysis added stronger results for first-time mothers than the preview had highlighted: it reported larger reductions in NICU admissions and neonatal morbidity than the preview’s overall-study figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “a 22% reduction in NICU admissions, a 30% reduction in severe neonatal morbidity, and a number-needed-to-screen-and-treat of 28”

in_line: Cash and the runway were broadly as expected: the company reported $80.3 million in cash and securities and said it funds operations through significant milestones into 2029, versus the preview’s $78–$80 million estimate and focus on reaffirming the through-2029 runway.
The fourth commercial partnership program launched as the preview expected, which had said a fourth program should land that quarter.

The preview highlighted uncertainty about when Illinois coverage would translate into cash flows and expected no reimbursement date in its base case. The reported gradual penetration path and minimal 2026 revenue impact are consistent with that near-term uncertainty.

surprises.description: NeuroPace reported Q2 revenue of $22.8 million versus the preview’s $22.6 million consensus, with RNS revenue growing 21.3%—above the preview’s key threshold of 20% and its roughly 16% consensus-based estimate. This was a modest beat, not the much larger revenue outcome described in the preview’s bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $22.8 million”; “RNS System revenue of $22.5 million growing 21.3% versus the prior year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $22.6M”; “Underlying RNS growth ≥20% in Q2 vs. the ~16% embedded in published consensus.”

surprises.description: The FDA’s request for additional clinical evidence leaves more of an evidence burden than the preview’s hoped-for path of additional analyses without new clinical data. However, the FDA called the application not approvable rather than disapproved, recommended the SIR process, and management expects a meeting within weeks and believes the amendment may be reviewed without restarting the full clock.
surprises.fact_evidence: The FDA “deemed NeuroPace's IGE PMA supplement not approvable in its current form,” citing “requests for additional clinical evidence”; it “recommended pursuing the interactive Submission Issue Request (SIR) process.” Management expects to schedule the meeting “within the next few weeks” and said the amendment may be reviewed without resetting the full 180-day clock, though the FDA retains discretion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for: SIR filed or not; whether FDA's ask is analytical (re-cuts of NAUTILUS 18-month data, literature context) or requires new clinical data”; “‘additional analyses, no new trial’ is the bull case; any hint of a confirmatory study is the bear case.”

surprises.description: The reported 24-month IGE results showed a 100% median reduction in generalized tonic-clonic seizures among evaluable patients, a stronger efficacy figure than the 77% median reduction at 18 months highlighted in the preview. The FDA’s questions were about clinical-benefit context, not safety, so the result did not eliminate the regulatory uncertainty.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 24-month IGE data showed a 100% median reduction in generalized tonic-clonic (GTC) seizures among evaluable patients,” and “the FDA's additional questions were about clinical benefit context, not safety.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NAUTILUS ... showed 77% median GTC seizure reduction and 40% GTC seizure freedom at 18 months.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $99.5–$101.5 million from $99–$101 million, but the increase came entirely from about $1 million of higher expected service revenue rather than a better RNS outlook. The underlying RNS growth outlook remained 21%–23%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 total revenue guidance was raised to $99.5–$101.5 million (from $99–$101 million), driven entirely by higher expected service revenue of ~$1 million; underlying RNS revenue growth guidance remains 21%–23%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance ... Revenue $99–101M = 21–23% underlying RNS growth”; “FY2026 revenue guide: $99–101M held, or not.”

surprises.description: The company improved its adjusted EBITDA loss outlook to $7.5–$8.5 million from $8.5–$9.5 million, better than the preview’s expectation that the existing loss range would be maintained. This is a separate improvement from the small revenue-guidance increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA loss guidance improved to $7.5–$8.5 million (from $8.5–$9.5 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA loss $8.5–9.5M (improved from $9–10M)”; “adj. EBITDA loss guide of $8.5–9.5M maintained (not widened by AI/R&D spend).”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin guidance increased to 82%–83% from 81.5%–82.5%, putting the full-year range above the preview’s roughly 82% expectation and its emphasis on simply sustaining that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin guidance was raised to 82%–83% (from 81.5%–82.5%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~82% (our est.)”; “Gross margin held ~82%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating expenses rose only about 3% while revenue grew 17%, and the adjusted operating loss narrowed to $2.8 million from $5.0 million a year earlier. That is favorable operating leverage against the preview’s concern that commercial investment and the sales-force ramp needed to convert into throughput.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted operating expenses rose only ~3% to $21.9 million against 17% revenue growth, narrowing adjusted operating loss to $2.8 million from $5.0 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With ~$46–48M of FY S&M spend, investors need evidence of throughput conversion, not just funnel-building.”

surprises.description: The company launched ECOG Assistant, but said it is bundled with the RNS system rather than separately monetized. The launch is progress on the preview’s commercialization watch item, while the lack of separate monetization is less than the preview’s possible monetization upside; the preview did not anticipate a timeline for remote care, which management now expects to submit to the FDA by year-end 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NeuroPace launched ECOG Assistant, its first AI tool built on a proprietary dataset of over 27 million intracranial EEG recordings,” which “is bundled into the RNS system rather than monetized separately”; remote care “is expected to be submitted to the FDA by end of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ECoG Assistant commercialization. FDA-approved May 29, 2026 ... Any framing of monetization — pull-through on implants, service/recurring revenue, or standalone pricing — is upside optionality nobody is modeling.”

in_line: Underlying RNS full-year growth guidance remained 21%–23%, consistent with the preview’s stated outlook.
The results imply second-half RNS growth of roughly 20%–25%, broadly consistent with the preview’s estimate that the full-year guide required a second-half acceleration of about 21%–25%.

surprises.description: Revenue was $54 million, about 6% above the $50.82 million consensus and above the $53 million high end of guidance. The preview had warned that consensus was pinned near the guidance midpoint, so this was a clear headline beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 total revenue was $54 million” and “above the high end of prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $50.82M” consensus; company guide “$49–53M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of approximately $0.34 substantially exceeded the $0.276 consensus, by about 23%. The preview’s guidance-math cross-check had suggested roughly $0.30, so the reported result also surpassed that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS was approximately $0.34.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | $0.276”; the guidance-math cross-check estimated “~$0.30 non-GAAP EPS.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was approximately 38%, about 3 percentage points above the roughly 35% expected for the quarter. The preview anticipated a step-down from Q2’s 40.7% margin, but the actual decline was smaller than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 38%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (est.) … ~35%”; the preview said “Q3 steps down to ~35%.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $195–200 million, fraud and identity guidance to $105–109 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 32–34%. This was a stronger update than the prior ranges and met the preview’s expectation that a fourth consecutive raise was needed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY2026 guidance was raised to $195-$200 million revenue,” “fraud and identity revenue of $105-$109 million,” and “adjusted EBITDA margin of 32%-34%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY2026 guidance was “Revenue $189–198M,” “Fraud & Identity $103–108M,” and “Adj. EBITDA margin 30–33%.” The preview said “the buy side is positioned for a fourth” raise.

surprises.description: Check verification revenue was $25 million, above the preview’s estimated $22–24 million and contrary to the expected H2 sequential decline. However, management attributed the increase to renewal timing for two large renewals rather than underlying growth, and said the business should remain around $90 million annually.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Check verification revenue was $25 million, up 24% due to renewal timing of two large renewals rather than underlying growth,” and “expected to remain range-bound around $90 million annually.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview back-solved “~$22–24M in Q3” and said management had guided the business “down sequentially through H2 on renewal timing.”

surprises.description: Fraud and identity revenue reached $29 million, above the preview’s implied $26–28 million range, but grew only 14% year over year. That growth was below the preview’s roughly 20% threshold for sustaining the segment’s growth narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fraud and identity revenue was $29 million (up 14%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The FY guide implied “$26–28M in Q3”; the preview said growth “decelerating below ~20%” would break the re-rating narrative.

surprises.description: The 37% growth reported for fraud and identity SaaS was not a clean measure of underlying demand: management said a one-time EMEA age-verification regulatory surge inflated it, with normalized SaaS growth in the high teens to low 20s. This makes the headline growth less durable than it might appear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SaaS growth of 37% was inflated by a one-time EMEA age verification regulatory surge, with normalized SaaS growth in the high teens to low 20s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Committed vs. consumption mix + Check Fraud Defender ACV” as a key metric and cited Q2 SaaS growth “+19%”; it did not anticipate a one-time regulatory surge.

surprises.description: Check Fraud Defender ACV exceeded $22 million and grew 73%, well ahead of the preview’s expectation that it had crossed $19 million with 50% growth. Its data coverage also reached about 70% of U.S. checking accounts versus the preview’s 60%+ figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Check Fraud Defender ACV grew 73% year-over-year and now exceeds $22 million,” with data sets covering “approximately 70% of U.S. checking accounts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CFD ACV crossed $19M, +50% Y/Y, covering 60%+ of U.S. checking accounts.”

surprises.description: A top-five U.S. bank completed its pilot and joined the Check Fraud Defender network, a concrete customer milestone consistent with the preview’s interest in new flagship commitments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A top 5 U.S. bank completed its pilot and moved into the Check Fraud Defender network.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “new multi-year flagship commitments named” as a bull-case signal.

surprises.description: Fiserv went live as a reseller, extending Check Fraud Defender access to thousands of institutions. The preview did not flag this channel launch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiserv went live as a reseller extending access to thousands of institutions.”

surprises.description: Trailing-12-month free-cash-flow conversion was 70%, down from 99% a year earlier, due to working-capital swings, higher cash taxes, lower interest income, and increased capitalized development costs. The preview did not identify this deterioration as an issue to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow was $48.6 million (70% conversion), down from 99% a year ago” due to the listed factors.

surprises.description: Net cash was approximately $46 million, about double the $23.1 million position cited in the preview, despite the company having retired its convertible notes. That is a stronger cash position than the preview’s baseline implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with a net cash position of approximately $46 million … after retiring its convertible notes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview stated “Net cash was $23.1M after retiring the $155M converts and drawing $50M on the term loan.”

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS was $1.79, above the preview’s $1.70 anchor estimate, though below its unverified $1.89 estimate. This is a modest beat against the preview’s preferred consensus figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income rose to $54.8 million ($1.79 diluted EPS).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 EPS | $1.70”; the preview says to treat “$119M / $1.70 as the anchor” and lists $1.89 as an undated forecast.

surprises.description: European and Japanese revenue was flat sequentially, rather than showing the ex-U.S. ramp the preview highlighted. Management attributed this to a reserve provision during German pricing negotiations, with German negotiations expected to finish in Q3 and actual German net revenue reporting to resume in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “European and Japanese revenue was essentially flat quarter-over-quarter due to a reserve provision tied to ongoing German pricing negotiations”; management expects to “complete German pricing negotiations in Q3 2026 and return to reporting actual net revenue in Germany by Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview calls ex-U.S. “the growth narrative” and lists “Ex-U.S. ramp beating the modest 24% YoY revenue bar” as an upside factor.

surprises.description: The KB801 neurotrophic keratitis study is expanding into a global trial, pushing expected data into early 2027. That is later than the preview’s expectation that enrollment would be complete by year-end, and the expansion adds time before results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The KB801 study in neurotrophic keratitis is being expanded to a global trial with EU sites, pushing expected data into early 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists “KB801 (neurotrophic keratitis) 60-patient enrollment complete by year-end.”

surprises.description: The company had more than 730 U.S. reimbursement approvals, exceeding its initial target of 60% penetration of the identified patient pool. The preview noted that reimbursement-approval KPIs would be disclosed, but did not anticipate this target having already been surpassed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “More than 730 U.S. reimbursement approvals,” surpassing the “initial 60% penetration target of the ~1,200 identified patient pool.”

in_line: Global VYJUVEK revenue was $119.2 million, essentially matching the preview’s $119.05 million anchor estimate and 24% year-over-year growth expectation.
Gross margin was 95%, in line with the preview’s expectation that it would hold at or above 95%.
Full-year 2026 non-GAAP R&D and SG&A guidance was reaffirmed at $175–195 million, unchanged from the preview’s cited range.
The KB803 study remained on track for a readout later in 2026, consistent with the preview’s Q4 2026 topline expectation.

surprises.description: Taysha reported 100% of the 12 REVEAL Part A patients as responders at 12 months, well above the FDA-aligned 33% pivotal response threshold. The preview focused on trial status and the threshold but did not anticipate this strong longer-term response result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “100% of the 12 patients were responders at 12 months,” and patients achieved “310 functional gains” across domains, averaging “26 gains per patient.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FDA has already confirmed clinical and commercial material are comparable, permitting pooled data” and the preview described the “FDA-aligned 33% pivotal response threshold”; it gave no expectation for the 12-month Part A response rate.

surprises.description: The planned six-month analysis may support a BLA submission and could move filing forward by at least two quarters versus waiting for 12-month data. The preview expected six-month topline data and FDA feedback in 1H 2027, but did not anticipate this potential filing acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A planned 6-month interim analysis of all 17 REVEAL pivotal patients may serve as the basis for a BLA submission,” potentially “accelerating the filing timeline by at least two full quarters versus filing on 12-month data.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The catalyst that matters — topline 6-month interim data plus FDA feedback on the BLA path — is guided to 1H 2027.”

surprises.description: One pivotal-trial patient had a treatment-related neuropathy that led to an overnight hospitalization, an SAE under the reported classification. That was unexpected against the preview's expectation of no treatment-related SAEs, although the event was moderate and the patient recovered substantially within 24 hours of discharge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One REVEAL pivotal patient experienced a moderate Grade 2 treatment-related peripheral sensory neuropathy” about six weeks after treatment, “was hospitalized overnight (classifying it as a serious adverse event), and demonstrated substantial recovery within 24 hours of discharge.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “As of the June 2026 cutoff: no treatment-related SAEs, no DLTs across REVEAL Phase 1/2 and pivotal.” The preview said that “any new adverse event disclosure in the now-fully-dosed pivotal cohort is the biggest single-point risk on the call.”

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter at $455.4 million, substantially above the preview's roughly $415–425 million estimate, helped by $230 million in gross financing proceeds versus the preview's description of a $200 million raise. However, management described runway only into the second half of 2028 and through potential BLA approval, not through commercial launch or explicitly into 2029 as the preview's more bullish case contemplated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Taysha held $455.4 million in cash as of June 30, 2026, boosted by $230 million in gross proceeds from a June 2026 follow-on financing, providing runway into the second half of 2028 and through potential BLA approval.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base-case Q2-end cash: ~$420M.” The preview said runway “into 2029 / through launch” was the bull case and that runway “that explicitly covers BLA submission and into commercial launch (i.e., into 2029)” would remove the financing overhang.

surprises.description: Management said CMC and comparability are not currently on the critical path, easing a risk the preview highlighted as a potential BLA-gating issue. The expected Q4 2026 PPQ completion timing was not reported as changed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management stated “CMC/comparability is not currently a critical path item.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CMC is the classic gating item that delays gene therapy BLAs”; the preview also said to watch for confirmation that “comparability still holds on PPQ lots.”

surprises.description: R&D expense was slightly above the preview's forecast range, reaching $38.6 million versus an estimate of $36–38 million. The reported $0.13 loss per share was still within the preview's own -$0.125 to -$0.13 estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses rising to $38.6 million from $20.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “R&D expense … My Estimate: $36–38M.”

in_line: Dosing was completed in both REVEAL and ASPIRE, as the preview said confirmation of ASPIRE dosing completion was required and described REVEAL dosing as already completed.
Top-line REVEAL six-month interim data and FDA feedback on the BLA pathway remain expected in 1H 2027, as the preview flagged.
The reported $0.13-per-share loss was within the preview's own -$0.125 to -$0.13 estimate; the preview also anticipated an EPS miss versus consensus and characterized it as likely immaterial.
The Catalent commercial-manufacturing partnership and expected Q4 2026 PPQ completion were consistent with the preview's discussion of Catalent and the planned PPQ schedule.

surprises.description: TAP’s Q2 underlying EPS was about $1.58, above the preview’s $1.51–$1.52 consensus estimate. The year-over-year decline was also smaller than the 25.9% decline implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Underlying EPS decreased 22.9% year-over-year in Q2 FY2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Underlying diluted EPS consensus: $1.51–$1.52, down 25.9% year-over-year.

surprises.description: The company now expects full-year Midwest Premium inflation to exceed $130 million, above the initial guidance floor of at least $125 million. The preview expected Q2 to be the peak inflation quarter, but did not flag this higher full-year cost outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Elevated Midwest premium added approximately $40 million of year-over-year cost to Q2 COGS, and full-year Midwest premium inflation is now expected to exceed $130 million versus the initial guidance of at least $125 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Full-year Midwest Premium inflation is now expected to exceed $130 million versus the initial guidance of at least $125 million.

surprises.description: Net debt to underlying EBITDA was already 2.53x at quarter-end, very close to the under-2.5x goal the preview said was targeted for year-end. That brings the company near its goal earlier than the preview’s stated timeline implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net debt to underlying EBITDA improved to 2.53x at quarter-end, approaching the company's stated year-end goal of under 2.5x following debt refinancing.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net debt/EBITDA guided below 2.5x by year-end.

surprises.description: Monaco Cocktails is tracking slightly ahead of its top- and bottom-line expectations, a favorable integration update. The preview identified the acquisition as a possible source of upside but did not expect this specific outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Monaco cocktails acquisition is tracking slightly ahead of top and bottom line expectations, with the brand expected to contribute 1% to 2% to NSR alongside Pivitre.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call says Monaco is tracking “slightly ahead of top and bottom line expectations.”

in_line: Consolidated net sales declined 3.6% in constant currency, close to the preview’s expected 3.4% decline and $3.09 billion consensus.
Underlying pretax income fell 27.8%, within the preview’s implied range of approximately 25% to 31% down.
U.S. domestic shipments declined 7.3%, within the company’s expected 6% to 9% reduction range.
Management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance, as the preview expected; the preview described a reaffirm as a modest positive and the base case.
The U.S. beer industry was down 4.2% in Q2, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of a mid-single-digit decline.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $133.5 million, above the preview’s $128 million base estimate and $122.07 million consensus. The preview expected a revenue beat partly from Flyover’s full-quarter contribution, but the reported growth was driven primarily by Tabacón and growth across existing geographies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 14% year-over-year to a record $133.5 million, driven primarily by the Tabacón acquisition and growth across existing geographies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My base” revenue: “$128M”; consensus revenue: “$122.07M.” The preview also said, “A headline revenue beat is therefore likely — and low quality,” due to Flyover being owned for all of Q2.

surprises.description: EBITDA margin fell roughly 90 basis points year-over-year, rather than holding or expanding from the prior-year level as the preview’s margin thesis anticipated. Poor weather hurt high-margin attractions while lower-margin lodging outperformed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA margin declined roughly 90 basis points year-over-year, as poor weather disproportionately hurt the high-margin attractions business while lower-margin lodging outperformed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2025 margin was 25.4% … Mix shift toward higher-margin attractions plus Tabacón should hold or expand this”; the preview flagged “Adjusted EBITDA margin ≥25.4%” as a key catalyst.

surprises.description: Pursuit reported a $4.6 million pretax insurance gain from Jasper business interruption, an unanticipated one-off benefit to reported pretax income that was excluded from adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pursuit reported a $4.6 million pretax gain from Jasper wildfire business interruption insurance (excluded from adjusted EBITDA), bringing total insurance proceeds since 2024 to approximately $29 million.”

in_line: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance rose to $128–138 million, matching the preview’s expected range and its warning that a raise reflecting Flyover and Eagle Wing timing, without a core lift, would be “a guidance non-event dressed as a raise.”

First-half attraction effective ticket price growth of 6% and Q2 same-store constant-currency RevPAR growth of 10% were broadly consistent with the preview’s expected mid-single-digit yield and high-single-digit RevPAR performance.
Adjusted EBITDA of $32.7 million was within the preview’s implied consensus range of approximately $32–34 million.
The roughly 1x pro forma net leverage and remaining buyback authorization were broadly in line with the preview’s expectations of leverage below 1x and about $60 million left to repurchase.

surprises.description: Westwood ended the quarter with $17.9 billion in total assets under management and advisement, well below the preview’s $19.8 billion model; AUM itself was $17.0 billion versus an $18.9 billion estimate. Market appreciation was $1.2 billion, below the preview’s modeled $1.6 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 ended at $17 billion AUM and $17.9 billion in total assets under management and advisement, with $1.2 billion in market appreciation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The estimate table modeled firmwide AUM/AUA of $19.8B and AUM of $18.9B; the blended appreciation model estimated a $1.60B increase.

surprises.description: Net outflows were dramatically worse than the preview’s expectation of roughly flat to $50 million of inflows. Institutional outflows were especially heavy, though the small-cap value outflow was tied to one client consolidation and a larger SMIDCAP allocation had been funded in July.
surprises.fact_evidence: The firm had $1.6 billion of net outflows, including $1.3 billion of institutional outflows concentrated in legacy large cap value; small cap value outflows were primarily tied to a single client, with a significantly larger SMIDCAP allocation funded in July.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview assumed net flows of roughly flat to +$50M and highlighted institutional flows as a key metric, noting Q1 net flows of –$50M.

surprises.description: Revenue fell short of the preview’s $26.5 million model, coming in at $25.3 million despite year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 total revenues were $25.3 million, up from $25 million in Q1 and $23.1 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Q2 total revenue of $26.5M.

surprises.description: Both reported earnings measures were below the preview model: GAAP diluted EPS was $0.17 versus $0.22 expected, and economic EPS was $0.33 versus $0.43 expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: GAAP net income was $1.5 million, or $0.17 per share, while non-GAAP economic earnings were $3 million, or $0.33 per share.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled GAAP diluted EPS of $0.22 and Economic EPS of $0.43.

surprises.description: Westwood reported nearly $147 million of new private-capital co-investment commitments during the quarter, taking total platform commitments above $500 million—an additional private-capital milestone not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Private capital closed nearly $147 million in new co-investment commitments during the quarter, bringing the platform to over $500 million in total commitments.

surprises.description: The call disclosed private-capital fee terms that the preview said had not been disclosed: annual management fees of 1% to 1.5% and potential carry of 10% to 15% above an 8% preferred return. The carry is not currently reflected in financial results.
surprises.fact_evidence: Private capital funds carry annual management fees of 1% to 1.5% plus potential carry of 10-15% over an 8% preferred return, though no carry is currently reflected in the financials.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Fund III fee economics had not been disclosed.

surprises.description: Management said managed investment solutions, ETFs, and private capital—three business lines that did not exist three years ago—have each reached roughly $500 million in assets, with a goal of exceeding $1 billion each. The preview discussed these businesses but did not identify this shared scale milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: Three business lines that did not exist three years ago—managed investment solutions, ETFs, and private capital—have each reached roughly $500 million in assets, with a stated goal to surpass $1 billion each.

surprises.description: Westwood announced a new PWRX ETF launch planned as the first listing on the Texas Stock Exchange in mid-September, a product and venue announcement not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company plans to launch the PWRX ETF as the first listing on the Texas Stock Exchange in mid-September.

in_line: The quarterly dividend remained $0.15 per share, as the preview expected.
The ETF platform continued its reported growth trajectory, surpassing $400 million in assets in July after the preview cited $388 million at June 29.

surprises.description: Revenue was about $285 million, roughly 8% below the $308.7 million consensus in the preview; the year-over-year decline was 17%, versus the preview’s implied decline of about 10%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 17% year-over-year to approximately $285 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $308.7M” and “Implied Y/Y | −10%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was about $7 million, below the $14 million low end of the company’s guide. The preview identified a below-guide result as the key downside risk; the call attributed the shortfall to expense timing, shekel FX headwinds, and elevated bad debts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $7 million, coming in below the company's guidance range due to expense timing, FX headwinds from the Israeli shekel, and elevated bad debts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | $14M – $22M”; “Coming in below $14M is the single most damaging outcome.”

surprises.description: Management suspended all guidance, including the full-year 2026 EBITDA target of about $100 million, rather than reaffirming or providing the H2 bridge the preview highlighted. The company cited volatility in direct response and SME.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company suspended all guidance, including its previously provided full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance, citing volatility in the direct response and SME business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 ~$100M: reaffirmed, softened, or withdrawn”; “This is what the buy-side needs to hear addressed with numbers, not adjectives.”

surprises.description: XTAC gross profit fell 14% year over year, a weaker trajectory than the preview’s roughly −8% to −12% thresholds for assessing whether the decline was narrowing. The reported $123 million was nevertheless within the company’s $121–$131 million guide range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “XTAC gross profit fell 14% to $123 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything better than roughly −8% supports the headwind-rolloff story; −12% or worse breaks it.”

surprises.description: CTV revenue grew 67% year over year to about $40 million, substantially above the preview’s stated growth hurdle of roughly 35%–40%. It also reached 13% of revenue, up from 7% a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CTV revenue grew 67% year-over-year to approximately $40 million, rising to 13% of Q2 revenue from 7% in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “This is the growth narrative — a deceleration below ~35% removes the last clean bull talking point”; “CTV growth rate + TiVo Ads contribution — the sole clean growth vector; needs to hold >~40%.”

surprises.description: Direct response and SME XTAC gross profit fell 30%, and management cited AI search summaries reducing publisher page views by 15%–25%. The preview had flagged DR stabilization as a key question and discussed quality-related cleanup headwinds, but did not anticipate this specific AI-driven page-view pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The direct response and SME business posted $34 million in XTAC gross profit, a 30% year-over-year decline amid AI search summaries reducing publisher page views by 15-25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for evidence it has stabilized rather than kept shrinking”; the preview also described “roughly $20M of Y/Y ex-TAC headwind from 2025 quality-related cleanups in the direct-response business.”

surprises.description: Cash and marketable securities ended the quarter at $91 million, below the preview’s expectation that cash rebuild toward $110 million or more; the company also reported only $3 million of free cash flow. Access to a $40 million revolver provides additional liquidity, but does not change the cash shortfall versus that benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $91 million in cash and marketable securities plus access to a $40 million revolving credit facility, generating $3 million of free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 should be a seasonal cash-build quarter”; “A Q2 cash balance that fails to rebuild toward $110M+ implies a genuinely tight Q3 after the August coupon.”

surprises.description: Enterprise advertiser spend was flat year over year for Q2, but management reported that both May and June had positive year-over-year growth and called the period the low point of the downturn. It also guided to mid-single-digit H2 XTAC growth, offering a positive turning-point signal despite the flat quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The enterprise business delivered $89 million in XTAC gross profit with advertiser spend flat year-over-year, and management guided to mid-single-digit XTAC growth in H2”; “Both May and June showed positive year-over-year growth in enterprise advertiser spend, which management characterized as marking the low point of the downturn.”

surprises.description: Management said it is deliberately accepting lower near-term EBITDA to keep investing in the higher-margin enterprise business, while operating the legacy Outbrain-related DR/SME business for profitability. The preview focused on the need for substantial H2 EBITDA growth and noted a planned compensation-run-rate reduction, but did not flag this explicit investment-versus-near-term-earnings tradeoff.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is deliberately trading off near-term EBITDA to continue investing in the higher-margin enterprise business, while running the legacy Outbrain-related DR/SME business for profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 target | ~$100M”; “>20% Y/Y reduction in compensation run-rate.”

in_line: XTAC gross profit of $123 million was within the company’s previewed Q2 guide range of $121 million to $131 million, even though its year-over-year decline was worse than the preview’s trajectory thresholds.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q3 adjusted EBITDA of about $1.9 million, above the $1.79 million prior-year result. Instead, the call reported EBITDA down $1.4 million year over year, with lower sales and gross margin not matched by lower payroll costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 EBITDA declined $1.4 million year-over-year,” driven by “a roughly 6.5% decrease in sales and gross margin without a corresponding reduction in payroll costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” estimate: “~$1.9M”; the preview also said adjusted EBITDA had been “up Y/Y in both FY26 quarters” and identified Q3 above the $1.79M prior-year mark as the margin test.

surprises.description: Cash was below the preview’s $10–11 million estimate, coming in at $9.4 million. Debt was $7.1 million, close to the preview’s $7.5 million estimate, but had risen $4.5 million from the prior quarter after a $5 million drawdown to fund the America construction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash stood at $9.4 million while debt rose to $7.1 million, up $4.5 million from the prior quarter after a $5 million drawdown in April to finance the America restaurant construction in Las Vegas.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash” at “~$10–11M” and “Funded debt” at “~$7.5M.”

surprises.description: The America restaurant was not fully reopened on the preview’s expected early-July schedule; it remained partially closed, with full reopening now expected sometime in September. That pushes the anticipated relaunch later than the preview’s timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The America restaurant in Las Vegas is partially closed and expected to fully reopen sometime in September.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the redesign was “targeting an early-July full reopening with a September consumer unveil.”

surprises.description: Ark finalized a Sequoia lease restructure that is expected to save $200,000 to $300,000 annually, a specific recurring benefit not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A newly finalized 2-year lease restructure at Sequoia, signed in early July, is expected to generate annual savings of $200,000 to $300,000.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a new construction deal at New York-New York with MGM, expected to start in 2–3 months and open early next year. The preview highlighted the America relaunch as Ark’s only organic growth catalyst and did not anticipate this project.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new construction deal at New York-New York with MGM is set to begin in 2-3 months and open in early next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the America relaunch as “the only organic growth catalyst on the board.”

surprises.description: Total company sales fell about 6%, less than the preview’s estimated 8% year-over-year revenue decline. The reported figure is sales rather than the preview’s revenue estimate, so the comparison is directional rather than exact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total company sales fell approximately 6% for the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Total revenue” at “~$40.2M (−8.0% Y/Y).”

in_line: Las Vegas and Florida remained weak: sales were down about 11% and 10%, respectively, broadly matching the preview’s cited regional declines of 11% and 10%.

The Bryant Park ruling and trial outlook were broadly anticipated: the preview said Ark won on breach of the Grill lease with damages to be set at trial, and expected a trial in late 2026 or early 2027; the call described potential damages and a trial early next year.

The Meadowlands referendum delay was anticipated: the preview said the missed ballot deadline pushed the earliest potential vote to November 2027, and the call said the referendum was excluded from this year’s ballot, with a possible vote next year.
New York-New York’s improved cash flow despite sales being down 10–11% was consistent with the preview’s focus on operating efficiencies and improved cash flow per dollar of revenue.

surprises.description: PubMatic’s Q2 revenue returned to double-digit growth at 11% year over year, well ahead of the preview’s $68–70 million company guide and $68.99 million consensus, both of which implied a decline from the prior-year quarter. The return to double-digit growth also happened earlier than the preview’s expected second-half inflection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 11% year-over-year, marking a return to double-digit growth ahead of schedule.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $68.99M | Company Guide … $68–70M … Implied YoY –3.0%”; “last full quarter of DSP drag.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was far above the preview’s roughly $9 million guide midpoint, and the 25% margin was much stronger than the preview’s expected 12–14% Q2 margin. This substantially exceeded the preview’s description of Q2 as a margin trough.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 38% year-over-year to $19.6 million (25% margin, up from 20% a year ago).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$9M (guide midpoint)”; “Guide is $8–10M (12–14% margin)”; “Q2 at 12–14% is the trough.”

surprises.description: Emerging revenue nearly doubled, exceeding the preview’s expectation that growth would hold above roughly 60–70% (and its bull-case threshold of 85%). However, its approximately 15% revenue mix was below the preview’s hoped-for 16–18%, making the result mixed against both expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Emerging revenues nearly doubled to an all-time high of ~15% of total revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “does the growth rate hold above ~60–70% … and does mix push toward ~16–18%”; bull case: “emerging rev >85% YoY and >15% of mix.”

surprises.description: PubMatic raised its full-year CapEx outlook to $20–25 million, above the preview’s expectation that spending would track at $16–19 million. Management tied the higher spend to AI workloads and the NVIDIA partnership and said it expects payback in approximately 12 months or less.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx outlook was raised to $20-25 million to support AI workloads and the NVIDIA partnership, with these investments expected to generate incremental revenue at a payback of approximately 12 months or less.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “capex tracking to the $16–19M FY guide.”

surprises.description: Agentic campaign activity accelerated to more than 80 campaigns from 30 in the prior quarter, with campaigns across all five global agency holding companies. That is stronger adoption than the preview’s cited activity level, although the preview had warned that campaign counts were not concrete revenue evidence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AgenticOS delivered over 80 agentic campaigns (up from 30 the prior quarter) across all five global agency holding companies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “PubMatic’s ‘1,000+ AI-powered deals’ and ‘30 autonomous campaigns’ are activity metrics, not revenue.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a deliberate reduction in gross impressions even as monetized impressions increased, and said the change should lift monetization rates in future quarters. The preview had identified take-rate and on-platform ad-spend commentary as secondary items to watch but did not anticipate this specific operating strategy.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced gross impressions sequentially by 2% while increasing monetized impressions by 4%, signaling an intentional strategy expected to lift monetization rates in future quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Secondary: … take-rate/ad-spend-on-platform commentary.”

surprises.description: PubMatic announced that CFO Steve Pantelick will retire, a leadership change the preview did not flag. His continued service as CFO into Q1 2027 and advisory role through July 1 provide a transition period, while Megan Ramm is set to join as Global Chief Revenue Officer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Steve Pantelick announced his retirement, remaining CFO into Q1 2027 and then advisory through July 1, with a new Global Chief Revenue Officer, Megan Ramm, joining August 10.”

surprises.description: The reported cash balance of $137.5 million with no debt was above the preview’s estimate of approximately $102 million in net cash. The preview did not specify an expected quarter-end cash balance, so the comparison is indicative rather than a precise forecast miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ended with $137.5 million in cash and zero debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net cash: ~$102M.”

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $75–77 million, or 12% growth at the midpoint, was around the preview’s approximately $75 million threshold for sustaining the second-half growth story and within its $74–76 million base case.

Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $17–19 million implies a margin in the low-to-mid-20% range, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of a recovery toward mid-20s margins in the second half; the forecast for Q4 margin to be similar to last year’s Q4 also supports that path.

CTV remained a relative growth concern rather than a newly resolved debate: global CTV grew 13%, while the preview had already highlighted the gap to Magnite’s 36% benchmark. The Americas’ 25% growth was stronger, but the preview had specifically identified CTV growth and the peer gap as key questions.

The company repurchased 2.1 million shares for $21.5 million, an aggressive quarter consistent with the preview’s note that more than 2% of shares would constitute an aggressive pace. The reported $63.6 million remaining authorization is also consistent with the preview’s cited $85 million remaining before the quarter’s repurchases.

surprises.description: Arrow's Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $5.45, above the preview's $5.00–$5.25 working whisper and well above the $4.45 consensus. The earnings beat was larger than the preview's already-elevated expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS surged 124% year-over-year to $5.45, above the guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My working whisper is ~$9.9–10.1B revenue and ~$5.00–5.25 non-GAAP EPS.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance fell short of the preview's $10 billion-plus revenue and $5.00-plus EPS bar: revenue guidance has a $9.9 billion midpoint, while EPS guidance has a $4.93 midpoint and implies a sequential decline from Q2. ECS is guided to only 2% year-over-year growth, although management attributed that to lapping a large partner addition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $9.6-$10.2 billion” and “non-GAAP EPS of $4.83-$5.03, implying a sequential earnings decline from Q2's $5.45.” ECS Q3 guidance is “$2.1-$2.3 billion (up only 2% YoY)” and “reflects lapping a large partner addition from last year rather than a change in business trajectory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Arrow needs to guide Q3 to at least ~$10B revenue and ~$5.00+ non-GAAP EPS to keep pace with that read-across.”

surprises.description: Memory's share of Global Components revenue was described as low double digits, above the preview's mid-single-digit estimate. Price inflation also contributed roughly one-third of sequential Components growth, so the upside was volume-led but had more memory and pricing exposure than the preview's baseline suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Memory now represents a low double-digit percentage of Global Components segment revenue”; price inflation contributed “roughly one-third of sequential Global Components growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Memory only a mid-single-digit percentage of revenue.”

surprises.description: ECS disclosed a $27 million charge tied to underperforming multiyear contracts with a strategic partner, reducing ECS operating margin by 100 basis points year over year; management expects additional, smaller charges in the second half. The preview did not flag these contract costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ECS took a $27 million charge on underperforming multiyear contracts with a strategic partner, cutting ECS operating margins by 100 basis points year-over-year, with additional but smaller charges expected in the second half.”

surprises.description: The reported supplier relationship departure was less damaging than the reported figure implied: management said it affected roughly $700 million of revenue, not $1.4 billion, and would not affect ECS revenue, margin, or profit because alternatives were available.
surprises.fact_evidence: The departure “impacted roughly $700 million in revenue (not $1.4 billion as reported) but is expected to have no impact on ECS revenue, margin, or profit due to alternative solutions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “not $1.4 billion as reported.”

surprises.description: Backlog and ordering indicators were stronger and extended further out than the preview's expectation of backlog building into Q3–Q4: ECS backlog was up more than 75% to an all-time high, book-to-bill remained above parity in all three regions, and backlog was building into the first half of 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ECS backlog grew over 75% year-over-year to an all-time high”; “book-to-bill ratios remain above parity in all three regions, and backlog is building into the first half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog building into Q3–Q4” and the preview asked whether “extending lead times are pulling double-ordering into the backlog.”

surprises.description: Global Components held a 5.4% operating margin, modestly above the preview's roughly 5.0% expected trough and its 5.3% threshold for a bullish outcome. Management also expects margins to remain around 5% in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: Global Components had “operating margins of 5.4%” and management “expects to sustain around 5% margins in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything holding ≥5.3% is a bull outcome” and the preview described “~5.0% expected trough.”

surprises.description: Cash generation and deleveraging were reassuring against the preview's concern about a possible cash burn: Arrow reported more than $1 billion in year-to-date operating cash flow and reduced gross debt to $2.2 billion, with adjusted leverage down to 1.75x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated over $1 billion in year-to-date operating cash flow, reduced gross debt by ~$650 million YoY to $2.2 billion, and improved adjusted leverage by over a full turn to 1.75x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If Arrow posts a large cash burn, the ‘earnings power’ narrative gets a real challenge.”

surprises.description: Share repurchases increased from the $25 million reported in Q1 to $43 million in Q2, a step-up in capital returns that the preview specifically watched for.
surprises.fact_evidence: Arrow was “repurchasing $43 million in shares.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether buybacks step up from the token $25M pace.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $10 billion landed within the preview's $9.9–$10.1 billion working whisper, even though it exceeded company guidance and the $9.45 billion consensus.
Global Components revenue of $7.4 billion was close to the preview's roughly $7.3 billion whisper / $7.35 billion base case.
Growth was primarily unit-volume driven, as the preview hoped, though price inflation still contributed roughly one-third of sequential Global Components growth.
Consolidated operating margin of 4% matched the preview's base-case expectation of roughly 4.0%.

surprises.description: BKTI reported Q2 revenue of $23.4 million, above the preview’s $22.6 million consensus and $22.7 million model, making the quarter’s growth stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 10.6% year-over-year to $23.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 consensus” revenue of “$22.6M”; the preview’s model estimated “$22.7M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 51.9%, beating the preview’s 51.0% estimate by nearly a percentage point, with the BKR 9000 and favorable mix supporting the expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 445 basis points to 51.9%,” driven by “favorable product mix and adoption of the higher-margin BKR 9000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s model estimated gross margin of “51.0%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.4%, below the preview’s roughly 20% estimate, indicating somewhat weaker operating profitability than modeled even as revenue and gross margin beat expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 19.4% from 20.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “~$4.6M (20%)” in adjusted EBITDA and described its base case as having “SG&A ~$7.5M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.01 edged above the preview’s $0.98 model, landing near the top of its stated base-case range despite declining year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted EPS fell to $1.01 from $1.30 in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled non-GAAP adjusted EPS of “$0.98” and gave a base-case range of “$0.92–1.02.”

surprises.description: The BKR 9500’s FCC approval is now expected in early 2027, later than the preview’s stated H2 2026 approval timing, although customer deliveries remain anticipated in H1 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: The radio “was submitted for FCC testing, with approval expected in early 2027 and customer deliveries anticipated in the first half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company was “Guided to H2'26 approval, H1'27 shipments” and flagged an FCC slip as a risk.

surprises.description: BKTI disclosed purchase orders for more than 200 BKR 9500 units before customers had seen the radio, an early demand signal the preview did not anticipate or quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new BKR 9500 in-vehicle multiband radio has drawn purchase orders exceeding 200 units sight unseen.”

surprises.description: Trailing 12-month after-tax free cash flow reached $19 million, up 49% and outpacing revenue growth, adding a stronger cash-generation result than the preview’s Q1-focused cash and FCF discussion anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month after-tax free cash flow reached $19 million, up 49% year-over-year and outpacing revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$4.1M FCF in Q1 (+44% YoY)” and listed cash, FCF, and buyback activity as a metric to watch, but gave no Q2 or trailing-12-month FCF estimate.

surprises.description: The call added a January 2027 target for general release of BKR Play, a tethering solution not mentioned in the preview, providing an additional product launch on the roadmap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The BKR Play tethering solution is targeted for general release in January 2027.”

surprises.description: BKTI described the Tango Tango agreement as extending InteropONE to more than 1,500 agencies and 35,000-plus active users and creating a recurring licensing-fee pathway; the preview had identified licensing economics as an open question, though no fee amount was reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A licensing agreement with Tango Tango extends InteropONE technology to over 1,500 public safety agencies and 35,000+ active users, creating a recurring licensing fee pathway.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said this was the “first chance for management to quantify royalty/licensing revenue” and that “any recurring-software disclosure” could matter.

in_line: GAAP diluted EPS was $0.79, in line with the preview’s $0.79 model despite being slightly above the cited $0.77 consensus estimate.

Management reiterated full-year guidance rather than raising it, as the preview’s base case expected; revenue guidance remained at least $90 million, with gross margin of 50%+, GAAP EPS of $3.15, and adjusted EPS of $3.55.
The higher 2026 tax burden was anticipated: the preview cited an approximately $0.44 full-year EPS headwind, while management estimated about $0.42 per share.
The company ended the quarter with record cash and no debt, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of roughly $29 million in cash and no debt.
BKR 9500 customer deliveries remained anticipated in H1 2027, consistent with the preview’s shipment timing, even though FCC approval shifted later.

surprises.description: Coeur’s revenue was above $1.1 billion, but below the preview’s $1.19–$1.24 billion consensus range. The record result therefore still represented a top-line miss of roughly 7–11% versus expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly revenue exceeding $1.1 billion”

surprises.description: New Afton’s ramp to 16,000 tonnes per day slipped from the expected end-of-Q2 timing to early Q4, a roughly three-month delay. That pushes out part of the operating contribution investors were looking for from the acquired assets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New Afton’s ramp to 16,000 tonnes per day was pushed roughly three months to early Q4 (from end of Q2)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “This is the first clean quarter of the ‘new’ Coeur — the first full three months consolidating New Gold’s Rainy River and New Afton mines”

surprises.description: The Rainy River acquisition-accounting inventory charge was a sizable drag on Q2 earnings and costs, with another charge still expected in Q3. The preview flagged PPA as a key cost issue, but the reported $140 million charge and its $834-per-ounce consolidated CAS impact were substantial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $140 million (~$0.10 per share) noncash charge from acquisition accounting on Rainy River stockpile inventory hit Q2 EBITDA, net income and CAS, with a remaining $38 million expected in Q3”; “inflated consolidated Q2 CAS by $834 per ounce out of $2,442 total”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “What matters: does management disclose an ex-PPA cost bridge, and does the PPA drag persist at ~$689/oz or step down?”

surprises.description: Free cash flow reached $388 million, up from the preview’s cited Q1 figure of $267 million, despite the preview’s concern that a lower-price quarter and full capex load would test cash conversion. The Canadian assets alone contributed about $175 million while still ramping.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly free cash flow reached $388 million … up 45% versus the prior quarter, with the Canadian assets contributing 45% (~$175 million) despite being in ramp-up mode”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 was $267M against capex guidance of $437–526M … FCF conversion in a lower-price quarter with a full capex load is the durability test.”

surprises.description: Cash rose to $1.1 billion from the preview’s cited $843 million, crossing $1 billion for the first time and taking total liquidity above $2 billion. This was a stronger balance-sheet outcome than the preview’s already-net-cash setup suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ending cash balance surpassed $1 billion for the first time ($1.1 billion at June 30), doubling from year-end 2025, with total liquidity over $2 billion”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash $843M, total debt $761M, net leverage (0.1x) — a net cash position”

surprises.description: Rainy River underground mining accelerated: July rates were about 3,300 tonnes per day versus 2,300 in Q2, with a target of 5,000 by year-end and underground grades roughly three times open-pit grades. That provides a more concrete and favorable ramp signal than the preview’s general expectation that Rainy River’s grade profile could support the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rainy River underground mining rates jumped over 40% from 2,300 tpd in Q2 to ~3,300 tpd in July, targeting 5,000 tpd by year-end, with underground grades roughly 3x higher than open pit grades”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “There is a real second-half story (Rochester ramp, Wharf, Rainy River grade profile, full New Gold contribution).”

surprises.description: Rochester reported record crushing and had 97% of throughput running through all three crushing stages, with the Phase 2a leach-pad expansion completed. That is a stronger operating update than the preview’s description of Rochester as a chronic underperformer, and supports the anticipated second-half production ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rochester achieved a record 6.8 million metric tons crushed (up 15% quarter-over-quarter) with 97% running through all three crushing stages, positioning it for a strong second-half silver production spike as the Phase 2a leach pad expansion completed”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Rochester. The chronic underperformer”; “The FY guide’s H2 ramp leans on Rochester.”

surprises.description: Coeur deployed $110 million on buybacks, about 45% of Q2 free cash flow, and also paid its first dividend in 30 years and reduced debt by $39 million. Buyback execution was a key open question; the amount was meaningful but below the preview’s $150 million-plus bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Coeur began actively repurchasing shares under its expanded $750 million buyback program, deploying about 45% of Q2 free cash flow via $110 million of buybacks, its first dividend in 30 years ($0.02), and $39 million of debt reduction”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “How many dollars of buyback were actually executed in Q2”; bull case: “$150M+ of buyback executed”; “The $750M buyback authorization and the new $0.02 semi-annual dividend were announced with Q1.”

surprises.description: The UK Ebstrocel filing had not reached submission as the preview’s expected early-Q3 window arrived; management now expects to submit by the end of Q3 or early Q4 2026. That pushes the filing later than the preview’s near-term expectation, even though management said the MHRA alignment had de-risked the path.
surprises.fact_evidence: “expects to submit the Ebstracell marketing authorization application to the UK MHRA… by end of Q3 or early Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “guided ‘early Q3 2026’ on the Q1 call”; the preview asked whether the MAA was “filed, or slipping?”

surprises.description: The US BLA timing is now Q1 2027, later than the preview’s expected Q4 2026 filing. The preview had already noted the EU filing’s move to 2027, so the clearly new timing gap is the US submission.
surprises.fact_evidence: “a US BLA in Q1 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 PR said… FDA BLA in Q4 2026”; the preview asked for “Reconfirmation of FDA BLA in Q4 2026.”

surprises.description: Q2 results were substantially better than the preview’s modeled loss: net loss was about $1.3 million versus an estimated $5.2–5.9 million, and R&D was a benefit rather than the expected $3.4–4.2 million expense. The swing was driven mainly by additional Australian rebates and management said rebates are not expected to recur at this level over the next 12 months, limiting how much of the improvement represents a repeatable cost reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss attributable to common stockholders fell to approximately $1.3 million”; “R&D expenses swung to a benefit of roughly $0.8 million… driven mainly by recognition of additional Australian R&D rebates that are not expected to recur at that level over the next 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net loss: $5.2–5.9M” and “R&D expense: $3.4–4.2M.”

surprises.description: Cash and runway came in better than the preview’s base expectation: June cash was $18.4 million, followed by a $4.2 million rebate, and management said resources should last into Q2 2027 rather than only through Q1 2027. The extension is tempered by management’s plan to use the ATM in small increments through 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$18.4 million in cash as of June 30, 2026,” an “additional $4.2 million Australian R&D tax rebate subsequently,” and resources expected “to fund operations into Q2 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “$16–18M” cash at June 30 and described prior runway guidance as “through Q1 2027”; it identified extension past Q1 2027 as a bull-case outcome.

surprises.description: Management supplied concrete commercial assumptions for Ebstracell that the preview did not include: annual pricing of £400,000–£500,000 per child and a target of about 100 UK patients within two years of approval. These are new company projections, rather than reported sales or an established market expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “priced Ebstracell at an expected £400,000-£500,000 per child per year” and “projects reaching roughly 100 UK patients within two years of approval.”

surprises.description: Management specified that the confirmatory open-label Phase 3 trial would take 18 months, with data around mid-2028. The preview focused on the filing and the XPro trial plan, and did not flag this Ebstracell confirmatory-trial timetable; it adds a defined, relatively distant data milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The confirmatory open-label Phase 3 trial will enroll roughly 40-45 patients… run 18 months, and produce data around mid-2028.”

surprises.description: Management introduced the potential value of a US rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, saying it could be worth $150–200 million and that proceeds would fund platform expansion. The preview did not discuss this potential source of value, which is contingent on US accelerated approval and voucher issuance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A US accelerated approval would carry a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher,” recently sold for “$150-200 million” in the secondary market, with proceeds “earmarked to fund platform expansion.”

in_line: The XPro MINDFUL white-matter/myelin biomarker result was consistent with the preview’s expectation of a statistically significant finding and larger effects in the biomarker-enriched population; the reported p-value was 0.0028, with effect sizes of 0.46 overall and 0.59 in the enriched population.
EMA submission timing in early 2027 was consistent with the preview’s note that the EU filing had already been described as a 2027 submission.

The company’s intention to use the ATM and the financing/dilution concern were already central to the preview; management’s plan to raise capital in small increments through the end of 2027 did not overturn that expectation.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $24 million, well above the preview’s roughly $21.5 million estimate and the prior-year $22.5 million level management had been expected to come in below. This was a stronger profit result than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA increased 7% to $24 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA: ‘slightly lower than prior year’ → below $22.5M”; the model estimated “~$21.5M.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $149 million exceeded both the preview’s $146 million model and its cited $143.88 million consensus. The result was stronger than the expected roughly 12%–13% growth pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 15% to $149 million,” with “Q2 organic (ex-ArrowEye) growth of 12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s model was “$146.0” million, with “+12.5%” YoY; cited consensus was “$143.88M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 32.5%, materially above the preview’s roughly 29.5% estimate. More than $3 million of tariff refunds contributed about 160 basis points, making part of the margin upside a one-time benefit rather than evidence of an equivalent recurring improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA benefited from “more than $3 million in tariff refunds that boosted gross margin ~160 basis points to 32.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled gross margin at “~29.5%” and flagged tariff refund recognition as uncertain and a “non-recurring optical boost.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year revenue growth guidance from high single digits to high single digits/low double digits. That is an upward revision beyond the previously affirmed high-single-digit outlook, though it is consistent with the preview’s upside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year revenue growth guidance to high single digits/low double digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 guidance was “high single-digit revenue growth” and described the bull case as guidance raised “to low-double-digit.”

surprises.description: First-half free cash flow was far stronger than the preview’s expectation of conversion similar to 2025, and the company raised its full-year outlook to $45–$50 million. Management cautioned that the first-half level was not repeatable because some of the improvement was timing-related.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First half free cash flow was a record $36 million versus just $1 million a year earlier”; guidance rose to “$45-$50 million,” but management cautioned “this level won't repeat” because some benefit was timing-related.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 guidance was for “FCF conversion similar to 2025.”

surprises.description: Integrated PayTech’s underlying growth remained weaker than the preview’s modeled Q2 inflection: the segment grew only 4% in Q2 and low single digits in the first half, versus an estimated roughly 10% Q2 increase. The roughly 20% full-year target therefore depends on a steep second-half acceleration, even with TRISM included.
surprises.fact_evidence: Integrated PayTech “grew only low single digits (4% in Q2) in the first half, implying steep second-half acceleration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Integrated PayTech at “~$16.5” million and “~+10%” YoY for Q2, and said it needed “a visible inflection.”

surprises.description: Prepaid weakness was described as likely to continue into late 2026, rather than being only a short-lived order-timing issue. That is weaker than the preview’s expectation of full-year growth and its view that a decline could still be explained by timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prepaid Solutions remains soft and is expected to stay choppy into late 2026 due to tough prior-year comparisons and uneven ordering.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “guided to full-year growth” and warned that a further decline could reframe the weakness from “timing” to “structural.”

surprises.description: Net leverage ended at 2.7x, better than the preview’s roughly 2.9x estimate, and the company subsequently redeemed $26.5 million of Senior Notes. This is a stronger deleveraging outcome than the preview’s expected gradual improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage fell to 2.7x from 3.6x a year earlier,” and CPI “redeemed $26.5 million of Senior Notes in mid-July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated net leverage at “~2.9x” and noted that net leverage was “just under 3.0x” in Q1.

in_line: Secure Card Solutions revenue was close to the preview’s estimate: Q2 revenue was $111 million versus an estimated roughly $110 million, with strong growth remaining the primary driver.
Integrated PayTech’s full-year growth guidance of approximately 20% was consistent with the preview, which said TRISM lifted the expected FY26 segment growth to around 20%.
