Adjusted EBITDA and net-leverage full-year guidance were held unchanged, consistent with the preview’s stated low-to-mid-single-digit EBITDA growth and 2.5x–3.0x year-end leverage outlook.
ArrowEye integration and transaction costs were still elevated in Q2 and expected to decline in the second half, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: Zoetis cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $9.12–$9.32 billion and adjusted diluted EPS to $6.15–$6.25, far below the preview’s existing ranges of $9.68–$9.96 billion and $6.85–$7.00. The preview treated a reaffirmation as the base case and a further cut as the bear case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance was cut to $9.12–$9.32 billion” and “adjusted diluted EPS of $6.15–$6.25.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance action. Reaffirm, narrow, or cut”; “Reaffirm = base case”; existing guidance was “Revenue $9.680–9.960B” and “Adj. diluted EPS $6.85–7.00.”

surprises.description: The Companion Animal portfolio fell 6%, much worse than the preview’s roughly 0.9% expected decline, while U.S. Companion Animal fell 11% versus an expected 3.5% decline. U.S. revenue overall was also weaker than the preview’s expected 2.2% decline, falling 7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. revenue declined 7%” and “U.S. Companion Animal fell 11% as the total Companion Animal portfolio declined 6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus showed “Companion Animal” at “−0.9%,” “U.S. Companion Animal” at “−3.5%,” and “U.S. total” at “−2.2%.”

surprises.description: Dermatology suffered a sharp decline, with global revenue down 16% and U.S. revenue down 18%; U.S. in-clinic share fell about 5 points sequentially and 10 points year over year. The preview identified the new competitor as a major risk, but the reported revenue and share losses show the pressure was pronounced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Key Dermatology revenue dropped 16% globally to $395 million (U.S. Dermatology down 18% to $251 million)” amid “intensified competition from a new U.S. entrant in Q2”; U.S. in-clinic share fell “5 points sequentially and 10 points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Apoquel/Cytopoint faced “Merck’s Numelvi oral JAK, launched Feb 2026,” and described the franchise as “the largest unquantified risk in the model.”

surprises.description: Zoetis’s full-year price outlook deteriorated from the preview’s 1–2% realization target to a range of 0% to -2%. The company attributed the change to Dermatology gross-to-net investments and price cuts on Cerenia and Convenia amid generic competition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year price realization is now expected between 0% and -2%, driven by gross-to-net investments in Dermatology and price cuts on Cerenia and Convenia amid generic competition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “FY price guidance was cut from 2–3% to 1–2%” and flagged whether pricing would hold around the “revised 1–2% target.”

surprises.description: Livestock growth was stronger than expected in Q2: global revenue grew 11% versus the preview’s 6.4% estimate, and U.S. Livestock grew 23% versus 6.2% expected. However, management said the pace would moderate in the second half as some current gains were temporary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Livestock grew 11% globally to $731 million, with U.S. Livestock up 23% to $222 million,” but management expects “second-half growth to moderate to mid-single digits as screwworm-driven and supply-timing gains are transitory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus expected “Livestock” growth of “+6.4%” and “U.S. Livestock” growth of “+6.2%”; the preview said livestock would “carry the quarter.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.87, a small beat against the preview’s $1.84–$1.86 estimate range, even though adjusted net income fell 2% and missed company expectations. Repurchases of more than $550 million—above the historical quarterly average—helped support EPS growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income down 2% to $781 million, falling short of company expectations”; the company repurchased “over $550 million of shares in the quarter—above its historical quarterly average—helping lift adjusted diluted EPS 4% year-over-year to $1.87.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave a published EPS band of “$1.84–$1.86” and noted that buybacks had “added ~3 points to Q1 adjusted EPS growth.”

surprises.description: The CFO is departing, and the incoming CFO will also take on COO responsibilities in a newly created role. The preview did not flag an executive transition or this change in the role’s scope.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Wetteny Joseph is departing after five years, with Jay Saccaro … joining August 17 in a newly created EVP CFO and COO role overseeing finance, manufacturing, and supply.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was approximately $2.5 billion and essentially matched the preview’s $2.49 billion estimate, but the reported result was flat year over year rather than the roughly 1.3% growth implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $2.5 billion, flat on a reported basis but down 1% organically.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 revenue at “$2.49B” versus approximately “$2.458B” a year earlier, or “+1.3%.”

in_line: Q2 revenue dollars were approximately in line with the preview’s $2.49 billion consensus estimate.
International revenue grew 6%, close to the preview’s 6.8% estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $214 million, above the roughly $211–212 million implied by consensus and management’s prior “about 14%” growth outlook. The resulting 15% year-over-year growth was a modest beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $214 million, up 15% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 revenue” consensus was “$211.24M”; management said “Overall growth in Q2 should be similar to Q1 at about 14%” (approximately $212M).

surprises.description: ATEC raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to approximately $140 million from $134 million, rather than simply delivering on the previously maintained $134 million target. The increase also lifts the stated margin target from 15% to 16%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $140 million (16% margin) from $134 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was “~$134M / 15% margin” and noted management had “held $134M adj. EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Revenue per case weakened more than the preview’s outlook suggested: it fell 2.7% year over year, and management cut full-year revenue-per-case guidance from flattish to a low-single-digit decline. Biologics weakness accounted for about three-quarters of the Q2 shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue per case declined approximately 2.7% year-over-year”; “Full-year revenue-per-case guidance was cut from flattish to a low-single-digit decline,” with “about three-quarters of the Q2 shortfall attributed to biologics.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call described the prior outlook as “flattish” before saying it was cut to a low-single-digit decline.

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 72.5%, up 260 basis points year over year, with the call attributing the improvement to inventory efficiency, cost reductions, and product mix. The preview noted Q1 gross margin of 71.6% but did not flag this degree of further improvement as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 72.5%, up 260 basis points year-over-year, driven by inventory efficiency, cost reductions, and product mix.”

surprises.description: ATEC reported that implant revenue at established EOS Insight accounts rose about 32% within six months of going live, a positive account-level adoption signal not anticipated in the preview. Overall EOS revenue, however, was essentially flat year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Established EOS Insight accounts showed implant revenue rising approximately 32% within six months of going live.”

in_line: Surgical revenue was $196 million, up 17%, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of about $197 million and 17% growth.
EOS revenue was $17 million, essentially flat year over year, in line with the preview’s near-flat EOS outlook and its view that a result around $16–18 million was the base case.

Surgeon adoption grew approximately 24% and procedural volume grew 20%, broadly consistent with the preview’s emphasis on durable surgical growth and its cited Q1 figures of 23% surgeon-user growth and 21% case growth.
Full-year revenue guidance remained approximately $882 million, in line with the preview’s stated guidance and consensus near $882 million.
Q2 free cash flow was about $1 million, consistent with management’s prior commitment to approximately zero; the full-year target of at least $20 million was maintained.
The refinancing and expected annual interest savings were already described in the preview: it noted the May 1 facility and savings of more than $6 million annually.

surprises.description: Net product revenue of $15.4M slightly exceeded the $15.22M consensus and the preview’s ~$15.0M implied estimate, but came in about $0.6M below the preview’s assumed ~$16M buy-side bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net product revenue grew 45% quarter-over-quarter to $15.4 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue vs. $15.22M” consensus; “Assume the buy-side bar is ~$16M.”

surprises.description: Although Q2 gross-to-net was 29.6%, better than the preview’s cited Q1 level of about 32%, management said GTNs would rise to the low-to-mid 30% range and could reach the mid-to-high 30s if a new PBM contract is signed. That outlook is less favorable than the preview’s expectation that gross-to-net would hold or show only modest erosion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross-to-net was 29.6% in Q2, but management guided GTNs will rise to the low-to-mid 30% range, potentially mid-to-high 30s if a new PBM contract is signed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bull case requires both seasonality and price stability”; base case: “modest price erosion.”

surprises.description: SG&A rose 31% to $27.7M rather than flattening as the preview’s operating-leverage bull case anticipated. Management attributed much of the increase to a $5.3M one-time, non-recurring sales milestone, which limits how much of the increase appears ongoing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A rose 31% to $27.7 million largely due to a $5.3 million one-time non-recurring sales milestone.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bull case requires SG&A to flatten”; “Flat-to-down SG&A on +40% revenue is the operating-leverage proof point.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA improved to negative $5.7M, better than the preview’s base-case range of negative $6M to negative $7M, while still delivering the expected first sequential improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved to negative $5.7 million in Q2 (from negative $8.0 million in Q1).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “Adj. EBITDA –$6.0M to –$7.0M”; the preview also called the “first sequential adjusted-EBITDA improvement” the signal management had promised.

surprises.description: The preview emphasized roughly 84% gross margin, but the call disclosed a $0.9M write-off of out-of-spec API inventory and said stepped-up inventory would keep unit costs above the expected normalized level for another 12–15 months. The eventual normalized cost is expected to be about $1,000 per unit, so the call also supplied a longer-term cost target that the preview had not specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “COGS included a $0.9 million write-off of out-of-spec API inventory,” and normalized per-unit cost is expected to reach “~$1,000” once stepped-up inventory is consumed over “the next 12-15 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “the ~84% gross margin” as the basis for operating leverage.

surprises.description: The company disclosed a restatement of Q1 2026 financials related to fair-value accounting for convertible debt under a subordination agreement, which the preview did not anticipate. Management said it does not change cash, revenue, expenses, operating loss, or adjusted EBITDA, so the surprise is in the accounting restatement rather than the operating results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company disclosed a restatement of Q1 2026 financials tied to fair value accounting of convertible debt under a subordination agreement,” but it “does not affect cash, revenue, expenses, operating loss, or adjusted EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Zepi’s Q1 2027 launch timing matched the preview’s early-2027 expectation, but Zegalyze was slated for Q3 2027 rather than the preview’s mid-2027 timing, pushing the second launch later.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Zepi (impetigo) in Q1 2027 and Zegalyze (head lice) in Q3 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “XEPI early 2027 / XEGLYZE mid-2027 timing.”

in_line: Q2 units were 11,925, within the preview’s 11,000–12,500 expectation; the reported 48% quarter-over-quarter increase was also close to the preview’s roughly 40% base-case growth.

Cash was $24.2M, within the preview’s $22–26M estimate. Access to an additional $10M under the Horizon term loan was consistent with the preview’s focus on confirmation of milestone achievement or tranche availability.

surprises.description: The Phase 2 AD trial’s top-line readout is now expected in Q3 2027, later than the preview’s secondary-reported mid-2027 timing. Management also expects enrollment to finish in early 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “enrollment completion expected early 2027 and top-line data in Q3 2027”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Secondary reporting points to topline in mid-2027”; the preview also said to listen for whether management “repeats or refines a data date.”

surprises.description: The planned HS study is a Phase 1b trial, not the Phase 2 initiation the preview expected to be reaffirmed for later in 2026. The stated plan is a small, up-to-25-patient, uncontrolled study.
surprises.fact_evidence: “plans to initiate a Phase 1b HS trial (up to 25 patients, no placebo, 200mg BID for 12 weeks)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “HS and asthma Phase 2 initiations — guided ‘later this year’”; the preview’s checklist asks whether “HS + asthma Phase 2 starts [are] reaffirmed for 2H26.”

surprises.description: The PTCL interim futility analysis is now projected for Q1 2027, and the interim will not disclose safety or efficacy results. The preview focused on Phase 3 enrollment progress and did not flag either this timing or the limited interim disclosure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Phase 3 PTCL trial's interim futility analysis is now projected for Q1 2027 (versus prior expectations)”; “no safety/efficacy data to be publicly disclosed at the interim.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An enrollment-complete or enrollment-ahead-of-plan comment would be a genuine upside surprise”; the preview does not state an interim-analysis date.

surprises.description: Corvus reported $215.2 million in cash and marketable securities, below the preview’s $219–224 million estimate. The runway remains into Q2 2028, as expected, so the cash-balance shortfall did not come with a shorter stated runway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ended Q2 2026 with $215.2 million in cash and marketable securities”; the balance includes “$189.4 million in net proceeds from a Q1 follow-on offering” and funds operations “into Q2 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash & marketable securities (6/30) … $219–224M”; “Runway … Reaffirm ‘into Q2 2028.’”

surprises.description: Corvus committed $5 million to Angel Pharmaceuticals’ financing, a cash investment not anticipated in the preview. The investment supports the existing collaboration, but also directs company cash to its partner.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Corvus invested $5 million in Angel Pharmaceuticals' $13.5 million financing and remains Angel's largest shareholder.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed Angel’s upcoming China data and noted “Nothing has been announced” on business development, but did not anticipate an investment in Angel.

surprises.description: Management described a prolonged benefit after soquelitinib dosing ends, without the rebound it contrasted with dupilumab, JAK inhibitors, and STAT6 agents. The preview covered the previously reported day-56 AD efficacy but did not anticipate this durability claim.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Soquelitinib showed prolonged treatment benefit beyond dosing without disease rebound, contrasting with rebound seen in dupilumab, JAK inhibitors, and STAT6 agents, attributed to enhanced T regulatory cell function.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Cohort 4 discussion gave day-56 response rates and described the study’s 56-day dosing, but did not mention post-dosing benefit or rebound.

surprises.description: Angel’s Chinese AD-trial data can be used in Corvus’s FDA filings, giving the partner-generated results a stated regulatory use beyond the China trial. The preview anticipated Angel data but did not mention this use.
surprises.fact_evidence: “its data is usable in Corvus's FDA filings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Angel’s China trial as “A second, independent readout on soquelitinib before the pivotal AD data,” without mentioning use in FDA filings.

surprises.description: The asthma Phase 2 is planned to include both T2 and non-T2 patients; the preview expected an asthma Phase 2 start but did not specify this broader population. Management said non-T2 patients represent about 40–50% of asthma patients.
surprises.fact_evidence: “a Phase 2 asthma trial enrolling both T2 and non-T2 patients (the latter representing ~40-50% of asthma patients) before year-end 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “HS and asthma Phase 2 initiations — guided ‘later this year’”; no asthma patient subgroups were specified.

surprises.description: R&D expense was $16 million, above the preview’s $13–15 million estimate, while the $18 million net loss was also slightly wider than its $15–17 million model. The preview explicitly framed R&D above $15 million and a wider loss as evidence of trial execution, so the expense overrun is favorable in that context.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 R&D expenses rose to $16 million”; “Net loss widened to $18 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “R&D expense … $13.0–15.0M”; “Net loss … $15–17M”; the preview says “R&D >$15M” is confirmation and that a wider-than-consensus loss “is a sign of trial execution, not deterioration.”

in_line: The company maintained the expected runway into Q2 2028 despite the cash balance coming in below the preview’s estimate.
The asthma Phase 2 remains planned before year-end 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a 2H26 start.
Angel’s first-cohort data by year-end 2026 is broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of China data “anticipated late this year.”
The previously reported Phase 1 AD Cohort 4 response rates—75% EASI-75, 25% EASI-90, and 33% IGA 0/1—match the figures already included in the preview.

Corvus reported a higher net loss than its model, but that was consistent with the preview’s stated view that a wider loss alongside elevated R&D would indicate trial execution rather than deterioration.

surprises.description: Cummins raised its FY2026 revenue-growth outlook to 10%–13% from 8%–11%, rather than merely narrowing the range toward its upper half as the preview’s base case anticipated. It also increased the midpoint of EBITDA-margin guidance to 18.25%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to 10%-13% (from 8%-11%) and increased the midpoint of EBITDA guidance to 18%-18.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base ... FY guide narrowed to the upper half rather than raised”; the preview also said the Street needed a guidance raise, not just a beat.

surprises.description: Q2 EBITDA margin was 17.5%, well below the preview’s implied 18.5%–19.1% range, and fell from 18.4% a year earlier. The preview expected a year-over-year margin increase, not a decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record EBITDA of $1.7 billion, though EBITDA margin declined to 17.5% from 18.4% a year ago due to tariffs and higher variable compensation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied EBITDA ... ~$1.73–1.78B, 18.5–19.1% margin”; the preview described this as “+30–60 bps.”

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS of $6.73 missed the $7.33 consensus estimate, despite being above the year-ago result. The $0.21-per-share unfavorable discrete tax items explain part, but not all, of the gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net earnings were $932 million, or $6.73 per diluted share, up from $6.43 a year ago, despite $29 million ($0.21 per share) in unfavorable discrete tax items.”

surprises.description: Power Systems revenue reached $2.3 billion, substantially above the preview’s $2.10 billion estimate and its expected 11.2% year-over-year growth. Its 24.5% margin, however, was essentially in line with the 24.7% estimate rather than the preview’s greater-than-27% upside-surprise threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Power Systems was the standout segment with record revenues of $2.3 billion (up 19%) and EBITDA margin expanding to 24.5% from 22.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Power Systems $2.10B” revenue, “+11.2%”; “consensus 24.7%” margin, with “any print above ~27%” described as a clean upside surprise.

surprises.description: Demand in China was much stronger than the preview specifically laid out: China revenue including joint ventures rose 30%, while power-generation equipment sales there rose 88% on accelerating data-center demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China revenues including joint ventures rose 30% year-over-year to $2.3 billion, with power generation equipment sales up 88% on accelerating data center demand.”

surprises.description: Cummins disclosed a multiyear hyperscaler agreement that provides visibility into several gigawatts of future backup-power genset demand, a concrete large-customer commitment not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cummins signed a multiyear agreement with a global hyperscaler securing visibility into several gigawatts of future backup power genset demand.”

surprises.description: New 95-liter diesel genset orders are booking into the second half of 2028, extending well beyond the preview’s expectation that orders would spill into the first half of 2027. Management also said demand is still growing rather than plateauing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diesel genset lead times have extended, with new 95-liter orders now booking into the second half of 2028, and demand continues to grow rather than plateau.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 build slots effectively sold out and orders spilling into 1H27 on EPA-2027 pre-buy.”

surprises.description: Higher incentive compensation tied to record earnings weighed on Q2 margins across segments, an added cost headwind not identified in the preview. Management expects it to ease by about $25 million per quarter in H2 and reset roughly $200 million lower going into 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Higher incentive compensation tied to record earnings weighed on Q2 margins across segments but is expected to be ~$25 million lower per quarter in H2 and reset roughly $200 million lower going into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview set an implied Q2 EBITDA margin expectation of “18.5–19.1%” and discussed tariffs and MY2027 launch costs, but did not identify higher incentive compensation as a margin headwind.

in_line: Power Systems EBITDA margin was 24.5%, close to the preview’s 24.7% consensus estimate.
The 10% dividend increase and 17th consecutive year of dividend growth had already been flagged in the preview as having occurred in July.
The limited January 2027 X10/X15 production and full X15 ramp in Q4 2027 were broadly consistent with the preview’s stated phased-transition timing.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $181 million, well above the preview’s $161–165 million base case and management’s steer of only slightly above Q1’s $160.8 million. Core organic growth was nearly 8%, making this a substantial upside to the expected quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $181 million,” with “core organic growth of nearly 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My base case” revenue was “$161–165M”; management had steered to revenue “slightly above Q1 levels” (Q1 was $160.8M).

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin fell to 20.3%, below the preview’s 21.5% guide-floor threshold and the 21.5–22.0% full-year margin outlook cited in the preview. The reported pressures included currency-driven material costs, MirrorEye transition inventory costs, and lower Smart2 tachograph sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross profit margin declined 277 basis points year-over-year to 20.3%,” pressured by “currency-driven material costs,” “inventory-related costs from the shift to factory-built MirrorEye,” and “lower Smart2 tachograph sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for adjusted gross margin to “Hold ≥21.5% (guide floor)” and listed FY adjusted gross margin guidance of “21.5–22.0%.”

surprises.description: Management said Q3 and Q4 revenue should each be modestly lower than Q2 due to seasonality, rather than following the preview’s expectation of heavier Q3/Q4 revenue after a modest Q2. The full-year revenue and EBITDA ranges were nevertheless reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Both Q3 and Q4 revenue [are] expected to be modestly lower than Q2 due to seasonality.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s revenue arithmetic described a “Modest Q2, heavier Q3/Q4” and said Q2–Q4 would average “$161–170M/qtr.”

surprises.description: SG&A showed stronger operating leverage than the preview specifically anticipated: expense rose by less than $400,000 despite a $24 million year-over-year increase in revenue, lowering SG&A to 14.3% of sales. This is an additional positive efficiency result beyond the headline revenue growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A expense fell 182 basis points to 14.3% of sales, rising less than $400,000 despite a $24 million year-over-year revenue increase.”

surprises.description: Stone Ridge Brazil’s adjusted operating margin reached 11.2%, above the preview’s expectation to sustain roughly 9% or better. The call attributed part of the result to a temporary competitive supply dislocation, so the outperformance may not be fully durable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stone Ridge Brazil delivered record sales of $20.5 million” and “adjusted operating margin of 11.2%, aided partly by a temporary competitive supply dislocation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified Brazil as the portfolio’s best-margin business at “9.5%” and said to watch whether it could “Sustain ~9%+ margin.”

surprises.description: IHS sharply raised its 2026 weighted-average OEM end-market growth forecast while cutting its 2027 forecast, citing orders moving into 2026. The preview highlighted improving near-term end-market data, but did not anticipate this pronounced year-to-year timing shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IHS raised its 2026 weighted-average OEM end-market growth forecast to 5.5% (up from 1.8% in May) while trimming 2027 growth to 5.4% (from 10%), primarily reflecting a timing shift of orders into 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said recent end-market data had “moved in Stoneridge’s favor,” citing June North American Class 8 orders “+230% YoY” and EU H1 heavy truck registrations “+11.1%”; it did not cite the IHS forecast revisions or a 2026-to-2027 timing shift.

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $5.5 million, at the top of the preview’s $4.5–5.5 million base case and at its threshold for a credible result; the FY $20–25 million EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed as expected.

MirrorEye sales of $37 million exceeded the preview’s >$35 million watch threshold and were consistent with its expectation of continued growth; the preview had also already noted the approximately $42 million bus/coach award.
Brazil sales grew nearly 26% excluding currency, broadly matching the preview’s cited 25.9% year-over-year growth benchmark.
The preview expected further debt paydown; the call reported net debt down roughly $39 million year-over-year.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance was far below the preview’s roughly $82M placeholder and $80–86M base-case range: the $68M midpoint excludes about $17M of product revenue delayed by Chinese supply-chain disruptions. The preview did not anticipate the recent Chinese scrutiny of dual-use optics components that is driving the delay.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $63-73 million (midpoint $68 million) excludes approximately $17 million of product revenue delayed due to Chinese supply chain disruptions”; China’s increased scrutiny on dual-use optics components is a recent development “over the past few weeks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 revenue guide vs. ~$82M sell-side placeholder”; the Base scenario expects “$80–86M,” and a guide “≤$78M” is the bear trigger.

surprises.description: Management expects JLWS to begin contributing in Q3 and ramp significantly in 2027, and says it should more than offset the anticipated HELSI-2 decline. That gives a firmer replacement-program outlook than the preview’s unresolved concern that consensus implied a 2H26 revenue decline and its question of whether JLWS dollars would arrive on schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “JLWS will begin contributing revenue in the current quarter, ramp significantly in 2027, and management expects it to more than offset the anticipated decline of the HELSI-2 program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says FY26 consensus implied “a ~6% sequential-half decline” and asks whether “the first guided quarter” can “embed JLWS revenue”; it also identifies JLWS timing as a key uncertainty.

surprises.description: Q3 product gross margin is guided to 34–40%, below Q2’s 41.2% and with a low end below the preview’s expected Q2 margin range. The stated reasons are reduced volumes and fixed-cost absorption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 product gross margin guided lower at 34-40% due to reduced volumes and fixed cost absorption.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gives a Q2 product gross-margin expectation of “~39%” consensus and a company range of “37–41%,” but does not provide a Q3 margin forecast.

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1–7M signals a substantial sequential step-down from Q2’s $10.7M, with management attributing it to lower expected volumes; the preview did not flag a Q3 EBITDA outlook this low.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $10.7 million in Q2… with Q3 guidance of just $1-7 million reflecting lower expected volumes.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue exceeded consensus by about $4.4M, with product revenue also slightly above the preview’s approximate estimate. The reported 34% total growth and 45% product growth were stronger than the preview’s implied year-over-year growth estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue hit a record $83 million, up 34% year-over-year, with record products revenue of $59 million growing 45% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$78.59M”; product revenue was estimated at “~$58M,” with implied growth of “+27.4%” overall and “~+35%” for products.

surprises.description: Operating cash flow was much stronger than the preview’s Q1 reference point, and the company repaid its credit-line borrowing while retaining substantial cash and investments. This contrasts with the preview’s concern that the Longmont buildout and JLWS investment could increase cash burn.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated a record $20.7 million in operating cash flow and ended Q2 with $330.8 million in total cash and investments, having repaid the $20 million drawn on its credit line.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cites “+$9.7M operating cash flow in Q1” and says capex is going up, with “Negative FCF” considered acceptable if framed as JLWS capacity.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $10.7M was close to the preview’s ~$10M consensus and within the company’s $8–12M guidance range.
Q2 product gross margin of 41.2% was within the preview’s 37–41% company guidance range and near its upper end, although below Q1’s record 43.6% as the preview anticipated a sequential step-down.

The exit from legacy cutting and welding, with no material revenue expected from those products in 2H26, is consistent with the preview’s warning that industrial strength included non-recurring last-time buys and that commercial revenue could decline.

surprises.description: Harrow retained its $350–365M FY26 revenue and $80–100M adjusted EBITDA guidance, despite saying first-half revenue was lighter than expected. That leaves roughly $250M of revenue to deliver in H2, weighted toward Q4—more demanding than the preview’s estimated $230–245M H2 requirement, even as retaining the guide is better than the preview’s base-case expectation of a trim.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reiterated full-year guidance of $350–365 million in revenue and $80–100 million in adjusted EBITDA; first-half revenue was approximately $115 million and management described an approximately $250 million second-half ramp weighted toward Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base ... FY revenue guide trimmed to low end (~$340–355M) and/or EBITDA guide cut”; the preview also said H2 “must deliver $230–245M.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was essentially at the preview’s consensus range but came in $0.3M below the company’s $71M guidance floor. Management also said the first half was lighter than expected, largely because of Vevye and AIHESO revenue timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $70.7 million”; management said first-half revenue was “lighter than expected largely due to Vevye and AIHESO revenue timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited consensus estimates of “$70.99M / $70.35M” and “$71M – $81M” company guidance, noting that a sub-$71M result would be a formal guidance miss.

surprises.description: Vevye revenue and demand indicators came in stronger than the preview’s implied quarterly bar: revenue was $29.4M versus the preview’s rough $26–27M quarterly estimate, while prescriptions continued to grow sequentially rather than showing the feared demand break after the pricing change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vevye delivered record quarterly revenue of $29.4 million”; prescriptions were up 21% sequentially, the prescriber base was up 15%, and branded dry-eye market share reached 14.6% versus 7.8% a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said more than $100M in FY Vevye revenue required roughly “$26–27M/quarter,” and warned that a sharp TRx deceleration would suggest the ASP gain came at the expense of volume.

surprises.description: AIHESO demand was much stronger than the preview’s expectation of a somewhat muted quarter: units reached a record and rose 44% sequentially. The expected 20–25% net price improvement is also now effective, while management said the product has less than 2% addressable-market penetration.
surprises.fact_evidence: AIHESO reached record quarterly unit demand of 65,477, up 44% sequentially and 34% year over year; net pricing improved about 25% effective July 1, gross margins exceeded 90%, and penetration is estimated below 2%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had pre-warned Q2 would be “somewhat muted” and described a “20–25% net price improvement in H2.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 71%, above the preview’s 66–68% estimate, and management expects it to move back toward the high 70s in H2. This is a better starting point for the recovery than the preview’s modeled quarter implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin was 71% in Q2” and is expected to trend back toward the high 70s in the second half as AIHESO’s revenue cycle normalizes and product mix improves.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 gross margin at “~66–68%E” and said anything below roughly 64% would signal pricing actions were not flowing through.

surprises.description: The Tervaia deal came with additional economics and operating costs not detailed in the preview: management expects more than $30M in 2027 revenue and exclusivity through 2034, but also roughly $20M of annualized SG&A once integrated. Integration costs may weigh on early quarters, though management said they will not reduce 2026 earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: The acquisition is for $30 million upfront funded from cash, with self-funded contingent milestones; management expects more than $30 million in 2027 revenue, accretive economics and assumed exclusivity through 2034, alongside roughly $20 million in annualized SG&A once fully integrated. Early integration costs are not expected to pull down 2026 earnings.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the announced deal had a “$30M TYRVAYA upfront,” was cash-funded, and was expected to be “accretive shortly after close.”

surprises.description: Management provided a new GMELT regulatory timeline that the preview did not discuss: a pre-NDA FDA meeting is scheduled for early Q4, with an NDA targeted for H1 2027 and potential approval and launch in 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: GMELT secured a pre-NDA FDA meeting for early Q4; NDA submission is targeted for the first half of 2027, potential approval for the first half of 2028, and commercial launch later that year.

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.2M, close to the preview’s roughly breakeven estimate and within its modeled -$2M to +$6M base-case range.
Q2-end cash of $83.9M, less the $30M cash-funded Tervaia upfront, implies roughly $54M after the payment—broadly consistent with the preview’s estimated $55–65M pro forma cash.

surprises.description: Relmada had not filed the NDV-01 IND or started RESCUE by the time of the call, despite the prior mid-2026 target. Management attributed the slip mainly to Piramal’s GMP production schedule and said manufacturing execution remained; enrollment can start after the 30-day IND review.
surprises.fact_evidence: The mid-2026 IND timeline slipped primarily due to delays getting on Piramal’s GMP production schedule; management characterized development activities as complete with only manufacturing execution remaining. Patient enrollment can begin shortly after the 30-day IND review period.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management guided at Q1 to “IND filing and Phase 3 RESCUE initiation in ‘mid-2026’”; the preview called whether the program had “actually started” the key issue.

surprises.description: The expected year-end 2026 initial three-month response-data disclosure may move to first-half 2027. Management said it preferred a more meaningful six-month readout from 15–20 patients over early three-month results.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management indicated the previously guided year-end three-month complete response data disclosure may be pushed to first-half 2027, favoring a more meaningful six-month readout with 15-20 patients over early three-month results.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “initial 3-month response data from the 2L BCG-unresponsive study by year-end 2026” and identified reaffirmation of that timing as a key metric.

surprises.description: Q2 R&D expense was well below the preview’s estimate, rather than stepping up to reflect Phase 3 startup spending. The $8.4 million result was below even the preview’s $10–16 million range and its stated expectation that a move to $12 million or more would corroborate that spend had started.
surprises.fact_evidence: R&D expense was $8.4 million in Q2 2026, driven by higher NDV-01 and sepranolone study costs plus increased manufacturing and drug storage costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 R&D at “$12.5M (range $10–16M)” and said “a move to $12M+ corroborates that spend has started.”

surprises.description: Sepranolone also missed the expected mid-2026 initiation timing: the company now plans to file its IND by year-end, with the Phase 2 study to begin only after clearance.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company plans to file an IND for sepranolone by year-end 2026, with the Phase 2 study to initiate upon IND clearance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said sepranolone Phase 2b was “also guided mid-2026” and flagged initiation status as a key metric.

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was materially smaller than expected: Relmada reported a $12.9 million net loss and a $0.11 per-share loss, versus the preview’s roughly $20.1 million loss and $0.19 estimated loss per share, as well as the cited $0.21 consensus loss per share. The lower per-share loss partly reflects a larger share count.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 net loss was $12.9 million ($0.11 per share), compared with $9.9 million ($0.30 per share) a year earlier; the lower per-share loss reflected a larger share count.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net loss … ~$20.1M” and “EPS … -$0.19,” and listed Q2 EPS consensus of “-$0.21.”

surprises.description: G&A expense came in below the preview’s estimate and range, declining year over year rather than landing near the anticipated $10 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: G&A expense declined to $6.6 million from $7.4 million year-over-year, primarily on lower stock-based and employee compensation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 G&A at “$10.0M (range $9–12M).”

in_line: Cash and short-term investments were $217.7 million, within the preview’s $208–220 million expected range, and management reaffirmed runway through 2029, including completion of the Phase 3 Rescue Program.
The RESCUE program had roughly 80 sites enrolled (60 primary and 20 backup), consistent with the preview’s expectation of approximately 80 North American sites.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case expected quarter-end cash of $1–2 million, but DRCT ended Q2 with only $0.5 million. Cash plus receivables also fell to $3.2 million from $3.9 million at year-end, leaving liquidity weaker than the preview’s base case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with just $500,000 in cash and cash equivalents,” and “Total cash plus accounts receivable was only $3.2 million as of June 30, 2026, down from $3.9 million at the end of 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case projected “cash $1–2M funded by facility draws.”

surprises.description: The preview treated a second covenant breach as a bear-case risk, while DRCT reported that it was not in compliance with certain financial covenants and had requested a lender waiver. The breach and ongoing waiver discussions are worse than the preview’s base case of no new covenant breach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct Digital was not in compliance with certain financial covenants under its credit facility and has requested a waiver from its lender, with discussions ongoing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “second consecutive breach requiring a Thirteenth Amendment” was a bear-case condition; its base case assumed “no refi news” and a going-concern reiteration.

surprises.description: DRCT reported new AI search, GEO, and web-infrastructure offerings, along with an approximately 80% retention rate for clients representing about 80% of first-half revenue. The preview looked for quantified Ignition+ traction but did not anticipate these specific product launches or this retention disclosure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched new AI search, GEO, and web infrastructure technology offerings” and reported “approximately 80% client retention among clients representing about 80% of first-half revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Ignition+ had “strong initial interest” but had “never put a number on it,” and that “any disclosed customer count or bookings figure would be new information.”

in_line: Revenue was $7.8 million, within the preview’s $7.5–8.0 million bottom-up base case, despite being below the stale $9.90 million consensus figure the preview cautioned against using.
Non-DSP revenue grew approximately 5% year-to-date, consistent with the preview’s expectation of mid-single-digit growth in the core business.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $2.3 million, within the preview’s base-case range of $1.8–2.4 million in losses.
Gross margin was 34%, in line with the preview’s expected 34–35% range.
Operating expenses were $5.6 million, down from $6.0 million a year earlier, consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued cost reductions.

surprises.description: Fortune Brands cut FY26 EPS guidance excluding tariff benefits to $2.70–$3.00 from $3.00–$3.30, about $0.30 lower at the midpoint, rather than reaffirming the prior range. Management attributed roughly $0.20 of the reduction to incremental investments and $0.10 to service-related volume loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its full-year EPS guidance excluding tariff benefits to $2.70-$3.00 (from a prior $3.00-$3.30), roughly $0.30 lower at the midpoint, with about $0.20 from incremental investments and $0.10 from service-related volume loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 EPS guidance: reaffirm $3.00–$3.30, or reset?” The preview also described reaffirmation as the buy-side expectation and a reset to around $2.75–$3.05 as the bear scenario.

surprises.description: Water, the largest segment, was weaker than the preview’s roughly 19.5%–20.5% margin base case: sales fell 6.5%, volume declined high-single digits, and operating margin excluding tariff refunds fell about 700 basis points year over year. The call attributed the volume weakness to service challenges and prior-year share losses, with service-related costs also pressuring margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water segment… sales decline 6.5% to $605 million (down 5.4% excluding China), with volume down high-single digits due to service challenges and prior-year share losses.” “Excluding tariff refunds, Water operating margin fell roughly 700 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Water operating margin… Anything with a 2-handle (>20%) validates the price/cost inflection; sub-19% breaks the H2 bridge.” The base scenario expected Water at “~19.5–20.5%.”

surprises.description: The tariff-refund benefit was much more concrete and material than the preview’s base case allowed for: Fortune Brands recognized $122 million gross, with $81 million flowing to operating income. It added 700 basis points to consolidated margin and $0.52 to quarterly EPS, helping lift reported operating margin to 20.4% versus the preview’s 13.0%–13.5% model.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recognized $122 million in gross tariff refunds during Q2, of which $81 million flowed to operating income, adding 700 basis points of margin and $0.52 of EPS in the quarter.” Reported operating margin was “20.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called refunds an “unmodeled tariff-refund wildcard” and said the base case assumed “no refund or refund deferred”; its modeled Q2 operating margin was “~13.0–13.5%.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance calls for a 12.5%–13% operating margin and EPS of $0.72–$0.76, with management citing growth investments and the absence of a prior-year $25 million variable-compensation benefit. That outlook adds near-term pressure to the preview’s expected second-half margin step-up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales down 1%-2% and EPS of $0.72-$0.76 with operating margin of 12.5%-13%, pressured sequentially by growth investments and comping a prior-year $25 million variable comp benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 EPS was “low-40% H1 / high-50% H2” and expected “~300bps margin step-up H1→H2.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales of $1.2 billion were slightly above the preview’s published consensus range of $1.16–$1.19 billion, although the 4% decline was broadly consistent with management’s earlier down-mid-single-digit guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 sales fell 4% to $1.2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales: $1.16B – $1.19B.”

surprises.description: Security sales returned to growth, rising 3.8% to $184 million, with new products contributing nearly 200 basis points to sales growth. Its reported margin rose 1,200 basis points to 26.8%, though tariff refunds accounted for 1,030 basis points of that increase, so the margin improvement was mostly refund-driven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Security sales grew 3.8% to $184 million with operating margin up 1,200 basis points to 26.8%, though tariff refunds contributed 1,030 basis points of that margin gain, and new products added nearly 200 basis points to sales growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that management had flagged “new product launches in Q2” and called Security a read on whether execution fixes were landing; Q1 sales were down 6%.

surprises.description: Net debt and leverage were lower than the preview’s Q1-based figures: net debt was about $2.3 billion and leverage 2.7x, versus the preview’s approximately $2.5 billion and 2.9x. Management still prioritized debt reduction and retained the goal of getting below 2.5x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt stood at approximately $2.3 billion with net debt-to-EBITDA of 2.7x, and management is prioritizing debt reduction to reach below 2.5x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Net debt ~$2.5B, 2.9x net debt/EBITDA (target <2.5x).”

surprises.description: Management said it is moving brand and marketing teams back into the business units, an organizational change the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reaffirmed its cost-savings program “while moving brand and marketing teams back into business units.”

in_line: Q2 sales fell 4%, consistent with management’s May guidance for a mid-single-digit decline, despite coming in slightly above the preview’s published consensus range.
The company reaffirmed the approximately $70 million annualized cost-savings program, with $15 million expected in 2026 and the full run rate targeted for Q1 2027, as outlined in the preview.
The Fiberon strategic review remained underway with advisers retained; the preview had identified the review as ongoing and discussed a process without a completed transaction as a plausible outcome.
Management continued to prioritize reducing leverage toward below 2.5x, consistent with the balance-sheet goal in the preview.

surprises.description: PARR reported adjusted EPS of $10.10, well above the preview’s $8.22 consensus estimate. The roughly 23% beat was a much stronger headline result than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income of $499 million, or $10.10 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $8.22.”

surprises.description: The preview said consensus required roughly 95–100% capture and treated capture as the central risk; PARR reported 125% system-wide capture, or 112% normalized. Hawaii’s $77 million net price-lag gain was a substantial contributor, making capture materially stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “System-wide refining capture was 125% (112% normalized), with Hawaii benefiting from a $77 million net price lag gain of $11.49 per barrel.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My bottom-up build says consensus requires PARR to convert its market index to realized margin at ~95–100%”; the preview also called capture “the whole trade.”

surprises.description: The combined refining index averaged about $33 per barrel, well below the preview’s roughly $43 full-quarter modeling assumption. That meant the market-margin backdrop in the reported quarter was weaker than the preview’s build assumed, even as PARR’s capture was much better.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The combined refining market index averaged approximately $33 per barrel.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Assume ~$43/bbl full-quarter” for the Q2 index.

surprises.description: Despite EPS coming in well above consensus, adjusted EBITDA was $571 million, below the preview’s derived estimate of about $600 million. The EBITDA shortfall was modest relative to that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $571 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (my est. of embedded number): ~$600M.”

surprises.description: PARR ended the quarter with a $312 million working-capital outflow, about half related to Hawaii pre-turnaround inventory builds, and said it expects much of the outflow to reverse. The preview focused on price lag and the Hawaii turnaround but did not anticipate or quantify this cash use.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Working capital outflows of $312 million (roughly half tied to Hawaii pre-turnaround inventory builds) are expected to substantially reverse after the turnaround and price stabilization.”

surprises.description: The preview characterized July cracks as reaching record levels, but the company said its consolidated refining index averaged $31.34 per barrel in July, about $1.60 below Q2’s average. This indicated sequential softening rather than further strengthening on the company’s index measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The July consolidated refining index averaged $31.34 per barrel, about $1.60 below the Q2 average, signaling some sequential margin softening.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “July cracks hit all-time highs” and called for an “explicit Q3 index quoted at July record levels” as a bull-case signal.

surprises.description: The company reported more than $220 million of net debt reduction, cut gross term debt by over $130 million, and ended with about $1.4 billion of liquidity. The preview disclosed a $500 million notes offering and prior balance-sheet figures but did not anticipate this quarter’s debt reduction or the resulting liquidity level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced net debt by over $220 million during the quarter, including a $500 million senior secured notes offering and cutting gross term debt by more than $130 million”; “Total liquidity ended the quarter at approximately $1.4 billion.”

in_line: The Hawaii turnaround was expected to weigh on Q3: the preview said its financial impact would land almost entirely in Q3 and flagged the turnaround as the largest guidance risk. The call’s expectation that Hawaii capture will fall below its typical 100%–110% range because of turnaround costs and imports is consistent with that concern.

The SRE/RIN issue remained prospective rather than clearly resolved. The preview emphasized uncertainty over whether PARR was included in the EPA decisions and the need for clarity; the call discussed the potential value of full exemptions and the September 1 compliance deadline.

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.23, far above the preview’s $0.07 consensus, while GAAP net income also turned positive at $9.1 million from a $20.3 million loss a year earlier. The EPS result was more than three times the consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “non-GAAP diluted EPS rising to $0.23 from $0.01”; “GAAP net income swung to a positive $9.1 million ($0.06 diluted EPS) from a net loss of $20.3 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” consensus: “$0.07”; the preview also says the guide midpoint was “at high end” of consensus.

surprises.description: Corsair raised FY2026 guidance instead of following the preview’s base case of reaffirming it. The revised adjusted EBITDA midpoint is $126 million, up about $19 million and above the preview’s bullish $115–125 million range; the revenue midpoint rose to about $1.435 billion, roughly in line with the $1.43 billion Street estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was raised, with the adjusted EBITDA midpoint increasing about $19 million (to $121-131 million) and revenue midpoint up roughly $35 million (to $1.4-1.47 billion).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (~50%)” scenario: “FY reaffirmed, not raised”; the preview says “A simple reaffirm is a de facto disappointment.” Its bull scenario projected “$115–125M EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA exceeded the high end of guidance even after excluding the tariff benefit, indicating a stronger underlying result than the preview’s roughly $15 million implied EBITDA expectation. That makes the EBITDA beat more than just a consequence of the one-time refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the $14.3 million tariff benefit, adjusted EBITDA of $16.7 million still exceeded the high end of guidance, indicating genuine operational improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance was “$12.5–15.5M”; the preview said consensus implied “~$15M.”

surprises.description: Company gross margin reached a record 33.2%, above the preview’s 31–32% base-case range, but about 500 basis points of the 640-basis-point year-over-year expansion came from a one-time tariff refund. The headline margin beat therefore substantially overstates the underlying year-over-year expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin hit a company record of 33.2%, expanding 640 basis points year-over-year, though approximately 500 basis points came from a one-time $15.6 million tariff refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “Gross Margin” of “31–32%.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow and the balance sheet were much stronger than the preview’s roughly net-neutral Q1 balance-sheet picture suggested: Q2 operating cash flow surged, first-half cash generation exceeded the prior two full years combined, and Corsair ended the quarter with substantial net cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow surged 148% year-over-year to $74.8 million, with first-half cash generation exceeding all of 2025 and 2024 combined, ending the quarter in a net cash position of approximately $75.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the Q1 balance sheet as “$119.7M cash vs. $119.8M total debt at Q1 (roughly net-neutral)” and flagged capital allocation as a key watch item.

surprises.description: The call put meaningful revenue contribution from desktop AI PCs mainly in late 2027 and beyond, rather than providing near-term commercial metrics for the AI-compute opportunity. The stated $22 billion market target gives market context, but leaves the preview’s request for CORSAIR PRO pipeline, backlog, or bookings figures unanswered.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “targeting the roughly $22 billion desktop AI PC market with revenue contribution expected mainly in late 2027 and beyond.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “CORSAIR PRO / AI compute — any numbers at all” and said pipeline, backlog, or bookings quantification would be the multiple-expansion lever.

surprises.description: Management identified GTA 6’s expected Q4 2026 launch as a console and peripherals tailwind, a specific demand catalyst the preview did not mention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management sees GTA 6's expected Q4 2026 launch as a console and peripherals tailwind.”

in_line: Revenue of $314.3 million was within the preview’s $308–320 million base-case range and above the $307.5 million guidance midpoint.
Peripherals revenue grew 13% year over year, consistent with the preview’s low-teens growth expectation.
Gaming Components & Systems revenue declined 9%, and its 26.3% gross margin was close to the preview’s expectation that the segment margin would step down to around 26%.

The TrackRacer acquisition and minority investment in Bitfocus had already been noted in the preview; the call’s expectation of immaterial 2026 contributions did not establish a material near-term earnings contribution.

surprises.description: Poland produced only $0.1 million of adjusted EBITDA, with the Rosa Casino closure, startup losses in Warsaw, and abnormally low table hold weighing on results. The preview modeled $1.6 million of Poland EBITDAR; the measures differ, but the call also said low table hold reduced gaming revenue by roughly $1 million versus expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Poland was a major drag, posting just $0.1 million adjusted EBITDA” and “abnormally low table hold that cut gaming revenue by roughly $1 million versus expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Poland … Q2'26E EBITDAR … $1.6M.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $152 million, below the $153.9 million consensus and the preview’s $155.5 million segment-build estimate. The reported 1% year-over-year growth was also below the consensus-implied 2% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net operating revenue reached a record $152 million (up 1% year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net operating revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $153.9M”; the preview’s segment build estimated “Total” revenue of “$155.5M (+3.1%).”

surprises.description: U.S. revenue came in above the preview’s estimate, and property margins expanded. The preview estimated $108.5 million of U.S. revenue; actual revenue was $111.6 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. operations generated $111.6 million revenue (up 5%)” and “U.S. average property margins expanding from 24% to 26%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “United States | Q2'26E Rev | $108.5M (+2%).”

surprises.description: Canada’s revenue fell short of the preview’s estimate: $20.4 million versus $21.5 million expected. The 2.2% year-over-year growth was also well below the preview’s forecast of 7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Canadian operations grew revenue 2.2% to $20.4 million.”

surprises.description: Despite Canada’s revenue shortfall, its profitability improved: EBITDA grew 11%, margins widened by two percentage points, and expenses declined. That resilience was better than the preview’s revenue-led Canada momentum thesis suggested, though the preview’s $6.3 million estimate was for EBITDAR, not EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA 11% to $6.2 million,” “margins expanding from 28% to 30%,” and “expenses declining 1.3% on lower payroll.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Canada … Century Mile momentum + FX”; the preview estimated “Q2'26E Rev … $21.5M (+7%).”

surprises.description: The Nugget’s exceptional growth proved repeatable for another quarter: revenue rose 16% and adjusted EBITDA increased more than 93%, with hotel cash revenue and transient corporate room nights surging. The preview highlighted the prior quarter’s 93% EBITDA gain but questioned whether it would recur.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Nugget delivered its third consecutive quarter of EBITDA growth with revenue up 16% and adjusted EBITDA up more than 93%,” with “hotel cash revenue up 36% and transient corporate room nights up over 300%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Nugget EBITDAR was +93% in Q1 off concert programming — is that a repeatable operating change or a comp artifact?”

surprises.description: Missouri outperformed the preview’s soft-market setup: Century’s Missouri operations led all 13 state casinos in year-over-year gaming revenue growth, while its properties extended their EBITDA-growth streak to seven quarters. The preview said Missouri needed share gains against a soft market but did not anticipate this degree of leadership or the cited enforcement tailwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Missouri properties posted their 7th consecutive quarter of EBITDA growth” and “led all 13 state casinos in year-over-year gaming revenue growth,” aided by enforcement against illegal skill games.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Missouri statewide AGR grew only +1.1% in April and +1.8% in June, so the Midwest segment needs share gains, not market growth.”

surprises.description: Management said normalized annual Poland EBITDA is around $8 million, below the prior peak of $10 million. The preview modeled the new Warsaw casino as diluting margins but did not flag a lower normalized earnings level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Poland's normalized EBITDA is around $8 million annually (down from a prior peak of $10 million).”

surprises.description: Poland showed a sharp early recovery after the weak first half: July generated nearly as much EBITDA as the entire first half. That rebound was not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of startup-related margin dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July generated nearly as much Polish EBITDA as the entire first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected the “2nd Wrocław casino … [to] add[] revenue, dilute[] margin.”

surprises.description: The asset-sale process had advanced beyond the interested-party stage described in the preview: two groups were in due diligence for Poland and Canadian packages, and management said a publicly disclosable transaction could occur before year-end. No signed deal was announced, but this was more concrete progress than the preview’s base case of discussions with no timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two groups in due diligence for Poland and Canadian packages potentially yielding a publicly disclosable transaction before year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Poland ‘progressing, no timeline’”; it said investors wanted “a counterparty, a structure … and a timeline.”

surprises.description: Leverage improved to 6.5x from the 6.9x reported at Q1, and management expected it to fall well below 6x by year-end. The preview had emphasized deleveraging credibility and covenant risk but did not project this specific improvement; the absence of debt maturities until Q2 2029 also provides a longer runway than the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 6.5x and management expects it to fall well below 6x by year-end, with no debt maturities until Q2 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “confirm … covenant/first-lien leverage disclosure” and described covenant headroom as a “tail risk.”

in_line: 2026 CapEx was guided to about $15 million, consistent with the preview’s $14–15 million expectation.

surprises.description: The preview expected more than 8.4 million pounds of Q2 production, with its base case at 9.0–9.5 million. Ironton produced only about 4.5 million pounds of PureFive; management attributed the decline to a planned turnaround.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ironton produced approximately 4.5 million pounds of PureFive in Q2 2026, down from the prior quarter due to a planned turnaround.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A sixth consecutive record (>8.4M lbs) keeps the operational narrative intact”; base case production was “9.0–9.5M lbs.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated roughly $500–525 million of pro forma liquidity after the financing, but the company reported total liquidity of $236.9 million, including $165.2 million of cash. That is substantially below the preview’s implied balance-sheet cushion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with total liquidity of $236.9 million (including $165.2 million cash), up from $131 million at the end of Q1, after June concurrent offerings … raising $450.5 million gross ($432 million net).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied pro forma liquidity: $131M (Q1 exit) + ~$435M net proceeds – ~$45M quarterly burn ≈ $500–525M.”

surprises.description: The preview put FY2026 project spending at $39–45 million, while management raised the range to $45–50 million. The new range is above the prior upper end and implies more project spending than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year project spend guidance was raised to $45-50 million from $39-45 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guide $39–45M and ‘majority discretionary.’”

surprises.description: The preview said P&G Tide caps had begun shipping in late May or early June, but the call said Tide caps were scheduled for Q3 retail. That suggests the retail rollout was less advanced than the preview led investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “P&G … now has Downy caps in commercial production, Tide caps scheduled for Q3 retail, and Vicks ZzzQuil child-resistant lids targeted for Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “P&G Tide caps began shipping (late May/early June); Vicks ZzzQuil approved for H2 2026.”

surprises.description: The call reported seven new customer conversions, including a first building-and-construction application. The preview was looking for evidence of at least two brand conversions, so the reported count and new application type indicate broader-than-expected customer traction, though no brands were named in the supplied facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “7 new customer conversions including a first building and construction application.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “should be able to name brands that have converted” and its bull case specified “2+ named NJ brand conversions.”

surprises.description: Downy caps were newly reported to be in commercial production, a P&G product milestone the preview did not identify. This adds a commercial launch beyond the Tide and Vicks developments discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “P&G … now has Downy caps in commercial production.”

surprises.description: Core operations spending declined about 8%, better than the preview’s expectation of flat-to-better monthly operating expense. The preview did not specify an expected decline of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core operations spending declined about 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “flat-to-better monthly opex on higher volume.”

surprises.description: The turnaround was completed ahead of schedule and below budget, a favorable execution outcome not anticipated in the preview. This is distinct from the lower production volume caused by the planned turnaround.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a turnaround with more than 170 site projects ahead of schedule and below budget.”

in_line: Revenue of approximately $4.5 million was within the preview’s $4.5–5.5 million base case and consistent with management’s prior framing that Q2 would look largely like Q1, despite differing headline consensus estimates.
Adjusted EBITDA of negative $31.7 million was within the preview’s base-case range of negative $30 million to negative $33 million.
Management reaffirmed the target for Ironton monthly cash breakeven in the second half of 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the H2 ramp would be reiterated.

The 12,000-pounds-per-hour throughput demonstration was consistent with the preview’s report that rate tests had already reached 12,000 pounds per hour; the call also said the plant is not yet routinely running at that rate.
Thailand’s expected second-half 2026 groundbreaking and 2028 operation remained consistent with the timeline in the preview.
Vicks ZzzQuil lids targeted for Q4 remained within the preview’s expectation that the product would be approved for H2 2026.

surprises.description: Celcuity set REVTORPYK’s price at $30,000 per treatment cycle, above the preview’s modeled $26,000–$28,000 per month. The preview also said a price at or above $28,000 would validate the TAM assumptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “priced REVTORPYK at a WAC of $10,000 per vial or $30,000 per treatment cycle.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Street models $26–28k/month”; “A number at/above $28k validates the $5–6B TAM math.”

surprises.description: Updated discontinuation rates in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort were substantially lower for gedatolisib combinations than for alpelisib, a favorable tolerability result against the preview’s concern about managing adverse effects. The preview’s 12% discontinuation figure concerned the wild-type-label triplet, so the cohort and comparison are not identical.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Updated treatment discontinuation rates due to adverse events in the mutant cohort were 5.2% for the triplet and 3.8% for the doublet, versus 19% for alpelisib.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Label: stomatitis in 72% of triplet patients (22% severe); 12% discontinuation on the triplet”; “community docs’ ability to manage mucositis ‘will be critical to commercial success.’”

surprises.description: SG&A reached $35 million, above the preview’s $27–32 million estimate and its expected roughly $28–30 million quarterly commercial run rate. The increase was attributed largely to building out the commercial launch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A rising to $35 million from $7.6 million on commercial launch buildout.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SG&A … $27–32M (launch build)”; “SG&A steps to ~$28–30M.”

surprises.description: The reported net loss was $1.44 per share, worse than the preview’s expected $1.15–$1.25 loss range. The preview had warned that a debt-extinguishment charge could push GAAP EPS to $1.30–$1.40, so the reported figure was also somewhat worse than that caveat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss widened to $78.9 million ($1.44 per share) from $45.3 million ($1.04) a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS … −$1.16”; “My estimate: −$1.15 to −$1.25 (GAAP ex-items)”; “could push GAAP EPS to −$1.30/−$1.40.”

surprises.description: R&D expense was below the preview’s $34–37 million estimate, falling to $31.1 million as clinical-trial costs declined, including from the VIKTORIA-1 wind-down. That provided some expense relief, though commercial spending was higher than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses decreased to $31.1 million from $36.4 million a year earlier, primarily due to a $7 million reduction in clinical trial costs including VIKTORIA-1 wind-down.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed an expected gross-to-net discount of about 20%, meaning the company expects to retain roughly 80% of WAC. The preview had highlighted payer access but gave no gross-to-net estimate; management said this discount is below the roughly 30% typical for oral therapies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a gross-to-net discount of about 20% (capturing ~80% of WAC), better than the ~30% discount typical for oral therapies.”

surprises.description: Celcuity expanded VIKTORIA-2 to study gedatolisib in treatment-naive, endocrine-sensitive patients, a setting the preview had not identified as part of the trial plan. Management cited prior Phase Ib results that were stronger than historical results for ribociclib plus letrozole, though the comparison is against historical data.
surprises.fact_evidence: “VIKTORIA-2 was expanded to add a study evaluating gedatolisib in treatment-naive endocrine-sensitive patients (roughly two-thirds of newly diagnosed cases), where a prior Phase Ib trial showed median PFS of 48.6 months and 79% ORR versus historical 25 months and 53% for ribociclib plus letrozole.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed VIKTORIA-2 enrollment pace and the existing 1L regimens as pipeline items to watch; it did not mention this treatment-naive, endocrine-sensitive study expansion.

in_line: Management maintained late-Q3 shipping: the preview’s base case expected “’Late Q3’ reaffirmed,” and the call said shipping would begin “late in Q3 2026.”

The PIK3CA-mutant sNDA remained planned for Q3, matching the preview’s expectation of a Q3 submission; the preview had also cited the reported mutant-cohort PFS results, which were reiterated in the call.

The company reported $754 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments and runway at least into 2029, consistent with the preview’s $740–790 million cash estimate and expectation of runway into 2029.
The approximately 37,000-patient target population and more-than-$6-billion annual TAM broadly matched the preview’s 37,000-patient estimate and $5–6 billion TAM framework.
The company reported 88 oncology sales specialists deployed; the preview expected the sales force to be onboarded in Q2 and asked whether it was fully onboarded.

surprises.description: Operating EPS was $1.30, above the $1.15 consensus and even the preview’s $1.20–$1.28 base-case range. The result was a stronger beat than the preview’s expected mid-single- to low-double-digit percentage surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted operating EPS rose 46% year-over-year to $1.30.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating EPS (diluted) | $1.15”; the base case forecast “$1.20–1.28.”

surprises.description: The combined ratio was 89.5%, better than the 90.7% consensus, while the 87.6% ex-cat ratio also came in below the preview’s roughly 88% buy-side reference. The implied catastrophe load was about 1.9 points, below the preview’s 2.5–3 point base-case assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The overall combined ratio was 89.5% (87.6% ex-cat).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Combined ratio | 90.7%”; “Ex-cat combined ratio vs. ~88% whisper”; base case “89.5–90.5% (cat 2.5–3 pts).”

surprises.description: Skyward Specialty’s expense ratio fell to 24.3%, far below the 28.4% consensus estimate cited in the preview. The call also attributed efficiency gains to AI, including faster submissions and quoting, which the preview had not anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Skyward Specialty expense ratio improved 2.7 points year-over-year to 24.3%, aided by AI-driven efficiency gains including 40% faster submissions and 35% improvement in speed to quote.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expense ratio | 28.4%.”

surprises.description: Gross written premiums grew 13%, with Skyward Specialty up 14%, slightly exceeding the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly 8–12% growth. This was stronger growth than the preview’s central scenario despite its emphasis on underwriting selectivity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross written premiums grew 13% to $741 million”; “Skyward Specialty GWP rose 14%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “GWP growth ~8–12%.”

surprises.description: Apollo GWP grew only 6%, a sharp slowdown from the 18.7% growth cited for Q1 in the preview. Management attributed the slower pace to seasonal property patterns; at the same time, fee-generating GWP continued to grow and fee guidance was maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Apollo GWP grew only 6% to $73 million due to seasonal property patterns (versus 45% in Q1), while fee-generating GWP rose 29%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Apollo +18.7% (led by Syndicate 1969)” in the Q1 baseline; the preview also flagged “Fee income and Apollo scaling.”

surprises.description: Apollo’s combined ratio was elevated by Middle East conflict catastrophe losses, an event and source of losses the preview did not flag. This contrasted with the relatively favorable consolidated catastrophe load.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Apollo at 97.6% due to 5.4 points of Middle East conflict catastrophe losses.”

surprises.description: Net investment income reached $31 million, modestly above the preview’s $29.5 million estimate. The beat was smaller than the strong year-over-year growth might suggest because the preview already expected roughly 59% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net investment income rose over 60% year-over-year to $31 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net investment income | ~$29.5M”; consensus expected “+58.7% YoY.”
