surprises.description: B&G’s Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $60.4 million, above the preview’s modeled $56–58 million, and its 15.8% margin exceeded the estimated 14.3–14.7%. The result was aided by the higher-margin acquisitions and tariff refunds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $60.4 million (15.8% of net sales) from $58 million (13.7%) a year earlier,” aided by “the higher-margin Collagen and Kitchen Basics acquisitions and tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: No published consensus found; model ~$56–58M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin: ~14.3–14.7% (est.).”

surprises.description: Base business sales fell 2.9%, below the preview’s expectation of flat to slightly down for the remainder of FY26. A 4.3% volume decline outweighed the 1.4% gain in pricing/mix, although year-to-date base business sales were essentially flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Base business net sales declined 2.9% to $346.3 million as a 4.3% volume drop outweighed a 1.4% gain in pricing/mix,” while year-to-date base business sales were “essentially flat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management then guided base business flat to slightly down for the remainder of FY26 — so anything at or above flat is a beat against their own bar.”

surprises.description: Reported net sales were $383.3 million, below the preview’s $394.9 million consensus and its $393–398 million base scenario, despite divestitures already being expected to reduce reported sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales fell 9.7% year-over-year to $383.3 million,” with the decline driven primarily by divestitures that had contributed about $68 million in Q2 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $394.9M” consensus; the base scenario expected “$393–398M.”

surprises.description: Green Giant Canada did not close in Q2 as the preview expected; it remains in company financials and guidance until the expected Q3 closing, delaying the anticipated transaction and leverage benefit. The company also said proceeds are likely near $60 million rather than the $32 million held-for-sale carrying value.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pending Green Giant Canada divestiture, expected to close in Q3, remains in company financials and guidance until closing, with proceeds likely near the ~$60 million level rather than the ~$32 million held-for-sale carrying value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the sale was “guided to close in Q2” and flagged “Green Giant Canada close confirmation” as a key item.

surprises.description: Tariffs were less of a net Q2 headwind than the preview’s discussion of a $5.1 million year-to-date tariff burden suggested: B&G recovered most of the tariff exposure for which it was importer of record, and expects additional modest refunds in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total incremental tariff exposure was estimated at $8-$9 million,” B&G was importer of record for less than half and “recovered most of that in Q2,” with “additional modest refunds expected in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said tariffs were “running −$5.1M YTD, concentrated in Spices & Flavor Solutions” and that guidance excluded further policy escalation.

surprises.description: The new Green Giant U.S. Frozen contract-manufacturing business was already generating $23.9 million in its first full quarter and was modestly profitable, at roughly a $100 million annualized pace. That provides concrete replacement-business scale against the preview’s concern that co-manufacturing might not replace the divested businesses’ contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new Green Giant U.S. Frozen contract manufacturing business generated $23.9 million in its first full quarter and is modestly profitable, running at roughly $100 million annualized.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified as a bear-case risk that “the divested businesses took more EBITDA with them than the co-manufacturing agreements replaced.”

surprises.description: B&G reported a notable reduction in SG&A and said further cuts were still expected into early Q3, an additional cost-saving development not specifically anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A fell 14% to $40.6 million (10.6% of sales) with further reductions expected into early Q3 to eliminate stranded costs before reaching a stable run rate.”

surprises.description: B&G appointed board member Rob Mills as CEO, a leadership change the preview did not flag; he is expected to join the Q3 earnings call in November.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Board member Rob Mills was appointed CEO and will join the Q3 earnings call in November,” with experience in digital, AI, M&A, and P&L at Tractor Supply Company.

in_line: B&G reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $1.735–$1.775 billion in net sales, $275–$290 million adjusted EBITDA, and $0.575–$0.675 adjusted diluted EPS, as the preview expected guidance to be reaffirmed or revised and its base case assumed an unchanged range.
Net interest expense of $38.5 million was within the preview’s expected quarterly range of roughly $37–$39 million.

surprises.description: VIAVI raised its $500 million-plus quarterly revenue run-rate target to calendar 2027, pulling it forward from the prior goal of exiting fiscal 2028. The preview described $500 million per quarter as an eventual target but did not anticipate this earlier timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management now expects to reach a $500 million+ quarterly revenue run rate during calendar 2027, pulled forward from the prior target of exiting fiscal 2028.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CPO manufacturing as the structural driver behind an eventual $500M/quarter run-rate”

surprises.description: Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance of $450–460 million is above the preview’s $425–435 million estimate implied by FY2027 consensus. It clears the preview’s $450 million threshold for forcing FY2027 estimates higher, although it falls short of the preview’s bull-case guide of at least $465 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q1 FY2027 guidance calls for revenue of $450-460 million with EPS of $0.40-0.42.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 consensus of $1.80B mechanically implies a Q1 in the $425–435M range” and “A guide of $450M+ would force FY27 numbers up across the board.”

surprises.description: NSE operating margin reached 20%, beating the preview’s 18.7% guided level and surpassing the 20% mark the preview identified as an early sign of stronger drop-through.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NSE revenue grew 69.2% year-over-year to $353.9 million, with operating margin surging to 20% from just 4.6% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guided 18.7%” and “NSE clearing 20% op margin would be an early beat on that path.”

surprises.description: NSE revenue of $353.9 million exceeded the preview’s approximate $344 million expectation and the company’s $340–348 million guidance range. This was a segment-level beat beyond the already anticipated strong overall quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NSE revenue grew 69.2% year-over-year to $353.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NSE revenue” consensus “~$344M (implied)” and company guidance of “$340–348M.”

surprises.description: Spirent contributed $47.7 million, slightly below the preview’s expectation that it would normalize near $50 million per quarter. However, management said integration was complete and guided at least 10% sequential growth into September, tempering the shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Spirent product lines contributed $47.7 million in Q4” and management guided “at least 10% sequential growth into September.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Spirent contributed $54.2M in Q3, guided to normalize near $50M/quarter. Below that raises integration questions.”

surprises.description: FY2026 EPS was $1.00 versus the preview’s $0.94 estimate, a modest beat. Full-year revenue of $1.518 billion was close to the preview’s $1.51 billion estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY2026 revenue was $1.518 billion (up 40%), with operating margin expanding 630 basis points to 20.6% and EPS doubling to $1.00 from $0.47.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 (full year): $1.51B rev / $0.94 EPS.”

surprises.description: VIAVI disclosed that its data center business excluding Spirent more than doubled year over year, a stronger quantified growth result than the preview specified. The preview highlighted data-center momentum and production testing but did not set an expectation for this business to more than double.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding Spirent, the data center business more than doubled year-over-year, driven by rapidly growing production testing for fiber optic modules, cables, and CPO.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Look for 800G volume vs. 1.6T transitioning from labs to production” and “CPO manufacturing as the structural driver behind an eventual $500M/quarter run-rate.”

surprises.description: The company completed a $575 million gross follow-on offering and used the proceeds to repay Term Loan B in full. The debt reduction addresses the preview’s balance-sheet concern, but the offering also raised the diluted share count to 261 million, an unanticipated dilution trade-off.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a follow-on offering issuing ~12.78 million shares at $45 for $575 million gross, using proceeds to fully pay off the Term Loan B, raising diluted share count to 261 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With $1.08B debt against $508M cash, a second consecutive negative-OCF quarter turns a valuation debate into a balance-sheet debate.”

in_line: Q4 revenue of $443.1 million and EPS of $0.34 were within the preview’s $443–448 million revenue and $0.33–0.34 EPS whisper ranges, even though both exceeded the company’s guidance highs.
Data center made up approximately 50% of NSE revenue, broadly matching the preview’s expectation that the share would reach or pass 50%.
Wireless demand remained weak but stable, consistent with the preview’s view that carrier and wireless products were still well below peak and would not provide an offsetting recovery.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected around $213.7 million, but Ducommun reported $224.5 million, about 5% above consensus and above the preview’s $220 million bull-case threshold. This was a materially stronger quarter than the preview’s base case of $214–217 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $224.5 million, up 12% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $213.7M”; the base case was “$214–217M,” while the bull case was “$220M+.”

surprises.description: The missile business grew 68% year-over-year in the quarter, far ahead of the preview’s expectation that the major framework-agreement revenue impact would arrive around year-end 2026 or early 2027. The reported surge suggests the ramp was already much stronger than the preview’s timing implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The missile business surged 68% year-over-year in Q2,” driven largely by “PAC-3 replenishment demand from Lockheed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The agreements were expected to have “revenue impact end-2026/early-2027, accelerating through 2027–28.”

surprises.description: Commercial Aerospace revenue grew 16%, whereas the preview said Q1’s 18% growth was flattered by timing and that management’s destocking outlook implied a mid-single-digit decline. The actual growth was substantially stronger than that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial Aerospace revenue grew 16% to $89 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Positive growth here is genuine upside; a mid-single-digit decline is what guidance implies.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.18 versus the preview’s $0.97–$0.98 consensus range, a much larger beat than expected. The call also said results benefited from a one-time executive compensation clawback tied to an earlier restatement, qualifying the strength of the reported result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS increased to $1.18 from $0.90, though results benefited from a one-time executive compensation clawback tied to an earlier restatement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | $0.97–$0.98.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached a record 28%, above the preview’s modeled 26.8–27.3% range. The improvement was therefore stronger than the preview’s expected modest expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 160 basis points to a record 28%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin (modeled) | ~26.8–27.3%”; the preview expected “+20 to +70 bps.”

surprises.description: The quarter’s 1.4x book-to-bill lifted remaining performance obligations to a record $1.16 billion, above the preview’s bull-case marker of $1.15 billion for early missile bookings. This was stronger backlog evidence than the preview’s $1.07 billion reference point suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligations hit a record $1.16 billion, up over $250 million year-over-year,” with “a 1.4x book-to-bill in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “RPO / backlog vs. $1.07B” and described “RPO >$1.15B on early missile bookings” as a bull-case outcome.

surprises.description: Management said some second-half production and revenue had been pulled into the first half, so H2 growth is now expected to moderate to low-to-mid single digits. The full-year mid-to-high-single-digit growth guidance was retained, but the second-half trajectory is weaker than the preview’s unchanged-guidance base case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management pulled forward some second-half production and revenue into the first half, expecting H2 growth to moderate to low-to-mid single digits while reiterating full-year guidance of mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected FY26 guidance to be “mid- to high-single digits” reiterated “verbatim,” with “destocking language unchanged.”

surprises.description: Ducommun disclosed an incremental 737MAX aftermarket retrofit order expected to support Commercial Aerospace revenue for several years, with possible future line-fit potential. The preview discussed 737MAX production rates and destocking but did not anticipate this specific order or its multi-year revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: Commercial Aerospace growth was “aided by an incremental 737MAX aftermarket retrofit order expected to sustain revenue for several years with future line-fit potential.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.1%, within the preview’s expected 16.9–17.2% base-case range and above its 17.0% proof-point.
The company reiterated its full-year revenue growth guidance of mid-to-high single digits, as the preview’s base case expected.
Engineered product content was 23% of trailing 12-month revenue, matching the preview’s stated 23% level.
The September 17 Investor Day and Vision 2032 strategy were already anticipated in the preview.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $1.8 billion, well above the preview’s roughly $1.66 billion consensus and guidance anchor; reported growth of 28% also exceeded the expected roughly 19.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 28% year-over-year to $1.8 billion in Q4 FY2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Consensus $1.66B”; “Revenue growth Y/Y … ~19.8%.”

surprises.description: Cloud grew 31%, exceeding the preview’s roughly 25.5% Q4 growth expectation; the call also said cloud revenue beat guidance by $49 million. Growth came mainly from cross-sell and seat expansion, rather than data center migrations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cloud revenue accelerating 31% to $1.2 billion”; “Cloud revenue beat guidance by $49 million, driven primarily by cross-sell and seat expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cloud revenue growth … ~25.5%.”

surprises.description: RPO growth reached 44%, above the preview’s threshold of 30% or more for validating demand through the Data Center pull-forward. This was stronger than the preview’s stated bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPO grew 44% year-over-year to $4.8 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If RPO growth holds ≥30%, it partially validates that the Data Center pull-forward is a timing issue, not a demand issue.”

surprises.description: The call gave positive Rovo adoption and usage indicators, including Fortune 500 usage and quarter-over-quarter growth in Rovo-assisted actions, but the facts provided include no dollar-denominated AI revenue figure. The preview specifically identified a hard dollar figure as the proof point bulls wanted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rovo is now used by over 80% of the Fortune 500” and “Rovo-assisted actions grew 50% quarter-over-quarter”; the call also said adopters grow ARR at more than twice the rate of non-adopters.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bulls need a hard, dollar-denominated AI number this quarter.”

surprises.description: Enterprise expansion was stronger and more concretely demonstrated than the preview had flagged: customers at both the $3 million and $5 million ARR levels set growth records, with the counts growing more than 50% and 70%, respectively.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enterprise expansion set records with $3 million ARR customers (164 total) growing over 50% and $5 million ARR customers (69 total) growing over 70% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a $14 billion cross-sell opportunity in the existing customer base and said that, despite 85% Fortune 500 penetration, those customers account for only about 10% of revenue. The preview did not identify this specific expansion runway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company sees a $14 billion cross-sell opportunity within its existing customer base,” and its enterprise motion is early, with “85% of the Fortune 500 penetrated representing only about 10% of total revenue.”

surprises.description: The call added a substantial Teamwork Graph performance claim: it spans more than 200 billion objects and connections, with grounded agents delivering more accurate answers while using fewer tokens. The preview did not flag these product-performance metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Teamwork Graph now spans over 200 billion objects and connections, delivering up to 44% more accurate answers while consuming 48% fewer tokens for grounded agents.”

in_line: Net revenue retention remained above 120%, matching the preview’s stated baseline of “>120%.”

surprises.description: Snap reported Q2 revenue of $1.6 billion, above the preview’s $1.53 billion consensus and the company’s $1.52–$1.55 billion guidance range. The result was about 5% above consensus and $50 million above the top of guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $1.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $1.53B, +13.97% YoY; company guidance is $1.52–$1.55B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $250 million, exceeding the previewed $175–$200 million company guidance by $50 million above its upper end. That is a substantially larger beat relative to the forecast range than the revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose $208 million year-over-year to $250 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: company-guided $175–$200M.”

surprises.description: Snap raised its full-year infrastructure cost guidance by $50 million at both ends of the range, citing additional AI and machine-learning investment. The preview had not flagged an increase in infrastructure costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year infrastructure cost guidance was raised to $1.65–$1.70 billion from $1.60–$1.65 billion, driven by additional AI and machine learning infrastructure investment.”

surprises.description: Management made free cash flow per share the company’s primary financial objective, a change in stated priorities that the preview did not anticipate. The call also reported positive quarterly and trailing-twelve-month free cash flow, but the preview provided no Q2 FCF estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company shifted its primary financial objective to free cash flow per share”; “Free cash flow was $121 million in Q2 … with trailing 12-month free cash flow of $706 million.”

surprises.description: Snap reported revenue growth of 19% against adjusted cost growth of only 4%, a degree of operating leverage not quantified or anticipated in the preview. This offers evidence of cost discipline alongside growth, though the preview had separately flagged cost-savings delivery as a key issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “19% revenue growth against just 4% adjusted cost growth in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “evidence the >$500M annualized reduction is on track and the size of Q2 restructuring charges.”

surprises.description: Management said Specs mass-market adoption is not expected until toward the end of the decade, tempering the near-term commercial potential of the product. The preview identified Specs monetization as an issue to watch but gave no adoption timeline expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects mass-market adoption only toward the end of the decade.”

surprises.description: Management guided to sustained positive net income beginning in 2027, a newly stated timeline not anticipated in the preview. The preview expected Q2 restructuring charges to weigh on GAAP results but did not provide a longer-term net-income outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “guided sustained positive net income beginning in 2027.”

in_line: Other revenue grew 85%, broadly maintaining the momentum the preview highlighted after Q1 Other Revenue grew 87%.
Specs pricing was $2,195, matching the launch price noted in the preview.
Advertising revenue growth accelerated to 9% from Q1’s 3%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of an advertising recovery, although the preview did not specify a Q2 ad-growth figure.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q3 revenue around $345–355M, with roughly $350M the key bar. Onto guided to $380–400M, substantially above that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $380-$400 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3'26 revenue guidance — the whole trade. Bar: ~$350M”; the base case was “$345–355M.”

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was expected at $1.68 consensus, with the preview's whisper at $1.75–1.80. The reported $1.93 also beat the prior guidance high end by $0.20, exceeding both expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS came in at $1.93, beating the high end of prior guidance by $0.20.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS: Consensus $1.68”; “My whisper … non-GAAP EPS $1.75–1.80”; prior guidance was $1.65–1.73.

surprises.description: The preview expected second-half revenue growth of at least 15% over the first half. Management raised that outlook to over 25% and said Q4 should exceed Q3, pointing to a much stronger second-half ramp than the preview's framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its second-half 2026 revenue growth outlook to over 25% versus the first half, up from a prior 15% expectation, with Q4 expected to exceed Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance: H2 revenue at least 15% above H1”; the preview's approximate split put Q3 at $340M and Q4 at $369M.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was expected at $325.6M consensus, and even the preview's $333–340M whisper was below the reported result. Revenue reached $343M, above the prior guidance high end of $330M.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached a record $343 million … exceeding the high end of guidance across revenue, gross margin, operating margin and EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: Consensus $325.6M”; prior guidance was $320–330M; “My whisper … revenue $333–340M.”

surprises.description: The preview treated advanced packaging growth above 50% for the year as the baseline and a raise as a possible upside case. Management instead raised full-year growth guidance to approximately 80%, driven by HBM and OSAT demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year advanced packaging growth guidance was raised sharply to approximately 80%, up from the 50% projected last quarter, driven by HBM and OSAT demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Advanced packaging — >50% FY growth”; the preview said “reaffirmed >50% is base case” and “raised” would be the bull trigger.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 gross margin of 56.0–56.5% and operating margin of 28.0–28.6%. Reported gross margin was 57% and operating margin was 30%, both above the expected ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin hit 57% … and operating margin reached 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin (non-GAAP): 56.0%–56.5%”; “Operating margin (non-GAAP): 28.0%–28.6%.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated roughly 50 basis points of gross-margin improvement per quarter and an operating-margin exit rate above 30%. Management now targets 350 basis points of gross-margin expansion and more than 750 basis points of operating-margin expansion for the year, with the year-end operating-margin exit above 33%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year targets now at 350 bps of gross margin and over 750 bps of operating margin expansion”; Q3 guidance has 32% operating margin, “exiting the year at 33%+ operating margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the path required “~+50bps gross margin per quarter” and a “>30% exit-rate operating margin.”

surprises.description: The preview's earnings bridge implied Q3 EPS of about $1.90. Onto guided to approximately $2.28, well above that implied level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for … EPS of approximately $2.28.”

surprises.description: The preview cited an approximately 25% full-year growth target for Advanced Nodes. The call reported 50% sequential growth in Q2 to about $120M and raised the full-year growth outlook to above 35%, with both memory and logic contributing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advanced nodes revenue grew 50% sequentially to approximately $120 million, with memory … up ~60% and logic up over 40%, and full-year growth expected to exceed 35%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Advanced Nodes — $80M in Q1 vs. ~25% FY growth target.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted limited Q1 cash and a prospective $710M Rigaku outlay as reasons to scrutinize post-deal liquidity. The call reported nearly $1.9B in cash alongside a new $1.5B 0% convertible offering, a materially larger cash position than the preview's cited starting point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a $1.5 billion 0% convertible debt offering (net ~$1.2 billion) … [and] holds nearly $1.9 billion in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “cash & marketable securities $654.2M” at Q1 and said the “$710M Rigaku outlay lands in H2 against a $654.2M pre-raise cash balance.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a single-OSAT Dragonfly order exceeding $200M, with most deliveries in 2027. The preview expected a Dragonfly ramp but did not anticipate an order of this size or its extended delivery visibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured over $200 million in Dragonfly orders from a single OSAT partner, with the majority to be delivered in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Dragonfly G5 as “<5–10% of Q1 revenue” and said management had indicated units would “nearly double each quarter”; it did not cite a large single-partner order.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a record backlog above $1.1B or that a substantial portion was already associated with 2027 deliveries. That adds stronger forward visibility than the preview's general H2 ramp discussion anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog surpassed a record $1.1 billion, with roughly 30-40% tied to 2027 deliveries, signaling strong customer visibility into next year.”

surprises.description: The call introduced silicon photonics as a future growth opportunity with a projected $500M market by 2030; the preview did not identify this opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management identified “silicon photonics ($500M SAM by 2030) … as [a] future growth driver.”

in_line: The approximately $200M of stock repurchases was broadly consistent with the preview's report that about $205M of the buyback had already been executed.

surprises.description: The preview characterized free cash flow as a significant pressure point, citing a cut in expected FY26 conversion to 30% and KUBRA’s capex needs and debt interest. Instead, Q2 free cash flow was $27.4 million, with 75% conversion (81% adjusted), a notably strong quarter against that concern, though it does not establish full-year conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $27.4 million (75% conversion), up 21% year-over-year, with adjusted free cash flow conversion of 81%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow conversion — cut from 45% to 30% for FY26. A real, underappreciated negative: KUBRA is more capex-intensive and the new debt carries heavy cash interest.”

surprises.description: Business payments grew faster than the preview’s Q1-based expectation: reported growth accelerated from 18% to 32%, and normalized growth rose from 16% to 19%. The reported rate includes political media contributions, but the normalized rate also accelerated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business payments revenue accelerated to 32% reported growth (19% normalized excluding political media).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Business Payments momentum. The genuine bright spot: +18% reported / +16% normalized in Q1.” The preview warned, “If this decelerates, the growth story loses its last clean leg.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in below the preview’s roughly $38 million estimate at $36.3 million, even though adjusted EPS matched consensus. The roughly 36% EBITDA margin was also below the preview’s approximate 37% estimate; management attributed the margin pressure almost entirely to KUBRA’s lower-margin mix, as the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA grew 14% year-over-year to $36.3 million”; adjusted EBITDA margin was “~36%,” with declines attributed “almost entirely to CUBRA's lower-margin mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2 adj. EBITDA estimate: ~$38M (~37% margin).”

surprises.description: The AP supplier network grew, but more slowly than the preview’s cited pace: it reached over 731,000 vendors, up 65% year-over-year, versus the preview’s expectation of 70% growth. This contrasts with the acceleration in business payments revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AP supplier network reaching over 731,000 vendors, up 65% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Supplier network +70% YoY to 665,000 vendors.”

surprises.description: Reported pro forma synergized net leverage was about 3.7x, slightly below the preview’s 4.0x net leverage figure at close. The measures are not stated on exactly the same basis, so the apparent improvement is modest rather than conclusive evidence of faster deleveraging.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma synergized net leverage stood at approximately 3.7x, with a target of below 3x within 18 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “4.0x net at close, targeting <3.0x within 18 months.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $100.7 million versus the preview’s approximately $102 million estimate, within its stated $99–106 million range; CUBRA’s approximately $21 million June contribution was also close to the preview’s roughly $22 million build.
Adjusted EPS was $0.20, matching the preview’s $0.20 consensus.

FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at $490–500 million and $168.5–176 million, as the preview expected. The stated expectation for organic growth to accelerate into double digits by year-end is consistent with the preview’s expectation that the back half would need to accelerate.
The preview anticipated lower blended margins from KUBRA’s lower-margin mix. Management attributed the margin declines almost entirely to that mix rather than pricing or competitive pressure.

The preview flagged early synergy confirmation as a credibility positive and cited an $8 million run-rate cost-synergy target within 2026. Repay reported over $4.5 million of annualized run-rate synergies exiting Q2 and maintained a target of over $8 million by year-end.

surprises.description: Revenue of $498 million was above the preview’s working estimate of about $475 million, though it was below the preview’s cited alternative estimate of $508.7 million. The revenue result therefore looks better against the working estimate, but the preview’s flagged consensus discrepancy makes the beat less definitive.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue rose to $498 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “I use ~$475M as the working consensus,” while also citing “$508.7M (Chartmill).”

surprises.description: Stimulation Services’ margin reached only 9%, below the preview’s key test of clearing roughly 11–12%. The segment’s EBITDA rose sequentially, but the margin result fell short of the price-capture improvement the preview said was central to the Q2 thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: Stimulation Services revenue grew to $430 million with EBITDA rising to $39 million, a 9% margin.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “If Stim margin doesn't clear ~11–12% in Q2, either the price increases didn't stick or they were given back in white space,” and listed “Stimulation margin ≥11%” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Free cash flow remained negative at $8 million, rather than reaching the preview’s roughly breakeven base-case expectation. The outflow did improve substantially from Q1, but year-to-date free cash outflow was still roughly $40 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Free cash flow was negative $8 million in Q2, improving from negative $25 million in Q1, with year-to-date free cash outflow of roughly $40 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “FCF ~breakeven” and flagged Q2 free cash flow as a key item to watch.

surprises.description: Liquidity was about $72 million, materially below the preview’s $108 million figure following the refinancing. ABL borrowings also rose to $162 million from $116 million quarter-over-quarter, leaving liquidity tighter than the preview’s setup suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: The new $300 million ABL replaced the prior $275 million facility, but total liquidity remained tight at approximately $72 million; ABL borrowings rose to $162 million from $116 million quarter-over-quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “total liquidity $108M” and said the new ABL “materially de-risks the near term.”

surprises.description: The CEO is resigning effective August 7, and Executive Chairman Matt Wilks will take over as CEO while retaining the chairman role. The preview did not flag an imminent leadership change.
surprises.fact_evidence: CEO Ladd Wilks is resigning effective August 7th to take a board seat, with Executive Chairman Matt Wilks assuming the CEO role while retaining his chairman title.

surprises.description: Flotek delivered a sharp sequential increase in both revenue and EBITDA, with revenue rising from $72 million to $102 million and EBITDA from $11 million to $19 million. The preview gave Q1 figures and identified Flotek as a secondary watch item, but did not forecast a Q2 result of this strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: Flotek revenue jumped to $102 million from $72 million and EBITDA rose to $19 million from $11 million.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $69 million was just below the preview’s $72 million buy-side whisper, although it remained within the preview’s broader $68–78 million base-case range. This is a modest shortfall against the more demanding expectation, not a miss against the stated base range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was $69 million, a 14% margin.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the buy-side whisper as “EBITDA ≥ $72M” and gave a base-case range of “$68–78M.”

in_line: Proppant EBITDA was $6 million, above the preview’s $5 million threshold, and the preview had already expected Q2 to be a down quarter for the segment. Competitive pricing pressure and the 5% margin were consistent with the concerns it flagged.
Fleet count remained in the low 20s, matching the Q1 baseline cited in the preview; the preview posed a possible increase as something to watch rather than a firm expectation.

Management said price increases with renegotiation windows would benefit Q3 and Q4 more than Q2, consistent with the preview’s expectation that pricing would layer in and become more pronounced in the back half.
The company reiterated FY2026 CapEx guidance within the preview’s cited range and maintained the $100 million annualized cost-savings program.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $392.4 million, well above the preview’s $360.2–360.7 million consensus and the company’s $355–365 million guidance. The roughly 9% beat versus the guidance midpoint was substantially larger than the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue reached a record $392.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus $360.2M (Zacks) / $360.7M”; “Q2 FY26 Guidance $355–365M.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $540–560 million was far above the preview’s approximately $410 million consensus and its $425 million-or-higher momentum threshold. The midpoint is about one-third above consensus, well beyond the preview’s bullish scenario of at least $445 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to $540-560 million, representing approximately 40% sequential growth at the midpoint, led by Scorpio-X Series volume production.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 ~$410M”; “a guide starting with a ‘4’ and midpoint ≥$425M”; bull scenario “≥$445M.”

surprises.description: Scorpio is expected to become Astera’s largest product line in Q3—one quarter earlier than the preview’s year-end 2026 expectation—and Scorpio-X is expected to exceed Scorpio-P revenue. That indicates a faster product-line transition than the preview’s anticipated Q3 Scorpio share test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scorpio is expected to become the company's largest product line by revenue in Q3, one quarter ahead of prior expectations, with Scorpio-X surpassing Scorpio-P revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management says it becomes the largest product line by end-2026”; the preview said the buy-side test was Scorpio “approaching ~25% or more of revenue this quarter.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $0.80, above the preview’s $0.69 consensus and $0.68–0.70 guidance. It even reached the lower end of the preview’s explicitly bullish $0.80–0.84 scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.80 in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS $0.68–0.70” guidance and “$0.69” consensus; bull scenario “$0.80–0.84.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating margin reached 39.1%, versus the preview’s roughly 36% expectation, and management guided to approximately 43% in Q3. The reported margin improvement and further expected operating leverage were stronger than the preview’s implied Q2 path.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin improved to 39.1% in Q2 (up 290 bps) and is guided to approximately 43% in Q3 (up 400 bps), reflecting significant operating leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin ~36% implied.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 73.7%, above the approximately 73% guidance and the preview’s 73.5% threshold for defusing the margin concern. However, Q3 guidance of approximately 72% is below that Q2 level and points to further mix-related pressure, matching a risk the preview had highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 73.7% (above 73% guidance), but Q3 gross margin is guided lower to approximately 72% due to increased switch/module mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Guidance ~73%”; “If reported GM lands ≥73.5% ... the margin scare defuses”; “If Q3 is guided to ~72% or below, the ‘Scorpio scales, margins fade’ bear case gets its evidence.”

surprises.description: PCIe 6 products across AI fabric and signal conditioning rose to more than half of Q2 revenue, compared with roughly one-third in Q1. The preview had flagged PCIe Gen 6 as just over one-third of Q1 revenue to watch, so the reported mix indicates a much faster shift toward these products than that baseline suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PCIe 6 products across AI fabric and signal conditioning represented more than 50% of total revenue in Q2, up from roughly one-third in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “PCIe Gen 6 mix (>1/3 of revenue in Q1) and signal conditioning (>1/3 of Q1 revenue) — is the legacy Aries/Taurus base still growing, or is Scorpio cannibalizing the mix?”

surprises.description: Management described a future Scorpio-X content opportunity well beyond $1,000 per XPU, targeting multiple thousands of dollars of total content per XPU. The preview already cited a $1,000-plus content target, so the materially higher multiple-thousands ambition is incremental upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management sees Scorpio-X content opportunity growing well beyond $1,000 per XPU in future generations, targeting total content of multiple thousands of dollars per XPU.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the “$1,000+ of content per accelerator” target.

surprises.description: Astera reported more than 10 customers engaged on Scorpio-X, with additional customers expected to reach production by late 2025 or early 2026. That is more quantified customer breadth and an earlier ramp outlook than the preview’s expectation of initial shipments to multiple hyperscalers and additional Scorpio-P customers toward the end of 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has over 10 customers engaged on Scorpio-X, with additional customers expected to ramp to production by late 2025 or early 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Scorpio X initial shipments to multiple hyperscalers” and Scorpio-P moving “to at least two additional major hyperscalers toward the end of 2026.”

surprises.description: Astera closed a new Leo memory-controller design win at a U.S. hyperscaler and expects volume CXL shipments to two U.S. hyperscalers in 2027. The preview mentioned Leo/CXL activity with Microsoft in private beta, but did not anticipate this additional win or the two-hyperscaler shipment outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new Leo memory controller design win was closed at a U.S. hyperscaler, with volume CXL shipments to two U.S. hyperscalers expected in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “Leo/CXL with Microsoft Azure M-series in private beta.”

in_line: Optical and custom solutions targeted for 2027 production were broadly consistent with the preview’s discussion of near-package optics volume in 2027 and existing custom-solution opportunities.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $9.41, well above the preview’s $7.40 working consensus midpoint and the listed $7.68 Zacks estimate, though just below the preview’s $9.50–10.50 bull case. The reported result exceeded the preview’s consensus-based expectation by roughly 27%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted earnings were $3.8 billion, with adjusted EPS of $9.41 and reported EPS of $9.55.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I use $7.40 as the working consensus midpoint below”; consensus adjusted EPS “$7.68.”

surprises.description: Phillips 66 reached its existing $17 billion debt target ahead of schedule, expects net debt below $16 billion by year-end, and introduced a lower net-debt target of approximately $13.5–14 billion. The preview anticipated a $17 billion target only by year-end 2027 and did not anticipate the new lower target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects net debt below $16 billion by year-end, and plans to hit its $17 billion debt target ahead of the 2027 schedule”; “signaled a new net debt target of approximately $13.5 billion to $14 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Debt walk toward $19B by YE2026 (then $17B YE2027).”

surprises.description: Refining captured 98% of its market indicator in Q2, a strong result against the preview’s concern that Phillips 66 might fail to capture the unusually strong refining environment. The preview did not state a specific Q2 capture-rate estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refining captured 98% of its market indicator in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If PSX's realized margin prints below ~$18–20/bbl, the market will read it as a capture-rate failure”; the preview also cited capture-rate concerns versus peers.

surprises.description: Rodeo Renewable Fuels ran at a record 106% utilization, while RD prices and RINs roughly doubled versus 2025 amid the Iran conflict. The preview discussed Middle East disruption as a chemicals headwind but did not anticipate this combination of strong renewable-fuels utilization and pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rodeo Renewable Fuels ran above nameplate at record 106% utilization, with RD prices and RINs roughly doubling versus 2025 due to the Iran conflict.”

surprises.description: The quarter included a one-time $100 million tariff-refund benefit that the preview did not flag, adding a discrete positive to results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A one-time $100 million tariff-refund benefit.”

surprises.description: Refining operating cost was $5.57 per barrel, already close to the $5.50 target set for 2027; management attributed the progress to more than 200 initiatives it described as structural and permanent. The preview identified the target but did not anticipate how close costs would already be or emphasize the permanence of the savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refining Q2 operating cost of $5.57/barrel is closing in on the annualized $5.50/barrel target for 2027, supported by over 200 cost-reduction initiatives that management describes as structural and permanent.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Secondary: refining opex/bbl (Q1 $6.21, targeting $5.50 by 2027).”

surprises.description: Management quantified substantial refining capacity outages in Asia, the Middle East, and Russia, and disclosed that each $1 widening in the WTI/WCS spread adds about $140 million to annual EBITDA. The preview discussed Iran-related crack strength but did not provide these outage totals or the quantified spread sensitivity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 7 million barrels/day of Asian/Middle East refining and 1.4 million b/d of Russian capacity is offline”; “every $1 widening in the WTI/WCS spread adds about $140 million to annual EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “the same Hormuz-region disruption that inflated refining cracks” was affecting the industry, but did not quantify offline capacity or WTI/WCS sensitivity.

in_line: Q3 refining guidance was constructive and consistent with the preview: management guided to roughly 95% market-indicator capture and worldwide crude utilization in the mid-90s, while the preview expected constructive Q3 commentary and utilization in the low-to-mid 90s.
Midstream remained on track for a $4.5 billion annualized EBITDA run-rate by year-end 2027, matching the preview’s stated milestone.
The roughly $450 million of favorable mark-to-market impacts were consistent with the preview’s expectation of a potentially large favorable derivative swing and a GAAP-versus-adjusted divergence.
Management expects to increase share repurchases in the second half, consistent with the preview’s expectation that investors wanted a step-up in buyback pace.
Western Gateway’s expected FID within about a month and late-2029 delivery broadly matched the preview’s expectation of a summer project milestone and 2029 in-service timing.

surprises.description: Kingstone reported diluted EPS of $1.05, above the preview’s $0.95 consensus and the $0.90–$1.00 base-case range. The beat was solid but not as large as the preview’s bull-case $1.10–$1.20.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS of $1.05, up 35% year over year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $0.95”; base case: “EPS $0.90–$1.00.”

surprises.description: The reported GAAP net combined ratio was 70.2%, materially better than the preview’s 75–77% base-case combined-ratio scenario. This is a GAAP net ratio, so it is not directly comparable to the preview’s separate 74–76% underlying combined-ratio guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The GAAP net combined ratio improved 1.3 points to 70.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “Combined Ratio 75–77%”; the preview also said to watch the “Underlying combined ratio vs. the 74–76% guide.”

surprises.description: The underlying loss ratio rose to 43.1%, contrary to the preview’s expectation that the Select mix could push the non-cat loss ratio into the mid-30s. This indicates weaker underlying loss performance than the preview’s favorable operating thesis anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The underlying loss ratio rose to 43.1% from 38.7% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether Select mix keeps pushing the non-cat loss ratio into the mid-30s.”

surprises.description: The quarter had a negative 0.8% catastrophe loss ratio, better than the preview’s already-low expectation of roughly 1–3 points. The June storms did not produce the cat load that the preview’s base case allowed for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The quarter benefited from a negative 0.8% catastrophe loss ratio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cat loss ratio vs. ~1–3 pt whisper”; base case assumed a “Modest June cat load (2–4 pts).”

surprises.description: Kingstone recorded $1.6 million of favorable prior-year reserve development, rather than the adverse development the preview identified as a possible downside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$1.6 million (2.7 points) of favorable prior-year reserve development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear case included “adverse PY development” as a possible driver.

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the full-year guidance range rather than narrowing it toward the upper half, which the preview said investors were looking for. The unchanged $2.20–$2.90 EPS range also remains below the preview’s roughly $2.54 FY26 EPS consensus at its low end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance,” including “EPS of $2.20-$2.90.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirm at this point reads as conservative-to-disappointing”; the bull trigger was “guidance narrowed to the upper half ($2.55–$2.90).”

surprises.description: Management warned that the market is softening and becoming more competitive, particularly in Dwelling Fire, and expects New York growth to moderate in the second half. The preview expected continued growth and focused on whether it would remain strong, but did not anticipate this explicit market-softening warning.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged a softening, increasingly competitive market—most visible in Dwelling Fire—and expects New York growth to moderate in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said growth “continued into the second quarter” at “slightly higher” premium growth and asked whether organic growth could remain “mid-to-high-teens.”

surprises.description: Diluted book value per share was $8.69, above the preview’s estimate of current BVPS of about $7.91. That is a substantially higher reported book value than the preview carried into the release.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted book value per share rose 35% year over year to $8.69.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Current BVPS ~$7.91.”

surprises.description: The new reinsurance placement did more than the preview’s expected roughly 15% cost reduction: it cut risk-adjusted core catastrophe excess-of-loss cost by over 15%, increased total catastrophe protection to $500 million, and added wildfire coverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The July 1 reinsurance placement increased total catastrophe protection 14% to $500 million, added wildfire coverage, and cut core cat excess-of-loss risk-adjusted cost by over 15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected a “15%-cheaper reinsurance tower.”

surprises.description: Kingstone disclosed that it had repurchased about 19,500 shares at an average price of $14.98. The preview identified Q2 buyback execution as incremental and worth watching, but the disclosed purchase was modest in scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased ~19,500 shares at an average $14.98.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any buyback execution in Q2 is incremental” and asked whether any authorization had been used at prices well below $20.80.

in_line: Direct premiums written grew 19%, broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of about 20% growth.

surprises.description: i3 Verticals reported Q3 revenue of $53.1 million, below the $54.99 million consensus, with total growth of just 2% and organic revenue down 2%. The preview expected roughly 6% growth and viewed flat organic revenue as the key threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 revenue rose only 2% to $53.1 million from $51.9 million, while organic revenue declined 2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $54.99M” and “Implied Y/Y +6.0%”; the preview also said, “If organic stays at zero for a third straight quarter” it would weaken the growth narrative.

surprises.description: The company cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $216–221 million, below the prior $221–229 million range, and lowered adjusted EPS guidance to $1.08–1.12 from $1.09–1.15. This was a second revenue-guidance reduction in the fiscal year, rather than the expected reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $216-221 million and adjusted EPS to $1.08-1.12,” including “a $6.5 million revenue reduction” attributed mostly to professional services and the rest to decelerating transaction revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirm at $221–229M / $61–65M / $1.09–1.15 is the buy-side expectation”; the preview called a second outright cut “the bear trigger.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $13.3 million, well below the preview’s roughly $15.4 million model, and its 25% margin fell short of the roughly 27–28% run rate the preview said was needed. The expected margin step-up had not yet appeared in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 5% to $13.3 million with margin improving to 25% from 24.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~ $15.4M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ~28.0% (modeled)”; and “Q3 is the first quarter where that has to actually show up in reported numbers.”

surprises.description: ARR reached $174.1 million and grew 8%, below the preview’s modeled $179–182 million and 11–13% growth. That missed the preview’s roughly 10% minimum for the recurring-growth thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annualized recurring revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $174.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARR ~$179–182M (modeled),” “+11–13%,” and “below ~10% breaks the ‘recurring engine intact’ thesis.”

surprises.description: Maintenance revenue fell 13% because of the timing of SaaS conversions, a steeper current decline than the preview anticipated. Management expects the decline to normalize to about 3.5% going forward, limiting the duration of the shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Maintenance revenue dropped 13% due to timing of SaaS conversions, expected to normalize to about a 3.5% decline going forward.”

surprises.description: A $9.9 million unrealized gain on a minority equity investment was recorded in other income, an unanticipated gain that increased reported income but was not a recurring operating result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Results included a $9.9 million unrealized gain on a minority equity investment recorded in other income.”

surprises.description: High commercial-card usage drove elevated interchange rates that reduced the payments net take rate by more than $1 million. Management described it as a data issue expected to be fixed with its processor in Q4, but it was an unanticipated near-term hit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Elevated interchange rates from high commercial card usage cut over $1 million from the payments net take rate,” and management expects “to fix” the issue “with its processor in Q4.”

surprises.description: Debt was $114.3 million and cash only $2.6 million, compared with the preview’s March balance-sheet figures of $81 million of debt and $7.1 million of cash. The company also had $285.7 million of revolver capacity, below the preview’s $319 million figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Debt stood at $114.3 million with $285.7 million of remaining revolver capacity and only $2.6 million cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Debt $81M, cash $7.1M at March 31” and “$319M of revolver capacity.”

surprises.description: The company lowered FY2027 revenue growth guidance to mid-single digits from previously guided high-single-digit growth, a weaker outlook than the prior expectation embedded in its guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY2027 revenue growth guidance was lowered to mid-single digits from previously guided high single-digit growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Previously guided high single-digit growth.”

surprises.description: The share count had fallen from over 34 million to under 28 million due to buybacks, indicating repurchases had been carried out rather than merely remaining a possible capital-allocation action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Buybacks reduced adjusted weighted average shares from over 34 million to under 28 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged “both acquisitions and buybacks” and that “an announced or executed repurchase” was a key capital-allocation signal to watch.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.25, slightly above the $0.24 consensus, even though EBITDA and revenue missed expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS from continuing operations rose 8.5% to $0.25 from $0.23.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. Diluted EPS $0.24 (range $0.23–$0.24).”

surprises.description: Professional services declined by $1.8 million, a smaller drag than the preview’s expected $2–3 million year-over-year decline. The weakness was still concentrated in utilities.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue was “hurt by a $1.8 million drop in professional services concentrated in the utilities market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “budget another $2–3M y/y drag in Q3” from professional services.

in_line: SaaS revenue grew 38%, broadly matching the preview’s cited 37% growth rate and exceeding its 30% watch threshold.
Recurring sources made up 82% of quarterly revenue, consistent with the preview’s emphasis on an 80%+ recurring mix.
Adjusted EPS growth of 8.5% was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of about 4.3% growth from the prior-year quarter, although the reported $0.25 was a small beat to consensus.

surprises.description: Paymentus reported Q2 revenue of $360.7 million, above the $345.4 million consensus estimate and even above the top of its $340–350 million guidance range. The result exceeded consensus by about 4.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $360.7 million, up 28.8% year-over-year, exceeding the top end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $345.4M”; “Q2 FY2026: revenue $340–350M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $48.8 million, well above the previewed Q2 guidance range of $38–40 million. That is more than 20% above the range’s upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 54% year-over-year to $48.8 million, achieving a record margin of 41.3% and a 740 basis point improvement over the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026: … adjusted EBITDA $38–40M.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year outlook above the already-raised guidance cited in the preview, especially for adjusted EBITDA: the new midpoint is about 6.8% higher than the previous midpoint. The revenue midpoint also rose, by about 1.3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.443-1.458 billion … and adjusted EBITDA of $175-185 million (raised ~6.8% at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 (raised): revenue $1.425–1.440B; adjusted EBITDA $165–172M”; the preview also calls a raise “the likely swing factor.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS of $0.25 exceeded the preview’s cited estimates of $0.16–$0.20, including the highest estimate by $0.05. The preview did not confirm the prior-year comparison, but the call reported growth from $0.15.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income rose 66.7% to $32.4 million, or $0.25 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$0.20” (MarketBeat), “$0.18” (Investing.com), and “$0.16” (Wolfe Research).

surprises.description: Transaction growth accelerated from the prior quarter’s 17.4% year-over-year pace to 21.4%, with sequential growth of about 5%—reported as the strongest since 2019. The preview gave the Q1 comparison but no Q2 transaction estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Transactions processed grew 21.4% year-over-year to 213.4 million, with Q2 sequential transaction growth of ~5%, the strongest since 2019.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 2026 … transactions 203.4M, +17.4% y/y.”

surprises.description: Despite the stronger Q2 results, Q3 guidance implies a marked slowdown in growth from Q2: 15.2% revenue growth and 18.5% adjusted EBITDA growth at the midpoint. The preview did not provide a Q3 outlook, so this is a new, mixed signal rather than a miss against a stated estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance implies decelerating growth of 15.2% revenue and 18.5% adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint, reflecting management's disciplined, high-confidence guidance philosophy rather than a business slowdown.”

surprises.description: Contribution margin declined slightly, consistent with the preview’s warning about pressure from larger, higher-volume enterprise billers, but contribution profit per transaction improved to $0.55 from $0.53. That per-transaction improvement is a favorable detail against the preview’s broader profitability concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contribution margin declined slightly to 32.7% from 33.4% a year ago due to adding larger, higher-volume enterprise billers, though contribution profit per transaction improved to $0.55 from $0.53.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The shift toward high-volume enterprise billers has pressured profitability metrics”; the preview said to “watch adjusted EBITDA vs. the $38–40M guide.”

surprises.description: The call reported $39 million of free cash flow, $379.7 million in cash, and no debt, leaving the company positioned for potential M&A. The preview did not discuss cash generation, leverage, or M&A capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated $39 million in free cash flow, ended the quarter with $379.7 million in cash and no debt, positioning it for potential M&A.”

in_line: The slight decline in contribution margin was in line with the preview’s warning that higher-volume enterprise billers had been pressuring profitability metrics.

surprises.description: CMT’s sales fell just 1.2% year over year, far better than the preview’s implied 24.2% decline. The result reflected a sharp split: truck sales fell 23%, while sales outside truck grew 20.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 production sales declined 1.2% year-over-year,” while “excluding the truck market, sales across remaining end markets grew 20.8%.” Truck “declined 23% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus revenue of $60.05M versus $79.2M a year earlier, implying “−24.2%” year over year.

surprises.description: Management said awards secured over the prior 24 months provide a path to production revenue opportunities that could exceed $300 million in 2027. The preview discussed the $63 million of 2025 awards and a longer-term $500 million revenue goal, but did not flag this nearer-term opportunity estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over $112 million in new business awards secured over 24 months provide line of sight to production revenue opportunities that could exceed $300 million in 2027.”

surprises.description: CMT ended the quarter with no debt and then expanded its credit facility to $100 million, maturing in 2031. The preview had cited $19.3 million of term debt and did not anticipate the debt-free position or larger facility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $12.1 million in cash and no debt,” and “in July expanded its credit facility to $100 million maturing in 2031.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 liquidity of $73.5 million and “term debt $19.3M.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2026 sales guidance of flat to up approximately 5%, consistent with the preview’s stated standing guidance.
Diluted EPS of $0.21 matched the preview’s $0.21 consensus estimate.
Gross margin was 20.3% (19.4% excluding the customer capacity charge), broadly sustaining the elevated level the preview had already flagged after Q1 gross margin of 20.4%.

The preview expected succession and Mexico-expansion costs to continue affecting the GAAP-versus-adjusted gap; the call cited $1.8 million of Mexico expansion and succession-related costs in elevated SG&A.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case expected tariff refunds to remain excluded or pending, although it identified recognition as a major upside possibility. Karat instead recognized and quantified a $25.8 million refund, adding about $1.00 per diluted share and driving reported gross margin to 56.6%; the refund was within the preview’s estimated claim range, but its recognition was not the base-case expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “1,890 basis points came from a one-time IEPA tariff refund of $25.8 million”; the refund “contributed $1.00 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “refund still ‘excluded/pending’”; it estimated a possible claim of “$20–28M” and said recognition was the “single biggest swing factor.”

surprises.description: Excluding the refund, gross margin was about 37.7%, above the preview’s roughly 36% consensus and the 35–37% company guidance range. That indicates underlying margin performance was modestly better than expected, apart from the one-time refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: Reported gross margin was 56.6%, with the refund contributing 1,890 basis points, “implying an underlying gross margin of roughly 37.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Gross margin ~36%” consensus and company guidance of “35–37%.”

surprises.description: Online sales grew 23.6%, and July growth accelerated to more than 37%, with Amazon up 49%. The preview said the channel needed a sharp acceleration to support the $100 million target; these reported growth rates show stronger momentum than the preview had quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Online sales grew 23.6% year-over-year and accelerated further into Q3, with July online growth exceeding 37% and Amazon sales up 49%,” keeping Karat on track for its “$100 million online revenue target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “>$100M” FY26 target “requires a sharp acceleration,” noting Q1 online growth of 9.8%, March growth of 19%, and double-digit growth in April.

surprises.description: Operating expenses rose by $7.0 million year over year, including $3.1 million of higher shipping costs tied to peak fuel prices. The preview did not flag this cost pressure; management expects some relief in Q3 as diesel prices fall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses rose to $39.6 million from $32.6 million,” including “$3.1 million higher shipping costs” amid diesel at $5.40 per gallon; management expects diesel to fall to around $4.25 in Q3.

surprises.description: The share of eco-friendly products increased to 33.8% of sales, supported by expanded paper-category SKUs. The preview did not identify this product-mix development as an expectation or debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Eco-friendly products rose to 33.8% of total sales, up from 31.8% in the prior year period, supported by SKU expansion in paper categories.”

surprises.description: Karat repurchased $2 million of shares during the quarter, an additional form of shareholder return not discussed in the preview. The preview had discussed the recently raised dividend, but not buyback activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased 73,510 shares for $2 million with about $10 million remaining under its buyback program.”

in_line: Net sales of $136.3 million, up 9.9% year over year, were close to the preview’s approximately $135.5 million consensus and its expected roughly 9% growth.
Core EPS of about $0.46–$0.48, excluding the tariff refund, was broadly in line with the preview’s $0.48 consensus.
The $0.47 quarterly dividend had already been announced before the release; the preview specifically noted the recent increase from $0.45.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.16, a penny below the preview’s $0.17 primary consensus, though within its $0.16–$0.18 base scenario and above the roughly $0.15 whisper estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated adjusted EPS came in at $0.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (Q2'26) | Consensus | $0.17”; the base scenario expected “$0.16–0.18,” and the whisper was “~$0.15.”

surprises.description: The IURC declined certain gas modernization tracker recovery, a regulatory setback the preview did not flag. Management said it would seek recovery through other mechanisms, with no change to the CapEx plan or EPS outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The IURC issued an order today declining certain gas modernization tracker recovery,” prompting NiSource to pursue recovery through the FMCA, other trackers, or rate cases; management said there was “no change to CapEx plans or EPS outlook.”

surprises.description: Storm activity and union-negotiation expenses pressured O&M, contrary to the preview’s stated expectation that management had committed to flat O&M. The preview did identify weather and O&M as items to watch, but the call reported actual pressure from both.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Higher-than-usual storm activity from a record number of tornadoes and elevated expenses tied to ongoing union negotiations pressured O&M,” partly offsetting benefits from new rates.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has committed to flat O&M through the plan.”

surprises.description: NiSource identified more than $40 million of 2026 cost-optimization initiatives, with benefits expected to continue improving the cost structure beyond 2026—an additional cost-control opportunity not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management identified over $40 million of cost optimization initiatives for 2026 that are expected to continue improving the cost structure beyond 2026.”

surprises.description: The Amazon and Alphabet agreements are expected to produce about $1.4 billion in bill reductions for existing NIPSCO electric customers, with savings beginning as early as Q4 2026. The preview discussed agreement review and data-center execution but did not flag these customer bill reductions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Amazon and Alphabet data center agreements are expected to deliver approximately $1.4 billion in bill reductions for existing NIPSCO electric customers, or up to $124 annually per residential customer, beginning as early as Q4 2026.”

surprises.description: NiSource disclosed a 9 GW data-center pipeline and said it was exploring expansion beyond that level. The preview focused on whether signed capacity would rise above roughly 4 GW; the reported signed amount remained 4 GW, but the broader pipeline and potential to expand beyond 9 GW were not anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The data center pipeline stands at 9 gigawatts, including 4 GW signed, 3 GW in active strategic negotiations, and about 2 GW of additional potential customers, with the company exploring expansion beyond 9 GW.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “total signed capacity moves above the ~4 GW disclosed at Q1” and flagged the GenCo pipeline as a metric to watch.

in_line: NiSource reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.02–$2.07, as the preview’s base case expected; management also said earnings would be weighted toward the second half, consistent with the preview’s expected back-half ramp.
The company reaffirmed its 6%–8% base-plan EPS growth through 2030 and 9%–10% adjusted EPS CAGR through 2033, matching the long-term outlook the preview expected to remain unchanged.
The five-year capital plan remained at $21 billion of base investment, $2 billion of upside opportunities, and $7.6 billion of GenCo capital, consistent with the preview’s stated plan.
The pipeline remained at 4 GW signed, in line with the preview’s roughly 4 GW reference; the preview’s potential trigger of signed capacity moving above that level did not occur.
The July 17 amendment increasing Amazon contracted load by 400 MW was already embedded in guidance, consistent with the preview’s focus on the Amazon expansion.

surprises.description: ANI lowered its full-year Cortrophin Gel outlook to $520–540 million, roughly $30 million below prior expectations. The revised range still implies 50–55% growth over 2025, but is below the preview’s $540–575 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management modestly lowered full-year Cortrophin Gel revenue guidance to $520-540 million from prior expectations (implying roughly a $30 million cut).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 Cortrophin (guide) $540–575M”; the preview also says “Any trim to the Cortrophin range” is a bear trigger.

surprises.description: The implied near-term Cortrophin ramp was slower than the preview’s roughly $175 million-per-quarter H2 expectation: Q3 guidance is $143–153 million, with management expecting a significantly larger step-up only in Q4. This shifts more of the ramp later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 Cortrophin revenue is guided to $143-153 million, with management expecting a significantly larger step-up in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said H2 would be “roughly $345–380M…or ~$175M per quarter versus ~$120M in Q2” and described “a ~45%+ sequential step-up in Q3, held in Q4.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was well above the preview’s expected $62–65 million, reaching $71.6 million. The preview anticipated a clean quarter around $63 million; the call also noted that Q2 included an $8 million Harmony milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA growing 32% to an all-time high of $71.6 million”; Q3 guidance notes “only $2 million remaining Harmony milestone (vs. $8 million in Q2).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $62–65M”; the preview also said “a clean ~$63M confirms underlying operating leverage.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was higher than the preview’s roughly 60–61% expectation, at 62.6%, despite declining year over year on product mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin declined about 230 basis points year-over-year to 62.6% due to product mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Non-GAAP gross margin ~60–61%” and warned that a clean Q2 margin below ~60% would indicate faster mix deterioration.

surprises.description: The call disclosed $17.7 million of Q2 revenue from the Harmony licensing deal, whereas the preview assumed the Q1 Harmony upfront payment would not recur and modeled only $7 million for royalties and other revenue. This was an unexpected source of Q2 revenue, though the preview recognized the prior upfront payment as nonrecurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Harmony licensing deal contributed $17.7 million in Q2 revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Royalties / Other $7M” and stated “Q1's $21.5M included $15M Harmony upfront — does not repeat.”

surprises.description: The gout launch showed specific early case-generation indicators, rather than only the deployment and qualitative progress the preview was waiting to assess: more than 95% of new reps generated multiple new cases, and over one-third of prescribers started at least two patient cases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 95% of new reps generating multiple new cases and over one-third of prescribers initiating two or more patient cases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “new prescriber breadth” and “whether any gout-driven scripts actually showed up in June,” while noting that the real impact was expected in 2027.

surprises.description: ANI explicitly expects Q3 adjusted EBITDA to decline sequentially, due to a smaller Harmony milestone and the first fully loaded quarter of gout expansion costs. That adds a near-term earnings headwind to the back-half ramp discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA is expected to decline sequentially due to only $2 million remaining Harmony milestone (vs. $8 million in Q2) and the first fully loaded quarter of gout expansion operating expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “55–58% of the year's earnings must land in H2” and framed the H2 hockey stick as “the entire story.”

surprises.description: Total Q2 revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s anchored consensus, reaching $266 million versus $262.7 million. The gap was small, and another aggregator cited in the preview had an estimate as high as about $269 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 total net revenues of $266 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total net revenue | Q2 2026 Consensus | $262.7M”; the preview noted other aggregators showed revenue “as high as ~$269M.”

in_line: Q2 Cortrophin Gel revenue was $117.1 million, close to the preview’s $120 million model and within its cited $113–132 million implied range.
Generics revenue of $99.1 million was close to the preview’s $100 million model; 12 launches in 2026 were consistent with the preview’s 10–15 full-year target.
Full-year company guidance was reaffirmed at $1.08–1.14 billion revenue and $9.19–9.69 EPS, matching the ranges in the preview.
The gout sales-force deployment was fully operational by the end of June, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Assurant reported Q2 adjusted EPS growth of 19% excluding catastrophes, reversing the preview’s expected 7.1% year-over-year decline; adjusted EBITDA also grew 18% excluding cats.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA grew 18% and adjusted EPS grew 19%, both excluding catastrophes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (ex-cat) $5.16” versus “$5.56” a year earlier, or “–7.1%.”

surprises.description: Assurant raised its full-year outlook from low-single-digit to mid-single-digit growth in adjusted EBITDA and EPS excluding cats, with underlying growth around 10%. The preview expected low-single-digit reported growth and cited a $94 million reserve-development headwind; the call put the lower favorable-development amount at $71 million.
