surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 outlook,” now expecting “mid-single-digit growth” in adjusted EBITDA and EPS excluding cats, or “approximately 10% underlying growth” excluding “$71 million of lower favorable prior year reserve development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Current: adj. EBITDA and adj. EPS ex-cat both low-single-digit growth (high-single-digit underlying).” The preview also cited a “$94M headwind from reduced prior-year development.”

surprises.description: Global Lifestyle adjusted EBITDA rose 21%, well above the preview’s implied growth of roughly 7%–12% from its $215–225 million estimate versus $201.4 million a year earlier. Connected Living grew 29%, or 22% excluding approximately $10 million of non-run-rate benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global Lifestyle adjusted EBITDA rose 21% ($43 million), with Connected Living EBITDA up 29% ($39 million), though normalized growth was 22% after excluding ~$10 million of non-run-rate benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Global Lifestyle adj. EBITDA (est. ~$215–225M vs. $201.4M LY).”

surprises.description: Global Housing adjusted EBITDA excluding catastrophes grew 18% to $287 million, rather than declining as the preview’s estimate implied. The favorable non-cat loss ratio and lower cat reinsurance costs helped the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global Housing Q2 adjusted EBITDA excluding cats grew 18% ($43 million) to $287 million,” aided by “a favorable non-cat loss ratio of ~35%” and lower cat reinsurance costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Global Housing adj. EBITDA ex-cat and the development disclosure (est. ~$205–215M vs. $244.2M LY).” The preview described a likely “Housing down ~13–16%” in its base case.

surprises.description: The full-year Global Housing outlook moved from an expected modest decline in adjusted EBITDA excluding cats to modest growth, a favorable change in the segment’s direction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year segment guidance was raised to … modest growth for Global Housing excluding cats.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Global Housing modest ex-cat decline.”

surprises.description: Assurant won a new lender-placed insurance partnership with Freedom Mortgage, a top 10 servicer covering approximately 2.6 million loans, with the program expected to ramp over the next 12 months. The preview did not identify this prospective partnership.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Assurant won a new lender-placed insurance partnership with Freedom Mortgage, a top 10 U.S. mortgage servicer with approximately 2.6 million loans that will ramp over the next 12 months.”

in_line: The full-year repurchase target was raised to the upper end of the $300–350 million range, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Assurant would target the upper end.

Lender-placed placement-rate movement was described as tied to a client’s loan transfer: the rate was flat year over year but down sequentially. The preview had flagged quarterly fluctuations from client loan movements as something to monitor.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue reached $373.9 million, above the $360.6 million consensus and the previous $350–370 million guidance range. The roughly 3.7% beat to consensus also exceeded the preview’s modeled Q4 revenue of about $360 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue grew 43% year-over-year to $373.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $350–370M | Consensus $360.6M”; the preview’s FY2026 setup also modeled Q4 revenue at “$360M.”

surprises.description: Home Services reached $141.6 million, well above the preview’s $120 million watch level and its $130 million bull-case threshold. Its 88% growth rate also surpassed the 63% growth reported in Q3, rather than merely continuing the prior trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The home services vertical was 38% of Q4 revenue, growing 88% to a record $141.6 million, now running well over $500 million per year in revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether Q4 HS clears ~$120M”; the bull scenario called for “Home Services >$130M.” Q3 Home Services was reported at “+63% YoY.”

surprises.description: FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $150–160 million is above the preview’s $135–150 million buy-side anchor and above its $135–145 million base scenario. Revenue guidance, by contrast, matched the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full fiscal year 2027 guidance is revenue of $1.45–1.55 billion (16% growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $150–160 million (38% growth, 10.3% margin, 160 bps expansion).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side is anchoring to ~$1.45–1.55B revenue and $135–150M EBITDA”; the base scenario expected “$135–145M EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Financial Services remained at a record level sequentially, while auto insurance growth accelerated from the 27% reported in Q3 to 37%. That was a stronger result than the preview’s concerns about carrier-spend durability and difficult comparisons suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The financial services vertical was 62% of Q4 revenue, growing 24% to a record $232.3 million, with auto insurance up 37% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q3 auto insurance was “+27% YoY” and warned that “2025’s ad-spend surge” created “brutal FY27 comps” and that carrier budgets were a key risk.

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $41.4 million, modestly above the roughly $40 million consensus, although it remained within the prior $37–43 million guidance range and the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA rose 87% year-over-year to $41.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | $37–43M | ~$40M (mid).” The base scenario expected “$39–41M.”

surprises.description: FY2026 results finished slightly above the preview’s midpoint-based estimates: revenue was about $1.3 billion versus roughly $1.28 billion modeled, and adjusted EBITDA was $112.5 million versus roughly $111 million estimated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full fiscal year 2026 revenue grew 18% to $1.3 billion, while adjusted EBITDA grew 38% to $112.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated FY2026 at “~$1.28B revenue (+17%) and ~$111M adj. EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects to close at least one, and possibly two, smaller accretive acquisitions before year-end. The preview identified a tuck-in as a possible positive catalyst, but the stated expectation of one or two deals gives that possibility greater specificity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to close at least one, possibly two, smaller accretive acquisitions before the end of the calendar year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “another tuck-in” as a possible positive surprise under capital allocation.

surprises.description: The company disclosed substantial repurchases—$14.6 million in Q4 and $31.4 million for the year—rather than merely the possible buyback authorization the preview flagged as a catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $14.6 million of shares in Q4 and $31.4 million for the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s capital-allocation checklist said “Buyback authorization or another tuck-in would be a positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Management estimated carriers are only about 20% through shifting toward digital and performance marketing, offering a longer runway than the preview’s focus on near-term carrier-budget durability and difficult spending comparisons anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “estimates carriers are only about 20% through the shift toward digital and performance marketing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted carrier-spend durability as a key risk, citing “brutal FY27 comps,” and focused its digital-marketing discussion on AI monetization rather than the extent of carriers’ shift to digital and performance marketing.

in_line: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.1%, within the preview’s expected 10.6%–11.6% guidance range and its 10.8%–11.2% base-case range; the preview had also flagged a margin of at least 10.6% as the key threshold.
FY2027 revenue guidance of $1.45–1.55 billion matched the preview’s buy-side anchor, and its 16% growth outlook was within the preview’s expected 15%–18% range.

surprises.description: LP's adjusted EPS was $0.40, well below the preview's $0.58 consensus, and EBITDA of $79 million was also far below the roughly $98–100 million implied consolidated estimate. The earnings shortfall was larger than the modest revenue miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: LP reported adjusted EPS of $0.40; EBITDA declined $63 million year over year to $79 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $0.58” consensus; “Implied consolidated Adj. EBITDA ~ $98–100M.”

surprises.description: Net sales were $664 million, below the preview's $674 million consensus. The gap was small in percentage terms, but the reported quarter did not reach the expected revenue level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales fell $90 million year-over-year to $664 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $674M (Aug 3).”

surprises.description: Siding sales rose 4% year over year, contrary to the preview's expectation of a decline based on $440.9 million consensus sales versus $460 million a year earlier. However, volume fell 11%, a little worse than the preview's cited 10% decline expectation, while 7% higher prices supported sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Siding sales rose 4% year-over-year as 7% higher prices partially offset an 11% volume decline against last year's all-time record quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Siding net sales $440.9M” versus “Q2'25 Actual $460M”; management had guided Q2 volume to “-10% YoY.”

surprises.description: Siding EBITDA appears to have fallen short of the top end of guidance and the preview's near-ceiling consensus expectation because of weather disruptions in Manitoba and equipment downtime at Dawson Creek. Management said that without those issues, EBITDA would have been at or above the top of guidance, so it characterized the shortfall as largely timing-related.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Absent unexpected weather-related disruptions in Manitoba and equipment downtime at Dawson Creek, Siding EBITDA would have been at or above the top end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Siding EBITDA guidance was “$115–120M”; consensus was “$119.5M,” described as sitting “at the top of the guide.”

surprises.description: The OSB outlook was materially weaker than the preview's setup, which saw a chance of OSB outperforming its Q2 loss guide and noted the guide assumed prices unchanged from May 1. LP now expects a $45 million OSB EBITDA loss in Q3 and a $120 million loss for the full year, after prices fell roughly 6% since the May call.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OSB EBITDA is guided to approximately negative $45 million in Q3 and negative $120 million for the full year, with prices having fallen roughly $12 (6%) since the May call.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “OSB EBITDA and the pricing assumption reset” were key to watch, noted guidance was based on prices “unchanged from May 1, 2026,” and described OSB as “the most likely source of an upside surprise.”

surprises.description: LP expects Siding to return to year-over-year revenue and volume growth in Q3, a more concrete and favorable inflection than the preview's expectation of gradual sequential improvement through year-end. The Q3 revenue range starts at a level that ties the prior record quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Siding is expected to return to year-over-year revenue and volume growth in Q3,” with revenue of “$460–470 million (low end tying the prior record)” and EBITDA of “$110–120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had promised “gradual sequential improvements through year-end” and identified Q2 as the first checkpoint for a Siding volume inflection.

surprises.description: LP cut full-year CapEx by $70 million rather than holding the roughly $390 million program the preview used in its base case. The reduction comes mainly from delaying non-essential OSB maintenance, while Siding still accounts for most spending and essentially all growth CapEx.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx guidance was cut by $70 million to about $320 million, primarily by delaying non-essential OSB maintenance projects, with Siding accounting for roughly three-quarters of spend and essentially all growth CapEx.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described FY26 CapEx of “~$390M” and its base case said “capex held”; it flagged a capex trim as something to watch.

surprises.description: LP generated $140 million of operating cash flow in Q2, a strong reversal from the negative $38 million reported in Q1 and better than the preview's cash-flow framing of a roughly zero-to-negative FCF year. The company attributed the quarter's cash generation partly to seasonal working capital, so it does not by itself establish a sustained improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: LP “generated $140 million in operating cash flow aided by seasonal working capital” and ended with “just under $1 billion in liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 operating cash flow of “-$38M” and characterized FY26 CapEx against EBITDA as “roughly a zero-to-negative FCF year.”

surprises.description: LP announced that CFO Alan Haughie will retire on September 1, with Aaron Howald succeeding him. The preview discussed Haughie's Q1 commentary but did not flag an impending CFO transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Alan Haughie will retire September 1 after nearly 7 years, with Aaron Howald succeeding him as CFO.”

in_line: Siding's 26% EBITDA margin was in line with the preview's expectation of roughly 26%.

surprises.description: KIDS reported $70.5 million of Q2 revenue, above the preview’s more likely $68.5 million buy-side bar and its $68.5 million base case. The result was within the preview’s $70–71 million bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 15% year-over-year to a record $70.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$68.5M as the more likely buy-side bar”; base case: “$68.5M”

surprises.description: Trauma and deformity revenue reached $52.6 million, well above the preview’s modeled roughly $47.3 million, with growth of 26% versus the preview’s expectation of a modest increase on an easy comparison. Early 3P HIP contributions and pull-through of legacy products helped drive the outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trauma and deformity revenue grew 26% to $52.6 million, aided by early 3P HIP contributions and pull-through of legacy products toward single-source contracts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “T&D ~$47.3M”; the preview also said T&D “faces an easy comp.”

surprises.description: Scoliosis revenue fell 9% to $16.9 million, sharply below the preview’s roughly $20.2 million base case and expectation of normal 5–10% growth despite the tough comparison. Zero 7D unit sales and lower Brazil set sales drove the decline, although underlying implant sales grew at a mid-teens rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scoliosis revenue declined 9% to $16.9 million due to zero 7D unit sales (versus ~$2 million a year ago) and lower Brazil set sales, though underlying implant sales grew mid-teens.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “Scoliosis ~$20.2M”; “Anything in the +5–10% range is normal comp math, not deceleration.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 74%, above the preview’s modeled 72–73% range. Management attributed the expansion to favorable mix, while indicating the full-year margin should be around 73% as some 7D sales resume in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 74% from 72% a year earlier, aided by favorable mix, though management expects roughly 73% for the full year as some 7D sales resume in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~72–73% (no formal consensus)”

surprises.description: VertiGlide had 124 surgeons trained, exceeding the preview’s approximate 80-surgeon marker. The preview had identified the Q2 launch and surgeon count as a key ramp check, but the actual count was substantially higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “VertiGlide now has 124 surgeons trained.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Vertiglyde to full market release in Q2 with increased set deployment (~80 surgeons trained).”

surprises.description: Despite the expanded VertiGlide rollout, Q2 set deployments were only $2.9 million, down from $4.6 million a year earlier. That contrasts with the preview’s expectation of increased set deployment, although management still expected to deploy about $5 million more, mostly in Q3, toward the roughly $10 million full-year plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Set deployments were only $2.9 million (down from $4.6 million), with about $5 million of the planned $10 million full-year set deployment remaining, mostly in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Vertiglyde to full market release in Q2 with increased set deployment”; company guidance included “set deployment ~$10M.”

surprises.description: Q2 free-cash-flow usage was $3.1 million, somewhat worse than the preview’s expected range of breakeven to a $2 million use. Management remained confident in positive free cash flow in the second half and breakeven or better for the full year, as the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow usage improved 78% ($10.8 million) to $3.1 million used, with management confident in achieving positive free cash flow in the second half and break-even or better for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 at breakeven-to-$(2)M keeps the story credible”; “FY breakeven requires roughly a $5–7M positive H2.”

surprises.description: DF2 had been adopted by more than 150 of roughly 300 U.S. children’s hospitals, with high margins and no inventory requirement. The preview flagged specialty-bracing growth but did not anticipate this specific scale of hospital adoption or the stated economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DF2 now adopted in over 150 of roughly 300 U.S. children's hospitals at high margins with no inventory requirement.”

in_line: Full-year revenue guidance was raised by $2 million to $265–269 million, in line with the preview’s expectation of a raise into roughly the $265–268 million range and its emphasis on lifting the low end to at least $265 million.
The roughly $25 million full-year adjusted EBITDA target was reiterated, as expected; Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $6.8 million was also above the preview’s modeled $5.5–6.5 million range.
Specialty bracing grew over 20%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of OPSB growth above 20%.
International revenue growth of 22% was broadly consistent with the preview’s cited 22% Q1 growth rate and its $15.5 million Q2 base-case estimate; Q2 revenue was $15.7 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $34 million, below the preview’s derived $38–42 million estimate. The preview noted that the revenue proxy was uncertain, but the reported result still fell short of its range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $34 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Derived street proxy ~$38–42M (mid ~$40M)”

surprises.description: Battery resale revenue was only $300,000, far below the preview’s $2–5 million base-case expectation and its watch for any Q2 sales. Management also said resales were trending toward the low end of the up-to-$40 million annual range and remained weighted to the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Battery hardware resale revenue is expected to trend toward the lower end of the up-to-$40 million range and is weighted to the second half”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … battery $2–5M”; “Any battery resale dollars vs $0”; “Any dollars booked in Q2 de-risk the $190M high end”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $6 million, well above the preview’s $2.5–3.5 million base-case range and the $2.7–4.3 million quarterly pace it said was needed for the annual target. The company said it was tracking toward the high end of full-year guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “positive adjusted EBITDA at $6 million (18% margin), up 63% year-over-year and more than double Q1 2026's level”; full-year adjusted EBITDA was “tracking toward the high end”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … adj. EBITDA $2.5–3.5M”; “adj. EBITDA cadence (needs ~$2.7–4.3M/qtr to hit $10–15M FY)”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin reached 55%, above the preview’s cited 52% Q1 record and the 40–50% full-year guidance range. The call also cautioned that second-half resale deals, with roughly 10–11% margins, would pressure margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin reached a record 55% (up from 49% in Q2 2025)”; battery resale deals “carry only ~10-11% margins” and “will pressure back-half margins”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “record 52% non-GAAP gross margin in Q1”; “non-GAAP GM 40–50%”; “Watch whether 52% non-GAAP GM holds as lower-margin battery resale returns”

surprises.description: Core revenue was $33 million, just below the preview’s $34 million track line for software, services, and edge hardware. It was nevertheless up 1% year over year, with PowerTrack revenue up 11% and edge hardware up 22%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding battery hardware resales, revenue from software, services, and edge hardware was $33 million, up 1% year-over-year”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Track line: ≥$34M” for core revenue

surprises.description: The company reaffirmed the full $140–190 million revenue range rather than narrowing it toward the low end, as the preview’s base case anticipated. This was despite the weaker resale outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $140-$190 million total revenue”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … guidance ‘reaffirmed’ but total-revenue range narrowed toward the low end”; “a narrow toward the low end is likely”

surprises.description: Bookings rose to $37 million, above the preview’s Q1 reference point of $26.5 million and even Q4’s $32.7 million; contracted backlog also increased to $27 million. That was stronger than the preview’s concern about whether utility-scale booking momentum had held.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bookings were $37 million in Q2, up 39% sequentially and 7% year-over-year, with contracted backlog rising 18% sequentially to $27 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bookings $26.5M (from $32.7M in Q4, seasonal); backlog $23.0M”; “Watch whether utility-scale PowerTrack EMS bookings momentum held”

surprises.description: Total ARR reached $62.4 million, below the preview’s $63 million Q2 track line. PowerTrack ARR grew, but managed-services ARR was roughly flat, leaving the total short of the preview’s indicated pace toward year-end guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “total ARR reached $62.4 million against year-end guidance of $65-$70 million”; “managed services ARR was roughly flat at $19.6 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Track line: ARR ≥$63M”; “Hitting $65–70M by year-end needs ~$1.3–2.9M of net adds per quarter”

surprises.description: Stem disclosed that it raised approximately $6 million through its ATM equity program at an average price of about $9.75. The preview discussed liquidity and cash risks but did not anticipate an equity raise; the proceeds support cash while the issuance dilutes shareholders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raised approximately $6 million via its ATM equity program at an average price of ~$9.75”

surprises.description: The call cited a new 420-MWh Chile project and a Hungary hybridization booking, and said PowerTrack EMS had expanded to six countries and three continents. The preview did not flag these specific international wins or expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “expanded PowerTrack EMS to six countries and three continents including a new 420-MWh Chile project and a Hungary hybridization booking”

in_line: Operating cash flow was positive $300,000, essentially at the preview’s base-case expectation of breakeven to a modest outflow.
The company retained its $0–10 million full-year operating-cash-flow guidance, consistent with the preview’s stated guidance range.

surprises.description: The preview said investors were looking for FY2026 revenue guidance of about $61–62 million, but Apyx reaffirmed its $59–60 million range. That leaves the expected post-Q2 guidance increase unrealized.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $59.0 million to $60.0 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus positioning is for a raise to ~$61–62M”; “anything below $61M at the low end disappoints.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $13.9 million exceeded the $13.18 million consensus estimate, although it landed within the preview’s $13.8–14.0 million whisper range. The beat versus published consensus was therefore positive but modest relative to the market’s higher bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 22% year-over-year to $13.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue $13.18M”; the preview also says the buy-side whisper was “closer to $13.8–14.0M.”

surprises.description: Surgical Aesthetics revenue was $12.4 million, above the preview’s roughly $11.7 million estimate, and grew 28% versus an estimated growth rate of about 21%. This was a stronger segment result than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Surgical Aesthetics sales [increased] 28% to $12.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Surgical Aesthetics rev ~$11.7M (est.)” and “~+21%.”

surprises.description: Apyx gave a more concrete and accelerated power-liposuction commercialization update than the preview’s limited-launch framing: initial shipments had begun in June, a full launch was expected in Q3, and management expects more than 95% of new AYON purchasers to include the feature. The expected handpiece replacements and per-case supplies also point to recurring revenue potential not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Began initial commercial shipments in June 2026, with a full commercial launch expected in Q3 2026”; “north of 95% of new AYON purchasers to include power liposuction,” with reusable handpieces replaced “2-4 times per year” and “roughly $100 of tubing and canisters per case.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “limited launch with early adopters” and said “any quantified ASP uplift, attach rate, or a decision to move to full launch in H2 is incremental to guidance.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 63.9%, above the preview’s expected 62–63% range and the upper end of company guidance. That was better than expected despite the preview’s concern that international mix and tariffs could pressure margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 63.9% from 62.3% year-over-year on favorable segment mix,” partially offset by tariffs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~62–63% (guide)” and “Gross margin ≥62%.”

surprises.description: The preview cited the prior quarter’s $0.6 million operating cash use and asked whether cash burn would remain low; Q2 operating cash burn was $3.5 million. That was a sharp increase versus the cited Q1 level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash burn increased to $3.5 million versus $1.2 million in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 operating cash use was “$0.6M” and flagged “Opex trajectory and cash burn” as a key issue to ask about.

surprises.description: Management said the company expects to maintain sufficient liquidity into 2028, extending the runway beyond the preview’s expectation that it was funded through 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 2026 with $27.6 million in cash and expects to maintain sufficient liquidity into 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said cash was “funded ‘through 2027.’”

surprises.description: OEM revenue was $1.5 million, slightly above the preview’s roughly $1.4 million estimate, and its 12% year-over-year decline was less steep than the estimated decline of about 18%. The annual OEM outlook remained roughly in line with the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The OEM segment declined 12% to $1.5 million” and is guided to fall to roughly $5.0 million for 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “OEM rev ~$1.4M (est.)” and “~(18)%”; the preview also listed FY2026 OEM at “~$5M.”

surprises.description: Apyx reported that AYON is attracting customers who have never used Renuvion, a positive sign of customer expansion beyond the existing-user base emphasized in the preview. The call did not quantify the share of new customers, so the extent of that shift remains unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AYON is attracting new customers who have never used Renuvion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “~80% of AYON units went to existing Renuvion customers” and described a shift toward new or greenfield accounts as “the bullish tell.”

in_line: Q2 diluted loss per share was $0.07, within the preview’s estimated loss range of $0.06–$0.08.
The company maintained its FY2026 gross-margin guidance of 62–63% and operating-expense cap of $45 million, consistent with the preview’s stated guidance.
The roughly $5 million FY2026 OEM outlook was consistent with the preview.

surprises.description: TPL reported revenue of about $246 million, below the preview’s $249.5 million consensus and well below its $265 million base estimate, despite record quarterly revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly total revenue of ~$246 million,” up 4% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus Q2'26: “$249.5M”; “My Base Est.”: “$265M.”

surprises.description: Oil and gas royalty production reached about 39,700 boe/d, above the preview’s roughly 38,000 boe/d estimate and stronger than its base case of flat-to-modestly higher volumes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oil and gas royalty production hit a record ~39,700 boe/d, up 7% sequentially and 20% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Royalty production” “My Base Est.”: “~38.0 MBoe/d”; the base scenario anticipated “volumes flat-to-up modestly.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was about $216 million with an 88% margin, beating the preview’s roughly $207 million estimate and substantially exceeding its assumed 78% margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $216 million (up 19% sequentially, 30% YoY) with an 88% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” “My Base Est.”: “~$207M (78% mgn).”

surprises.description: Water sales fell sharply sequentially rather than holding near the prior quarter’s strong level; management attributed the drop to weak in-basin gas prices shifting development away from the Delaware Basin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water sales volumes declined 19% sequentially to 663,000 barrels per day due to weak in-basin gas prices shifting development away from the Delaware Basin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 had “the second-best water sales and produced water royalty volumes in company history” and urged investors to judge the segment on “three-quarter trends, not single quarters.”

surprises.description: Surface Land Easements & Materials revenue reached $24 million, above the preview’s $18 million base estimate, although the preview had flagged this line as lumpy and did not expect it to be a reliable trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Surface Land Easements & Materials revenue rose 37% sequentially to $24 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base-case build estimated “easements/other surface (SLEM) $18M.”

surprises.description: Rather than only offering general pipeline commentary, management said it was in advanced conversations covering 25 gigawatts of projects and expected at least one major definitive agreement soon. No definitive agreement was reported as signed on the call.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In advanced conversations with multiple hyperscalers, AI labs, and power generators on 25 gigawatts of projects” and “expects to announce at least one major definitive agreement in the near term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “no new deal, but constructive pipeline commentary”; it described deal #3 as the market’s need and the bull case as requiring “a signed deal.”

surprises.description: TPL disclosed a roughly $100 million acquisition of more than 10,000 acres in Shackelford and Jones County, extending its data-center and power strategy beyond the Permian Basin—an investment and geographic expansion the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired over 10,000 acres in Shackelford and Jones County for ~$100 million, expanding its data center and power strategy beyond the Permian Basin.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that it is prioritizing cash accumulation for M&A, land, power, and desal investments over share buybacks, indicating a stronger preference for funding growth investments than the preview had discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is prioritizing cash build for M&A, land, power, and desal investments over share buybacks.”

surprises.description: The call connected the previously announced land sale and water agreement to Chevron’s Project Kilby, but the preview had specifically looked for the deal’s consideration, acreage, and water volumes to be quantified; those terms are not included in the supplied call facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company revealed its previously announced land sale and water agreement is tied to Chevron's Project Kilby,” described as “a multi-gigawatt power and data center development in Reeves County, Texas.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Quantification on the call is the highest-value disclosure available”; the preview said “Chevron consideration, acreage, and water volumes were all undisclosed.”

in_line: Free cash flow was about $156 million, close to the preview’s roughly $158 million estimate.

surprises.description: The preview expected reported GAAP EPS near a loss of $0.45–$0.50 because of the pre-flagged stock-compensation charge. NRXS reported a loss of just $0.19 per share, although that was slightly worse than the cited $0.16 loss consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $2.1 million from $1.7 million a year earlier, though EPS improved to a loss of $0.19 from $0.22.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS should land near −$0.45 to −$0.50 against a −$0.16 consensus.”

surprises.description: The preview expected prior-authorization approval of roughly 35–40% in its base case and identified a rate flat near 32% as a warning sign. NRXS reported 31% year-to-date, slightly below the prior 32% Q1 level and below the base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Internal prior authorization approval rate jumped to 31% year-to-date in 2026 versus 12% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: Prior-auth ~35–40%”; “flat at ~32% is a yellow flag.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for ASP around $1,050 in its base case and highlighted more than $1,050 as a key threshold. Q2 ASP was $992, below that expectation, despite rising 28% year over year as the mix shifted toward full-reimbursement payers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IB-Stim average selling price rose 28% to $992 per device in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … ASP ~$1,050”; “Watch for ASP >$1,050.”

surprises.description: The preview expected burn of about $1 million per quarter or less for the rest of 2026. Q2 burn was about $1.1 million, and management said it expects burn to rise in the second half as hiring accelerates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarterly burn improving to about $1.1 million from $1.5 million in 2025, though management expects burn to rise in the second half due to accelerated hiring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CFO Tim Henrichs guided to ~$1M/quarter burn or less for the balance of 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview said the story had shifted from covered lives to claims paid and treated incremental coverage announcements as noise absent a top-five national payer. NRXS reported meaningful direct-conversation progress with two of its largest remaining uncovered commercial payers, with coverage potentially arriving in the second half of 2026 or early 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Meaningful direct-conversation progress with two of its largest remaining uncovered commercial payers, with coverage possibly landing in the second half of 2026 or early 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The story has shifted from ‘lives covered’ to ‘claims paid.’ Treat new-lives headlines as noise unless they name a top-5 national payer.”

surprises.description: The preview cited more than 100 million covered lives but did not describe a target to more than double that base. Management set a goal of exceeding 200 million covered lives by the end of 2027, a more ambitious expansion target than the preview had laid out.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Targets exceeding 200 million covered lives by the end of 2027 versus the current 100 million-plus.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~100M+ as of Dec 2025”; the preview said incremental announcements were “now small relative to the base.”

surprises.description: The preview cited revenue per ordering account of $24,000 and a 53% year-over-year increase. NRXS reported $40,000 per account, up 68%, indicating a stronger increase than the preview’s cited trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue per ordering account rose 68% to $40,000 from $24,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue per ordering account $24K annualized (+53%).”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $1.928 million was within the preview’s $1.9–$2.1 million base range and close to its roughly $2.0 million model; the approximately 20% sequential increase was also consistent with the expected 20–30% range.
Gross margin of 85.9% was essentially in line with the preview’s 86–87% base expectation and remained above its 85% downside threshold.
The VA channel rollout was anticipated as an item to watch: the preview flagged a VA/Federal Supply Schedule ramp and a nearly 7 million-patient eligible population.

surprises.description: The Closed Block lost $110 million, far worse than the preview’s base-case estimate of a $30–40 million loss. That drove total adjusted operating income to about $2 million (the $112 million ex-Closed Block result less the Closed Block loss), versus the preview’s roughly $73 million estimate; management also warned full-year actual-to-expected losses could exceed about $300 million if first-half trends continue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Closed Block segment posted an adjusted operating loss of $110 million, driven by a $127 million pretax actual-to-expected variance loss primarily in LTC,” and “full-year A/E losses could exceed the ~$300 million expectation if first-half trends persist.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected Closed Block AOI of “‑$30M to ‑$40M”; its estimated total adjusted operating income including Closed Block was “~$73M.”

surprises.description: Genworth raised its full-year share-repurchase outlook above the preview’s $195–225 million range, now guiding to $225–250 million. Q2 repurchases themselves were within the preview’s expected $60–70 million pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Genworth raised its full-year 2026 share repurchase guidance to $225 million-$250 million,” after repurchasing “$62 million of shares” in Q2 and another “$4 million in July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 allocation was guided to “$195–225M” and its base case expected buybacks to continue “near $60–70M.”

surprises.description: Enact is expected to send Genworth substantially more capital in 2026 than the preview’s roughly $405 million framing: the new $445–485 million outlook is about $40–80 million higher. Its $103 million Q2 return also exceeded the preview’s $95 million threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enact returned $103 million of capital to Genworth in the quarter,” and Genworth now expects “$445 million-$485 million from Enact for full-year 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited guidance of “~$405M to Genworth in 2026” and said “Anything below ~$95M this quarter” would be a concern.

surprises.description: CareScout Services revenue was $6 million, below the preview’s $7 million-plus Q2 threshold, while match volumes are pacing below what is needed to reach the roughly 7,500-match annual target. The company nevertheless continues to expect $25 million of full-year revenue and $50–55 million of investment spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CareScout Services generated only $6 million of revenue in Q2 ($12 million first half), and match volumes are pacing below the level needed to hit the full-year target of ~7,500 matches”; the company “continues to expect CareScout Services full-year revenue of $25 million while investing $50 million-$55 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 needed “roughly 1,900+ matches and $7M+ revenue to keep the target credible,” against FY26 targets of “7,500 matches” and “$25M service revenue” with “$50–55M investment spend.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a potentially significant legal recovery that the preview did not flag: a decision on the AXA/Santander appeal is expected in 3–6 months, and a favorable, fully resolved outcome could return about $750 million tax-free. The outcome remains uncertain and is not included in capital plans, so this is a new contingent possibility rather than a realized gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AXA/Santander appeal hearing occurred in July with a decision expected within 3-6 months; a favorable, fully-resolved outcome would recover approximately $750 million tax-free, though not currently factored into capital plans.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating income excluding the Closed Block was modestly above the preview’s estimate: $112 million versus about $107 million, with EPS of $0.29 versus $0.28 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income excluding the Closed Block of $112 million ($0.29/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$107M” of adjusted operating income ex-Closed Block and listed “$0.28” adjusted operating EPS consensus.

in_line: Enact contributed $143 million to Genworth, broadly in line with the preview’s $138–142 million base-case range.
Q2 buybacks of $62 million were within the preview’s expected $60–70 million pace.

The MYRAP full-year value expectation of around $1 billion on a net-present-value basis was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of roughly $1 billion, with approvals described as broadly in line with 2025.

surprises.description: The preview framed LBRDK as having “no standalone revenue” and said GCI was in discontinued operations, but the reported facts included $261 million of Q2 revenue and $96 million of adjusted OIBDA, down 11% year over year. The operating results were therefore much more substantive—and weaker on OIBDA—than the preview’s information-free-print framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $261 million (flat year-over-year) while adjusted OIBDA declined 11% year-over-year to $96 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Standalone revenue: None (GCI in disc. ops)” and “The earnings print is close to information-free.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a new shareholder distribution policy, but Liberty Capital announced a quarterly dividend of about $15 million, or $60 million annually, beginning in December 2025. Management expects it to use about half of next year’s free cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Liberty Capital announced a new capital allocation policy initiating a quarterly dividend of approximately $15 million ($60 million annually) beginning in December 2025, which is expected to represent about half of next year's free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The earnings print is close to information-free.”

surprises.description: The preview gave no indication that trailing free cash flow was declining, but reported TTM free cash flow was only $59 million and was down year over year. Management attributed the decline to higher capital expenditures, lower OIBDA, and working-capital swings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow was $59 million, a decline year-over-year driven by higher capital expenditures, lower OIBDA, and working capital swings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The earnings print is close to information-free.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a high-spending year or a subsequent spending step-down. Management now expects 2026 capital spending to peak at approximately $290 million, with meaningful declines in 2027 and 2028 as capital intensity returns to historical levels.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects 2026 to be the peak year for capital spending at approximately $290 million, with meaningful declines forecast for 2027 and 2028 returning to historical capital intensity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The earnings print is close to information-free.”

surprises.description: The preview did not discuss the pending Quintillion acquisition or its expected operating contribution. Management expects it to close in 2025, contribute $50–$55 million of adjusted OIBDA including synergies in 2026, and be accretive to free cash flow in its first year after closing; projected synergies are about $20 million over 24 months, with roughly half in the first year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pending Quintillion acquisition is expected to close in 2025, contribute $50-$55 million of adjusted OIBDA including synergies in 2026, and be accretive to free cash flow in the first year after closing”; “approximately $20 million in run-rate synergies over 24 months, with roughly half achieved in the first 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The earnings print is close to information-free.”

surprises.description: The preview did not highlight consumer wireless growth or convergence, but wireless lines increased by 2,100 in the quarter. The reported attachment figures were also substantial: 42% of broadband customers took wireless service, and 63% of postpaid wireless lines were sold in converged relationships.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumer wireless lines grew by 2,100 during the quarter, with 42% of broadband customers now taking wireless service and 63% of postpaid wireless lines sold as part of converged relationships.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The earnings print is close to information-free.”

surprises.description: The preview provided no broadband subscriber outlook, while the reported figures showed organic subscriber losses partly masked by an acquisition: broadband subscribers fell organically by 500, but the small fixed-wireless-provider acquisition added 5,400 to the base.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumer broadband subscribers declined organically by 500, but a small fixed wireless provider acquisition added 5,400 customers to the base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The earnings print is close to information-free.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag pressure on business margins, but business gross margin fell to 75.5%. Management attributed the decline to a $9 million increase in distribution costs, including about $3 million related to restoring service on the Quintillion Network.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business gross margin fell to 75.5% due to a $9 million increase in distribution costs, of which about $3 million related to restored service on the Quintillion Network.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The earnings print is close to information-free.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on the $864 million current Margin Loan Facility and whether Charter share repurchases would fund debt service, but the reported facts instead supplied operating-level leverage figures and note-repurchase activity. Consolidated net leverage was 2.1x, GCI leverage was 2.8x against a roughly 3x long-term operating-level target, and about $129 million of senior notes had been repurchased through July 31.
surprises.fact_evidence: “At quarter end, Liberty Capital's consolidated net leverage was 2.1x and GCI's net leverage was 2.8x, with the company targeting a long-term operating-level leverage ratio of approximately 3x and having repurchased about $129 million of senior notes through July 31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Margin Loan Facility — $864M is current. Confirmation that Charter share repurchases from LBRD continue to fund debt service through close.”

surprises.description: MARA's net loss was $611.3 million, or $1.60 per diluted share, worse than the preview's estimate of a $480–525 million loss and $1.25–1.35 loss per share. The $343 million Bitcoin mark-to-market loss was close to the preview's roughly $350 million estimate, so the bottom-line shortfall was larger than expected despite the anticipated mark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss of $611.3 million (negative $1.60 per diluted share)” and “a $343 million unrealized mark-to-market loss on Bitcoin holdings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss ... −$480M to −$525M”; “EPS (GAAP) ... −$1.25 to −$1.35”; “Fair-value mark on treasury ... ~−$350M.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $174.9 million was below the preview's cited $206–210 million consensus, but well above its own $140–155 million estimate. That is a smaller consensus miss than the preview's stated 25–30% base case and a better result than its bottom-up forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell to $174.9 million,” as a 28% decline in Bitcoin's average price reduced revenue despite higher Bitcoin production.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue of ~$206–210M”; “My Estimate ... $140–155M”; “a headline ‘revenue miss’ of 25–30% ... [is] the base case.”

surprises.description: MARA's reported adjusted EBITDA was negative $360.9 million. The preview expected roughly breakeven to positive $15 million excluding fair-value changes; given the reported $343 million Bitcoin mark, the result implies approximately negative $18 million excluding that mark, modestly below the preview's operating expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was negative $360.9 million ... dominated by the Bitcoin mark-to-market change”; the unrealized Bitcoin mark-to-market loss was “$343 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (ex-FV) ... ~$0 to +$15M.”

surprises.description: Management said tenant demand for AI infrastructure had exceeded initial expectations and expressed confidence in signing at least two leases before year-end. The preview identified year-end leases as the key catalyst but described its base case as leases remaining in advanced negotiation, so the stronger demand commentary is an upside development, although no signed leases or economics were reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expressed confidence in signing at least two AI infrastructure leases before year-end through its Starwood partnership” and “tenant demand has exceeded initial expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the key checkpoint was “tenant leases signed by year-end” and described the base case as leases “in advanced negotiation.”

surprises.description: MARA said the pending $1.5 billion Long Ridge acquisition would be funded entirely through non-dilutive financing. The preview highlighted dilution and possible Bitcoin sales as key funding risks and required no equity raise for its bull case, so the disclosed financing approach is better than that concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Long Ridge acquisition is “a $1.5 billion enterprise value deal” and “is being funded entirely through non-dilutive financing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “the equity/debt split, and whether MARA sells more BTC to fund it” and said the bull case required “no equity raise.”

surprises.description: Long Ridge's expected contracted share was reported at about 70%, below the preview's 76% figure. Its roughly $144 million annualized EBITDA contribution, however, matched the preview's estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Long Ridge is expected to contribute “roughly $144 million in annualized EBITDA with about 70% of output under long-term contracts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Long Ridge as having “$144M annualized adj. EBITDA, 76% contracted.”

surprises.description: MARA disclosed new $600 million Bitcoin-backed credit facilities, with a 7.56% weighted average borrowing cost and 54% of its Bitcoin holdings pledged as collateral. The preview focused on liquidity, debt, Bitcoin sales, and dilution but did not anticipate this borrowing and collateral arrangement.
surprises.fact_evidence: MARA entered “two Bitcoin-backed credit facilities ... totaling $600 million in incremental borrowings at a 7.56% weighted average cost of debt, bringing 54% of its Bitcoin holdings pledged as collateral.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Liquidity, debt, and the ATM” and the “Bitcoin treasury policy and the sell/hold decision,” but did not mention new Bitcoin-backed facilities.

surprises.description: MARA acquired rights to a Matagorda County site with potential for up to 2 gigawatts, existing transmission lines, and no required utility infrastructure improvements. The preview discussed MARA's power pipeline and Texas land but did not anticipate this specific site or its stated infrastructure advantages.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired rights to a 1,200-acre Matagorda County, Texas site with potential for up to 2 gigawatts of capacity,” with “no required utility infrastructure improvements and existing transmission lines.”

in_line: The $343 million Bitcoin mark-to-market loss was close to the preview's estimate of roughly $350 million.
Energized hashrate was 70.3 exahash, close to the preview's estimate of about 70.7 and its expectation of flat-to-down sequentially.
The approximately 4.8-gigawatt total power portfolio was consistent with the preview's discussion of a 4.8-gigawatt pipeline.
Long Ridge's roughly $144 million expected annualized EBITDA matched the preview's estimate; the acquisition remained pending, consistent with the preview's expectation that it had not closed.
MARA's Bitcoin holdings increased from 35,303 at the end of Q1 to 35,577 at quarter-end, consistent with the preview's expectation of net Bitcoin additions in Q2.

surprises.description: Oportun reported adjusted EBITDA of $49 million, $10 million above the top of its $34–39 million guidance range. The preview expected Q2 EBITDA near the $37 million midpoint, so this was a substantial beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $49 million, up 56% year-over-year and well above the $34-39 million guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA — Company Guide (May 7, 2026): $34–39M (mid $37M)”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.42 versus the preview’s $0.33 consensus, a much larger result than the expected modest year-over-year increase. The preview also noted a roughly $0.32 effective whisper, widening the gap further.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $0.42 (up 35% YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $0.33”; the preview also said “the effective whisper is roughly $0.32.”

surprises.description: Oportun’s annualized net charge-off rate was 12.0%, better than the 12.2% guidance midpoint, and management lowered its full-year forecast to 11.7% from 11.9% ±50 basis points. The preview expected an approximately 12.2% Q2 result and highlighted the need to reaffirm an H2 “11 handle”; the Q2 result and lower full-year outlook improved on that setup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The annualized net charge-off rate improved 65 basis points sequentially to 12%, beating guidance, with Q3 guided to 11% and full-year revised down to 11.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Annualized NCO rate — Company Guide: 12.2% ±15bps”; the preview also described FY NCO guidance as “11.9% ±50bps” and said to watch for an “11 handle” in H2.

surprises.description: Delinquencies reached 4.0%, below the preview’s expected 4.1%–4.2% range. That was a modest but clear improvement on the anticipated credit metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 30-plus day delinquency rate fell to 4.0%, below the 4.1-4.2% expectation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “30+ day delinquency — 4.1%–4.2%.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $233 million, about $1 million above the company’s guidance ceiling and above the preview’s consensus range of roughly $231 million. The preview characterized Q2 as tightly guided and largely de-risked, so the beat was positive but small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue was $233 million, roughly flat year-over-year but $1 million above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus: $230.7M–$231.2M | Company Guide: $227–232M”; the preview said “Q2 itself is largely de-risked.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by 6% at the midpoint, to $168 million, rather than merely maintaining the prior $150–165 million range. Adjusted net income and EPS guidance remained unchanged, with management citing fair-value headwinds despite lower interest expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised 6% at the midpoint to $168 million (13% growth), while adjusted net income ($74-82 million) and adjusted EPS ($1.50-1.65) guidance were maintained as fair value headwinds offset lower interest expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$150–165M” and described FY adjusted EPS guidance of “$1.50–1.65,” with the key question whether management would “reiterate, narrow, or cut” it.

surprises.description: Interest expense fell 30% year over year, and Oportun improved its full-year reduction target to at least 15% from 10%. The preview already identified funding costs as running ahead of plan, but the larger revised savings target was stronger than the stated plan; the reported Q2 decline also included a noncash recognition change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interest expense fell 30% year-over-year to $42 million, aided by a ~$7 million noncash change in interest expense recognition, and full-year interest expense is now guided to decline at least 15% versus the prior 10% guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the FY target as “≥10% reduction” and said interest expense was “the one line item consistently running ahead of plan.”

in_line: Originations returned to 1% year-over-year growth, consistent with the preview’s Q2 expectation of approximately $485–500 million, or flat to 4% growth versus the prior year.
Management retained full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $1.50–1.65, within the range the preview identified as the key guidance test.
Q3 net charge-offs were guided to 11%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that management would reaffirm an H2 “11 handle.”
The $30 million corporate-debt reduction and $15 million of annualized run-rate interest savings were broadly consistent with the preview’s focus on debt paydown and the funding-savings opportunity.

surprises.description: ATI reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $284 million, $29 million above the high end of its $245–$255 million guidance and well above the roughly $250 million implied consensus estimate. The quarter was its strongest EBITDA result since 2007.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached $284 million” and was “$29 million above the high end of prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA ~$250M (implied)” and company guidance of “$245–$255M.”

surprises.description: Revenue reached $1.3 billion, above the preview’s $1.22 billion consensus estimate, while growing 11% year over year. That is a clear reversal of the preview’s concern that ATI had repeatedly missed revenue estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue up 11% to $1.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: “$1,220M”; the preview also said ATI had “missed revenue repeatedly over two years.”

surprises.description: ATI’s full-year adjusted EBITDA midpoint rose to $1.160 billion, above both the prior $1.010–$1.060 billion guidance range and the preview’s stated bar of a raise to roughly $1.05–$1.09 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year guidance across all metrics: adjusted EBITDA midpoint to $1.160 billion (35% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY26 guidance was “$1,010–$1,060M”; the preview said the bar was “a raise to roughly $1.05–$1.09B.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EPS midpoint increased to $5.04, substantially above the prior guidance range of $4.20–$4.48 and the preview’s bull-case range of about $4.40–$4.60.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS midpoint to $5.04 (56% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview estimates listed FY26 adjusted EPS of “$4.20–$4.48”; its bull case cited FY EPS of “~$4.40–$4.60.”

surprises.description: ATI raised its full-year free-cash-flow midpoint to $575 million, above the previous $465–$525 million guidance range. The preview had highlighted the back-half-loaded FCF target as something to monitor, but the updated midpoint is higher than that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow midpoint to $575 million (51% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 adjusted FCF guidance was “$465–$525M.”

surprises.description: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 22.6%, versus the preview’s roughly 20.5% expectation. The margin increase was therefore stronger than the preview’s already positive year-over-year margin outlook implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 440 basis points year-over-year to 22.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview consensus implied an “Adj. EBITDA margin ~20.5%” and “+~200bps.”

surprises.description: AA&S margins were much stronger than the preview’s expected move toward 19%: the reported margin was 23.7%, or 22% excluding the asset-sale gain, and management now expects sustained mid-20% margins. This also turns the segment’s prior-year margin decline into a substantial expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AA&S segment margins expanded 930 basis points to an all-time high of 23.7% (22% excluding a $10 million asset sale gain, versus 14% a year ago), with management now guiding to sustained mid-20% margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for AA&S margin “pushing toward 19%+.”

surprises.description: Backlog increased to $4.4 billion, up 7% sequentially from the $4.1 billion Q1 record. That exceeds the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly flat to 5% growth and its bull-case threshold of more than $4.3 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record backlog reached $4.4 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 7% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 backlog of “$4.1B,” a base case of “~flat to +5%,” and a bull threshold of “backlog >$4.3B.”

surprises.description: Defense revenue grew 36% to an all-time high, and management raised its full-year defense growth expectation to the high teens. That is stronger than the preview’s mid-teens reference for full-year defense growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense revenue grew 36% year-over-year to an all-time high,” prompting management to raise full-year defense growth expectations to “high teens.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the existing FY defense guide as “mid-teens.”

surprises.description: ATI disclosed that approximately $30–40 million of HPMC revenue shifted from the first half into the second half because qualifications at the new Mexico facility and EB2 titanium furnace took longer. The revenue is delayed rather than described as lost, and carries high incremental margins, but the timing shift was not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $30-40 million of HPMC revenue at 40-50% incremental margins shifted from the first half into the second half due to qualification timing at the new Mexico facility and EB2 titanium furnace.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year consolidated incremental margin guidance from 40% to 50%, a sizeable improvement in the expected profitability of incremental revenue that the preview did not specify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year consolidated incremental margin guidance from 40% to 50%.”

surprises.description: Management’s implied Q4 EBITDA of about $335 million corresponds to an annualized exit rate of roughly $1.35 billion, above the newly raised $1.16 billion full-year EBITDA midpoint. This points to a stronger year-end run rate than the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Implied Q4 EBITDA of ~$335 million translates to a ~$1.350 billion annualized exit rate.”

surprises.description: Jet-engine revenue grew 13% year over year, with high-teens full-year growth expected, and ATI reported lead times reaching 20 months for premium titanium and over 24 months for isothermal forgings. Those lead times extend well beyond the preview’s general expectation of one-year-plus lead times for differentiated materials.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Jet engine revenue grew 13% year-over-year (high-teens full-year growth expected)” and lead times were “20 months on premium titanium, and over 24 months on isothermal forgings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “1yr+ lead times on differentiated titanium/nickel.”

in_line: The roughly $1 billion naval nuclear contract renewal was contemplated in the preview as a possible specialty-energy contract. The reported agreement is roughly $1 billion over five years through 2030.

surprises.description: The preview looked for Q3 revenue of roughly $290–320 million, with anything below $280 million putting the full-year math at risk. AOI instead guided to $255–290 million, a notably weaker range whose midpoint is $272.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $255-290 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 guided $290–320M” in the base case; “Anything with a 2-handle below $280M breaks the FY math.”

surprises.description: The preview's central expectation was that AOI would defend full-year revenue above $1.1 billion. Management instead reaffirmed revenue of “around” $1.1 billion, a softer formulation, while saying production capacity and supply chain cap results below estimated demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AOI reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue of around $1.1 billion,” capped by capacity and supply chain.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management defends a FY26 guide (>$1.1B revenue)” and the base case expected “FY reiterated at >$1.1B.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged equity issuance as a financing risk, but AOI did raise substantial equity: it raised $538.8 million net through its at-the-market offering. That is a significant dilution event relative to the preview's expectation of a reaffirmation without a raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised $538.8 million net under its new at-the-market equity offering.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for equity/convert issuance language — a raise on this print would be poorly received.”

surprises.description: The preview's margin math implied roughly 37% gross margin in 2H to support its expected full-year operating income. Management's stated Q4 target was only about 32–33%, below that implied level, even though it expects a longer-term return to roughly 40%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expecting Q4 to reach roughly 32-33% as 1.6T mix increases” and targeting a long-term return to “~40%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2H gross margin near 37%” was implied by the preview's full-year operating income math.

surprises.description: The preview discussed laser and MOCVD constraints, but did not flag a shortage of memory that would prevent customers from sourcing 100G switches. AOI expects that issue to cut Q3 100G revenue by $20–25 million and persist into late 2026 or early 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A Q3 decline of $20-25 million in 100G revenue” due to customers' inability to source 100G switches; the memory shortage is expected to persist “until late 2026 or early 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Supply chain / laser constraint” and MOCVD backlog, but did not identify a memory shortage disrupting customers' 100G switches.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 CATV revenue of $75–80 million and questioned whether the business would hold up as data center revenue scaled. CATV reached $80.6 million and AOI guided to $100–110 million for Q3, indicating continued growth rather than merely holding steady.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CATV revenue hit a record $80.6 million” and Q3 guidance was “$100-110 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CATV rev” Q2 guide was “$75–80M”; the preview asked “whether it holds as data center scales.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a specific DOCSIS 4.0 customer win. Mediacom selected AOI as its primary vendor for DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades, a new positive indication for the CATV business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mediacom selected AOI as primary vendor for DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 manufacturing capacity of about 150,000 units per month. AOI said it was already approaching 200,000, and also gave a new target of more than 930,000 units per month by the end of 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Monthly manufacturing capacity is approaching 200,000 units” and targets are “over 650,000 units/month by end of 2026 and over 930,000 units/month by end of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capacity exited Q1 at ~100k units/month with a Q2 target of 150k/month, >650k/month by YE26.”

surprises.description: AOI reported $565.5 million in Q2 capital investments, including $280 million in equipment prepayments. The preview noted rising capex and the need to expand capacity, but its stated Q1 capex was $68.7 million and it did not anticipate investment at this scale in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Made $565.5 million in Q2 capital investments (including $280 million in equipment prepayments).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 capex was $68.7M and rising.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was expected at $0.02–$0.03, but AOI reported $0.06 per diluted share and returned to non-GAAP profitability. The beat was partly aided by foreign tax benefits and government subsidies, so the reported result was stronger but included benefits the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income of $5.5 million or $0.06 per diluted share,” beating guidance, “aided by foreign tax benefits and government subsidies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” consensus was “$0.02–0.03”; Q2 guidance was “$(0.03) – $0.03.”

surprises.description: The preview expected an 800G ramp in Q2 and meaningful later-year growth, but did not anticipate management guiding to roughly fivefold sequential growth in Q3. Q2 800G revenue was already $12.8 million, more than doubling sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “800G revenue reached $12.8 million,” more than doubling sequentially, with management guiding for “roughly 5x sequential growth in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 800G to become the largest data-center line and cited roughly 4x sequential unit growth, but gave no comparable Q3 revenue-growth outlook.

in_line: Q2 revenue of $191.9 million was close to the preview's $191.1 million consensus and within the cited vendor consensus range of $190.5–194.3 million.
Q2 non-GAAP gross margin of 29.8% was within the preview's expected 29–30% guidance range and close to its approximately 29.5% consensus.

surprises.description: Revenue was $29.8 million, about $3.7 million below the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $33.5 million and below its $32.5 million lower bear-case threshold. Instead of the expected 7.7% year-over-year growth, revenue declined from $31.12 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $29.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~ $33.5M (derived, not published)” and “Q2 revenue vs. ~$33.5M derived / ~$33M whisper”; the preview described sub-$32.5M as a bear outcome.

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $0.01, well below the preview’s $0.04 MarketBeat consensus and $0.06 Zacks estimate. The preview considered $0.02–$0.04 a plausible base range, so the reported result also came in below that anticipated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income fell to $1 million ($0.01 per diluted share) from $0.05 per diluted share a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) Consensus: $0.04 (range $0.02–$0.06)” and “My base case is Q2 GAAP EPS of $0.02–0.04.”

surprises.description: Selling and marketing reached 34% of sales, versus the preview’s expected gross margin/opex setup that already allowed for rising expenses, and management said this elevated spending rate will continue. The preview did not anticipate this degree of ongoing S&M intensity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Selling and marketing expense jumped to 34% of net sales from 26.4% a year ago,” and management indicated the elevated run rate “will continue” with investment in retail rollout, brand campaigns, and China expansion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “opex up again on pharma R&D” and flagged that “S&M, R&D (NB4168), and G&A” were guided higher, but did not forecast S&M at 34% of sales or that this rate would persist.

surprises.description: Ingredient revenue was only $5.4 million, and management expects it to decline year over year amid NMN and NAD competition and lower Life Extension purchases. That is worse than the preview’s hoped-for stabilization in the B2B and ingredient lines.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ingredient business generated only $5.4 million ($4.9M food-grade, $0.4M pharma-grade) and is expected to decline year-over-year due to competitive pressure from NMN and NAD, partly reflecting lower purchases from Life Extension.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “These are the lines that caused the Q1 shortfall — they need to stop getting worse.”

surprises.description: Gross margin held at 64.8%, above the preview’s expected 63.5–64.0% and contrary to its anticipated 100–150 basis-point year-over-year decline. The actual margin was nearly flat against the prior-year 65.0%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin held roughly stable at 64.8% versus 65% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~63.5–64.0%” and “−100 to −150bp.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that NB4168’s Ataxia-Telangiectasia indication alone could support a $200–400 million NPV, with a potentially transferable priority review voucher recently valued at $150–180 million. The preview discussed the pharmaceutical pivot as a potential option but did not anticipate these quantified value estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimates the lead pharmaceutical candidate NB4168's Ataxia-Telangiectasia indication alone could support a net present value of $200-400 million, plus a potential transferable priority review voucher recently valued at $150-180 million.”

surprises.description: The expected NB4168 development commitment was quantified at only about $30 million over four years through approval, with first-in-human studies expected next year and the company expected to remain cash-flow positive. This addresses the preview’s concern about an unquantified R&D step-up or possible need for outside funding more favorably than it anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total drug development spending for NB4168 from now through approval is projected at only about $30 million spread over four years, with first-in-human studies expected next year, keeping the company cash-flow positive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for a “quantified FY R&D dollar commitment” and whether spending was funded from net cash, warning that “a raise hint” would be a downside catalyst.

surprises.description: China cross-border revenue through May had already exceeded all of 2025, and the company had received Mainland China approval for topical/skincare products while dietary-ingredient approval remained pending. The preview did not flag this degree of China traction or the topical-product approval.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China cross-border revenue through May 2026 already exceeded the full-year 2025 total (which was under $1 million), and the company recently received topical/skincare product approval in Mainland China though dietary ingredient approval remains pending.”

surprises.description: NanoClouds sold out its limited 3,000–4,000-unit run, leading to a broader relaunch planned for October/November; management also disclosed discussions with two large global skincare companies about potentially exclusive Niagen deals. These commercialization developments were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The branded skincare product NanoClouds sold out its limited run of 3,000-4,000 units with strong new-to-brand and repeat purchases, prompting a broader relaunch in October/November, while two large global skincare companies are in discussions about potentially exclusive Niagen deals.”

surprises.description: Management described 2026 as an investment year and positioned it as a springboard for accelerated growth in 2027. That emphasizes a later growth payoff rather than the near-term H2 acceleration the preview said was needed to support the full-year growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management framed “2026 as an investment year and a springboard for accelerated growth in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the guide required “a sharp H2 acceleration” and that H2 needed to grow “+11–14% after an H1 of ~+6%.”

surprises.description: A temporary Amazon marketplace listing issue in June reduced reported e-commerce growth from an estimated 19% absent the issue to 14%, although the issue has since been resolved. The preview had not anticipated this disruption; the reported growth still met its healthy-growth benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “E-commerce revenue grew 14% to $20.5 million, but the company estimates growth would have been 19% absent a temporary Amazon marketplace listing issue in June that has since been resolved.”

in_line: E-commerce grew 14%, matching the preview’s cited Q1 e-commerce growth benchmark and remaining above its stated concern threshold of growth below roughly 10%. The company also reiterated full-year 2026 e-commerce growth guidance of 10–15%.

surprises.description: LMAT missed the Q2 sales expectation: sales were about $1.1 million below guidance, whose midpoint was essentially the $71.47 million consensus. The shortfall was attributed in equal thirds to a stronger U.S. dollar, Middle East war-related export delays, and cardiac allograft supply constraints.
