surprises.fact_evidence: “The company missed its Q2 sales guidance by $1.1 million,” attributed “in equal thirds to a stronger U.S. dollar, Middle East war-related export delays (~$400,000 of orders blocked), and cardiac allograft supply constraints.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 sales consensus was “$71.47M”; guidance was “$70.5 – $72.5M (mid $71.5M).”

surprises.description: Q2 earnings fell short of the preview’s $0.81 EPS expectation: fully diluted EPS was $0.74. Operating income was also below the preview’s $21.6 million expectation, at $20.4 million, with a 29% operating margin versus the expected 30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating income reached a record $20.4 million (up 26%) for a 29% operating margin,” and “fully diluted EPS grew 23% to $0.74.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 diluted EPS consensus was “$0.81”; expected operating income was “$21.6M” and operating margin “30%.”

surprises.description: The full-year outlook was cut rather than raised: revenue guidance is now $276.3 million and organic growth 11%, below the previous $277–283 million range and 12% organic-growth outlook. Full-year EPS guidance of $2.89 is also below the previous $2.93–$3.08 range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance was updated to $276.3 million,” with “organic growth cut from 12% to 11% reflecting Q2 results, export weakness, and RFA supply constraints.” Full-year fully diluted EPS guidance is “$2.89.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 guidance of “Sales $277–283M (mid $280M, +12% organic); EPS $2.93–$3.08 (mid $3.00).” It also said the buy side wanted the sales line lifted.

surprises.description: Cardiac allograft supply is limiting growth despite strong recent results, and the company is shifting tissue processing to address the constraint. This adds a specific supply bottleneck to the preview’s discussion of RestoreFlow momentum and expected Q2 activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cardiac allograft (RFA) revenue grew 17% in Q2 and cardiac allografts specifically rose 39% quarter-on-quarter, but growth is slowing due to supply constraints being addressed by moving tissue processing to Burlington, Massachusetts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “RestoreFlow allografts (+25% in Q1; Germany implants were to begin in Q2, Irish approval H2).”

surprises.description: The headline organic growth masked a sharp catheter decline: catheters fell 11% because of recall-driven overstocking in the prior year, while organic growth excluding catheters was 12%, with 5% unit growth. The preview’s unit-growth debate centered on whether volume could reach 4%, so the stronger ex-catheter volume was offset by an unflagged product-specific drag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 organic sales grew 10% (7% price, 3% units), but excluding catheters organic growth was 12% (7% price, 5% units), as catheters fell 11% due to year-earlier recall-driven overstocking.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “units ≥4%” as the key watch item and described a base case of “~7% price / 3% unit.”

surprises.description: International Artegraft sales are ahead of the preview’s pace: Q2 international sales rose to $2.8 million, above the roughly $2.5 million needed to stay on the preview’s $10 million full-year target. The company now expects $11 million of international sales for 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International Artegraft sales rising from $2.1 million in Q1 to $2.8 million in Q2 and full-year 2026 international sales expected at $11 million versus $4 million in 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the business “needs ~$2.5M+ in Q2 to stay on plan” for a “$10M FY2026 target.”

surprises.description: The FDA indicated that a clinical trial is likely needed for the Artegraft Quick Stick indication, pushing any timeline out by years and leaving LMAT unsure whether it will pursue the indication. The preview did not flag this regulatory hurdle.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA indicated a clinical trial is likely required for the Artegraft Quick Stick indication, pushing the timeline to years and leaving the company uncertain whether to proceed.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted warehouse and tissue-transfer costs as a possible gross-margin drag, but management reported European gross-margin gains of 5–9 percentage points year over year from its relocalization strategy, alongside plans to open about seven new or larger warehouses across 2026–2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is opening “about 7 new or larger warehouses across 2026/2027 as part of a ‘relocalization’ strategy driving European gross margin gains of 5-9 full points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 gross margin was guided “down 60 bps sequentially from 72.7% on the Irish warehouse standup and tissue-processing transfers,” and warned that sub-72% would validate concerns about margin expansion being capped.

in_line: Q2 gross margin was 72.1%, exactly matching the preview’s expectation and company guidance.
The overall Q2 sales mix of about 7% price growth and 3% unit growth matched the preview’s base case, although it did not reach the preview’s ≥4% unit-growth watch threshold.
Sales reps increased from 158 exiting Q1 to 163 in Q2, progressing toward the 170–180 year-end target flagged in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview expected NRR around 108–110% in its base case and warned that a result below 105% would signal broader franchise weakness. OPRX reported NRR of 90%, alongside sequential declines in average revenue per top-20 pharma customer and revenue per FTE.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue retention rate fell to 90%, average revenue per top-20 pharma manufacturer was $2.7 million, and revenue per FTE was $750,000, all showing sequential declines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base ... NRR ~108–110%”; “Below ~105% signals a franchise problem, not a client problem.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the disrupted major client might contribute to Q3–Q4 buying acceleration if its situation improved. Instead, a large customer generated no revenue in Q2, and the revenue decline was concentrated in a small number of large customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The decline [in revenue was] concentrated in a small number of large customers including one that generated no revenue this quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Possible Q3–Q4 buying acceleration”; “If this client has deteriorated further, the guide breaks.”

surprises.description: Management held the annual revenue guide, as expected, but said Q4 alone is expected to provide 35–40% of full-year revenue. That makes the forecast notably dependent on a very large Q4 contribution, beyond the preview’s general expectation of a strong second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $95-100 million in revenue ... with Q4 expected to represent 35-40% of full-year revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The guide requires $55–60M in H2”; management had framed the requirement as “nearly 60% in H2.”

surprises.description: The preview treated roughly 67% gross margin as the reference point, while management raised its full-year margin outlook to the high-60% to low-70% range. Favorable mix and the wind-down of low-margin managed services are expected to support the improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin guidance was raised, with full-year 2026 gross margins now expected in the high-60% to low-70% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At 5.9x EBITDA on a 67% gross margin...”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was slightly above the preview’s $20.20 million consensus estimate, despite a year-over-year decline of 30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue was $20.5 million ... but exceeded consensus expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus Revenue: $20.20M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS came in above the preview’s $0.11 consensus estimate. GAAP EPS, by contrast, was close to the preview’s approximate $(0.05) estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income ... $0.16 per diluted share”; “net loss ... $0.04 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS $0.11”; “GAAP EPS ~$(0.05).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA appears to have exceeded the preview’s estimated range based on the $4.9 million figure, although the CFO also cited $4.1 million, which falls within that range. The reported decline from the prior year included $1.7 million of severance expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $4.9 million (or $4.1 million per CFO remarks) ... impacted by $1.7 million in severance expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (est.): ~$3.5–4.5M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected DSP contribution later in 2026. The DeepIntent DSP integration went live during the week of the call, an earlier operational milestone, and management described access to programmatic channels as a potential way to double the business over two years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The DeepIntent DSP integration went live during the week of the call”; management said programmatic channels account for 60% of buys in its space and DSP access could be “a potential driver to double the business over two years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Contribution expected late 2026.”

surprises.description: The AI-enabled DAAP and software offerings posted specific growth rates that the preview had not quantified: more than 30% for DAAP and 25% for AI-enabled software. This provides evidence of growth in the recurring-subscription shift beyond the preview’s general description of these products as future drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AI-enabled Dynamic Audience Activation Platform (DAAP) grew over 30% year-over-year and AI-enabled software offerings grew 25%.”

surprises.description: OPRX paid down debt faster than the preview’s discussion of refinancing and interest savings suggested: it made an extra roughly $5 million principal payment in Q2 and paid another $3 million after quarter-end. Management also described debt paydown as a capital-allocation priority.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paid $5.3 million in principal during Q2 (roughly $5 million ahead of schedule) plus an additional $3 million post-quarter, reducing outstanding debt to about $16.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “~$1.5M annual interest savings from the refinancing” and asked investors to watch for buyback activity.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the $10 million buyback and suggested an aggressive repurchase could signal conviction. Management instead emphasized debt paydown and described the buyback as conditional on the stock declining further; the facts do not report a repurchase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital allocation prioritizing debt paydown and a $10 million buyback if the stock declines further.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Aggressive repurchase at $7 signals conviction”; “Buyback activity — $10M authorization effective March 12, 2026.”

surprises.description: The company announced a CFO transition that the preview did not flag: Edward Stelmakh will step down at year-end, with Andy D'Silva taking over on January 1 and Stelmakh staying on as a strategic adviser through 2027. The planned handover offers continuity, but it is still an unanticipated leadership change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Edward Stelmakh will step down effective December 31, 2026, with Chief Business Officer Andy D'Silva succeeding as CFO on January 1, 2027, and Ed remaining as strategic adviser through 2027.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the $95–100 million FY2026 revenue guidance, the key outcome the preview identified as the bar.
Management also maintained the $21–25 million FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance, which the preview flagged as a critical credibility anchor.
GAAP EPS was approximately in line with the preview’s roughly $(0.05) estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $5.6 million, above both preview estimates of $4.70 million and $5.15 million. The beat was meaningful but not a dramatic departure from the higher estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $5.6 million” and was “up from $3.7 million in Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $4.70M” and “$5.15M”; the preview also described revenue of “~$4.7–5.2M expected.”

surprises.description: The reported $42.5 million backlog substantially exceeded the preview’s hoped-for move from $16 million to a figure above roughly $25 million. Management said the 12–18 month contracts are expected to sustain operations into at least Q3 2027, adding useful visibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contract backlog stood at approximately $42.5 million as of June 30, 2026,” consisting of “12-18 month contracts expected to sustain operations into at least Q3 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Backlog “was $16M at 3/31/26”; the preview said to watch for “a backlog print above ~$25M.”

surprises.description: Management provided a FY2026 revenue framework despite having given no forward guidance last quarter. The $20–25 million legacy-QCi outlook is near the preview’s $21.88 million full-year consensus, but the additional $7–16 million expected from NHanced lifts the combined indicated range to roughly $27–41 million; management cautioned that revenue is lumpy and back-end weighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue expectations of $20-25 million for legacy QCi, with NHanced expected to add between $7 million and $16 million,” while warning results are “lumpy and back-end weighted.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 revenue consensus of “$21.88M” and said, “Management gave no forward guidance last quarter.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a sizeable Fab 2 investment requirement—estimated at $50–100 million, likely around $75 million—which the preview had not quantified. Only a small portion is expected to be spent in 2026, tempering the near-term cash impact but leaving a material future capital commitment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Planned Fab 2 capital expenditures are estimated at $50-100 million (likely around $75 million),” with “only a small portion” expected to be spent in 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market wanted Fab 2 “utilization/capacity commentary, not another capex headline,” but gave no capex estimate.

surprises.description: The Planck Dynamics update retained the initial five-system order and potential value above $10 million, but described a path to “dozens more,” rather than the preview’s pathway to 100 systems. The facts also do not provide the hard 2026 delivery timing the preview was watching for.
surprises.fact_evidence: The framework “includes an initial order for 5 NeuraWave systems and a pathway to dozens more,” with “potential aggregate program value exceeding $10 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “pathway to 100 systems and >$10M” and said to watch for “a hard ship date for the first five Planck Dynamics systems.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that 70–80% of revenue comes from government contracting, primarily as a subcontractor, with commercial work second and education a distant third. The preview anticipated M&A-driven revenue and asked about pass-through versus branded product, but did not flag this degree of government and subcontractor concentration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 70-80% of company revenue currently comes from government contracting, primarily as a subcontractor, with commercial second and educational a distant third.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked “how much is Luminar/NHanced pass-through vs. QCi-branded product?” and said organic quantum/photonics revenue was “still de minimis,” but gave no expected government-revenue share.

in_line: GAAP EPS of -$0.05 was close to the preview’s -$0.04 aggregator estimate and within the wide -$0.12 to -$0.04 consensus range; the preview warned that EPS was heavily affected by non-operating marks. The reported smaller derivative loss was consistent with that warning.

The first five-system Planck Dynamics order and potential program value above $10 million matched the preview’s expectations; the difference was the less expansive ‘dozens more’ pathway and lack of a reported ship date.

The roughly $180 million spent on acquisitions and the resulting cash decline were broadly consistent with the preview’s focus on announced M&A spending and its reported $1.4 billion cash-and-investments balance at March 31.

surprises.description: AMETEK was expected to report about $1.96 billion in sales, with organic growth of roughly 6–7%; it reported $2.04 billion and 10% organic growth. Both the headline sales result and underlying growth were stronger than the preview’s bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales reached a record $2.04 billion” and “organic sales up 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $1.96B”; “consensus embeds roughly +6–7% organic.”

surprises.description: EPS was expected to be $1.99, at the top of company guidance; AMETEK reported $2.09, above both consensus and the $2.00 high end of its guidance. The result also exceeded the preview’s bull-case range of $2.05–$2.08.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS was a record $2.09” and “above the guidance range of $1.96 to $2.00 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $1.99”; company guidance “$1.96–$2.00”; bull case EPS “$2.05–2.08.”

surprises.description: Orders were expected to remain strong but could decelerate to single-digit growth, with book-to-bill at least 1.0 and backlog near $3.9 billion. Instead, organic orders grew 25%, book-to-bill was 1.12, and backlog reached $4.1 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Orders were a record $2.3 billion, up 28% overall and 25% organically,” with “record backlog of $4.1 billion” and “a book-to-bill of 1.12.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Deceleration to single-digit order growth is tolerable”; watch for book-to-bill “≥1.0” and backlog “near $3.9B.”

surprises.description: The full-year EPS raise was stronger than the preview’s base expectation of roughly $8.05–$8.20: AMETEK lifted its range to $8.20–$8.30, reaching the preview’s bull-case high. It also expects overall sales up about 10% and organic sales up mid-to-high single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AMETEK raised full-year EPS guidance to $8.20-$8.30” from “$7.94-$8.14,” and “now expects overall sales up ~10% with organic sales up mid-to-high single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The buy-side was expected to look for a midpoint “up $0.05–$0.10, to roughly $8.05–$8.20”; the bull case was “$8.15–8.30.”

surprises.description: Core margin expansion of 110 basis points was above the preview’s base-case expectation of 60–90 basis points, while incrementals were about 40% versus the 35% framework cited in the preview. The margin result was solid but within the preview’s bull-case range, rather than an outsized beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core operating margins expanded 110 basis points to 27.1%,” driven by “~40% incrementals,” positive price over inflation/tariffs, and a raised productivity target of $160 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case called for “core margin +60–90 bps”; guidance assumed “35% incrementals”; the bull case called for “core margin +100–150 bps.”

surprises.description: EMG’s organic sales growth of 15% and organic order growth of 35% showed more momentum than the preview’s roughly 12% segment sales-growth estimate and its expectation that medical growth would slow to mid-single digits. EMG’s 290-basis-point margin expansion was also strong, though below its 410-basis-point expansion in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EMG delivered exceptional results with 15% organic sales growth, 35% organic orders growth, and core margins up 290 basis points to 26.2%, led by Paragon Medical's medtech strength.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated EMG sales of “~$690M (+12%)” and described “Medical: low double digits in Q1, guided down to MSD on comps — a likely ‘decel’ headline.”

surprises.description: Free-cash-flow conversion of 111% was in line with the preview’s full-year 110–115% expectation, but the reported 220-basis-point improvement in operating working capital and 37% rise in free cash flow were additional favorable cash-generation details not specifically anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow rose 37% to $452 million with 111% conversion, while operating working capital improved 220 basis points to 16.4% of sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY conversion was guided to “110–115%” and noted Q1 free cash flow of “$426M at 107%.”

in_line: Indicor’s expected second-half 2026 closing remained on track, and management reiterated confidence in 10–12% cost synergies, consistent with the preview’s expectations.
Free-cash-flow conversion of 111% was within the preview’s stated full-year guidance range of 110–115%.

surprises.description: Virgin Galactic had been expected to begin its first commercial spaceflight in Q4 2026, but now says the first flight is delayed until February 2027. The delay was attributed to modest extensions across hundreds of installation tasks rather than one specific issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Delayed its first commercial spaceflight to February 2027,” citing “modest time extensions across hundreds of small installation tasks rather than any single issue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview calls for “reaffirmation of Q4 2026 first commercial spaceflight” and says a shift to “late 2026 / early 2027” would be a bear-case timeline slip.

surprises.description: Q3 free cash flow is now forecast at negative $95–100 million, substantially worse than the preview’s expected negative $70–80 million. The company says the delay will bring temporary extra spending, including two shifts seven days a week and additional workers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 free cash flow is guided to negative $95-100 million with a temporary capex increase”; the delay also drives incremental spending in Q3, including “operating two shifts seven days a week” and extra workforce.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says a Q3 guide of “$(70)–(80)M confirms” sequential improvement, while “anything at or beyond $(85)M” would imply stickier burn.

surprises.description: The cash balance was stronger than the preview’s estimated range: Virgin Galactic ended Q2 with $286 million, above the preview’s $180–230 million band. The balance was supported in part by equity issuance.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “ended Q2 with $286 million in cash and marketable securities, up from $251 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated an “implied 6/30/26 balance” of “~$180 – 230M” and used roughly $195–210 million as its base case.

surprises.description: The ATM equity program raised $134 million, above the preview’s estimated range of up to about $100 million in additional Q2 equity issuance. This means the cash balance came with more financing and dilution than the preview’s estimate allowed for.
surprises.fact_evidence: Virgin Galactic “raised $134 million through its now substantially complete ATM equity program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The cash bridge estimated “Additional Q2 equity issuance +? (0 to ~100)” and noted that the amount and timing were uncertain.

surprises.description: The company reduced principal on its 2027 and 2028 notes by $93 million, materially more than the preview’s specific reference to a $30.5 million note conversion. It says only $17.9 million remains payable on the 2027 notes and no required 2028-note payments are due until March 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reduced principal on its 2027 and 2028 notes by $93 million,” leaving “just $17.9 million in principal payments” on the 2027 notes and “no required payments on 2028 notes until March 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlights a “$30.5M 9.80% First Lien Note conversion” and says the remaining principal is pushed to March 2028.

surprises.description: Virgin Galactic now targets 10 or more spaceflights per month by the end of Q2 2027, above the preview’s expected cadence of about eight per month by Q2. The second spaceship is expected to join the New Mexico fleet in March 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The second spaceship is now expected to join the New Mexico fleet in March 2027,” while the company maintains a target of “10 or more spaceflights per month by the end of Q2 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says management had committed to “roughly 4 flights/month by January 2027” and “~8/month by Q2 2027.”

surprises.description: The $750,000 ticket tranche was oversubscribed, adding more than $50 million to expected future spaceflight revenue, and management plans to offer a new tranche at higher prices. This is stronger evidence of demand and pricing power than the preview’s watchlist of whether deposits and reservations would rise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's $750,000 price tranche was oversubscribed, adding over $50 million to expected future spaceflight revenue,” and management plans to open a new tranche “at higher price points this fall.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says the market was watching for a “sequential increase” in customer deposits as evidence demand at the new price was real, and notes deposits on a “meaningful portion” of available seats.

surprises.description: Q2 capex was $41 million, modestly below the preview’s $43–46 million estimate. The quarter’s free cash flow, however, landed within the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capex dropped to $41 million” in Q2.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 capex of “~$43–46M.”

in_line: Q2 free cash flow was negative $91 million, within the preview’s expected negative $87–92 million range.

surprises.description: SM generated $467 million of adjusted free cash flow, above the preview’s $300–400 million estimate. The preview expected strong cash generation, but the reported result exceeded the top of its range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SM Energy generated $467 million of adjusted free cash flow in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted FCF: $300–400M.”

surprises.description: SM had actioned $355 million, or about 95%, of its $375 million synergy target, ahead of the preview’s estimate that approximately $300 million had already been actioned. The target itself was not raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Actioned approximately 95% ($355 million) of its raised $375 million run-rate synergy target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$300M already actioned” against a “$375M run-rate” target.

surprises.description: Second-half production guidance was raised to 435,000–440,000 Boe/d, above the preview’s expectation of roughly 430,000 Boe/d. Management also described the new range as a cleaner baseline for modeling 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised second-half 2026 production guidance to 435,000–440,000 Boe/d … framing this as the cleaner baseline for modeling 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided 2H to ~430 MBoe/d” and the buy-side wants “2H volumes held near 430 MBoe/d.”

surprises.description: Q2 capital expenditures were $717 million, below the preview’s $815–855 million company-guidance range and its $835 million midpoint. The shortfall was attributed to drilling and completion timing, while full-year capital guidance was reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 capital expenditures were $717 million, below the $835 million guidance midpoint due to D&C timing, while full-year capital guidance of $2.65–$2.85 billion was reaffirmed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 capex guidance was “$815–855M”; the preview also said “capex held at $2.65–2.85B” was the expected answer.

surprises.description: SM lowered full-year recurring G&A guidance by about $50 million at the midpoint and characterized the reduction as durable. The preview discussed integration costs as a risk but did not anticipate this run-rate cost reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year recurring G&A guidance was lowered by approximately $50 million at the midpoint, described as a durable run-rate reduction driven by accelerated integration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “integration costs persist beyond Q1’s $135M” as a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: The company redeemed all $819 million of its 2026 senior notes and called its remaining 2027 notes, leaving no senior note maturities until mid-2028. The preview expected divestiture proceeds to reduce debt, but did not anticipate this specific extension of the maturity runway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Used Galvan divestiture proceeds to redeem all $819 million of 2026 senior notes and called the remaining 2027 notes, leaving no senior note maturities until mid-2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “~$900M net South Texas divestiture proceeds applied to debt” and modeled net debt of “~$6.2–6.5B.”

surprises.description: Uinta completion pace exceeded 2,600 feet per day—more than twice its early-2026 rate—and delivered over $1 million per well in savings over six months. The preview highlighted Uinta execution as a risk and noted the move to 4-mile laterals, making the reported execution and cost savings favorable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Uinta completion pace exceeded 2,600 feet per day (more than double the early-2026 rate), delivering over $1 million per well in cost savings over the past six months alongside 4-mile lateral development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Uinta carries the portfolio’s best cash margin … and is moving to 4-mile laterals; Uinta execution is also the risk third parties flag most often on this name.”

surprises.description: The Galvan divestiture substantially achieved the company’s $1 billion divestiture target within a year of the merger and was used to high-grade South Texas toward higher-margin, liquids-rich Austin Chalk development. The preview noted South Texas divestiture proceeds but did not spell out this target achievement or portfolio shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Galvan divestiture substantially achieved the $1 billion divestiture target within a year of the merger and high-graded South Texas toward higher-margin, liquids-rich Austin Chalk development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview mentioned “~$900M net South Texas divestiture proceeds applied to debt,” but did not discuss the target achievement or the Austin Chalk shift.

in_line: Adjusted net income of $526 million, or $2.19 per diluted share, was within the preview’s $2.00–$2.20 adjusted EPS estimate range, although above the cited $1.93 consensus.
Adjusted EBITDAX of $1.4 billion matched the preview’s estimate of approximately $1.40 billion.
Net debt of approximately $6.25 billion was within the preview’s modeled range of $6.2–6.5 billion.
Full-year capital guidance of $2.65–2.85 billion was reaffirmed, as the preview expected.

SM executed $84 million of buybacks and paid $53 million in dividends. The preview expected buybacks to commence and described a modest start as its base case; the $150 million-plus figure appeared only in its bull scenario.
The $375 million run-rate synergy target was not raised, consistent with the preview’s base case, even though actioning progress exceeded its estimate.

surprises.description: Merck reported Q2 revenue of $16.6 billion, about $270 million above the $16.33 billion consensus and above the preview’s $16.3–$16.5 billion base case. The beat was positive but not as large as the preview’s $16.7 billion bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $16.6 billion, up 5% (4% ex-FX)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … $16.33B”; base case “$16.3–16.5B”; bull case “$16.7B+”

surprises.description: The KEYTRUDA family brought in $8.4 billion, well above the $8.06 billion estimate, with 4% growth versus the preview’s expected 1.3%. This total-sales beat came alongside management’s caution that U.S. growth will moderate as key indications approach peak penetration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “KEYTRUDA family sales rose 4% to $8.4 billion,” while management said “U.S. KEYTRUDA growth will moderate as key indications reach peak penetration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Keytruda (total, incl. Qlex) $8.06B, +1.3%”; consensus implied “US ~$4.73B, ~flat/-0.4%.”

surprises.description: WELIREG sales reached $271 million, substantially above the $214 million estimate, and grew 67% rather than the expected roughly 8%. Merck also reported a newly secured earlier-stage adjuvant renal-cell-carcinoma indication.
surprises.fact_evidence: “WELIREG sales grew 67% to $271 million” and it “secured its first earlier-stage indication (adjuvant renal cell carcinoma) via the LITESPARK-022 approval.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Welireg $214M | +~8%.”

surprises.description: Management described accelerated pipeline de-risking, including positive Phase III readouts for sac-TMT and tulisokibart and an IDXD readout occurring earlier than the previously expected 2027 timing. The preview did not anticipate these specific readouts or the faster timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “accelerated pipeline de-risking” and “positive Phase III readouts for sac-TMT (endometrial cancer), tulisokibart (ulcerative colitis induction), and IDXD occurring faster than the previously expected 2027 timing.”

surprises.description: Merck lowered its full-year gross-margin outlook to about 81% because of higher inventory reserves, below the preview’s roughly 82% margin framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin was lowered to approximately 81% on higher inventory reserves.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin ~82% (mgmt framing).”

surprises.description: The new full-year EPS range of $2.66–$2.76 was above the preview’s mechanically Terns-adjusted range of roughly $2.57–$2.69, with the new midpoint about $0.08 higher. This is a modestly favorable guidance difference, though the range overlaps the prior mechanical estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised and narrowed full-year 2026 … EPS guidance to $2.66–$2.76.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Mechanically folding Terns in takes $5.04–5.16 → ~ $2.57–$2.69”; the preview also said the tell was whether “the ex-charge midpoint moves up.”

surprises.description: The reported Q2 loss was $0.13 per share, better than the expected $0.26 loss. The Terns charge was also slightly smaller than anticipated—$2.31 per share versus about $2.35—so the headline beat largely reflects the one-time accounting charge rather than operating EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merck reported a Q2 loss of $0.13 per share,” driven by a “one-time $2.31 per share (~$5.7 billion) charge from the Terns Pharmaceuticals acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus Q2 non-GAAP EPS is –$0.26”; the preview said this embeds a “~$5.8B (~$2.35/sh) one-time asset-acquisition charge for Terns Pharmaceuticals.”

surprises.description: QLEX sales were $463 million, with adoption increasing after the permanent J-code took effect. The preview highlighted conversion as an important watch item and cited a 30–40% target over 18–24 months, but provided no Q2 sales estimate; the reported sales therefore indicate meaningful early uptake without a precise forecast comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “KEYTRUDA QLEX generated $463 million with adoption increasing since the permanent J-code took effect in April.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “targets 30–40% conversion within 18–24 months” and flagged QLEX revenue and conversion as a key metric; it cited Q1 sales of $128 million.

surprises.description: Merck reported FDA approval of LIPFENDRA and said it is targeting roughly 30 million untreated U.S. patients rather than patients switching from injectable PCSK9 drugs. The preview expected launch commentary but did not identify this specific target-market strategy.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merck received FDA approval for LIPFENDRA, the first oral PCSK9 inhibitor,” with management “targeting the ~30 million untreated U.S. patients rather than switching from injectables.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for Lipfendra launch commentary on “access/formulary wins, DTC strategy, script trajectory, capacity.”

in_line: WINREVAIR sales of $588 million were within the preview’s estimated Q2 range of roughly $570–$600 million.

The revenue guidance raise and narrowing to $66.3–$67.3 billion was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation for a raise toward the upper half of the prior range and roughly $66.5 billion or more.
The approximately $3 billion share-repurchase pace matched the preview’s stated plan.
Management’s warning that the prior-year wholesaler timing benefit would not repeat in Q3 was anticipated: the preview flagged a Q3 headwind from the Q3 2025 wholesaler benefit.

surprises.description: Revenue growth was stronger than the preview’s consensus implied: revenue rose 13% sequentially versus an expected 8.3%, and 50% year over year versus an expected 43%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenues increased 50% year-over-year and 13% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus revenue of $9.44M, “+43%” year over year and “+8.3%” sequentially.

surprises.description: The company reported its first-ever positive operating cash flow at the consolidated level, a milestone the preview did not forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company achieved its first-ever positive cash flow from operating activities of roughly $500,000.”

surprises.description: Sky Harbor Capital generated nearly $3 million of quarterly operating cash flow and extended its streak to ten consecutive positive-cash-flow quarters; the preview did not discuss this group-level cash-flow record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The obligated group (Sky Harbor Capital) grew revenues 79% year-over-year and 22% sequentially, with quarterly operating cash flow of nearly $3 million, up from $2.2 million a year ago, marking 10 consecutive quarters of positive operating cash flow.”

surprises.description: The company proceeded with a $40 million equity placement despite the preview identifying new equity as a negative surprise given the existing liquidity and the share price above $11. The placement was priced at a 4.6% discount to the 30-day VWAP.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised $40 million via a direct equity placement at $10 per share (a 4.6% discount to the 30-day VWAP).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Any equity signal is a negative surprise at $11+,” and that “New equity would be the negative narrative shift.”

surprises.description: Construction activity is scaling rapidly: the company reported a record $65 million year-to-date increase in assets under construction and completed construction, and said space under construction is expected to roughly double by year-end. The preview discussed existing projects and their schedules but did not anticipate this expansion in construction scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Assets under construction and completed construction reached over $393 million, a $65 million year-to-date increase representing the highest six-month growth in company history”; space under construction is “set to roughly double” to over 1.2 million square feet by year-end.

in_line: Management reaffirmed the $42–$46 million annualized revenue run rate and $4–$6 million annualized adjusted EBITDA run rate for year-end, as the preview’s base case expected.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative but improved to approximately negative $0.9 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would remain negative while narrowing.
The 19% average rent step-up on trailing-12-month lease renewals was in the teens, which the preview said was acceptable, although it was below the previously reported 23% re-leasing escalation.

Construction cost was about $242 per square foot versus the preview’s cited $244.37 per square foot GMP average on undelivered projects, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of falling costs.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $15.1 million, below the preview’s $16–18 million estimate, and the margin was 13% rather than the roughly 14% implied by the preview’s base case. That leaves more of the full-year target dependent on second-half performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA fell to $15.1 million from $17.3 million a year earlier, with margin compressing to 13%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 est. | ~$16–18M”; the base case expected “$16–17M (~14%).”

surprises.description: Intelligence & Advisory declined more sharply in Q2 than the preview’s discussion of possible inflection off consulting weakness suggested: the segment fell 7.1%, with softer consulting bookings cited as the main driver. The preview had flagged consulting weakness, but not a further acceleration in the decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Intelligence & Advisory revenue declined 7.1% year-over-year in Q2 and 5.5% in the first half, driven primarily by softer consulting bookings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I&A/Omdia ($30.9M, −3.9%): any inflection off go-to-market consulting weakness?”

surprises.description: Brand to Demand did not reaccelerate: after growing 4.7% in Q1, it declined 1.7% in Q2, although it remained up 1.2% for the first half. This was weaker than the preview’s bull-case requirement for a return to high-single-digit growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brand to Demand revenue declined 1.7% in Q2 to $85.9 million but grew 1.2% for the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bull needs B2D back to high-single-digit growth”; the preview also asked, “B2D ($75.2M, +4.7% in Q1, 71% of mix): is it decelerating?”

surprises.description: Management offered positive pipeline and deal-size signals to support its confidence in second-half acceleration, but backlog was broadly flat and the reported facts do not provide a quantified EBITDA or margin bridge. The outlook therefore had more qualitative support than the preview’s bull case called for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management cited a weighted pipeline value materially up year-over-year, higher average deal values, and stable win rates and sales cycles as the basis for confidence in second-half acceleration, with backlog broadly flat entering H2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the guide was “reaffirmed but H2 back-loading questioned” and that the bull case required “a credible, quantified H2 cost bridge.”

surprises.description: Intelligence subscription ACV was flat overall despite double-digit growth in AI, data center and cloud, as weakness in telecoms and service providers offset it. The AI-related growth provides some evidence of monetization, but it did not translate into growth in total subscription ACV.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Intelligence subscription ACV was broadly flat, with double-digit growth in AI, data center and cloud offset by weakness in telecoms and service providers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described AI as an opportunity and said to “watch for monetization evidence.”

surprises.description: Q2 GAAP net loss was far smaller than the prior-year loss, which had included a noncash goodwill impairment; the preview had identified another impairment test as a live risk. The reported figures did not show a comparable impairment-driven loss this quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss narrowed dramatically to $21.7 million in Q2 from $398.7 million a year earlier, which had included a noncash goodwill impairment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Goodwill impairment #4” as a key metric to watch and said “another test is live”; its bear scenario included “new impairment.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $116.1 million, within the preview’s implied range of roughly $115–117 million; first-half revenue was also broadly flat, as anticipated.
Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth guidance, including the $95–100 million adjusted EBITDA range, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Under Armour cut its FY27 revenue outlook from a slight decline to a mid-single-digit decline, a clear deterioration from the preview’s expected slight-decline outlook. It kept adjusted operating income guidance at $140 million to $160 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its full-year fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to a mid-single-digit decline (from previously slightly down) due to softer consumer demand, while maintaining its adjusted operating income guidance of $140 million to $160 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guide… revenue slight decline”; “FY27 adj. EPS guide ($0.08–$0.12): reiterate, raise, or trim.”

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $1.1 billion, down 3%, slightly below the $1.11 billion consensus and the preview’s base-case range of $1.11–$1.12 billion, though it was around the low end of company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 revenue declined 3% to $1.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue… Consensus $1.11B (range $1.10–1.12B)”; base case: “$1.11–1.12B (-1 to -2%).”

surprises.description: North America revenue fell 9%, worse than the preview’s expected 7%–8% decline and below the stabilization trajectory investors were watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America down 9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “North America… Co. guidance: -7% to -8%”; “Any read that NA is tracking better than -7% reframes the year.”

surprises.description: The quarter’s gross-margin expansion was far greater than the preview’s expected 30–80 basis points: margin rose 590 basis points, with a 640-basis-point contribution from IEEPA tariff refunds. The refunds were recognized despite the preview highlighting uncertainty around their timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 590 basis points year-over-year to 54.1%, driven largely by 640 basis points of benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds related to fiscal 2026 costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q1 GM print of only +30–80bps YoY is consistent with the full-year guide”; “refunds of duties already paid remain procedurally unsettled.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating income and EPS both beat the company’s Q1 outlook: operating income was $52 million versus a $30–$40 million range, and EPS was $0.05 versus $0.00–$0.02 guidance. EPS also exceeded the preview’s $0.02 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income of $52 million significantly exceeded the company's outlook range of $30 million to $40 million, and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.05 also beat guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating income… $30–40M”; “Adj. diluted EPS… $0.00–$0.02”; consensus EPS “$0.02.”

surprises.description: Management reversed the expected increase in marketing investment: it now expects marketing to fall as a share of revenue and in absolute dollars, rather than adding the incremental marketing spend embedded in the preview’s discussion of the full-year plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects marketing spend to decline as a percentage of revenue (toward the low end of the 10%-11% range) and in absolute dollars, reversing prior guidance for higher marketing investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The FY27 guide “embeds… ~$30M of incremental marketing”; the base case expected marketing spend “weighted to the back half.”

surprises.description: The Q2 EPS outlook was below UBS’s previewed $0.03–$0.05 expectation: Under Armour guided to an adjusted loss of $0.01–$0.03 per share. The preview had warned that a Q2 guide below $0.03 would imply a more back-loaded year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For Q2, the company guided to… an adjusted diluted loss per share of $0.01 to $0.03.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “UBS preview… Q2 guide of $0.03–$0.05”; “A Q2 guide below $0.03 implies an even more back-loaded year.”

surprises.description: Traffic weakened sharply from mid-to-late May, particularly in North America and APAC, and China faced additional stock-outs and aggressive discounting by licensees. This added a specific deterioration in recent demand and China conditions to the preview’s concerns about stabilization and the order book.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Traffic deteriorated sharply from mid-to-late May forward, particularly in North America and Asia Pacific, with China further hurt by stock-outs and aggressive discounting by licensees.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the fall/holiday order book “the forward signal” and flagged North America as “the swing factor.”

surprises.description: DTC weakness extended beyond the preview’s reference to prior-year e-commerce declines: e-commerce fell 12%, owned stores fell 3%, and DTC overall fell 6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DTC revenue fell 6% (e-commerce down 12%, owned stores down 3%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “eCommerce -7% in FY26; owned stores +1%. Deliberate discount restraint has cost e-comm volume — has that annualized?”

surprises.description: Footwear declined 8%, less than the double-digit decline contemplated in the preview’s bear case and an improvement on the prior-year declines highlighted there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Footwear revenue declined 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear case described “footwear still down double digits”; the preview cited declines of “-11% in FY26” and “-14% in Q1 FY26.”

surprises.description: Under Armour announced another planned 25% SKU reduction over the next 18 months, beyond the 25% reduction the preview said was already complete, targeting roughly 40% cumulative reduction by FY28.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Targeting an additional 25% SKU reduction over the next 18 months, building on a prior 25% cut, for a cumulative reduction of roughly 40% by the end of fiscal 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~25% SKU reduction is complete.”

surprises.description: APAC revenue fell 7% (10% in constant currency), diverging from the preview’s expectation of low-single-digit growth for EMEA/APAC in the full year; EMEA and Latin America instead grew 12% and 8%, respectively.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC down 7% (10% constant currency), while EMEA rose 12% and Latin America rose 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “International… EMEA/APAC LSD growth (FY).”

in_line: FY27 adjusted operating income guidance remained $140 million to $160 million, as the preview expected the existing range to be reiterated.
Inventory declined 3%, matching the preview’s stated expectation of a 3% decline.

The company had incurred $266 million of its planned approximately $305 million restructuring cost, close to the preview’s $261 million incurred through FY26; the preview’s concern about another extension was not borne out by the facts provided.

surprises.description: Vanda's Q2 net loss was $62.5 million, far worse than the preview's estimate of about $36 million implied by consensus EPS and its own estimated EPS loss of roughly $0.76. The call attributed the higher loss to R&D and SG&A spending on clinical programs and commercial launches.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vanda posted a Q2 2026 net loss of $62.5 million,” driven by “higher R&D and SG&A tied to clinical programs and commercial launches.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus EPS of −$0.60 implies a net loss near $36M”; the preview's estimate was “≈ −$0.76.”

surprises.description: Hetlios sales were only $5.6 million versus the preview's $14.5 million estimate. Generic competition and a shipment timing issue explain much of the gap, although the preview had already expected generic erosion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hetlios net product sales fell 66% year-over-year to $5.6 million” due to generic competition and a shipment timing issue that “pushed roughly $7 million of revenue into Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Hetlios at “$14.5M” and noted generic erosion, with management warning the decline was “potentially significant.”

surprises.description: Nereus recognized just $1 million in sales, below the preview's $2.5 million estimate. The call also revealed that most initial wholesaler stocking was constrained over demand and return uncertainties, a further indication that the launch's early sales were limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nereus generated only $1 million in recognized net product sales”; “$12.6 million of the $15.2 million initial wholesaler stocking was constrained due to demand and return uncertainties.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “NEREUS … $2.5M” for Q2 and said “~$0–1M turns the guide into a liability.”

surprises.description: The $150–170 million 2026 product-sales target was described as combined FNAPT and Basanti, whereas the preview presented that range as the Fanapt guide and noted that Basanti had no separate forecast. Including Basanti in the same range makes the target less supportive of Fanapt sales alone, though the combined range still implies growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined FNAPT and Basanti 2026 net product sales are guided at $150–170 million,” implying roughly 36% growth versus 2025 FNAPT revenue, with Basanti launch expected in the second half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the “FY2026 guide” for “Fanapt” as “$150–170M” and said management “did not separately forecast BYSANTI revenue.”

surprises.description: The preview modeled cash and securities of about $155 million at quarter-end; Vanda reported $170 million. Management also said existing funding should last through at least the end of 2027, addressing the preview's central concern about funding the launch cycle and 2027 runway.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cash, equivalents and marketable securities were “$170 million as of June 30, 2026,” and management guided to funding “through at least end of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash + securities (EOQ) … ≈ $155M” and described funding the launch cycle before Fanapt's November 2027 loss of exclusivity as the central question.

surprises.description: Management gave a specific outlook for operating expenses to start declining by year-end 2026 and fall more substantially in 2027 as Phase 3 programs and commercial supply build-out conclude. The preview raised opex as a key issue but did not anticipate this expense-reduction timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses [are expected] to begin decreasing by end of 2026 and more substantially in 2027” as Phase 3 programs and commercial supply build-out conclude.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “Opex trajectory” and asked whether there would be “any sign of a ceiling,” but gave no expense-reduction timing.

surprises.description: The Hetlios jet-lag disorder application is moving to a formal FDA administrative hearing culminating in December 2026, with a favorable judge recommendation only hoped for in early 2027. This regulatory process and uncertainty were not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Hetlios jet-lag disorder application is proceeding to a formal FDA administrative hearing culminating in December 2026,” with a favorable judge recommendation hoped for in early 2027.

surprises.description: FNAPT sales came in modestly above the preview's estimate, at $36 million versus $35 million, with prescriptions also up strongly year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FNAPT net product sales grew 23% year-over-year to $36 million,” with total prescriptions up 31% and new-to-brand prescriptions up 32%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Fanapt at “$35.0M.”

in_line: Vanda reiterated full-year 2026 total revenue guidance of $240–290 million, as the preview specifically identified holding that range as an important outcome.
Management said 2026 cash burn will exceed 2025, consistent with the preview's statement that management had explicitly guided to greater 2026 cash burn.
The December 12, 2026 PDUFA date was already flagged in the preview as an upcoming catalyst.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue guidance of $415–425 million was well above the preview’s $375–390 million level it said might be needed to satisfy marginal buyers, and far above the $360–365 million implied by FY26 consensus. Management also forecast 35% sequential Data Center growth and 20% I&D growth, pointing to broader strength than a Data Center-only ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY26 guidance calls for revenue of $415-425 million” and implies “about 35% sequential Data Center growth and 20% I&D growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Assume $375–390M is what's needed to satisfy the marginal buyer”; FY26 consensus “implies Q4 of roughly $360–365M.”

surprises.description: The quarter beat the preview’s consensus and the company’s prior guidance: revenue was $342.2 million versus $335.1 million consensus and a $331–339 million guide, while adjusted EPS was $1.40 versus $1.34 consensus and a $1.31–1.37 guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY26 revenue was $342.2 million” and “adjusted EPS of $1.40.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$335.1M”; company guide was “$331–339M.” Consensus EPS was “$1.34”; company guide was “$1.31–$1.37.”

surprises.description: Data Center revenue came in above the preview’s build, and the FY26 growth trajectory moved above the preview’s roughly 70% bull-case trigger. The preview estimated about $132.6 million for the quarter and described a raise toward ~70% as a potential catalyst; reported revenue was $137.6 million and the company is trending toward roughly 74% full-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data Center revenue reached a record $137.6 million” and is “trending toward roughly 74% full-year growth in FY26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q3 Data Center revenue at “~$132.6M” and said to watch for “a third raise toward ~70%.”

surprises.description: Bookings strengthened further rather than merely sustaining the preview’s already-record Q2 level: book-to-bill reached 1.6:1 versus 1.5:1 at Q2, with the highest quarterly bookings in company history.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 book-to-bill ratio hit a record 1.6:1 with the highest quarterly bookings in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q2 book-to-bill of “1.5:1” and said “≥1.3x sustains the upgrade cycle.”

surprises.description: Management gave a stronger FY27 Data Center growth frame than the preview’s >40% watch threshold: Data Center is trending toward 50% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Annualizing Q4 guidance implies “Data Center trending toward 50% year-over-year growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that “any qualitative FY27 Data Center framing (>40% growth?) sets the 2027 bar.”

surprises.description: Management set out a steep operating-margin trajectory—approximately 37% in Q4 and a target of breaching 40% in FY27—which the preview had not forecast, despite discussing operating leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted operating margin was “31.5%,” with Q4 “guided to approximately 37%” and a “target of breaching 40% in FY27.”

surprises.description: The company raised its 2027 serviceable addressable market estimate to approximately $15 billion, with Data Center and I&D each representing about $6 billion. The preview did not flag a higher market-size estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2027 SAM estimate to approximately $15 billion” and said it was “up 20-30% from 2026.”

surprises.description: Management described a broader base of large customers than the preview had discussed: customers contributing more than $10 million grew from about 8 two years ago to over 20, while the top 10 end-customers remain under 40% of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers above $10 million in revenue grew from about 8 two years ago to over 20 today”; “top 10 end-customers remain under 40% of total revenue.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a $61 million investment in IQE and a $41 million noncash GAAP gain associated with it, which was excluded from non-GAAP results. This investment and one-off accounting gain were not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “made a $61 million investment in IQE that generated a $41 million noncash GAAP gain excluded from non-GAAP results.”

in_line: Adjusted gross margin was 59.7%, consistent with the preview’s ~59.5% expectation and 59.0–60.0% company guide; Q4 guidance of 60–61% also supports the preview’s expectation of an approximately 60% exit.

Annualizing Q4 guidance midpoint implies FY27 company growth of roughly 27–28%, broadly in line with the preview’s FY27 consensus growth implied by $1.60 billion of revenue versus $1.26 billion for FY26.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was about $1.44, inferred from the reported $0.21 increase to $1.23 a year earlier, well above the preview’s $1.26 consensus. The company said trailing-four-quarter repurchases of about $650 million helped drive the 17% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 17% ($0.21) year-over-year,” aided by “approximately $650 million in share repurchases” over the trailing four quarters.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS **$1.26**” for Q2 consensus.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin reached 11.3%, above the preview’s roughly 10.9% guide-implied expectation. Every business unit also expanded margins, rather than the preview’s key concern being whether pressure in weaker businesses would ease.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin expanded 100 basis points to 11.3%” and “every business unit expanded margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. op. margin ~10.9% (guide-implied)”; the preview also flagged “BES trajectory + PDS loss” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $492 million, substantially above the preview’s $250 million checkpoint for validating the full-year cash-flow bridge after only $13 million in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Generated $492 million of free cash flow during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FCF >$250M in the quarter confirming the FY bridge”; the preview noted Q1 FCF was “only $13M.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year adjusted EPS range to $5.05–$5.30 from $5.00–$5.20, lifting the top end above the preview’s $5.18 Street estimate. The increase was primarily due to first-half buybacks, rather than an improvement to the sales, margin, or FCF outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.05-$5.30 (from $5.00-$5.20) primarily due to first-half buybacks,” while sales, margin, and FCF guidance were maintained.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Street FY26 sits at $14.18B / $5.18 EPS”; the preview called for a possible guide “to ~$5.05–5.20” in its base case.

surprises.description: The Board added $1 billion to the buyback authorization, bringing the total to $1.35 billion through 2029. The preview discussed buybacks as dependent on cash generation but did not anticipate this larger authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved a $1 billion increase to the buyback authorization,” bringing total authorization to “$1.35 billion” through 2029.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FCF “gates the buyback” and noted recent repurchases, but did not forecast an authorization increase.

surprises.description: The effective full-year margin midpoint was described as 10.6% after incremental second-half industrial R&D spending, below the preview’s 10.8% midpoint expectation. The spending supports data-center product readiness, but is a near-term margin cost.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Increasing second-half industrial R&D spending by an incremental $10-15 million,” lowering the midpoint to “10.6% (from 10.8% excluding it),” to accelerate data-center product readiness.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. op. margin 10.7–10.9%”; the preview also framed the expected margin around “~10.9%.”

surprises.description: The battery business is now expected to weigh about 170 basis points on full-year sales growth, around 20 basis points more than the preview’s estimate. The underlying pressures—lack of North American incentives and weaker European demand—were already anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The battery business is expected to be a roughly 170 basis point headwind to full-year sales growth” due to “lack of North American incentives and weaker European demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “BES is a ~$210M / ~150bp headwind to FY growth on weak NA EV incentives and European demand.”

surprises.description: Management’s China production outlook of down 4–7% extends below the preview’s expected down 4% to down 1.5% range. With China representing about 20% of global sales, this is a weaker regional outlook than the preview’s market assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China represents about 20% of global sales,” and management guides “regional production to China down 4-7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s market assumption was “China −4% to −1.5%.”

surprises.description: Sales were roughly flat year over year, better than the preview’s 1.5% decline expectation, and slightly above the $3.58 billion consensus. The difference was modest, with the reported amount only just over $3.6 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales exceeded $3.6 billion, roughly flat year-over-year,” with organic sales up 0.5%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue **$3.58B**” consensus and “−1.5%” year over year.

in_line: Full-year sales guidance of $14.0–$14.3 billion and FCF guidance of $900 million–$1.1 billion were maintained, in line with the preview’s stated guidance.
The full-year organic sales outlook of down 3.5% to down 1.5% remained unchanged, consistent with the preview’s guidance.

The turbine generator program remained on track for a 2027 launch with 2 GW of announced capacity and about $300 million of first-year revenue, consistent with the preview’s stated program outlook. No expansion beyond 2 GW or second customer was reported, matching the preview’s base case of no new capacity news.
Europe’s production outlook was down slightly, broadly consistent with the preview’s expected decline-to-flat range.

surprises.description: Thryv cut FY2026 SaaS adjusted EBITDA guidance to $42–44 million from $70–75 million, far below the preview’s expected range. Management attributed the reduction to first-half underinvestment in sales headcount and marketing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Thryv lowered its full-year SaaS revenue guidance to $453-457 million and SaaS adjusted EBITDA guidance to $42-44 million, reflecting first-half underinvestment in sales headcount and marketing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SaaS adj. EBITDA $70–75M”

surprises.description: FY2026 SaaS revenue guidance was lowered to $453–457 million, below the preview’s expected $463–471 million range. This is a clear downward revision, though smaller than the cut to SaaS adjusted EBITDA guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Thryv lowered its full-year SaaS revenue guidance to $453-457 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SaaS revenue $463–471M”

surprises.description: Seasoned net revenue retention was 90%, below the preview’s 92–93% base-case expectation, while SaaS subscribers ended at 95,000 versus the 96,000 figure highlighted in the preview. This points to somewhat greater customer attrition than expected, though the NRR result was at—not below—the preview’s cited 90% concern threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Seasoned net revenue retention was 90%, reflecting attrition of smaller, lower-spend clients”; “ending the quarter with 95,000 SaaS subscribers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NRR ~92–93%” and “SaaS client count (96,000)”; the preview also said “NRR below ~90%” would signal uncontrolled churn.

surprises.description: Reported leverage was 2.5x, materially above the preview’s cited 1.6–1.7x, even though ending net debt of $241 million was below the preview’s $258.6 million snapshot. The leverage figure therefore came in worse than the preview’s stated expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with net debt of $241 million and a 2.5x leverage ratio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net debt $258.6M ... leverage ~1.6–1.7x.”

surprises.description: Thryv announced an approximately $25 million restructuring charge, split between workforce reductions and vendor spend, with roughly $60 million in expected run-rate savings. The preview discussed the need for cost actions in a possible bull case but did not anticipate this specific charge-and-savings plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a restructuring charge of approximately $25 million (split evenly between workforce reductions and vendor spend) expected to yield roughly $60 million in run-rate savings.”

surprises.description: Thryv raised the low end of its FY2026 Marketing Services revenue guidance to $161 million from the preview’s $157 million low end, a modestly better outlook for the legacy business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raising the low end of marketing services revenue guidance to $161-163 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Marketing Services revenue $157–163M”

surprises.description: Thryv’s reported adjusted EBITDA for Q2 SaaS was $13.6 million, above the preview’s expected $12–13 million range, including a result above its high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 SaaS revenue was $114.5 million with adjusted gross margin of 66.6% and adjusted EBITDA of $13.6 million (12% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SaaS adj. EBITDA ... $12–13M (~10.4–11.3% mgn)”

surprises.description: Thryv was reclassified by the JICs as a software company, a new external validation of its transformation that the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SaaS now represents 76% of Thryv's total revenue, and the company was reclassified by the JICs as a software company, validating its transformation to a pure-play SaaS business.”

surprises.description: Thryv announced strategic partnerships with Wix and Ooma and integrations with Breezy and Jobber to broaden distribution. These specific ecosystem relationships were not part of the preview’s stated expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company entered strategic partnerships with Wix and Ooma and launched integrations with Breezy and Jobber to expand distribution into new customer ecosystems.”

in_line: Q2 SaaS revenue was $114.5 million, within the preview’s $114–115 million expectation.
Q2 adjusted SaaS gross margin was 66.6%, broadly in line with the preview’s reference point of 67% and its expectation that migration-related dilution could weigh on the metric.
Thryv said it plans to begin migrating its existing customer base to the new platform in 2027, consistent with the preview’s focus on a 2027 platform and growth framework.

surprises.description: Revenue grew 48% year over year, well above the preview’s roughly 31–32% consensus growth estimate. That is a much larger top-line beat than the preview’s base case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 48% versus Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue consensus is tight and reliable (~$20.3–20.7B)” and the consensus table showed implied YoY growth of “+31%” to “+32%.”

surprises.description: Even including $3.30 per share of acquired IPR&D charges, non-GAAP EPS was $8.38. Adding back that stated charge implies $11.68 before the charge, above the preview’s $8.84 ex-large-IPR&D consensus and its $9.10–9.40 base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $8.38 (including $3.30 of acquired IPR&D charges).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS — ex-large IPR&D” consensus was “$8.84”; the preview’s “Working base case” was “non-GAAP EPS $9.10–9.40 ex-IPR&D.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 86.3%, 2.9 percentage points above the preview’s 83.4% consensus. The margin result was substantially stronger than expected despite the preview’s concern about capacity scaling and lower-priced mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin rose 1.3 points to 86.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin” consensus was “83.4%.”

surprises.description: Mounjaro and Zepbound together generated $14.9 billion, above the preview’s base-case combined estimate of about $13.6 billion and even above its bull-case threshold of more than $14.1 billion. Their $6.3 billion contribution to year-over-year growth also shows these products drove a particularly strong quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mounjaro and Zepbound combined for $14.9 billion in revenue and contributed $6.3 billion of year-over-year growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Q2 ~$9.2B / ~$4.4B” for Mounjaro and Zepbound; its bull case called for “Mounjaro >$9.5B, Zepbound >$4.6B.”

surprises.description: Lilly raised full-year revenue guidance to $85–87 billion, putting the new floor at the top of the preview’s expected $83–85 billion base-case band and the top end above it. The preview expected a raise, but this was stronger than its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lilly raised full-year revenue guidance to $85–$87 billion (up $3 billion at the low end and $2 billion at the high end).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the guide to be raised to the “$83–85B” band; its bull case was “$84–86B.”

surprises.description: The underlying full-year EPS outlook increased by $2.78 at the midpoint before the IPR&D charge, as the preview expected an upward revision. But after the $3.03 per-share charge impact, the stated $35.50–36.50 range has a lower high end than the existing $35.50–37.00 range, so the reported range did not deliver the anticipated upward reset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Lilly] lifted non-GAAP EPS guidance to $35.50–$36.50, a $2.78 midpoint increase before the $3.03 IPR&D charge impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The existing guidance was “$35.50B – $37.00” and the preview’s base case expected the “EPS band narrowed upward.”

surprises.description: U.S. net price declined only 3% on the reported measure, better than the preview’s low-to-mid-teens full-year erosion concern. The decline was 9% excluding favorable rebate and discount estimate adjustments, which narrows the apparent outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. net price declined 3% (or 9% excluding favorable rebate/discount estimate adjustments).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided to “low-to-mid-teens price erosion for FY26” and noted Q1 U.S. price decline of “~7–10%.”

surprises.description: Foundayo’s reported launch indicators were stronger than the preview’s concern about scripts declining for three straight weeks: prescribers rose from about 8,000 to 36,000, it reached roughly one in four U.S. new starts, and management said volume doubled in late July versus a month earlier. The call facts do not provide quarterly revenue, so the preview’s revenue estimate cannot be assessed here.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Orforglipron (Foundayo) prescribers grew from about 8,000 to 36,000, U.S. new starts reached roughly 1 in 4, and management cited volume doubling in the last week of July versus a month earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Foundayo scripts were “down for three straight weeks” after peaking in week 10 and asked whether management would “reaffirm the launch trajectory, or reset it.”

surprises.description: The Medicare bridge launch matched the preview’s expected July 1 timing and $50 monthly price, but the call added evidence of a sizable coverage expansion and early uptake: 20 million eligible seniors, a 35% increase in U.S. obesity-medicine coverage, and most early users being new patients.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Medicare GLP-1 bridge program launched July 1 [and] gives 20 million eligible seniors obesity coverage at $50 per month, expanding U.S. obesity-medicine coverage by 35%, with early uptake skewing ~80% injectable and 60%-70% new patients.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “July 1 Medicare GLP-1 Bridge at $50/mo” and said guidance commentary on its impact would matter, but did not give these coverage or uptake figures.

surprises.description: The call reported positive results in three Phase III retatrutide trials, including high-dose weight loss approaching bariatric-surgery levels and a large reduction in osteoarthritis knee pain. The preview mentioned possible early-2027 filing color, but did not anticipate these trial results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retatrutide posted positive results in three Phase III Triumph trials (with high-dose weight loss approaching bariatric-surgery levels and ~75% osteoarthritis knee-pain reduction).”

surprises.description: Lilly reported that selpercatinib cut recurrence or death risk by 83% in adjuvant RET-positive lung cancer. The preview did not identify this readout as an expectation or debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Selpercatinib reduced risk of recurrence or death by 83% versus placebo in adjuvant RET-positive lung cancer.”

surprises.description: Lilly also reported a substantial pirtobrutinib benefit in previously treated CLL, including among patients previously treated with a BTK inhibitor. This result was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pirtobrutinib cut progression or death by 45% (68% after prior BTK inhibitor) in previously treated CLL.”

in_line: The Medicare GLP-1 bridge program’s July 1 launch and $50 monthly price matched the preview’s description.
Retatrutide’s planned U.S. filing timing in early 2027 was consistent with the preview’s reference to early-2027 BLA timing.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.12B, above the $1.08B consensus and the company’s $1.07–1.08B guide. It reached the preview’s upper whisper range, so the beat was against consensus rather than beyond the most optimistic preview case.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue reached $1.12 billion, up 36% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance, with a record quarter-over-quarter revenue addition of $115 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was $1.08B; the preview’s functional buy-side whisper was closer to $1.10–1.12B, with a $95–110M sequential add.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $1.135–1.145B fell short of the preview’s $1.16B-or-higher bull-case threshold and implies a sharp slowdown from Q2’s 36% growth to 28–29%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 revenue guidance of $1.135–$1.145 billion implies decelerating growth of 28–29% year-over-year, notably below the 36% posted in Q2.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q3 guide ≥$1.16B” in its key metric ranking and listed “Q3 guide ≥$1.16B” among the bull-case conditions.

surprises.description: Management disclosed that its largest customer will reduce usage beginning in Q3, a concrete instance of the optimization risk the preview warned about. The customer’s nine-figure renewal and management’s statement that the reduction was fully derisked in Q3 and full-year guidance partly offset the concern.
