surprises.fact_evidence: Management disclosed a usage reduction from its largest customer beginning in Q3, which they fully derisked in both Q3 and full-year 2026 guidance despite the customer signing a 9-figure renewal.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said any “renegotiation, in-housing, or optimization language” would be a multi-turn de-rate and identified largest-customer concentration commentary as a key debate.

surprises.description: Full-year revenue guidance rose to $4.45–4.47B, above the preview’s roughly $4.42B buy-side bar. The preview’s bull case anticipated $4.45B or more, so the increase cleared the central bar but landed at the bull-case level; full-year EPS guidance also rose above the previously stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $4.45–$4.47 billion (30% growth) with non-GAAP EPS of $2.50–$2.54.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview set a functional buy-side bar of “≥$4.42B” and a bull case of “FY26 guide to $4.45B+”; it listed the then-current full-year revenue guide as $4.30–4.34B and EPS as $2.36–2.44.

surprises.description: Q2 operating margin reached 23%, above the preview’s expected 21–22% range. This was a modestly better profitability result than the preview’s operating-income estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 operating margin improved to 23% from 20% a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated non-GAAP operating income of about $230M, or a 21–22% margin, and listed Q2 company guidance of 21–22%.

surprises.description: Free-cash-flow margin was 25%, below the preview’s expectation of at least 27%, although free cash flow was still $279M.
surprises.fact_evidence: Free cash flow was $279 million at a 25% margin.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s “good looks like” threshold for FCF margin was “≥27%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin slipped to 79.6%, below the preview’s preferred 80%-or-higher level and slightly below its base-case range, though it remained above the preview’s sub-79.5% bear threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin declined to 79.6% from 80.9% a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “≥80%” was the good outcome, with a base case of “~79.5–80%” and a bear trigger of “GM <79.5%.”

surprises.description: NRR remained in the low 120s rather than reaching the preview’s hoped-for mid-120s or explicitly ticking up again. That left the anticipated further expansion unconfirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net revenue retention held in the low 120s.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Mid-120s, or explicit ‘up again’” would be the good outcome and flagged a flat print as a sign Q1’s improvement may have been a one-off.

surprises.description: The $100k-plus ARR customer count reached about 4,720, above both the preview’s roughly 4,633 consensus and its 4,650-plus good-outcome threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Customers with $100,000+ ARR grew to about 4,720 from 3,850 a year ago and now generate roughly 91% of total ARR.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus of approximately 4,633 $100k+ ARR customers and said “4,650+” would look good.

surprises.description: AI customer spending metrics exceeded the counts cited in the preview’s Q1 baseline: 31 customers now spend over $1M annually versus 22 cited previously, and 8 spend over $10M versus 5. The report that all 10 leading AI companies are customers also adds breadth beyond the preview’s stated baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: AI customers now number over 750, including 31 spending more than $1 million annually and 8 spending more than $10 million annually, with all 10 of the top 10 AI leaders as customers.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q1 baseline reported 22 AI customers spending $1M+ and 5 spending $10M+; it also said the largest customer was widely believed to be OpenAI and highlighted the importance of AI-native growth.

surprises.description: Enterprise new-logo bookings were notably strong, with enterprise new-logo annualized bookings more than doubling year over year and new customers contributing a larger share of revenue growth than in Q1. The preview highlighted the prior quarter’s record new logo but did not anticipate this bookings growth or contribution share.
surprises.fact_evidence: Enterprise new-logo annualized bookings more than doubled year over year, and new customers contributed about 30% of revenue growth, up from 25% in Q1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that the largest new logo in company history had landed in Q1 and asked for quantification of its contribution, but gave no expectation for enterprise new-logo bookings or new-customer contribution to growth.

in_line: Non-AI customer revenue growth was in line with the preview’s core-business expectation: it reached the high 20s, matching the preview’s desired mid-to-high-20s growth rather than decelerating toward the low 20s.
The $115M sequential revenue addition matched the preview’s bull-case figure and exceeded its $95M-plus good-outcome threshold, even though the preview’s upper whisper range had also included $115M.

surprises.description: The preview focused on ALTITUDE-AD’s timing and endpoints, but did not flag uncertainty over how the two doses would be judged. Management declined to say whether each dose is independently powered against placebo or disclose the powering framework, leaving investors without clarity on what would count as a positive result.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management declined to disclose the trial's statistical powering framework or whether each dose is independently powered against placebo, leaving uncertainty about what constitutes a positive study.

surprises.description: Q2 R&D and losses were higher than the preview’s base case: R&D was $27.8 million versus an estimated $25.3 million, and net loss was $32.7 million versus about $30 million. The preview expected R&D to include the JCR option payment and modeled roughly $16 million of underlying R&D, so the reported spend was above that estimate even as management cited lower manufacturing, materials, and CRO costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: R&D expenses fell to $27.8 million in Q2 2026, driven by reduced manufacturing, materials, and CRO costs as the clinical trial nears completion. Q2 2026 net loss was $32.7 million with a loss from operations of $32.6 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2'26E R&D: $25.3M; loss from operations: $30.1M; net loss: ~$30.0M. The model assumed “~$16.0M run-rate + $9.25M JCR option payment.”

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was above the preview’s expected range, at $110.2 million versus roughly $99–104 million. The stated runway nevertheless remained only into early 2027, as the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 2026 with $110.2 million in cash and marketable securities, which is expected to fund operations only into early 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Cash + marketable secs: “~$99–104M”; the base case expected runway “into early 2027.”

surprises.description: Management newly emphasized sabirnetug’s IgG2 format and oligomer selectivity as potential safety differentiators versus IgG1 competitors. The preview did not flag this safety-positioning claim, and the call fact describes a potential advantage rather than demonstrated lower ARIA rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is positioning sabirnetug's IgG2 antibody format and oligomer selectivity as differentiating safety advantages over IgG1 competitors Kisunla and Leqembi by potentially reducing ARIA risk.

in_line: ALTITUDE-AD topline remained expected in late 2026, matching the preview’s central timing expectation.
The stated cash runway remained into early 2027, as expected in the preview.
G&A was roughly flat at $4.7 million, close to the preview’s $4.8 million estimate.
The ACU301/ACU401 program retained a mid-2027 IND target, consistent with the preview’s expected EBD-program cadence.

surprises.description: Sempra’s Q2 adjusted EPS was $1.16, well above the preview’s $1.00–$1.05 estimates and its roughly $1.01 consensus. The result also exceeded the preview’s bull-case range of $1.08–$1.15.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.16 ($762 million)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $1.01” (Zacks); “$1.00” (alt. compiler); KeyCorp “$1.05”; bull case “$1.08–$1.15.”

surprises.description: Sempra Texas earnings rose $138 million year over year, above the preview’s modeled increase of about $87 million (from an estimated $208 million to about $295 million). The reported increase included a roughly $50 million catch-up benefit tied to the Oncor settlement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sempra Texas earnings rose $138 million year-over-year, including a favorable ~$50 million catch-up benefit from Oncor's base rate settlement approved in April 2026 that related to Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Sempra Texas at “~$295M” versus “$208M” in Q2'25, and said the catch-up timing could swing quarterly EPS by “±$0.05–$0.10.”

surprises.description: The Oncor batch-zero process has a substantial audit-related delay: after the governor called for comprehensive data-center audits, ERCOT sought a good-cause exception and Sempra said batch-related capital visibility would not arrive until later in 2027. The preview treated Texas load and incremental capital as a near-term catalyst to watch, without anticipating this delay.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Governor Abbott's August 3 letter calling for comprehensive audits of data centers has delayed the batch zero timeline,” with ERCOT “seeking a good cause exception at the August 20 PUC meeting” and “batch-related capital visibility not expected until later in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for watching “for a formal capital plan raise or a pre-announcement of one” and described a hard number on Texas capex above the existing plan as a potential catalyst.

surprises.description: ECA LNG Phase 1 suffered equipment damage and substantial completion moved to Q4 2026, rather than the preview’s commissioning-ramp outlook after noting that the first cargo had already been exported. The call said this does not prevent the SI Partners transaction from closing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ECA LNG Phase 1 suffered damage to equipment connected to its mixed refrigerant compressors, pushing substantial completion into Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “ECA Phase 1 commissioning ramp” and listed first cargo exported July 29 as “a milestone already banked.”

surprises.description: Oncor’s system already has about 8 GW of the 44 GW batch-zero load connected and ramping toward full use. The preview discussed a large Texas load queue, but did not identify this much demand as already connected and actively ramping.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 8 gigawatts of the 44 GW batch zero load is already connected to Oncor's system and ramping toward full utilization.”

in_line: Sempra reaffirmed FY26 adjusted EPS guidance at $4.80–$5.30 rather than narrowing it; the preview identified an unchanged range as its base case.
The company reaffirmed FY27 EPS guidance of $5.10–$5.70 and long-term EPS growth of 7%–9%, as the preview expected.

The SI Partners 45% sale remained on track for a Q3 close, consistent with the preview’s Q3 timing expectation; the call also said the sale would remove over $10 billion of debt and displace the need for common equity in the base capital plan.
The roughly $10 billion of incremental Oncor capital opportunities through 2030 was broadly consistent with the preview’s approximately $9 billion estimate of incremental Texas opportunity.
Port Arthur LNG Phases 1 and 2 remained on time and on budget, consistent with the preview’s focus on their cost and schedule.

surprises.description: BRINSUPRI revenue reached $309.2 million, above the preview’s $285 million script-derived estimate and the $290–300 million buy-side chatter. Sequential growth was 49%, stronger than the preview’s modeled 38%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BRINSUPRI generated $309.2 million in revenue in its third full quarter of launch, up 49% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “BRINSUPRI (brensocatib) revenue: ~$285M”; buy-side chatter “$290–300M”; the bottom-up estimate modeled “$288M (+38% q/q).”

surprises.description: Management raised 2026 BRINSUPRI guidance to $1.25–1.4 billion, well above the preview’s stated de facto bar of at least $1.10 billion. This was a substantially larger raise than the preview’s base case of a soft “$1.0B+” indication.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 BRINSUPRI revenue guidance to $1.25-1.4 billion, up from prior guidance of greater than $1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise to ≥$1.1B is now the de facto price of admission”; the base case anticipated guidance “raised” only to a soft “$1.0B+ and trending above.”

surprises.description: Q2 added about 7,000 BRINSUPRI patients, above the preview’s 6,300 organic-start comparison, and management said all additions came from organic demand after the ready-and-waiting cohort was exhausted. That provided a stronger clean-quarter demand signal than the preview’s threshold anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BRINSUPRI added approximately 7,000 new patients in Q2, beating the prior expectation of 6,300, with all coming from organic demand as ready-and-waiting patients are exhausted.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Q2 the “first clean read on organic demand” and said the bull case required “organic new starts ≥ Q1's ~6,300 ex-cohort.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed substantially higher long-term BRINSUPRI peak-sales potential, raising its estimate to greater than $7 billion from greater than $5 billion. The preview did not anticipate a company estimate increase, although it cited a BMO model of $9.2 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BRINSUPRI's global peak sales estimate was raised to greater than $7 billion from greater than $5 billion, excluding potential upside from comorbid COPD and asthma populations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “BMO initiated Outperform, $192 PT on July 21, 2026, modeling $9.2B peak BRINSUPRI sales.”

surprises.description: Insmed raised TPIP’s peak-sales estimate to greater than $6 billion from greater than $2 billion, contingent on clinical and regulatory success across four indications. The preview highlighted TPIP as central to the pipeline story but did not anticipate this large estimate increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TPIP's peak sales estimate was increased threefold to greater than $6 billion from greater than $2 billion, assuming clinical and regulatory success across all four indications (PH-ILD, PAH, PPF, IPF).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “TPIP now carries the entire pipeline narrative” and discussed upcoming OLE and trial milestones, but gave no TPIP peak-sales estimate.

surprises.description: The call reported strong 12-month TPIP open-label-extension results, including improved walk distance, reduced NT-proBNP, high treatment continuation, and many patients reaching refined low-risk status. The preview said OLE data were due in Q3, so the detailed results were reported earlier than expected, with no outcome benchmarks specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TPIP's 12-month PAH open-label extension showed ~55-meter 6-minute walk improvement, ~60% NT-proBNP reduction, 91% treatment continuation, and 65% of patients reaching refined low-risk status.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Phase 2b OLE data due Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: BRINSUPRI’s gross-to-net outlook improved to mid-to-high 20s and narrowed from the prior mid-20s-to-low-30s range, reducing the risk of landing at the high end of the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BRINSUPRI gross-to-net guidance was improved and narrowed to mid-to-high 20s from mid-20s to low 30s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited gross-to-net “mid-20s to low-30s%” and warned of a step-down “toward the ‘low 30s’ end.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that 30% of BRINSUPRI writers were prescribing for at least five patients, up from 20% in March, and that the prescriber base had grown to over 6,300. The preview noted more than 5,000 prescribers but did not forecast this level of growth or the increase in writer depth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cumulative BRINSUPRI prescribers grew to over 6,300 (up ~1,300 from March) out of roughly 28,000 total physicians, with 30% of writers now prescribing for at least 5 patients versus 20% in March.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “>5,000 cumulative prescribers” as the Q1 comparison point but gave no Q2 prescriber or multi-patient-writer expectation.

in_line: Management reiterated the expectation of cash-flow positivity in 2027 without additional capital, consistent with the preview’s expectation of an unqualified reaffirmation against the existing approximately $1.2 billion cash position; the reported Q2 cash balance was approximately $1.2 billion.
Payer approval rates around 90% and approvals in under a week for most patients were consistent with the preview’s stated approximately 90% approval rate and most approvals arriving within a week.

surprises.description: After-tax distributable earnings were $0.69 per share, above the preview’s $0.62–$0.64 consensus range. That is a clear beat against a preview that emphasized the difficult year-over-year comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: TPG reported after-tax distributable earnings of $280 million, or $0.69 per Class A share.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “After-tax DE per share: $0.62 (Zacks) — $0.64 (other providers).”

surprises.description: Fee-related revenue reached $628 million, above the preview’s roughly $550–$573.5 million range. The result also exceeded the preview’s modeled growth estimate of 15.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fee-related revenue grew 27% year-over-year to $628 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total fee revenues: $573.5M (+20.4% YoY per Zacks)” and “StockStory models +15.6% → ~$550M.”

surprises.description: Fee-related earnings were $315 million, well above the preview’s $265–$275 million base case, and the quarterly FRE margin was 50% versus an expected 46–47%. Management cautioned that the margin was boosted by pulled-forward transaction fees and kept full-year margin guidance at 47%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fee-related earnings rose 43% to $315 million, producing a 50% FRE margin, though management cautioned this margin was elevated by pulled-forward transaction fees and reaffirmed 47% full-year FRE margin guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FRE: base case $265–275M” and “FRE margin: ~46–47%.”

surprises.description: Management said Q2 benefited from transaction closes pulled forward from Q3 and expects transaction and monitoring fees and capital-markets revenue to step down in the second half. The preview focused on fundraising cadence and did not flag this pull-forward as a source of an H2 revenue decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 benefited from a pull-forward of transaction closes originally forecast for Q3, so transaction and monitoring fees and capital markets revenue are expected to step down in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case described “Q2 comp step-down flows through fully” and focused on the H2 fundraising ramp; it did not anticipate transaction-fee pull-forwards or a related H2 revenue step-down.

surprises.description: TPG raised $16 billion in Q2, above the preview’s roughly $12–$14 billion base-case expectation and enough to put year-to-date fundraising above the preview’s $22–$25 billion H1 credibility range. The more positive pace was tempered by real estate fundraising not activating until near year-end, with its FRE benefit shifted into 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TPG raised $16 billion in Q2 and over $26 billion year-to-date,” while “real estate fundraising [is] largely not activating until near year-end and shifting FRE benefit into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “~$12–14B raised”; it said “H1 needs to be ~$22–25B” and described 2026 fundraising as “back-half weighted” with real estate and infrastructure closings.

surprises.description: Fee-earning AUM reached $181 billion, slightly below the preview’s watch range of about $182–$185 billion. This is a modest shortfall against the preview’s stated tracking level, despite strong year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fee-earning AUM [was] up 24% to $181 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch FAUM tracking toward ~$182–185B.”

surprises.description: The stated annualized revenue opportunity from AUM not yet earning fees was about $290 million, above the preview’s roughly $250 million estimate. This points to a larger prospective fee opportunity than the preview had outlined.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$39 billion of AUM not yet earning fees representing a ~$290 million annualized revenue opportunity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “$33B not yet paying fees plus $12B subject to step-ups” as “roughly $250M of annual run-rate fee opportunity.”

surprises.description: Jackson Financial added $2.5 billion in new commitments during the quarter, bringing total commitments to $4.5 billion since February—above the preview’s reference to $2 billion of initial commitments. The preview had noted the partnership but not this larger subsequent commitment total.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Jackson Financial partnership added $2.5 billion in new commitments this quarter, bringing total commitments to $4.5 billion since February.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Jackson Financial at $2B initial commitments.”

surprises.description: TPG reported that only about 5% of its most software-exposed fund was in the AI-disruption “mitigate” category, with no new additions. The preview raised credit-market concerns but did not discuss AI exposure in the portfolio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only about 5% of TPG's most software-exposed fund (TPG VIII) is classified in the AI-disruption 'mitigate' category with no new additions.”

surprises.description: TPG disclosed a commitment of more than $4 billion of initial capital as lead founding partner of the OpenAI DeployCo platform, an investment initiative not anticipated in the preview. Its effect on future earnings or returns was not specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The firm committed over $4 billion of initial capital as lead founding partner of the OpenAI DeployCo platform.”

surprises.description: Private-equity portfolio value rose about 6% in the quarter, with management calling it the second-highest increase since IPO, and net accrued carry increased 15% to $1.4 billion. The preview discussed realized performance allocations but did not set an expectation for these portfolio marks or accrued carry.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Private equity portfolio value appreciated approximately 6% in the quarter (second highest since IPO), driven roughly equally by mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth, multiple expansion, and debt paydown, lifting net accrued carry 15% to $1.4 billion.”

in_line: TPG reaffirmed its target to raise more than $50 billion in 2026, consistent with the preview’s base case.
The $0.59 dividend was within the preview’s expected range of approximately $0.53–$0.59 per share.
The 47% full-year FRE margin guidance was reaffirmed, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q3 gross margin jumped to 45.3%, well above the preview’s expected 37.5–38.5%, and operating income rose to $18.3 million. But roughly $15 million of tariff refunds drove the reported strength: excluding them, gross margin would have been modestly below last year, and management said no further meaningful refunds are expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 gross margin improved 7.7 points to 45.3%,” but “excluding the ~$15 million tariff refund, margin would have been modestly lower than the prior year”; operating income was “boosted by roughly $15 million in tariff refunds,” and management “does not anticipate additional meaningful tariff refunds going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin vs. the 37.6% comp”; the base case expected “37.5–38.5%,” and “holding ≥38% would be a genuine positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses rose 11.5% while sales rose 5%, falling short of the preview’s expectation for meaningful incremental operating leverage. About half the expense increase came from variable compensation, with the rest from volume-related and other costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses increased about $7 million (11.5%) year-over-year,” with “roughly half attributable to higher variable compensation and the remainder to volume-related and other costs”; sales rose 5%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 needs demonstrated operating leverage — flow-through of at least ~25–30% on incremental revenue.”

surprises.description: Camping and watercraft faced a challenging quarter on weak market conditions, rather than the preview’s expectation that the segment would be flat to modestly up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The camping and watercraft business (Jetboil and Old Town) faced a challenging quarter on weak market conditions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “C&WR/Diving flat-to-up modestly.”

surprises.description: Inventory edged higher from the Q2 level instead of drawing down in the expected seasonal cash-harvest quarter. Management attributed the build to supporting sales demand, so the reported increase does not by itself indicate a demand miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory rose to $188.3 million,” up about $24.5 million from the prior-year quarter, “reflecting a build to support sales demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Q3 “the seasonal cash-harvest quarter” and listed “inventory drawdown from $186.9M” as a catalyst to watch.

in_line: Total Q3 sales rose 5% year over year, matching the low end of the preview’s base-case expectation of 5–8% growth.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance has a $1.20 billion midpoint, slightly below the preview’s roughly $1.21 billion bar, and implies slower 13–15% growth. Management cited about three points of sequential headwinds from FX, Prime Day timing, and non-recurring World Cup spend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $1.190-$1.210 billion implies decelerating growth of 13-15%, pressured by roughly 3 points of sequential headwinds from FX, Prime Day timing, and non-recurring World Cup spend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 '26 revenue (implied bar) … ~$1.21B (+15%)”; the base scenario expected “$1,195–1,225M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA substantially exceeded the preview’s estimate, and the margin was far above the roughly 23% expected. Instead of the feared margin pressure, adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 26% year over year, prompting a higher full-year target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $311 million with a margin of 26% (up 130 basis points year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA $270M (23.4% margin)” and showed company guidance of “$256–276M”; it warned that the 29% full-year margin target faced a demanding H2 ramp amid AI infrastructure spending.

surprises.description: Pinterest raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin target to approximately 30%, rather than merely reaffirming the preview’s 29% target. That is a 100-basis-point improvement despite the preview’s concern about AI infrastructure costs and the difficult H2 margin ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 margin results “prompt[ed] management to raise full-year 2026 EBITDA margin guidance to approximately 30% from 29%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin target (~29%)” and the preview’s base scenario expected “FY 29% margin reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue beat the preview’s estimates and buy-side whisper, reaching $1.180 billion rather than roughly $1.15–$1.165 billion. The beat was not broad-based: UCAN was identified as the primary driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $1.180 billion, growing 18% year-over-year (17% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s model estimated “revenue $1,152M (+15.4%)”; its whisper was “~$1.155–1.165B,” versus consensus of “~$1,147M.”

surprises.description: UCAN growth materially outpaced the preview’s expected pace and consensus, accelerating sequentially to 18% and reaching $880 million. The preview expected about $837 million and 12.4% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “UCAN revenue accelerated 5 points sequentially to 18% year-over-year growth, reaching $880 million and serving as the primary driver of Q2 outperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. & Canada … $837.4M | +12.4%”; the preview also said UCAN was guided to “repeat double-digit growth from Q1.”

surprises.description: Europe grew more slowly than the preview’s consensus estimate, with reported growth of 12% and constant-currency growth of 7% versus expected reported growth of 16.1%. Management also said Q3 will be the region’s most difficult comparison of the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Europe growth decelerated to 12% reported (7% constant currency) amid go-to-market restructuring and cross-border retailer regulatory pressure, with Q3 expected to be the most difficult comparison of the year for that region.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Europe consensus at “$221.8M | +16.1%” and described expected Q2 “modest disruption” from go-to-market realignment and other pressures.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS growth was much stronger than the preview’s forecast, with management attributing 30% growth partly to reduced share dilution from repurchases. The preview expected 9.1% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Repurchases “reduc[ed] Q2 net dilution 12% year-over-year and driv[ed] 30% non-GAAP EPS growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview forecast non-GAAP EPS of “$0.36” and “+9.1%.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a substantial AI-model cost advantage that the preview had not quantified: open-source models cost less than 8% as much per transaction as comparable closed proprietary models. This offers a specific potential offset to the preview’s concern about AI infrastructure spending and margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company uses open source AI models achieving cost per transaction at less than 8% of comparable closed proprietary models, supporting margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “AWS $4B commitment” and said to watch how AI infrastructure spend affected the P&L; it did not anticipate this model-cost comparison.

surprises.description: Recent Performance+ model updates reportedly improved SMB return on ad spend by 28%, a concrete performance result beyond the preview’s focus on adoption and lower-funnel spending growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recent model updates driving a 28% ROAS improvement for SMBs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted Performance+ penetration and said adopters grew lower-funnel spend “~2x non-adopters”; it did not cite an expected ROAS improvement.

surprises.description: The company said Q2 stock-based compensation was the peak for the year and that both SBC dollars and year-over-year growth should step down from Q3. The preview focused on operating-cost pressure and margin risk but did not anticipate this specific expense trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 stock-based compensation rose due to the annual grant cycle at a lower stock price and is expected to be the year's peak, with both SBC dollars and year-over-year growth stepping down starting Q3.”

in_line: Global MAUs reached 640 million, within the preview’s stated buy-side bar of 638–642 million, and double-digit growth continued as expected.

surprises.description: DNOW generated $133 million of operating cash flow in Q2, a record, turning the first-half total positive despite the $95 million Q1 cash outflow. That was much stronger than the preview’s expectation of roughly breakeven Q2 cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated a record $133 million in operating cash flow, driving a positive $38 million year-to-date cash inflow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Cash flow roughly breakeven”; the preview also noted that a second consecutive cash-burn quarter would make the annual cash-flow guide difficult to achieve.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $1.3 billion, modestly above the preview’s $1.266–$1.29 billion consensus range and above the company’s implied Q2 guidance range. The result also represented 10% sequential growth, above the preview’s implied roughly 7% consensus growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $1.3 billion, up $124 million or 10% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus revenue of “$1.266B – $1.29B” and implied “~+7%” sequential growth; May guidance implied revenue of “$1.242B – $1.289B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.12 exceeded the preview’s $0.08–$0.10 consensus range. Adjusted EBITDA was $60 million, slightly above the preview’s $58 million base case but within management’s guided range, so the earnings beat was more evident in EPS than in EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $60 million,” and Q2 had “$0.12 adjusted EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave adjusted EPS consensus of “$0.08 – $0.10” and a base case of “$58M (4.6%)” adjusted EBITDA.

surprises.description: DNOW raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to approximately $5.0–$5.1 billion rather than simply reaffirming a target of approaching $5.0 billion. The EBITDA-margin outlook of approaching 4.5% was broadly unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to approximately $5 billion to $5.1 billion in revenue with EBITDA margin approaching 4.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected FY2026 guidance to be “reaffirmed at ~$5.0B / ~4.5% EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance called for 5%–5.5% EBITDA margins, which management said was above its prior guidance. The preview did not provide a specific Q3 margin expectation, so the positive surprise is based on the company’s stated comparison with its previous outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for low-to-mid single-digit sequential revenue growth with EBITDA margin targeted at 5% to 5.5%, above prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Above prior guidance.”

surprises.description: Working-capital metrics improved sharply: DSO fell to 62 days and inventory declined by $131 million in Q2. The inventory reduction was already a preview focus, but the reported reduction came ahead of the preview’s stated goal of cutting inventory by $100 million by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DSO improved 7 days sequentially to 62 days and inventory fell $131 million to $1.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q1 DSO at “69 days” and inventory at “$1.2B”; it also cited a “target –$100M by YE.”

surprises.description: DNOW reduced net debt to $360 million and reached 1.7x trailing leverage in Q2, already below the preview’s stated 1–2x year-end target range. This moved the balance-sheet goal forward rather than merely keeping the company on track for year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt was reduced by $95 million to $360 million, lowering the trailing 12-month net debt leverage ratio to 1.7x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “a guided path to 1–2x by year-end” from Q1 net debt of $455 million and 2.3x leverage.

surprises.description: U.S. revenue reached $1.1 billion, above the preview’s estimated $1.03–$1.07 billion range. This indicates the U.S. business outperformed the geographic expectation, beyond the modest beat in total company revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. revenue growing 13% to $1.1 billion, exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s management-guidance table estimated “US ~$1.03–1.07B.”

surprises.description: U.S. midstream revenue passed $1 billion on an annualized basis for the first time, a milestone the preview had not anticipated. The preview discussed the company’s sector mix but gave no specific midstream growth or threshold expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. midstream revenue surpassed $1 billion on an annualized basis for the first time.”

surprises.description: Gas utilities grew 15% sequentially to an 11-quarter high. The preview identified gas utility as a source of resilience but did not forecast growth of this size or a new multi-quarter high.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gas utilities grew 15% sequentially to an 11-quarter high.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described gas utility as “the counter-cyclical ballast against upstream softness” and flagged gas utility demand as a metric to watch.

in_line: The approximately $30 million synergy run-rate was in line with the preview, which already said the year-1 annualized figure had been raised to about $30 million; the $70 million year-3 target was also described as unchanged.
The full-year EBITDA-margin outlook of approaching 4.5% broadly matched the preview’s expected reaffirmation.
The company continued repurchasing shares, consistent with the preview’s expectation that continued buybacks would signal management conviction.

surprises.description: EHC raised its full-year 2026 revenue, EBITDA, and EPS ranges instead of merely narrowing guidance to the upper half as the preview treated as the base case. The new EPS midpoint is $6.135, up from $6.00, though it remains below the preview’s $6.15 bull-trigger threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance” to net revenue of $6.41B-$6.49B, adjusted EBITDA of $1.365B-$1.395B, and adjusted EPS of $6.02-$6.25.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A narrow-to-upper-half is the base case and is roughly neutral.” The preview also said “an EPS guidance raise” was needed for the bull case.

surprises.description: The 89% success rate in adjudicated MA admit-and-appeal cases was a strong initial result, and management plans to scale certain high-success diagnoses. The preview anticipated pilot data might arrive and discussed scaling as a potential outcome, but gave no expected success rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: The pilot “has admitted 298 patients through July, with 128 of 144 adjudicated cases won (89% success rate),” and management “plans to scale certain high-success diagnoses in coming quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any quantified approval-rate improvement plus a commitment to scale beyond nine hospitals is a 2027 estimate-raiser.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue growth and discharge growth ran ahead of the preview’s estimates: revenue grew 9.6% versus the implied 7.7%, while discharges grew 5.6% versus the derived 4.3% estimate. The reported facts do not specify same-store discharge growth, so they do not resolve that specific debate in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 9.6% year-over-year, driven by 5.6% discharge growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 revenue growth of “+7.7%” and total discharges of “+4.3%.”

surprises.description: The company cut its expected 2026 provider-tax benefit to adjusted EBITDA by about half, from roughly $21 million to $10 million. Retroactive Florida Medicaid adjustments also reduced Q2 year-over-year results, an adverse item not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net provider tax benefit to 2026 adjusted EBITDA” is now expected to be “about $10 million, down from the prior ~$21 million estimate,” including “an $11.5 million year-over-year decrease in Q2.”

surprises.description: EHC raised its full-year SWB-per-FTE growth guidance to 3.5%-4%, indicating more wage growth than the preview’s labor-leverage case suggested. The increased career-ladder participation supports retention, but it also raises the cost outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 SWB per FTE growth guidance was raised to 3.5%-4% due to increased participation in career ladder programs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said salaries and wages per FTE had run “+3.7% in Q1” and identified “clinical-ladder wage inflation” as an offset to the labor story.

surprises.description: The Board increased the quarterly dividend and expanded the buyback authorization, adding to shareholder returns beyond the preview’s stated $0.19 dividend and Q1 repurchase pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Board “increased the quarterly dividend to $0.21 per share and raised the stock repurchase authorization to $1 billion,” with “$145.8 million of shares repurchased year-to-date.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed a “$0.19 quarterly dividend” and “$71.6M repurchased in Q1,” and said buyback pace mattered for EPS.

surprises.description: EHC reported higher Q2 occupancy and record census milestones, rather than the capacity constraint remaining at the prior-year occupancy level described in the preview. Average daily census exceeded 9,000 for the first time in two quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 occupancy reached 77.4%, up 290 basis points year-over-year,” and the company had its “first two quarters ever with average daily census above 9,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1 occupancy as “78.7% flat Y/Y” and framed capacity-constrained volume as the key debate.

surprises.description: Beyond the 2026 opening cadence discussed in the preview, management disclosed a substantial post-2026 pipeline and a set of newly accessible North Carolina markets. The preview did not anticipate these specific expansion opportunities.
surprises.fact_evidence: EHC has “a post-2026 pipeline of 13 hospitals with 606 beds,” plus “15 prioritized North Carolina markets following CON repeal effective October 1.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $348 million, matching the preview’s derived Q2 estimate of about $348 million.
Adjusted EPS growth was 10.7%, matching the preview’s implied 10.7% year-over-year growth and approximately $1.55 estimate.
The expected approximately 2.3% net Medicare revenue-per-discharge increase from the CMS 2027 IRF rule was confirmed.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $718 million, below the preview’s $726.1 million consensus and its +2.5% implied growth rate; reported growth was 1.3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 total revenue rose 1.3% to $718 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $726.1M”; implied year-over-year growth “+2.5%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was well below the preview’s estimated $115–120 million at $96 million, but the gap reflected a nonroutine $16 million self-insurance adjustment and a $4 million fuel headwind. Excluding those items, EBITDA was $116 million at a 16.2% margin, within the expected range; management said the claims charge should not recur.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported adjusted EBITDA was $96 million (13.3% margin), but excluding a $16 million self-insurance adjustment and $4 million fuel headwind, EBITDA would have been $116 million at a 16.2% margin”; the charge was “largely tied to adverse development of 2023-and-prior claims,” with “over 85%” closed and “it should not recur.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (derived, no clean published consensus) | ~$115–120M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~15.8–16.5%.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was cut sharply to $70–80 million from $100–115 million, with fuel and self-insurance impacts cited as the reasons. The preview treated the existing range as the base case and flagged a trim as a downside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow guidance was cut to $70-$80 million from the prior $100-$115 million due to fuel and self-insurance impacts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance … adjusted FCF … $100–115M”; the base case expected the “FY FCF guide” to be reaffirmed, while the bear case said it could be “trimmed.”

surprises.description: Management guided to 3%–6% Land growth in Q4, a forward growth range not specified in the preview, while identifying ancillary revenue as the key swing variable. Full-year Land growth guidance remained 2%–3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year Land revenue guidance of 2%-3% growth and guides Q4 Land growth of 3%-6%, with ancillary being the key swing variable.”

surprises.description: The company reported stronger selling momentum than the preview discussed: it had added 200 net sellers since the end of 2024 and new contract sales were up about 20% year-to-date. The expansion carried costs of $4 million in Q3 and $16 million year-to-date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added a net 200 sellers since end of 2024 (toward a 500 target), lifting new contract sales ~20% year-to-date,” with sales investments costing “$4 million (60 bps) in Q3 and $16 million (80 bps) year-to-date.”

in_line: Land Maintenance grew 2.3%, within the preview’s 2%–3% full-year growth guide and consistent with its expectation that Q3 would confirm the return to growth; it was the second consecutive quarter of organic growth.

Underlying adjusted EBITDA of $116 million and a 16.2% margin, excluding the identified self-insurance and fuel items, were within the preview’s estimated $115–120 million and 15.8%–16.5% margin ranges.
Customer retention of 84.6% was close to the preview’s roughly 85% expectation.
Full-year revenue guidance of $2.75–$2.78 billion was essentially unchanged from the prior $2.745–$2.795 billion range cited in the preview.
The preview flagged fuel as a key EBITDA risk; the call quantified a $4 million Q3 headwind and described mitigation from lower fuel consumption and hedging.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue less ancillary services reached $164 million, above both the $154.3 million consensus and the guidance range’s $159.4 million high end. Travel and hospitality strength helped drive the beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue less ancillary services reached $164 million, up over 28% on a spot basis and 27% FX-neutral, beating the midpoint of guidance largely on Travel/hospitality strength.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “RLA (Revenue Less Ancillary Services) $154.3M” consensus; Q2 guidance was “$151.7M–$159.4M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $24 million at a 14.6% margin, above the preview’s roughly $21 million estimate and well above the 13.75% guide-midpoint margin. The preview identified 14.5% or more as a clear beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $24 million with a 14.6% margin, expanding ~160 bps year-over-year and coming in above the upper end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (my est., not consensus) ~$21M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ~13.75%”; “≥14.5% is a clear beat.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY2026 FX-neutral revenue growth guidance to 21%–27% from 18%–24%. Both ends of the range moved up by three percentage points, rather than the reaffirmation the preview treated as its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 21%-27% FX-neutral revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (raised at Q1): 18–24% FX-neutral RLA growth”; the base case expected “FY26 18–24% reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The company’s FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin-expansion outlook also improved, to 200–400 bps and about 23% at the midpoint, from the preview’s 175–375 bps and roughly 22.8% midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to … ~200-400 bps of EBITDA margin expansion (reaching ~23% at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin +175–375 bps to ~22.8% at midpoint.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin fell about 450 bps in Q2, worse than the preview’s estimated 250–400 bps decline. The full-year decline is now expected to be closer to 350 bps, also worse than the preview’s 200–300 bps outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin fell ~450 bps year-over-year to 56.6% … with full-year margin decline now expected closer to 350 bps reported.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2 math … implies … −250 to −400 bps Y/Y”; “FY26 guide is for −200 to −300 bps compression.”

surprises.description: U.K. visa conditions became an explicit drag: management incorporated higher rejection rates and expects U.K. revenue growth to decelerate below the company’s overall growth rate by year-end. The preview highlighted U.K. issuance as a risk but hoped for no new U.K. caveat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management held its U.S. student visa assumption at a 30% decline and baked in higher U.K. visa rejection rates, expecting U.K. revenue to decelerate and exit the year below overall company growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Truist's July downgrade was specifically about worsening UK issuance”; the preview’s bogey was “no new UK caveat,” and it said silence on the U.K. issue would be negative.

surprises.description: Payment volume grew much faster than the preview’s expected 25%–30% TPV growth, but it also outpaced revenue growth—43% versus 27% FX-neutral RLA growth. The preview specifically warned that TPV outrunning revenue could signal take-rate compression, so the volume strength came with that concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Transaction payment volume” grew 43%; “total revenue less ancillary services” grew 27% FX-neutral.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TPV +25–30%, revenue growing at or above it”; “If TPV outruns revenue in Q2, take rate is compressing.”

surprises.description: Travel and hospitality strength was a notable contributor to the Q2 revenue beat, whereas the preview treated travel cross-sell conversion as something to watch rather than an established growth driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue beat guidance “largely on Travel/hospitality strength.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “evidence of that cross-sell converting” in Travel / Sertifi and noted “$2.5B of capturable volume inside existing US hospitality clients.”

surprises.description: Management upgraded full-year GAAP net income to more than $50 million, or fourfold growth, an outlook the preview did not provide and which contrasts with its warning that GAAP earnings could remain thin or negative in the seasonally weak Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “upgraded GAAP net income to grow fourfold to over $50 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the seasonally weakest quarter and GAAP could still print thin or negative.”

surprises.description: The company set a new long-term target of $1 billion in annual organic revenue at a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, and said it expects to reach about 25% margin by 2027. The preview did not discuss these targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company set a multiyear target of $1 billion in annual organic revenue with 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, and expects to reach ~25% EBITDA margin by 2027 when transformation investment peaks.”

surprises.description: Three new U.S. SFS deals carried twice the ARR value of the same quarter a year earlier, a stronger deal-value signal than the preview’s focus on the number and geographic mix of client additions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its three new U.S. SFS deals carried double the ARR value of the same quarter in 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Client adds: ~200/qtr, ~5,100 total globally”; the preview’s client-add bogey was “≥200 adds, with 60%+ of education adds from non-Big-4.”

in_line: Management held the U.S. student visa assumption at a 30% decline, matching the preview’s stated assumption.

The company signed over 200 clients for a second consecutive quarter, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of about 200 quarterly adds; roughly two-thirds of new education clients were in non-Big-4 markets, above the preview’s 60%+ mix bogey.

surprises.description: Q2 net product revenue was $13.5 million, well above the preview’s $7.10 million consensus and $9.5 million estimate, driven by Tonmaya sales of about $11 million versus roughly $4 million implied in the preview. This was a much larger sales beat than the preview’s already-bullish Tonmaya estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total net product revenue reached $13.5 million in Q2 2026 ($11M Tonmaya plus $2.5M migraine products)” and “Tonmaya generated approximately $11 million in net sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” My Q2'26E: “$9.5M”; Q2'26 consensus: “$7.10M.” The preview also estimated “TONMYA net revenue” at “$6.3M” and said consensus was “~$4.0M (implied).”

surprises.description: Migraine-product sales were $2.5 million, below the preview’s roughly $3.1 million consensus expectation and $3.2 million estimate. The Tonmaya beat therefore more than offset a shortfall in the legacy migraine products.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 net product revenue comprised “$11M Tonmaya plus $2.5M migraine products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Zembrace/Tosymra” at “$3.2M” and listed consensus at “~$3.1M.”

surprises.description: SG&A rose to $36 million, exceeding the preview’s $31 million estimate by $5 million. The preview anticipated launch and sales-force ramp costs, but the reported expense was still materially higher than its estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A expenses surged to $36 million (from $16.2M) year-over-year, reflecting launch investment and pipeline prioritization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “SG&A” at “$31M” and noted the “pre-ramp of +50 reps.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross-to-net was helped by favorable channel mix and lower copay buy-downs, rather than the erosion the preview had allowed for. However, management expects gross-to-net to keep fluctuating around Q1/Q2 levels through the rest of 2026 before stabilizing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Q2 gross-to-net benefited from favorable channel mix and lower copay buy-downs”; management expects “continued fluctuations at similar Q1/Q2 levels through Q3 and Q4 before stabilizing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said it “haircut for gross-to-net erosion (copay support, Medicaid rebates, bridge/free goods)” and flagged that “a drop toward $400–450” net per script would indicate volume bought with discounts and free goods.

surprises.description: R&D expense was $19.4 million, slightly above the preview’s $18 million estimate. The increase reflects launch and pipeline prioritization, but exceeded the expected spend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses rose to $19.4 million (from $10.8M) year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “R&D” at “$18M.”

surprises.description: The planned addition of 50 sales representatives is now expected to be fully deployed by September, later than the preview’s target of mid-third quarter. The expansion itself was anticipated, but the stated completion timing is somewhat later.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is “adding 50 reps (bringing the field force to roughly 150) fully deployed by September.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “+50 targeted ‘by mid-third quarter 2026’ to reach ~150” and described the confirmation as a key item to watch.

surprises.description: Refill prescriptions rose 207% quarter over quarter while new-patient prescriptions rose 36%, providing a notably strong refill signal on the durability question the preview highlighted. Total prescriptions were around the preview’s expected level, so the surprise is in the reported refill growth rather than the overall script count.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tonmaya prescriptions totaled 12,592 in Q2, up 100% quarter-over-quarter, with new patient prescriptions up 36% and refills up 207%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called “prescriber breadth and refill rate” a key metric and said “Refill persistence is the durability test for a fibromyalgia product — new patient adds without refills is a leaky bucket.”

surprises.description: The call provided an additional development update on TNX-4800: its Lyme-prevention Phase 2 study has FDA-aligned minutes, is expected to begin enrolling in Q1 2027, and could be pivotal if positive. The preview did not discuss this program or study timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: The “TNX-4800 Lyme prevention Phase 2 adaptive field study (~3,300 participants) has FDA-aligned minutes,” is “expected to begin enrolling in Q1 2027,” and “could serve as a pivotal registrational study if positive.”

in_line: Tonmaya prescriptions totaled 12,592, broadly matching the preview’s estimate of about 12,600 Q2 scripts and its 11,000–14,000 base-case range.
Cash of $176.2 million was within the preview’s estimated $170–180 million range, and the runway into early Q2 2027 was unchanged from the prior guidance the preview highlighted.
The Horizon Phase 2 MDD study began in June, as the preview expected for the mid-2026 pipeline milestone.
The planned addition of 50 sales representatives and expansion to roughly 150 were anticipated in the preview; the deployment timing is addressed separately above.

surprises.description: The preview focused on Ovaprene enrollment and the prior positive DSMB review but did not flag a change to the FDA protocol requirements. The FDA approved removing the 250-completer expectation, while still strongly recommending at least 250 completers for adequate safety characterization—a regulatory relaxation with a continuing safety-data caveat.
surprises.fact_evidence: The FDA approved Daré's protocol amendment removing the 250-completer expectation for the Ovaprene Phase III trial, though it continued to strongly recommend a minimum of 250 completers for adequate safety characterization.

surprises.description: The preview did not discuss DARE-HPV, but Daré reported that its approximately 100-woman Phase II study had started with ARPA-H funding and that a second $1 million NIAID tranche brought total project funding to $2 million. This adds a funded clinical program and non-dilutive support not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The DARE-HPV Phase II study (~100 women) was initiated with ARPA-H funding, and the company secured a second $1 million NIAID tranche bringing total project funding to $2 million, with top-line results expected in 2027.

surprises.description: The preview estimated a Q2 net loss of about $3.3 million. The reported loss was about $3 million, a modestly narrower loss than expected, with nondilutive funding offsets contributing to the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net loss improved to approximately $3 million in Q2 2026 from approximately $4 million in the prior-year period, aided by nondilutive funding offsets.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss n/a” for consensus; “My Estimate: ~$3.3M.”

surprises.description: The preview did not identify a 2027 commercialization plan for DARE to RECLAIM. Daré now targets commercial availability of its menopause ring through 503B compounding beginning in 2027, adding a prospective product to its stated 2026–27 commercial lineup.
surprises.fact_evidence: DARE to RECLAIM estradiol/progesterone intravaginal ring for menopause is targeted for commercial availability via 503B compounding beginning in 2027, positioning Daré for a diversified multiproduct revenue profile across 2026-2027.

in_line: Q2 revenue was approximately $0.2 million, matching the preview's $0.20 million estimate and its $0.15–0.25 million base range. The preview also expected Flora Sync LF5 to have no material Q2 product revenue because it became purchasable in July.
Flora Sync LF5 launched in June, with sales beginning in July, consistent with the preview's account that DTC availability began July 1.
DARE to PLAY's targeted start of prescription dispensing in Q3 remains within the preview's expected summer 2026 timing.
Ovaprene's DSMB recommended continuing the Phase III study without modification, consistent with the preview's expectation of a positive interim review and continued enrollment.

surprises.description: Mattel’s constant-currency sales grew 9%, above the preview’s expected 6%–8% growth. The quarter was stronger on revenue than the preview’s roughly $1.08–$1.10 billion sales estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales grew 10% as reported and 9% in constant currency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales … +6% to +8%”; base case: “$1,085M (+6.5%)” against consensus of “$1,080M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.01, below the preview’s $0.03–$0.05 consensus range. That was a weaker earnings result despite the better-than-expected sales growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS dropped to $0.01 from $0.21.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $0.03 (Zacks) · $0.04 (AAII, 12 analysts) · $0.05 (alt. compiler)”; base case: “$0.04.”

surprises.description: North America gross billings grew 12%, ahead of the preview’s estimate of about 7%. This was a stronger result in the region the preview highlighted as a key test against an easy comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America gross billings up 12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “North America ~$545M (+7%)”; the preview also said, “If Mattel’s NA doesn’t grow against a −16% comp, that’s a company-specific problem.”

surprises.description: Hot Wheels grew 12%, modestly ahead of the preview’s 10% forecast for Vehicles. Mattel also said the brand is approaching $2 billion in annual revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hot Wheels grew 12% in the quarter” and “is approaching $2 billion in annual revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Vehicles gross billings growth of “+10%” and noted “Hot Wheels ran +13% cc in Q1.”

surprises.description: Masters of the Universe showed stronger commercial momentum than the preview’s concern about muted performance around the film suggested: gross billings more than tripled year-to-date, and the film was a major streaming hit despite the preview’s negative box-office framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Masters of the Universe gross billings more than tripled year-to-date” and the film became “the #1 movie on Prime Video globally and the most-watched movie across U.S. streaming in its first week.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Goldman cited “muted performance” around the MOTU release and described the film as “a confirmed bomb,” citing its box office.

surprises.description: Management gave a constructive 2027 outlook, including Barbie returning to growth, which was not covered in the preview’s expectations. This added a positive longer-term message while management characterized 2026 as an investment year.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided to 2027 delivering “mid- to high-single-digit top-line growth, strong double-digit bottom-line growth, and Barbie returning to growth.”

surprises.description: Mattel said it would delay most of the planned $40 million in digital performance marketing until UNO Wild’s commercial launch in early 2027. The preview discussed strategic-investment ROI but did not anticipate this timing change; management said it would not affect 2026 guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is delaying the majority of $40 million in digital performance marketing spend to coincide with UNO Wild's commercial launch in early 2027, with no impact to 2026 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “ROI on the ~$150M strategic-investment program” and said management would be pressed on the program’s performance, but did not mention delaying this spend.

in_line: Adjusted gross margin was 48.6%, essentially in line with the preview’s roughly 48.5% expectation.
Adjusted operating income was $39 million, close to the preview’s approximately $40–55 million estimate and $42 million base case.

Mattel reaffirmed its 2026 guidance for 3%–6% constant-currency sales growth, about 50% adjusted gross margin, $580–$630 million adjusted operating income, and $1.27–$1.39 adjusted EPS, as the preview expected.
The company remained on track for $400 million of 2026 share repurchases, matching the preview’s stated full-year target.

surprises.description: Nutex reported Q2 revenue of $210.8 million, about 2.9% below the preview’s working consensus of roughly $217 million. The reported decline was attributed to unusually strong IDR-driven revenue realization in the year-ago quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue fell 13.6% to $210.8 million” due to “unusually strong IDR-driven revenue realization in the 2025 comparison period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working consensus” revenue: “~$217M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $90 million, well above the preview’s warning that a result below roughly $60 million would signal a structural margin problem. This points to substantially stronger quarterly profitability than that downside threshold implied, despite the revenue miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 25.7% to $90 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A print below ~$60M with revenue in line means the margin problem is structural, not timing.”

surprises.description: Same-hospital visits grew 6.3%, a much stronger result than the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly flat same-hospital activity. Total visits also grew 9.6%, above the preview’s +5% threshold used in its bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hospital visits grew 9.6% to 49,962 in Q2 2026 with same-hospital visits up 6.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case assumed “same-hospital flat”; the bull scenario cited “visits +5%+.”

surprises.description: A renegotiated Halo MD contract shifted arbitration fees to pay-on-collected terms retroactive to 2024, contributing $38.4 million to lower facility operating costs. The company also expects total contract services costs to be 25%–30% lower going forward, a specific cost reduction not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The contract change “contribut[ed] about $38.4 million to a $49.6 million decrease in facility operating costs” and is expected to lower “total contract services costs an expected 25%-30% going forward.”

surprises.description: The final federal IDR rule reduced CMS administrative fees from $115 to $15 per party, generating another $4.3 million of quarterly savings. The preview focused on arbitration-cost normalization but did not anticipate this additional regulatory fee reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The final federal IDR rule cut CMS administrative fees from $115 to $15 per party,” contributing “about $4.3 million in cost savings for the quarter.”

surprises.description: Net revenue per visit settled around $4,000–$4,200 and management expects it to stay there, rather than retaining the prior-year quarter’s unusually high $5,185 level. That suggests a lower ongoing revenue-per-visit level than the headline comparison alone might suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue per visit normalized to roughly $4,000-$4,200,” down from “$5,185 in Q2 2025,” and management “expects this level to persist.”

surprises.description: Management said 50%–60% of claims continue to be submitted through IDR, with high award and collection rates. That is reassuring against the preview’s flagged concern that IDR submissions were declining, though it does not indicate that submission rates have increased.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “continues submitting 50%-60% of claims through IDR, winning over 85% of award determinations with an average collection rate over 80%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged that “submissions are declining, ‘possibly due to better initial payments by payers,’” and asked for an update on IDR submission rates.

in_line: The three planned H2 2026 hospital openings—West Little Rock, San Antonio, and Jacksonville—remain on schedule, consistent with the preview’s expectation for those openings.
Management maintained a pace of 3–5 hospital openings per year, consistent with the preview’s stated development pace.

surprises.description: YETI reported adjusted EPS of $0.67, far above the preview’s $0.52–$0.54 consensus range, which implied an approximately 18%–21% year-over-year decline. Instead, adjusted EPS grew 2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 2% to $0.67 in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.52–$0.54” and “–18% to –21%.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 59.5%, well above the preview’s estimated 54%–55% and reversing the expected year-over-year decline. The preview identified gross margin as the central risk and said a result of at least 55.5% would de-risk the H2 bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin expanded 170 bps to 59.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin ~54–55%” and “A Q2 adj. GM ≥55.5% de-risks the H2 bridge.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year gross-margin guidance by 100 bps to 57.5%–58%, a substantial improvement over the preview’s existing 56.5%–57.0% range and its expectation of a 60-bps year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin guidance was raised 100 basis points to 57.5%–58%, implying a 40 bps year-over-year increase versus a prior expected 60 bps decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY adj. GM guided 56.5–57.0%” and the preview describes a “~60 bps decline” versus the prior year.

surprises.description: YETI quantified an IEEPA tariff refund benefit of $8.2 million, or 170 bps of Q2 gross margin. The preview called refund quantification un-modeled upside, so this was a favorable one-off contribution not included in the expected margin picture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Including an $8.2 million (170 bps) benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any quantification of YETI's refund receivable is un-modeled upside” and “IEEPA tariff refund quantification — pure un-guided upside.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EPS range rose to $2.94–$3.00 from $2.83–$2.89, exceeding the preview’s existing guidance and delivering the raise the preview said investors were looking for. The new upper end also reaches the preview’s bull-case threshold of above $2.95.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $2.94–$3.00 … from prior $2.83–$2.89.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus expects at least a reaffirm of … $2.83–$2.89 EPS”; the preview says the buy-side was “positioned for a raise, not a reaffirm” and its bull case calls for “EPS >$2.95.”

surprises.description: YETI raised full-year adjusted operating-margin guidance to approximately 14.9%, up 30 bps, rather than keeping the approximately 14.6% outlook cited in the preview. The company also expects second-half margins to rise about 280 bps year over year, supporting the margin recovery that the preview said the guide depended on.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted operating margin guidance was raised to approximately 14.9% (up 30 bps) … with second-half margins up roughly 280 bps year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin ~14.6%”; the preview says the FY guide “rests on H2 margin recapture.”

surprises.description: U.S. Drinkware was flat, rather than extending the U.S. growth streak the preview viewed as evidence of an inflection. Management said three SKUs were dragging 2026 U.S. Drinkware growth by about 600 bps, though it expects that drag to lap by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Drinkware grew only 2% … with U.S. Drinkware flat”; management flagged “a roughly 600 basis point drag on 2026 U.S. Drinkware growth from just 3 SKUs, expected to fully lap by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 was the second straight quarter of category growth and the called-out ‘U.S. inflection’”; the preview says a third consecutive quarter of growth would “confirm the inflection thesis.”

surprises.description: Adjusted SG&A rose 19% and deleveraged 410 bps, a notable cost and margin headwind not highlighted in the preview’s margin discussion. Management attributed much of it to a brand campaign shifting from last year’s Q4 into this Q2, plus higher incentive compensation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted SG&A rose 19% and deleveraged 410 bps to 45.4% of sales, largely due to the brand campaign shifting from Q4 last year into Q2 this year plus higher incentive comp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s margin discussion focuses on tariff effects, capacity, and lower product costs; it does not flag a Q2 SG&A deleverage of this size.

surprises.description: YETI repurchased $130 million of shares in Q2 alone, more than the roughly $100 million of buybacks the preview said was embedded in the full-year outlook. The call also reported more than $600 million of buybacks since 2024, with about $370 million still authorized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased 2.8 million shares for $130 million in Q2,” with “total buybacks since 2024 to over $600 million” and “roughly $370 million remaining on authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$100M of buybacks embedded against a $500M authorization.”

surprises.description: Management outlined an expansion from four live international markets to a planned 11 by the end of 2026, a specific rollout plan the preview did not anticipate. International sales growth itself was within the preview’s high-teens-to-20% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International sales grew 19% to $93 million … with the company expanding from 4 to a planned 11 live markets by end of 2026.”

in_line: Sales were approximately $484 million, essentially matching the preview’s $483.8 million consensus and its implied 8.5% year-over-year growth.
International sales grew 19%, within the preview’s stated high-teens-to-20% growth expectation.

surprises.description: Drug discovery revenue reached $23 million versus the preview’s derived estimate of about $14 million, helped by a $10 million Ajax milestone; the company also raised its full-year drug discovery revenue range to $65–75 million from $55–65 million. The two reported segments add to about $55.5 million of revenue, well above the $47.2–47.4 million consensus total.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Drug discovery revenue rose to $23 million from $13.9 million, boosted by a $10 million Ajax milestone,” and management raised full-year guidance “to $65-75 million from $55-65 million.” Software revenue was $32.5 million, making the two segments’ combined revenue about $55.5 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $47.2M – $47.4M”; “Drug discovery revenue: ~$14M (derived)”; FY drug discovery guidance was “$55M – $65M.”

surprises.description: ACV excluding contribution was $22.6 million, at the upper end of the $19–23 million range the preview identified as the key demand test. Its 23% growth also exceeded the preview’s 4%–26% implied range midpoint of about 15%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ACV excluding contribution of $22.6 million (up 23%) landing at the upper end of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 ACV (ex-contribution): $19M – $23M”; the implied year-over-year range was “+4% to +26%, midpoint ~+15%.”

surprises.description: Hosted revenue rose to 47% of software revenue, substantially above the 34% share reported in Q1; some customers were converted ahead of renewal, inflating the quarter’s mix. This is faster hosted adoption, but it also brings the revenue-recognition and margin headwinds the preview warned about.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hosted revenue jumped to 47% of software revenue ($15.2 million of $32.5 million) versus 31% in Q2 2025,” with some customers converted “ahead of renewal, inflating the quarter’s figure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Hosted was “34% of software in Q1” and management targets “~75% by 2028”; the preview described the hosted transition as producing reported-revenue distortion.

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the $218–228 million full-year ACV range despite the preview’s concern that a large amount of ACV remained to be generated in the back half. The reaffirmation is encouraging, though management’s note that Q4 typically contributes more than half of annual ACV underscores the concentration of the remaining requirement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 ACV guidance of $218-228 million (10-15% growth), noting Q4 typically accounts for over 50% of annual ACV.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY guide might be “reaffirmed, narrowed, or cut,” noted that reaffirmation “is itself a positive surprise,” and flagged the “extreme Q4-weighted back half.”

surprises.description: Software gross margin was 71%, above the preview’s 68–69% level for a transition-related drag and above its 70% bull-case threshold, even as the hosted shift reduced margin versus a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Software gross margin declined to 71% from 76% in Q2 2025, reflecting the planned accelerated transition to hosted licensing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Gross margin holding ≥68–69%” would indicate a transitional drag and used “gross margin ≥70%” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: The call clarified that the expanded Bristol Myers Squibb software agreement is monetized through increased throughput-based platform usage, providing commercial substance beyond a deployment announcement. It did not quantify the resulting ACV or revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “signed an expanded strategic software agreement with Bristol Myers Squibb, monetizing it through increased throughput-based platform usage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the BMS announcement was “an ACV-accretive enterprise expansion or a co-development arrangement with deferred economics,” and said commercial quantification would turn the narrative into a number.

in_line: Software revenue was $32.5 million, close to the preview’s derived estimate of about $33 million.
The hosted transition remained the stated driver of lower software gross margin, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the transition would pressure reported revenue and margins.

The Ajax-related gain and resulting positive GAAP earnings were broadly consistent with the preview’s warning to expect a large, non-operational GAAP earnings benefit; the call reported $48.9 million of other income tied to the Ajax acquisition and $6 million of net income.
Full-year operating expenses are expected below 2025 levels, as the preview expected; quarterly operating expenses were $74 million, down 6% year over year.
Bunsen’s early-access launch was not new versus the preview, which noted that early access began July 27.

surprises.description: Revenue was $15.2 million, above the preview’s $14.57 million consensus estimate by about 4%. The preview cautioned that the refranchising-driven mix shift made revenue less informative than comps, but the reported top line still exceeded its estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $15.2 million.”
