surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026 Consensus | $14.57M.”

surprises.description: The company cut its 2026 new-clinic openings outlook to 22–26 from the preview’s cited 30–35 target, and said its net clinic count will finish the year below 2025. That is a weaker unit-growth outlook than investors were expecting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year new clinic openings guidance was cut to 22-26 from the prior 30-35, and net clinic count will end 2026 lower than 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “30–35 new franchised openings (ex-refranchised).”

surprises.description: Pricing increases had reached more than 500 clinics already, ahead of the preview’s roughly 300-clinic status and expected full-portfolio rollout in Q3. Management also reported no meaningful patient pushback and said the low-single-digit revenue benefit should reach the high end of that range in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pricing increases of $5 and $10 have been adopted by over 500 clinics with no meaningful patient pushback, contributing a low single-digit revenue benefit expected to reach the high end of that range in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A $5–10 price increase live in ~300 clinics with ‘little or no pushback,’ full-portfolio rollout in Q3.”

surprises.description: Management had previously sold investors on positive comps in Q3 and Q4, but the reported outlook only said comps should continue improving in the second half, with Q4 higher than Q3. That keeps the sequential-improvement message but stops short of affirming the expected return to positive comps.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comp sales were negative 2.8% in Q2, a 140 basis point improvement from Q1, with management expecting continued improvement in the second half and Q4 higher than Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Slightly negative comps in Q2, positive in Q3 and Q4, with Q4 stronger than Q3.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow and free cash flow rose sharply, a positive cash-generation result the preview did not flag as an expected catalyst or provide a benchmark for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash flow from operating activities grew 152% year-over-year to $2.2 million, driving free cash flow up $1.6 million to $1.9 million.”

surprises.description: The company reported its best patient retention in more than five years, with the $35 Align One plan lifting lapsed-patient conversion by several hundred basis points. The preview discussed the plan as a comp lever but did not anticipate this retention and conversion result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company posted its best patient retention rate in over five years, driven by new flexible plans such as the $35 Align One option that raised lapsed-patient conversion by several hundred basis points.”

surprises.description: Four RD territory buybacks completed year-to-date are expected to save about $630,000 in annualized royalties, a specific cost-saving benefit not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed four RD territory buybacks year-to-date expected to save ~$630,000 in annualized royalties.”

in_line: Q2 comps were negative 2.8%, within the preview’s expected roughly negative 2% to negative 3% range.
The company reiterated the previewed full-year ranges for system-wide sales ($519–552 million), comps (-3% to +3%), and consolidated adjusted EBITDA ($12.5–13.5 million).

surprises.description: Sabre reported Q2 revenue of $712 million, about $15 million above the $697.4 million consensus, with 4% year-on-year growth rather than the roughly 1.5% growth implied by consensus and the company’s flat-to-nominal guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 4% year-on-year to $712 million, exceeding management's guidance of flat to nominal growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $697.4M” and company guidance of “Flat-to-nominal growth.”

surprises.description: Normalized adjusted EBITDA was $151 million, $21 million above the approximately $130 million guide-anchored expectation. The preview anticipated EBITDA holding around the guide despite weak bookings, not this size of beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Normalized adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to $151 million versus a guide of approximately $130 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma Adj. EBITDA | ~$130M (guide-anchored)” and “If rate/mix + cost hold EBITDA at guide on soft volume.”

surprises.description: Air distribution bookings grew 1% instead of merely coming in near flat; the preview specifically warned that the stale guide could translate to a 2%–4% decline. The reported result was therefore materially better than the preview’s expected volume miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Air distribution bookings grew 1% year-on-year, beating expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sabre guided Q2 air distribution bookings to ‘near flat’” and “Watch for ‑2% to ‑4%.”

surprises.description: Sabre raised full-year pro forma adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $600 million, $15 million above the preview’s expected reaffirmation at approximately $585 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sabre raised full-year 2026 pro forma adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $600 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma Adj. EBITDA ~$585M … — reaffirmed at Q1.”

surprises.description: Full-year free cash flow guidance improved to approximately negative $65 million rather than being reaffirmed at negative $70 million, modestly better than the preview’s expected target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Improved free cash flow guidance to approximately negative $65 million (from negative $70 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 free cash flow (~‑$70M)” and “FY FCF ~‑$70M reaffirmed, hedged, or cut.”

surprises.description: Management said corporate volumes, about 45% of Marketplace bookings, stayed resilient and offset weaker leisure demand, reversing the prior-year pattern. The preview anticipated that Sabre’s North American skew could cushion industry weakness, but did not flag this corporate-versus-leisure reversal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Corporate volumes, representing nearly half (about 45%) of Marketplace bookings versus 25%-30% industry-wide, remained resilient and offset softness in leisure demand, reversing last year's trend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sabre skews more North American than Amadeus, so expect better.”

surprises.description: Sabre doubled its active agentic AI pilot and production partners from 30 to 60 in the quarter, a faster expansion than the preview’s cited 30-plus-partner pipeline suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sabre doubled its active agentic AI pilot and production partners from 30 to 60 in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Agentic AI pipeline (30+ partners in pilot/production).”

in_line: Airline Technology revenue was $135 million, which the call described as in line with expectations.
Sabre reaffirmed its full-year revenue and air distribution bookings growth outlook, consistent with the preview’s expectation that those outlooks would be defended.
The Q3 and Q4 bookings outlook of flat to low-single-digit growth in Q3 and low-to-mid-single-digit growth in Q4 was consistent with the preview’s expected H2 bookings inflection.
The extended debt maturity profile was consistent with the preview’s note that there were no large maturities until 2029.

surprises.description: Lumentum guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $1.225–$1.275 billion and EPS to $4.05–$4.35, well above the preview’s derived expectations of about $1.15 billion and $3.50–$3.60. The revenue midpoint also reaches the company’s revenue target more than a quarter early.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 guidance of $1.225–$1.275 billion (midpoint $1.25 billion, over 130% YoY growth) reaches the company's revenue target more than a quarter ahead of schedule, with EPS guided to $4.05–$4.35.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sept-quarter figures used below are derived from the $16.67 FY27 EPS consensus and a normal ramp shape (~$3.50–$3.60 EPS, ~$1.15B revenue).”

surprises.description: Q1 operating margin guidance of 39.5%–40.5% is much stronger than the preview’s status-quo ramp framing; management said it already matches the margin assumed in its $2 billion quarterly-revenue model at far lower revenue and suggested raising that model’s top end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 non-GAAP operating margin is guided to 39.5%–40.5%, already at the midpoint of the company's $2 billion revenue-level target model at much lower revenue, prompting management to suggest raising the top of that model by 100–200 bps.”

surprises.description: Pump-laser commentary was substantially more constructive than the preview’s concern about a sudden supply constraint: shipments grew over 80% year over year, a fourfold increase is expected over coming quarters, and mostly three-year take-or-pay agreements back the ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pump laser shipments grew over 80% year-over-year with a fourfold increase expected over coming quarters, backed by mostly three-year take-or-pay agreements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pump constraint was ‘unanticipated’ and ‘relatively sudden’ in Q3”; the preview’s bogey was “No new constraint,” and it said a signed take-or-pay agreement would be upside.

surprises.description: OCS progress came with a stronger near-term revenue milestone than the preview quantified: shipments doubled sequentially and Q1 is expected to be the first quarter above $100 million in OCS revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OCS shipments doubled from Q3 to Q4, and Q1 guidance includes the first triple-digit (over $100 million) OCS revenue quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called OCS “the biggest single tightrope” and set the bogey as “On/ahead of plan,” without giving a revenue milestone.

surprises.description: Lumentum disclosed a near-term CPO/NPO laser opportunity with demand far exceeding supply, including roughly $50 million of ELS-module and ultra-high-power-laser revenue by year-end and a first triple-digit quarter in fiscal Q3—more concrete and earlier revenue milestones than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ultra-high-power laser chip demand for CPO/NPO has surged well beyond supply, with ELS module and ultra-high-power laser revenue expected to reach roughly $50 million by year-end and a first triple-digit quarter in fiscal Q3, ahead of customer scale-up deployments in 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described scale-up CPO as a “>$5B” opportunity but said to treat it as “narrative fuel, not near-term estimates”; it also said the 5th InP fab was excluded from projections and contributes about six quarters out.

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $3.23 exceeded the preview’s $2.97–$3.02 consensus and its roughly $3.10 base case, as well as the company’s prior guidance ceiling of $3.05.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 36.6%, up 2,160 basis points year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $3.23 well above prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” consensus: “$2.97 – $3.02”; the base scenario expected “~$3.10.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was 50.4%, below the preview’s implied 51%–52% range and its 52% bogey, despite a large sequential and year-over-year improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP gross margin crossed 50% (50.4%, up 250 bps sequentially and 1,260 bps year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Implied non-GAAP GM” at “~51–52%” and set the bogey at “≥52%.”

surprises.description: Q4 operating margin reached 36.6%, modestly above the 35.0%–36.0% company guide and the preview’s roughly 35.5% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 36.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company guidance of “35.0% – 36.0%” and an expected margin of “~35.5%.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue of $1.01 billion slightly exceeded the $988.6 million consensus, though it remained within the prior company guide and near the preview’s approximately $1.00 billion base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 revenue surged 109% year-over-year to $1.01 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus was “$988.6M”; the base scenario expected “~$1.00B.”

surprises.description: The conversion of $1.1 billion of convertible notes produced a $7.8 billion non-cash GAAP charge and a $7.2 billion GAAP net loss, an unexpected headline accounting loss; the debt conversion itself also reduced outstanding convertible debt by about 35%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company equitized $1.1 billion of convertible notes (about 35% of outstanding convertible debt), triggering a one-time non-cash GAAP charge of $7.8 billion and a Q4 GAAP net loss of $7.2 billion.”

in_line: The preview expected strong, supply-constrained Q4 growth; revenue of $1.01 billion was within the prior guide of $960 million–$1.01 billion and close to its roughly $1.00 billion base case.

surprises.description: Q1 net sales were $168 million, about 8% below the preview’s $183 million consensus and also below its $180–190 million base-case range. The preview noted that a year-over-year decline could still fit the annual guidance, but this quarter’s sales were weaker than its central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 net sales were $168 million,” which management characterized as “in line with expectations but impacted by the timing of orders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $183.0M” consensus; the base scenario expected “$180–190M.” The preview also said reported revenue “down mid-single-digits Y/Y is consistent with guidance being on track.”

surprises.description: Reported gross margin fell to 16.2%, below the preview’s roughly 19–21% model and its warning that below 19.5% could put the operating-income guide at risk. However, adjusted gross margin was 20.2%, broadly within the expected range; a weakening dollar versus the peso contributed an unanticipated 2 percentage-point, or $3.5 million, headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 gross margin fell to 16.2% from 18% a year earlier,” while “excluding noncash (2.4%) and onetime items (1.6%), adjusted gross margin was 20.2%.” A weakening U.S. dollar versus the Mexican peso had “an unfavorable foreign exchange impact of approximately 2% or $3.5 million on gross margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled gross margin at “~19–21%” and said “Anything below ~19.5% gross margin puts the full-year op income guide at risk.”

surprises.description: The company used cash in Q1 despite the preview identifying the seasonally cash-building quarter as a time when a return to cash burn would be a negative surprise. The $11.3 million outflow contrasted with the $10.0 million generated in Q1 FY26.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company used $11.3 million in cash from operating activities in Q1 due to an inventory ramp-up for new business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q1 is seasonally the cash-build quarter” and “a return to cash burn would be a negative surprise”; it cited Q1 FY26 operating cash flow of “$10.0M.”

surprises.description: Net bank debt was $99.7 million, higher than the preview’s $80 million net-debt reference point and its stated expectation that net debt at or below $80 million would support deleveraging. The reported 1.26 net-debt-to-trailing-adjusted-EBITDA ratio was described as low, but does not erase the gap versus that debt expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net bank debt was $99.7 million against trailing adjusted EBITDA of $79.1 million, yielding a low net bank debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 1.26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “net debt at or below $80M keeps the deleveraging narrative intact” and cited FY26 year-end net bank debt of “$80.0M.”

in_line: Fiscal 2027 guidance was reaffirmed at $780–800 million of sales, $86–91 million of operating income, and $95–100 million of EBITDA, matching the preview’s base-case expectation.

Management reiterated more than $100 million of additional annualized sales by fiscal 2027 year-end and a target of over $900 million in annualized net sales, consistent with the preview’s expected 2H ramp and its emphasis that this business was excluded from guidance.
Adjusted gross margin of 20.2% was broadly within the preview’s modeled 19–21% range, despite the lower reported margin.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 29%, below the preview’s 31–34% estimate. Management attributed the shortfall to manufacturing utilization well below capacity and setup costs on new programs that are not yet covered by revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin was approximately 29%,” held down by “manufacturing utilization running well below capacity” and “setup costs for new programs not yet covered by revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Q2 model estimated “Gross margin … 31–34%.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating cash burn was worse than the preview’s estimate, at $11.1 million versus an expected $9–10 million. Management nevertheless reiterated full-year burn guidance and expects a lower second-half pace, making the overall message mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Operating cash burn, including CapEx, was “$11.1 million in Q2,” above the guided $8–9 million quarterly average; full-year burn guidance of $32–36 million was reiterated, with an expected second-half pace of “~$12 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Q2 model estimated “Operating cash use … $(9.0)–(10.0)M”; the preview also noted the $8–9 million quarterly guide.

surprises.description: The company secured rights to Americanize and manufacture three IAI loitering munitions, a potentially very large program not mentioned in the preview. The revenue opportunity remains conditional: initial units may be available in about 18 months once a government demand signal materializes.
surprises.fact_evidence: Palladyne secured rights to “Americanize and manufacture IAI's Harop, Harpy, and Mini Harpy” and management said the program could ultimately generate “hundreds of millions to billions of dollars in revenue,” with initial units potentially available in about 18 months after a government demand signal.

surprises.description: Quarterly bookings included a defense-prime follow-on order five times larger than its prior order, helping lift backlog to $24.6 million from the preview’s $24.0 million expectation. The preview had flagged the backlog level but did not anticipate this order or the roughly $13 million of Q2 bookings.
surprises.fact_evidence: Backlog reached “approximately $24.6 million,” reflecting “roughly $13 million of new bookings”; a defense prime placed a follow-on order “five times larger than its prior order,” covering more than 1,000 Brain FC1 units valued at approximately $2.3 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Backlog (6/30): $24.0M” and described a “majority” converting over 12–18 months.

surprises.description: Palladyne said it had submitted proposals to more than 20 Department of War funding programs with several hundred million dollars of aggregate initial potential value, an additional pipeline development not anticipated in the preview. These were proposals, not awards.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “has submitted proposals for more than 20 Department of War funding programs with aggregate initial potential value of several hundred million dollars.”

surprises.description: A $2.3 million charge for stock-based compensation from June executive equity awards was identified as a driver of higher G&A, an expense detail the preview did not flag. The reported $12.3 million net loss and $0.27 GAAP loss per share were still within the preview’s broader stated in-line range.
surprises.fact_evidence: GAAP net loss was $12.3 million, with G&A rising to $8.1 million, “driven by $2.3 million in stock-based compensation from June executive equity awards.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated net loss of “$(11.6)–(12.1)M” and GAAP EPS of “$(0.25)–(0.26),” while describing a GAAP print of “–$0.25 to –$0.27” as roughly in line on its model.

in_line: Q2 revenue was $5.8 million, as already pre-announced and expected in the preview.
FY2026 revenue guidance of $24–27 million was reaffirmed, as the preview’s base case anticipated.
Cash and securities ended the quarter at approximately $43.7 million, essentially in line with the preview’s approximately $44 million expectation.
The $2.9 million Air Force robotics contract expansion, bringing the total to over $10.6 million, was already flagged in the preview as an exercised option.
The reported $12.3 million net loss and $0.27 GAAP loss per share were within the preview’s stated broader in-line range, despite landing slightly worse than its central model estimates.

surprises.description: CEVA raised its FY2026 revenue-growth outlook to 13–15%, above the preview’s expected reaffirmation of the prior 8–12% range and its top-end framing. The new range starts above the old ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to 13-15%, up from the previous 12% guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided FY26 revenue to the top end of +8–12%”; the preview said to watch for a reaffirmation of the “top end of 8–12%.”

surprises.description: Royalty revenue was $10.8 million, above the preview’s roughly $10 million expectation and far better than its modeled 7% year-over-year decline: royalties were marginally above the prior-year quarter. That offers more support for the royalty recovery than the preview’s base case assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Royalty revenue was $10.8 million … up 17% sequentially but only marginally above the prior-year’s $10.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected royalty revenue of “$10.0M (–7% YoY)” and said “anything at/above $10M” would keep the FY bridge intact.

surprises.description: Management now expects non-GAAP operating income to grow approximately 70% in 2026, above the preview’s expected +40–50% range. The net-income growth outlook of approximately 50%, by contrast, is at the top of that expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects non-GAAP operating income to grow approximately 70% and non-GAAP net income approximately 50% year-over-year for 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the expected FY26 target as “non-GAAP operating income/net income +40–50% YoY.”

surprises.description: Management identified memory pricing and broader supply constraints as risks to second-half handset royalties, qualifying the expected recovery with specific ongoing risks. The preview emphasized the H2 royalty ramp and said an unqualified reiteration of recovery would support the FY bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged memory pricing dynamics and broader supply constraints as key risk variables that could affect second-half handset royalties.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “an unqualified reiteration of the H2 recovery” and described the FY guide as dependent on “a royalty recovery.”

surprises.description: The AI-platform custom-silicon selection was already anticipated in the preview, but the call added that this customer category is expected to generate meaningfully higher royalty per unit than typical NPU offerings. The preview had specifically called for clarification of the deal’s royalty economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A leading global AI and computing platform company selected CEVA's new NPU IP for its next-generation custom AI silicon, a new category of customer expected to yield meaningfully higher royalty per unit than typical NPU offerings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “major U.S. software/AI platform company licensing NeuPro-M for a custom AI silicon program” and said to watch whether management quantified “prepaid/royalty economics.”

surprises.description: CEVA signed 10 licensing agreements, below the preview’s expectation that the count would hold in the low-to-mid teens. The quarter did include two first-time customers and two direct OEM agreements, which partly offsets the lower count.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEVA signed 10 licensing agreements in the quarter, including two with first-time customers and two directly with OEMs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a healthy signature would be a “deal count holding in the low-to-mid teens.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $29 million exceeded the preview’s $28.15–28.6 million consensus range and $28.6 million base case, although it remained within the company’s $26–30 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 13% year-over-year and 7% sequentially to $29 million, exceeding internal expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 consensus of “$28.15M” and “$28.6M” and a base case of “$28.6M.”

in_line: Licensing and related revenue was $18.2 million, close to the preview’s roughly $18 million implied expectation and $18.6 million base case.
Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.08 was at the top of the preview’s $0.073–$0.08 consensus range, though below its $0.09 base case.
The approximately 50% FY2026 non-GAAP net-income growth outlook was at the top of the preview’s expected +40–50% range.

surprises.description: Q2 net sales were $510 million, about 8% above the $472.1 million consensus in the preview. Residential sales also exceeded the preview’s estimated $395–405 million range, with OmniMax contributing $182 million versus the roughly $150 million modeled for a full quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Gibraltar Q2 2026 net sales rose 64.6% to $510 million”; residential sales were “up 85% to $425.9 million (OmniMax contributing $182 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $472.1M”; residential estimate “$395–405M,” built with “~$150M full-quarter OmniMax.”

surprises.description: Combined pro forma building products organic growth was 15.5%, far stronger than the preview’s expectation of roughly a 3% residential organic decline. The reported growth included 9.7% price/mix and 7.1% participation gains despite a market down 1.3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “On a combined pro forma basis, building products grew 15.5% organically, comprised of 9.7% price/mix and 7.1% participation gains, offsetting a market down 1.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated residential sales “less ~3% organic decline” and noted residential organic growth “−3% in Q1.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.11, above the preview’s $1.02 consensus, even with a larger-than-modeled net interest impact. The preview estimated about $14.6 million of quarterly net interest, while the call cited a $20.6 million impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS reached $1.11 including a $20.6 million net interest impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $1.02”; the preview also said “~$14.6M/quarter of net interest.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $88 million landed within the preview’s $85–90 million estimate, but the 17.3% margin was below the preview’s estimated 18.0–19.0% range. The margin nevertheless expanded 350 basis points sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 59.7% to $88 million with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 350 basis points sequentially to 17.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | est. $85–90M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | est. 18.0–19.0%.”

surprises.description: Management raised the 2026 synergy commitment to $29.4 million, above the $26 million target expected in the preview, and said it was running roughly a year ahead of plan. It expects $17 million realized in 2026, with $7 million realized to date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its 2026 synergy commitment to $29.4 million executed with $17 million realized in 2026, of which $7 million has been realized to date, running roughly a year ahead of plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The 2026 synergy target was raised to $26M at Q1”; the preview sought evidence of a “hard exit run-rate” against that target.

surprises.description: The reiterated adjusted EBITDA guidance range topped out at $315 million, below the preview’s stated $326 million high end. Sales and adjusted EPS guidance were reiterated at the ranges the preview had listed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reiterated full-year 2026 guidance of net sales between $1.76 billion and $1.83 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $310 million to $315 million, and adjusted EPS of $3.65 to $4.05.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$310M” to “$326M” and expected the “FY guide reaffirmed unchanged” in its base scenario.

surprises.description: Roofing demand commentary was weaker than the preview’s near-term residential setup suggested: management estimated first-half end-market demand down mid-single digits, retail POS down 8% to 10%, and expected softness to persist for the rest of the year. The preview had cited April shipments and bookings ahead of 2025 levels and modeled only about a 3% residential organic decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimates actual end-market roofing demand was down mid-single digits in the first half (with retail POS down 8% to 10%) and expects this soft demand to persist through the rest of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “April shipments and bookings were ‘on plan and ahead of 2025 levels,’ with early May consistent,” and estimated “~3% organic decline” for residential.

surprises.description: Ag-tech backlog was $66.2 million, below the $84 million level highlighted in the preview, and was down 34% year over year. The call attributed the decline to project timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ag-tech net sales grew 8.7% organically to strong margins … but backlog fell 34% year-over-year to $66.2 million on project timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Agtech $84M” as the backlog level to watch.

surprises.description: The company announced a new supply agreement adding 630 locations for trims and flashings, taking coverage for a key customer above 1,700 locations. The preview did not flag this agreement; revenue is expected to start in late Q4 2026 and primarily affect 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company won a new supply agreement adding 630 locations to bring trims and flashings supply to over 1,700 locations for a key customer, with revenue starting late Q4 2026 but primarily impacting 2027.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $88 million, within the preview’s estimated $85–90 million range.
The company reiterated sales guidance of $1.76–$1.83 billion and adjusted EPS guidance of $3.65–$4.05, matching the ranges in the preview.
Net debt of $1.2 billion, net leverage of 3.9x, and the target of approximately 2.5x leverage by Q1 2028 were consistent with the preview’s balance-sheet discussion.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.90, above the preview’s working consensus of $0.84 and its $0.82 Zacks estimate, though it landed within the preview’s stated $0.90–$0.92 buy-side whisper range. The beat was therefore positive versus published consensus but not versus the higher investor bar the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS reached $0.90,” representing “14% underlying growth in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.84 (Public.com); $0.82 (Zacks)” and “the functional buy-side bar is $0.90–0.92.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached the top of the preview’s expected range, and the quarter also benefited from $8 million of tariff refunds that the preview explicitly said were not assumed. The refund benefit was partly offset by ongoing tariff costs and unplanned inflation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margins hit 62%,” aided by “an $8 million benefit from 2025 tariff refunds,” partly offset by “$4 million of ongoing tariff impact and $2 million of unplanned inflation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin (est.) ~61.5–62.0%”; the preview also said “no refunds assumed.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.9%, just below the preview’s 18.0–18.3% Q2 expectation and its roughly 18.0% base case. The shortfall was small, but the preview noted that the full-year guide required roughly 19% margins in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.9%, up 70 basis points on an underlying basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs ~18.0–18.3% to keep that credible”; the base case assumed “margin ~18.0%.”

surprises.description: First-half free cash flow was already slightly positive, indicating better progress by midyear than the preview’s description of the greater-than-25% conversion target as back-half loaded. The full-year conversion target itself was reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $31 million, a $27 million improvement versus prior year,” delivering “slightly positive first-half free cash flow” with full-year conversion guidance “greater than 25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the “>25% conversion target” “back-half loaded” and said FCF was the “single biggest swing factor.”

surprises.description: Leverage was 3.1x, slightly above the preview’s estimate of roughly 3.0x net leverage. Management’s goal of moving below 3x this year would open more M&A flexibility, but that goal was not yet achieved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Leverage was reduced to 3.1 times” with a goal of “moving below 3 times this year,” which would “open more flexibility for M&A.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “roughly 3.0x” FY26 EBITDA net leverage.

surprises.description: Nebula’s competitive-user adoption was strong: more than 80% of new instrumentation sets went to competitive users. The preview highlighted Nebula-driven conversions as important but did not specify an adoption level this high.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nebula continued driving growth with over 80% of new instrumentation sets going to competitive users in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case required “Hip/Knee” growth on “Nebula/Surgical Impactor conversions.”

surprises.description: Management specifically flagged a seasonally softer Q3, attributing it to Western Europe softness and Middle East disruption, with sales acceleration expected in Q4. The preview anticipated Middle East exposure and Q4 acceleration, but did not flag this Q3 softness as a distinct near-term outlook issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects a seasonally softer Q3 due to Western Europe softness and Middle East disruption, with sales acceleration anticipated in Q4”; the conflict created “a 100 basis point headwind to international growth” and “about a 40 basis point headwind to total Enovis growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “international/Middle East softness (~$1–2M monthly exposure)” and expected the “other half” of selling-day recovery “in Q4.”

in_line: Sales of $583 million and 5% organic growth were in line with the preview’s working revenue estimate of about $582 million and base expectation of roughly 5% organic growth; the Dr. Comfort divestiture headwind was also anticipated.
Recon grew 6% organically, meeting the preview’s target of at least 6%; P&R grew 3%, meeting its target of at least 3%.
Adjusted gross margin of 62% was within the preview’s estimated 61.5–62.0% range, apart from the unanticipated tariff-refund benefit noted above.
Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed, as the preview considered a reaffirmed guide the likeliest outcome.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $13.4 million, far above the preview’s derived $5–6 million expectation and even within the preview’s $9–14 million bull scenario. Management attributed the increase primarily to higher milestone revenue from partners’ clinical progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $13.4 million,” primarily “driven by higher milestone revenue from partner clinical progress.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$5.0–6.0M (derived)” and the preview’s bull scenario of “$9–14M.”

surprises.description: OmniAb raised its FY2026 revenue guide to $32–36 million, above the prior $28–33 million range and above the preview’s $30.81 million consensus. The increase was less than the preview’s bull-case guide of roughly $33–38 million, but still exceeded its base-case expectation of reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $32-36 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The current guide was “$28–33M”; FY2026 revenue consensus was “$30.81M”; the base case expected the guide to be “reaffirmed at $28–33M.”

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was much smaller than expected: Q2 net loss was $5.9 million, or $0.05 per share, versus the preview’s consensus EPS loss of $0.12. The preview noted EPS was a low-signal metric, but this was still a substantial gap versus estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss improved to $5.9 million ($0.05/share),” reflecting “operating efficiencies in R&D and G&A.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 EPS consensus was “–$0.12”; HC Wainwright estimated “–$0.10” and Leerink “–$0.15.”

surprises.description: The company raised its year-end cash outlook to $37–41 million, above the prior $33–38 million guide. The preview’s liquidity discussion treated roughly $42 million or more as acceptable, but that figure referred to total liquidity, so it is not directly comparable to this cash-only forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: OmniAb now expects “to end the year with $37-41 million in cash,” versus its prior guidance of $33–38 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior year-end cash guide was “$33–38M”; the preview said total liquidity of “≥$42M is fine.”

surprises.description: The portfolio and partner base grew beyond the preview’s Q1 baseline: active programs rose from 409 to 425, clinical-stage or approved programs from 32 to 34, and active partners from 107 to 110. The two new Q2 licensing agreements also contrast with the preview’s concern that partner adds had been flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: OmniAb reported “425 active programs,” “34 active clinical programs and approved products,” and “110 active partners”; it signed agreements with “Argenix” and “Enrosa Therapeutics.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “409” active programs, “32” clinical-stage/approved programs, and “107” active partners, noting partner adds were “flat vs. YE25.”

surprises.description: xPloration moved beyond the preview’s modest Q1 contribution and sales-funnel discussion: it sold two instruments in Q2, bringing the installed base to four, and management described strong instrument margins with even better consumables margins. The preview had flagged the first meaningful instrument and consumable sales as something to watch, but did not anticipate these sales or margin details.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The exploration single B-cell screening platform sold two instruments in Q2, bringing the installed base to four units,” with “strong margins on instruments and even better margins on consumables.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: xPloration “contributed just $54K in Q1 with a ‘growing sales funnel’”; the preview said to “watch for the first real instrument/consumable dollars.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that six Phase 1 or Phase 2 clinical programs now use OmniAb’s genetically engineered chicken platforms, describing the technology as globally unique. The preview discussed the broader clinical portfolio but did not flag this platform-specific level of clinical validation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Six clinical programs (Phase 1 or Phase 2) now derive from” the OmniDab and OmniChicken platforms, validating a technology OmniAb claims is “unique globally.”

surprises.description: Management added that many royalty agreements have tiered rates that increase as partner product revenue grows. The preview identified royalties as a future growth driver and cited an average royalty rate, but did not mention this feature that could raise rates as successful products scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Many royalty agreements [are] structured as tiered rates that rise with partner product revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described royalties as “the line that eventually justifies the bull case” and cited an “~3.4% average contracted royalty rate.”

in_line: Management said milestone revenue is front-end loaded in 2026, implying weaker second-half revenue; the preview had already warned that the first-half milestone strength could leave a decelerating back half.

Management continued to position royalties as a future growth driver, consistent with the preview’s focus on royalty revenue as a longer-term driver; the call facts do not establish a near-term royalty inflection.

surprises.description: Azenta reported Q3 revenue of $161 million, about 8% above the preview’s $149.2 million consensus, a substantially stronger quarter than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 total revenue was $161 million, up 12% as reported and 9% organically, exceeding company outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $149.2M”

surprises.description: Instead of another cut or guidance narrowed toward the low end, Azenta raised its full-year revenue outlook and improved its organic outlook from a range that included a 2% decline to flat-to-up 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $613-618 million and improved organic revenue outlook to flat to up 1% (versus prior down 2% to up 1%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any further cut, or a narrowing to the low end, is the main risk.” The base scenario anticipated “FY guide narrowed toward the low end ($603–610M).”

surprises.description: Azenta started using its buyback authorization, repurchasing about $50 million of shares despite the preview noting that no shares had been repurchased to date and that continued inaction would be notable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “During the quarter, the company repurchased approximately 2.3 million shares for $50 million, leaving roughly $200 million available under the buyback authorization through December 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$250M authorization running through December 2028, and zero repurchased to date” and “continued inaction on the buyback would be a notable signal.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS came in at $0.16, above the preview’s approximately $0.11 consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $0.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | ~$0.11.”

surprises.description: The Q4 outlook calls for a low-single-digit organic revenue decline, rather than the growth implied by the preview’s estimate that Q4 would need to deliver $161–178 million against $159.2 million a year earlier. The unusually strong Q4 2025 comparison and the pulled-forward order add to the near-term hurdle.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects Q4 organic revenue to decline low single digits due to a tough comparison against Q4 2025, which was Multiomics' highest quarterly revenue in company history”; a “$3 million preclinical order” was “pulled forward from Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If Q3 lands at consensus $149.2M, Q4 must be $161–178M vs. $159.2M a year ago — i.e. +1% to +12% YoY in a single quarter.”

surprises.description: Multiomics performed better than the preview’s concern about another weak quarter: it grew 8% organically and its gross margin improved. But North America remained below prior-year levels, and management attributed part of the improvement to delayed NIH projects catching up and an order shifted forward from Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiomics growing 8%” organically and its gross margin “improved 550 basis points to 46.5%.” North America “improved from a mid-teens decline in the first half but remained below prior-year levels,” with part of the Q3 gain from delayed NIH-funded projects and a “$3 million preclinical order pulled forward from Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second consecutive weak quarter would question the December 2025 Investor Day long-range plan.”

surprises.description: Sample Management Solutions grew 9% organically, a stronger outcome than the preview’s concern about continued weakness in automated stores and cryogenic systems.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sample Management Solutions growing 9% organically.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Automated Stores and Cryogenic Systems drove the Q2 organic decline” and that “Order/backlog commentary matters more than revenue.”

surprises.description: Despite that organic growth, Sample Management Solutions gross margin fell 750 basis points year over year to 45.9%, with lower volumes and fixed-cost absorption weighing on automated stores and cryogenic systems.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sample Management Solutions gross margin fell 750 basis points year-over-year to 45.9%, driven by lower volumes and unfavorable fixed cost absorption in automated stores and cryogenic systems.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged adjusted gross margin as “where management flagged the problem” and identified automated stores and cryogenic systems as drivers of the Q2 decline, but gave no segment-margin estimate.

surprises.description: Azenta disclosed a $6.5 million partial reversal of a held-for-sale valuation allowance related to B Medical Systems, an accounting benefit not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recorded a $6.5 million partial reversal of a held-for-sale valuation allowance.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin recovered to approximately 11.4%, up 610 basis points sequentially but still below the 12.3% year-ago margin, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a recovery from Q2’s trough that would remain below the year-ago level.
Full-year free cash flow is still expected to improve 10–15% year over year, matching the outlook the preview said had been reset to that range.

surprises.description: Total orders were $28.9 million, well below the preview’s $35 million bogey and even below its sub-$31 million bear-case threshold. Orders fell 9% sequentially, ending a three-quarter run above $30 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 orders were $28.9 million, down 9% sequentially but up 4% year-over-year, ending three consecutive quarters above $30 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview set “≥$35M” as the orders bogey and said the bear case involved “Orders <$31M.”

surprises.description: Backlog ended at $45.4 million, well short of the preview’s $52 million bogey, weakening the expected backlog support for the second-half revenue ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog stood at $45.4 million, down 12% sequentially but up 20% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q1 exit $51.8M” and set a backlog bogey of “≥$52M.”

surprises.description: The material weakness was not yet remediated: management expected remediation to be effective by fiscal year-end. That is less reassuring than the preview’s expectation that management believed the weakness had already been remediated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company disclosed a material weakness in internal controls at Alfamation tied to the Q1 restatement, with remediation expected to be effective by fiscal year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company “believes that the material weakness has now been remediated” and listed “Confined + remediated” as the control bogey.

surprises.description: Auto EV orders dropped sharply after four strong quarters, a weaker demand signal in a market the preview flagged because of Alfamation’s exposure. The preview did not quantify an expected decline in Auto EV orders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Auto EV orders declined 67% sequentially after four strong quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch Semi … and Auto/EV (Alfamation's exposure, and the source of the margin problem).”

surprises.description: Semi orders were exceptionally strong, surging sequentially and year over year to their highest intake in six quarters. This was stronger than the preview’s general expectation that semi order strength would continue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Semi orders surged 56% sequentially and 64% year-over-year, the strongest semi order intake in six quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull-case operating assumptions said, “Semi and Defense/Aero order strength continues.”

surprises.description: The company reported $0.04 diluted EPS, above the preview’s own approximate GAAP breakeven estimate. The preview did not have a GAAP consensus estimate, so the gap is against its derived estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income was $0.5 million ($0.04 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “GAAP EPS ≈ $0.00” and listed preliminary GAAP EPS as “~$0.00 (est.).”

surprises.description: Cash rose to $22.1 million, substantially above the preview’s cited $12.9 million, while total debt was $6.2 million rather than the approximately $8.5 million cited there. This left the company with $62 million of liquidity and low leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $22.1 million in cash (up $6.4 million), $62 million in total liquidity, total debt of $6.2 million, and a low leverage ratio of 0.8x trailing-12-month adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “cash $12.9M vs. ~$8.5M debt” and flagged positive operating cash flow as a bogey.

in_line: Revenue was effectively in line with the pre-announced result: the preview cited preliminary revenue of approximately $35.0 million, and reported revenue was $35.3 million.
Gross margin was broadly in line with the pre-announced level: the preview cited approximately 40%, and reported gross margin was 40.5%.
The full-year revenue and gross-margin guidance was already known from the July 31 revision: $135–140 million revenue and approximately 43% gross margin.

surprises.description: The preview expected adjusted EBITDA to be roughly breakeven in its base case, but AMTX reported positive adjusted EBITDA of $9.7 million. Operating income also turned positive at $5.8 million, and net loss narrowed to $9.4 million—well below the preview’s implied base-case net loss of roughly $20–23 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved by $15.5 million to a positive $9.7 million”; “Operating income swung to a positive $5.8 million”; “net loss narrowed to $9.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … EPS -$0.28 to -$0.32” and “adj. EBITDA roughly breakeven.”

surprises.description: AMTX’s quarter-end cash was only $1 million, below the $4.8 million reported exiting Q1, despite the preview’s focus on 45Z monetization as a source of cash. The preview also cited about $14.5 million of net proceeds from a July 9 credit sale, but those proceeds arrived after quarter-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash was just $1 million at quarter-end, though the company received $17.6 million in net proceeds from selling 45Z credits on July 9.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash was $4.8M” exiting Q1; the preview noted the July 9 sale “netting ~ $14.5M cash” and identified balance-sheet and refinancing language as the highest-weight issue.

surprises.description: Management outlined substantial prospective 45Z upside not anticipated in the preview: a DOE correction to dairy RNG’s emissions rate could lift its credit value from $15.20 to over $75 per MMBtu. The preview cited the current $15.20 value but did not flag the expected correction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 45Z credit for dairy RNG was valued at only $15.20 per MMBtu at a negative 42 emissions rate, but management expects a DOE correction toward negative 375–420 that could yield over $75 per MMBtu.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 credits ran … ~$15.20/MMBtu of RNG,” computed under the updated DOE model.

surprises.description: Management also forecast new 45Z value streams beyond the preview’s discussion of existing credit monetization: $6–24 million of ethanol credits, including an 18-month look-back catch-up, and $12–15 million per year from CO2 reuse. These are prospective amounts, not reported Q2 results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management anticipates three separate 45Z updates worth: $6–24 million (ethanol, with an 18-month look-back catch-up), $12–15 million/year (CO2 reuse), plus dairy RNG upside.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed existing 45Z credits and monetization, including “2026 credits ran ~ $0.33/ethanol gallon and ~ $15.20/MMBtu of RNG,” but did not anticipate these additional updates or amounts.

surprises.description: Q2 India biodiesel revenue was only $2.5 million, below the preview’s base-case narrative of sequential growth driven partly by an India ramp. The preview did flag that the newly announced allocations might not ship until Q3, so the weak Q2 revenue contrasts with the expected ramp but does not contradict the allocations themselves.
surprises.fact_evidence: “India biodiesel revenue fell to $2.5 million in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case projected “Sequential growth from $54.6M on India ramp,” while the preview noted that the Aug. 4 allocations might mean shipments slipped past quarter-end.

surprises.description: The quarter included $8.6 million of 45Z credits, slightly above the preview’s expected $5–8 million contribution. The preview’s range was close, so the excess was modest rather than a major departure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Section 45Z credits contributed $8.6 million in Q2 ($6.4 million ethanol, $2.2 million dairy RNG).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected a “45Z contribution $5–8M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected about $14.5 million in net proceeds from the July 9 45Z credit sale, while the call reported $17.6 million. The proceeds were higher than previewed, although they arrived after quarter-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received $17.6 million in net proceeds from selling 45Z credits on July 9.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the July 9 sale was “netting ~ $14.5M cash.”

in_line: Revenue was $62.7 million: below the $67.69 million consensus figure, but within the preview’s $60–65 million base case and near its $60–63 million buy-side whisper, which it described as the more relevant expectation.

The MVR project remained on track for operation by the end of 2026 and was still expected to add roughly $32 million in annual cash flow by reducing natural gas use about 80%, as the preview anticipated.
The India allocation was in line with the preview: over 18 million liters to three government oil marketing companies over three months, worth approximately $17 million.

surprises.description: Vontier raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $3.45–$3.55 from $3.35–$3.50, despite lowering its operating-margin-expansion outlook. The preview expected the EPS range to be maintained or narrowed, with an increase toward $3.45–$3.50 only in its bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $3.45-$3.55, representing 8%-11% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect either a maintain or a narrowing”; the bull case described “FY EPS raised toward $3.45–3.50.”

surprises.description: Mobility Technologies delivered a stronger-than-expected margin recovery: underlying margins expanded 170 bps to about 21%, above the preview’s base-case recovery toward 18% and even its bull-case level near 19%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Underlying margins expanding 170 bps to ~21%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “explicitly guided to recovery in Q2”; its base case anticipated MT margin “partially recovers (~18%)” and its bull case “back toward 19%.”

surprises.description: Vontier cut FY26 operating-margin-expansion guidance to about 100 bps from 130 bps, even as it raised EPS guidance. That is a deterioration from the margin outlook the preview expected to be maintained or narrowed only modestly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trimming full-year operating margin expansion guidance to ~100 bps from a prior 130 bps.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described FY26 guidance as “~130 bps of adj. margin expansion” and expected “either a maintain or a narrowing” of the guide.

surprises.description: Repair Solutions’ weakness became more consequential than the preview’s warning of continued erosion: margins fell another 180 bps, management changed the segment’s leadership, and it revised its outlook down by $7–8 million, with full-year margins now expected to fall about 150 bps to around 19%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repair Solutions margins declined 180 basis points and were the primary drag, prompting a leadership change and a $7-8 million downward revision, with full-year segment margins now expected down ~150 bps to around 19%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “continued erosion is a drag” and noted Q1 Repair Solutions margin was “-180 bps to 19.9%.”

surprises.description: Q2 core sales were flat rather than the roughly 1% decline implied by guidance, a small upside to the expected trajectory, with Environmental & Fueling Solutions driving the beat. The preview cautioned against relying on reported revenue because of the Teletrac timing issue and directed investors to core growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 core sales were approximately flat year-over-year against a tough ~11% core growth comparison from the prior year, but came in slightly ahead of guidance driven by Environmental & Fueling Solutions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview table listed Q2 core sales growth at “~-1% (midpoint)” and warned that the reported revenue line was not a clean signal.

surprises.description: The reported 190-bp year-over-year adjusted operating-margin expansion substantially exceeded the preview’s expected roughly 80 bps, but about 120 bps came from a one-time tariff refund, leaving underlying expansion at 70 bps—slightly below that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin expanded 190 basis points year-over-year, though ~120 basis points came from a onetime IEEPA tariff refund, leaving underlying margin expansion of 70 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview table expected “+~80 bps Y/Y” in adjusted operating margin.

surprises.description: Environmental & Fueling Solutions raised its full-year growth outlook from low-to-mid-single digits to mid-single digits, an upgrade beyond the preview’s focus on whether the segment’s growth and dispenser demand would hold up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Environmental & Fueling Solutions delivered ~5% core growth with double-digit dispenser growth, and full-year guidance was raised from low-to-mid to mid-single-digit growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called EFS the company’s growth carrier and said to watch whether “the c-store capex cycle is still intact” and dispenser demand remained durable; it did not anticipate a higher FY growth guide.

surprises.description: Mobility Technologies’ full-year growth outlook was cut from low-to-mid-single digits to low-single digits as car-wash software upgrades slipped because of permitting delays. This weakens the growth trajectory the preview said needed to support the company’s roughly 3% full-year core-growth guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mobility Tech full-year guidance was lowered from low-to-mid to low-single-digit growth as DRB/Patheon car wash software upgrades slipped due to permitting delays, with 90% of the installed base still on legacy technology.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “FY ~3% core guide” required a “meaningful H2 step-up” and flagged core growth trajectory as a key issue.

surprises.description: Mobility Technologies’ reported core sales declined because of a roughly $25 million prior-year vehicle-identification shipment comparison, even though underlying demand grew mid-single digits. The preview did not flag this specific headwind, so the underlying demand picture was stronger than the reported segment result suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mobility Technologies core sales declined due to a ~$25 million (10-point) headwind from prior-year vehicle identification shipments, but underlying demand grew mid-single digits.”

surprises.description: Vontier disclosed an acquisition not anticipated in the preview: EKOS, a fleet energy-management business with about 80% recurring revenue and 25% annual growth. It paid $43 million in cash plus an earn-out, and expects $15–17 million of FY27 revenue at mid-teens margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired EKOS for $43 million cash plus an earn-out, a fleet energy management business with ~80% recurring revenue growing 25% annually and expected to generate $15-17 million revenue in fiscal 2027 at mid-teens margins.”

surprises.description: Vontier increased its share-repurchase authorization to $1 billion, beyond the buyback activity already known to the preview. The preview noted about $200 million of repurchases in H1, but did not anticipate the larger authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company increased its share repurchase authorization to $1 billion,” and “expects ~$250 million in buybacks for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Vontier had repurchased “$70M in Q1 and $130M in Q2” and called buyback pace a live issue; it did not mention a $1 billion authorization.

surprises.description: Cost savings were running ahead of the full-year commitment, a favorable cost-control update not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost savings are tracking above the $50 million full-year commitment.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted free cash flow rose to $98 million, about 80% conversion. The preview wanted a visible recovery from Q1’s $28 million and described its base case as improving FCF with the 95% full-year conversion target still back-half weighted; the reported figure is consistent with that broad expectation, though it does not establish that the annual target will be met.

Environmental & Fueling Solutions produced about 5% core growth and double-digit dispenser growth, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the segment would remain a source of growth and its focus on continued dispenser strength.

surprises.description: Gross profit was $10.4 million, below the preview’s expected seasonal lift to roughly $11.0–$11.3 million and even slightly below its $10.5 million downside threshold. Gross margin was 16.3%, well short of the roughly 17.6% implied by the preview’s seasonal pattern.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross profit was $10.4 million; gross margin was 16.3%, versus 18.5% a year ago and 15.7% in the prior quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Seasonality alone should deliver ~$11.0M+”; the base case expected “$11.1–11.3M / ~17.7%,” and the preview said “Below $10.5M means the mix drag is worse than framed.”

surprises.description: The company recorded an $11 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge, which the preview did not anticipate. Management said it was triggered by the decline in market capitalization and did not affect liquidity, cash flow, or debt covenants.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded an $11 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge triggered by a decline in market capitalization,” with “no impact on liquidity, cash flow, or debt covenants.”

surprises.description: Revenue slightly exceeded the $63.55 million consensus, and the year-over-year increase was stronger than the preview’s expected 6.8%. The beat was modest, but it confirmed the expected return to year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue was $64.1 million, up 8% year-over-year and 4% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$63.55M” with “+6.8%” year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: Industrial volumes improved in Q2, contrary to the preview’s base case that they would remain flat. Management also expects industrial volumes to ramp at select large customers, supporting sequential revenue growth and flat-to-slightly-higher gross margins in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue was driven in part by “~$3.3 million in industrial volume improvements”; management guided to sequential Q3 revenue growth and gross margins “flat to slightly up” as industrial volumes ramp at select large customers.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “industrial still flat”; it described a Q2 confirmation of industrial improvement as “the first real macro green shoot in two years.”

surprises.description: The company reported four new wallet-share wins in Q2, including one with a large national automotive parts retailer, and said it had closed nine seven-figure wallet-share opportunities since the second half of 2025. The preview focused on a QSR account and did not flag this broader set of wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company landed four new wallet-share wins in Q2, including one with a large national automotive parts retailer,” and “has closed nine seven-figure wallet-share opportunities since the back half of 2025.”

surprises.description: SG&A was lower than the preview’s $8.6 million base-case estimate, despite revenue growth, extending the cost reductions into the first half. It also remained comfortably below the preview’s $9 million caution threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: SG&A fell 11% year-over-year to $8.2 million despite 8% revenue growth; first-half SG&A was down 20%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected SG&A to “hold[] ~$8.6M”; the preview said “Anything at or above $9.0M without an explanation undercuts the cost-out narrative.”

surprises.description: Working-capital efficiency improved more than the preview had discussed: DSOs fell from the mid-70s in Q1 to about 70 days, and working-capital days dropped to 5. The preview highlighted cash generation and debt repayment but did not identify these operating metrics as expected improvements.
surprises.fact_evidence: DSOs improved to roughly 70 days from the mid-70s in Q1, with a near-term target of the mid-60s; working-capital days dropped to 5 from 12 in Q1 and 19 a year ago.

in_line: The company made the second voluntary $2 million early payment on its Monroe Capital term debt, matching the preview’s explicit focus on a second voluntary prepayment.
Management said macroeconomic uncertainty is elongating the sales cycle for new large-brand opportunities, consistent with the preview’s base case of delayed pipeline conversion.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.25 billion, above the preview’s $1.22 billion estimate and above the preview’s bull-case threshold of $1.24 billion. That was a stronger beat than the preview’s base case of $1.21–$1.23 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $1.25 billion,” with results “at the high end or above guidance ranges.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate: Revenue $1.22B”; the bull scenario was “≥$1.24B,” while the base scenario was “$1.21–1.23B.”

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS of $3.30 exceeded the preview’s $3.00–$3.05 estimate and the $3.20 ceiling of the company’s guidance range. The preview expected a beat, but the reported result was materially above its estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net earnings were $232 million or $3.30 per diluted share,” “exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate: … EPS ~ $3.00–3.05”; company guidance was “$2.90 ± $0.30.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $1.35 billion at the midpoint is well above the preview’s roughly $1.26 billion base expectation and above its $1.30 billion bull-case threshold. This signals a stronger next-quarter revenue outlook than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $1.35 billion (±$40M),” with continued sequential and accelerating year-over-year growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Q3 Rev Guide ~$1.26B”; the bull case expected “≥$1.30B.”

surprises.description: Q3 EPS guidance of $3.58 at the midpoint is above the preview’s roughly $3.25 Q3 estimate. The preview therefore understated the earnings level implied by the company’s outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for … EPS of $3.58 (±$0.31).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s FY26 build assumed “Q3E ~$3.25.”

surprises.description: The semiconductor outlook is stronger than the preview’s caution around a Q3 figure below roughly $590 million: management said Q3 implies semiconductor year-over-year growth above 50%, far ahead of estimated WFE growth. That points to acceleration rather than the deceleration the preview identified as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance implies semi YoY growth accelerating to over 50%, well ahead of estimated WFE growth of 25-30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “If Q3 semi guides below ~$590M, the buy-side reads deceleration”; it also highlighted a “Q3 semi guide vs. a ~$600M whisper.”

surprises.description: Electronics & Packaging revenue reached $381 million, substantially above the preview’s $350 million guide and its $360 million bull-case marker. The reported chemistry-equipment demand and visibility through 2027 also extend beyond the preview’s near-term durability discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Electronics & Packaging revenue rose to $381 million (up 44% YoY),” with “chemistry equipment demand described as the strongest ever and visibility now extending through 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 Electronics & Packaging guidance of “$350M ± $15M,” and its bull case called for “E&P >$360M.”

surprises.description: Specialty Industrial revenue of $313 million came in above the preview’s $300 million guide and its $310 million upper end. The segment’s highest level since 2023 and growth driven by datacom and defense were additional strength versus the preview’s expectation of only a slight uptick.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty Industrial revenue grew to $313 million (up 14% YoY), the highest since 2023, driven by datacom and defense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 Specialty Industrial guidance of “$300M ± $10M” and described the expected trend as a “slight uptick.”

surprises.description: The margin outlook fell short of the preview’s hoped-for inflection: Q3 gross margin is guided at 47%, not 48%, and factory ramp costs are expected to weigh on results. Q2’s 47.6% headline margin also included about 100 basis points of discrete benefits, making it less evidence of durable margin expansion than the preview’s bull case sought.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 gross margin is guided to 47% (±100bps), down from Q2's reported 47.6% which included roughly 100bps of discrete benefits mainly from tariff/duty refunds,” with “50-80bps of quarterly headwind expected from factory ramp costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “Q3 guide of 48%” was the margin-inflection datapoint bulls wanted; its bull case called for “GM 47.5%+ with 48% Q3 guide.”

surprises.description: Management raised the scale of the capacity plans beyond the preview’s general references to Malaysia and China expansion: Penang can now support WFE of $200–$250 billion, and Guangzhou chemistry-equipment capacity is being doubled. The higher supported WFE range is a more expansive capacity signal than the preview’s $170–$180 billion 2027 WFE framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is doubling capacity at its Guangzhou chemistry equipment factory (online Q3 2027)” and “reconfigured plans so that filling out its Penang facility can support WFE in the $200-250 billion range, an increase from prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “the Malaysia supercenter and China capacity expansion ramp” and noted management had floated “$170–180B WFE for 2027.”

surprises.description: Chemistry’s AI-related revenue share is now 15–20%, above the 10% figure cited as prior guidance, and chemistry-equipment revenue this year is expected to significantly exceed its prior peak. These are stronger AI exposure and chemistry-demand indicators than the preview quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-related applications now represent 15-20% of chemistry revenue, up from 5% in 2024 and 10% in prior guidance,” while chemistry-equipment revenue “this year will significantly exceed the prior peak of roughly $200 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed chemistry equipment and AI-related advanced-PCB demand, but did not anticipate a 15–20% AI share or chemistry-equipment revenue exceeding the prior peak.

surprises.description: Leverage reached 3.0x, better than the preview’s expectation of roughly 3.2x and its sub-3.3x bull-case marker. The $100 million prepayment itself was anticipated, but the lower leverage and plans for further Q3 and Q4 prepayments were stronger than the preview’s base expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Leverage declined to 3x trailing-12-month adjusted EBITDA of $1.1 billion (down a full turn YoY),” with “a $100 million term loan prepayment made this week and additional prepayments planned for Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected leverage to move “toward ~3.2x” and said “Sub-3.3x plus a fresh term loan paydown” was the bull case.

in_line: Q2 semiconductor revenue of $554 million was close to the preview’s $550 million expectation and within its $550 million ± $15 million guidance range.
Q3 free cash flow of $188 million, about 15% of revenue, is consistent with the preview’s expectation of a sharp H2 step-up from Q1’s seasonal low.
The $100 million term-loan prepayment was anticipated; the surprise was the lower-than-expected 3.0x leverage and plans for additional prepayments.

surprises.description: The preview framed Sandersville’s roughly $2 billion buildout as a major funding gap and wanted an explicit answer on equity issuance. Management said the project’s equity portion is fully funded, no equity raises are planned for the project, and the investment-grade tenant supports favorable-rate financing without credit wrappers or equity backstops—meaningfully more reassuring, although no completed financing facility was reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The equity portion already fully funded and no equity raises planned for the project”; the tenant is “high investment-grade” and enables financing “without credit wrappers or equity backstops at favorable rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The gap is real and the market knows it. What I want: a named structure (project finance / ABS against the investment-grade lease, JV capital, or a construction facility), an indicative cost of capital, and an explicit statement on equity issuance.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $138 million, above the preview’s own $128–133 million estimate, even though it was slightly below the cited $139.4 million consensus. That makes the quarter less weak than the preview’s model implied, but not a clear consensus beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue was $138 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I model $128–133M, roughly 5–7% light”; the preview also cites “Revenue $139.4M” as consensus.

surprises.description: Gross margin declined to 38% as power prices rose, a further deterioration from the 40% Q2 level cited in the preview. The preview flagged mining unit economics as a key debate, but did not explicitly forecast another margin decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declining to 38% from 40% as power prices rose $0.01.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin fell to ~40% in Q2 FY26 from 47% in Q1”; the preview said to “watch marginal cost to mine and whether power costs are being absorbed by curtailment credits.”

in_line: The $133 million unfavorable Bitcoin mark-to-market adjustment was within the preview’s estimated $120–135 million non-cash loss.
The first Sandersville data hall remains on track for Q4 2027, matching the preview’s expected delivery start.
Texas remained under exclusivity without a signed lease, consistent with the preview’s base case of no definitive Texas lease.

surprises.description: Calumet reported $175 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes, well above the preview’s $115–125 million base estimate. The result came despite three planned turnarounds at Princeton, Cotton Valley and Montana Renewables.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Calumet delivered $175 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes in Q2 2026, despite absorbing three planned turnarounds at Princeton, Cotton Valley and Montana Renewables.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “my base build $115–125M”; the preview also said “Anything under ~$95M breaks the recovery narrative.”

surprises.description: Specialty Products & Solutions adjusted EBITDA reached $161.7 million, far above the preview’s $85–95 million estimate. The preview expected the March price increases to flow through, but the reported result also reflected more than 20 realized increases and record specialty production.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty Products & Solutions adjusted EBITDA more than doubled year-over-year to $161.7 million, driven by over 20 realized specialty price increases and a record specialty production quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SPS segment | $85–95M (est.)”; “20+ price increases implemented in March should flow through in Q2.”

surprises.description: Montana Renewables generated only $17 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes, below the preview’s $28–38 million estimate. It was offline all of April and half of May, foregoing roughly $40 million of margin, although management estimated a normalized quarterly run rate near $60 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Montana Renewables generated only $17 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes due to being offline all of April and half of May, foregoing roughly $40 million of margin, implying a normalized quarterly run rate near $60 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Montana/Renewables | $28–38M (est.)”; the preview expected Q2 to capture “only ~2 of 3 months” after MaxSAF 150 came online in early May.

surprises.description: Performance Brands EBITDA was $6.3 million, well below the preview’s $14–16 million estimate. The call cited a $7 million LIFO headwind, which the preview had not flagged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “taking a $7 million LIFO headwind in Performance Brands, whose EBITDA fell to $6.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Performance Brands | $14–16M (est.).”

surprises.description: Management described a new, capital-efficient way to expand SAF capacity by reusing a refinery reactor for SAF polishing, enabling up to 200 million gallons at 17,000 bpd by 2028 for a fraction of the originally expected capital. The preview focused on the MaxSAF 150 ramp and DOE funding for MaxSAF 300, not this expansion approach or capacity.
