surprises.fact_evidence: “A novel, capital-efficient expansion repurposing a second reactor from the fossil refinery into a patent-pending SAF polishing service will enable up to 200 million gallons of SAF at 17,000 bpd throughput by 2028 for a fraction of the originally expected capital.”

surprises.description: Calumet said renewable index margins were about $2.60 per gallon and rising, and expected Montana Renewables’ Q3 earnings to be meaningfully higher with a full quarter of production. The preview anticipated a MaxSAF ramp but did not give this Q3 earnings outlook or margin level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Renewable index margins are approximately $2.60 per gallon and rising, with management expecting Q3 Montana Renewables earnings to be meaningfully higher from a full quarter of production.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch: SAF gallons produced,” the “realized $1–2/gal SAF premium over RD,” and MaxSAF 150’s “4–5x SAF volume increase on a run-rate basis.”

surprises.description: Management said more than 10% of global paraffinic base oil capacity was offline and expected the resulting tight market to persist through 2026. The preview discussed specialty margin recovery and price increases but did not anticipate this supply disruption or its expected duration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 10% of global paraffinic base oil capacity (roughly 700,000 bpd market) is offline due to the Iranian and Russia-Ukraine wars, creating a structurally imbalanced, tight market that management expects to persist through 2026.”

surprises.description: Management said delaying the reactor reconfiguration until winter would let Montana Renewables capture more than $50 million of unexpected EBITDA during peak asphalt season. The trade-off is a planned roughly two-week fossil-side downtime early in winter, neither of which was anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Delaying the reactor reconfiguration to winter allows CMR to capture over $50 million of unexpected EBITDA during peak asphalt season before the tie-in”; the planned tie-in includes “a ~2-week fossil-side downtime.”

surprises.description: Restricted group leverage was already below 4x, with management expecting it to fall below 3x next quarter, aided by a $115 million repurchase that terminates the CMR truck rack sale-leaseback. The preview flagged deleveraging to watch, but did not anticipate that leverage milestone or the additional transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restricted group leverage fell below 4x and management expects to surpass 3x next quarter, aided by calling $100 million of 2028 notes and a $115 million repurchase terminating the CMR truck rack sale leaseback.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch FCF, the deleveraging trajectory, and DOE $1.44B facility draws against MaxSAF 300.”

surprises.description: The company generated more than $90 million of cash flow from operations despite a $70 million working-capital build. The preview flagged the prior quarter’s working-capital squeeze and said to watch cash generation, but did not set an expectation for this level of cash flow alongside another build.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated over $90 million of cash flow from operations despite a $70 million working capital build,” including crude inventory, receivables and MRL; fuel hedges offset about $20 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 saw a $100M+ working-capital squeeze”; “Watch FCF, the deleveraging trajectory.”

in_line: The $100 million call of 2028 notes was already reported in the preview as having been redeemed on July 15, 2026.

surprises.description: The preview's base case expected the post-offering runway to extend into the first half of 2028, but REGENXBIO said the strengthened balance sheet extends runway only into Q4 2027. That is shorter than the preview's central expectation, although it still covers the anticipated RGX-202 PDUFA date and wet AMD readouts.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company said its pro forma cash position of over $310 million extends its cash runway into Q4 2027, covering the expected RGX-202 PDUFA date and top-line wet AMD data readouts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected runway "into first half of 2028"; the preview also said the key distinction was "the gap between 'into 2028' and 'into mid-2027.'"

surprises.description: The call added a sizable commercial opportunity and launch-readiness detail for CERAVEC that the preview did not discuss: management estimated a roughly $10 billion wet AMD market at launch and said more than 500 surgeons had been trained on the delivery procedure. These are favorable new details, but the preview supplied no benchmark for either claim.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimated the wet AMD market could reach approximately $10 billion at launch and said over 500 surgeons globally have been trained on the CERAVEC subretinal delivery procedure.

surprises.description: The call disclosed royalty sources and potential product scale that the preview did not address: royalties continue in about 20 ex-U.S. countries after the U.S. Zolgensma patent expired, and worldwide royalties apply to an Abecma follow-on product that management said could reach up to $2 billion in sales. The U.S. patent expiry is a negative, while the continuing and potential royalties are positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: The U.S. patent on Zolgensma has expired, but royalties continue in about 20 ex-U.S. countries; the company also has worldwide coverage on Abecma/Novartis's follow-on product, which management noted could reach up to $2 billion in sales.

surprises.description: The call provided a specific plan for an ex-U.S. randomized RGX-202 study that the preview did not mention: about 100 patients, 2-to-1 active-to-placebo randomization, planned crossover, and a start in the first half of 2027. The preview gave no expectation against which to judge the study's size or design.
surprises.fact_evidence: The new ex-U.S. Affinity Rise trial will enroll approximately 100 patients at 2-to-1 active-to-placebo randomization with a planned crossover and is set to initiate in the first half of 2027.

in_line: The pro forma cash total was broadly in line with the preview's roughly $313 million estimate: the call reported over $310 million after the AbbVie milestone and offering.
RGX-202's first BLA module remains planned for Q3 2026, consistent with the preview's expectation that the Q3 BLA timing would be reaffirmed; the call also gave a Q1 2027 completion target.
RGX-202 confirmatory enrollment and dosing were completed, consistent with the preview's statement that confirmatory dosing had already been completed and the registrational program was complete.

The FDA's position that RGX-121 can proceed toward accelerated approval without additional studies, and the Q3 2026 resubmission target, were consistent with the preview's discussion of June FDA alignment and expected resubmission confirmation.
CERAVEC top-line data from the Atmosphere and Ascent studies remain expected in Q4 2026, as the preview flagged.

surprises.description: Revenue was slightly above the preview’s $376.2–$376.3 million consensus, at $377.4 million; reported 8% growth also edged the preview’s 7.7% implied growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $377.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$376.2–376.3 million”; “Implied YoY revenue growth | +7.7%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.73 modestly exceeded the preview’s estimate range of roughly $1.69–$1.70.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS up 16.1% to $1.73.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | ~$1.70 (one source: $1.69).”

surprises.description: The company reported a 13% Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin and said full-year margin should land toward the high end of its 12%–13% range, a stronger outlook than the preview’s expectation that margin stay above 12%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 13% in Q2, with management guiding full-year margin toward the higher end of its 12%-13% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expected to stay above 12%.”

surprises.description: Home health was still contracting in Q2, down 2.8% same-store, despite the preview’s note that management expected a return to growth in the second half. The decline narrowed from Q1’s 6.6%, and new admissions rose 9.8%, so the results showed improvement but not yet the expected growth inflection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Home health same-store revenue declined 2.8% but improved from a 6.6% first-quarter drop, with same-store new admissions up 9.8% following new leadership hires.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Home health segment declined but was expected to return to growth in 2H 2026”; “Q2 results will be an early read on whether that inflection is materializing.”

surprises.description: The tax rate reached 26.9%, and management now expects it to remain in the upper-20% range, above the preview’s mid-20% expectation; management attributed the change to the Work Opportunity Tax Credit program’s expiration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The tax rate rose to 26.9% and is expected to stay in the upper-20% range due to expiration of the Work Opportunity Tax Credit program at the end of 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Effective tax rate mid-20% range.”

surprises.description: A Medicare Cap accrual of just over $3 million, primarily in Ohio, unexpectedly pressured hospice margins. Management said it expects no additional cap expense and sees possible mitigation for the rest of the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A Medicare Cap accrual of just over $3 million, primarily in the Ohio market, pressured hospice margins, though management expects no additional cap expense and potential mitigation for the rest of the year.”

surprises.description: Personal Care’s fill rate improved to 84%–85%, with management attributing the improvement to faster-than-expected caregiver-app adoption in Texas—an operational improvement not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The consolidated fill rate improved to 84%-85% from the lower 80s, driven by faster-than-expected caregiver app adoption in Texas.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Faster-than-expected caregiver app adoption in Texas.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow rose to $40 million, but the call tied roughly $20 million of first-half working-capital benefit to the increase and said it is not expected to persist; the preview did not flag this cash-flow boost or its temporary nature.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow surged to $40 million from $22.5 million a year earlier, aided by roughly $20 million in first-half working capital benefits that are not expected to persist.”

surprises.description: The company reduced bank debt by $30 million sequentially and reported substantial cash and revolver availability, leaving it positioned for larger acquisitions. The preview flagged M&A as an issue to watch but did not anticipate this improvement in acquisition capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced bank debt to $64.3 million (down $30 million sequentially) with ~$100 million cash and $577.8 million in revolver availability, positioning it for larger acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “M&A/acquisition update — Addus closed the HomeCourt Home Care (Indiana) acquisition in Q1 FY2026 and had a second Indiana deal pending; watch for confirmation of closing and integration commentary.”

surprises.description: Management said the Medicaid 80/20 provision could potentially be eliminated by year-end, a new potentially favorable policy outlook not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects the Medicaid 80/20 provision to potentially be eliminated by year-end.”

in_line: Personal Care same-store hours rose 2.2%, within the 2%–2.5% target range the preview identified as a key benchmark.

surprises.description: Aethlon said its current cash resources are sufficient to fund operations for at least the next 12 months, a more reassuring statement than the preview’s base expectation that the prior going-concern language would be retained. The preview had identified softened or removed language as an upside case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management states current cash resources are sufficient to fund operations for at least the next 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side expects: retained” [going-concern language]; the preview also said the language “could plausibly be softened or removed” in its bull case.

surprises.description: Operating expenses were approximately $1.6 million, below the preview’s $1.85 million estimate and even below its $1.70 million low end. The preview expected expenses near the prior-year level, while Aethlon reported an 11.9% year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated operating expenses fell 11.9% to approximately $1.6 million, down from $1.8 million in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Total opex” of “$1.85M” with a “range $1.70–2.10M.”

surprises.description: Aethlon gave a concrete window for completing all Cohort 3 treatments and follow-up—by the end of calendar 2026 or early 2027—and said only two more participants are needed. The preview expected enrollment to be ongoing and did not expect a dated completion or analysis window.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only 2 additional participants needed to complete the trial”; management aims to complete treatments and the “8-week follow-up measurement period by the end of calendar 2026 or early 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said buy-side expected “Cohort 3 enrollment ongoing,” with “no date” for the readout; it called for a date for the independent statistician’s dose-response analysis.

surprises.description: The Cohort 2 biomarker changes were described as more consistent across participants and lasting up to eight weeks, compared with changes in only two of three Cohort 1 participants that lasted two to three weeks. The preview had noted that Cohort 2 replicated the direction of Cohort 1’s biomarker results, but did not flag this greater consistency and persistence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cohort 2 ... showed biomarker signals that were more consistent across participants and persisted longer—up to the 8-week mark—compared with cohort 1 ... changes in only 2 of 3 participants lasting 2-3 weeks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Cohort 2 replicated Cohort 1 biomarker direction,” including tumor-derived EVs, miRNA, and immune-cell measures.

in_line: June 30 cash was approximately $4.9 million, within the preview’s estimated $4.70–$5.50 million range, though slightly below its $5.15 million midpoint estimate.
The approximately $4 million gross post-quarter offering was broadly in line with the preview’s expected July follow-on of approximately $4 million gross.

The first Cohort 3 participant’s lack of device-related serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities was consistent with the preview’s note that the DSMB had cleared advancement to Cohort 3 with no safety concerns or DLTs.
Cohort 2’s reported biomarker direction was consistent with the preview’s account that Cohort 2 had replicated Cohort 1’s biomarker direction.

surprises.description: Same-station revenue fell 9.6%, worse than the preview’s -6% to -8% base case and beyond its stated -9% bear-case threshold. That indicates the top-line decline was more severe than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell approximately 9.6% on a same-station basis to about $44.1 million from $49.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “-6% to -8% same-station”; it said “worse than -9% breaks the ‘stabilizing’ narrative.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached about $5.3 million, well above the preview’s $2.5–3.5 million base case. Cost benefits therefore appeared sooner or were stronger than the preview allowed for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to approximately $5.3 million from $4.7 million in Q2 2025 and reversed a negative $0.4 million in Q1 2026, reflecting early cost-cut benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adjusted EBITDA … $2.5–3.5M (cost cuts partially offset revenue decline).”

surprises.description: The debt restructuring produced a $91.8 million GAAP gain, exceeding the preview’s expected $70–85 million range. The accounting gain was larger than anticipated, though the preview already expected a substantial gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: The restructuring “produced a $91.8 million GAAP gain on debt restructuring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “a book gain on extinguishment in the ~$70–85M range.”

surprises.description: The May expense program is expected to save about $10.5 million annually, above the roughly $7 million in annualized reductions the preview described. That points to a larger cost-savings opportunity than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The May expense reduction program is expected to generate about $10.5 million in annualized run-rate savings, with roughly $5 million benefiting 2026 and full impact realized in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$2M annualized from an early-retirement offering plus ~$5M of further annualized reductions.”

surprises.description: Same-station digital revenue grew about 7%, below the preview’s expectation of high-teens growth. Owned-and-operated digital still grew, but its 10% Q2 increase also fell short of the preview’s high-teens digital growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Overall same-station digital revenue rose roughly 7%”; “Owned-and-operated digital revenue … grew about 10% in Q2 and 18% in the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview forecast “high-teens” same-station digital growth and estimated digital revenue of “$11.5–12.5M.”

surprises.description: Local direct revenue grew 9%, while national revenue excluding political fell 21% and local agency revenue fell 12%. Local direct demand held up better than the preview’s key debate implied, but weakness in national and agency channels was consistent with its identified downside risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-station local direct revenue grew approximately 9% year-over-year, while national revenue (ex-political) fell about 21% and local agency revenue declined about 12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case required “late-cycle local direct demand holding up” and identified “national/agency weakness” in its bear case.

surprises.description: Management described Q4 pacing as very strong even though only minimal political revenue had been booked, suggesting strength beyond a political-advertising lift. The preview expected a midterm political tailwind but did not anticipate this strong Q4 pacing with little political already booked.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “characterized Q4 pacing as very strong with only minimal political revenue booked.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “2026 is a midterm year; political should be a Q3/Q4 tailwind.”

surprises.description: More than 25% of the full-year political budget was already booked or tracking, giving a concrete progress measure for the expected midterm tailwind that the preview had not quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Beasley has booked more than 25% of its full-year political budget tracking with the 2024 presidential cycle.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any quantification is the most useful forward datapoint on the call,” but gave no expected booking level.

surprises.description: The company agreed to sell two stations for $8 million and plans to use the proceeds to reduce debt, with no expected EBITDA impact. The preview discussed debt and capital structure but did not anticipate this asset sale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company agreed on July 31 to sell two radio stations in Charlotte and Las Vegas to EMF for $8 million, expected to close in 60-90 days, with proceeds reducing debt and no expected EBITDA impact.”

surprises.description: The company said its ‘Summer of Influence’ and ‘America 250’ programs had generated nearly $6 million in closed business, an unanticipated commercial update that adds evidence of enterprise-level sales activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its enterprise ‘Summer of Influence’ and ‘America 250’ programs have generated nearly $6 million in closed business.”

in_line: Post-restructuring long-term debt was about $129 million, consistent with the preview’s rough mid-$130-million estimate, although the preview also noted conflicting reports of about $110 million.

surprises.description: Elanco’s Q2 revenue was $1.368 billion, above the preview’s roughly $1.31 billion consensus and above the company’s $1.325 billion guidance ceiling. Organic constant-currency growth was 8%, versus the 4–6% guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “8% organic constant currency revenue growth in Q2,” with “total revenue of $1.368 billion,” and the company “outperforming the high end of guidance for revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$1.31B”; Q2 company guidance was “$1,300–1,325M (+4–6% OCC).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.34 substantially exceeded the preview’s $0.27 consensus estimate and the company’s $0.25–$0.28 guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 31% year-over-year to $0.34,” exceeding expectations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | $0.27 (Zacks); $0.28 at some feeds”; company guidance was “$0.25–$0.28.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $288 million, well above the preview’s roughly $250 million consensus and the company’s $260 million guidance ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $288 million,” exceeding expectations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$250M”; company guidance was “$240–260M.”

surprises.description: Elanco raised its full-year outlook across revenue, EBITDA, and EPS, rather than merely reiterating the existing ranges. The new EPS midpoint of $1.13 also exceeds the preview’s cited buy-side expectation of roughly $1.08–$1.10.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year guidance to 6-7% organic constant currency growth (from 5-7%), adjusted EBITDA of $1.01-1.035 billion … and adjusted EPS of $1.10-1.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY guidance of “Revenue $5,010–5,085M (+5–7% OCC),” “Adj. EBITDA $975M–1.005B,” and “Adj. EPS $1.03–1.09”; it said the buy-side expected the EPS midpoint “to move to ~$1.08–1.10.”

surprises.description: The gross-margin rebound was stronger than the preview’s roughly 57% consensus and its expectation that margins be only flat-to-up year over year. Elanco also raised its full-year gross-margin expansion outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 80 basis points to 58.1% in Q2,” and “full-year gross margin expansion guidance [was] raised to 50 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put Q2 adjusted gross margin consensus at “~57%” and said it “needs to be flat-to-up” year over year.

surprises.description: Zenrelia’s commercial progress exceeded the preview’s cited clinic-penetration and market-share markers: penetration is now above 60% of U.S. clinics and share gains reached 9 points year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: Zenrelia is “penetrating ~18,000 U.S. clinics (>60% of the base)” and “improving U.S. JAK market share by 9 points year-over-year,” with an “over-80% reorder rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “>50% U.S. clinic penetration,” “>80% reorder rate,” and U.S. JAK share “+5pts vs. Q4.”

surprises.description: Credelio Quattro expanded its clinic reach and gained market share faster than the preview’s earlier rollout markers suggested, with coverage now above half of U.S. clinics and another 4 points of share gained in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: Credelio Quattro “gained 4 points of market share in Q2 (on top of 3 points in Q1)” and expanded to “over half of U.S. clinics,” adding “~3,000 clinics since Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “40% clinic penetration” and “+2,500 new clinics YTD.”

surprises.description: Elanco raised its innovation revenue target again, to approximately $1.25 billion, rather than holding the $1.2 billion target the preview identified as the current goal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The full-year innovation revenue target was raised by $50 million to approximately $1.25 billion,” with Q2 innovation revenue of “$340 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “innovation revenue $1.2B” and said a second raise would be “the cleanest bull signal available on the print.”

surprises.description: The company’s year-end net-leverage target improved beyond the preview’s expected 3.0–3.2x range, with management now targeting approximately 3x.
surprises.fact_evidence: Elanco “improved its year-end net leverage target to approximately 3x from a prior 3x-3.2x range,” after cutting net debt by roughly $90 million year to date.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed year-end net leverage guidance of “3.0–3.2x.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses grew faster than organic revenue, a cost pressure not highlighted in the preview’s outlook for margin improvement. Management attributed the spending to DTC investment and expected another increase in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses grew 10% in constant currency (outpacing organic revenue growth),” and “Q3 OpEx [is] expected to rise ~11%”; management said DTC investments were directly correlated to market-share gains.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected an adjusted gross-margin rebound from lapping inventory costs and U.S. Pet Health mix, and said Q2 gross margin “needs to be flat-to-up” for the H2 EBITDA bridge to hold.

in_line: U.S. Pet Health grew 11%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of high-single-digit to low-double-digit U.S. Pet Health growth in H2.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $2.45, above the preview’s $2.21–$2.24 consensus range and just above the $2.40 top of the May guide. The quarter beat the expected range despite the preview describing Q2 as largely pre-sold by guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 delivering $2.45.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS Consensus: $2.21” and “Company Guide (May 5): $2.00 – $2.40.”

surprises.description: Engineered Materials was expected to be down year over year, with previewed adjusted EBIT of $190–$210 million versus $214 million a year earlier. Management instead expects adjusted EBIT to grow at double-digit rates, closer to 15%, despite inventory absorption, Micromax divestiture, and lower equity earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EM is expected to grow adjusted EBIT at double-digit rates (closer to 15%) this year” despite a “$45 million inventory-reduction absorption hit,” “$35 million of lost EBIT from the Micromax divestiture,” and “about $10 million of equity earnings decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Engineered Materials adj. EBIT: ~$200M” and “Guided down Y/Y”; the preview gave a $190–$210M range versus $214M a year earlier.

surprises.description: Working capital was a much larger cash use than the preview’s roughly neutral full-year assumption implied: nearly $300 million year to date, including an almost $200 million build in Q2. The company maintained its FCF guide, but the reported cash use leaves a larger working-capital reversal or offset needed to reach it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 free cash flow was $140 million despite an almost $200 million working capital build in the quarter (nearly $300 million year-to-date use of cash).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said ~half of 2026 EBITDA growth converts to FCF this year (rest deferred to 2027 on working-capital timing), with working capital roughly neutral for the year.”

surprises.description: The Ibn Sina joint venture’s extended downtime created an unanticipated earnings headwind: equity earnings are now expected to be about $10 million below the company’s original expectation, with nearly all the impact falling in Q3. The plant is running again, with dividends expected to help in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Equity earnings will be about $10 million lower than originally anticipated this year because the Ibn Sina joint venture did not operate for much of Q2, with nearly all the impact hitting Q3.”

surprises.description: Accelerated Lanaken and EM closures create an additional second-half inventory absorption charge in Acetyl Chain that the preview did not identify. This adds a near-term cost even as the closures are part of the company’s footprint actions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Accelerated closure of the Lanaken acetate tow plant and pulled-forward EM closures are driving a heavier second-half inventory absorption hit, including an incremental $20 million absorption charge in AC in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified an “~$50M absorption hit from nylon inventory drawdown” for EM, but did not flag an incremental second-half AC charge.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a broader cost-reduction target than the preview’s roughly $30 million of nylon savings: actions now target $80–$100 million of reductions for 2027, including Lanaken and nylon/EM footprint savings. Some of those savings are already expected to be captured in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management has taken actions targeting $80 million to $100 million of cost reductions for 2027,” with roughly one-third of Lanaken’s $20–25 million savings and about half of the $30–35 million nylon/EM footprint savings captured in 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$30M of Nylon 66 cost savings” and described about one-third of those savings in H2.

surprises.description: Management gave more specific, favorable detail on the earnings quality and growth opportunity in electronics and medical than the preview provided, including a sizable AI data-center server content opportunity. The preview flagged these markets to watch but did not describe their contribution margins or the server opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: Electronics is “about 10% of revenue but 10-15% of contribution margin”; medical is “under 10% of revenue but roughly 20% of contribution margin”; and AI data-center servers offer “3x traditional servers” content opportunity.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “China automotive … plus medical and electronics.”

surprises.description: The company extended its $700–$800 million 2026 FCF guidance into a longer-term framing, calling that range a sustainable baseline for the next few years. The preview focused on whether the 2026 target would be maintained, not on a multi-year baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 free cash flow guidance maintained at $700 million to $800 million, now framed as a sustainable baseline for the next few years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 FCF guidance of “$700 – $800M” and focused on whether it would be reaffirmed.

in_line: The roughly $6 full-year EPS guide was reaffirmed, close to the preview’s $6.05 consensus; the preview also identified a possible H2 trim from roughly $3.00 toward $2.70–$2.90 as its base case.
The $700–$800 million full-year FCF range was maintained, matching the preview’s central expectation, although the working-capital use was worse than its roughly neutral full-year assumption.

The regional acetyl picture was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that Asian pricing had moderated while Western Hemisphere profitability remained the key support: Asia was back to pre-war levels by mid-Q2, while Western Hemisphere margins stayed elevated.

The preview expected net debt around $10 billion at year-end 2026 and leverage near 4.8x; management’s roughly $10 billion net-debt outlook and leverage below 5x were broadly in line. The 2027 outlook of around $9 billion was also close to the preview’s expectation of less than $9 billion.

surprises.description: Gross margin was expected around 30–35%, but came in at approximately 43%. The improvement was attributed to favorable contract mix and Novera QPU contributions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to approximately 43% in Q2 2026,” reflecting “favorable contract mix and Novera QPU contributions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~30–35% (no formal consensus).”

surprises.description: The preview expected another optically large noncash GAAP fair-value gain, but Rigetti instead reported a $52.6 million GAAP net loss, largely due to fair-value adjustments on warrant and earn-out liabilities.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss widened to $52.6 million from $39.7 million a year ago, largely due to noncash fair value adjustments on warrant and earn-out liabilities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With the stock down sharply over the quarter, expect another optically large, meaningless GAAP gain.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses were higher than the preview’s roughly $28–29 million expectation, reaching $30.3 million. Operating loss, however, remained within the preview’s modeled range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total operating expenses increased to $30.3 million,” while operating loss was “$28.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Opex ~$28–29M”; operating loss modeled at “~-$26 to -$29M.”

surprises.description: Cash and investments ended the quarter at $541.3 million, below the preview’s modeled $545–555 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 2026 with approximately $541.3 million in cash and investments and no debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash + investments ~$545–555M (modeled).”

surprises.description: Prepayments on the C-DAC order drove a significant increase in deferred revenue, adding a favorable revenue-visibility detail that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prepayments driving a significant increase in deferred revenue.”

in_line: Revenue was approximately $5.1 million, in line with the preview’s $5.09–5.13 million consensus range.
Non-GAAP diluted loss per share was $0.05, matching the preview’s -$0.05 consensus.
Operating loss of $28.1 million was within the preview’s modeled range of roughly $26–29 million.
The $8.4 million C-DAC system remained expected to be recognized in Q4 2026 after installation and acceptance testing, as the preview anticipated.
The CHIPS Act arrangement remained a non-definitive LOI for up to $100 million over three years with a government equity stake, consistent with the preview’s expectations.
Elevated 2026 CapEx and investment of up to $100 million over time in the U.K. ProQure initiative were consistent with the preview’s discussion of higher capex and the U.K. commitment.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $818 million, below even the preview’s $850–865 million working whisper and well below its published consensus range. The reported 11% year-over-year growth also fell short of the preview’s expected 16–20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $818 million, up approximately 11% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat the working whisper as ~$850–865M revenue”; consensus was “$887.7M” / “$873.3M,” implying “+18% to +20%.”

surprises.description: CELSIUS brand net sales declined about 12%, far below the preview’s expectation of roughly 3–6% growth or its ≥5% bogey. Tracked retail sales fell only 2%, with management attributing roughly half of the larger net-sales-versus-retail gap to distributor inventory rebalancing from SKU rationalization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brand CELSIUS net sales declined approximately 12% year-over-year while its tracked-channel retail sales fell only 2%, with roughly half of that gap attributed to distributor inventory rebalancing from SKU rationalization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CELSIUS brand organic growth” bogey: “≥ +5%”; the base case expected “CELSIUS +3–6%.”

surprises.description: Alani Nu net sales were $364 million, below the preview’s expected $390–410 million of shipments. Its 56% tracked retail growth did clear the preview’s ≥50% sell-through expectation, so the surprise was the gap between strong retail growth and lower reported sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Alani Nu net sales grew approximately 21% year-over-year to $364 million while tracked retail sales grew 56%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Shipments ~$390–410M; retail growth still ≥ +50%.”

surprises.description: Management said CELSIUS would remain flat sequentially in Q3 and return to growth only as it exits 2026 into 2027. That is a weaker near-term trajectory than the preview’s hope that trends improve as SKU rationalization laps and that the 2027 setup is clean.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects brand CELSIUS to remain flat sequentially in Q3 (in both dollars and percentage terms) before returning to growth as it exits 2026 into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the buy-side wanted “trends improve as rationalization laps” and “a clean 2027 setup”; its base case assumed the “14-SKU discontinuation drag ends this year.”

surprises.description: Gross margin of about 48% was within the preview’s expected Q2 range, but management now expects it to stay in the high 40s in Q3 as commodity inflation offsets savings. This weakens the preview’s expected low-50s margin recovery path for the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was approximately 48%, flat with Q1, and is expected to stay in the high 40s in Q3 as commodity inflation (aluminum, diesel) largely offsets integration and cost savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “48.0–48.5%” in Q2 and said management had guided to a flat “sidestep” before “Q3/Q4 improvement toward low 50s”; it called for the “low-50s path reaffirmed for 2H.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA fell to $184 million, below the preview’s estimated $210–215 million and its modeled 24–25% margin range; the reported margin was 22.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to $184 million (22.5% of revenue) from $210 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$210–215M (my est.),” modeled off a “24–25% margin.”

surprises.description: The combined portfolio held roughly 20% share, below the preview’s ≥21% share bogey and the 20.9% Q1 baseline cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The combined portfolio holding roughly 20% dollar share (1 in 5 energy drinks) in tracked U.S. channels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Portfolio share ≥ 21%” as the bogey and reported Q1 portfolio share of “20.9%.”

surprises.description: SG&A was essentially flat year over year and fell to 29% of revenue from 32%, better leverage than the preview’s concern about a marketing step-up and its focus on the SG&A ratio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A was $238 million, essentially flat year-over-year, improving to 29% of revenue from 32%, as costs were held flat while revenue grew 11%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “marketing step-up” and listed the “adj. SG&A ratio” as a metric to watch.

surprises.description: The company repurchased about $100 million of stock in Q2, a sharp acceleration from the $24.1 million repurchased in Q1 and more than the preview’s general expectation of an accelerated pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately $100 million of stock in Q2 ($124 million in the first half) and intends to continue using its $300 million authorization this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “buyback acceleration at $29 vs. $24.1M in Q1.”

surprises.description: Management said the second North Carolina manufacturing line should provide margin benefits as it ramps in the back half, earlier than the preview’s expectation that the line’s benefit would come in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects margin benefits from a second North Carolina manufacturing line ramping in the back half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the second North Carolina line as “H2'26 install, 2027 benefit.”

surprises.description: Management set a target for international markets to exceed 15% of revenue over the next five years and said Alani Nu would launch in select international markets in 2027; the preview did not anticipate this expansion target or launch timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets international markets to represent more than 15% of revenue over the next five years” and “plans to launch Alani Nu in select international markets in 2027.”

in_line: Q2 gross margin was approximately 48%, within the preview’s expected 48.0–48.5% range, even though the Q3 outlook weakened the expected second-half recovery.
Alani Nu tracked retail sales grew 56%, above the preview’s expectation that retail growth remain at least 50%.
Rockstar sales of approximately $66 million and completion of integration in June were in line with the preview’s $65–70 million expectation and its expectation that integration finish in H1 2026.

surprises.description: WLFC reported diluted EPS of $1.31, versus the preview’s post-split consensus of $0.90—about 46% above expectation. EBT was lower year over year, but the preview noted that the prior-year quarter included a one-time $43 million gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 delivered EBT of $38.1 million, net income of $28.7 million, and diluted EPS of $1.31; the prior-year EBT of $74.3 million included a one-time $43 million gain on the BAML sale.
surprises.expectation_evidence: EPS: $0.90 (post-split).

surprises.description: Utilization slipped to 85% from 85.8% in Q1, rather than moving back toward the roughly 88% level the preview described as the cleanest bullish signal. The average lease rate did edge up, from 1.0% to 1.03%, but utilization remained weaker.
surprises.fact_evidence: Average fleet utilization declined to 85% from 87.2% a year earlier, though the average lease rate ticked up from 1.0% to 1.03%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: A further sequential slip would undercut the lease-rent growth story; a recovery toward 88% is the cleanest bull signal.

surprises.description: Short-term maintenance reserve revenue fell to $39 million from $50.2 million, with management attributing the decline to lower customer flying on less fuel-efficient engines amid elevated fuel prices and the Iran conflict. The preview identified fuel-price and retirement dynamics as a key debate, but the reported revenue impact was concretely adverse.
surprises.fact_evidence: Short-term maintenance reserve revenues fell to $39 million from $50.2 million as customers flew fewer hours on less fuel-efficient CFM56 and V2500 engines amid elevated fuel prices and the Iran conflict, though recovery began at the tail end of Q2.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Call commentary: funding plan and JV structure for the WNG portfolio, economics of the P&W storage/lease-return agreement, and the fuel-price/retirement dynamic management flagged in May as a two-sided risk to midlife asset values.

surprises.description: The asset-management platform showed stronger scale and monetization than the preview quantified: Willis Aviation Capital AUM nearly doubled, while management and advisory fees more than doubled, including $2.8 million of GP fees from newly launched funds.
surprises.fact_evidence: Willis Aviation Capital AUM grew nearly 80% year-over-year to $1.4 billion, with fund seeding now largely complete and future growth expected to come from third-party purchases. Management and advisory fees more than doubled (up 113%) to $5.5 million, driven by $2.8 million in GP fees from the newly launched Blackstone and Liberty Mutual funds.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The asset-management platform — Willis Aviation Capital ($2.7B managed with Blackstone/Liberty Mutual; $4.1B total AUM) fee and carried-interest contribution is the emerging non-capital-intensive earnings stream to watch in the disclosure.

surprises.description: Management described substantial growth capacity despite the preview’s focus on funding the announced $379.3 million WNG portfolio and monitoring leverage: WLFC cited about $1.3 billion of deployable capital and leverage of 2.78x. The leverage figure is slightly above the preview’s 2.7x baseline, but the stated capital pool is a notable funding cushion.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company holds roughly $1.3 billion of additional deployable capital in discretionary funds, undrawn revolver capacity, and low leverage of 2.78x to fund its growth pipeline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Funding plan and JV structure for the WNG portfolio ... and where net leverage sits vs. 2.7x, given ~$379M of Q3 acquisitions to fund.

surprises.description: Management put a sizeable value cushion on the portfolio, estimating appraised market value roughly 20% above book value, and cited recent asset sales that generated a $32 million gain. The preview raised fuel-related asset-value risks but did not anticipate this quantified valuation assertion.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimates the overall portfolio carries an embedded ~20% gain, meaning book value is roughly 20% below appraised market value, with recent asset sales of $224.8 million producing a $32 million gain (14.2% gross margin).
surprises.expectation_evidence: The fuel-price/retirement dynamic management flagged in May as a two-sided risk to midlife asset values.

surprises.description: Beyond the already announced Pratt & Whitney agreement, management said it was in advanced discussions to establish another engine repair center in Asia. That potential expansion was not identified in the preview’s discussion of the P&W deal.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company signed a major engine storage agreement with Pratt & Whitney and is in advanced discussions to establish another engine repair center in Asia.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Call commentary: ... economics of the P&W storage/lease-return agreement.

in_line: WLFC did not provide quarterly or annual guidance, consistent with the preview’s statement that the company does not issue guidance.
The Pratt & Whitney engine storage agreement was already announced before the release; the call confirmed the agreement rather than revealing a new signed deal.
The $0.133 per-share dividend was consistent with the previously announced, split-adjusted Q3 dividend.

surprises.description: VAALCO expanded Egypt from the previewed six-well program to 10–15 wells and raised Egyptian production and sales guidance about 10% above its original estimates, while keeping full-year CapEx unchanged. This was stronger than the preview’s base case of maintained guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “expanded the Egyptian drilling program to 10-15 wells and raised production and sales guidance about 10% above original estimates while keeping full-year CapEx unchanged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Egypt six-well program”; the base case assumed “FY guide maintained,” while a second FY guidance raise was described as the bull scenario.

surprises.description: Ebouri-5H’s water cut rose faster than modeled, and management said this was the main reason Gabon guidance moved to the lower end. The preview’s base case assumed guidance would be maintained, although it identified a possible sales-guidance trim as a bear risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “water cut rose faster than modeled toward the field average of 75-80%, prompting a downward revision that is the main driver of lower-end Gabon guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … FY guide maintained”; the bear case included “FY sales guidance trimmed.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end net debt was $147 million, below the preview’s expected Q2 exit range of $160–185 million. VAALCO did draw $25 million on its RBL, but the reported net debt was lower than the preview’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “VAALCO drew $25 million on its RBL in Q2, ending with $177 million drawn, net debt of $147 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net debt likely exits Q2 at $160–185M.”

surprises.description: The offshore workover budget was cut to zero for the year, contrary to the preview’s expectation that Phase 5 would include two workovers in H2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “the offshore workover budget was cut to zero for the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Phase 5 (4 producers, 2–3 injectors, 2 workovers) in H2.”

surprises.description: Management outlined a stronger near-term production and lifting profile: Q3 total production is expected to rise about 23% from Q2, and Q4 is expected to be stronger with five liftings planned. The preview focused on Q2 lifting timing and did not anticipate this specific Q3/Q4 schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects total production up ~23% versus Q2 … and Q4 is expected to be stronger with five liftings planned.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDAX of $54.8 million came in above the preview’s approximately $50 million base case, though it was not as high as the preview’s $70 million bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “adjusted EBITDAX of $54.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case ~$50M”; the scenario table estimated “Adj. EBITDAX ~$50M” in the base case.

surprises.description: A new gas supply well is expected to eliminate diesel use on the Teli FSO and generate recurring savings, an operating benefit the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “expected to eliminate expensive diesel usage on the Teli FSO, saving roughly $500,000-$600,000 per month gross (VAALCO ~58% share), while improving reliability and gas lift-driven production.”

surprises.description: Q2 earnings received an additional boost from exploration expense falling by nearly $23 million versus Q1 because Q1 included West Etame dry-hole and seismic costs; the preview did not flag this expense reduction as a source of earnings upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 earnings benefited from a near $23 million drop in exploration expense (from West Etame dry hole and seismic costs in Q1).”

in_line: Revenue was about $135.2 million, calculated from Q1 revenue of $62.6 million plus the reported $72.6 million sequential increase. That was close to the preview’s ~$135 million base estimate, even though it exceeded the preview’s cited $116.25 million consensus.
NRI sales of 17,812 BOPD were within the previewed Q2 guidance range of 16,800–18,300 BOPD and slightly above its midpoint-based expectation.

The roughly $40 million unrealized hedging gain was consistent with the preview’s expectation that the sharp decline in the forward curve would produce a large non-cash reversal. The call facts do not specify the realized hedge loss, so that separate expectation cannot be assessed.
Baobab resumed production in June, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the restart was on schedule.

surprises.description: SEI reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $108 million, above its $83–93 million guide and the preview’s $92 million-plus bar. That is a substantial beat, not merely a result near the top of the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $108 million, up 30% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: Company guide: $83–93M”; the preview also said “$92M+ is the bar.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted pro forma EPS was $0.39, far above the preview’s $0.26 consensus estimate and its $0.27–$0.31 base-case range. This was a notable upside surprise given the preview’s warning that interest expense and GESA shares could weigh on EPS even if EBITDA beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted pro forma net income of $37 million or $0.39 per fully diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $0.26”; the base scenario projected “$0.27–0.31” and warned that “EPS light on interest step-up.”

surprises.description: SEI raised Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $90–105 million from the existing $80–95 million range, and also issued initial Q4 guidance of $100–120 million. The upward Q3 revision and further Q4 ramp were stronger than the preview’s base case of reaffirming Q3 guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $90-105 million and established initial Q4 2026 guidance of $100-120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q3 guidance as “$80–95M” and said “reaffirm is neutral”; its base scenario expected “Q3 reaffirmed $80–95M.”

surprises.description: Revenue of approximately $219 million exceeded the preview’s modeled whisper of $203–210 million. The beat was meaningful but smaller in percentage terms than the EBITDA and EPS upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached approximately $219 million, up 12% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Model the whisper at $203–210M revenue.”

surprises.description: Contracted capacity was reported at 2.3 GW, above the preview’s estimate of roughly 2.0–2.1 GW. The capacity gain came with three investment-grade technology customers, rather than a newly announced fourth counterparty.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Solaris has 2.3 gigawatts currently under long-term contract with three investment-grade technology customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~2.0–2.1 GW is under long-term contract with three investment-grade technology customers.”

surprises.description: The Hatchbo agreement was converted to a turnkey 660 MW capacity and operating contract, and its term was extended to as long as 18 years. The preview had described the relevant contract as having a 10-year term plus a 5-year option, so the longer stated term and turnkey arrangement were more favorable than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Hatchbo agreement was amended to a turnkey 660-megawatt capacity and operating contract, extending the term from up to 15 years to up to 18 years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a contract with “10-yr tenor + 5-yr option unchanged.”

surprises.description: A large energy customer increased contracted capacity from 60 to approximately 80 MW and extended its contract from four to six years after learning grid interconnection was 7–8 years away. The preview did not anticipate this customer-specific expansion and extension.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One large energy customer, informed that grid interconnection is now 7-8 years away, expanded contracted power capacity from 60 to approximately 80 megawatts and extended the term from 4 to 6 years.”

surprises.description: Management made an unexpectedly forceful valuation claim, asserting that cash flow from current contracts already exceeds SEI’s entire enterprise value. The preview discussed the company’s valuation and future fleet earnings potential but did not report this claim about cash flow from current contracts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management asserts that cash flow from current contracts already exceeds the company's entire enterprise value.”

surprises.description: The company’s early-stage SMR investment, Deployable Energy, achieved reactor criticality under a DOE program, an unanticipated development outside the preview’s earnings and operating outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its early-stage SMR investment (Deployable Energy) achieved reactor criticality under a DOE program.”

in_line: No fourth long-term customer was announced: the preview’s base case expected contracted capacity to remain around 2.1 GW with no new contract, and the reported book still has three customers.
Hatchbo revenue beginning in January 2027 is broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that deliveries for the large contract would begin in January 2027.
The $0.12-per-share dividend was consistent with the preview, which listed a $0.12 quarterly dividend.
The July GESA acquisition and its installation, commissioning, and O&M capabilities were already disclosed and anticipated in the preview.

surprises.description: DSP’s Q3 revenue outlook was below the preview’s $112–115 million estimate: the company guided to $107.5–110.5 million. The shortfall contrasts with contribution ex-TAC guidance, which landed within the preview’s expected $65–67 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $107.5M-$110.5M (up 27%), contribution ex TAC of $65M-$67M (up 25%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bar: Q3 contribution ex-TAC ≈ $65–67M (+24–26% YoY), revenue ~$112–115M.”

surprises.description: The revenue-to-contribution spread was worse than the preview’s already-compressed expectation. Q2 revenue of $104.3 million against $60.2 million of contribution ex-TAC implies a ratio of about 57.7%, below the preview’s 59.5% guide-mid ratio and its stated bar of at least 59.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 34% year-over-year to $104.3 million”; “Contribution ex TAC grew 24% year-over-year to $60.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 guide (mid) … Ratio 59.5%”; “Implied take rate ≥ 59.5% — if the revenue/contribution ex-TAC ratio compresses more than the guided 260bp, the revenue beat is cosmetic.”

surprises.description: Direct access penetration rose much further than the preview’s cited level: it was over 80% of CTV spend in Q2, up from just over 50% in Q1. Management also reported 35% CPM reductions for advertisers, an additional concrete benefit not forecast in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct access penetration jumped to over 80% of CTV ad spend in Q2 from just over 50% in Q1”; the company was “delivering 35% CPM reductions for advertisers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With >50% of CTV spend now transacts through Direct Access”; the preview also listed “Direct Access penetration” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: The preview anticipated Iris coverage reaching above 75%, but management’s year-end expectation was about 70% of viable inventory. The reported nearly 50% bidstream penetration was also roughly level with the preview’s cited Q1 coverage rather than showing clear progress toward that higher target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Iris content ID reached nearly 50% bidstream penetration and is expected to hit ~70% of viable inventory by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “IRIS ID CTV bid-request coverage (~50% in Q1, targeting >75%).”

surprises.description: The new Outcomes product had already reached over 5% of platform spend just six months after launch, with spend coming from existing customers reallocating performance budgets. The preview flagged adoption as something to watch but gave no comparable adoption level or timing expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new autonomous 'Outcomes' AI product already accounts for over 5% of total platform spend just six months after launch, sourced from existing customers reallocating performance budgets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch: … ViantAI ‘Outcomes’ adoption against search/social budgets.”

surprises.description: TVision pilot campaigns produced a concrete conversion result that the preview had not specified: more than 80% of 42 campaigns achieved higher conversion rates, averaging a 1.4x lift. This is positive early evidence for the acquired product’s campaign performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “42 TVision pilot campaigns saw over 80% achieve higher conversion rates with an average 1.4x lift.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was materially above the preview’s estimated $163–175 million range after the TVision cash outlay, coming in at $193.1 million. The company also reported no debt, which was expected in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $193.1 million in cash, no debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Balance sheet: ~$163–175M cash est. at 6/30 … no debt.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $104.3 million was above guidance, but the preview explicitly said a roughly 3% beat over the guide high end was habitual and “fully expected”; the reported result was about that size.
Q2 contribution ex-TAC of $60.2 million was close to the preview’s $60.3 million base estimate, though just below its $60.5–61 million whisper range.

Adjusted EBITDA of $14.2 million was in line with the preview’s $14.2 million base estimate and its expectation of at least $14 million; the implied contribution margin was also close to its 23.5% estimate.
Q3 contribution ex-TAC guidance of $65–67 million, or about 25% growth, matched the preview’s $65–67 million and 24–26% growth bar.

The preview expected TVision to be dilutive near term and anticipated a 200-basis-point Q3 margin drag; the reported 150-basis-point Q2 and roughly 200-basis-point Q3 drags are consistent with that expectation.
The company’s stated longer-term goal of adjusted EBITDA margins above 40% was already flagged in the preview as a target.

surprises.description: EVC reported Q2 revenue of $227.9 million, about 4% above the preview’s $219 million estimate. The preview expected $173 million of ATS revenue, but ATS delivered $182.8 million, with 18% sequential growth rather than the forecast 12%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenue surged 126% year-over-year to $227.9 million”; “ATS segment revenue jumped 230% year-over-year to $182.8 million and grew 18% sequentially from Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” estimate: “~$219M”; “ATS revenue” estimate: “$173M”; ATS sequential growth assumption: “+12% q/q.”

surprises.description: Despite beating the preview’s expected Q2 ATS run-rate, management said Q2 ATS performance was exceptional and guided to a sequential revenue decline in Q3. That reverses the preview’s expectation of continued sequential growth, although management still expects more than 100% year-over-year ATS growth in both Q3 and Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 ATS performance was exceptional and unlikely to repeat,” with “a sequential revenue decline from Q2 to Q3 2026”; ATS is “still expected to deliver more than 100% year-over-year growth in both Q3 and Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “real bar” was whether the “Q1 2026 ATS run-rate ($154.6M/qtr) … holds sequentially” and modeled Q2 ATS growth of “+12% q/q.”

surprises.description: The Media segment was weaker than the preview’s near-flat, roughly breakeven base case: revenue fell 1% year over year instead of rising about 1%, and the segment posted a $3.3 million operating loss. National advertising fell 19%, while local advertising rose 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Media segment revenue declined 1% to $45.1 million and swung to a $3.3 million operating loss”; “Media national advertising revenue fell 19% year-over-year while local advertising revenue rose 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Media revenue of “$46M” with “+1%” year-over-year growth and described the base case as “Media flat”; it also cited “Media roughly breakeven.”

in_line: ATS operating margin was approximately 21.9% ($40.0 million of operating profit on $182.8 million of revenue), close to the preview’s roughly 22% estimate.
Media revenue of $45.1 million was close to the preview’s $46 million estimate, despite being slightly below it.

There was no reported progress on renewing the Televisa/Univision affiliation agreement, consistent with the preview’s note that there had been no renewal news and that the agreement expires December 31, 2026.
The company declared the expected $0.05-per-share dividend and reduced debt, consistent with the preview’s discussion of dividends and debt paydown; no buyback authorization was reported.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $23.1 million, below the preview’s implied $26–31 million quarterly pace needed to support full-year guidance. It was also only at the bottom of the preview’s $23–27 million base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 40% year-over-year to $23.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA vs. the implied ~$26–31M quarterly run-rate”; the preview also gave a “Base” scenario of “$23–27M.”

surprises.description: RNG production reached 1.3 million MMBtu, but management said it was below expectations and implied utilization was only in the high-50% range of nameplate capacity. That fell short of the production pace the preview said was needed for the full-year target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 RNG production was 1.3 million MMBtu, up approximately 8% year-over-year but below management's expectations, implying utilization only in the high-50% range of the 9 million MMBtu nameplate capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guide of 5.4–5.8M MMBtu implies ~1.4–1.5M MMBtu/quarter for the balance of the year”; the preview also called for “RNG production ≥1.3M MMBtu” as its threshold for the promised acceleration.

surprises.description: Renewable Power adjusted EBITDA fell sharply, and OPAL recorded a non-cash impairment tied to decommissioning a project for the CMS RNG conversion. The preview discussed CMS as a construction project but did not anticipate this segment decline or impairment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Renewable Power segment adjusted EBITDA fell to $0.3 million from $2.2 million, and the company took a non-cash impairment from decommissioning a renewable power project tied to the CMS RNG conversion.”

surprises.description: Liquidity was $162.2 million, down about $71 million from the $233 million cited in the preview for Q1, amid more than $52 million of first-half investment. Management said existing resources are sufficient to fund all projects currently in construction, which partly offsets the concern but was not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $162.2 million of liquidity, including $91.4 million cash”; OPAL “invested over $52 million” in the first half and stated “existing resources are sufficient to fund all projects currently in construction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$233M liquidity at Q1 ($133M cash)” and said to “watch the burn against a $407M market cap.”

surprises.description: Management identified G&A cost savings as a driver of EBITDA growth, a favorable earnings contributor the preview had not flagged among its expected Q2 drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA growth was “driven by 45Z production tax credits, Fuel Station Services growth, and G&A cost savings amid flat RIN pricing.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a further growth opportunity from non-capital-intensive plant improvements: a potential 5–10% production uplift that would largely flow through to EBITDA. The preview focused on wellfield expansion and construction projects, but did not identify this operational uplift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management sees non-capital-intensive plant improvements (gas collection quantity/quality and efficiency) potentially delivering 5-10% production uplift that largely flows to EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Management identified more than 4 million MMBtu of renewable power conversion candidates as a future growth pipeline, an opportunity not quantified or flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “identified over 4 million MMBtu of renewable power conversion candidates for future growth.”

surprises.description: OPAL said its projects in construction are expected to add approximately 3 million MMBtu of annual design capacity over the next 24 months. The preview named several construction projects and expected their completion, but did not give this capacity-addition figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Projects in construction (Cottonwood, Burlington, CMS, plus Stone's Throw and Grady Road) are expected to add approximately 3 million MMBtu of annual design capacity over the next 24 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Cottonwood, Burlington and CMS” as expected to complete “end of this year into 1H27,” without specifying the resulting capacity.

in_line: OPAL maintained full-year 2026 guidance, as the preview’s base case explicitly anticipated guidance being maintained.
Fuel Station Services EBITDA increased to $12.5 million from $10.9 million, consistent with the preview’s focus on possible margin recovery in the segment.

45Z credits contributed to Q2 EBITDA growth, consistent with the preview’s expectation that 45Z monetization would be an important earnings driver; the call facts provided no capture amount to compare with the preview’s annual estimate.

surprises.description: National Vision delivered much stronger Q2 profitability than the preview’s roughly flat-margin, $0.17 EPS setup: adjusted operating margin was 6.3% versus an expected 4.8%–5.2%, and adjusted EPS was $0.25. The margin expansion and EPS beat were substantially larger than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 6.3%, and adjusted EPS rose to $0.25 from $0.18 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $0.17”; “Adj. operating margin ~4.8%–5.2%”; “Roughly flat Y/Y margin (~4.9%) is the base case.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted operating income outlook was raised materially, rather than merely reaffirmed or narrowed: the range increased from $107–$133 million to $119–$139 million. The new midpoint implies about 120 basis points of margin expansion, above the preview’s roughly 100-basis-point standing outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year adjusted operating income outlook to $119-$139 million (implying ~120 bps of margin expansion at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating income $107–$133M (~100 bps of margin expansion)”; the preview said “a reaffirm-without-narrowing” was a likely outcome and described a raise as unlikely.

surprises.description: Traffic weakness was much more pronounced than the prior-quarter figure cited in the preview, and management identified a specific lower-value customer problem: value-seeking customers are taking about two weeks longer to return, creating an estimated two-point full-year traffic headwind. Higher-value managed care customers, by contrast, grew in both ticket and traffic.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 7.1% increase in average ticket offsetting a 4.9% decline in customer traffic”; weakness is concentrated in “value-seeking” customers whose purchase cycle “lengthened by about 2 weeks,” creating “roughly a 2-point full-year traffic headwind,” while managed care customers grew in ticket and traffic.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 traffic of “−1.2%” and warned that “a second consecutive quarter of negative cash-pay traffic with widening magnitude” would be the bear thesis.

surprises.description: Management’s back-half margin commentary was more cautious than the preview’s focus on a back-half ramp: it expects Q3/Q4 operating-margin expansion to be flat-to-modest, partly because it will reinvest a roughly $5 million tariff refund in marketing. This tempers the otherwise raised full-year operating-income outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management plans to reinvest a “~$5 million tariff refund” into incremental back-half marketing, “keeping Q3/Q4 operating margin expansion flat-to-modest.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “back-half hockey stick” embedded in FY26 guidance was the key debate and described roughly 100 basis points of full-year margin expansion as the standing outlook.

surprises.description: The lower end of full-year adjusted EPS guidance is now $0.90 rather than the preview’s stated $0.85, even though the call described the range as maintained. That raises the guidance floor while leaving the top end unchanged at $1.09.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance was maintained at $0.90-$1.09.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed standing adjusted diluted EPS guidance of “$0.85–$1.09.”

surprises.description: Inventory was up sharply to support store segmentation, a balance-sheet development the preview did not flag. Management expects the growth pace to moderate through 2026, but the reported 37% increase is a notable build.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory rose approximately 37% year-over-year to support the store segmentation strategy, with management expecting the growth pace to moderate through 2026.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $499 million and adjusted comparable-store sales growth of 2.2% were in line with expectations; the preview’s consensus revenue was $499.8 million and its derived comp range was about +1% to +2%.

The full-year revenue and comp outlook was narrowed at the top end, with the revenue ceiling moving from $2.09 billion to $2.08 billion and the comp ceiling from 6% to 5%, while the floors remained unchanged. This was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of a narrowed guide and a top-end trim rather than a cut to the revenue floor.

The preview expected replatform-related pressure on Q2 comps. The reported comp was 2.2%, and management said the e-commerce replatform reduced total adjusted comps by about 150 basis points; excluding it, America’s Best comps would have been slightly above 4%.

surprises.description: Revenue was $1.2 billion and declined about 1% year over year, rather than growing the 3.3% implied by the preview’s $1.20 billion consensus. The reported amount matched the consensus after rounding, but the growth rate was materially weaker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue declined approximately 1% year-over-year to $1.2 billion.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow was $72 million, above the preview’s estimated $0–40 million range, despite the expected step-up in capital spending. This was a stronger quarterly cash result than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was positive $72 million (up 19%), driven by operating cash flow of $291 million (up 13%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow | ~$0–40M”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $381 million came in just below the preview’s estimated $385–400 million range, with a 7% year-over-year decline versus the preview’s estimated 2%–6% decline. The company said EBITDA would have been roughly flat without the $22 million combined headwind from the Navarino sale and lower IP licensing revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA down 7% to $381 million, though EBITDA would have been roughly flat excluding a $22 million combined headwind from the Navarino sale ($3M) and lower IP licensing revenue ($19M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$385–400M (est.; no clean public consensus)” and “–2% to –6%” year over year.

surprises.description: Viasat won the next phase of the Protected Tactical SATCOM-Global program, with a $4 billion ceiling, and company-wide awards and backlog rose 10% and nearly 19%, respectively. The preview noted the earlier PTSG IDIQ award and DAT backlog momentum, but did not anticipate this new phase award or the reported backlog growth; the full ceiling is not booked, since only the awarded base order enters backlog.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company won the next phase of the Protected Tactical SATCOM-Global (PTS-G) program, which carries a $4 billion ceiling value, though only the awarded base order (excluding options) is booked in backlog.” “Company-wide awards rose 10% to about $1.3 billion and backlog grew nearly 19% to $4.2 billion, with DAT backlog up 32%.”

surprises.description: Fixed broadband had fallen to 115,000 subscribers, below the preview’s cited 130,000, while fixed services revenue was down 27%. The preview expected continued subscriber decline and tied stabilization to ViaSat-3 Flight 2, so the lower subscriber level is the clearest adverse difference.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fixed services revenue fell 27% as U.S. broadband subscribers dropped to 115,000 (at $111 ARPU), with stabilization not expected until after ViaSat-3 Flight 2 enters service.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Fixed broadband subs (130K, declining)” and “Fixed-broadband stabilization ... hangs on [ViaSat-3 F2].”

in_line: FY27 guidance was reaffirmed at mid-single-digit revenue growth, with Communication Services at low-single-digit growth, DAT at mid-teens, and adjusted EBITDA flat to up slightly—the guide the preview said was the key benchmark.
The company reaffirmed approximately $180 million of FY27 free cash flow guidance, matching the preview’s expectation.
FY27 CapEx guidance of $950 million to $1 billion matched the preview’s stated range.

Aviation revenue growth of 11% and aircraft in service growth of 10% were within the preview’s 10%–12% base-case growth and approximately 10% aircraft-growth expectations. The preview had also flagged competitive pressure.

The preview characterized maritime vessel counts as a structural pressure point and NexusWave as an offset; reported maritime revenue declined 7% even as NexusWave installations and the order book expanded.
The DAT strategic review remained ongoing without a separation or spectrum-monetization decision, consistent with the preview’s description of an unresolved review.

surprises.description: G&A was $24.7 million, slightly below the preview’s $25–32 million range and $3.3 million below its $28 million estimate. That indicates somewhat lower launch-related overhead than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “G&A rose to $24.7 million from $8.5 million on higher professional fees and headcount.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “G&A … My Q2’26 Est. $28M | Range $25–32M.”

surprises.description: Management cited research showing physicians preferred lorundrostat’s profile to baxdrostat’s by roughly 2:1. The preview expected discussion of baxdrostat’s launch and payer positioning, but did not anticipate a quantified physician-preference result favoring lorundrostat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Market research showing roughly a 2:1 physician preference for lorundrostat's profile over competitor baxdrostat based on comparable BAX-HTN and Launch-HTN trials.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Mineralys will be asked directly how AZ's launch is proceeding — payer coverage terms, list price, prescriber uptake”; the preview also noted that payers “expressed interest in having two assets to evaluate.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted lorundrostat’s kidney-related data with a 52% placebo-adjusted UACR reduction in patients with baseline albuminuria and Explore-CKD data extending to eGFR 30, versus baxdrostat’s label down to 45. The preview noted that Explore-CKD data might affect lorundrostat’s label, but did not spell out this specific comparative renal-range advantage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lorundrostat achieved a 52% placebo-adjusted reduction in urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio in patients with baseline albuminuria, and Explore-CKD extended data down to eGFR of 30 versus baxdrostat's label to 45.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has flagged that whether … Explore-CKD (albuminuria/UACR benefit) data make it into the label is under negotiation.”

surprises.description: Management put numbers on the potential U.S. market—about 20 million adults with uncontrolled or resistant hypertension—and the focused prescriber audience of roughly 50,000 physicians. The preview described the targeted prescribing segment but did not provide these market or physician counts.
