surprises.description: The GAAP net loss widened to $11.1 million, worse than the preview’s $7.5–9.0 million modeled range. The excess loss was driven mostly by non-cash debt-extinguishment losses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $11.1 million” from $9.3 million in Q1 and $7.4 million a year earlier, “driven mostly by non-cash losses on debt extinguishment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 base case” GAAP net loss: “($7.5–9.0M).”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was $2 million, below the preview’s expected $3–5 million and indicating greater liquidity pressure than modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash fell sharply to $2 million at the end of Q2 2026 from $7.6 million at year-end 2025, signaling significant liquidity pressure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash (period end)” Q2'26 base case: “$3–5M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted net loss was $7 million, slightly worse than the preview’s $5.8–6.6 million range, despite improving from $7.4 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net loss improved slightly to $7 million versus $7.4 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 base case” adjusted net loss: “($5.8–6.6M).”

surprises.description: Operating expenses were $6.9 million, above the preview’s $5.5–5.9 million model, even though they declined year-over-year. The decrease was not enough to meet the modeled expense level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses declined $1.6 million year-over-year to $6.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 base case” operating expenses: “$5.5–5.9M.”

surprises.description: Management said cautious operator spending at $55–60 oil prices would push several anticipated Gulf projects into 2027 and beyond, extending project delays beyond the quarter’s revenue shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “operators' cautious spending at $55-$60 oil prices to push several anticipated Gulf projects into 2027 and beyond.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview framed Q2 as the test of the seasonal-rebound story and modeled a partial revenue rebound; it did not flag several Gulf projects being pushed into 2027 or later.

surprises.description: ToolKITT was formally released to energy and defense fleet operators, a product milestone, but management expects recurring, predictable revenue only starting in 2027. That falls short of the preview’s hoped-for first named licensing customer with dollars attached in the near term.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nauticus formally released its Toolkit software for ROVs to energy and defense fleet operators,” and expects recurring, predictable revenue “starting in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “a first named licensing customer with dollars attached” and described product news to date as “pre-revenue positioning.”

surprises.description: Management described a shift to acting as the primary international contractor, using fixed-price contracts and vessels of opportunity instead of long-term charter commitments. This was a new strategic approach not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is “shifting to a primary contractor model internationally using fixed-price contracts and vessels of opportunity to capture autonomy-driven margins while avoiding long-term charter commitments.”

surprises.description: Management said a reverse stock split was not required to maintain the Nasdaq listing because the share price had recovered, easing a shareholder concern the preview highlighted amid the company’s recent reverse splits.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management stated “a reverse stock split is not required to maintain its NASDAQ listing given recent share price recovery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “two reverse splits in eight months” and described the stock’s recovery off its late-July low, but did not say another split was unnecessary.

surprises.description: AMTM guided FY27 revenue growth of only 0–1%, well below the roughly 8% growth sell-side models cited in the preview. The outlook also assumes a 3% NASA headwind rather than the previously guided ~1%, with the intentional exit of low-margin programs adding another ~1% offset; the margin-accretive nature of these headwinds makes the picture mixed rather than wholly negative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now expects NASA's workforce insourcing directive to reduce FY27 revenue by 3%, up from the ~1% impact guided on the prior quarter's call”; “FY27 to only 0-1% total revenue growth” as the NASA headwind and “~1% intentional exit of low-margin base operations programs largely offset mid-single-digit growth in the remaining portfolio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sell-side is modeling ~8% revenue growth” for FY27; the preview also described NASA as a “known ~1% FY27 revenue headwind.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was slightly below the $3.572 billion consensus, despite the preview describing the revenue bar as fair. The reported $3.5 billion included only about 1% normalized growth, with procurement delays and lower low-margin material volume cited as factors.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY26 revenue reached $3.5 billion with only ~1% normalized growth, coming in slightly below expectations due to procurement delays and lower low-margin material volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $3.572B” consensus; “the bar on revenue is fair.”

surprises.description: Profitability substantially outperformed the preview’s estimates: adjusted EPS was $0.67 versus $0.611 consensus, while adjusted EBITDA was $290 million versus an estimated ~$279 million. The 8.3% margin also exceeded the preview’s estimated 7.8–7.9% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% year-over-year to $290 million with record quarterly margins of 8.3%, a 60 basis point improvement, while adjusted diluted EPS grew 20% year-over-year to $0.67.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $0.611”; “Adj. EBITDA *(est.)* ~$279M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin *(est.)* ~7.8–7.9%.”

surprises.description: The company cut FY26 revenue guidance instead of reaffirming the range expected in the preview. The new $13.8–13.95 billion range is below the prior $13.95–14.3 billion range, with awards under protest and lower materials volume cited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY26 revenue guidance was lowered to $13.8-13.95 billion (citing ~$175 million from awards under protest and lower materials volume).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed May 11, 2026): Revenue $13,950–14,300M”; the preview’s base case expected the “full FY26 range reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue reduction, AMTM raised its FY26 adjusted EBITDA and EPS guidance, rather than merely maintaining the prior ranges. The new EPS range is $2.40–2.50 versus $2.25–2.45, and EBITDA guidance is $1.115–1.14 billion versus $1.10–1.14 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $1.115-1.14 billion and adjusted EPS guidance increased to $2.40-2.50.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $1,100–1,140M” and “Adj. diluted EPS $2.25–2.45”; the preview expected the full FY26 range to be reaffirmed in its base case.

surprises.description: AMTM disclosed concrete lifetime economics for the Savannah River project, whereas the preview’s base case anticipated progress without disclosed terms. The project is expected to generate over $1 billion in revenue, with potential additional economic interest in commercial operations, tokens, and electrons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The DOE-selected Savannah River AI data center and nuclear project is expected to generate over $1 billion in revenue over its life”; there may be “additional economic interest in commercial operations, tokens, and electrons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the base case was SRS “progressing, no terms disclosed” and called for details on “revenue recognition timing” and project economics.

surprises.description: AMTM announced new nuclear partnerships that were not anticipated in the preview, expanding its position beyond the Savannah River project. The arrangements include a global delivery role with Rolls-Royce and a long-term alliance with Westinghouse.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed strategic partnerships expanding its nuclear position, including as global delivery partner to Rolls-Royce (SMR wins in Sweden, U.K., and Czech Republic) and a long-term alliance with Westinghouse covering the AP1000 and AP300 platforms.”

surprises.description: AMTM reached 3x net leverage a quarter earlier than the preview’s year-end target, and reported substantial debt repayment during the quarter and over the trailing 12 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage was reduced to 3x at quarter end—one quarter earlier than the Capital Markets Day target—supported by $125 million in debt repayments during the quarter and nearly $700 million over the trailing 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management was “on track” for below 3x, or “high-2x,” leverage “by fiscal year-end.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that 92% of anticipated FY27 revenue is already covered by existing or follow-on work, providing a specific level of revenue visibility that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 92% of anticipated FY27 revenue is already covered by existing or follow-on work.”

in_line: Bookings and backlog were broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of book-to-bill at or above 1.0x and continued funded-backlog growth: quarterly book-to-bill was 1.1x, backlog was $48 billion, and funded backlog was up 10% year over year.

The preview expected FY27 margin expansion as digital and other ramping programs matured; management’s expectation of a 20-basis-point year-over-year margin increase is consistent with that direction.

surprises.description: eHealth reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $21.8 million, below the preview’s base-case range of a $12 million–$16 million loss and even worse than its bear-case threshold of a $20 million loss. The operating loss was therefore materially worse than the preview’s expected range for the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss of $21.8 million (widening from a $14.1 million loss a year ago).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Adj. EBITDA: $(12)M to $(16)M”; its bear case cited “$(20)M or worse.”

surprises.description: Medicare submissions fell 44%, worse than the preview’s watchpoint of a decline no worse than about 35%. That deeper contraction makes the volume pullback look less favorable than the preview’s hoped-for disciplined reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medicare submissions declined 44%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “submissions decline no worse than ~–35%.”

surprises.description: Unit economics weakened: MA-equivalent acquisition cost per approved member rose 16%, while Medicare Advantage LTV declined 1%. The preview was looking for LTV:CAC to hold at or above 1.3x, so these results point in the opposite direction from the expected resilience.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total acquisition cost per MA-equivalent approved member rose 16%,” including “a 42% increase in customer care/enrollment cost per member”; “Medicare Advantage LTV declined 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “LTV:CAC holding ≥1.3x” and flagged LTV:CAC as a key metric.

surprises.description: The revised full-year net adjustment revenue range is $16 million–$20 million, compared with the preview’s cited $8 million–$20 million range. Although the top end is unchanged, the floor has doubled, a better outlook at the low end than the preview indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year 2026 net adjustment revenue outlook to $16 million–$20 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited the FY26 range as “Net adjustment revenue: $8–20M.”

surprises.description: Q2 ancillary cross-sell rates doubled year over year, and management offered a mature Medicare cross-sell target of roughly 0.5. The preview expected a first read on attach but did not anticipate this reported growth rate or the stated long-term target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ancillary product cross-sell rates doubled year-over-year in Q2,” and management sees “a mature Medicare cross-sell rate of roughly 0.5 as a realistic long-term target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q2 as “the first full quarter” for the lifetime advisory and ancillary attach read, but said “any disclosed attach rate is a new datapoint”; it gave no expected rate.

surprises.description: Medicare Supplement and Part D LTV rose substantially even as MA LTV slipped: Supplement was up 16% and Part D was up 52%. The preview focused on MA LTV and overall LTV:CAC and did not forecast these product-specific gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medicare Supplement LTV rose 16% and Medicare Part D LTV rose 52%.”

surprises.description: First-half operating cash flow remained positive at $30.8 million, so the company had not yet recorded the meaningful first-half burn the preview inferred from its full-year cash-flow guidance. Q2 itself was negative $5 million, but that was far less negative than the year-earlier quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow for the first six months was $30.8 million, with Q2 operating cash flow at negative $5 million, a substantial improvement from negative $41.2 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 OCF range “implies meaningful H1/H2 burn ahead.”

surprises.description: Management said Q3 marketing spend would be cut even more than the 45% year-over-year reduction in Q2, implying steeper enrollment and revenue declines. The preview anticipated a weak, back-end-loaded year but did not specifically anticipate an even deeper Q3 marketing cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 marketing spend will be cut even more than the 45% year-over-year reduction seen in Q2, implying steeper enrollment and revenue declines, with the majority of the annual marketing budget deployed in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described 2026 as an “intentional bridge year” and said Q2–Q4 guidance was “extraordinarily back-end-loaded”; it also identified further carrier marketing pullback into AEP as a bear-case risk.

in_line: Q2 revenue of $33.6 million was within the preview’s $33.3 million–$35.2 million consensus range.
Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue, GAAP net income, adjusted EBITDA, and operating cash flow, as the preview’s base case expected.
Management reiterated a return to sustainable revenue growth beginning in 2027, consistent with the preview’s expected 2027 growth framework.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $481 million, far above the preview’s $402.3 million consensus and $405–415 million estimate. The result also exceeded the preview’s $425 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 48% year-over-year to $481 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2'26 Consensus $402.3M”; “My Estimate $405–415M”; bull scenario: “Revenue | ≥$425M.”

surprises.description: Royalty revenue reached $308 million, above the preview’s roughly $280 million consensus and its $278–288 million estimate. This was a stronger result than the preview’s already favorable partner read-throughs suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Royalty revenue of $308 million (up 50% YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Royalty revenue | ~$280M (implied)”; “My Estimate $278–288M”; the preview said partner data supported royalties “at or above the high end” of that range.

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $2.28, well above the $1.79 consensus and $1.80–1.88 estimate. That also greatly surpassed the preview’s bull-case threshold of $1.95.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $2.28.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $1.79”; “My Estimate $1.80–1.88”; bull scenario: “Non-GAAP EPS | ≥$1.95.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $328.8 million with a margin above 65%, far above the preview’s $245–260 million estimate. This also substantially outpaced the preview’s concern that the remaining quarters required a steep EBITDA step-up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose 46% to $328.8 million with a margin above 65%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$245M (implied)”; “My Estimate $245–260M”; the preview said the low end of full-year guidance required “~$302M/quarter for the remaining three quarters.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year guidance beyond the level the preview expected: revenue is now $1.835–1.91 billion, royalties $1.22–1.245 billion, and EPS $8.65–9.00. The preview expected a raise to roughly $1.78–1.83 billion in revenue and an EPS floor of at least $8.00, while the prior guide was $1.710–1.810 billion revenue, $1.130–1.170 billion royalties, and $7.75–8.25 EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to total revenue of $1.835-1.91 billion … royalty revenue of $1.22-1.245 billion … and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $8.65-9.00.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side is positioned for a raise to roughly $1.78–1.83B revenue and an $8.00+ EPS floor”; prior guidance: “Revenue $1.710–1.810B … Royalty $1.130–1.170B … Non-GAAP EPS $7.75–8.25.”

surprises.description: The preview identified four 2026 agreements and expected the Incyte upfront to land in Q3; the call reported five agreements in 2026 and $35.5 million in upfront collaboration revenue, split roughly evenly between ENHANZE and Hypercon. The reported upfront total and deal count point to more collaboration activity than the preview had identified, though the call facts do not specify which agreements contributed the upfronts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Halozyme signed five new collaboration and licensing agreements in 2026 (four in Q2, one in July), contributing $35.5 million in upfront collaboration revenue split roughly evenly between ENHANZE and Hypercon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Vertex, Oruka, GSK, and Incyte as deals signed in 2026, and said: “Watch for the Incyte upfront landing in Q3 rather than Q2.”

surprises.description: Royalties from the newer Opdivo SC, Ocrevus SC, and Rybrevant SC launches grew approximately 80% quarter-over-quarter, expanding the diversified royalty base to six products. The preview highlighted individual partner read-throughs but did not anticipate or quantify this combined contribution from newer launches.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Newer launch products (Opdivo SC, Ocrevus SC, Rybrevant SC) grew royalty contributions approximately 80% quarter-over-quarter, expanding the diversified royalty base to six products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed Opdivo Qvantig and Ocrevus Zunovo ramps, but gave no combined royalty-growth expectation for these newer launches.

surprises.description: Halozyme reported repurchasing $332.8 million of shares in Q2, a large portion of the $400 million full-year target already completed in one quarter. The preview flagged buyback pace as important but did not forecast this level of execution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $332.8 million of shares in Q2 against a $400 million full-year buyback target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “$400M targeted for 2026” and that “Q2 pace tells you how management reads its own valuation,” without stating an expected quarterly amount.

surprises.description: Halozyme expanded ENHANZE into ADCs and nucleic acids and estimated that at least 100 commercial and development products could benefit. The preview discussed adding ENHANZE development programs but did not anticipate this expansion into new modality areas or the stated potential reach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expanded ENHANZE into two new modality areas—ADCs and nucleic acids—via GSK and an undisclosed partner, estimating at least 100 commercial and development products could benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said nine ENHANZE products in development were “going to 13 by YE26,” but did not mention ADCs, nucleic acids, or a potential 100-product reach.

surprises.description: The call gave a specific long-term Hypercon outlook: its first two products are projected to launch in 2030–2031, with about $1 billion in royalty revenue by the mid-2030s from five to seven launches. The preview highlighted Hypercon commercialization but provided no comparable launch schedule or revenue target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hypercon is projected to launch its first two products in the 2030-2031 timeframe and reach approximately $1 billion in royalty revenue by the mid-2030s from an assumed five to seven launches.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Hypercon/Surf Bio commercialization” but did not state launch dates or a royalty-revenue target.

in_line: The preview expected the ENHANZE development pipeline to grow from nine programs toward 13 by year-end 2026; the call said the company expects up to 13, currently nine.

The partner sales read-throughs for DARZALEX and VYVGART were broadly in line with the preview’s already favorable figures: the preview cited DARZALEX sales of $4.207 billion, up 17.6%, and VYVGART sales of $1.516 billion, up 60%.

surprises.description: The preview mentioned wildfire season as a watch item but did not anticipate a Spokane-area event that left about 7,300 electric and 5,300 gas customers without service. A key transmission line has been restored and reduced the risk of capacity-related outages, though additional line and distribution damage still needs assessment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiple wildfires near Spokane have left roughly 7,300 of Avista's 429,000 electric customers and about 5,300 of its 386,000 natural gas customers without service”; crews “repaired and energized a key transmission line,” though “a few transmission lines and significant distribution damage remain to be assessed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Wildfire season and resiliency spend” was listed as something to watch.

surprises.description: Despite the fires, management said Avista facilities did not start them and estimated the infrastructure damage was far below the scale that would require securitization. Because the damaged assets are long-lived, management also expects minimal regulatory lag and may seek cost recovery from the UTC.
surprises.fact_evidence: Avista said its facilities “were not involved in starting any” of the fires; the monetary impact was “nowhere near the scale that would require securitization”; management expects “minimal regulatory lag impact” and may file a UTC cost-recovery petition.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the possibility of resuming negotiations on the 500 MW data-center project. Instead, Avista removed it from its capital plan and paused the MOU while it works through internal processes and customer-affordability protections; management said it will proceed only if existing-customer reliability is maintained and current customers receive a net benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: Avista “removed the 500-megawatt data center project from its capital plan and paused the MOU”; management “will not proceed with a new large data center customer unless existing customer reliability is maintained and there is a net benefit for current customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any update on resuming negotiations is the main strategic swing factor.”

surprises.description: A settlement in the Washington rate case now appears difficult because of a fundamental disagreement over the four-year plan term, rather than being merely an open procedural question. Management expects a September 17–18 hearing and a mid-December commission order; it also said public counsel's return-level and power-supply-adjustment positions are the main disagreements, while staff is relatively close to Avista.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said a settlement would be “difficult due to fundamental disagreement over the 4-year plan term”; the hearing is set for September 17–18 and the commission order is expected mid-December. Public counsel's main disagreements are the return level and power supply adjustment, while staff's position is “relatively close to the company's.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch for settlement or procedural commentary.”

surprises.description: The nonregulated segment had a strong quarter driven by ERock going public, an investment-mark gain the preview did not anticipate specifically. Management also warned that an expected gain next quarter will likely reverse at ERock's current stock price, adding near-term earnings volatility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The nonregulated segment delivered a strong quarter driven by an EIP investment (ERock) that went public,” but an “expected gain next quarter will likely reverse given the current ERock stock price.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the prior-year clean-tech fund losses made the comparison easy “if non-utility marks don't repeat,” and identified investment marks as the main source of headline-EPS noise.

surprises.description: Hertz reported $2.4 billion of Q2 revenue, above the preview’s $2.28 billion consensus and its $2.26–$2.30 billion base case. The beat was achieved with a 1% smaller fleet, making revenue stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 10% year-over-year to $2.4 billion, achieved with a 1% smaller fleet and beating both consensus and prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $2.28B” consensus; the derived base case was “$2.26–2.30B.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted corporate EBITDA came in just above the top of the pre-announced $50–$80 million range. That is a small upside surprise rather than the broadly expected in-range result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted corporate EBITDA reached $81 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted Corporate EBITDA of $50–80M” was pre-announced; the scenario analysis also put the base case at “$55–75M.”

surprises.description: RPD growth reached 9%, above the preview’s approximately 6.5% build. The stronger pricing result exceeded the expected acceleration in an already-strong metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPD increased 9%,” with “U.S. airport RPD up 12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The derived operating build assumed “RPD ~$59.3 (+6.5%, ‘accelerating above Q1’s +5.5%).’”

surprises.description: Utilization was 79%, materially below the preview’s 82–84% base case. The reported 80-basis-point year-over-year improvement did not prevent utilization from missing that expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total fleet utilization improved 80 basis points to 79%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s utilization base case was “82–84%.”

surprises.description: Q3 EBITDA guidance of $275–$325 million is above the preview’s modeled $250–$300 million range. The outlook therefore points to a stronger next quarter than the preview’s base case expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects adjusted corporate EBITDA of $275-$325 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview scenario analysis modeled “Q3 $250–300M.”

surprises.description: Q3 net DPU guidance of $285–$295 is below the preview’s expected $290–$305 range, suggesting a somewhat better unit-cost trajectory than anticipated. The range also keeps Q3 DPU below $300, which the preview identified as a positive surprise threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects … net DPU of $285-$295.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Q3 DPU guided $290–305”; it also said “any number starting with a ‘2’ is a positive shock.”

surprises.description: The reported full-year EBITDA range of $225–$275 million is stronger than the preview’s modeled outcome of roughly $35–$250 million and its expectation that guidance might be cut to around a 1–3% margin. The range’s lower end is still not an unambiguous confirmation of the original 3–6% margin framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance calls for adjusted corporate EBITDA of $225-$275 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a realistic H2 implied FY26 EBITDA of “roughly $35–250M,” and its base case expected the margin guide to be “cut/narrowed to ~1–3%.”

surprises.description: Pro forma liquidity after the financing was only slightly above $1 billion, well short of the preview’s roughly $1.35 billion expectation. Separately, the year-end liquidity outlook was reduced from about $1.5 billion to $1.0–$1.4 billion after excluding ATM proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company had “$984 million in liquidity” at Q2 end; after the notes and greenshoe, pro forma liquidity was “slightly above $1 billion.” Full-year guidance gave “year-end liquidity of $1.0-$1.4 billion (lowered from ~$1.5 billion after removing ATM proceeds).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Q2-end liquidity vs. ~$1.0B + $350M” and flagged “Q2-end liquidity vs. ~$1.35B pro forma”; it also cited year-end guidance of “>$1.5B.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that Oro is expected to generate more than $600 million in revenue this year and gave a later-this-year launch window for its Lucid/Nuro AV partnership. The preview identified Oro as an important potential value driver and sought economic details, but did not anticipate these specific disclosures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Oro mobility platform … is expected to generate more than $600 million in revenue this year,” with an AV partnership “launching in the San Francisco Bay Area later this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that “any disclosed economics, contracted volume, or separate-capitalization commentary” on Oro would be a meaningful vector.

surprises.description: Hertz said RPU reached $1,542, surpassing its $1,500 North Star target. This is a positive target overrun that was not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPU rose 8% to $1,542, surpassing the $1,500 North Star target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call identified a “$1,500 North Star target.”

surprises.description: The company reaffirmed its roughly $1 billion 2027 EBITDA target, as the preview expected, but also stated that it expects its first full year of positive net income and free cash flow in 2027—an additional favorable outlook not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Hertz was “reaffirming the ~$1 billion EBITDA target and first full-year net income and free-cash-flow positivity for 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview treated the “2027 $1B EBITDA target” as a key question and said dropping it would be a bear signal; it did not give an expectation for 2027 net income or free cash flow.

in_line: Q2 net DPU was approximately in line with the preview’s expectation: the call reported $302, roughly matching the target, versus the preview’s approximately $300 guidance.
Q2-end liquidity before the financing was close to the preview’s expectation of just under $1 billion: the company reported $984 million.
The RPD-to-DOE spread expanded 17% year over year, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the spread would hold or widen.

Recall activity was broadly as anticipated: the preview cited about 16,000 affected vehicles per month and a roughly 200-basis-point utilization drag; the call reported an average of 15,000 vehicles monthly and nearly the same utilization drag.
The 2027 EBITDA target was reaffirmed, as the preview expected it might be.

surprises.description: WLDN reported net revenue of $117 million, about 14% above the $102.27 million consensus estimate, while contract revenue reached $231 million. The preview expected only about $180–190 million of contract revenue and modeled net revenue growth of 7.7%, versus the reported 23% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue up 23% to $117 million” and “contract revenue grew 33% year-over-year to $231 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue… $102.27M”; “Contract revenue (est.): ~$180–190M”; implied net revenue growth of “+7.7%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $33 million, well above the preview’s derived estimate of about $23–25 million, and the 28.2% margin on net revenue substantially exceeded the roughly 24% Q2 run rate the preview said was needed. The reported margin was also the highest in WLDN’s history.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 51% to a record $33 million, achieving a record 28.2% adjusted EBITDA margin on net revenue—the highest quarterly margin in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (derived) ~$23–25M”; “Q2 needs ~24%” adjusted EBITDA margin.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS reached $2.07, far above the $1.30 consensus estimate and the preview’s expectation of a year-over-year decline. The $5.3 million tax benefit aided the reported EPS, although pre-tax income also rose 88%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 38% to $2.07, aided by a $5.3 million tax benefit that pushed pre-tax income up 88% to $19.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $1.30” and implied year-over-year change of “-13.3%.”

surprises.description: WLDN raised its full-year 2026 guidance rather than merely reaffirming the prior range the preview considered sufficient. The revised ranges are higher by $5 million at both ends for net revenue, $3 million at the low end and $2 million at the high end for adjusted EBITDA, and $0.10 for adjusted EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net revenue of $415–430 million, adjusted EBITDA of $103–107 million, and adjusted diluted EPS of $5.00–5.15.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “clean reaffirm of $410–425M / $100–105M / $4.90–5.05” could be sufficient and identified guidance action as the key metric.

surprises.description: WLDN reported a 150-basis-point decline in gross margin, despite the unexpectedly high adjusted EBITDA margin. The preview highlighted Q1 gross-margin improvement but did not anticipate a Q2 decline attributed to a change in project mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined 150 basis points in Q2 due to a mix shift toward performance engineering and commercial projects carrying heavier equipment and subcontractor loads.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Q1 delivered 40.7% gross margin (vs 37.8% LY)” and focused on Q2 EBITDA margin, without flagging an expected gross-margin decline.

surprises.description: WLDN disclosed $110 million of new LADWP work plus two other sizable contract wins, totaling $212 million in awards. The preview discussed the existing LADWP contract and prior wins, but did not anticipate this new set of awards.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Notable new contract wins since the last call include a $110 million LADWP solar streetlight expansion (half already authorized), a $53 million City College of New York plant upgrade, and a $49 million five-year SoCalREN contract.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$214M of wins… at Q1, plus the $31M Encina cogeneration award” and said the market wanted “named or quantified new bookings.”

surprises.description: WLDN reported net debt of 0.3x trailing EBITDA, below the 0.6x leverage level the preview cited after the Burton acquisition. This leaves the company with less leverage than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The balance sheet carries only $33 million net debt (0.3x trailing EBITDA) with $165 million in total liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Burton transaction took leverage “to 0.6x net debt / TTM EBITDA.”

surprises.description: WLDN cited $34 million of deferred tax assets, above the $28 million cushion described in the preview, and said they survive the 179D provision’s sunset. That is a larger stated tax asset cushion than investors were told to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Targeting over 70% conversion of adjusted EBITDA to free cash flow, aided by $34 million in deferred tax assets that survive the June 2025 sunset of the 179D provision.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$28M of deferred tax assets expected to offset liabilities well into 2027 and beyond.”

in_line: APG was projected to nearly triple year-over-year to roughly $75 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that APG could “approach tripling” in 2026.
LADWP was expected to ramp substantially in the back half; management said the new LADWP work should ramp through Q3 2026 and into early 2027, without reporting a delay.
Management still expects the revolver to be fully repaid by year-end, matching the preview’s stated expectation.

surprises.description: The preview expected servicing to return to profitability or at least improve as runoff eased. Instead, servicing adjusted pretax income fell more than 60% year over year, with MSR runoff nearly 80% higher than a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Servicing adjusted pretax income declined over 60% year-over-year as lower interest rates drove MSR runoff up nearly 80% versus the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Servicing back to +$25M” in its bull case and said the base case had “Servicing profitable but subdued”; it also expected runoff to improve as rates rose.

surprises.description: Management pointed to an adjusted pretax ROE operating level around 9%, below the preview’s 10% low end, and directed investors to the low end of the range. The preview said a result materially below its roughly $20 million adjusted pretax-income threshold would put the guidance at risk, although its base case already allowed for a low-end posture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered expectations, guiding to the low end of its full-year 2026 adjusted pretax ROE range of 10% to 15%, currently operating around the 9% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs ≥ ~$20M adjusted pretax income for the low end of guidance to remain credible”; the base case anticipated guidance “reaffirmed but explicitly ‘low end.’”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted pressure on origination margins and hedge effectiveness, but reported origination adjusted pretax income grew more than threefold year over year on record funded volume. The call attributed the volume chiefly to B2B correspondent and co-issue, though it did not provide margin figures to show whether the preview’s margin concerns eased.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Origination adjusted pretax income grew over 3x year-over-year on record funded volume of $15.5 billion (up 64% YoY), driven primarily by the B2B correspondent and co-issue channel.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Originations margin, not volume” was the key issue, describing “hedge effectiveness and loan sale margins” as pressured.

surprises.description: Servicing portfolio growth was stronger than the preview’s H1 subservicing target: first-half subservicing additions exceeded $28 billion, while total servicing UPB also grew faster than the industry despite planned transfers and client sales. This supports the growth-engine thesis more strongly than the preview’s target alone implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half subservicing additions of $35 billion exceeded guidance”; “Total servicing UPB grew 10% year-over-year versus industry growth of 3%, with servicing additions net of runoff of $76 billion despite planned Rithm transfers and client MSR sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Subservicing additions vs. the $28B H1 target” as a key metric and said Q1 had delivered $28B of total servicing additions.

surprises.description: The preview anticipated a GAAP gain from the reverse-mortgage sale, while the reported quarter included a net loss and about $33 million of pretax costs tied collectively to the reverse asset sale, legacy subservicing transfer, and unfavorable fair-value adjustments. The call also reported a $12 million unfavorable reverse-MSR fair-value swing, rather than a clearly favorable quarter-end effect from the exit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Onity reported a Q2 2026 net loss that included approximately $33 million of pretax costs from the Finance of America reverse asset sale, legacy subservicing transfer to Rithm, and unfavorable market-driven asset fair value adjustments”; the reverse portfolio had “a $12 million net unfavorable fair value swing in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FAR sale closed inside the quarter and that “Any book gain lands in GAAP but should be excluded from adjusted.”

surprises.description: The preview emphasized rising rates and the risk of weaker refinance activity, but Onity reported better refinance recapture and rapid growth in home-equity lending. These call metrics were not specifically anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refinance recapture rate improved to 51%, up 3 percentage points year-over-year, exceeding the ICE industry average, with home equity product volume doubling and second lien volume more than doubling (over $70 million funded) year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described rising rates as potentially having “crushed refi volume” and framed the quarter as a possible “worst-of-both-worlds crossover.”

in_line: The low-end guidance posture itself was anticipated in the preview’s base case, which expected guidance to be reaffirmed but explicitly at the low end; the notable miss against that expectation is the reported operating level around 9%, below the 10% range floor.

The preview already identified a $20 million buyback authorization and about $10 million of H1 repurchases. The reported $10 million buyback and additional $20 million authorization therefore do not establish a clear surprise relative to the preview.

surprises.description: KULR reported Q2 revenue of $2.1 million, far below the preview’s $5.5 million estimate and the cited $8.5–9.0 million consensus range. Revenue also fell from both Q1 and the year-earlier quarter, rather than coming in roughly flat to modestly higher sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $2.1 million, down significantly from both the prior year and Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … My estimate: $5.5M”; “Consensus … ~$8.5–9.0M”; and the base case expected “sequential revenue roughly flat-to-up modestly.”

surprises.description: Instead of holding gross margin in the preview’s expected 25–28% range, KULR reported a gross loss. That is a major reversal from the preview’s key test of whether Q1’s 29% margin could be sustained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The quarter produced a gross loss, missing management's expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … My estimate: 25–28%”; the preview called for margin to “hold mid-to-high 20s” in the base case.

surprises.description: Management said supply-chain bottlenecks and long lead times delayed planned Q2 battery shipments, whereas the preview expected a modest sequential revenue increase and described the Q3 production ramp as on track. Management expects the delayed shipments to recover in the second half, but that recovery was not yet reflected in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New program supply chain bottlenecks and long lead times delayed planned Q2 battery shipments, which management expects to recover in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “sequential revenue roughly flat-to-up modestly” and the ramp to be “on track for Q3”; the preview said any line-start slip would directly affect the second-half revenue ramp.

surprises.description: KULR disclosed that it had secured a defense drone battery opportunity exceeding $5 million, alongside Q2 orders from two new customers using new battery configurations. The preview identified defense and UAV programs as possible catalysts, but did not anticipate this specific opportunity or its stated size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was driven principally by two large orders from new customers involving new battery configurations, and the company secured a defense drone battery opportunity exceeding $5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said defense/UAV programs might “convert to shipped revenue” in its bull case, but gave no expectation of a secured opportunity exceeding $5 million.

surprises.description: The Board authorized management to sell any or all remaining Bitcoin, indicating a move toward full divestment rather than merely using some Bitcoin to repay the Coinbase facility. The preview treated the longer-term treasury policy as unresolved and asked whether Bitcoin would remain a funding reserve or strategic holding.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized management to sell any and all remaining Bitcoin holdings, signaling a full divestment of the crypto treasury to focus on the operating business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the treasury was “now a funding reserve to be drawn down, or still a strategic hold” and said a clear “no new BTC purchases with cash” reaffirmation would remove an overhang.

in_line: KULR fully repaid the $20 million Coinbase credit facility with Bitcoin-sale proceeds, consistent with the preview’s description of the July sale and expectation that the company would be effectively debt-free.
The Texas facility was not contributing in Q2 but is expected to become operational in Q3, consistent with the preview’s expected Q3 production start.
KULR avoided ATM share issuance during the first half, consistent with the preview’s account that the ATM was paused and Bitcoin sales were the stated alternative funding source.

surprises.description: Qualys raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $732–738 million, above the preview’s expected base-case raise to roughly $726–729 million and even above its bull-case threshold of $729 million. The increase is positive, though the gap is modest relative to the forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $732–738 million from prior $721–727 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 raised to ~$726–729M” in the base case; the bull case called for “FY26 revenue raised to $729M+.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in above both the roughly $178.7 million consensus and the preview’s estimate of a normal Qualys beat at about $180.5–182 million. At $182.2 million, it reached the preview’s bull-case revenue level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 11% year-over-year to $182.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “~$178.7M,” and said a “normal” quarter produces “~$180.5–182M”; its bull case was “$182M+.”

surprises.description: Q2 EPS of $1.98 exceeded the preview’s functional buy-side bar of roughly $1.88–1.95, although it was just below the preview’s bull-case threshold of $2.00. This was a modest positive surprise rather than an outsized beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EPS was $1.98.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Treat the functional buy-side bar as ~$1.88–$1.95”; its bull case was “$2.00+.”

surprises.description: Total-company NDR improved to 105%, exceeding the preview’s stated expectation that it would remain flat at 104%. The ETM/CSAM cohort NDR, by contrast, stayed at 107%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net dollar expansion rate improved to 105% from 104% last quarter, while the ETM/CTEM customer cohort NDR held steady at 107%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided that “total NDR stays flat this year” and described “105%+” as “a genuine upside surprise.”

surprises.description: LTM ETM/CSAM share of total bookings reached 12%, modestly above the preview’s 11% reference point. Its 14% share of new bookings matched the preview’s stated 14% figure, while cohort NDR remained at 107% rather than moving toward the preview’s 109–110% upside target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ETM and CSAM combined reached 12% of total bookings and 14% of new bookings on an LTM basis”; cohort NDR “held steady at 107%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “11% of LTM total, 14% of new” and said to watch cohort NDR moving toward “109–110%” and total-bookings mix toward “13%+.”

surprises.description: Qualys repurchased $76.8 million of shares in Q2, above the preview’s roughly $54 million quarterly run-rate estimate based on the remaining authorization. This indicates a faster buyback pace than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $76.8 million of shares in Q2, leaving $229.8 million remaining in its buyback authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “$54M/quarter run-rate” and flagged the buyback pace as a narrative wildcard.

surprises.description: QFlex produced a low seven-figure upsell and a six-figure upsell in the quarter, earlier commercial activity than the preview’s framing of QFlex as a beta product expected to go live later in the year. The deals are limited in number, so the surprise is small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The quarter included a low 7-figure and a 6-figure QFlex upsell.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described QFlex as “in beta with a go-live ‘later this year’” and a “2027 growth unlock.”

in_line: Second-half current billings growth guidance of 7–8% matched the preview’s 7–8% baseline assumption; the preview identified acceleration to 9%+ as upside, not its base expectation.
The ETM/CSAM cohort NDR remained at 107%, consistent with the preview’s base-case expectation of 107–108%, even though it fell short of the preview’s upside target.
The 14% LTM share of new bookings from ETM/CSAM matched the preview’s 14% reference point.
The FY2026 EPS guidance raise to $7.74–7.88 was broadly consistent with the preview’s expected base-case range of $7.65–7.85 and bull-case level of $7.80+.

surprises.description: Q1 non-GAAP EPS was $1.94, well above the $1.52 consensus and the preview’s $1.52–$1.58 base case. That is a much larger beat than the preview’s expected, largely priced-in EPS beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $1.94” for the quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS $1.52” consensus; preview base case “$1.52–1.58.”

surprises.description: Fee-related earnings reached $124 million, versus the preview’s $92–96 million base case. The 53% FRE margin also exceeded the preview’s roughly 50% base case, with management attributing the performance to strong fee-related performance revenues.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 fee-related earnings rose 49% year-over-year to $124 million, with FRE margin expanding to 53% from 51% a year earlier, aided by strong fee-related performance revenues.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case (mine): … FRE $92–96M”; base scenario: “FRE ~$93M, margin ~50%.”

surprises.description: Evergreen net inflows were nearly $640 million, below the preview’s $0.7–1.1 billion base-case range and the greater-than-$1-billion quarterly whisper. However, the company reported fund-level detail: 10 of 12 funds had positive inflows, while the non-U.S. multi-strategy equity fund had outflows; platform AUM surpassed $19 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Evergreen platform generated nearly $640 million of net inflows and surpassed $19 billion in AUM, with 10 of 12 funds showing positive net inflows while the non-U.S. multi-strategy equity fund posted net outflows.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “evergreen ~$19–20B, net inflows $0.7–1.1B”; catalyst: “Evergreen net flows vs. the ‘>$1B/quarter’ whisper”; the preview also called for flows “by fund.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a pipeline of three portfolio monetizations, including expected proceeds and gains for Russell and Canoe and a public listing for Securitize. The preview highlighted exit activity as a key watch point and called a named realization pipeline a bull-case signal, but did not identify these transactions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Russell (expected ~$50 million proceeds, ~$18 million gain, closing Q1 CY2027), Canoe's Bloomberg acquisition (~$30 million proceeds, ~$15 million gain), and Securitize (now public at $6.94/share with ~1.5 million shares under a 180-day lockup).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “commentary on exit activity/DPI” and identified “a named realization pipeline” as a bull-case signal.

surprises.description: The company repurchased approximately $50 million of shares during the quarter, bringing total spending under the program to $70 million. The preview identified buyback execution as a signal to watch, but did not make this level of repurchases part of its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately 559,000 shares at a weighted average $89.51 for roughly $50 million during the quarter, bringing total program spending to $70 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “buyback usage against the $100M authorization” and said aggressive repurchase would be a credibility signal in the bull case.

surprises.description: The latest direct equity fund had already committed nearly 30% of its capital, an early deployment detail not anticipated in the preview. The $3.8 billion raise itself was expected, but this commitment progress adds a positive detail beyond the announced close.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The direct equity platform closed its raise at $3.8 billion ($3.3 billion in fund plus $500 million in separate accounts), representing over 57% growth versus the prior fund, with nearly 30% of capital already committed.”

surprises.description: The blended fee rate rose to 69 basis points as fee-earning AUM shifted toward higher-fee specialized funds. The preview said the direction of the blended rate mattered, but did not project an increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total fee-earning AUM grew 12% year-over-year to $83.7 billion, with the blended fee rate rising to 69 basis points as mix shifted toward higher-fee specialized funds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Blended fee-rate direction matters more than headline FEAUM.”

in_line: Total management and advisory fees were $161 million, within the preview’s $158–166 million base-case range.
Evergreen AUM surpassed $19 billion, within the preview’s expected ~$19–20 billion range.
The $0.60 quarterly dividend and $2.40 FY27 target matched the preview’s stated dividend expectations.
The direct equity fund’s $3.8 billion close matched the close announced in the preview.
Fee-earning AUM grew 12%, consistent with the preview’s prior-year growth benchmark of 13% and above its bear-case watch level of below 10%.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.38, well below the preview’s $0.46–$0.49 consensus range and its roughly $0.49–$0.50 whisper. The shortfall was about $0.09 versus the preview’s $0.47 working consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.38.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.46 – $0.49”; “Treat ~$0.47 as the working consensus and $0.49–0.50 as the whisper.”

surprises.description: Archrock cut the top of its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA range by $30 million, leaving the new range at $865–$885 million rather than narrowing toward the upper half as the preview expected. Management attributed the reduction to cost pressures, AMS customer deferrals, and stock-driven incentive compensation, not weaker demand fundamentals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered the top end of its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $865-$885 million from the prior $865-$915 million,” citing “lube oil and make-ready cost pressures, AMS customer deferrals, and higher stock-driven incentive compensation rather than any change in demand fundamentals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side is positioned for a narrowing to the upper half ($885–915M).” The preview also said a second unchanged reaffirmation would be the bear trigger.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was essentially flat year over year and came in below the preview’s $222–$226 million estimate by roughly $9–$13 million. That was a shortfall even though the preview expected a modest step-up from Q2 2025.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $213 million (essentially flat year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA ~$222–226M (not formally polled; derived from FY guide).” The preview also listed Q2 2025 adjusted EBITDA as $212.7 million.

surprises.description: Aftermarket services revenue fell to $42 million from $65 million a year earlier as customers deferred major maintenance. This contrasts with the preview’s expectation that AMS seasonality would help drive the quarter’s revenue step-up, although the facts provided do not state the segment’s sequential revenue change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aftermarket services revenue fell to $42 million from $65 million a year ago as customers deferred major maintenance amid high crude prices, though segment adjusted gross margin improved to 24% from 23%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “In-line-to-slightly-light revenue (AMS seasonality carries the QoQ step-up more than contract ops).”

surprises.description: Operating horsepower was 4.5 million and utilization was 94.4%, below the preview’s thresholds of at least 4.55 million horsepower and 95% utilization. The horsepower decline was largely due to a larger sale of nonstrategic units than the preview’s Q1 high-grading reference.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating horsepower declined to 4.5 million from 4.7 million year-over-year largely due to the sale of ~165,000 nonstrategic horsepower”; contract operations utilization was “94.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Need: HP ≥4.55M, utilization ≥95%”; the preview noted “~40,000 hp of non-strategic units sold for $21.3M in Q1.”

surprises.description: Archrock disclosed a new eight-year contract with an existing strategic customer covering about 665,000 horsepower. The preview sought disclosure about contracted newbuild horsepower but did not anticipate this specific large, long-term agreement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed an 8-year long-term contract (with a 2-year extension option) with an existing strategic customer covering approximately 665,000 horsepower for midstream applications.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The critical disclosure: what percentage of 2027 newbuild horsepower is already under contract, at what returns?”

surprises.description: The company set out a substantial 2027–2030 growth-capital plan: $1.4–$1.6 billion to add roughly 1 million horsepower, with average annual spending about 40–45% above 2026. The preview discussed growth-capex framing but did not specify an expansion plan of this scale; the new customer contract provides some support, though the call facts do not quantify how much planned newbuild capacity it covers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Introduced a long-term capital allocation framework targeting $1.4-$1.6 billion of cumulative growth capital from 2027-2030 to add roughly 1 million new horsepower, implying roughly a 40-45% increase in average annual spend versus 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any upward revision to growth capex needs to arrive paired with contract coverage”; the preview also asked what percentage of 2027 newbuild horsepower was contracted.

surprises.description: Caterpillar engine lead times were nearly 200 weeks, longer than the roughly 160 weeks cited in the preview, and Archrock had placed orders for 2029 delivery. The added wait may constrain the timing of the growth the company outlined.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Caterpillar engine lead times remain extended at nearly 200 weeks with orders now placed for 2029 delivery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~160-week Caterpillar lead times effectively rationing new supply”; “With Cat lead times near 160 weeks, Archrock is placing multi-year orders now.”

surprises.description: The preview wanted a visible acceleration in buybacks, but the call facts cite the remaining authorization and past repurchases without announcing an accelerated buyback. The company did, however, set a broader target to return 25%–35% of operating cash flow to shareholders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plans to return 25%-35% of operating cash flow to shareholders and retains $113 million of remaining share buyback authorization, having repurchased 4.6 million shares at an average $20.91 since April 2023.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With the stock 16% off its high, the buy-side wants to hear buyback urgency”; “a visible buyback acceleration would be a genuine narrative shift.”

in_line: Contract operations adjusted gross margin was 71%, a one-point step down from the preview’s 72% reference and within its anticipated 70%–71% downside range. Management’s around-70% second-half margin outlook was also consistent with the preview’s flagged lube-oil cost and pass-through concerns.
The quarterly dividend increase to $0.23 was already reflected in the preview, which said the dividend had been raised to that amount in July.
Leverage of 2.6x was in line with the preview’s stated 2.6x level.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected around the preview’s $32.0 million base case, within a recent $30.3–$30.7 million plateau. It reached $33.5 million, above the base case and the preview’s $32 million breakout threshold, though below its $34.5 million bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 9.3% year-over-year to $33.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: $32.0M (+4.3%)”; the catalyst checklist asks, “Does revenue break $31M?”

surprises.description: The preview’s base case called for 16.2% gross margin and flagged 16.5% as the recovery threshold. Actual margin was 17%, above that threshold and the prior Q4 2025 high of 16.7%, matching the preview’s bull-case margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved 120 basis points to 17%”; management called first-half margins “a company record.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … Gross margin 16.2%”; “Gross margin: recovery to 16.5%+”; the bull case was 17.0%.

surprises.description: The preview expected aerospace and defense growth to be tested for durability after Q1’s 41.2% increase and highlighted the ramp as a key issue. Instead, Q2 aerospace/defense sales declined 12.8%, with one customer reducing post-COVID inventory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aerospace/defense declined 12.8% on one customer reducing post-COVID inventory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Aerospace & Defense +41.2% on customer approvals and production transfers”; the preview asks whether “the +41.2% A&D growth [is] a sustainable ramp or a one-quarter catch-up.”

surprises.description: The preview expected industrial sales to be flat based on Q1. They fell 4.7% year-over-year in Q2 instead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial fell 4.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Industrial flat.”

surprises.description: Medical-device sales accelerated well beyond the Q1 growth rate cited in the preview: Q2 growth was 36%, versus 10.4% in Q1. Medical imaging also grew, though its 12.2% increase was below the preview’s cited Q1 growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medical device sales jumped 36% year-over-year and medical imaging rose 12.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Medical devices +10.4%; industrial flat” and “medical imaging +15%” in the preview’s Q1 end-market summary.

surprises.description: Operating income was $623,000, about $207,000 below the preview’s $830,000 base case despite revenue and gross margin exceeding that case. A $533,000 increase in incentive compensation offset the revenue gains, indicating a larger expense drag than the base model allowed for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating income declined to $623,000 from $742,000 a year earlier, as a $533,000 increase in incentive compensation offset revenue gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … Opex $4.35M; Operating income $0.83M”; the preview also identified whether the Q1 opex spike was one-time as a key swing factor.

surprises.description: The preview identified cash generation and the revolver as key risks, including the possibility of a working-capital build. The reported first-half cash use, low quarter-end cash, and limited remaining revolver availability show that pressure was substantial: operations used $2.4 million of cash, cash and restricted cash were $1.7 million, and only $3.6 million of revolver availability remained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and restricted cash stood at just $1.7 million at quarter-end, with $7.6 million drawn on the revolving credit facility and only $3.6 million of unused availability”; “Operations used $2.4 million of cash in the first half,” including a $4.5 million receivables/contract-asset build and a $3.5 million inventory increase.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash generation and the ABL” was a ranked catalyst; the preview asks “did Q2 generate free cash flow?” and flags “a working-capital build that pushes ABL borrowings up.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed emerging fiber-optic opportunities tied to data-center build-outs, which the preview did not identify, but said they had not gained significant traction yet. This is a new potential opportunity without evidence of a near-term contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “sees emerging fiber-optic opportunities in data center build-outs without significant traction yet.”

in_line: Diluted EPS was $0.11, close to the preview’s roughly $0.12 base case and its cited Q2 2025 EPS of $0.12.
Total backlog of $93.8 million was slightly above the preview’s $88–93 million base-case range, while remaining below its bull-case trigger of more than $95 million.

surprises.description: GoodRx reported Q2 revenue of $200.4 million versus the preview’s $193.2 million consensus and roughly $193 million base case. That is a clear beat and also above the preview’s base range, though within its bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $200.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $193.2M” and “My Q2'26 base … Total … ~$193M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $63.7 million, above the preview’s estimated $56–59 million, and the 31.8% margin exceeded its roughly 30% estimate. The margin also avoided the preview’s bear-case threshold of below 29%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “adjusted EBITDA of $63.7 million, representing a 31.8% adjusted EBITDA margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$56–59M (30% margin)” and the bear case described “EBITDA margin dips below 29%.”

surprises.description: Pharma Direct revenue reached $61.6 million, well above the preview’s roughly $53 million base case and its $57 million bull-case threshold. Its 76% year-over-year growth also outpaced the preview’s expected 51% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pharma Direct revenue grew 76% year-over-year to $61.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2'26 base … ~$53M | +51%” and the bull case expected “Pharma Direct $57M+.”

surprises.description: Management raised its full-year Pharma Direct growth expectation to more than 70%, up from the 50% expectation in the preview. That is a materially stronger outlook than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its full-year Pharma Direct growth expectation from 50% to more than 70% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guide >50% growth” and the catalyst checklist expected “reaffirmed >50% FY growth.”

surprises.description: GoodRx raised its full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, with management saying it is on track for year-over-year revenue growth earlier than previously expected. The preview’s prior revenue range was $765–785 million and EBITDA guidance was at least $235 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $790-805 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $240-250 million, putting it on track for year-over-year revenue growth earlier than previously expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Currently $765–785M revenue / ≥$235M adj. EBITDA”; the preview said the bar was “a narrowing to the upper half or a raise.”

surprises.description: Subscription revenue was $28.5 million, above the preview’s roughly $25.5 million base case, with 39% year-over-year growth versus the expected 24%. The revenue result was stronger than forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue rose 39% year-over-year to $28.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2'26 base … Subscription … ~$25.5M | +24%.”

surprises.description: Subscription plans grew only 14%, rather than showing the “step-change” the preview identified as a bull signal. The much faster subscription revenue growth therefore came alongside comparatively slower plan growth, indicating higher average revenue per plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription plans grew only 14%” while “subscription revenue rose 39% year-over-year,” indicating “rising average revenue per plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscription plans were 717K in Q1 … — a step-change in that number is the bull tell.”

surprises.description: Prescription transaction revenue was $106.4 million, below the preview’s roughly $111 million estimate; that implies a year-over-year decline of about 26%, worse than the preview’s expected decline of about 22%. Management also expects continued moderation in transaction revenue, while saying Pharma Direct and subscriptions should more than offset the declines in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prescription transaction revenue was $106.4 million”; management “expects continued moderation in MAC and prescription transaction revenue” and expects Pharma Direct and subscriptions to “more than offset those declines in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2'26 base … Prescription transactions … ~$111M | -22%”; the preview said to watch for improvement to “the low-20s/high-teens.”

surprises.description: Monthly active consumers fell to 5.0 million, down 12% year over year, rather than holding around the preview’s expected 5.3 million. The reported figure is also below the preview’s 5.1 million-or-lower bear-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “monthly active consumers declining 12% year-over-year to 5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second straight quarter at ~5.3M validates the bottom; 5.1M or below breaks the thesis.”

surprises.description: GoodRx now has more than 135 consumer direct pricing programs and added named brands including Jardiance, Nurtec, Otezla, and Rapaflo. The preview identified a named manufacturer contract as a possible bull-case development, but did not anticipate this specific breadth of program additions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GoodRx now operates more than 135 consumer direct pricing programs, adding brands like Jardiance, Nurtec, Otezla, and Rapaflo.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case said to watch for management to “adds a named manufacturer contract.”

surprises.description: GoodRx made Companion its primary subscription offering over Gold, a product-positioning decision not specified in the preview. The preview had focused instead on early adoption and said Q2 revenue contribution would be immaterial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched GoodRx Companion in May … and made it the primary subscription offering over Gold.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue contribution will be immaterial; member adds, attach rate, and CAC commentary are what the buy-side wants.”

surprises.description: CFO Chris McGinnis departed and was replaced by Justin Fengler, a 10-year GoodRx veteran. The preview did not flag a CFO departure; the successor’s company tenure provides some continuity but does not remove the unexpected leadership change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Chris McGinnis departed and was replaced by Justin Fengler, a 10-year company veteran previously serving as Chief Strategy and Operations Officer.”

in_line: GoodRx Companion launched in May at $14.99 per month; the preview had already identified a late-May launch at that price and described the offering’s included generics and services.

surprises.description: Unity Vector grew 23% sequentially, versus the 12–13% growth Unity had guided, and passed a $1 billion annual run rate two quarters ahead of schedule. Strategic Grow reached $329 million, above the preview’s roughly $304 million expectation, with 63% year-over-year growth versus the expected 50–52%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unity Vector grew 23% quarter-over-quarter in Q2, nearly double the 12-13% growth the company had guided, and reached over $1 billion in annual run rate two quarters ahead of schedule”; “Strategic Grow revenue rose 63% year-over-year to $329 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Strategic Grow” consensus was “~$304M,” with implied growth of “+50–52%”; the preview also says the company had guided to 12–13% sequential Vector growth.

surprises.description: Q3 Strategic revenue guidance of $540–550 million is above the preview’s roughly $535 million modeled requirement for Q3 and its $525–540 million base-case range for total Q3 revenue. The guide also calls for 68–70% Strategic Grow growth and 19–21% sequential Vector growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for strategic revenue of $540-550 million (up 44-47% YoY)”; Strategic Grow is expected to grow “68-70%” and Vector “19-21% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says the FY26 model required “Strategic revenue of roughly $535M in Q3”; its base scenario gives Q3 total revenue of “$525–540M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $160 million, well above the preview’s $130–135 million company guide and roughly $133 million consensus. Its 29% margin also exceeded the expected 26% margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 77% YoY to $160 million with margins reaching a record 29%, expanding 800 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$130–135M” and consensus of “~$133M (26% margin).”

surprises.description: Unity pulled forward its target for GAAP net income profitability from Q4 2026 to Q3 2026, with Q3 marking its first-ever GAAP profitability. The preview did not anticipate this earlier milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company pulled forward its GAAP net income profitability target from Q4 2026 to Q3 2026, marking its first-ever GAAP profitability.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin is guided to 33%, a substantial further expansion after Q2’s 29% record margin; the preview only discussed Q2’s roughly 26% margin and the possibility of margins climbing with mix shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 margins are guided to 33% (up 1,000 bps YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch whether mix shift out of low-margin non-strategic keeps margins climbing,” and listed Q2 EBITDA margin guidance of “~26%.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow reached $202 million, up 59% year over year, against a preview that highlighted the $127 million year-ago figure as a demanding comparison but gave no expectation for this quarter’s cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow rose 59% YoY to $202 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2’25 free cash flow of “$127M” and called it “a demanding comp.”

surprises.description: The ironSource Ad Network sunset contributed only $3 million to Vector’s growth, showing that the sharp acceleration was not substantially driven by legacy revenue migration. The preview flagged the sunset and runoff but did not anticipate this limited contribution to Vector’s growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The sunset of the ironSource Ad Network contributed only $3 million to Vector's growth, indicating the acceleration was organic rather than driven by legacy migration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the ironSource Ads Network sunset and said non-strategic revenue was expected to fall to “~$50M” in Q2, but did not specify its contribution to Vector growth.

surprises.description: Unity moved from net debt to net cash, reported a $2.36 billion cash balance, and plans to repay its 2026 convertible note in November. The preview did not set an expectation for this balance-sheet change or repayment plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unity flipped from a net debt to a net cash position with a $2.36 billion cash balance, planning to pay off its 2026 convert in November.”

surprises.description: Stock-based compensation fell 25% year over year to 14% of revenue, its lowest level ever, an improvement the preview did not flag or quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stock-based compensation fell 25% year-over-year to 14% of revenue, its lowest level ever.”

surprises.description: Unity completed the Supersonic sale to Tripledot Studios on August 4; the preview only noted that an advisor had been engaged and that a signed deal was a possibility. The call facts provide no sale terms or proceeds, so the financial effect is unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unity closed the sale of Supersonic to Tripledot Studios on August 4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a financial advisor “was engaged in March” and asked whether there was a “signed deal.”

surprises.description: Unity made a strategic investment in AppsFlyer alongside Meta, Google, and Moloco, a capital-allocation development not anticipated in the preview. The facts do not provide the investment size or terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Unity] made a strategic investment in AppsFlyer alongside Meta, Google and Moloco.”

in_line: Strategic Create revenue was $157 million, within the preview’s $154–158 million estimate, and its 14% year-over-year growth was within the expected 11–14% range.

surprises.description: Cemetery/Mortuary pretax earnings rose sharply, but operating earnings fell 4.8%; the increase came from investment income surging 169.5%. That is weaker operating performance than the preview’s estimated 14% underlying pretax growth after excluding the investment tailwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Investment income that surged 169.5% to $2 million while operating earnings fell 4.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Strip it: EBT goes from $3,041K to ~$2,041K vs. $1,794K prior year — +14% underlying, not +69.5%.”

surprises.description: Mortgage loans more than 90 days past due rose to $15.8 million from $6.5 million at year-end, an adverse credit-quality development not identified in the preview’s mortgage discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mortgage loans more than 90 days past due jumped to $15.8 million as of June 30, 2026 from $6.5 million at year-end, a credit-quality trend management is monitoring closely.”

surprises.description: Life segment investment income weakened: six-month net investment income fell 14%, mainly because homebuilder profit-share income and construction lending income were lower. The preview raised investment income mix as a possible concern, but did not anticipate these specific sources of the decline.
