surprises.description: Management cited consumer-durables categories declining 2–3% in dollars and 7.5–10% in units, a weaker category backdrop than the preview’s required H2 revenue acceleration implied. Lifetime was said to have outperformed the market, which partly offsets the concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Third-party data showed the company's consumer durables categories down 2-3% in dollars and 7.5-10% in units, though management stated Lifetime outperformed the market.”

in_line: Full-year net sales guidance remained $650–$700 million, in line with the preview’s base case expectation that management would reaffirm the sales range.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $19.9 million, well above both the $17.80 million consensus and the preview’s $18.0–18.2 million effective whisper. It also broke the expected flat-to-modest sequential trend with 15% sequential growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $19.9 million,” up 16% year-over-year and 15% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $17.80M” consensus; the preview said the working number was likely “$18.0–18.2M, not $17.80M” and described consensus as asking for the first real sequential step-up.

surprises.description: Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $72–75 million from $70–73 million, rather than simply reaffirming the existing range. The new midpoint is above the prior guide’s midpoint and reaches beyond the preview’s expected base case of an unchanged guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $72-75 million from the prior $70-73 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the base case was that the “$70–73M guide simply [be] reaffirmed” and called reaffirmation the minimum acceptable outcome.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was essentially breakeven, far better than the preview’s expected $2.3–2.7 million loss. Management cautioned that this near-breakeven result is not expected to continue in the second half, and reiterated breakeven at about $80 million in annual revenue rather than giving a calendar date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to roughly $0.1 million (essentially breakeven)” and management “does not expect this near-breakeven level to be sustained in the second half of 2026”; the company reiterated breakeven at “around $80 million in annual revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated adjusted EBITDA loss of “$(2.3)–$(2.7)M” and said management had “pointedly refused to give a breakeven date.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was just under $25 million, materially above the preview’s expected $18–19 million and its roughly $18 million watch level. The reported facts do not provide the requested explanation of the Q1 cash drawdown.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “ended Q2 with just under $25 million in cash plus $37 million in combined cash and accounts receivable.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “quarter-end cash $18–19M” and emphasized watching cash against “~$18M,” alongside a bridge for the Q1 drawdown.

surprises.description: Gross margin was just over 61%, above the preview’s 58.5–59.5% estimate range. Management also said it now expects to exit 2026 at 60% or higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached just over 61%” and management now expects to “exit 2026 at 60% or above.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at “58.5–59.5%” and said “60%+ validates the operating-leverage thesis.”

surprises.description: AVISE CTD volume grew 11% year over year, above the preview’s base-case expectation of 7–8% and meeting its ≥10% bull-case threshold. This was a stronger volume result than the central expectation, even though the preview identified 10% or more as a possible bull tell.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AVISE CTD test volume hit a record ~39,000 tests, up 11% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Volume +7–8%”; its bull tell was “≥10%.”

surprises.description: Pharma services rose from the preview’s Q1 reference point of about $300,000 to more than $1 million in quarterly revenue, while backlog grew by about $1 million to over $6 million. That indicates a faster near-term contribution than the preview’s lower-weight treatment of the opportunity suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pharma services generated record quarterly revenue exceeding $1 million (up over 200% year-over-year), with contract backlog growing about $1 million to over $6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described pharma services as “~$300K in Q1 with a $5M+ backlog recognizable over 2–3 years” and assigned the pipeline “lower near-term weight.”

surprises.description: Trailing 12-month ASP reached $446, slightly below the preview’s roughly $448 expectation, and the quarter included more than $1 million collected on claims older than 360 days. The preview had highlighted aged-claims collections as a quality-of-growth question, so this result did not clearly establish that ASP growth was being driven by in-period collection strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month ASP expanded to $446 (up 4%), marking the 13th consecutive quarter of ASP growth”; quarterly ASP benefited from “over $1 million collected on claims older than 360 days.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “TTM ASP ~$448 with modest aged-claims help” and asked how much ASP reflected “in-period collection strength versus another aged-claims harvest.”

in_line: The myositis standalone product remained on track for an early 2027 launch, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $207.1 million, well above the preview’s $178.3 million consensus and management-anchored expectation. That is a much larger result than the roughly 13.5% year-over-year growth the preview anticipated; reported growth was 32%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales grew 32% year-over-year to $207.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales $178.3M”; the preview also says management pre-framed Q2 at “~$178M revenue.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA significantly exceeded the preview’s roughly $31 million expectation and 17.5% margin anchor. The call reported 56% year-over-year adjusted EBITDA growth, implying a much stronger Q2 margin than the preview’s target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increasing 56%” year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (implied by mgmt) ~$31M @ 17.5% margin”; the preview calls for “≥17.5%.”

surprises.description: Cadre raised its full-year sales and adjusted EBITDA ranges instead of simply reaffirming the prior outlook. The new ranges are above the preview’s expected $736–758 million in sales and $136–141 million in adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of $749-769 million and adjusted EBITDA of $139-144 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed May 2026): Net sales $736–758M … Adj. EBITDA $136–141M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin rose to 42.6%, whereas the preview estimated roughly 40% and expected a year-over-year decline. The reported expansion was 120 basis points, or 209 basis points excluding inventory step-up amortization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margins expanding 120 basis points (209 bps adjusted for inventory step-up amortization) to 42.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~40% (est.)” and “−~100bps”; the preview also said Q2 needed to show recovery after Q1’s gross-margin decline.

surprises.description: The nuclear business showed more resilience than the preview’s discussion of the downblending suspension might suggest: nuclear organic growth was in the high-single to low-double digits, and the executive-order impact was said to affect less than 8% of nuclear revenue. The preview had highlighted the suspension and watched for further slippage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nuclear organic growth ran in high-single to low-double digits” and “the downblending executive order affecting less than 8% of nuclear revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Nuclear / plutonium downblending” and described the program suspension as unchanged, with investors watching for “further slippage.”

surprises.description: The nuclear backlog increased by $13 million since year-end, providing positive order momentum beyond the preview’s focus on converting the existing backlog and monitoring organic order intake.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nuclear backlog increased $13 million since year-end, driven primarily by commercial nuclear energy and environmental remediation in both the U.S. and Northern Europe.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Backlog and its convertibility” and said to watch for “organic order intake ex-acquisition.”

surprises.description: Cadre secured another $8.4 million purchase order for the Med-Eng BEMO military program, bringing received orders to $18.4 million against the five-year contract. The preview did not anticipate this additional order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cadre secured a second $8.4 million purchase order for the Med-Eng BEMO military program, bringing total received to $18.4 million against a 5-year $50 million IDIQ contract.”

surprises.description: Safariland’s SXHP ballistic panel was selected for the FBI and incorporated into a large multi-agency IDIQ contract, a new award not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Safariland's SXHP ballistic panel was selected for the FBI, integrated into Predictive Ballistics' 5-year $61 million IDIQ contract that also serves the U.S. Marshals, DEA and other DOJ agencies.”

surprises.description: Alien Gear contributed $4.8 million in Q2 and outperformed expectations. The preview mentioned acquired revenue as a metric to watch but did not forecast this level of quarterly performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The recently acquired Alien Gear generated $4.8 million in the quarter and outperformed expectations, though guidance conservatively bakes in only $11 million for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic growth ex-TYR/Alien Gear” was a catalyst to watch; no specific Alien Gear quarterly revenue expectation was given.

surprises.description: Net leverage was 2.5x, better than the preview’s estimate of just under 3.0x, leaving more acquisition capacity than expected. The preview had anticipated additional M&A in 2026, which management reiterated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage declined to 2.5x, providing substantial dry powder against a 3.5x ceiling, and management expects at least one more acquisition in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Net leverage just under 3.0x” and noted that management had flagged “additional M&A in 2026.”

surprises.description: Q3’s approximately 18% adjusted EBITDA margin is below the roughly 20.8% average H2 margin the preview said was needed to meet the prior full-year EBITDA midpoint. The raised full-year guidance and expectation for Q4 to resemble Q2’s stronger profile partly offset this, but leave more of the H2 profit delivery dependent on Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to approximately $190 million with ~18% adjusted EBITDA margins, with Q4 expected to resemble Q2's stronger profile.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview calculated that H2 required “~$86M in H2, requiring ~20.8% margins,” and called the H2 math the “central bear argument.”

surprises.description: Q2 earnings faced a $6.6 million foreign-exchange headwind, an unanticipated drag even as sales and adjusted EBITDA substantially exceeded expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FX headwinds hurt Q2 earnings by $6.6 million.”

in_line: Organic growth was 5%, at the high end of the preview’s expected 3–5% full-year range.
Management’s expectation of at least one more acquisition in 2026 was consistent with the preview’s expectation of additional M&A.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $176.1 million, well above the $143.9 million consensus and opposite the expected year-over-year decline: revenue instead rose 14%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 14% year-over-year to $176.1 million.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $1.77 exceeded even the preview’s $1.50+ bull-case threshold, although GAAP diluted EPS was close to consensus. The adjusted result was substantially stronger than the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income of $38.7 million ($1.77 adjusted diluted EPS).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … Adj. EPS $0.70–1.10”; “Bull … Adj. EPS $1.50+.”

surprises.description: Backlog reached $4.5 billion versus the preview’s $3.9 billion, and Centrus said financing contingencies had been removed from more than $3 billion of customer LEU and HALEU contracts. That is a larger and more de-risked backlog position than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total backlog grew to $4.5 billion extending through 2040”; “removed all financing contingencies on its more than $3 billion in customer LEU and HALEU contracts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total commercial backlog $3.9B through 2040 ($3.1B LEU, $2.4B under definitive agreement).”

surprises.description: Centrus reported new commercial HALEU arrangements: a definitive offtake contract with X-energy and an Oklo letter of intent covering up to five Aurora powerhouses, with both structured to include nondilutive prepayments. The preview’s base case anticipated no new contract news.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed a definitive HALEU offtake contract with X-energy and a letter of intent with Oklo to supply up to five Aurora powerhouses starting in 2029, both structured to include nondilutive prepayments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ‘On track,’ reiterated ranges, no change to the 2029 capacity … milestones”; “Bull: … incremental HALEU offtake named.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a steep SWU revenue decline, but the call also reported rising average SWU costs that compressed margins: SWU cost was up 13% while price rose only 3%. That cost and price mix left less margin support than the preview’s discussion of rising realized prices suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SWU revenue fell $25.7 million on a 23% volume decline, only partially offset by a 3% price increase, while average SWU cost rose 13% year-over-year, compressing SWU margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With the U.S. average SWU price at ~$108.70 (2025, +11% Y/Y) … realized price should keep climbing. The question is whether price is still outrunning the volume decline.”

surprises.description: Centrus raised its 2026 Piketon workforce addition target from over 100 to over 175 net new employees, an increase to its previously stated hiring plan that the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its 2026 Piketon workforce addition guidance from over 100 to over 175 net new employees.”

surprises.description: Centrus said it expects to complete its first centrifuge at Oak Ridge in 2026, a specific manufacturing milestone that was not highlighted in the preview’s expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects to complete its first centrifuge at the Oak Ridge facility in 2026, a first-of-a-kind U.S. manufacturing milestone toward commercial enrichment.”

surprises.description: Centrus used its ATM for $53.9 million of proceeds, whereas the preview said it had been unused as of Q1 and flagged any new capital raise as a concern. The company described the use as opportunistic and said it had sufficient funds for near-term capital requirements, tempering the dilution signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Using its ATM only opportunistically for $53.9 million in proceeds” and “sufficiently funded for near-term capital requirements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The ATM was unused as of Q1”; “any signal of a new raise is a clean negative.”

in_line: GAAP diluted EPS was $0.77 versus the preview’s $0.79 consensus estimate, essentially in line.
The $450–500 million 2026 revenue guidance was reaffirmed, as the preview’s base case expected.
Capital-spending guidance of $350–500 million was reaffirmed; the preview identified that range as the existing plan to monitor.
The SWU revenue decline was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of about a 25% Q2 decline.
The $900 million DOE task order and first new capacity targeted for 2029 were already described in the preview as signed/targeted developments.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.22, well above the preview’s $0.93 consensus, a beat of about 31% despite expectations for a year-over-year decline. The call reported a 7% year-over-year increase instead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 7% to a record $1.22.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | Q2 FY2026 consensus | $0.93” and implied “−18.4%” year over year.

surprises.description: Management raised full-year guidance above the previously unchanged ranges: the new sales range is $765M–$805M versus $750M–$795M, adjusted EBITDA is $120M–$135M versus $110M–$125M, and adjusted EPS is $2.90–$3.40 versus $2.55–$3.05. The EPS midpoint rose 12.5%, exceeding the preview’s $2.85 annual consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of $765M-$805M, adjusted EBITDA of $120M-$135M (up 8.5% at midpoint), and adjusted EPS of $2.90-$3.40 (up 12.5% at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Current (2026-05-04)” guidance: net sales “$750–795M,” adjusted EBITDA “$110–125M,” and adjusted diluted EPS “$2.55–3.05”; FY2026 annual consensus EPS was “$2.85.”

surprises.description: Work Truck Attachments sales were $129.3M, about 10% below the preview’s roughly $143M estimate. The reported 20% growth was strong, but materially slower than the preview’s implied 32.4% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Work Truck Attachments net sales jumped 20% to $129.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Work Truck Attachments sales | ~$143M” and implied “+32.4%.”

surprises.description: Work Truck Solutions sales were roughly flat at $85.3M, missing the preview’s roughly $93M estimate and expected 8% growth. Strong municipal demand offset softness in commercial operations, but did not produce the anticipated segment growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Work Truck Solutions net sales were roughly flat at $85.3 million with adjusted EBITDA of $8.8 million, as strong municipal demand offset softness in commercial operations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Work Truck Solutions sales | ~$93M” and implied “+8.0%.”

surprises.description: Municipal production bookings extended well into 2027 and backlog was near the company’s 2022 record, stronger than the preview’s already-positive description of bookings beyond 2026 and above-traditional backlog.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is “booking municipal production dates well into 2027 with backlog near its 2022 record.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “above traditional” municipal backlog with production “booked beyond 2026.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date free cash flow was negative $32.5M, down $14.6M, as inventory and receivables increased. The preview discussed capex and capital returns but did not flag this cash-flow decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow fell $14.6 million to negative $32.5 million on higher inventory and receivables.”

surprises.description: Consolidated sales came in slightly below the preview’s $216.8M consensus: $214.6M, a shortfall of about 1%, despite reaching a record and growing 10%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 net sales increased 10% to a record $214.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2 FY2026 consensus | $216.8M.”

in_line: Preseason Work Truck Attachments shipments split roughly 50-50 between Q2 and Q3, matching the preview’s expectation of an approximately 50/50 split rather than last year’s 60/40 Q2-heavy split.

The new Missouri facility was operational and added roughly 10% municipal capacity, broadly matching the preview’s expectation that the Henderson upfit center would begin production around midyear and add about 8–10% capacity.
Work Truck Attachments margin pressure associated with the Benco Ventura acquisition was anticipated as a watch item; the call attributed the decline in its 27.7% margin partly to the acquisition.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $56.2 million, well above the preview’s $51.5 million anchor and even its $53.5–55 million bull range. Sales also grew 1.6% year over year rather than declining as consensus expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 sales rose just 1.6% year-over-year to $56.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My anchor is $51.5M”; the bull scenario projected “$53.5–55M,” while consensus was “$51.54M (–6.6% YoY).”

surprises.description: Adventure sales fell 11.9%, substantially less than the preview’s roughly 21.5% decline estimate and the market concern about a 30% decline in Australian demand. That makes the segment’s Q2 performance more resilient than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adventure down 11.9% due to weakness in North American and Australian wholesale markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base-case build expected Adventure “–21.5%”; the preview said retail partners signaled “–30% YoY demand” and that anything better than “~–20%” would be a positive surprise.

surprises.description: Outdoor sales grew 8.5%, far stronger than the preview’s roughly flat base case and its bull case of about 3% growth. This was a much stronger result from the company’s expected growth engine.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Outdoor up 8.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base-case segment build expected Outdoor “+0.3% YoY”; the bull scenario assumed “Outdoor +3%.”

surprises.description: Underlying consolidated gross margin was 38%, above the preview’s roughly 37% estimate, even excluding the one-time tariff refund. The reported 48.9% margin was much higher, but the call attributed much of that headline figure to the $6.1 million refund; the preview had already flagged the refund as a possible upside item.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the tariff refund, consolidated gross margin was 38%”; reported gross margin was “48.9% versus 35.6% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at “~37%” and said “37%+ would be an impressive tell”; it also flagged “recognition of the $6.2M IEEPA tariff refund” as a possible bull-case driver.

surprises.description: Adventure margin expanded 420 basis points to 41.5% despite the segment’s sales decline. The preview highlighted the risk of margin pressure from Adventure volume deleverage, so the improvement and the accompanying cost reductions were better than that concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adventure's gross margin expanded 420 basis points to 41.5% through pricing and cost actions, with headcount down 20% and the cost base 11% lighter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether gross margin could “hold through Adventure volume deleverage” and identified margin durability as a key watch item.

surprises.description: Black Diamond apparel grew 22.9%, ahead of the preview’s expectation of double-digit apparel growth, while clearance merchandise fell 61%. Together these figures showed a stronger full-price mix than the preview had quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Black Diamond's Apparel in-line sales grew a robust 22.9% while clearance merchandise fell 61%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “double-digit apparel growth” was expected and cited Q1 “full-price apparel +10.1%.”

surprises.description: FY adjusted EBITDA guidance jumped to $12–13 million from $3–5 million, far beyond the preview’s base case of reaffirmation and its bull-case notion of only raising the low end. The increase is substantially less indicative of recurring performance than the headline suggests: roughly $8 million came from the tariff refund and elimination of about $2 million in expected legal costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised sharply to $12-13 million from the prior $3-5 million, but roughly $8 million of the increase stems from the tariff refund and elimination of ~$2 million in expected legal expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected FY guidance of “$245–255M” revenue and reaffirmation; its bull case said “FY low end raised.” It also said roughly “$3M of legal/regulatory expense is embedded in FY26 guidance.”

surprises.description: Adventure’s FY revenue outlook is now about $68 million, below the approximately $70 million guide the preview described as already in place. The company maintained its consolidated revenue range, so this is a modest segment-level deterioration rather than a total-revenue guide cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance was maintained at $245-255 million, with Adventure now expected at ~$68 million and Outdoor at ~$182 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “FY Adventure guide was cut $80M → $70M” and expected FY26 guidance reaffirmation.

surprises.description: Cash ended at $28.9 million, above the preview’s expected Q2 landing range of $22–25 million. The balance was lower than the $36.7 million at year-end, but the cash draw was less severe than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company remains debt-free with $28.9 million in cash (down from $36.7 million at year-end).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch cash landing near “$22–25M.”

surprises.description: The strategic-review commentary was more concrete than the preview’s base case of no update: management is exploring alternatives with Jefferies, including a potential sale of all or part of the business. The preview had identified concrete process progress or a segment divestiture as a bull-case signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is exploring strategic alternatives with Jefferies, including a potential sale of all or part of the business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated review “ongoing, no update”; its bull case cited “advanced discussions,” an LOI, or a segment divestiture as concrete progress.

surprises.description: The DoJ closed its criminal investigation into Black Diamond’s avalanche-transceiver reporting, removing an overhang the preview described as unresolved and involving grand jury subpoenas and former executives named as targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The DoJ closed its criminal investigation into Black Diamond's avalanche transceiver reporting on June 4, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described an “unresolved DOJ criminal investigation” with “grand jury subpoenas and two former executives named as targets.”

in_line: FY26 revenue guidance remained at $245–255 million, as the preview’s base case expected reaffirmation.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $14.5 million, above the preview’s $12.9 million consensus and $13.1 million estimate; U.S. revenue of $12.6 million also exceeded the preview’s roughly $10.6 million model. The quarter grew about 120% year over year, versus the preview’s roughly 95–103% base-case growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue grew approximately 120% year-over-year to $14.5 million, with U.S. revenue up more than 150% to $12.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $12.9M” consensus and “My Estimate $13.1M”; the model build estimated “US ~$10.6M.”

surprises.description: Management raised 2026 revenue guidance to $62–66 million rather than reaffirming $60–64 million as the preview’s base case expected. The higher range is a modest positive versus that expectation, though its midpoint is close to the preview’s $62.2 million FY consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full year 2026 global net revenue guidance to $62-66 million from $60-64 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirm at $60–64M is table stakes”; base case: “FY guide reaffirmed at $60–64M.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 59%, above the preview’s 56–57% expectation, and management raised full-year margin guidance to 58–61% from 55–58%. This was stronger than the preview’s concern that lower-margin Europe mix could cause margin deceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 59% in Q2… the strongest organic margin in company history,” prompting a full-year guidance increase “to 58-61% from 55-58%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 gross margin estimate: “57%”; the preview’s base case expected “GM 56–57%,” and the existing FY guide was “55–58%.”

surprises.description: The loss was worse than expected despite the revenue beat: GAAP EPS was $(0.63) versus the preview’s $(0.55) consensus and $(0.56) estimate. The call attributed the wider loss to SG&A of $32.9 million after commercialization moved in-house from Ascensia.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $36.7 million ($0.63 per share) from $14.5 million ($0.36 per share) a year ago, driven by SG&A rising to $32.9 million from $9.7 million after bringing commercialization in-house from Ascensia.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) $(0.55)” consensus and “My Estimate $(0.56)”; the preview also estimated SG&A of “$30.5M.”

surprises.description: The European transition did not close in Q2 as the preview expected, and outside-U.S. revenue was only $1.9 million versus the preview’s roughly $2.5 million model. Management attributed the weakness to delayed European tender updates following a later-than-planned Ascensia transition, while saying the shortfall would shift into Q3 and Q4 and Europe would remain about 20% of full-year revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Outside-U.S. revenue grew only about 12% to $1.9 million due to delayed European tender updates from the later-than-planned Ascensia transition,” with the shortfall “shifting into Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the transition was “guided to close in Q2 2026” and its model estimated “OUS ~$2.5M.”

surprises.description: The Eon Care network was already above 90 nurses and handling about 40% of U.S. insertions, with management expecting it to exceed half by year-end. The preview did not flag this network’s progress as a key metric; the call said the provider count was ahead of the company’s 100-by-year-end goal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Eon Care network added 28 providers to exceed 90 nurses (ahead of its 100 by year-end goal), now performs about 40% of all U.S. Eversense insertions, and is expected to exceed half by year-end.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed animal testing with 100% Bluetooth success within 8 feet for Freedom, a technical result not anticipated in the preview. Freedom’s first-in-human study remains planned for later this year, broadly matching the preview’s timing expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Freedom's first in-human study is planned for later this year, supported by animal data showing 100% Bluetooth success within 8 feet.”

in_line: About 60% of new-patient growth came through DTC, matching the preview’s expectation that roughly 60% of new patients would be DTC.
Freedom’s first-in-human study remains planned for later this year, broadly in line with the preview’s H2 2026 expectation.
The reported $90 million of net equity proceeds was broadly consistent with the preview’s estimate of roughly $85 million in offering proceeds.

surprises.description: KVH ended the quarter with approximately 10,700 subscribing vessels, above the preview’s expected range of 10,300–10,600. The more than 1,000 net additions also show strong conversion to subscribers despite terminal shipments falling from Q1’s record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added over 1,000 net subscribing vessels in the quarter, ending with approximately 10,700, an 11% sequential increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Look for ~10,300–10,600 vessels.”

surprises.description: Ending cash was $57.7 million, above the preview’s estimated $50–54 million. Cash fell only $1.4 million, with the decline primarily attributed to stock repurchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ending cash balance fell $1.4 million to $57.7 million, primarily due to $2.3 million in stock repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash … Q2’26E … ~$50–54” and “Cash at 6/30 is the tell on how much of that $45M remains to be funded.”

surprises.description: KVH said its GEO/VSAT bandwidth commitments predominantly expire at the end of 2026, with only a small commitment remaining in 2027. The preview focused on LEO-related margin pressure and VSAT churn but did not flag this near-term reduction in legacy bandwidth exposure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's GEO/VSAT bandwidth commitments predominantly expire at the end of 2026, with only a small remaining commitment in 2027, de-risking future margin exposure as LEO grows.”

surprises.description: LEO connectivity reached 55% of airtime revenue, above the preview’s expectation that the mix would cross roughly 50%. Management also described Starlink as its fastest-growing segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LEO connectivity now accounts for 55% of airtime revenue, with growth driven by Starlink, which management called their fastest-growing segment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “LEO mix crossing ~50% of airtime.”

surprises.description: The land-based Starlink initiative had grown to approximately 1,600 sites, adding roughly 500 in the quarter and broadening recurring revenue beyond maritime. The preview discussed other expansion and commercial traction but did not anticipate this scale of land-based activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The land-based Starlink initiative grew to approximately 1,600 sites, an increase of roughly 500 during the quarter, broadening the recurring revenue base beyond maritime.”

surprises.description: Managed IT and cybersecurity services began converting from pilots into recurring revenue, providing concrete monetization progress beyond the preview’s general watch for commercial traction. KVH also launched multi-network plans and put Link streaming into beta, developments the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New multi-network service plans (spanning Starlink, OneWeb, and VSAT) launched this quarter, while Link streaming entered beta trials and managed IT/cybersecurity services began converting from pilots into recurring revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “managed IT / CommBox commercial traction” as a narrative watch and mentioned the “vessel-based managed IT launch.”

surprises.description: KVH said it expects to complete and conclude the full $15 million buyback authorization within the current month. The preview did not discuss this accelerated completion timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The full $15 million buyback authorization is expected to be completed and concluded within the current month.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $33.7 million, matching the preview’s $33.7 million consensus estimate.
Service revenue was $29.7 million, matching the preview’s Q2 model estimate.
Service gross margin improved to 36%, within the preview’s 35–36% base-case expectation.
Adjusted EBITDA was $3.0 million, within the preview’s $3.0–$3.4 million base-case scenario range.

surprises.description: Q2 consolidated EPS was reported at $2.19, well above the preview’s $1.27 adjusted-EPS consensus and the company’s previously stated adjusted-EPS floor of $1.25. The supplied call facts do not specify whether the $2.19 uses the same adjusted basis, so the comparison is not strictly like-for-like.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated EPS of $2.19” on Q2 pretax income of $64.5 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS **$1.27**”; company guidance was “Adj. EPS **≥ $1.25**.”

surprises.description: Management assumed Q3 fuel of $3.80 per gallon and Q4 fuel of $3.70, substantially below the preview’s fuel-risk framing around Q2’s roughly $4.20 realized price and its bear case of Q3 fuel at $4.50 or higher. Alongside those assumptions, management guided to full-year 2026 EPS above $6.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guided full-year 2026 consolidated EPS of greater than $6,” assuming “fuel of $3.80/gallon in Q3 and $3.70/gallon in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Q3 fuel the “single largest swing factor,” noted Q2 realized “~$4.20/gal,” and described a bear case with “Q3 fuel guided ≥$4.50.”

surprises.description: Despite the lower-than-feared fuel assumptions, the company guided to a Q3 loss of about $0.50 per share and only a 2% operating margin at the midpoint. The preview emphasized the Q3 guide but did not provide a numerical Q3 EPS forecast, so the loss is a newly disclosed weak outlook rather than a miss against a stated consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for a consolidated loss of approximately $0.50 per share and a 2% operating margin at the midpoint.”

surprises.description: The preview already flagged elevated unit costs, citing Q1 CASM ex-fuel growth of 7.1%, but the call indicated a sharper near-term increase: legacy Allegiant nonfuel unit costs are expected up 9–10%, and consolidated nonfuel CASM ex-cargo up 10–12% in Q3, its year-over-year peak.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy Allegiant nonfuel unit costs expected up 9-10% and consolidated nonfuel CASM ex-cargo up 10-12% in Q3, marking the peak year-over-year CASM ex increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 CASM ex-fuel was “8.64¢, +7.1% YoY — already running hot” and flagged CASM ex-fuel as a key item to watch.

surprises.description: The company announced a $275 million pilot retention bonus payable from cash in the coming weeks, with management expecting net leverage to reach its peak after the payment. The preview discussed liquidity and leverage but did not anticipate this large cash outlay.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pay a pilot retention bonus of approximately $275 million (including payroll taxes) from cash on hand,” expected “to push net leverage to its peak from the current 2.6x pro forma level.”

surprises.description: The preview’s FY aircraft CapEx guide was $570–590 million, but management raised full-year 2026 CapEx to about $850 million and expects roughly 20 additional MAX aircraft in 2027. The higher investment plan is a substantial step-up from the preview’s stated baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 CapEx raised to approximately $850 million”; the MAX fleet is expected to grow by “~20 aircraft in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY aircraft capex guide **$570–590M**.”

surprises.description: Sun Country faced elevated junior-pilot attrition in Minneapolis–St. Paul because the largest Twin Cities carrier was hiring more pilots, leading to a temporary reduction in off-peak MSP capacity in the second half. The preview did not flag this staffing and capacity issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sun Country experienced elevated junior pilot attrition in Minneapolis-St. Paul driven by increased hiring at the largest Twin Cities carrier, prompting a temporary reduction of off-peak MSP capacity in the back half of the year.”

surprises.description: The preview said investors wanted a quantified first-year synergy tranche, but management only reiterated confidence in at least $140 million of run-rate synergies by 2029. The long-term target matched the preview; the lack of a first-year amount left the requested near-term detail undisclosed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reiterated confidence in at least $140 million in run-rate Sun Country synergies by 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for a “quantified first-year tranche” and that investors wanted “a number and a bridge, not a reaffirmation.”

surprises.description: The new Expedia partnership was already live across the company and generating bookings, with more than half from net-new customers—an early customer-acquisition result the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly launched Expedia partnership went 100% live on July 10 and already accounts for approximately 3% of bookings, with more than half coming from net-new customers.”

surprises.description: Cobrand card remuneration grew 24% year over year, and management set a goal of doubling its share of revenue from 5% to 10%. The preview did not flag this revenue stream or the stated growth target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cobrand card remuneration rose 24% year-over-year toward a goal of doubling from 5% to 10% of revenue.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed at least $140 million in Sun Country annual run-rate synergies by 2029, consistent with the preview’s $140 million target within three years.
The company provided the single operating certificate timing the preview asked investors to watch for, targeting the first half of 2028.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $321 million, about 3.7% above the preview’s roughly $309.4–$309.7 million consensus, with growth of 8% in constant currency versus the preview’s implied 5.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue rose 9.2% to $321 million (8% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenues: $309.4M – $309.7M”; “Implied Y/Y: +5.2%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $166 million, above the preview’s modeled $158–$161 million. The 51.6% margin, however, was in line with the preview’s model.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 10% to $166 million with margins expanding 36 basis points to 51.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: *not published* — model ~$158–161M”; the model table estimated “~$160M (51.6%).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.26, above the preview’s approximately $0.24 estimate. The company also raised the lower end of its full-year adjusted EPS range by $0.02, while leaving the upper end unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 30% year-over-year to $0.26, and the company raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $0.95-$1.01 from $0.93-$1.01.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: ~$0.24 ($0.2389)”; the preview listed FY26 adjusted EPS guidance of “$0.93–1.01.”

surprises.description: The full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised rather than reaffirmed: both ranges increased by 25 basis points. The preview considered a raise constructive, but its base case was reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 outlook,” with constant-currency revenue growth of 5.25% to 6.75% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 5.75% to 7.25%, “a 25 basis point increase to both from prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance verb: ‘reaffirm’ vs. ‘raise/narrow up’”; the preview’s base case was “FY reaffirmed,” while its bull case expected “FY guide raised or narrowed to upper half.”

surprises.description: Nordion’s 16.7% constant-currency growth was far above the preview’s low-single-digit expectation and its roughly $43 million model. The strength was partly timing-related: second-half shipments shifted into Q2, leaving tougher comparisons later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nordion posted 16.7% constant currency revenue growth,” but “first-half revenue exceeded the guided 40%-45% of full-year range as second-half shipments shifted into Q2, implying tougher second-half comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Nordion’s FY guide as “low-to-mid single digits cc” and modeled Q2 revenue of “$43M” with “+1.4%” year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: Nelson Labs returned to growth more strongly than the preview’s expectation of a slight return to growth: constant-currency revenue rose 5.4%. Its 32.4% margin was around the preview’s modeled 32.2%, and the year-over-year margin decline was anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nelson Labs exceeded expectations with 5.4% constant currency revenue growth and improved segment margin 438 basis points sequentially to 32.4%, though margins declined year-over-year due to higher costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected a “slight return to growth” in Q2 and modeled a 32.2% segment margin; it also warned that a decent quarter would “likely show segment margin down Y/Y against 34.2%.”

surprises.description: Net leverage reached 3.0x, better than the preview’s starting point of 3.2x and the expected deleveraging path, putting the company at the upper end of its long-term target range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage ratio improved to 3x, reaching the company's long-term target range of 2-3x, with roughly $950 million of liquidity and nothing drawn on the revolver.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 net leverage was “3.2x” and described Q2 as a chance for “a clean cash quarter to keep the 3.2x → deleveraging narrative alive.”

surprises.description: Borrowing costs fell more than the preview’s interest-cost discussion implied, and the interest expense outlook narrowed to a lower ceiling. Repricing the term loan by 100 basis points in under a year helped drive the improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interest expense fell over $6 million to $34 million after repricing lowered borrowing costs on the $1.4 billion term loan by 100 basis points in under a year,” and the outlook narrowed to “$135-$142 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited annual interest expense of “~$135–145M/yr guided.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its capital expenditure range and restarted a previously paused greenfield project, rather than keeping the investment plan at the preview’s stated range. Management also said capex should step down meaningfully in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new X-ray facility begins generating revenue in Q3 and a previously paused second greenfield project is now fully underway,” with full-year CapEx guidance of “$200-$225 million” and “a meaningful step down expected in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed capex guidance of “$175–225M” and noted that capacity/emissions-control capex was proceeding “regardless of regulatory uncertainty.”

surprises.description: The New Mexico EO litigation was resolved for an immaterial amount, a case outcome not discussed in the preview. Other EO matters remain outstanding, with a Georgia appellate ruling awaited and the California trial expected in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management resolved the New Mexico EO litigation in July for an immaterial amount, awaits a spring/summer appellate ruling in Georgia, and expects the California trial in January or April 2027.”

in_line: Sterigenics’ 7% constant-currency growth met the preview’s expectation of roughly 6–7% and cleared its key threshold of at least 6% against the tough comparable.

Sterigenics’ pricing and volume/mix both contributed to growth, consistent with the preview’s focus on the price-versus-volume split; its 4.3% pricing was only modestly above the preview’s cited high end of 3–4%.
Nelson Labs’ year-over-year margin decline was anticipated against the prior-year 34.2% margin and higher costs, even though its revenue growth exceeded the preview’s expectation.

surprises.description: Ouster reported $55 million of Q2 revenue, above the preview’s $51.6–51.9 million consensus and the $52.5 million top of company guidance. That is a clear beat, though it was also within the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 revenue of $55 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus: $51.6–51.9M”; company guidance “$49.5–52.5M”; the preview’s bull case was “$54–56M.”

surprises.description: The 49% GAAP gross margin looks substantially better than expected, but a one-time refund added roughly 1,000 basis points; normalized margin was only in the high-30s, below the preview’s 42–44% buy-side expectation. The headline beat therefore masks weaker underlying margin than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin was 49%, but included a one-time refund benefit of roughly 1,000 basis points, meaning normalized gross margin was in the high-30s”; management reaffirmed a “35%-40% long-term range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP gross margin: ~42–44% (buy-side).”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance has a $56 million midpoint, within the preview’s $55–58 million buy-side anchor, but its $54.5 million low end falls below that range. Management also said upside flexibility is limited because output is constrained to protect backlog, making the outlook less open-ended than the midpoint alone suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance is $54.5 million to $57.5 million” and “limited upside flexibility since output is constrained to protect backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Q3 buy-side anchor was “$55–58M”; the preview also called for a guide “≥$56M” as a catalyst threshold.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $4 million, better than the preview’s expected loss of roughly $5–7 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was negative $4 million, a roughly $1 million improvement versus Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~–$5 to –$7M (buy-side).”

surprises.description: Operating expenses rose about 10% year over year, faster than the preview’s expected opex-growth framework of less than 5–8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP operating expenses rose about 10% year-over-year to $47 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case described “reaffirmation of the … <5–8% opex growth framework.”

surprises.description: Rev8 had meaningful commercial validation, including multiple million-dollar-plus Fortune 500 orders and a statewide Utah DOT deployment, but contributed only minor prototype sales in Q2 and production volumes are not expected until the end of Q3. That gives investors sizable orders, but not the near-term realized revenue the preview said the market needed to see.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rev8 contributed only minor prototype sales in Q2, with production volumes expected by the end of Q3”; it “already secured multiple million-dollar-plus orders from Fortune 500 customers, plus a Utah DOT order covering several hundred intersections statewide.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market now needed “dollars, not logos” and described “design wins with no revenue attached” as the disappointment case.

surprises.description: The company ended Q2 with substantially more cash than the preview’s Q1-based liquidity estimate implied, but also disclosed a further $98 million of ATM proceeds and about 72 million shares outstanding—more dilution than the preview’s modeled July offering alone. Management’s statement that no more capital is expected to be needed is consistent with the preview’s expectation that the financing removed near-term funding risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ouster ended Q2 with $263 million in cash and no debt (including ~$98 million from ATM),” raised “an additional ~$191 million net in a July 6 stock offering,” and had “~72 million shares outstanding.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$175M including short-term investments” at Q1 and an expected “~$191.9M net” July raise, with “3.62M shares,” producing “roughly $360M+” pro forma liquidity.

in_line: Full-year expectations were unchanged, consistent with the preview’s base case of a reaffirmed framework.
Management reaffirmed the 35–40% long-term gross-margin range, which the preview already identified as the company’s target.
Management said it does not expect to need additional capital for its operating plan on the path to profitability, consistent with the preview’s view that the July financing removed financing risk.

surprises.description: Strata raised 2026 revenue guidance to $285–295 million from $260–275 million, putting even the new low end above the preview’s cited $275.8 million consensus. It also raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to $33–35 million from $29–33 million, a stronger increase than the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Strata raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $285-295 million from $260-275 million previously, and increased adjusted EBITDA guidance to $33-35 million from $29-33 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue consensus of ~$273–276M sits at or above the top end of management's own $260–275M guide”; the bull case anticipated a raise to “~$270–285M / EBITDA $31–34M.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $72.5 million, above the preview’s $68–70 million management-framework range and roughly $69.5 million base case. Gross profit of $15.2 million also exceeded the preview’s approximately $14.6 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue grew 60.7% year-over-year to $72.5 million”; “gross profit [was] up 68.9% to $15.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue (mgmt framework) | ~$68–70M”; the model lists Q2 revenue of “~$69.5” and gross profit of “~$14.6.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $7.9 million with a 10.9% margin, above the preview’s roughly $7.0 million and 10.1% base case. The result also cleared the preview’s $7.0 million catalyst threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $7.9 million in Q2 2026 from $6.4 million in Q1, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 140 basis points to 10.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “~$7.0M (10.1%)” and its catalyst checklist called for “Adj. EBITDA ≥ $7.0M.”

surprises.description: Clinical revenue reached $24.3 million, well above the preview’s $21.2 million estimate. Growth was 15.1% sequentially even excluding acquisitions, while transplant clinical revenue grew 23.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clinical revenue rose 22.6% sequentially to $24.3 million (15.1% excluding Q2 acquisitions), led by 23.8% growth in transplant clinical revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 model estimated Clinical revenue at “~21.2”; it also flagged clinical momentum and transplant growth as key metrics to watch.

surprises.description: Logistics gross margin fell to 18.4%, below the preview’s roughly 20% expectation and management’s prior outlook for margins to remain in the 20% range. Management now expects only 18.5–20% in the second half and a return to 20% in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Logistics gross margin fell to 18.4% in Q2 2026 versus 19.3% in Q1 and a 20% expectation, with management guiding to 18.5-20% for the second half and a return to 20% in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 Logistics gross margin at “~20.0%” and said management had guided margins to “remain in the 20% range” for the rest of 2026.

surprises.description: Logistics faces an unanticipated customer-related revenue headwind: one nonexclusive customer cut flying for an organ type, with the full impact expected in Q3. Strata now expects Q3 Logistics revenue to fall high single digits sequentially, rather than the preview’s roughly flat sequential estimate, before recovering by Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Logistics faces a roughly 3% revenue headwind from one nonexclusive customer that reduced flying for one organ type starting in June, expected to fully hit in Q3 before recovering by Q4”; Q3 Logistics revenue is expected “to decline high single digits sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said its framework implied “Logistics roughly flat sequentially at ~$48M” and highlighted Logistics organic revenue as a key question.

surprises.description: Strata completed three clinical bolt-on acquisitions year-to-date, adding over $20 million of revenue and $6.3 million of projected annualized adjusted EBITDA at mid-single-digit multiples. That is more concrete and greater realized acquisition contribution than the preview’s description of an active pipeline capable of adding low-single-digit millions of adjusted EBITDA annually.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed three bolt-on clinical acquisitions year-to-date at mid-single-digit multiples, adding over $20 million of revenue and $6.3 million of projected annualized adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described an “active tuck-in M&A pipeline” capable of “low single digit millions of adjusted EBITDA annually.”

surprises.description: Management expects higher-margin Clinical to rise to roughly 40% of revenue and nearly 50% of gross profit in the second half. The preview anticipated Clinical growth, but did not indicate this degree of expected mix shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The business mix is shifting toward higher-margin clinical, expected to reach roughly 40% of revenue and nearly 50% of gross profit in the second half, up from 30% and 35% respectively in Q1 2026.”

surprises.description: The call indicated that a $17.5 million performance earn-out is expected to be received in full by year-end, adding near-term certainty and timing detail not specified in the preview’s discussion of earn-out payments extending through March 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company anticipates a $17.5 million performance earn-out to be received in full by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “up to $45M in Joby earnout payments through March 2027,” without specifying this $17.5 million amount or a full receipt by year-end.

surprises.description: CareCloud’s adjusted EBITDA was $5.9 million, below the preview’s $6.8–7.0 million base case and below its $6.8 million credibility threshold. The company nevertheless reaffirmed its full-year EBITDA range, leaving a steeper second-half ramp than the preview already viewed as demanding.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to $5.9 million.” Management “reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance” of $29–31 million adjusted EBITDA, implying a materially stronger second half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My base case has Q2 at $6.8–7.0M”; “Adjusted EBITDA ≥ ~$6.8M” was the catalyst threshold, and “Anything with a ‘5-handle’ makes the full-year EBITDA guide arithmetically very hard.”

surprises.description: R&D expense more than doubled because CareCloud began expensing AI development instead of capitalizing it. The preview wanted hard AI monetization metrics but did not anticipate this near-term earnings pressure from the accounting treatment of development costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expense more than doubled as the company shifted AI development to current expense rather than capitalizing it, pressuring near-term earnings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bar is now customers, ARR, or pricing disclosure — not another TAM slide.”

surprises.description: CareCloud reported $13.4 million of cash, well above the $3.4 million Q1-end balance that framed the preview’s liquidity concern. However, net working capital was only $695,000, so the reported cash improvement came alongside a still-thin working-capital position.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with about $13.4 million in cash and net working capital of only $695,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash was $3.4M at Q1-end” and the preview flagged liquidity, cash balance, and FCF as items to watch.

surprises.description: The recurring technology-enabled business solutions mix reached about 75% of revenue, versus 69% a year earlier, and totaled $24 million. That is a favorable mix update against the preview’s concern about whether organic growth could hold up, although the call facts do not separate acquisition-driven growth from organic growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring technology-enabled business solutions rose to approximately 75% of revenue this quarter, up from 69% a year ago, reaching $24 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “whether that services erosion stabilizes determines whether H2 organic growth exists” and flagged “organic growth disclosure” as important.

surprises.description: CareCloud added that Empower’s president had historically referred business now representing about 10% of CareCloud’s annualized revenue. The preview expected Empower to be immaterial near term and identified cross-selling as a possible catalyst, but did not give this scale for the existing referral relationship.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Empower's president Mitchell Brey has historically referred business now representing approximately 10% of CareCloud's annualized revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Closed May 22, 2026; management said not material to FY2026. Any framing of it as a growth driver should be discounted; the compliance SaaS launch is a 2H26 event.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $31.9 million, essentially in line with the preview’s $31.85 million consensus estimate and within its $31.8–32.3 million base-case range.
Management reaffirmed all three FY2026 guidance ranges—$128–132 million revenue, $29–31 million adjusted EBITDA, and $0.20–0.23 GAAP EPS—as the preview’s base case expected.
GAAP net income fell year over year, as the preview cautioned that the preferred-stock redemption and financing change would make the comparison noisy and that GAAP net income could look worse.
The Series B preferred stock redemption using debt and with zero dilution was already described in the preview; the reported redemption and elimination of preferred dividends were not a new surprise.

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 73.6%, well above the preview’s 66–69% estimate and the prior record, rather than merely holding around the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached a company record of 73.6%, improving 510 basis points sequentially and 810 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … My estimate: 66–69%.”

surprises.description: The cash position was slightly below the preview’s estimate, but the more notable difference was management’s warning that $5.1 million would fund operations for only at least nine months—shorter than the preview’s base-case expectation of runway into Q3 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $5.1 million in cash, which management expects to fund operations for only at least the next 9 months”; Q2 cash usage was “approximately $1.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash (6/30/26) … My estimate: $5.2–5.5M”; the base case expected “runway into Q3 2027 reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Momentum continued after quarter-end: July e-commerce and subscription revenue both set new monthly records, an additional positive update beyond the preview’s focus on the Q2 print and pre-announced growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July results showed continued momentum with record e-commerce revenue of $245,000 (up 19% from June) and record subscription revenue of $52,000 (up 22% from June).”

in_line: Total Q2 revenue of $770,000 was within the preview’s $0.75–0.80 million estimate and above its $689,000 record-level bar; the preview had already said the revenue beat was largely pre-confirmed.
E-commerce revenue of $511,000 was close to the preview’s reverse-engineered estimate of about $500,000, and its 186% sequential growth had already been pre-announced.
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.4 million was at the favorable end of the preview’s $1.4–1.6 million expected range.
Subscriber growth was broadly in line with the preview’s pre-release note that the active online subscriber base had more than doubled sequentially.

surprises.description: Total revenue was $218 million, below the preview’s $221.9–$224.5 million consensus range and its $223 million base model. The shortfall was modest, but the headline print missed expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total net product revenue reached $218 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $221.9M – $224.5M”; “My Q2'26 build… Total revenue $223M.”

surprises.description: SG&A jumped to $208.1 million, well above the preview’s $193 million model and its expectation that spending at or below roughly $195 million would validate the guide. Management expects SG&A to plateau at this higher level for the rest of the year, rather than at the lower level investors were modeling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A surging to $208.1 million from $130.3 million a year earlier”; management “guided that SG&A should plateau at the Q2 level of ~$208 million for the rest of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “SG&A $193M,” said “Anything at or below ~$195M validates the guide,” and flagged “$205M+” as breaking the operating-leverage story.

surprises.description: SYMBRAVO revenue was far below the preview’s $6 million estimate: sales were $2.3 million, with gross-to-net discounts rising into the high 80% range rather than remaining in the expected high-70% range. Demand nevertheless increased sequentially, so the revenue miss came alongside worse-than-expected discounting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SYMBRAVO net sales fell to $2.3 million… as gross-to-net discounts deviated into the high 80% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “SYMBRAVO $6M” and said discounts were “elevated in the high-70% range.”

surprises.description: Auvelity prescriptions reached about 266,000, above the preview’s watchpoint of the mid-240,000s or better. The strong prescription growth contrasts with Auvelity sales of $180.3 million, slightly below the preview’s $183 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total prescriptions of ~266,000 (up 34% YoY)”; Auvelity sales were “$180.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for sequential TRx acceleration into the mid-240Ks or better” and modeled “AUVELITY $183M.”

surprises.description: The early Alzheimer’s agitation launch showed a quantified acceleration among older patients: new-to-brand prescriptions for patients 65 and older rose 126% versus the prior quarter’s comparable eight-week period. The preview expected qualitative launch color and sought quantified ADA metrics, but had no comparable growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In the first 8 weeks of the Alzheimer's disease agitation launch, new-to-brand prescriptions among patients 65 and older rose 126% versus the same period in the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to expect management to discuss launch activity and listed “first quantified ADA launch metrics” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter at about $320 million, above the preview’s expected $255–$270 million range. Management also reiterated that the balance should fund operations into cash-flow positivity without additional financing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Axsome ended the quarter with ~$320 million in cash, which management expects is sufficient to fund operations into cash flow positivity without additional financing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “cash ~$255–270M” and said a balance near or below ~$250 million could revive dilution concerns.

surprises.description: R&D expense was $46.2 million, below the preview’s $58 million model. That is a meaningful underspend relative to expectations, even though management expects R&D to rise going forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D declined to $46.2 million”; management guided that “R&D rises” after Q2.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “R&D $58M.”

surprises.description: Management described a goal of roughly one NDA filing per year through 2030, adding a specific filing cadence to the pipeline outlook that the preview did not set out.
surprises.fact_evidence: The pipeline was described as “targeting roughly one NDA filing per year through 2030.”

in_line: EPS was $0.99 per share in losses, at the lower end of the preview’s stated $0.85–$0.99 loss consensus range.
The FDA acceptance of the AXS-12 NDA and May 1, 2027 PDUFA date matched the preview’s pipeline expectation.
ENGAGE top-line results expected in Q4 2026 were consistent with the preview’s 2H26 timing expectation.

The preview anticipated improved Auvelity access and highlighted Medicare coverage; reported access was about 89% of total lives, with roughly 100% government coverage and 100% Medicare coverage for Alzheimer’s agitation.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $4.3 million, well below the preview’s $5.2 million company guide and $4.85 million consensus, and it declined 2% year over year rather than delivering the expected return to growth. Sequential growth was only 3%, versus the roughly 15%–24% implied by the preview’s estimates and guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $4.3 million, down 2% year-over-year but up 3% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue: ~$5.2M” and “Revenue $4.85M”; the preview also says a $5.2M quarter would mark “first year-over-year revenue growth in years.”

surprises.description: The anticipated Q2 non-GAAP net loss was about $0.42 million, but the reported loss was $0.989 million—more than twice the preview’s base estimate. The preview’s modeled Q2 opex was also slightly below the reported $4.4 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net loss narrowed to $989,000”; “Non-GAAP operating expenses fell 26% year-over-year to $4.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “Non-GAAP net loss” of “-$0.42M” and modeled non-GAAP opex of “~$4.28M.”

surprises.description: The new carrier deployment expected by the end of Q2 had not launched by quarter-end; management instead expected two customer launches by the end of August. The timing is later than anticipated, although both customers had fully executed contracts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to launch two new customers by month-end”—one SafePath OS device deployment and one SafePath Connect deployment in Europe—“both with fully executed contracts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says the Q1-signed carrier’s “delivery [was] expected by end of Q2” and identifies whether it “actually went into revenue” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Management expects non-GAAP operating expenses to rise by as much as 6% sequentially in Q3 to add engineering headcount. That is a shift away from the cost-reduction trajectory the preview was looking to confirm, though the added spending is intended to support the pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to a sequential increase of up to 6% in Q3 to add engineering headcount to support the pipeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says to “confirm the 8%–11% sequential decline” in non-GAAP opex and asks whether cuts have gone so deep that they impair delivery.

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was higher than the preview’s roughly $2.0 million estimate, at $2.8 million. That is a favorable balance-sheet difference, although the reported amount remains limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company held only $2.8 million in cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “Cash (period end) … ~$2.0M.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a significant multi-year extension with an existing Tier 1 customer that was close to signing and expected to drive revenue growth beginning in Q3. The preview highlighted customer concentration risk but did not anticipate this specific extension.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A significant multi-year contract extension with an existing Tier 1 customer is within days of signing and is expected to generate revenue growth beginning in Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flags that three customers represented “~99% of the business” and says any hint of “churn or renegotiation” at the largest account is a key risk.

surprises.description: The SafePath SDK/API opportunity had advanced beyond general positioning: management described one contract as near signing, alongside additional opportunities and a growing senior-focused pipeline. The preview specifically left open whether the offering would convert into pipeline or remain positioning.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New SafePath SDK/API offerings targeting carrier ‘super apps’ reaching tens of millions of subscribers are described as a high-margin future growth driver, with one contract near signing and additional opportunities including a growing senior-focused pipeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says to look for whether the SDK/API expansion “has produced pipeline conversion or is still positioning.”

in_line: Q2 gross margin was 81.3%, within the preview’s 81%–83% guidance range.
GAAP net loss was $2.7 million, close to the preview’s approximately $2.75 million estimate; the reported $0.52 loss per share was also close to its -$0.50 estimate.
Q3 revenue guidance of $5.0–$5.4 million implies sequential growth, meeting the preview’s key test that a second consecutive quarter of sequential growth be guided.
The June warrant inducement raised $1.6 million, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: UHAL.B earned $0.63 per share, below the preview’s roughly $0.80 base estimate and down from $0.73 a year earlier, rather than delivering the preview’s expected year-over-year growth. The preview cautioned that reported EPS consensus was unreliable, so the comparison is to its own estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings fell to $123 million ($0.63 per nonvoting share) from $142 million ($0.73 per share) a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (UHAL.B) ~ $0.80” and “Δ YoY +10%”; the preview also said to “Treat the EPS consensus as unusable.”

surprises.description: Moving and storage costs rose sharply, cutting EBITDA margin by just over 1.5%; freight and shipping costs alone were up about $22.5 million. Management expects that freight pressure to persist through the rest of the fiscal year, whereas the preview flagged U-Box freight headwinds but did not anticipate this scale or duration of the cost drag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Moving and storage operating expenses rose $55 million, cutting EBITDA margin by just over 1.5%,” including “~$22.5 million in higher freight and shipping costs”; freight pressure is “expected to peak in July and remain a headwind through the rest of the fiscal year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U-Box. Transactions and box counts up, but revenue per transaction is falling on shorter moves, freight headwinds, and competitive intensity. … Watch for margin, not just volume.”

surprises.description: Disposal results were far better than the preview’s expected roughly $15 million of losses: UHAL instead reported a $1.9 million gain. Management cautioned that the strong resale market may be temporary and could lead the company to hold retired units longer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Losses on disposal of retired rental equipment improved by $24 million year-over-year, resulting in a $1.9 million gain”; management said the strong Q1 resale market “appears temporary” and may prompt holding units longer.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “disposal losses ~$15M,” and its disposal watchpoint said “Watch for losses under ~$15M.”

surprises.description: Equipment depreciation still increased $13.5 million for the quarter, above the preview’s flat-year-over-year base expectation, so the inflection was not yet fully visible in the quarterly figure. However, only $800,000 of the increase came after April, and management expects no further per-unit increases next year, tempering the shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fleet depreciation increased $13.5 million for the quarter, but only $800,000 came after April”; management said the cargo van depreciation-driven headwinds are subsiding and “no further per-unit increases” are expected next year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed depreciation “~flat YoY” and said “Q1 depreciation growth must be near zero or negative YoY.”

surprises.description: Equipment rental revenue grew by $29 million, a little below the preview’s $1.095 billion estimate (about $37 million above the prior-year figure). Growth across both In-Town and one-way markets and July tracking in line with Q1 were constructive, but the result did not reach the preview’s growth estimate or management’s 4.5–5% target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Equipment rental revenues rose $29 million year-over-year with transaction and revenue growth across both In-Town and one-way markets, and July revenue tracked in line with Q1 results.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated equipment rental of “$1,095M” versus $1,058M a year earlier and said management was targeting “4.5–5%.”

surprises.description: The dealer and location rollout was further along than the preview’s stated one-third progress toward the independent-dealer goal: UHAL reported being roughly halfway to its goal of net-gaining 3,000 dealers, alongside 75 net new company-operated locations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added 75 net new company-operated locations and over 1,100 net independent dealers year-over-year, reaching roughly halfway toward its goal of net-gaining 3,000 independent dealers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said dealer expansion should show up in Q1 and described the company as “only one-third of the way to the dealer expansion goal.”

surprises.description: New storage customer rates rose about 2.5% while departing customer rates fell just under 2%, creating a positive spread that management described as unusual versus industry peers. That is more favorable pricing behavior than the preview’s concern about compressed street rates and the rate-versus-occupancy tradeoff suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New customer storage rental rates rose about 2.5% year-over-year while departing customer rates fell just under 2%, an unusual positive spread versus industry peers seeing move-in rates below move-out rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “street rates” as “compressed” and said to watch “whether [revenue per occupied sq ft] decelerates as the rate-vs-occupancy tradeoff bites.”

in_line: Storage same-store occupancy reached 88.3%, up from 86.1% in Q4, meeting the preview’s key test of a sequential seasonal build. It was still down 456 basis points year over year, which the call attributed to a harder line on delinquent accounts; the preview’s base case anticipated occupancy remaining down year over year while improving from Q4.

Storage revenue increased $16 million, about 7%, and average revenue per occupied foot improved over 6%, broadly in line with the preview’s $249 million storage estimate (about 6.5% growth) and its expectation that revenue per occupied foot would remain an important support.

The buyback was active rather than the zero-repurchase outcome the preview identified as disappointing: about $48 million had been repurchased through June, with roughly $50 million more bought since quarter-end. The preview’s base case expected the buyback to have started.

surprises.description: Dropbox added about 96,000 net new paying users sequentially, versus the preview’s expectation of roughly 10,000–14,000 additions and about 18.10 million users. It was also the third consecutive quarter of user growth, a much stronger confirmation of the recovery than the preview’s expected second positive quarter.
