surprises.fact_evidence: “Dropbox added approximately 96,000 net new paying users sequentially to reach 18.9 million,” marking its “third consecutive quarter of paying user growth” and “strongest gain in about three years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Paying users ~18.10M (unguided)” and “Q1 broke a multi-quarter decline with ~+10–14K net adds”; “A second consecutive positive quarter converts ‘stabilization’ into a trend.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $631.5 million, above the $625.6 million consensus and the $627 million high end of company guidance that the preview treated as the functional whisper. The beat was modest, and constant-currency growth was only 0.1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue rose 0.9% year-over-year to $631.5 million,” with growth of 1.7% excluding Form Swift and 0.1% on a constant-currency basis.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $625.6M” consensus; company guide “$624–627M”; “the high end of guide ($627M) as the whisper.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating margin reached 39.7%, above the 38.5% guide and the preview’s expected range of about 38.5%–39%. The year-over-year decline was about 180 basis points, less than the roughly 300-basis-point compression implied by the preview’s guide comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin reached 39.7%, beating guidance of 38.5%,” though it declined “roughly 180 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin ~38.5–39%”; company guide “~38.5%”; the guide “implies ~300bp of YoY compression.”

surprises.description: Dropbox raised full-year revenue guidance by $13.5 million to $2.513–$2.523 billion, putting the range above the preview’s $2.51 billion consensus and its stated $2.515 billion raise threshold. However, the increase came with only about 80 basis points of growth excluding Form Swift and was aided by a $31 million currency tailwind, so the underlying outlook remained weak.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance was raised by $13.5 million to $2.513-$2.523 billion,” implying “only about 80 basis points” of growth excluding Form Swift and “aided by a $31 million currency tailwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guide/consensus: Revenue $2.497–2.512B (cons. $2.51B)”; a raise “below ~$2.515B is a non-event”; the bull case calls for a raise “to ≥$2.515B.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year non-GAAP operating margin outlook by 50 basis points to 40.0%–40.5%, above the preview’s expected 39.5%–40.0% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 non-GAAP operating margin guidance by 50 basis points to 40.0%-40.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guide/consensus: … non-GAAP op. margin 39.5–40%.”

surprises.description: Full-year unlevered free cash flow guidance rose by $15 million to at least $1.070 billion, above the preview’s expected floor of $1.055 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “lifted unlevered free cash flow guidance by $15 million to at or above $1.070 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guide/consensus: … unlevered FCF ≥$1.055B.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell only about 60 basis points year over year to 81.6%, a narrower decline than the 180-basis-point fall the preview cited for Q1. But management said AI compute costs would create further pressure in the second half, tempering the improvement in the margin trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined about 60 basis points year-over-year to 81.6% due to compute costs from AI rollout,” with “further back-half pressure partially offset by infrastructure efficiencies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin fell 180bp YoY to 81.1%” in Q1; “The tension: is margin compression an investment cycle or structural? GM trajectory is the tell.”

surprises.description: Dropbox authorized a new $900 million share repurchase program and bought back about $315 million of shares in Q2. The new authorization was not anticipated in the preview, which highlighted concern about the pace and per-share economics of buybacks at higher prices.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a new $900 million share repurchase authorization and repurchased approximately 12.6 million shares for about $315 million in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation at 34% higher prices. Q1 retired 14.3M shares for ~$367M … Watch pace, and any commentary on leverage — the debt-funded buyback is the standing bear objection.”

surprises.description: The Simple SKU was the largest contributor to net new paying-user growth, and Teams returned to positive license growth for the first time since 2024. The preview discussed self-serve changes and Teams as possible growth drivers but did not forecast these specific results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ‘Simple’ SKU was the largest contributor to net new paying user growth, while Teams turned to positive license growth for the first time since 2024.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bull-case discussion says to watch for “Teams/self-serve pricing-and-packaging changes cited as the driver of net adds.”

surprises.description: Integrations with Claude and ChatGPT had already attracted more than 150,000 connected users despite minimal dedicated investment. This added a concrete early usage signal for the AI ecosystem, although the facts provided do not establish AI monetization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Integrations with tools like Claude and ChatGPT have already attracted over 150,000 connected users despite minimal dedicated investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said there was “still no disclosed revenue contribution” from Dash and identified pricing, packaging, attach rates, or a named enterprise SKU as the major potential upside.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $72.8M, about 8% below the $79.4M consensus; Revuforj at $55M was below the $61–62M consensus-implied level and drove the shortfall. It was, however, close to the preview’s own $73M estimate and $55.5M Revuforj estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue was $72.8 million”; “Revuforj net revenue was $55 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus total revenue of ~$79.4M therefore implies Revuforj net revenue of ~$61–62M”; the preview’s own estimates were “$73.0M” total revenue and “$55.5M” Revuforj.

surprises.description: New Revuforj patient starts fell sequentially to 250, rather than growing with the NPM1 ramp the preview anticipated. Total prescriptions still rose 15% quarter over quarter, and management called the start decline a temporary anomaly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Revuforj prescriptions were approximately 1,500 (up 15% QoQ), but new patient starts declined sequentially to 250, which management characterized as a temporary anomaly.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 was ~330 starts. NPM1 label came Oct 24, 2025 plus NCCN inclusion; that cohort should still be in steep ramp”; the preview’s base case expected starts to grow.

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter at $575M, far above the preview’s expected $305–315M, after Syndax raised $244M net from convertible notes. Management also said it remained fully funded through profitability, consistent with the preview’s runway expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $575 million in cash including $244 million net from June's $250 million 2.25% convertible notes offering, and maintains full funding through profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect ~$305–315M”; the preview also said cash above $305M and reaffirmed funding through profitability would address the financing concern.

surprises.description: The call added two Q4 pipeline events beyond the preview’s named IPF and frontline chronic GVHD readouts: a NUP98 relapsed/refractory publication and updated frontline AML trial data. These broadened the set of anticipated fourth-quarter updates, though no results were reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiple fourth-quarter catalysts are pending, including … NUP98 relapsed/refractory publication, and updated frontline AML trial data.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist named “IPF topline and frontline cGVHD” as the two 2H narrative offsets.

in_line: Revuforj’s $55M revenue and 12% quarter-over-quarter growth were close to the preview’s own $55.5M estimate and 13% growth estimate, even though they missed the consensus-implied level noted above.

The KMT2A transplant cohort was beginning to return to therapy as anticipated: 50% of patients who proceeded to transplant had resumed, up from 45% last quarter, with management still targeting 70%–80% ultimate return-to-therapy.

NPM1’s contribution was consistent with the preview’s expected steep ramp: it accounted for at least 40% of new patients and more than 30% of Revuforj revenue. The call also noted that fewer than 15% of the estimated 4,500 annual relapsed/refractory NPM1 patients had received a menin inhibitor.

Niktimvo collaboration revenue was broadly in line with the preview’s ~$17.5M implication: the call reported $18.1M, and its expected near-term margin contribution of 25%–30% was consistent with the preview’s cited 28.9% Q1 rate.
The ~$400M 2026 R&D plus SG&A guidance excluding $50M of noncash stock compensation matched the preview’s expectation; the call also reaffirmed full funding through profitability.
The Q4 Phase II IPF and frontline chronic GVHD data remained on the catalyst calendar, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Getty reported Q2 revenue of $229.1 million, down 2.5%, versus the preview’s roughly $235 million and flat-year-over-year expectation. Revenue recognition timing added about 50 basis points, so the underlying result was weaker still.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 2.5% to $229.1 million (down 4.1% currency-neutral), with results aided by roughly 50 basis points from revenue recognition timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$235M … | Implied Y/Y ~0%”; “Revenue vs. consensus is the third-most important thing in this release.”

surprises.description: Getty declined to provide any earnings guidance while evaluating its capital structure, rather than reaffirming the FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges. This also left the preview’s expected H2 margin normalization unconfirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company declined to provide any earnings guidance due to the ongoing capital structure evaluation, signaling uncertainty around its financial outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue guide | $948–988M (reaffirmed at Q1)”; “FY26 adj. EBITDA guide | $279–295M”; “CFO Jennifer Leyden said margins ‘normalize to approximately 30%’ in H2.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $62.3 million, below the preview’s $64–66 million estimate, and its 27.2% margin was below the expected 27.5–28%. The decline and margin compression reflected lower revenue and higher cost of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 8.4% to $62.3 million with margin compressing to 27.2% from 28.9%, reflecting lower revenue and higher cost of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$64–66M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~27.5–28%.”

surprises.description: Annual subscriber trends were worse than the preview’s already-negative figures: active annual subscribers were 240,000 rather than 258,000, and retention was 88.4% rather than 90%. Getty attributed the deterioration to the free-trial exit and traffic headwinds, including weaker iStock search-engine and affiliate traffic that hurt new-customer acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annual subscription revenue retention fell to 88.4% … and active annual subscribers dropped to 240,000 from 321,000”; “iStock continued to suffer from search-engine and affiliate traffic declines hurting new customer acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Active annual subscribers fell to 258K from 318K Y/Y; annual subscription retention slipped to 90% LTM from 92.7%.”

surprises.description: Getty ended Q2 with only $51.6 million of cash, down $45 million from Q1, and then drew another $30 million on its revolver in July, taking the $150 million facility to its limit. That left no remaining revolver capacity, a worse liquidity position than the preview’s pro forma estimate based on the $120 million April draw.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Getty ended Q2 with only $51.6 million of balance sheet cash (down $45 million from Q1)”; “drew an additional $30 million on its revolver, maxing out the $150 million facility to bolster liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma for redemption and the $120M April revolver draw, gross debt is roughly $1.48B and net debt ~$1.38–1.40B”; “What matters is the cash balance and undrawn revolver capacity exiting Q2.”

surprises.description: The agency business fell 13%, a steep contraction amid secular pressure and customers producing more content internally with AI. The preview discussed AI exposure in Creative, but did not anticipate or quantify this agency decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The agency business declined 13% amid secular headwinds and AI-driven internal content production.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Creative is the structurally AI-exposed segment.”

surprises.description: Despite the subscriber-base concerns highlighted in the preview, annual subscription revenue grew 7.1% and reached 58.8% of total revenue; Premium Access grew 5.5% and its customer revenue retention was near 100%. This points to resilience in subscription revenue even as subscriber counts and overall retention weakened.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annual subscription revenue grew 7.1% to 58.8% of total revenue, with Premium Access (over 40% of revenue) growing 5.5% and Premium Access customer revenue retention near 100%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscriber base erosion” was ranked as a key metric to watch, with the preview noting falling active annual subscribers and retention.

in_line: Free cash flow was deeply negative as the preview expected because of the Alta warrant litigation payment: Getty reported negative $122.6 million, driven largely by the $110.9 million judgment payment, partly offset by $31.5 million of insurance proceeds.
Getty redeemed the $628.4 million of escrowed 10.5% Senior Secured Notes at par after the merger termination, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the notes would be redeemed.

surprises.description: ACV’s adjusted EBITDA was $21 million, above the preview’s $18–20 million guidance range, and EBITDA per unit reached a record, up 11% year over year. That was a stronger result than expected against a preview that anticipated Q2 margin compression.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $21 million exceeded the high end of guidance,” and “adjusted EBITDA per unit hitting a record, up 11% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 guidance itself embeds YoY margin compression ($18–20M vs $18.6M in Q2'25)” and “Adj. EBITDA: $18–20M.”

surprises.description: Rather than showing a clear unit-growth inflection, ACV cited a 600-basis-point drag on unit growth from a buyer-seller price dislocation and a 300–350-basis-point conversion-rate contraction as macro pressure affected June and July. This is a headwind to the go-to-market-driven acceleration the preview was watching for, though the facts do not state the final unit-growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 600 basis point drag on unit growth resulted from a price dislocation between sellers and buyers, driving a 300-350 basis point conversion rate contraction as macro headwinds pressured June and July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The single question the market will answer tonight: did the go-to-market spend buy units?” and “Below +3% is a red flag; above +6% resets the narrative.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $214 million, below the preview’s cited consensus estimates of about $215.5 million and $219.2 million, and its +10% growth was below the preview’s implied +11% to +13%. It nevertheless landed within company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $214 million, up 10% year-over-year, landing within guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$215.5M” and “$219.2M” consensus; implied year-over-year growth of “+11% to +13%.”

surprises.description: ACV said full-year operating-expense growth would be about 6%, below the preview’s roughly 8% expectation, while still absorbing about $10 million of go-to-market investment. This implies more expense restraint and margin expansion than the preview’s baseline assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year OPEX growth is guided to ~6% … enabling ~100 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin expansion even while absorbing ~$10 million of go-to-market investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “non-GAAP opex growth ~8%” and “$11M of incremental go-to-market spend.”

surprises.description: ViPR had reached commercial availability, with more than half of the top 50 dealer groups in active conversations and management targeting 500 to potentially 1,000 units in 2027. The preview focused on 2026 deployments and did not anticipate this stated 2027 scale target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ViPR launched commercial availability with over 50% of the top 50 dealer groups in active conversations, 100+ units being built in 2026, and management targeting 500 to potentially 1,000 units in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1: 18 deployed, ~75 backlog, 60–70 more planned in 2026.”

surprises.description: Five regions where ACV had added field capacity delivered mid-teens unit growth, including one region above 30%. That is evidence of productivity from the field expansion the preview said needed to start working, even as the overall unit-growth picture faced conversion pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Five emerging regions where the company leaned into field capacity delivered mid-teens unit growth (one exceeding 30%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Requires the field-expansion hires … to be productive within one quarter.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag CFO Bill Zerella’s departure or Tim Fox’s succession as a Q2 development. The facts give no reason for the transition, so its implications are unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Bill Zerella is departing and being succeeded by Tim Fox.”

in_line: ACV reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $845–855 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $73–77 million, as the preview said a reaffirm was the minimum expected outcome.

Non-GAAP cost of revenue rose about 300 basis points year over year with a higher no-reserve sales mix, consistent with the preview’s warning that no-reserve penetration and gross-margin pressure were key issues to watch.

surprises.description: LENSAR reported Q2 revenue of $16.5 million, above the preview’s $14.65–$15.00 million consensus range and its $14.4 million base estimate. The roughly 10%–15% gap was a clear upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 18% year-over-year to $16.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $15.00M | $14.65M | $14.4M”; “I sit ~2–4% below the revenue consensus.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in at $3.6 million, far ahead of the preview’s expectation of a $0.3 million loss. This was a substantial positive gap, not merely a return to break-even.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company delivered its strongest adjusted EBITDA to date at $3.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | … | ‑$0.3M.”

surprises.description: LENSAR swung to $3.5 million of GAAP net income, while the preview expected a GAAP loss based on consensus EPS of about negative $0.17 to negative $0.21. That reversal was a sizeable upside surprise, although the preview cautioned that GAAP EPS could be misleading.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Swung to GAAP net income of $3.5 million versus a net loss of $1.8 million in Q2 2025.”

surprises.description: Worldwide procedure volume reached 58,682, well above the preview’s estimate of about 54,500 and the 54,000-plus level it identified as a key threshold. The actual result also showed much stronger year-over-year growth than the preview’s concern about low-single-digit growth suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Procedure volume reached 58,682, up 13% year-over-year and 8% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Procedures (WW) … ~54,500”; “procedure growth reaccelerating above ~5%”; “procedures ≥54,000.”

surprises.description: U.S. procedure share rose to 24.1%, above the preview’s 23.4% Q1 reference and its stated watchpoint of share above 23.4%. The gain was a positive development against the preview’s concern that share had been flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. procedure market share increased to 24.1% from 23.4% in Q1 and 21.4% in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. procedure market share was 23.4% at Q1, flat vs. Dec 31”; “U.S. share >23.4%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was well above the preview’s 46%–49% guided band and 48% base estimate. Even excluding the $1.1 million tariff refund, margin was about 52%, so the upside was not solely the refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin rose to approximately 59% (52% excluding a $1.1 million tariff refund benefit).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … My Base Estimate | 48%”; “Gross margin vs. the 46–49% guided band.”

surprises.description: Management warned that Q3 is historically the weakest quarter for cataract procedures because of holidays and summer vacations. The preview did not flag this seasonal caution, adding a near-term headwind to the otherwise strong procedure results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 is historically the seasonally weakest quarter for cataract procedures due to holidays and summer vacations.”

surprises.description: Management said it plans to modestly increase commercial spending and make its first-ever direct appearance at ESCRS to expand in Europe. The preview discussed rebuilding after the merger but did not anticipate this specific commercial investment or event presence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management plans to modestly increase commercial spending, including a first-ever direct presence at ESCRS in Q3 to expand in Europe.”

in_line: LENSAR placed 10 ALLY systems, within the preview’s expected range of 10–12, and its backlog of 13 was above the preview’s key threshold of 12.
Ending cash of $13.6 million was broadly in line with the preview’s expected range of about $12–13 million and above its downside threshold of $11 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $4.4 million, well below the preview’s roughly $7.0 million consensus and its $5.4 million base estimate. It also declined 12% year over year, rather than the preview’s base case of 9% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 12% year-over-year to $4.4 million from $5.0 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “~$7.0M” and a “Q2 FY26E (base)” total of “~$5.4M” with “+9% y/y.”

surprises.description: LiqTech cut its full-year 2026 revenue range to $20–23 million from $23–27 million, rather than reaffirming the range the preview identified as the primary swing factor. The company attributed the cut to a major Water for Energy project delay after the customer restarted its internal approval process.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $20-23 million after a major Water for Energy project was delayed due to a customer's organizational change that restarted its internal approval process.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “reaffirmed $23–27M twice” and framed the key question as “reaffirm, trim, or cut.”

surprises.description: Commercial Pool did achieve a record quarter, but its $1.5 million revenue was below the preview’s $1.8 million segment estimate. It met the preview’s roughly $1.5 million credibility threshold, while falling short of the modeled ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial Pool achieved record quarterly revenue of $1.5 million, nearly doubling from $0.8 million in both Q2 2025 and Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Commercial Pool at “$1.8M” for Q2, and said a result “under ~$1.5M” would break credibility on order-book conversion.

surprises.description: Gross margin was only 8.4%, far below the preview’s base expectation of 20% and even below its 15% level flagged as undermining the unit-economics story. The reported explanation—unfavorable mix and low utilization—also points to weaker fixed-cost absorption than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 8.4% from 9.8% a year earlier, remaining below the level needed to fully absorb fixed production costs, reflecting unfavorable product mix and lower manufacturing utilization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario assumed “20%” gross margin, said “>20% is on-track,” and warned that “<15% on a record pool quarter undermines the entire unit-economics story.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.6 million, substantially worse than the preview’s base estimate of negative $0.85 million and slightly worse than its negative $1.55 million bear case. The preview had no published consensus for this measure, so the gap is against its scenario estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to negative $1.6 million from negative $1.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario estimated adjusted EBITDA of “$(0.85)M” and its bear scenario “$(1.55)M.”

surprises.description: Marine revenue was $0.7 million, below the preview’s $1.0 million estimate despite year-over-year growth. The four-system China EGR order was already anticipated, so the surprise is the weaker quarterly revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marine revenue rose to $0.7 million from $0.4 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s segment build estimated Marine revenue at “$1.0M” for Q2.

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash including restricted cash reached $15.7 million, above the preview’s estimated $12–13 million pro forma balance, and the company repaid senior promissory notes and original issue discount notes. The cash comparison is approximate because the reported figure includes restricted cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A June underwritten public offering generated approximately $18 million in net proceeds, boosting cash including restricted cash to $15.7 million from $2.7 million at the end of Q1, and enabled repayment of senior promissory notes and original issue discount notes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$12–13M cash” after the offering and expected “~$4.1M” of senior-debt repayment.

in_line: Commercial Pool delivered the record quarter management had promised, reaching $1.5 million versus $0.8 million in each of the two comparison quarters.
The $2.1 million follow-on order for four steel-manufacturer wastewater systems was broadly in line with the preview’s already-reported “>$2M follow-on” for four systems.
The four-system China EGR order was already anticipated in the preview, which said the order would deliver in Q4.

surprises.description: Gran Tierra entered an agreement to sell all of its Colombia and Ecuador oil businesses, a transaction the preview did not anticipate. The sale requires special stockholder approval, and management gave no details, so its implications remain uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “entered a definitive share purchase agreement to sell all of its Colombia and Ecuador oil businesses”; the transaction requires “special stockholder approval,” and management declined to discuss details.

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was about $6 million, well below the preview’s expected $25–35 million. The preview expected a strongly positive quarter, while reported capex was also higher than modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was approximately $6 million,” compared with $2.7 million in Q2 2025; capex rose to $54 million from $45 million in the prior quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow … Q2/26E: +$25 to +$35M”; the scenario table also expected “FCF … +$25–35M.”

surprises.description: Production averaged about 41,500 barrels per day, below the preview’s 43,000–44,000 estimate. The reported shortfall reflected Canadian dispositions and temporary artificial-lift failures at Acordionero and Cohembí.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 average working interest production was approximately 41,500 barrels per day, down 9% sequentially and 12% year-over-year,” reflecting “Canadian dispositions and temporary artificial lift system failures at Acordionero and Cohembí.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 production … 43.0–44.0 Mboe/d”; the model used “Production … Q2/26E: 43,500.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $85 million, below the preview’s $90–100 million estimate, though above the preview’s stated threshold for a more severe hedge-related shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $85 million,” from $74 million in the prior quarter and $77 million in Q2 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … $90–100M”; the preview said “Below $85M = the hedge book is worse than modeled.”

surprises.description: Net income was $25 million, below the preview’s expected $40–80 million profit. The preview attributed its anticipated larger profit mainly to an unrealized derivative reversal; the call instead cited stronger commodity prices and lower operating costs as drivers of the reported turnaround.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $25 million,” versus a $119 million loss in the prior quarter, “driven by stronger commodity prices and lower operating costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net income … +$40 to +$80M”; the preview said the gain was “Driven by unrealized derivative reversal, not operations.”

surprises.description: Capex reached $54 million, above the preview’s $38–45 million estimate. The call said spending was elevated because the capital program was weighted toward the first half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital expenditures rising to $54 million from $45 million in the prior quarter due to a first-half-weighted capital program.”

surprises.description: Net debt was $479 million, essentially flat with Q1’s $481 million and above the preview’s roughly $450 million base-scenario expectation. The modest reduction was less deleveraging than that scenario anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$127 million cash, $606 million total gross debt, and $479 million net debt,” plus $53 million of undrawn credit facilities.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Net debt (Q1): $481M” and its base scenario expected “net debt to ~$450M.”

surprises.description: The company bought back an additional $50 million face value of its 9.75% notes after quarter-end at a 10% discount. The preview anticipated further discounted note repurchases but did not suggest a buyback of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: It “bought back an additional $50 million face value at a 10% discount after quarter-end”; it had also repurchased $6 million face value during the first half at a 12% discount.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for further open-market note repurchases” and listed “incremental note buybacks” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: The $123 million Suroriente capital carry commitment was completed, with the post-carry period beginning July 18 and expected to improve the block’s economics and cash generation. The preview did not flag this milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “completed its $123 million capital carry commitment in Suroriente,” with “the post-carry period beginning July 18 and expected to improve economics and cash generation on the block.”

surprises.description: The lodgepole sale removed $13 million of asset retirement obligations while generating $9 million and shedding about 850 barrels per day of production; the company characterized the result as a net benefit. This disposition was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The lodgepole disposition sold a 54% working interest for $9 million while removing $13 million in asset retirement obligations and roughly 850 barrels per day of production, resulting in a net benefit to the company.”

surprises.description: New resource reports assigned Canadian assets about 6.5 million barrels of 2C contingent resources and 67 million barrels of combined unrisked best-estimate prospective resources, with drilling planned for 2027. The preview did not discuss these resource estimates or plans.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New McDaniel resource reports assigned Canadian assets approximately 6.5 million barrels of 2C contingent resources and about 67 million barrels of combined unrisked best-estimate prospective resources across Dawson Clearwater and Mount Head, with drilling planned for 2027.”

surprises.description: Political advertising was $147 million, at the top of the preview’s $120–150 million base case, but management said pacing was running ahead of expectations and that internal targets had been raised multiple times. That forward-pacing commentary was stronger than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 political advertising reached $147 million” and management indicated “internal political targets have been raised multiple times with pacing running ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My base case is $120–150M combined”; the preview also said “Q3/Q4 pacing commentary” mattered.

surprises.description: Nexstar repaid $409 million of debt in Q2, more than the roughly $332 million of paydowns the preview cited through April 30 and post-quarter. The faster repayment is a positive difference in the deleveraging cadence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repaid $409 million of debt in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “quarterly debt paydown ($182M through April 30 plus $150M post-quarter)”

surprises.description: Although the preview expected management to maintain its no-guidance posture, the call gave a Q3 nonpolitical advertising outlook: a mid-single-digit decline, slightly better than Q2. The decline remains weak, but the modest improvement and added forward detail were not expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 nonpolitical advertising is guided to decline mid-single digits but slightly better than Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management gave no forward guidance on the Q1 call, citing litigation constraints. Expect the same posture.”

surprises.description: Distribution performance was split: legacy Nexstar distribution revenue rose 3.1%, but TEGNA distribution revenue declined while it remained on its own contracts. That TEGNA weakness contrasts with the preview’s expectation that renewal-rate gains would push combined distribution revenue ahead of subscriber erosion; the call facts do not provide a combined growth figure to measure the overall result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TEGNA distribution revenue declined year-over-year because it continues operating under its own contracts rather than Nexstar's, whereas legacy Nexstar distribution revenue rose 3.1% ($23 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 carries a heavy retrans renewal cycle that should push rate ahead of the ~6–8% subscriber erosion”; “Anything below ~+1% YoY pro-forma is a problem.”

surprises.description: Management added a specific full-year CW loss outlook—losses are expected to improve by more than 30%—beyond the preview’s focus on the Q4 profitability target. This gives a more favorable quantified view of the path toward profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The CW remains on track for profitability in Q4 2026 with full-year losses expected to improve by more than 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CW is still guided to Q4 2026 profitability — a reiteration matters.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted a planned Nielsen local-measurement change that could significantly boost local ad impressions, an incremental potential advertising benefit the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A planned August 31 Nielsen local measurement change lowering the viewing threshold from 5 minutes to 1 minute could significantly boost local ad impressions.”

in_line: Net revenue of $1.99 billion was essentially in line with the $1.98 billion consensus estimate; combined-basis growth of 4.7% was also close to the preview’s roughly 4% estimate.
Adjusted EBITDA of $633 million was within the preview’s $630–680 million estimate.
Q2 nonpolitical advertising declined 5.8%, in line with the preview’s expected mid-single-digit decline.
The $147 million of Q2 political advertising fell within the preview’s $120–150 million base-case range.
The CW remained on track for Q4 2026 profitability, as the preview expected.
The July 2027 TEGNA trial timing remained consistent with the preview’s expectation of a trial in July 2027.

surprises.description: Revenue was $372 million versus preview consensus of about $300–302 million, and diluted EPS was $1.51 versus $0.53 expected. The large beat was substantially driven by the European ERC increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to PRA rose to $58 million, or $1.51 per diluted share,” with the European ERC increase “driving total revenues up 29% to $372 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $300.0M (MarketBeat) / $301.6M (Investing.com)” and “Diluted EPS: $0.53.”

surprises.description: Cash collections reached $559 million, below the preview’s modeled $570–585 million and up 4% year over year, below the preview’s +6% threshold for maintaining the growth narrative. The company nevertheless said collections were 4% above its own expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash collections grew 4% year-over-year to $559 million” and “total collections came in 4% above the company's expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash collections (~$570–585M base)” and “anything under +6% Y/Y breaks the two-year compounding narrative.”

surprises.description: PRA increased European ERC by $349 million after a portfolio review, an unanticipated upward revision that management said reflects repeated overperformance. It expects about $260 million of additional portfolio income over the remaining cash curves, although the near-term annualized contribution is about $25 million and the 2026 net income effect is nominal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company increased its European ERC by $349 million” following “26 consecutive quarters of overperformance,” and expects “approximately $260 million of additional portfolio income” over the remaining life of the cash curves, with “only nominal net income impact in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ERC: ~$8.6–8.8B modeled” and the preview identified changes in expected recoveries as a swing factor, but gave no expectation of a European ERC write-up.

surprises.description: Beyond the legal-cost moderation already anticipated, PRA announced a second wave of cost reductions expected to produce about $20 million of annualized net savings, bringing the two waves to roughly $35 million annually.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A second wave of cost reductions eliminated 100 U.S. corporate/overhead roles and 35 offshore roles,” expected to generate “about $20 million in annualized net savings,” with combined savings of “approximately $35 million annualized.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed expected moderation in legal collection cost growth, but did not anticipate a second wave of workforce reductions or these savings.

surprises.description: The Board authorized a new share repurchase program of up to $150 million, a larger formal authorization than the preview’s reference point of only $10 million repurchased in Q1 and its call for a possible step-up in buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized a new share repurchase program of up to $150 million,” after “$10 million repurchased in the quarter and $40 million over the past 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only $10M repurchased in Q1” and “any step-up in buyback authorization or pace is an outsized catalyst.”

surprises.description: PRA refinanced its $730 million European credit facility and extended its maturity by five years, leaving no debt maturities until February 2028; this refinancing and maturity extension were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company refinanced its $730 million European credit facility extending maturity by 5 years with no debt maturities until February 2028.”

in_line: Portfolio purchases were $297 million, within the preview’s modeled $280–320 million range, and PRA maintained its $1.0–1.3 billion full-year investment target.
U.S. legal cash collections grew 26%, consistent with the preview’s bull-case marker of 25%+ growth; management also said legal-cost growth is expected to moderate, as previously guided.

Net leverage was 2.67x, within the preview’s expected 2.65–2.70x range and consistent with the stated goal of reaching the mid-2x range. Adjusted EBITDA growth of 10% also remained ahead of collections growth.

surprises.description: OXY reported adjusted EPS of $2.40, well above the preview’s $1.84–$1.88 cluster and even its $2.10–$2.25 bull case. The preview expected a strong windfall quarter, but the reported result exceeded its high-end scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 delivered adjusted EPS of $2.40”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working range | $1.66 – $1.96 (cluster $1.84–$1.88)” and the bull scenario projected “Adj. EPS $2.10–2.25.”

surprises.description: Midstream and marketing earnings were far above the preview’s $350–550 million Q2 guidance range: OXY reported about $960 million, more than twice the range’s midpoint, and raised full-year segment guidance by $300 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Midstream and marketing set a record with ~$960 million in adjusted earnings, more than double guidance midpoint, prompting a $300 million increase to full-year segment guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance for Q2 ... midstream & marketing pre-tax income $350–550M”; the preview also flagged this segment as a potential upside surprise.

surprises.description: OXY’s debt ended at $11.8 billion, above the preview’s expected $10.5–11.5 billion range. The $1.5 billion reduction was substantial, but left debt slightly higher than the preview’s anticipated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Occidental reduced principal debt by $1.5 billion to $11.8 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “That could put principal debt at $10.5–11.5B.”

surprises.description: OXY announced a further 8% quarterly dividend increase, taking the dividend to $0.28 per share. The preview listed the existing $0.26 dividend and emphasized uncertainty about a formal capital-return framework, but did not anticipate another dividend hike.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved an 8% increase to the quarterly dividend to $0.28 per share, enabled by structural interest savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Dividend | $0.26/qtr (raised 8% after Q4'25).”

surprises.description: OXY laid out a new plan to add more than $4 billion of annual sustainable cash flow by 2030 versus 2025, with about half of the improvement expected in 2026–27. The preview focused on the Q2 windfall and near-term capital-return choices, not this longer-term cash-flow roadmap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oxy laid out a plan to add over $4 billion of annual sustainable cash flow by 2030 versus 2025”; “roughly $2 billion (about 50%) ... will be captured between 2026 and 2027.”

surprises.description: OXY reported Q2 production at the top of its guided range, 23,000 BOE/day above the midpoint despite Middle East disruptions. The preview’s base case was about 1.405–1.420 million BOE/day, so the result was stronger than that central expectation, though within the stated guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 production averaged 1.43 million BOE/day, exceeding the guidance midpoint by 23,000 BOE/day, driven by Permian and Gulf of America strength offsetting Middle East disruptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance for Q2 ... total production 1,390–1,430 Mboed”; the base scenario expected “Production ~1,405–1,420.”

surprises.description: OXY provided a 2027 starting point of $5.9 billion in capital spending, implying roughly flat production versus 2026, while about $400 million of Stratos LCV capital rolls off beginning next year. The preview gave 2026 capital guidance but no 2027 spending or production outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2027 capital spending starting point is $5.9 billion (~$5.0-5.1 billion sustaining) implying roughly flat production versus 2026, while Stratos LCV capital of ~$400 million rolls off beginning next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 capex guidance of “$5.5–5.9B” but did not provide a 2027 outlook.

in_line: Free cash flow was about $3 billion before working capital, within the preview’s estimated Q2 range of $2.5–3.4 billion.

The preview’s base case expected management to remain non-formulaic on buybacks and to focus on debt reduction; the call likewise said buybacks would remain opportunistic and lower priority, with debt reduction and cash accumulation ahead of the 2029 preferred redemption.

surprises.description: RPID reported a $12.9 million net loss, versus the preview’s roughly $12.0 million consensus estimate and $11.9 million estimate. That was a worse loss than expected, although the preview had warned that a bottom-line miss was a key risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $12.9 million from $11.9 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss | ~$12.0M” and “My estimate | –$11.9M.”

surprises.description: The company’s funding plan appears more conditional and smaller than the preview’s $25 million of undrawn Trinity capacity: management is relying on a $10 million tranche later this year, a *potential* $10 million tranche in mid-2027, and warrant exercises. The preview explicitly questioned whether the remaining facility was gated, but the call facts do not establish access to the full $25 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is relying on a $10 million debt tranche from Trinity Capital later this year, a potential second $10 million tranche in mid-2027, and warrant exercises to fund a path to positive cash flow by end of 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$25M undrawn under the Trinity Capital facility” and “Key call question: what conditions gate the remaining $25M?”

surprises.description: Recurring revenue growth slowed to 14%, and consumables growth was over 20%—below the preview’s 25%+ benchmark for evidence of durable installed-base growth. Consumables still set quarterly records, but the reported pace was weaker than the preview’s hoped-for confirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue rose 14% to $5 million while consumable revenue grew over 20% and hit new quarterly records.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second consecutive 25%+ consumables quarter is the strongest evidence” and “Consumables/recurring growth ≥25%.”

surprises.description: MilliporeSigma’s contribution is expected to build meaningfully in the second half and into 2027, but the partnership will not fully meet its calendar-year commitment. That leaves a timing shortfall even as management describes improving contribution ahead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MilliporeSigma partnership contributed to first-half placements and is expected to increase meaningfully in the second half and into 2027, though it will not fully deliver on its calendar-year commitment.”

surprises.description: RPID ended the quarter with about $20 million in cash and short-term investments, well above the preview’s roughly $14 million estimate. The higher balance indicates less cash depletion than the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with only about $20 million in cash and short-term investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash & investments (EOQ) | ~$14M.”

surprises.description: Management set explicit longer-term targets that the preview had not anticipated: average annual revenue growth above 20% and gross margin above 50% exiting 2028, with 2027 gross margin expected to exceed the 2026 exit rate. These targets extend the outlook beyond the preview’s focus on the FY26 and Q4 margin bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management set long-term targets of greater than 20% average annual revenue growth and 50%+ gross margin exiting 2028, with 2027 gross margin expected to exceed the 2026 exit rate.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year validation target to at least 27 systems, above the preview’s cited target of at least 25. This improves the expected validation pace, while the full-year revenue and placement guidance remained unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year validation guidance to at least 27 systems while reaffirming full-year revenue guidance of $37–41 million and 30–38 system placements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Validations are the other tell: 5 completed in Q1 against a ≥25 FY target.”

surprises.description: Management announced a new efficiency program expected to reduce expenses and cash usage by about $1 million for the rest of 2026 and roughly $3 million annually from 2027. The preview discussed the need for opex discipline but did not flag this specific additional savings program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A newly executed efficiency program is expected to cut expenses and cash usage by roughly $1 million for the rest of 2026 and about $3 million annually beginning in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Clean run-rate needs ~$12.5M/quarter to stay inside the guide.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $8.1 million, matching the preview’s estimate of $8.1 million and landing within its $7.9–$8.2 million base case, despite exceeding May guidance and consensus.

Gross margin reached 15%, in line with the preview’s mid-teens consensus range and 12–16% base case; the preview also anticipated a mid-20s Q4 margin trajectory, consistent with guidance to reach the mid-to-high 20s by Q4.
Full-year revenue guidance of $37–41 million and placements guidance of 30–38 systems were reaffirmed, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q2 TTV was about $169 million, far below the preview’s $350–550 million base-case range and below its roughly $400 million threshold for keeping the ramp plausible. Bakkt nevertheless kept its $2.5 billion full-year target unchanged, leaving about $2.1 billion to be achieved in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second quarter total transacting volume (TTV) was approximately $169 million, with first-half TTV of approximately $410 million, meaning the company must achieve roughly $2.1 billion in the second half to hit its unchanged full-year target of ~$2.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TTV $350–550M — directionally up but back-end-loaded”; “A Q2 TTV below ~$400M makes the $2.5B exit rate arithmetically implausible and should force a reset.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was $1.94, dramatically above the preview’s $0.03 consensus, although the preview anticipated that positive EPS could come from non-cash strategic-asset marks. The reported profit was largely driven by the Transchem warrant fair-value remeasurement rather than operating performance, so the source of the gain was expected but its reported size was not.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GAAP net income of $80.8 million with diluted EPS of $1.94, though this was largely driven by the Transchem warrant fair value re-measurement rather than operating performance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS +$0.03”; “Any positive EPS this quarter will almost certainly come from non-cash mark-to-market gains on the Bakkt Global strategic holdings.”

surprises.description: Cash and restricted cash ended the quarter at $50.7 million, down from the $82.6 million cash balance the preview cited at March 31. That is a larger cash decline than the preview’s estimate of roughly $13–14 million in quarterly adjusted EBITDA burn would suggest, though the call facts do not specify the causes of the additional decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $50.7 million in cash and restricted cash and no long-term debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$82.6M cash, zero long-term debt at 3/31/26”; “a ~$13–14M quarterly adjusted EBITDA burn.”

surprises.description: Bakkt gave an initial year-end target of about 25,000 monthly active users for Bakkt Agent but said it currently has zero because the products lack meaningful activity. The preview had expected a Q3 commercial launch and MAU disclosure at launch; the call facts do not confirm whether the launch occurred or was delayed, but the zero-activity disclosure is weaker than the expected initial traction datapoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bakkt set an initial target of approximately 25,000 monthly active users for Bakkt Agent by year-end (a year-end target, not an annual average), currently reporting zero as products lack meaningful activity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided to a Q3 2026 launch”; “committed to disclosing Monthly Active Users at launch.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects adjusted EBITDA break-even at some point in Q4 2026, a more favorable near-term outlook than the preview’s Q2 base case of a roughly $13–16 million adjusted EBITDA loss. The timing and scale of client activations make the break-even expectation conditional.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to reach adjusted EBITDA break-even at some point during the fourth quarter of 2026, contingent on the timing and scale of client activations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … adj. EBITDA loss ~$13–16M”; the preview also cited Q1 adjusted EBITDA of “-$13.7M.”

surprises.description: Strategic asset value was reported at about $119 million, versus the preview’s $76 million March 31 figure. The increase was driven by Transchem warrants valued at $107.9 million, while the Japan investment was valued at $10.6 million compared with the preview’s $31.7 million figure; the call said the measure was redefined this quarter to match the financial statements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Strategic asset value (redefined this quarter to match financial statements) was ~$119 million as of June 30, comprising $10.6 million equity method value for the Japan investment and $107.9 million fair value of Transchem warrants.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$76M at 3/31: Bitcoin Japan Corporation $31.7M … and Transchem Limited warrants $44.3M.”

surprises.description: Bakkt disclosed that six commercial offerings are live on one integration framework and set Q4 2026 targets for co-branded cards and Neobank-as-a-Service, subject to regulatory approvals. The preview discussed partner integrations and the planned Agent launch but did not anticipate these specific offerings or their timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now has six live commercial offerings connected through one integration framework, with co-branded card programs and Neobank-as-a-Service targeted for Q4 2026 subject to regulatory approvals.”

in_line: The preview anticipated that any positive EPS could be driven by non-cash marks on Bakkt Global strategic holdings; the reported profit was largely driven by a Transchem warrant fair-value remeasurement, even though EPS was far above the preview’s consensus figure.
The preview expected partner integrations to begin activating. Payments entered TTV for the first time following the May 1 integration, although lower trading activity drove an overall TTV decline.

surprises.description: DuPont raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to a $7.24 midpoint, above both the $7.14–$7.15 consensus and the preview’s stated $7.20 threshold for a meaningful raise. The outlook also calls for slightly more than 4% organic growth and about 6% organic growth in the second half, including 5% in Q3 and 7% in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DuPont raised full-year 2026 guidance” to “$7.24 adjusted EPS midpoint”; second-half organic growth of “~6% is expected (5% in Q3, 7% in Q4 excluding prior-year timing).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 Adj. EPS: $7.14–$7.15” consensus; “Anything short of a raise to ≥$7.20 reads as a cut”; the preview’s bull tell cited “H2 organic ≥4%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.88 beat the $1.76 consensus and even the preview’s inferred $1.82–$1.85 whisper. However, the reported 21% year-over-year EPS growth was well below the preview’s statement that the underlying quarter implied about 55% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 21% year-over-year to $1.88,” with $0.17 from stronger operations and $0.15 from below-the-line items.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS: $1.76” consensus; the preview inferred a “whisper” of “$1.82–$1.85” and described the underlying quarter as “~+55% adjusted EPS growth.”

surprises.description: Operating EBITDA and margin both came in well above the preview’s Q2 framing: EBITDA was $448 million versus about $430 million expected, and margin was 24.6% versus an implied roughly 23.9%. This was stronger than anticipated despite the price/cost headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating EBITDA increased 8% to $448 million with margin expanding 80 basis points to 24.6%, despite a 30 basis point headwind from price/cost dynamics.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put Q2 operating EBITDA at “~$430M” and said Q2 was “guided ~23.9% on mix (~40bp) + price-cost (~30bp).”

surprises.description: Water remained only a low-single-digit growth business as Middle East conflict-related project delays continued, rather than delivering the recovery the preview expected from the Q1 delayed shipment. DuPont consequently cut its full-year Water outlook to low-to-mid single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water sales grew only low single digits due to Middle East conflict-driven project delays”; the company cut its full-year Water outlook to “low-to-mid single digits,” although growth excluding the Middle East was mid-single digits.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 “should get [the Q1 delay] back plus growth” and flagged that water should be “positive ex-catch-up.”

surprises.description: Cash conversion was stronger than the preview’s already demanding full-year target: Q2 conversion reached 127%, and the full-year outlook is now closer to 100% rather than merely above 90%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow of $326 million delivered 127% conversion, with full-year conversion now expected closer to 100%, ahead of the 90% target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 conversion of “65%” and a full-year guide of “>90%,” requiring “a material H2 step-up.”

surprises.description: DuPont added a specific, sizable growth outlook for its EV battery adhesives business: from about $70 million of revenue today, it expects the business to reach triple-digit millions by 2026–2027, with the broader EV portfolio approaching half of its automotive business. The preview noted EV battery adhesives were growing but gave no comparable scale or target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The EV battery adhesives business (~$70 million revenue today) is expected to grow into triple digits by 2026-2027,” while the broader EV portfolio is “approaching half of the $900 million automotive business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “aerospace and EV battery adhesives up” but gave no quantified outlook for the EV business.

in_line: Q2 sales were about $1.8 billion with 4% organic growth, broadly matching the preview’s approximately $1.8 billion company guide and 3–4% organic-growth framing.

The Q2 price/cost headwind was 30 basis points, matching the preview’s estimate of a roughly 30-basis-point Q2 headwind; the preview also expected the full run-rate pricing to be realized in the second half.

Capital deployment remained within the preview’s buyback-versus-M&A debate: DuPont plans a $250 million Q3 repurchase while retaining more than $1 billion of capacity for Water and Healthcare/CDMO M&A opportunities.

surprises.description: Koppers reported $520 million of sales, $71 million of adjusted EBITDA and $1.37 of adjusted EPS, all above the preview’s estimates of about $503 million, $67 million and $1.15–$1.25, respectively. Adjusted EBITDA also topped the preview’s stated $70 million buy-side bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales rose 3% to $520 million”; “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA fell 7.9% year-over-year to $71 million”; “adjusted EPS of $1.37.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$503M” of sales and “~$67M” of adjusted EBITDA, with “Adj. EPS estimate: ~$1.15–1.25”; it said to treat the buy-side bar as “EBITDA ≥ $70M.”

surprises.description: Performance Chemicals substantially outperformed the preview’s estimate: adjusted EBITDA was $38 million versus about $29 million expected, and margins exceeded 20% versus an estimated 18.1%. The preview had specifically flagged a possible inventory-payback quarter and margin below 17% as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Performance chemicals adjusted EBITDA jumped 31% to $38 million on 10% ex-FX sales growth, including 11% Americas growth and 26% Australasia growth, with margins exceeding 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated PC at “~$160M / ~$29M (18.1%)” and flagged a possible “payback quarter” with “margin <17%.”

surprises.description: Koppers raised its quarterly dividend 12.5% to $0.09, contrary to the preview’s expectation that the $0.09 dividend would be unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned $47 million to shareholders in the first half … and raised its quarterly dividend 12.5% to $0.09 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the dividend “a non-event: $0.09 declared Aug 5, unchanged.”

surprises.description: CMC adjusted EBITDA came in at $8 million, above the preview’s roughly $6 million estimate, despite substantial cost pressure. That is a modest upside against the estimate, though it remained below the preview’s threshold of more than $10 million for a genuine upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CMC adjusted EBITDA fell to $8 million from $17 million,” with “$9 million in higher raw material, operating and SG&A costs plus a ~$2.3 million Q2 oil-price impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated CMC adjusted EBITDA at “~$6M” and said “Above $10M is a genuine upside surprise.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a further $4.6 million oil-price impact expected in CMC in the second half. The preview anticipated elevated oil costs and pass-through pressure, but did not specify this additional second-half burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: CMC had a “~$2.3 million Q2 oil-price impact, with another $4.6 million impact expected in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “oil costs still elevated” and CMC’s “oil-linked raw material inflation” and pass-through lag, without quantifying a second-half impact.

surprises.description: First-half cash generation reached records: $73 million of free cash flow and $96 million of operating cash flow, with inventory alignment cited as the driver. The preview highlighted Q2 cash flow and leverage progress as important to watch but gave no specific cash-flow estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half operating cash flow hit a record $96 million (up from $28 million) and free cash flow reached a record $73 million (up from $1 million), driven by inventory alignment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Deleveraging and FCF” and said “Q2 FCF and any leverage reduction determine” whether the equity re-rates further, without setting a Q2 or first-half estimate.

surprises.description: Catalyst transformation benefits had reached $33 million by June 30, already at the midpoint of the prior full-year target, and the company identified over $90 million of benefits for 2026–2028. The preview recognized Catalyst as part of the bull case but did not anticipate this reported progress or pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Catalyst transformation delivered $33 million in year-over-year benefits through June 30 (already at the prior full-year target's midpoint), with over $90 million in benefits identified for 2026-2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited the “Catalyst cost program” as part of the bull case and described it as one of the factors behind the stock’s run, but gave no expected benefit amount or progress milestone.

in_line: Management narrowed FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $240–250 million and adjusted EPS guidance to $3.80–$4.20, while sales guidance remained $1.9–$2.0 billion. This matched the preview’s highest-probability call of narrowing to the low half, which specifically identified $240–250 million as a possible narrowed range.

The Stickney closure and stated annual benefits were consistent with the preview’s expectation that the closure plan and $15–20 million of annual adjusted EBITDA and $1.00–$1.20 of EPS improvement remained intact; the preview expected the savings to arrive in 2027.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $5.8 million, well above the preview’s $3.6 million estimate and the roughly $3.7 million level used as the flat-to-up YoY whisper. The preview’s bridge required about $4.8 million per quarter in Q2–Q4 to reach even the low end of full-year guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached approximately $5.8 million,” up from $3.7 million in the prior-year period.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimates: revenue $29.5M, adj. EBITDA $3.6M”; “the whisper is effectively ‘at least flat YoY’”; Q2–Q4 required “~$4.8M/qtr” at the low end of the FY26 EBITDA guide.

surprises.description: Revenue of approximately $30 million exceeded both the preview’s $28.6 million consensus and its $29.5 million estimate. The beat was modest, and management said chemicals revenue fell short because of timing, which it expects to recover later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $30 million”; chemicals revenue “fell modestly short due to timing that management expects to recover later in the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 2026 consensus revenue was “~$28.6M”; “My estimates: revenue $29.5M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached approximately 38.5%, a much stronger result than the preview’s concern that a margin below 34% ex-charges would undermine the standalone PAC case. Management attributed the improvement partly to the absence of GAC start-up costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved roughly 520 basis points to approximately 38.5% due to the absence of GAC start-up costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything sub-34% ex-charges undermines the ‘PAC is a good standalone business’ argument”; Q1 gross margin was 34.2%.

surprises.description: Management said there would be no GAC production or sales in 2027, pushing output beyond the restart timing contemplated in the preview’s cited summer-2027 model. That leaves the business without GAC revenue for longer than the preview’s modeled restart path.
surprises.fact_evidence: “No GAC production or sales are expected in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Clear Street models summer 2027” for restart timing.

surprises.description: The estimated cost to convert GAC capacity was $40–60 million for Phase 1, far above the preview’s optimistic scenario of less than $15 million. These are consultant estimates rather than an approved investment budget, but they indicate a potentially much larger funding requirement than the preview’s bull case assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAC conversion cost estimates from two independent engineering consultants range widely at $40-60 million for 25 million pounds of Phase 1 capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull scenario assumed “modest (<$15M) capex”; it flagged the GAC capex figure as a key issue to watch.

surprises.description: Unrestricted cash was only about $0.9 million at quarter-end—$12.1 million of total cash included $11.2 million restricted—versus $4.7 million unrestricted cash reported in the preview for Q1. It recovered to about $3.1 million by July 31, but remained below the Q1 level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total cash of $12.1 million (of which $11.2 million restricted); unrestricted cash rose to about $3.1 million by July 31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported “Cash / restricted” of “$4.7M / $11.2M” for Q1 and highlighted liquidity as a key risk.

surprises.description: Management set a goal to grow core PAC adjusted EBITDA by up to 50% to roughly $30 million next year, explicitly without any bituminous-based GAC contribution. The preview focused on whether PAC could support the FY26 guide and did not flag this specific next-year target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company set a goal to grow core PAC business adjusted EBITDA by up to 50% to roughly $30 million next year, entirely without any contribution from bituminous-based GAC.”

surprises.description: Management described a new PAC product for PFAS as carrying substantially higher selling prices and margins than base PAC, with meaningful volume and margin contribution expected in 2027. The preview did not identify this product or its potential as an earnings driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new PAC for PFAS product is expected to carry substantially higher ASP and margins than base PAC, with only minor sales in H2 2026 but meaningful volume and margin contribution anticipated in 2027.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern that a dilutive raise could be punitive, management said it intends to fund a GAC investment through debt rather than equity if it proceeds. That avoids an announced equity-financing plan, although the proposed debt funding would add to financing risk given the estimated project cost.
surprises.fact_evidence: “They intend to fund it through debt rather than equity dilution if pursued.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a raise at $2.05 would be “punitive” and highlighted the risk of “an equity raise” and financing language.

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $120–125 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $17–20 million, as the preview expected the guide to be reaffirmed or changed.

The GAC go-forward decision remained unresolved, broadly matching the preview’s base case that management might defer a decision to a later call; management said it could decide later in 2026 or push the decision into 2027.

surprises.description: Q1 net bookings were about $1.39 billion, $20 million above the top of the $1.32–$1.37 billion guidance range. The preview’s functional whisper was at or slightly above the $1.37 billion high end, so the beat was positive but narrow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 net bookings reached approximately $1.39 billion, slightly above the high end of guidance ($1.32B-$1.37B), driven by outperformance from NBA 2K and Grand Theft Auto.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Assume the functional whisper on net bookings sits at or slightly above the $1.37B high end of guidance.”

surprises.description: Recurrent consumer spending declined only 1%, rather than the approximately 3% decline expected for Q1. That indicates the recurring business held up better than the preview’s baseline while mobile itself declined as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 recurrent consumer spending declined only 1% (better than the guided 3% decline) and accounted for 84% of net bookings, while mobile declined 7% as expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Recurrent Consumer Spending (RCS): ~−3% YoY”; “Q1 net bookings vs. $1.32–1.37B and RCS vs. −3%.”

surprises.description: NBA 2K26 showed strong unit sales and engagement, but recurrent spending growth was 7%, below the preview’s roughly 10% reference point for the NBA 2K recurring engine. The operating signals therefore mixed robust activity with somewhat softer spending growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NBA 2K26 sold over 12 million units, up 9% versus NBA 2K25, with recurrent consumer spending up 7%, average daily active users up 15%, and average games played per user up 35%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “NBA 2K26 RCS (+10% in Q4) and 2K27 setup” and described the scenario expectation as “NBA 2K RCS holds ~+10%.”

surprises.description: Management described GTA VI preorders as “unprecedented and astonishing,” a distinctly bullish characterization beyond the preview’s expectation of no new disclosure. However, it gave no unit figure and did not raise guidance, limiting how much new evidence the comment provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management calling preorders ‘unprecedented and astonishing’ but declining to raise guidance since no units have yet been sold.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Rockstar historically discloses nothing. Any hard unit number … is the biggest upside surprise available.”

surprises.description: Cost of revenue rose 17% and included a $43 million impairment charge tied to canceling an unannounced third-party title—an unexpected expense and project cancellation not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 cost of revenue rose 17% to $651 million, including a $43 million impairment charge from canceling an unannounced third-party developer title.”

surprises.description: Take-Two now expects to finish FY2027 with net cash, a stronger position than the preview’s reference to approximately $836 million of net debt. The preview already expected more than $1 billion of operating cash flow, but did not state a net-cash year-end target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects FY2027 operating cash flow exceeding $1 billion, a net cash position by fiscal year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$836M net debt”; “Operating cash flow: >$1B.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY2027 capex to approximately $290 million for a planned real estate purchase, an investment and capital-allocation detail not anticipated in the preview. The material provides no prior capex expectation to quantify the increase against.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised capex to ~$290 million due to a planned real estate purchase.”

in_line: Take-Two reaffirmed its FY2027 net bookings outlook of $8.0–$8.2 billion, as the preview expected.
Management confirmed GTA VI’s November 19, 2026 release date, the unqualified reaffirmation the preview treated as the expected base case.
Mobile declined 7%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that mobile would be weak against tough comparisons.
FY2027 operating cash flow above $1 billion was already stated in the preview’s full-year framing.
No preorder unit or sell-through figure was disclosed, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Rockstar historically does not disclose preorder metrics.
The $80 GTA VI Standard Edition price was essentially the same as the $79.99 price already reported in the preview.

surprises.description: Net sales of $649.1 million were modestly above the preview’s roughly flat $630–640 million estimate and the top of its $615–645 million base case. They were still below the preview’s seasonality-based estimate of about $665 million, so the result was stronger than the flat-revenue view but not as strong as that calculation implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 consolidated net sales rose just 1% year-over-year to $649.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described StockStory’s expectation as “roughly flat YoY” (≈$630–640M), gave a base scenario of $615–645M, and said Q1 “should” be about $665M based on seasonality.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.28 exceeded the preview’s $1.15–1.20 de facto whisper range, although the call facts say it declined from $1.41 a year earlier. The preview’s cited $0.98 consensus was lower still.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS declined to $1.28 from $1.41.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to treat “$1.15–1.20 as the de facto whisper, not $0.98.”

surprises.description: Professional services revenue fell 5.1%, a milder decline than the preview said was most likely, which was a double-digit decline given the difficult comparison and project delays.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Professional services revenue declined 5.1% to $68.1 million due to project delays tied to product delivery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a double-digit decline here is the most likely source of an ugly-looking services line.”

surprises.description: Managed services growth accelerated beyond the preview’s expected 10–11% run rate, with revenue surpassing $50 million for the first time and growing over 15%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Managed services net sales surpassed $50 million for the first time, growing over 15% year-over-year, driven by data center and cloud demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described managed services as “running ~10–11% growth.”

surprises.description: Security gross billings grew 15.6% and reached 24.2% of trailing-12-month gross billings, with multiple multiyear enterprise software licensing agreements supporting growth. The preview discussed gross billings and AI monetization but did not flag this security result or licensing activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Security gross billings grew 15.6% and represented 24.2% of gross billings on a trailing 12-month basis, aided by multiple multiyear enterprise software licensing agreements.”

surprises.description: Working capital improved more than the preview’s inventory build concern suggested: inventory fell by $54.9 million, the cash conversion cycle improved by 10 days sequentially, and cash rose from fiscal year-end. This is a favorable contrast to the preview’s warning that the inventory build could weigh on cash conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The cash position strengthened to $448.9 million from $410.8 million at fiscal 2026 year-end, while the cash conversion cycle improved 10 days sequentially to 41 days as inventory fell $54.9 million to $146 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted inventory of $200.9 million and said “the inventory build may be deliberate pre-buying ahead of the memory shortage — bullish for Q1/Q2 fulfilment, bearish for free cash flow.”

surprises.description: Management authorized repurchases of up to 1.5 million shares, a concrete expansion of buyback capacity beyond the preview’s reference to only 90,000 shares repurchased in Q4 and its discussion of possible buyback acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management announced “a new authorization to repurchase up to 1.5 million shares.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “only 90k shares repurchased in Q4 FY26” and said “buyback acceleration or an M&A announcement” could be a signal.

in_line: Management maintained fiscal 2027 guidance, as the preview identified reiteration as the bar and included an unchanged guide in its base case.
Consolidated gross margin was 23.3%, within the preview’s 23.0–24.0% base-case range; the preview flagged a margin below roughly 23% as a concern.
