Adjusted EBITDA of $47.8 million was within the preview’s $44–49 million base-case range.
Open orders were up substantially, consistent with the preview’s references to rising open orders and record backlog; the facts do not say that orders converted faster than expected.
Management cited the worldwide memory chip shortage and customer-specific retail project delays, both of which the preview had flagged as potential headwinds and timing risks.
The $0.27 quarterly dividend was already reflected in the preview, which described the raised dividend at that level.

surprises.description: Arista reported just over $3.0 billion of Q2 revenue, above the preview’s $2.90–$2.95 billion buy-side bar, not merely the $2.83 billion published consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue of just over $3 billion,” up 37.7% year over year and “above guidance of $2.8 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The real bar is revenue ~$2.90–2.95B”; published Street consensus was “$2.83B.”

surprises.description: Reported diluted EPS of $1.02 exceeded the preview’s $0.94–$0.96 buy-side estimate and its $0.88–$0.89 consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS was $1.02,” up from $0.73 in the prior year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The real bar is … EPS ~$0.94–0.96”; the preview’s consistent-basis consensus was “$0.88–$0.89.”

surprises.description: Arista raised full-year revenue guidance to about $12.6 billion, materially above the preview’s expected $11.9–$12.0 billion range. The increase was $1.1 billion over its prior projection, rather than the more modest raise the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance for the third time this year to approximately $12.6 billion,” an incremental “$1.1 billion above the prior $11.5 billion projection.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bar is a raise to ~$11.9–12.0B”; the base case expected FY26 to be “nudged to $11.7–11.8B.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin came in above the preview’s roughly 62–62.5% expectation, at 63.4%. The quarter-on-quarter improvement was partly helped by tariff refunds, while management’s Q3 gross-margin guide is around 63%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin was 63.4%,” up from 62.4% in the prior quarter; tariff refunds provided a “20-30 bps benefit.” Q3 gross margin is guided “around 63%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~62–62.5%” and said “62.4% in Q1”; its base case expected “GM ~62–62.5%.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of about $3.3 billion points to a stronger near-term run rate than the preview’s implied H2 pace of roughly $2.95–$3.1 billion per quarter from its FY26 outlook. The preview did not provide a separate Q3 consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of approximately $3.3 billion,” with diluted EPS of $1.06–$1.08 and operating margin of 48%–49%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s FY26 math said Q2 of about $2.90 billion would leave “~$5.89B for H2,” and its expected FY26 guide was ~$11.9–$12.0 billion.

surprises.description: The AI revenue goal rose only slightly to at least $3.6 billion, falling short of the preview’s expected $4.0 billion target despite the much larger overall revenue-guidance increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: The full-year AI fabrics goal was set at “at least $3.5 billion”; the company also described an “at least $3.6 billion AI target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “AI to $4.0B” was the buy-side bar and that “AI to ~$3.7–3.8B” was the base case.

surprises.description: Scale-Across is expected to contribute about 30% of the AI target, below the preview’s expectation that it would represent at least one-third of AI revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scale-Across is expected to represent about 30% (~$1.2 billion) of Arista's at least $3.6 billion AI target in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “scale-across contribution (guided to at least one-third of AI revenue)” as a secondary item to watch.

surprises.description: Supply commitments increased further to about $9.7 billion, and management expects industry-wide tightness to persist through 2028. That is a larger commitment book and a longer-lasting constraint than the preview’s stated one-to-two-year shortage framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiyear purchase commitments nearly tripled year-over-year to approximately $9.7 billion,” up from $8.9 billion in Q1; industry-wide tightness is “expected to persist through 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said commitments had reached “$8.9B” and described the shortage as a “‘1 to 2 year’ issue”; it asked whether the tone would shift from “constrained” to “improving visibility.”

surprises.description: International revenue’s share jumped to 23% from 15.5% in the prior quarter, a sharp geographic mix shift the preview did not forecast or flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International revenue jumped to $697.8 million (23% of total) from 15.5% last quarter,” driven by organic growth and mix shifts among large global customers.

in_line: Inventory rose modestly to $2.5 billion, while turns remained at 1.7, consistent with the preview’s focus on inventory from about $2.38 billion and turns of 1.7.

surprises.description: Q4 diluted EPS was $2.91 versus the preview's $2.42 consensus, a substantial beat. The preview had put the implied Q4 range at $2.35–$2.45, so the result was also well above the upper end of that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 diluted EPS grew 40% to $2.91.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | Consensus | $2.42”; “guidance-implied Q4 EPS at $2.35–$2.45.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $63.7 billion, below the preview's $65.0–$65.6 billion consensus range. This was a notable top-line miss despite the strong EPS result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 enterprise operating income rose 30% to $935 million on revenue of $63.7 billion (up 6%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $65.0–65.6B.”

surprises.description: FY27 EPS guidance of $12.40–$12.60 came in well above the preview's $12.01 consensus and its $12.04–$12.26 algorithm range. The company framed growth as 13%–15% on a normalized $10.95 base, rather than using the tariff-boosted reported FY26 figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 EPS guidance is $12.40 to $12.60, representing 13% to 15% growth off a normalized baseline of $10.95 that excludes the $0.31 tariff refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Initial FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance vs. $12.01”; “Applying management's own FY26–FY28 algorithm ... implies $12.04–$12.26.”

surprises.description: Cardinal recognized a material IEEPA tariff refund benefit even though the preview said no financial impact had yet been recognized and none was in guidance. The company identified a nonrecurring $100 million net operating earnings benefit in GMPD, which also contributed $0.31 to Q4 EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$0.31 ... came from a nonrecurring IEEPA tariff refund benefit”; “a onetime $100 million net operating earnings benefit in GMPD from roughly $200 million in IEEPA tariff refunds,” explicitly labeled nonrecurring.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No financial impact has been recognized and none is in guidance”; management had sized the potential net benefit at “~$100M after customer sharing.”

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted free cash flow reached $5 billion, above the preview's stated FY26 guidance range of $3.3–$3.7 billion. The preview had identified cash flow as an important capital-return offset, but the reported result exceeded that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow rising to $5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adjusted FCF guide is $3.3–3.7B.”

surprises.description: The FY27 free-cash-flow outlook was $3.5–$4.0 billion, below FY26's $5 billion result, while capex rises to $700 million. The preview flagged the forthcoming FCF guide as an important offset but did not anticipate a lower outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 adjusted free cash flow is guided lower at $3.5 billion to $4 billion (versus $5 billion in fiscal '26), with CapEx rising to $700 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A FY27 FCF guide plus an above-baseline repurchase commitment is the most credible offset to a soft EPS guide.”

surprises.description: GMPD's Q4 result included a one-time refund benefit that the preview had not expected to be recognized: excluding the $100 million benefit, segment profit was $50 million versus the preview's $42 million consensus. Thus the underlying result was only modestly above consensus, while the refund drove the much larger reported benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the $100 million tariff refund, GMPD Q4 segment profit was only $50 million”; the company recorded a “$100 million net operating earnings benefit in GMPD.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GMPD segment profit | $42M”; “no financial impact has been recognized and none is in guidance.”

surprises.description: Pharma segment profit was $645 million, modestly above the preview's $628 million estimate, and grew 21% versus the preview's expected 17% growth. The forward outlook was more measured: FY27 profit growth is expected to normalize to 8%–11%, with revenue growth of 3%–5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Pharma segment posted 21% profit growth to $645 million in Q4, but fiscal '27 guidance calls for more normalized profit growth of 8% to 11% and revenue growth of just 3% to 5%, excluding outsized demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pharma & Specialty segment profit | $628M | +17%.”

surprises.description: Other-business revenue was $1.7 billion, below the preview's $1.80 billion estimate, although profit was slightly above its estimate. The FY27 outlook calls for 11%–13% revenue growth and 15%–18% profit growth, with about two points of growth aided by the Strive and AdaptHealth diabetes acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 'other' growth businesses grew Q4 revenue 7% to $1.7 billion and profit 14% to $183 million, with fiscal '27 guidance of 11%-13% revenue and 15%-18% profit growth, aided by ~2 points from Strive and AdaptHealth diabetes acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Other revenue / profit | $1.80B / $181M | +12% / +13%.”

surprises.description: The company raised its baseline FY27 buyback commitment to at least $1 billion and added $5 billion to repurchase authorization, above the preview's $750 million-plus annual baseline. This was a larger capital-return commitment than the preview's stated baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized a $5 billion increase to share repurchase authority (bringing total to $6.4 billion) and raised the fiscal '27 baseline buyback to at least $1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Baseline buyback commitment is $750M+/yr for three years”; the preview also flagged an “above-baseline repurchase commitment” as a possible offset.

in_line: Q4 other-business profit was broadly in line with the preview: $183 million reported versus $181 million expected.

surprises.description: OneSpan raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $248–252 million from $244–249 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $67–71 million from $64–68 million. The higher outlook also puts the revenue midpoint above the preview’s cited FY2026 consensus of $246.4 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $248-252 million (from $244-249 million) and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $67-71 million (from $64-68 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY2026 guidance … total revenue $244–249M … adjusted EBITDA $64–68M”; FY2026 consensus revenue “$246.4M.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $60.5 million, above the preview’s main $57.75 million estimate and also above its $58.3 million alternative. Instead of the expected year-over-year decline, revenue grew 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue grew just 1% year-over-year to $60.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $57.75M (−3.5% YoY)” and alternative estimates of “$58.3M / ~$60M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $16.9 million at a 27.9% margin, below the preview’s watch level of 29–30% and below Q2 FY2025’s 29.5% margin. The preview anticipated margin pressure from reinvestment, but the reported margin fell further than that stated threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to $16.9 million (27.9% margin) from $17.6 million (29.5%) … reflecting increased costs from acquisitions and organic go-to-market investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether Q2 FY2026 holds ≥29–30%”; Q2 FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was “$17.6M / 29.5% margin.”

surprises.description: Cybersecurity revenue declined 7.5% and operating income fell to $13.8 million from $19.8 million, with margin down to 34% from 45%. The preview highlighted hardware and retention risks, but did not anticipate this degree of segment revenue and profitability deterioration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cybersecurity division revenue declined 7.5% to $40.9 million and operating income fell to $13.8 million (34% margin) from $19.8 million (45%),” pressured by a “$3 million known headwind, hardware/perpetual maintenance declines, and acquisition costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described hardware as “in secular decline” and asked whether the “Cybersecurity GRR gap is structural,” but gave no expectation of a Q2 Cybersecurity revenue decline or this operating-income decline.

surprises.description: Hardware guidance moved higher rather than weakening: OneSpan raised its 2026 range to $46–48 million from $43–45 million on stronger first-half bookings. This reversed the preview’s concern that hardware weakness could weigh on revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hardware revenue guidance was increased to $46-48 million (from $43-45 million) due to stronger first-half bookings, with a seasonally weak Q3 followed by a much stronger Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called hardware “the most plausible source of a top-line miss” and cited FY guidance of “$43–45M.”

surprises.description: Digital Agreements accelerated to 25.2% revenue growth, and operating income nearly doubled to $7 million as its margin expanded to 35.7%. The preview showed 11.2% growth in Q1 but did not anticipate this stronger Q2 growth and profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The digital agreements division delivered 25.2% revenue growth to $19.5 million, with operating income nearly doubling to $7 million (35.7% margin) from $2.9 million (18.4%) a year ago, boosted by strong overage revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 Digital Agreements revenue growth of “11.2%” but gave no Q2 segment forecast.

surprises.description: Cash and liquidity weakened: OneSpan ended Q2 with $43.3 million in cash and $5 million of credit-facility debt, versus $49.8 million of cash and no debt at Q1-end, while operating cash flow was slightly negative. The preview gave Q1 operating cash flow but did not anticipate this Q2 reversal and new debt.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $43.3 million in cash and $5 million in credit facility debt, down from $49.8 million cash and no debt in Q1, with operating cash flow a modest $0.1 million outflow.”

in_line: ARR was $189.7 million, down from Q1’s $192.1 million but within the preview’s anticipated roughly flat-to-down range of about $189–193 million as the pre-announced non-renewals landed.
The DigiPASS One launch itself was already known from the preview, which said the platform was too new to affect Q2 numbers.

surprises.description: The preview expected the synergy target to remain at $90 million, but MasterBrand raised it to more than $100 million of annual run rate by year three after closing. That is a meaningful increase over the stated target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its cost synergy target to over $100 million of annual run rate by year 3 post-close, exceeding the original target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$90M run-rate by end of year three”

surprises.description: The preview expected tariff costs to be fully offset on a run-rate basis exiting 2026. Instead, MasterBrand said Q2’s $41.9 million of gross tariff costs had a net breakeven impact after mitigation, suggesting the impact was already neutralized in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined company gross tariff costs were $41.9 million in Q2 with a net breakeven impact after mitigation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management committed to offsetting 100% of tariff dollar costs on a run-rate basis exiting 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated that the American Woodmark stub would dilute margins, noting its prior 6.7% adjusted EBITDA margin. The reported 32-day contribution produced only $4 million of EBITDA on $126 million of sales, about a 3% margin, and management said its fiscal Q3 and Q4 performance was below expectations because of excess capacity and absorption pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “American Woodmark's fiscal Q3 and Q4 performance came in below expectations due to excess fixed capacity and absorption pressure,” and its 32-day period had “$126 million sales and $4 million EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AMWD's own adj. EBITDA margin fell to 6.7% by its fiscal Q3.”

surprises.description: The preview discussed cost actions but did not flag further plant consolidations. MasterBrand said it had already initiated two manufacturing facility consolidations to address excess capacity, adding another concrete capacity-reduction measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two manufacturing facility consolidations have already been initiated to address excess capacity.”

in_line: Legacy MasterBrand sales fell 5.6%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a mid- to high-single-digit decline; its $58 million of adjusted EBITDA was within the company’s $51–61 million standalone guide.

Combined Q2 sales of $815 million were at the top of the preview’s $770–815 million build, and the roughly $62 million of adjusted EBITDA from legacy MasterBrand and the American Woodmark stub was within the preview’s $59–74 million estimate. The preview had also warned that the headline revenue figure would be mechanically boosted by the merger stub.

Management provided combined second-half guidance, as the preview identified reinstatement of a combined-company outlook as the key question. The preview did not provide a comparable numerical second-half estimate.
Q2 free cash flow of $129 million was consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would rebound sharply from the seasonally weak first quarter.

The reported 3.9x trailing net leverage was broadly in line with the preview’s estimate of roughly 4x or more; the preview specifically cautioned that the stated ratio and its definition would matter.
The 5%–6% full-year tariff exposure and goal of fully offsetting it by year-end were broadly consistent with the preview’s tariff expectations.
The expected year-end diluted share count of 203.6 million was close to the preview’s estimate of about 205 million going forward.

surprises.description: AESI reported Q2 revenue of $293.2 million versus the preview’s roughly $282.2 million consensus, a beat of about 3.9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $293.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 revenue | ~$282.2M.”

surprises.description: Management guided Q3 adjusted EBITDA to $30–$45 million, below Q2’s $49.5 million, rather than sustaining the momentum suggested by the preview’s expectation that volumes would remain elevated through 2026. Customer completion breaks and the decision to hold pricing on sand tenders are driving the step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 EBITDA guidance is $30 million to $45 million, a sequential step-down from Q2's $49.5 million, driven by customer completion breaks (~40-50% of variance) and a deliberate decision to hold pricing on sand tenders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 commentary said volumes should ‘remain elevated for the remainder of 2026’; any softening would pressure the story.”

surprises.description: Q2 sand volumes were 5.6 million tons and came in below expectations, with late-June rig moves and schedule changes cited. That falls short of the preview’s referenced expectation for elevated volumes through the rest of 2026; Q3 volume guidance is also broad at 5.3–6.0 million tons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 sand volumes of 5.6 million tons came in below expectations due to late-June rig moves and schedule changes, with Q3 volumes guided to a wide 5.3-6.0 million ton range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 commentary said volumes should ‘remain elevated for the remainder of 2026’.”

surprises.description: AESI said it is willing to give up near-term sand volume to hold pricing, aiming to force “capacity discovery” and improve the economics of 2027 pricing as contracts turn over. The preview flagged sand volumes and pricing as issues to watch, but did not anticipate this deliberate trade-off.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is intentionally trading near-term sand volumes to hold pricing, aiming to force ‘capacity discovery’ and drive accretive 2027 pricing as a significant portion of the contract book turns over.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sand volumes/pricing into H2 2026 — Q1 commentary said volumes should ‘remain elevated for the remainder of 2026’; any softening would pressure the story.”

surprises.description: Management now expects only 2–4 projects to contract the remaining uncommitted power capacity, versus its prior assumption of 8–10. It said project sizes have grown and contract tenors are now 15–20 years rather than the initial 10-year target, so fewer contracts may cover the capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now believes only 2 to 4 projects (versus a prior assumption of 8 to 10) could contract its remaining uncommitted power capacity, as project sizes and contract tenors (now 15-20 years vs. an initial 10-year target) have grown substantially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Prior assumption of 8 to 10” projects, as described on the call.

surprises.description: The preview already identified the 120 MW technology-infrastructure PPA, but did not give its economics. AESI said the project requires about $190 million of capital and is expected to generate about $55 million of annualized adjusted free cash flow, with a cash-on-cash payback under 3.5 years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Atlas signed its first behind-the-meter contract, a 120-megawatt PPA with an investment-grade tech infrastructure subsidiary, requiring ~$190 million in project capital and expected to generate ~$55 million of annualized adjusted free cash flow with a cash-on-cash payback under 3.5 years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Power segment ramp — progress against … the 120 MW five-year PPA with an investment-grade technology-infrastructure customer.”

surprises.description: AESI provided a more specific funding plan than the preview: it expects future power projects to be funded primarily with debt, but only after contracts are signed. It also expects quarterly maintenance CapEx for sand and logistics to fall to $5–$7.5 million, providing new detail on the capex cadence the preview flagged as a concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AESI holds ~$168 million in cash and ~$125 million of undrawn ABL capacity, expects sand/logistics maintenance CapEx to fall to $5-7.5 million per quarter, and plans to fund future power projects primarily with debt (60-70%) only after contracts are signed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Balance sheet / liquidity — after the $450M 0.50% convertible notes due 2031; capex cadence on power equipment following the dividend suspension.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $49.5 million was essentially in line with management’s approximately $50 million Q2 guide.

surprises.description: The preview put Q2 revenue consensus at about $105–107 million and the buy-side whisper around $100–102 million. Redwire reported $117.1 million, roughly 9–11% above consensus and also well above the whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Redwire posted record quarterly revenue of $117.1 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $105.3M | $106.96M”; the preview also estimated “a whisper in the high-$90s to ~$102M on revenue.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a hard sequential backlog step-down and book-to-bill near or below 1.0x after Q1’s IDIQ-inflated quarter. Instead, Redwire reported 1.42 book-to-bill and record backlog of $542.1 million, up from Q1’s $498.1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bookings of $165.8 million produced a 1.42 book-to-bill for the quarter and 1.52 on an LTM basis, driving record backlog of $542.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A book-to-bill near or below 1.0x is the reasonable base case”; the preview also said to “expect a hard sequential step-down” in backlog.

surprises.description: Defense Tech revenue substantially exceeded the preview’s modeled $47–50 million, reaching $61.9 million. The preview’s Space estimate was $55–58 million, and reported Space revenue of $55.2 million was within that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense Tech revenue reached $61.9 million (up ~40% sequentially, largely from the Edge Autonomy acquisition) versus Space revenue of $55.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Segment split (no published consensus; modeled off Q1 mix): Space ~$55–58M, Defense Tech ~$47–50M.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin of 27.8% was above the preview’s 26–27% base case and close to its bull-case threshold of above 28%. However, management also said margins may return to the low-to-mid 20s near term, tempering the preview’s expectation that holding above 26% would confirm a durable mix shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin hit a record 27.8%, though management guided expectations back to the low-to-mid 20s range near term due to potential future EAC adjustments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “GM ~26–27%”; the preview said “Holding 26%+ confirms the mix shift is structural; slipping toward 22–23% suggests Q1 was a mix artifact.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated adjusted EBITDA of negative $4–8 million in its base case. Redwire remained loss-making on this measure, but the reported negative $3.2 million was better than that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$3.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Adj. EBITDA $(4)M to $(8)M”; the preview also said consensus expected it to remain negative.

surprises.description: The preview expected the FY2026 revenue range of $450–500 million to be reaffirmed without narrowing. Redwire did reaffirm it, but also reported visibility of about 90%, up from 75% after Q1, adding a more concrete signal of coverage than the preview had anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $450 million to $500 million”; “visibility now at ~90% versus 75% after Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “FY $450–500M reaffirmed but unnarrowed”; the preview called reaffirmation the key guidance outcome to watch.

surprises.description: The preview estimated shares outstanding at about 237.8 million and flagged ATM use as a risk. Redwire reported 249.9 million shares outstanding after $487.9 million in net ATM proceeds—more issuance than that share-count estimate implied—while the proceeds also sharply improved liquidity and reduced debt and interest expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash rising over 6x to $557.8 million (aided by $487.9 million in net ATM proceeds), total debt cut 75% to $48.9 million, and net interest expense falling to under $1 million from $23.8 million”; “common shares outstanding to 249.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated shares outstanding at “~237.8M now” and said to watch for “post-quarter ATM draws” under the “$500M ATM” program.

surprises.description: Redwire reported selection as one of 15 vendors on the $981 million NITE-STAR IDIQ, a strategic award not identified in the preview’s catalyst discussion. The preview’s named defense catalyst was potential conversion of Golden Dome/SHIELD positioning into a funded task order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Key strategic wins included selection as 1 of 15 vendors on the $981 million NITE-STAR IDIQ.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “named, funded” Golden Dome/SHIELD task order as the key upside catalyst; it did not mention NITE-STAR.

surprises.description: SpaceMD agreed to buy an entire SpaceX Starfall spacecraft, intended to launch in 2028 and carry up to 32 PIL-BOXes. This commercial opportunity was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SpaceMD's agreement to purchase an entire SpaceX Starfall spacecraft (launching 2028) capable of carrying up to 32 PIL-BOXes.”

surprises.description: Inventory rose 23% sequentially, with further increases expected in Q3 to support faster UAS delivery turnaround. The preview did not flag this operating investment or working-capital development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory rose 23% sequentially (with further increases expected in Q3) to support faster UAS delivery turnaround.”

in_line: Redwire reaffirmed the preview’s flagged FY2026 revenue guidance range of $450–500 million; the unexpected element was the reported increase in visibility.
Space revenue of $55.2 million was within the preview’s modeled $55–58 million range.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative, consistent with the preview’s expectation, although the reported loss was smaller than its base-case estimate.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $18.3 million, materially below the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly breakeven to slightly positive. Management attributed the result to pre-revenue operating and development costs ahead of new HPC capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was negative $18.3 million versus negative $4.1 million in Q1, reflecting pre-revenue operating and development costs ahead of new HPC capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “adj. EBITDA roughly breakeven to slightly positive”; the preview also said, “Positive adj. EBITDA on lower DR proceeds would be a genuine quality beat.”

surprises.description: Management said parent unrestricted liquidity of about $1.45 billion, including the Abernathy payment, was enough to fund near-term commitments without accessing equity markets. That is more reassuring than the preview’s central concern about equity dilution and its base case of funding being described but not finalized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Parent unrestricted liquidity of ~$1.45 billion including the Abernathy payment, sufficient to fund near-term commitments without accessing equity markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “the equity-dilution question is the central bear input”; the base case anticipated “funding described but not finalized.”

surprises.description: Wulf Compute’s estimated remaining capex is about $1.7 billion, versus the preview’s approximately $2.2 billion remaining as of Q1. The lower remaining amount is a favorable funding update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “~$1.7 billion of capex remaining and about two-thirds committed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “WULF Compute had ~$2.2B of capex remaining as of Q1 against $1.5B spent.”

surprises.description: Lake Mariner entered Q3 with 102 critical megawatts operating and CB-3 fully online, which is a firmer operational update than the preview’s concern about whether CB-3 had commenced rent and its request for a quarter-end MW count. CB-3 completion also made $600 million of Google credit support for FluidStack’s lease obligations effective.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Entered Q3 with 102 critical megawatts operating at Lake Mariner, with CB-3 fully online and its completion triggering effectiveness of $600 million of Google credit support for FluidStack's lease obligations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CB-3 rent commencement date (the single biggest swing factor)”; the preview said rent commencement depended on customer hardware deployment and called for “a hard number” of MW energized and rent-commencing at quarter-end.

surprises.description: FluidStack lease amendments add an expected $500 million-plus of lease revenue over the initial terms, including increased capacity at CB-4 and CB-5, in exchange for about $150 million of tenant fit-out costs. The preview discussed fit-out costs and the CB-4/CB-5 schedule but did not anticipate these amended economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FluidStack lease amendments require TeraWulf to contribute ~$150 million for tenant fit-out costs but are expected to generate over $500 million of incremental lease revenue over the initial lease terms, including capacity increases from 162 to 168 megawatts at CB-4 and CB-5.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 as-reported was ~50% vs. the ~85% long-term target; management attributed the gap to one-time tenant fit-out and pre-revenue JV costs”; the preview also listed CB-4 and CB-5 as targeted for 3Q/4Q26.

surprises.description: The Abernathy sale had been expected, but the preview cited a 4Q26 target; instead, TeraWulf had already received $250 million in July, with total proceeds of about $530 million. The remaining installments are still due later, through April 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Agreed to sell its 50.1% interest in the Abernathy joint venture for approximately $530 million, representing a 20% IRR, with $250 million received in July, $150 million expected by December 31 2026 and ~$130 million by April 30 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Abernathy JV targeted 4Q26”; the preview said to watch “closing timing, exact proceeds.”

surprises.description: TeraWulf expanded its Kentucky platform with the gigawatt-scale Muskie site, which could support up to 2 gigawatts and has initial electric service expected in Q4 2028. The preview did not flag this site or expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expanded the Kentucky platform via the gigawatt-scale Muskie site (potentially up to 2 gigawatts) with initial electric service expected in Q4 2028.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $44.8 million was essentially in line with the preview’s $44.71 million consensus estimate and within its alternative $46.02 million estimate; HPC lease revenue of $31.9 million was within the preview’s implied $30–33 million range.
The 401 MW Anthropic lease and approximately $19 billion of contracted revenue were already described in the preview as part of the announced build.

The preview anticipated another large noncash GAAP loss from Google warrant revaluation and explicitly cautioned that the GAAP headline should be ignored; the reported $755.7 million warrant-related loss fits that expectation.
Management reaffirmed its target to contract an additional 250–500 megawatts of critical IT capacity annually, matching the preview’s expected contracting cadence.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to be $417.8 million and within the company’s $405–430 million outlook, but it reached $443 million, above the outlook ceiling, on skilled-business outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue rose 12% year-over-year to $443 million, exceeding the company's outlook range driven by outperformance in skilled businesses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $417.8M”; company guide “$405–430M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was expected at 21.1%–21.5%, but came in at 20.7%, below the low end. The reported reasons included lower-margin energy mix, as well as prior-year workers’ compensation favorability and a government subsidy benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 20.7% from 23.6% a year earlier,” primarily due to “non-recurring prior-year workers' compensation favorability, a $3 million government subsidy benefit, and lower-margin energy revenue mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ... Company Guide ... 21.1%–21.5%”; preview called this “the single most important number.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was expected to be about $1–3 million, but rose to $11 million, more than tripling from the prior year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to $11 million from $3 million in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$1–3M (implied).”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s expectation of an adjusted loss, adjusted net income turned positive. The reported net loss included a non-cash write-down of the Tacoma headquarters, an unanticipated charge that partly obscured the adjusted improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a net loss of $3 million that included a $3 million non-cash write-down of its Tacoma headquarters, while adjusted net income turned positive at $2 million versus a $2 million loss a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | –$0.10.” The preview also said to watch for “any new ... impairment language.”

surprises.description: SG&A was expected to decline 1%–5%, but instead fell 7% while revenue grew 12%; all three segments also expanded profit margins, indicating stronger operating leverage than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A was reduced by 7% while revenue grew 12%, demonstrating improved operating leverage, and all three segments expanded profit margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected SG&A of “$85–89M (–1% to –5%).”

surprises.description: PeopleReady’s on-demand business did more than merely stabilize: it returned to growth across all four regions, and PeopleReady’s exit growth rate accelerated to 30%. This was stronger than the preview’s expectation of an on-demand inflection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The on-demand business returned to growth in the quarter, exiting with all four regions growing and a majority of territories now in growth for the year”; PeopleReady revenue growth accelerated “from +16% exiting Q1 to +30% exiting Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether on-demand was “actually inflecting” and noted that a majority of U.S. territories had returned to growth in Q1.

surprises.description: PeopleManagement improved from shrinking to growing by quarter-end, and management said July trends were similar to that exit rate. That is better than the preview’s expectation that the segment needed to stop shrinking.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PeopleManagement improved from -7% to +4%,” and “July trends [were] similar to the quarter's exit rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said PeopleManagement “needs to stop shrinking” and described Q1 as “–6% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook called for revenue growth of 7%–11%, with PeopleReady up 11%–15% and PeopleManagement up 3%–8%. The PeopleManagement growth range is notably better than the preview’s expectation that the segment was still soft; the overall guide also points to a stronger growth outlook than a merely consensus-bracketing case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 revenue growth of 7% to 11%, with segment ranges of +11% to +15% for PeopleReady, +3% to +8% for PeopleManagement, and -6% to +3% for PeopleSolutions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q3 guidance “bracketing consensus” was the base case and described PeopleManagement as needing to stop shrinking.

in_line: PeopleSolutions returned to a double-digit segment profit margin, as management had explicitly committed to for Q2.
PeopleSolutions revenue remained weak, declining 5%, broadly consistent with the preview’s warning that hiring volumes were subdued and its discussion of a 7% organic decline in Q1.

surprises.description: The preview estimated Q2 adjusted EBITDA of about $4.5 million ex-Movies, but SCOR reported only $1.3 million, with a 1.7% margin rather than the preview’s modeled 5.7%. The shortfall was especially sharp because largely fixed data and compensation costs magnified the impact of weaker revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA collapsed 85% to $1.3 million with margin falling to 1.7%”; management said “largely fixed data and compensation costs mean top-line underperformance has a disproportionate impact on the bottom line.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (ex-Movies) … ~$4.5M (5.7% margin).”

surprises.description: The preview expected Cross-Platform revenue of about $14.0 million, up 22%, but SCOR reported $12.5 million, down 2.1%. Management attributed the weakness to lower Proximic activation usage amid broader weakness across major buying platforms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cross-platform revenue declined 2.1% to $12.5 million, hurt by lower usage of Proximic activation products” and broader weakness across major buying platforms.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cross-Platform … $14.0M … +22%.” The preview also said that growth below roughly 15% would break the “growth engine offsets legacy decay” narrative.

surprises.description: Research and Insight Solutions fell further than the preview modeled: revenue was $11.5 million, down 9.2%, versus an estimate of $12.3 million and a 5% decline. The reported causes were lower renewals and delivery timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Research and Insight Solutions revenue dropped 9.2% to $11.5 million due to lower renewals and delivery timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Research & Insight Solutions … $12.3M … –5%.”

surprises.description: The FY2026 revenue range overlaps the preview’s expected range, but its low end is lower, and management added that it does not anticipate near-term growth while forecasting only a low-to-mid-single-digit adjusted EBITDA margin. The preview had not specified an EBITDA-margin guide or anticipated this explicit no-growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management lowered full-year guidance to “revenue of $315–325 million” with an adjusted EBITDA margin “only in the low-to-mid single digits,” and “does not anticipate near-term growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s expected FY26 range was approximately “$318–325M rev.” It also expected savings to phase in “progressively through fiscal 2027,” but gave no specific FY26 EBITDA-margin forecast.

surprises.description: The new CEO outlined specific growth initiatives the preview did not identify, including testing a next-generation local TV measurement platform this year and negotiating with AEO/GEO firms to monetize opt-in panel prompt data. These are early-stage opportunities without quantified financial impact, so their shareholder direction is uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: The CEO is directing investment toward “local TV measurement (testing a next-gen platform this year), creator media, activation expansion, and AI,” including “monetizing opt-in panel prompt data via negotiations with leading AEO/GEO firms.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $79.2 million was broadly in line with the preview’s approximately $78–79 million ex-Movies estimate.
The ROI realignment plan’s $20–25 million annual run-rate savings and $7–9 million of one-time severance-related charges matched the preview’s stated expectations.
Eliminating roughly $40 million of term debt with proceeds from the Movies sale was expected in the preview.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $210.4 million, above the preview’s $196.2–200.1 million consensus range and even the $203–207 million bull-case range. The 12.7% reported growth also substantially exceeded the mid-single-digit growth expected for the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 total revenue rose 12.7% year-over-year to $210.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $196.2M (+5.0% YoY)” and “$200.1M (+7.2% YoY)”; the bull scenario was “$203–207M (+9–11%).” Management’s prior framing was that Q1 revenue should grow “mid-single digits.”

surprises.description: The revenue beat was much less strong on an underlying basis: management attributed roughly $10–15 million to government-related orders pulled forward into Q1 and said normalized growth would have been mid-single digits. The preview described Q2 as the federal volume quarter, but management now expects Q2 revenue to be roughly flat year over year because of the pull-forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly $10-15 million of primarily government-related orders were pulled into Q1,” and “normalized growth would have been mid-single-digits.” Q2 revenue is expected to be “roughly flat versus the prior-year period due to the Q1 order pull-forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “US federal FY-end is Sept 30, so Q2 is the volume quarter”; the preview also said management was “monitoring for normalization.”

surprises.description: Reported operating margin expanded to 20.8%, far above the preview’s roughly 14.5% Q1 margin implication. The 660-basis-point expansion was attributed to favorable product mix and disciplined expense management.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 660 basis points to 20.8%,” reflecting “favorable product mix and disciplined expense management.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus EPS of $0.38 implies roughly flat-to-+30bps at ~14.5%” operating margin.

surprises.description: Cybersecurity grew only 0.6%, well below the preview’s expectation for low-double-digit growth with a contribution from DigiCert. The reported growth was also far below the preview’s cited FY26 Cybersecurity growth of 7.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cybersecurity grew only 0.6% against a tough prior-year comparison that had grown ~18%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With DigiCert adding ~$3.3M in Q1 … cyber needs to print low-double-digit growth.” The preview also cited FY26 Cybersecurity growth of “+7.8%.”

surprises.description: Service Assurance growth accelerated sharply to 19.7% and accounted for 67% of revenue, rather than resembling its slower recent growth. Management said the increase was driven by government orders and Omnis Sensor/Streamer sales, so it was not simply broad-based recurring acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Service Assurance revenue grew 19.7% (67% of total revenue), driven by government orders and Omnis Sensor/Streamer sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described FY26 Service Assurance revenue as “$547.0M, +2.6%.”

surprises.description: Federal government revenue reached the mid-teens as a share of Q1 revenue, far above its typical mid-to-high single-digit share. That concentration makes the quarter’s unusually strong results more dependent on government orders than the preview’s discussion of federal activity suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Federal government revenue, typically mid-to-high single-digit percent of total, spiked to mid-teens percent of revenue in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said federal had run at “the high end” in FY26 and that management was “monitoring for normalization.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS rose to $0.52, above both the preview’s $0.38–0.39 consensus and its stated $0.43–0.47 whisper range. This exceeded even the upper end of the preview’s bull-case EPS range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS jumping to $0.52 from $0.34 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The real bar on EPS is ~$0.43–0.47, not $0.38”; the bull scenario expected “$0.46–0.52.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2027 revenue guidance of $885–915 million and non-GAAP EPS of $2.65–2.80, matching the preview’s base-case expectation of a reaffirmation rather than a raise.
Gross margin was 80.6%, close to the preview’s cited 80.8% level and above its 79.5% downside watch threshold; the feared material gross-margin slippage did not occur.

The Arbor Cloud mitigation capacity increase to 33 Tbps and the acquisition’s immediate recurring-revenue contribution were consistent with the preview’s discussion of the 33 Tbps buildout and the deal’s expected accretion.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $249.7 million versus the preview's $32.54 million consensus, far above the expected range. The reported total included $126.4 million of accelerated Pfizer deferred revenue and a $50 million Pfizer approval milestone, neither of which was anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue of $249.7 million,” including “$126.4 million of accelerated Pfizer deferred revenue” and “a $50 million Pfizer milestone from VEPPANU's approval.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $32.54M” consensus; the preview said “residual Pfizer collaboration revenue is near zero” if the Rigel upfront was recognized.

surprises.description: Arvinas now expects its next PSP clinical trials for ARV-102 to begin in 2027, a setback from the preview's expectation that the FDA hold might be resolved in time for a late-2026 registrational-trial start.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA requested additional information before authorizing the Phase Ib trial,” and Arvinas expects to begin its next PSP clinical trials “in 2027 rather than 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called ARV-102 “resolved or near-resolved” the highest-priority issue and cited “potential to initiate a registrational trial in PSP in late 2026.”

surprises.description: The $62.5 million Rigel license revenue exceeded the preview's modeled $35 million upfront and possible $7.5 million transition payment. The call said only $35 million had been received, so the amount recognized in Q2 was higher than the preview's identified Rigel components.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 included “a $62.5 million Rigel license (of which $35 million was received).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Arvinas' share of the Rigel upfront was “$35M,” with a further “$7.5M” tied to transition activities.

surprises.description: ARV-806 will advance only through a partner, rather than under Arvinas' own funding. The preview focused on timing for initial Phase I data and did not anticipate this capital-allocation decision.
surprises.fact_evidence: Arvinas made the “strategic decision to advance its KRAS G12D program (ARV-806) only through a partner, citing capital allocation priorities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described ARV-806 as a wholly-owned pipeline asset and focused on its initial Phase I data being shared “later this year.”

surprises.description: Although initial ARV-393 data remains on track for year-end, the call said most patients were dosed below the expected efficacious range and the cohorts skew toward T-cell lymphoma. More mature monotherapy and combination data, including DLBCL patients, will not come until 2027, limiting the near-term readout.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Most patients were dosed below the expected efficacious range” and cohorts “skew toward T-cell lymphoma patients”; more mature data “including DLBCL patients” will be disclosed “in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected an ARV-393 Phase 1 update at a “2H26 medical congress” and noted early responses below predicted effective exposure.

surprises.description: The out-license still leaves Arvinas with a $52.7 million liability for VEPPANU development obligations, an obligation the preview did not flag when describing the asset as out-licensed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Arvinas booked “a $52.7 million liability for remaining VEPPANU development obligations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said VEPPANU was “out-licensed it entirely to Rigel” but did not mention remaining development obligations.

surprises.description: Cash ended below the preview's estimate, at $567.9 million versus an expected roughly $590 million. The company nevertheless maintained the expected runway into the second half of 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: Arvinas ended Q2 with “$567.9 million” in cash and securities, providing runway “into the second half of 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated cash and marketable securities at “~$590M” and said runway into 2H28 was expected to be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: The call disclosed single-agent activity for the HPK1 degrader in seven checkpoint-resistant preclinical models, a positive efficacy signal not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: ARV-6723 was described as “showing single-agent activity in 7 checkpoint-resistant preclinical models.”

in_line: Cash runway remained into the second half of 2028, as the preview expected.
Initial ARV-393 Phase I data remained on track for year-end 2026, broadly matching the preview's expected second-half 2026 update.
R&D expense of $52.6 million was close to the preview's $54 million estimate.
ARV-6723 was still on track to begin Phase I enrollment soon, consistent with the preview's mid-2026 initiation expectation.

surprises.description: AWR reported Q2 EPS of $1.09, well above the preview’s $0.93 consensus and $0.93–$0.96 base case. The 25.3% year-over-year increase was far stronger than the preview’s expected 6.9% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS rose 25.3% year-over-year to $1.09 from $0.87.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 EPS (diluted) | Consensus | $0.93 | +6.9% vs. $0.87”; “The base case is EPS $0.93–0.96.”

surprises.description: Golden State Water earned $0.91 per share, above the preview’s roughly $0.78 base case. Higher consumption and a better water-supply mix lifted results, whereas the preview’s base case assumed a modest net-negative supply-mix effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water segment (Golden State Water) earnings grew $0.18 to $0.91 per share”; EPS was “driven by new 2026 customer rates, a 4% increase in water consumption, and lower reliance on purchased water.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Water EPS $0.77–0.80, ASUS $0.15–0.17, electric $0.08–0.09”; “Rate increases carry the quarter and mix is a modest net negative.”

surprises.description: Electric segment EPS was $0.04, well below the preview’s expected $0.08–$0.09. This was a notable miss against the preview’s expectation, even though Electric earnings were up $0.01 year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Electric segment $0.04 (up $0.01).”

surprises.description: Revenue was about $181.3 million, based on the reported $18.2 million year-over-year increase from the preview’s cited $163.1 million comparison. That was above the preview’s roughly $175 million modeling estimate, though the preview cautioned that this was a derived, thinly sourced figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenue increased $18.2 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 Revenue | ~$175M (est.)”; “Treat it as a modeling anchor, not a published number.”

surprises.description: The new water rate-case filing included a request for approximately $1 billion in capital budgets for 2028–2030. The preview expected the filing and highlighted the capital ask as important, but did not state an expected request amount; the scale is notable against the cited $573.1 million authorized for 2025–2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Golden State Water filed a new water general rate case on July 1 requesting approximately $1 billion in capital budgets for 2028-2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If filed, the capital ask and rate base request are the single most important disclosures”; “Current authorized: $573.1M of capital for 2025–2027.”

surprises.description: A pending acquisition involves a Norwalk, California water system serving nearly 900 connections, with a proposed decision expected in Q4 2026. The preview did not flag this specific acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pending acquisitions include a Norwalk, California water system serving nearly 900 connections with a proposed decision expected in Q4 2026.”

in_line: ASUS contributed $0.16 per share, within the preview’s expected $0.15–$0.17 range; its full-year 2026 contribution projection of $0.63–$0.67 matches the preview’s stated guidance.
The preview expected the 2028–2030 water rate-case filing by July 1; Golden State Water filed on July 1.
The 11.3% compound annual growth in Golden State Water’s adopted average rate base matches the preview’s cited rate-base trajectory.
The $200 million ATM program’s completion and the company’s plan not to issue additional equity through at least year-end 2029 match the preview.
The 8.2% dividend increase and 72 consecutive annual increases were already described in the preview as completed and expected.
The company’s stated 2026 infrastructure-investment pace of $185 million to $220 million is broadly consistent with the preview’s $185 million to $225 million company-funded capex range.

surprises.description: The net loss was $4 million, or $0.27 per share, versus the preview’s expected loss of roughly $0.12–$0.15 per share and consensus EPS of -$0.13. The company attributed part of the wider loss to an $870,000 debt-extinguishment charge and $470,000 of severance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $4 million ($0.27 per share) versus a $1.5 million loss ($0.10 per share) a year ago, partly due to an $870,000 charge from debt extinguishment and a $470,000 severance charge.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) -$0.13”; the base scenario expected “EPS -$0.12 to -$0.15.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 44%, below the preview’s 45–48% base-case range and the 46.2% Q1 reference. The reported explanation was an unfavorable mix shift as higher-margin legacy search contracted and lower-margin audience modeling grew.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin compressed sharply to 44% from 75% a year ago, reflecting the shift in revenue mix as high-margin legacy search contracted and lower-gross-margin audience modeling grew.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “GM 45–48%”; the preview also flagged gross margin “vs. 46.2%.”

surprises.description: Despite the announced financing, quarter-end immediately available cash was only $886,000, while the additional $6.2 million remained restricted and undrawn pending redemption-related milestones. That leaves more of the reported financing unavailable for current liquidity than the preview’s financing reconciliation and roughly-a-year runway framing implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inuvo ended the quarter with only $886,000 in cash plus $6.2 million in restricted cash, with the restricted B note (at 5%) still undrawn and its release tied to milestones around redemptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected the “$12.97M financing” to be reconciled, including a “$6.2M note at 5%,” and said the July raise “bought roughly a year.”

surprises.description: Management gave a substantially lower cash-neutral-to-cash-positive revenue threshold for IntentKey—mid-$20 millions—and a target of reaching it sometime in 2027, recalibrating from the prior roughly $100 million breakeven level associated with legacy search. The preview had said that a dated breakeven path would be a material positive, but did not anticipate this lower threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects IntentKey to reach cash-neutral to cash-positive in the mid-$20 million revenue range, targeting that milestone sometime in 2027, a recalibration from the prior ~$100 million breakeven driven by legacy search.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any path-to-breakeven commentary with a date attached is a material positive”; the preview also said the base case had “no breakeven date.”

surprises.description: The company reported selling its Ranger QA tool for $450,000 in July, a cash-generating asset sale that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sold its Ranger QA tool for $450,000 in July.”

surprises.description: CFO Wally Ruiz is retiring, and Derric Ciccone is joining as President and CFO on August 17. The preview did not flag an executive transition, so its implications for continuity are unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Wally Ruiz is retiring after 16 years, with industry veteran Derric Ciccone … joining as President and CFO on August 17.”

surprises.description: Management described expanding IntentKey into workforce recruitment and the health-insurance open-enrollment market, neither of which the preview identified as a near-term opportunity. The potential is unquantified, so the significance is uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expanding IntentKey into workforce recruitment and a $150 billion health insurance open-enrollment market.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $7.5 million, close to the $7.76 million consensus and within the preview’s $7.4–$8.2 million base range; the sharp year-over-year decline was largely expected.

Audience Modeling / IntentKey grew 19% year over year, within the preview’s 15–20% base-case range and consistent with the expected strong double-digit growth, although below the preview’s 25%+ acceleration aspiration.

Legacy Search revenue was roughly $4 million after an 80% year-over-year decline, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of a sequential floor around $4 million and its forecast of continuing steep declines.

surprises.description: Q2 net loss was far smaller than the preview's $19–21 million estimate, and EPS was much better than the expected $0.23–$0.25 loss. The improvement was substantially helped by a $9 million non-cash warrant fair value gain, so the headline beat overstates the improvement in underlying operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $6 million ($0.07/share) from $23.5 million ($0.61/share), aided by a $9 million non-cash warrant fair value gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (loss) … ($0.25)” and “Net loss … $19M – $21M.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses came in materially below the preview's modeled $21–22 million range, at $18.6 million. The preview expected cost discipline and lower spending, but not a decline of this size versus its estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 operating expenses fell 19% to $18.6 million from $23.1 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … Opex ~$21–22M”; the model estimated R&D of $13.5–15.5M and G&A of $7.5–8.5M.

surprises.description: The FDA review advanced more cleanly than the preview's merely scheduled late-cycle review: it was completed, and the required pre-licensure inspections produced just one reported observation that Inovio believes it addressed. This is a favorable process update, though it does not resolve accelerated-approval eligibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA [has] completed its late cycle review meeting and all scheduled pre-licensure inspections that yielded only one reported observation, which Inovio believes it has addressed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Late-cycle review was scheduled for Q3 2026. Has it occurred? Was it clean?”

surprises.description: Inovio expects to begin label negotiations with the FDA in September, a more specific sign of advanced review progress than the preview's conditional possibility of labeling discussions. The preview had identified late-stage labeling talks as a soft positive tell.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inovio anticipates beginning label negotiations with the FDA in September 2026, signaling it believes it is in the final stages of the regulatory review process.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any information request, labeling discussion, or REMS conversation — late-stage labeling talks are a soft positive tell.”

surprises.description: The stated runway reaches only late Q1 2027, short of the preview's roughly mid-2027 estimate after the July raise. The company also says the cash should cover a potential launch, but the endpoint is less extended than the preview's modeled runway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The July 2026 public equity offering [netted] approximately $18.3 million, extending its cash runway into late first quarter 2027 and through a potential INO-3107 launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At ~$18M/qtr that funds into roughly mid-2027”; the preview also said to listen for an updated runway statement and flagged “into Q1 2027” as shorter than hoped.

surprises.description: The competitor's reported reach appears more limited than the preview's portrayal of PAPZIMEOS as a rapidly scaling, broadly established standard of care: the call said it had treated about 200 patients and achieved only low-single-digit penetration. That leaves a larger opening for INO-3107 than the preview's competitive framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Papzimios has achieved only low single-digit penetration with approximately 200 patients treated, leaving the vast majority of the prevalent RRP population open to a new treatment option.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “PAPZIMEOS did $53.1M in Q2 2026 revenue, up 145% sequentially”; the preview also described it as at a “$212M annualized run-rate” and “the new first-line standard of care.”

surprises.description: The call provided a concrete treatment-burden comparison not supplied in the preview: 83% of Papzimios Phase 1/2 participants needed at least one surgery during dosing, while INO-3107 does not require scoping or surgery during dosing. This supports a potential practical differentiation for INO-3107.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In Papzimios's Phase 1/2 trial, 83% of participants required at least one minimal residual disease surgery during the dosing window, whereas INO-3107 does not require scoping or surgery during dosing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked, “What is the differentiated clinical claim?” but did not identify this surgery-during-dosing comparison.

surprises.description: Inovio said that, if approved, INO-3107 is expected to receive seven years of orphan drug market exclusivity based on its differentiated delivery and mechanism of action. The preview did not flag this potential exclusivity as part of the investment case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “If approved, Inovio expects INO-3107 to receive seven years of orphan drug market exclusivity based on its differentiated delivery and mechanism of action.”

in_line: The FDA held the informal clinical meeting in July but did not comment on accelerated-approval eligibility because the application is under active review. The preview's base case anticipated a meeting with no resolution disclosed; it also highlighted that eligibility remained unresolved.
The October 30, 2026 PDUFA target date remained on track, as the preview expected.
The July offering's approximately $18.3 million of net proceeds was close to the preview's roughly $18 million post-offering estimate.

The preview already noted ApolloBio's positive VGX-3100 Phase 3 results in China and flagged possible milestone recognition; the call's report of positive top-line results and plans to pursue approval was not a new result surprise.
Fabry disease and hypophosphatasia were already listed in the preview as D-Prop platform targets, so adding them as targets and seeking partners was not a surprise.

surprises.description: The preview said Q3 revenue needed to reach at least $11 million to support FY26 consensus; Enovix guided to only $9–10 million. That is below the preview’s required ramp, even though it is above Q2 revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $9-10 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3'26 revenue guidance — needs ≥$11M to hold FY26 consensus.”

surprises.description: The preview expected non-GAAP gross margin around 25%, but Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 19.9%, down year over year. Management attributed the decline to South Korea product mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin was 19.9%, down year-over-year due to South Korea product mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin ~25% (unpub.).”

surprises.description: The preview looked for the smartphone qualification to remain on track for 2H26 system-level deployment, but the call said one final accelerated hybrid cycle-life test is expected only by year-end, before phone field testing. Cells did pass the 1,000-cycle test, so the test result was positive even as the stated sequence points to later field testing than the preview’s hoped-for deployment timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The lead smartphone customer independently confirmed cells passed more than 1,000 cycles on the 0.2C discharge test, with one final accelerated hybrid cycle life test expected to complete by end of 2026 before phone field testing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “‘on track for 2H26 system-level deployment’ vs. any softening”; the preview also says the target was “system-level deployment” in 2H26.

surprises.description: The preview expected Fab2 Zone 1 dicing yield to reach 90% with the mechanical dicer online this year; the reported yield was 84%. That is an improvement from Q1’s 80%, but it remains below the preview’s stated target and the throughput bottleneck persists.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Zone 1 dicing yield, the primary throughput bottleneck, improved to approximately 84% from 80% in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hybrid laser/mechanical dicing was supposed to reach 90% with the mechanical dicer online ‘this year.’”

surprises.description: Enovix said smart eyewear will have negative gross margins for the rest of 2026 as ramp overhead moves above the gross-margin line. The preview anticipated low-margin eyewear ramp volume but expected the company to sustain roughly 25% or better gross margin, not negative eyewear margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects smart eyewear to carry negative gross margins for the balance of 2026 as ramp overhead moves above the gross margin line before reaching scale.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sustaining ~25%+ while mixing in low-margin eyewear ramp volume matters.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the eyewear reference-platform ramp to begin in Q3, but Enovix had already shipped about 2,100 batteries in Q2 and reported a planned jump to about 19,000 packs in Q3, with a 50,000-unit order due for completion in Q4. The early Q2 shipment and disclosed Q3 volume make the ramp more concrete and earlier than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enovix shipped approximately 2,100 smart eyewear batteries to a Tier 1 customer in Q2 for its first eyewear revenue and expects to deliver ~19,000 packs in Q3 (a ninefold increase), part of a 50,000-unit order to be completed in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Did the A1 lead-customer reference-platform ramp start on schedule in Q3?” and “management targets only ~50,000 A1 units in 2026.”

surprises.description: The South Korea drone/defense/industrial pipeline was larger than the preview’s cited baseline: it grew from about $130 million to $183 million, with drones alone above $100 million and more than $40 million in active testing or design-in. The preview described a global pipeline above $130 million, but did not anticipate this reported growth and stage detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The South Korea drone/defense/industrial pipeline grew 41% to approximately $183 million from $130 million in Q1, with drones alone exceeding $100 million and over $40 million already in active testing or design-in stages.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “a stated >$130M global pipeline, >60% drone-linked.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $9 million, above the $8.43 million consensus and at the high end of company guidance. The preview characterized Q2 as close to a non-event, with consensus near the guide midpoint, so the reported result was a better-than-expected beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $9 million, up 21% year-over-year and 19% sequentially, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth and landing at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $8.43M” consensus; “Q2 itself is nearly de-risked … consensus sits at the midpoint.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating loss and EPS were at or better than the favorable ends of their ranges: non-GAAP operating loss was $28.8 million, slightly better than the $29–32 million guide, and EPS loss was $0.13 versus consensus loss of $0.14. The preview generally expected results around the guide and consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating loss was $28.8 million (better than the $29-32 million guidance) and non-GAAP net loss per share was $0.13, at the favorable end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS ($0.14)” consensus and “Non-GAAP loss from ops ~($30M)” consensus.

surprises.description: Cash use was lighter than the preview’s approximate $40 million quarterly burn expectation: operating cash use plus capital expenditures totaled about $31.4 million. Q2 capex itself was within the company’s $9–13 million guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with approximately $552.1 million in cash and marketable securities, used $21.8 million in operating cash, and had $9.6 million in capital expenditures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “burn near −$40M/qtr”; Q2 capex guide was “$9 – $13M.”

in_line: Q2 capex of $9.6 million was within the preview’s cited $9–13 million company guide.
Q3 non-GAAP operating loss guidance of $29–32 million and EPS loss guidance of $0.13–0.17 remained within the ranges already cited in the preview for Q2.

surprises.description: Abeona’s Q2 loss was worse than the preview’s expected range: the reported $20.2 million net loss and $0.35 loss per share exceeded the preview’s $13–16 million loss estimate and were below the EPS consensus range of –$0.23 to –$0.28.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss of $20.2 million ($0.35 per share)”

surprises.description: Five patients were treated in Q2, but low-yield and out-of-spec batches prevented revenue recognition on multiple treatments. That is a manufacturing-related revenue shortfall beyond the preview’s base case of 4–5 treatments and its bull case assumption that the manufacturing cycle ran cleanly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue was not recognized on multiple treatments due to a low-yield batch in Q2 and an out-of-spec batch in Q3”; commercial yields average “about 9 sheets per lot,” while batches yielding “fewer than 4 sheets” trigger no revenue recognition.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case is therefore 4–5 treatments”; the bull case required “the ~14-day biopsy-to-graft manufacturing cycle [to] run clean with no batch issues.”

surprises.description: Q2 net revenue of $11.4 million fell short of the preview’s $12.2 million consensus estimate, though it was within the preview’s $11–13 million base-case scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net ZEVASKYN revenue of $11.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net product revenue: ~$12.2M” consensus; base scenario revenue “$11–13M.”

surprises.description: Two scheduled biopsies were cancelled at the last minute because patients’ health deteriorated, and the slots could not be reassigned. The preview expected six Q2 biopsies to be scheduled and described only one or two treatments potentially slipping into July.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two scheduled biopsies were cancelled last-minute in Q2 due to patient health deterioration,” and “cancelled slots cannot be refilled by other patients.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “6 biopsies scheduled for Q2”; CFO had flagged that “1 or 2” could push into July treatments.

surprises.description: Management abandoned scheduled-biopsy indicators and will report only completed patients and recognized revenue, because the forward indicators proved unreliable. This reverses the preview’s view that biopsies performed were a cleaner demand signal than recognized treatments.
surprises.fact_evidence: Abeona is “shifting its reporting to anchor solely on completed patients treated and net revenue recognized,” abandoning scheduled-biopsy indicators that “proved unreliable for predicting revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Biopsies performed is the cleaner demand signal than treatments recognized — biopsy-to-treatment is a manufacturing-lag conversion, not a demand event.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was about 63%, below the preview model’s implied roughly 70% gross margin from its 30% COGS assumption. Management also gave a higher normalized margin outlook of 85–90% at full operating capacity, above that model assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margins were approximately 63%,” with “a normalized gross margin of 85% to 90% once full operating capacity is reached.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview model assumptions: “COGS ~30% of revenue.”

surprises.description: Cash and short-term investments ended Q2 at $146.8 million, below the preview’s estimated $150–155 million exit balance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Abeona “held $146.8 million in cash and short-term investments as of June 30, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash + ST investments (exit): ~$150–155M (my est.).”

surprises.description: Abeona quantified that its QTCs provide in-state access to roughly 40% of the addressable market, with additional out-of-state reach. The preview discussed the seven-center footprint but did not provide this access-coverage figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “now provides in-state QTC access to roughly 40% of its addressable market, with QTCs also serving a substantial portion of out-of-state patients.”

in_line: Five patients were treated in Q2, within the preview’s expected base case of 4–5 treatments.
The seventh QTC was activated, as the preview already reported Cincinnati Children’s activation and noted that the year-end target had been reached early.
CMS NTAP status was already disclosed in the preview as granted effective October 1, 2026.
QTC activation-to-first-treatment timing varied from a few months to as long as a year, broadly consistent with the preview’s warning that onboarding can take months and sometimes exceed a year.

surprises.description: Etsy marketplace GMS was $2.6 billion, up 7.5% year over year—above the preview’s $2.48–$2.53 billion company-guide range and its $2.55 billion bull-case threshold. The growth rate also exceeded the preview’s cited 3–5% guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Etsy marketplace GMS grew 7.5% year-over-year to $2.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Etsy marketplace GMS: $2.48–2.53B (co. guide, +3–5% Y/Y)”; “Bull: ≥$2.55B (+6%+).”

surprises.description: Revenue of $668 million exceeded the preview’s $645.1–$649.7 million consensus range by about $18–$23 million, although the preview cautioned that consolidated year-over-year comparisons were distorted by the divestitures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue was $668 million (up 9.3% for the Etsy marketplace stand-alone).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $645.1M (StockStory) / $649.7M (Zacks).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $195 million at a 29.2% margin, above the preview’s implied $174–$187 million and its 27–29% margin range. Nearly half of Etsy marketplace revenue growth flowed through to adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $195 million at a 29.2% margin, and nearly half of Etsy marketplace revenue growth flowed through to adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin | 27–29%”; “Implies ~$174–187M.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guide was tightened upward: its lower bound moved from 28% to 29%, while the upper bound remained 30%. The preview had described the 28–30% range as unchanged.
