surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was raised to mid-single-digit GMS growth with adjusted EBITDA margin tightened upward to 29%-30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA margin | 28–30% (unchanged).”

surprises.description: Take rate reached 25.9%, 20 basis points above the preview’s approximately 25.7% guide. The reported year-over-year increase included about 80 basis points from the Reverb divestiture, with additional gains from Etsy Ads and off-site ads.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Take rate reached 25.9%, up 130 basis points year-over-year, including roughly 80 basis points from the Reverb divestiture, with additional gains from Etsy Ads and off-site ads.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Take rate | ~25.7% (co. guide).”

surprises.description: Habitual and repeat buyer cohorts grew sequentially for the first time since 2023, a more specific frequency improvement than the preview’s expected second sequential increase in active buyers. The preview had identified repeat purchasing as a potential bull-case driver but did not forecast this cohort milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Habitual and repeat buyer cohorts showing sequential growth for the first time since 2023.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operationally, what each requires: Bull: buyer reactivation converting to repeat purchase”; “Active buyers — sequential direction: Up Q/Q, Y/Y decline narrowing toward flat.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that agentic AI traffic remained under 1% of total traffic, rather than providing evidence of a meaningful AI-commerce contribution. That puts a concrete, small scale on the AI channel the preview had identified as a key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Agentic AI traffic remains under 1% of total traffic.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Agentic commerce disclosure … Zero quantification so far”; “Any sizing of AI-referred GMS”; “Continued silence caps upside.”

surprises.description: Etsy announced a $2 billion new repurchase authorization, in addition to $578 million remaining, and bought back about $250 million in Q2—roughly 70% more than in Q1. The preview anticipated a new or upsized authorization but did not specify an authorization of this size or the accelerated quarterly pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a new $2 billion share repurchase authorization on top of $578 million remaining, after repurchasing approximately $250 million (3.9 million shares) in Q2, about 70% more than Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation … New/upsized authorization”; “An upsized buyback is the most likely ‘cushion’ if the operating print is merely in-line.”

surprises.description: Mobile app GMS growth accelerated to 12.5% year over year, above the preview’s cited Q1 rate of 11.2%, but app mix remained about 47%, below the preview’s 48% bogey.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mobile app GMS growth accelerated to 12.5% year-over-year, now representing about 47% of total GMS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “App GMS mix | ~47% of GMS, +11.2% Y/Y in Q1”; “Mix ≥48%, growth sustained.”

surprises.description: The company said investments in YouTube and TikTok drove a fivefold increase in visits from millennial and Gen Z audiences in the first half of 2026. The preview did not anticipate this quantified social-channel traffic result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Investments in YouTube and TikTok drove a fivefold increase in visits from millennial and Gen Z audiences in the first half of 2026.”

surprises.description: Etsy announced a workforce reduction of about 220 employees, or 12%, and expects roughly $35 million in restructuring charges. The preview did not flag a workforce restructuring or related charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restructuring and reducing its workforce by approximately 220 employees (about 12%) to roughly 1,600 people, incurring about $35 million in charges substantially complete by end of Q3 2026.”

in_line: Active buyers increased sequentially by 350,000 to approximately 87 million while remaining roughly flat year over year, consistent with the preview’s expectation of another sequential gain and a year-over-year decline narrowing toward flat.
Full-year GMS guidance moved to mid-single-digit growth, matching the preview’s stated buy-side expectation and its identified need for a second guide raise.
Depop’s sale closed on July 30 for about $1.4 billion in cash, as the preview had anticipated.

surprises.description: VSE reported $449 million of Q2 revenue, above the preview’s $432–440 million modeled range and $425 million consensus. The result was also above the preview’s $445 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $449 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My modeled base case (bottom-up, not consensus): revenue $432–440M”; the bull scenario forecast “$445M+.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $86 million with a 19.2% margin, well above the preview’s $78–81 million and 18.1–18.5% base case. The margin also exceeded the preview’s 18.9% bull-case threshold, clearing the key margin hurdle by more than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled, rising 98% to a record $86 million,” and margin expanded “approximately 320 basis points to a record 19.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My modeled base case” was “Adjusted EBITDA $78–81M (18.1–18.5%)”; the bull case was “$84M+ (18.9%+).”

surprises.description: VSE raised both full-year outlook ranges rather than merely reaffirming them: revenue growth guidance moved to 61–64% from 57–61%, and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance moved to 18.7–19.0% from 18.1–18.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 61%-64% (from 57%-61%) and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 18.7%-19% (from 18.1%-18.5%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said FY26 guidance would be “reaffirmed, not raised”; it described a revenue raise or margin-band lift as a bull-case outcome.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.75, above the preview’s $1.30–1.45 modeled range, even though equity issued for the PAG acquisition limited EPS growth relative to adjusted net income growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income rose 101% to $55 million,” while “adjusted diluted EPS grew only 33% to $1.75 due to share dilution from the equity-funded PAG acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My modeled base case” put “Adjusted EPS $1.30–1.45.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end adjusted net leverage was already 2.4x, below the preview’s roughly 2.9x base-case expectation and ahead of the stated goal of getting below 2.5x by year-end. Management also expected further deleveraging in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net leverage of 2.4x came in better than pro forma guidance, with management expecting further deleveraging in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “leverage ~2.9x”; it noted a goal of “<2.5x by year-end.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow was positive at about $19 million despite roughly $10 million of PAG transaction costs, somewhat better than the preview’s roughly breakeven base case and avoiding the feared repeat of Q1’s large outflow. Management expects stronger generation in the second half as working-capital intensity eases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was ~$19 million” and “stronger generation [is] expected in the second half as working capital intensity eases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case forecast “FCF roughly breakeven” and warned that “a second consecutive large outflow” would break the recovery narrative.

surprises.description: Management said most of the PAG synergies would benefit 2027 rather than 2026, limiting the near-term contribution. The preview had highlighted possible earlier synergy capture as an upside case, although its base case did not assume quantified new synergies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PAG synergies (initial run-rate expectation of ~$15 million) will mostly benefit 2027 rather than 2026,” and the guidance raise was “driven primarily by core business strength rather than synergy capture.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case cited “quantified PAG synergy capture ahead of the ‘>$15M annualized’ target”; its base case anticipated “no new quantification.”

surprises.description: The Pratt & Whitney Canada APU distribution agreement ramped ahead of expectations, a favorable program update. The preview had flagged the agreement’s ramp as something to watch but did not specify a benchmark for its pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Pratt & Whitney Canada APU distribution agreement ramped ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Program ramps,” including the “Pratt & Whitney Canada life-of-program exclusive distribution,” among the key metrics to watch.

in_line: Organic growth was approximately 14%, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of low-to-mid-teens organic growth ex-PAG.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $358 million, well above the preview’s $305–315 million estimate, and the 35.8% margin substantially exceeded the preview’s roughly 30.7–31.7% estimate. The margin was also above the preview’s 32% threshold for a clear beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 29% to $358 million, delivering a 35.8% margin (up 230 bps year-over-year), the second-highest margin in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (derived) ~$305–315M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin (derived) ~30.7–31.7%”; “32%+ would be a clear beat.”

surprises.description: Q1 revenue of more than $1 billion modestly topped the $992.5 million consensus estimate. Organic growth of 9% was at the top of the preview’s anticipated 6–9% range, rather than a material upside to that organic-growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 revenue exceeded $1 billion for the first time in company history, rising 21% year-over-year, with organic revenue up 9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales $992.5M”; the preview said consensus implied “~+6% to +9% organic growth.”

surprises.description: Management quantified $25–30 million of sales pulled forward into Q1, but said the buying was primarily in stormwater/nonresidential, whereas the preview expected the pre-buy to come from agricultural customers. The pull-forward also means some Q1 sales are not incremental demand and shift into Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $25-30 million of revenue was pulled forward from Q2 into Q1 as customers bought ahead of price increases, primarily in the stormwater/nonresidential segment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Q1 volumes may be elevated from agricultural customers buying ahead of announced price increases” and asked for “Q2 pre-buy payback quantification.”

surprises.description: Management said Q2 EBITDA margin will compress sequentially by more than the usual 300 basis points as resin changes from a benefit to a significant cost headwind, with costs peaking in Q2 and Q3. The preview anticipated margin and price-cost pressure generally, but not this specific larger-than-usual sequential compression and resin timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q2 EBITDA margin to compress sequentially by more than the typical 300 basis points as favorable resin costs flip to a significant headwind, with resin costs peaking in Q2 and Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “price/cost squeeze plus freight” as a bear-case risk and cited dollar-for-dollar pricing against material and transportation inflation, but did not forecast a greater-than-typical Q2 sequential margin decline.

surprises.description: Nonresidential organic sales grew 14% and management described the trend as modestly better than expected. That is an upside to the preview’s concern about the large-project pipeline and its characterization of demand strength as part of the bull case rather than the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nonresidential sales grew 14% organically, driven by resilient data center, warehouse, and commercial construction activity, and are tracking modestly better than expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the bear case required the “non-residential large-project pipeline to soften” and treated “real Allied/Wastewater strength” as a bull-case driver.

surprises.description: Residential organic sales were flat and performed modestly worse than anticipated, adding a weaker result to the preview’s already cautious view of affordability, rates, and uneven residential demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Residential organic sales were flat as affordability pressures and elevated interest rates weighed on demand, performing modestly worse than anticipated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described residential as “slowed” and “uneven” and flagged affordability and elevated interest rates as concerns.

surprises.description: The company returned nearly $250 million to shareholders in one quarter, including repurchasing 9.5 million shares amid stock-price dislocation. The preview highlighted accelerated repurchases as a possible swing factor but provided no expectation of a buyback at this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned nearly $250 million to shareholders in Q1, including dividends and the repurchase of 9.5 million shares amid stock price dislocation.”

surprises.description: Net leverage was about 1.5x, slightly below the preview’s stated 1.6x level, while available liquidity of about $901 million was below the preview’s $950 million-plus figure. Together these were a mixed, modest change in the balance-sheet picture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage stood at ~1.5x (below the 2x target), and available liquidity was approximately $901 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “leverage at 1.6x net” and “$950M+ liquidity.”

in_line: NDS contributed $95 million in revenue, within the preview’s estimated $85–110 million range for the seasonally strongest quarter; management also cautioned against annualizing that contribution.
Full-year guidance was maintained at $3.35–3.55 billion in net sales and $1.00–1.05 billion in adjusted EBITDA, matching the preview’s base expectation of an unchanged reaffirmation.
Pricing was expected to offset inflationary costs dollar-for-dollar, consistent with the preview’s description of management’s existing pricing approach.
CapEx guidance of approximately $200 million matched the preview’s stated FY2027 guidance.

surprises.description: INNOVATE reported Q2 revenue of $421.6 million, well above the preview’s roughly $373 million estimate. The $48.6 million gap is a substantial top-line beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue rose 74.2% year-over-year to $421.6 million, driven primarily by the Infrastructure segment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s real-bar table estimated “Total revenue” at “~373” million.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in at $46.3 million, more than twice the preview’s approximately $19.5 million estimate. This was a much larger earnings contribution from operations than the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total adjusted EBITDA nearly tripled to $46.3 million from $15.7 million in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Consolidated adj. EBITDA” of “~19.5” million.

surprises.description: Instead of the roughly $16 million net loss and $1.20 loss per share expected in the preview, INNOVATE reported net income and positive diluted EPS. The swing from an expected loss to a profit is a major earnings surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company swung to net income of $10.4 million ($0.71 per fully diluted share) versus a net loss of $22 million ($1.67 per share) a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net loss attrib. / EPS” at “~(16) / (1.20).”

surprises.description: DBM Global delivered $414 million of revenue versus the preview’s $365 million Infrastructure estimate, while its adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 11.8%. That sharply contrasts with the preview’s concern that large-project mix was diluting margins and its roughly 6.6% implied Q2 margin estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DBM Global posted record Q2 revenue of $414 million (up 77.6%) and adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding roughly 350 basis points to 11.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Infrastructure revenue of “365” million and adjusted EBITDA of “24” million, and said to watch whether margin dilution continued; its Q2 estimate implies an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 6.6%.

surprises.description: Infrastructure adjusted backlog reached $2.7 billion, far above the preview’s $1.8 billion reference point. The preview treated a result below roughly $1.7 billion as a break in the visibility narrative, whereas the reported figure indicates a substantial increase in forward coverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Infrastructure adjusted backlog grew to $2.7 billion from $1.8 billion at year-end 2025, providing revenue visibility into 2027 and 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described adjusted backlog as “was $1.8B” and said “Below ~$1.7B adjusted would break the ‘durable visibility’ narrative.”

surprises.description: Life Sciences revenue was $2.2 million, below the preview’s $2.5 million estimate, and R2’s backlog was only about 110 systems worth $1.4 million rather than the preview’s roughly 160 systems worth about $2 million. The call also attributed weaker unit sales to liquidity constraints, rather than reporting the expected backlog conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Life Sciences revenue fell 31.3% to $2.2 million as R2 experienced lower Glacial FX and Glacial Spa unit sales due to liquidity constraints”; “R2 ended the quarter with backlog of about 110 systems (~$1.4 million of future revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Life Sciences revenue of “2.5” million and described “~160-system backlog worth ~$2M,” asking whether it would convert to revenue.

surprises.description: Cash was lower than both the preview’s Q1 consolidated cash figure and the year-end balance cited in the call, indicating further cash depletion against an already highly emphasized liquidity concern. The call also reported higher principal indebtedness, though the preview had already warned about debt growth from PIK interest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents declined to $87.8 million from $108.2 million at year-end 2025, while total principal indebtedness rose to $626.4 million driven by PIK interest at the nonoperating and Life Sciences segments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “consolidated $134.6M” cash at Q1 and emphasized “Corporate liquidity and the September wall,” while noting that consolidated cash was trapped at subsidiaries.

in_line: The CONX/Broadcasting transaction terms broadly matched the preview: INNOVATE retained about 25% and CONX committed up to $75 million of post-closing equity capital, consistent with the preview’s focus on confirmation of the $75 million commitment and retained stake.

surprises.description: Five9 reported $312 million of Q2 revenue, above the preview’s $306.6 million consensus and the $309 million high end of company guidance. The beat was stronger than the preview’s base-case range, though it landed within its bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $312 million” and was “above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus revenue of “$306.6M,” company guidance of “$303.0M – $309.0M,” and a base case of “$307–310M.”

surprises.description: AI revenue grew much faster than the preview’s base case, reaching a run rate above $150 million. Five9 also raised its full-year AI growth outlook to at least 60%, versus the prior commitment of more than 40% and the preview’s expected range of roughly 55–65% for the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI revenue grew 78% year-over-year to approximately $39 million (over $150 million annual run rate)” and management “raised full-year 2026 AI growth guidance to at least 60% year-over-year, up from a prior outlook of more than 40%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for AI ARR “at/above ~$140–150M,” described a base case of “AI ~+55–65%,” and noted the existing FY outlook of “AI revenue growth >40% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance came in above the preview’s base-case range and directional Street figure, exceeding even the preview’s bull-case threshold. That is a stronger signal for the expected second-half ramp than the preview’s central case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to a $319 million midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a directional next-quarter figure of “roughly $313M,” a base case of “$312–317M,” and a bull case of “Q3 guided ≥$318M.”

surprises.description: A Fortune 100 financial-services customer signed a large multiyear deal that the preview did not anticipate. Its eventual subscription ARR is meaningful, but the company expects negligible contribution in 2026 and the ramp mainly from 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: The win has “approximately $100 million total contract value over 5 years,” is expected to “ramp to roughly $25 million in subscription ARR,” and has “negligible 2026 contribution” with meaningful increases beginning in 2027.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross and EBITDA margins were both weaker than the preview’s margin benchmarks, despite the stated FY EBITDA-margin target above 24%. Management attributed the pressure to temporarily expanded professional-services capacity for faster AI deployments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin fell to 61% from 63% a year ago and adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 22% from 24%,” pressured by “temporary expansion of professional services capacity to meet accelerated AI deployments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited an FY adjusted EBITDA-margin guide of “>24%,” a consensus-derived range of “~23–24%,” and flagged “Margin and FCF durability” as a key issue.

surprises.description: CCaaS growth was 7%, a little below the preview’s 8% reference point. However, the operating details were reassuring on the seat-compression concern: agent seats grew roughly in line and subscription revenue per seat increased in the single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CCaaS revenue grew a stable 7% year-over-year,” with concurrent agent seat count “growing roughly in line” and subscription revenue per seat “increasing in the single digits, showing no seat compression.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said legacy CCaaS “grew only +8%” in Q1 and flagged whether AI was “substituting rather than adding” and whether seat compression was outrunning AI attach.

surprises.description: Although subscription retention remained at the expected 107%, management now expects it to rise by about one percentage point in Q3. That near-term improvement, driven by backlog, is more encouraging than the preview’s base case of steady retention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LTM subscription dollar-based retention rate held steady at 107% and is expected to inflect up by approximately 1 percentage point in Q3, driven by existing backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “DBRR steady at 105/107%” and said subscription-only DBRR “ticking to 108% would confirm AI is expanding wallet share.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was only 5% of revenue, a weak result against the preview’s focus on FCF durability and its cited Q1 conversion of 16%. The facts provided do not indicate whether this reflected timing or a more persistent change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was $15 million (5% of revenue)” with $654 million in cash and investments.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Margin and FCF durability” and cited Q1 FCF of “$49M (16% of revenue).”

in_line: Subscription revenue grew 14% year over year, consistent with the preview’s key threshold of sustained growth at 13% or higher.
Subscription dollar-based retention held at 107%, matching the preview’s base case of steady 107% retention.

Full-year revenue guidance moved to a $1.266 billion midpoint, matching the preview’s base-case upper-end expectation of $1.262–$1.266 billion, though it was below the bull-case threshold of at least $1.270 billion.

The $90 million ASR had an initial delivery of about 80% of the expected shares, in line with the preview’s expectation that the repurchase would be underway through Q3; the additional $200 million authorization remained available.

surprises.description: Q2 collaboration revenue was $65 million, above the preview’s $48–55 million estimate, as the $20 million Sanofi KT-485 milestone landed alongside the expected $45 million Gilead fee. The preview allowed for the Sanofi milestone in its bull case, but not in its base estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 collaboration revenue was $65 million, comprising a $45 million Gilead option exercise fee and a $20 million Sanofi milestone for KT-485 entering Phase I.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $48–55M” from “Gilead $45M option milestone + ongoing collaboration amortization; upside if Sanofi KT-485 Phase 1 dosing milestone also lands.”

surprises.description: Kymera reported a much broader Phase III execution build-out than the preview described: it is developing capabilities for potentially more than 10 Phase III studies over the next two to three years. The preview focused on KT-621’s planned Phase III start and funding, not this potential scale of future trials.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is building capabilities to execute potentially more than 10 Phase III studies over the next 2-3 years.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed leadership transitions beyond the already-announced appointment of Terence Rooney: CMO Jared Gollob is retiring, and the board chair is transitioning to Felix Baker. The preview anticipated Rooney’s first appearance but did not flag Gollob’s retirement or the chair transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chief Medical Officer Jared Gollob is retiring (staying as adviser through year-end), succeeded by Terence Rooney from J&J, alongside a board chairman transition to Felix Baker.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s secondary watch list mentioned “new CMO Terence Rooney (appointed Jul 27) presenting for the first time.”

surprises.description: Kymera specified that KT-579 healthy-volunteer data should come before BROADEN-2’s atopic-dermatitis data later in the second half of 2026. The preview expected KT-579 data in 2H26 but did not establish this order of catalysts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The IRF5 (KT-579) healthy volunteer data is expected to be released before the BROADEN-2 atopic dermatitis data later in the second half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described KT-579 healthy-volunteer data as “guided 2H26” and a “Q3/Q4 catalyst,” without specifying that it would precede BROADEN-2.

surprises.description: R&D expense was above the preview’s estimate, although the gap was much smaller excluding stock compensation: reported R&D was $119.5 million versus a $102–108 million estimate, while the ex-stock-comp figure was $109.1 million. That points to a modestly higher underlying spend than the preview modeled, with stock compensation accounting for much of the reported gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses were $119.5 million ($109.1 million excluding stock comp), up 22% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “R&D $102–108M” and said Q1 was $98.2M, “+18% q/q on a cash basis.”

in_line: BROADEN-2 enrollment completion and the year-end 2026 top-line timing were consistent with the preview’s expectation that management would reaffirm the accelerated year-end readout; the planned Phase III start around mid-2027 was also in line.

Cash and investments of approximately $1.5 billion and runway into 2029 matched the preview’s $1.50–1.53 billion cash estimate and expectation of runway into 2029. The preview also expected funding for both Phase 2b trials and substantial Phase III spending.
KT-579 data timing and its stated goals of greater than 90% IRF5 degradation and 50–80% inflammatory-biomarker reduction were in line with the preview’s 2H26 timing and stated target ranges.
Management’s expectation that KT-621 efficacy would be in the ballpark of dupilumab’s week-16 results matched the preview’s stated efficacy bar for a dupilumab-like result.
The BREADTH asthma program’s late-2027 top-line timing was consistent with the preview’s watch for progress against the late-2027 guide.

surprises.description: The preview implied roughly 7% organic growth and $4.95 billion of revenue; Aramark reported 9% organic growth and $5.0 billion. Management said growth would have been about 11% without the education calendar shift, which it expects to be fully recaptured in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 organic revenue grew 9% to $5 billion,” and would have risen “approximately 11% excluding a calendar shift in education that is expected to be fully recaptured in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said consensus implied “~7%” organic growth and listed Q3 revenue consensus of “$4.95B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was above both the $0.48 consensus and the preview’s inferred $0.50–$0.51 whisper range. The reported $0.52 also rose nearly 30% year over year, versus the 20% growth implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose nearly 30% to $0.52,” or “almost 45% excluding the calendar shift.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EPS consensus of “$0.48” and inferred a buy-side bar of “$0.50–0.51.”

surprises.description: Aramark raised its FY26 organic revenue growth outlook to 9%–10%, above the prior guidance’s high end of 9%. This exceeded the preview’s base case of holding the organic outlook at the high end of the existing range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aramark raised its fiscal 2026 organic revenue growth outlook to 9%-10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described guidance in force as “high end of 7–9%” and its base case as “FY organic reaffirmed at high end.”

surprises.description: The Nexus opportunity was quantified with an expanded first-site scope and additional sizable sites: the first site’s annualized value rose from about $100 million to $140 million, and a second larger site is expected at about $160 million annually. Three mobilizing sites are expected to reach $400–$500 million in annualized revenue during FY27–28, with above-company-average margins and low capital intensity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Aramark Nexus hyperscaler contract scope increased approximately 40%,” taking the first site from “about $100 million to roughly $140 million,” with “a second larger site expected at around $160 million per year.” Three sites are expected to generate “$400-$500 million” annualized revenue in FY27–28 “at above-company-average margins with low capital intensity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Nexus as having “several hundred million dollars of annualized revenue potential” and said that quantifying the contract was a key item to watch.

surprises.description: The near-term Nexus contribution appears limited despite the large longer-term opportunity: the preview highlighted revenue starting in FY26 and the possibility of including Nexus in FY26 guidance, while management said Nexus would contribute about 1% of revenue in Q4 and that none of the signed sites was fully ramped.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nexus is expected to contribute approximately 1% of revenue in Q4,” with “eight total sites signed” and “none yet fully ramped”; the three actively mobilizing sites are expected to ramp in FY27–28.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Nexus had “revenue starting this fiscal year” and flagged the possibility of folding it into FY26 guidance.

surprises.description: Year-to-date new client wins were substantially above the preview’s cited $1 billion record level, reaching more than $1.6 billion and increasing 51% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date new client wins totaled more than $1.6 billion, up 51% versus the prior year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “a record $1B of YTD new-business wins now mobilizing.”

surprises.description: International delivered stronger organic growth and AOI growth than the preview’s consensus growth rates, with nearly 60 basis points of constant-currency margin expansion. The reported revenue figure was about $1.5 billion versus the preview’s $1.52 billion estimate, so the surprise is in the underlying growth and profitability rather than reported revenue dollars.
surprises.fact_evidence: International posted “11% organic revenue growth to $1.5 billion with AOI up 24% and margins expanding nearly 60 basis points on a constant currency basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed International revenue consensus of “$1.52B” and AOI growth consensus of “+21.2%.”

surprises.description: Management signaled that FY27 organic growth should exceed the company’s prior 5%–8% algorithm, giving an above-algorithm outlook beyond the preview’s request for initial FY27 framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “signaled fiscal 2027 growth above its prior 5%-8% organic revenue algorithm.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “first FY27 framing” as a possible catalyst but did not anticipate a specific outlook above the prior algorithm.

surprises.description: Management described 30–40 basis points of ongoing core-business margin accretion, with Nexus adding a further tailwind; this is stronger than the preview’s roughly 25–30 basis-point Q3 margin-expansion estimate, though the periods are not exactly comparable.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects to continue delivering “30-40 basis points of core-business margin accretion, with Nexus providing an additional tailwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s derived Q3 expectation was “~+25–30 bps of expansion.”

in_line: Adjusted operating income of $261 million was near the preview’s derived consolidated AOI estimate of approximately $258–262 million.
FY26 AOI growth guidance of 12%–17% and adjusted EPS growth guidance of 20%–25% were reaffirmed, as the preview’s base case anticipated.
Client retention remained around the preview’s flagged level: the preview noted retention above 98% at Q2, and the call reported approximately 98%.

surprises.description: CVRx cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $58–60 million from the previously stated $63–67 million range, well below the preview’s $65.28 million consensus, and guided to only $13.5–14.5 million of Q3 revenue. This is a much weaker second-half outlook than the preview’s expected reaffirmation or possible increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $58-60 million and guided Q3 revenue to $13.5-14.5 million, signaling a weaker second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue: $65.28M”; company guide “$63–67M”; the preview’s base case expected guidance “Narrowed to $64–67M,” and its bear case “Reaffirmed, or trimmed to $61–65M.”

surprises.description: The company attributed the outlook cut primarily to a severe salesforce ramp problem: roughly 60% of quota-carrying territory managers joined within 18 months, and some high-turnover, least-tenured regions have negative implant growth. The preview expected territory growth and discussed productivity, but did not anticipate this scale of onboarding disruption; seasoned regions are still delivering strong double-digit growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 60% of quota-carrying territory managers joined within the last 18 months, straining onboarding and slowing productivity ramps, which is the primary driver of the guidance cut”; in the highest-turnover regions “implant growth is actually negative year-to-date,” while stable, seasoned regions “continue to post strong double-digit growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated “~3 US territories/quarter (56 → ~59)” and described the base case as “H2 acceleration asserted but not evidenced”; it did not flag onboarding disruption or negative implant growth in certain regions.

surprises.description: The largest Medicare Advantage payer’s approval rate sharply deteriorated after introducing AI-based prior authorization tools, falling from about 80% to roughly 25% and remaining below 30% despite CVRx’s responses. That is a significant payer-specific setback against the preview’s expectation that approvals would reach at least 55%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The largest Medicare Advantage payer's 30-day approval rate collapsed from roughly 80% to about 25% in February-March after AI-based prior authorization tools were implemented, and it remains below 30% despite company countermeasures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything ≥55% validates that Category I CPT codes structurally fixed the denial problem. A stall near 50% reopens the reimbursement bear case.”

surprises.description: A DOJ civil investigative demand concerning certain sales and marketing practices was not anticipated in the preview. The company is cooperating while also undergoing a CFO transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received a DOJ civil investigative demand in May 2026 related to certain sales and marketing practices, and is undergoing a CFO transition while cooperating with the investigation.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $15.7 million was slightly below the preview’s $15.8 million estimate and the high-end seasonal/buy-side bar of about $16.1 million, although it was marginally above the stated consensus range. The quarter was therefore close to consensus but missed the preview’s more demanding expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $15.7 million, up 16% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2'26E” total revenue was “$15.8M”; the preview also said normal seasonality put Q2 at “$16.1–16.3M” and that “the buy-side whisper is effectively the top of the guide.”

surprises.description: Despite the sharp deterioration at the largest payer, the overall 30-day Medicare Advantage approval rate reached 60%, above the preview’s 55% validation threshold. Humana approvals exceeding 90% helped lift the aggregate rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Overall 30-day Medicare Advantage prior authorization approval rate rose to 60% in Q2 2026 from 44% in 2025, aided by the Humana coverage policy where approvals now exceed 90%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything ≥55% validates that Category I CPT codes structurally fixed the denial problem”; the preview described approvals of roughly “52–55%” in its base case.

surprises.description: Traditional Medicare is now paying approximately 96% of submitted Barostim claims across all seven Medicare administrative contractors, and the inpatient payment rate is set to rise from $43,000 to $45,000 on October 1. The preview noted reimbursement advances but did not anticipate these specific payment and claims-acceptance figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Traditional Medicare now pays approximately 96% of submitted Barostim claims across all seven Medicare administrative contractors, and the inpatient payment rate rises from $43,000 to $45,000 effective October 1st.”

surprises.description: Gross margin came in at 87%, above the preview’s 86–86.5% expectation and at the top of the previously stated 85–87% full-year range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improving to 87% from 84% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 gross margin at “86.5%” and cited a prior company guide of “85–87% (FY).”

surprises.description: CVRx lowered full-year operating expense guidance to $99–101 million. The preview had no stated full-year expense estimate, so the revision is new information, though the material provided does not quantify the change from the prior expense outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year operating expense guidance was lowered to $99-101 million.”

surprises.description: The quarter-end cash balance was higher than the preview’s estimate, but the stated runway was shorter than the preview’s cited expectation of more than two years. The $40 million undrawn debt capacity was consistent with the preview’s description of available financing capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and equivalents stood at $64.6 million (estimated 18+ months of runway) with $40 million still undrawn on the debt facility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Q2-end cash” of “~$60–62M” and said management was “claiming 2+ years of runway”; it also cited “~$40M” of available facility capacity.

in_line: Q2 revenue growth of 16% year over year was broadly in line with the preview’s estimate of approximately 16% growth, even though the $15.7 million total was below its high-end seasonal expectation.

surprises.description: KNF raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $3.4–$3.6 billion, lifting both ends of the prior $3.3–$3.5 billion range. The preview had identified a guidance revision as a key issue but did not specify that revenue guidance would be raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $3.4–$3.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The market will look for a formal raise or narrowing of the $3.3–3.5B revenue / $520–560M adjusted EBITDA ranges.”

surprises.description: Despite revenue growth, adjusted EBITDA was flat as reported, rather than following the preview’s more optimistic setup of results trending toward the upper half of the full-year EBITDA range. Excluding asset-sale gains, EBITDA grew 7%, as the prior-year Beaumont gain was much larger than this year’s.
surprises.fact_evidence: “As-reported adjusted EBITDA was flat versus last year”; excluding asset-sale gains, “adjusted EBITDA rose 7%,” with a “$10.3 million prior-year Beaumont, Texas property gain versus only $0.6 million this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “In May [management] said that results are ‘trending toward the upper half’ of both ranges.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the $520–$560 million adjusted EBITDA range but said results were trending toward its midpoint, a step down from the preview’s report of management expecting the upper half. That is a weaker outlook within the unchanged range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed adjusted EBITDA guidance of $520–$560 million while signaling results are trending toward the midpoint rather than the upper end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “In May [management] said that results are ‘trending toward the upper half’ of both ranges.”

surprises.description: KNF reported roughly $24 million of Q2 external headwinds from higher energy costs, delayed Texas, Hawaii, and Alaska projects, and the timing or type of incentive-bearing work. The preview highlighted weather as a possible downside scenario but did not flag these specific pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Three external headwinds totaling roughly $24 million in Q2: ~$6 million from higher energy costs, ~$10 million from delayed projects (Texas, Hawaii, Alaska), and ~$8 million from unfavorable project type/timing of incentives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A repeat of last year's Q2 guidance cut (weather, Oregon economy) is the key downside scenario.”

surprises.description: Aggregates volume grew 14%, materially faster than the preview’s mid-single-digit aggregates growth assumption. Mix-adjusted pricing rose 8%, but reported pricing was only up 3% because of a large sale of lower-priced natural fines.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aggregate volumes grew 14% (75% organic, 25% from acquisitions) with product-mix-adjusted pricing up 8%, though as-reported pricing rose only 3% due to a 630,000-ton sale of lower-priced natural fines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance assumes mid-single-digit aggregates price/volume growth.”

surprises.description: The company cut its expected full-year aggregate margin expansion to about 100 basis points from its prior 200-basis-point target, citing higher delivery volumes and fuel surcharges booked at cost. The preview had not flagged a reduction to this margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aggregate margin expansion guidance for the year was lowered to roughly 100 basis points from a prior 200-basis-point target, pressured by 41% higher delivery volumes and fuel surcharges booked at cost.”

surprises.description: Diesel added about $10 million of year-over-year cost, but only $4 million was recovered through Q2 fuel surcharges; management expects another roughly $4 million to be recovered through DOT escalators in Q3. The preview did not discuss these cost increases or the timing of recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Higher diesel prices added about $10 million in costs year-over-year, of which $4 million was recouped via fuel surcharges in Q2 and another ~$4 million is expected to be recovered through DOT escalators in Q3.”

surprises.description: The Strata acquisition is now expected to have a record 2026 and exceed its original EBITDA projections by more than 15%, supported by a record North Dakota DOT budget. The preview discussed acquisition contributions generally but did not anticipate this specific outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Strata acquisition is expected to deliver a record 2026, outperforming original EBITDA projections by more than 15%, supported by a record North Dakota DOT budget.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 Mountain-segment deals … plus earlier acquisitions underpin the ~12% expected revenue growth.”

surprises.description: Ready-mix volumes were in line with the preview’s mid-teens expectation, but the call also reported 6% lower production cost per cubic yard and 21% higher gross profit. Asphalt volumes and gross profit rose 24% each, an additional operating strength not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ready-mix volumes rose 15% … with production costs down 6% per cubic yard and gross profit up 21%; asphalt volumes rose 24% with gross profit up 24%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance assumes … mid-teens ready-mix volume growth.”

surprises.description: Net leverage was 3.2x at Q2, up from 2.9x at Q1, rather than holding at the level cited in the preview while the market watched acquisition-related leverage. Management expects to finish 2026 near its 2.5x long-term target and with no revolver borrowings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ended Q2 at 3.2x net leverage (vs. 3.1x a year ago), and expects to finish 2026 near its 2.5x long-term target with no revolver borrowings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net leverage 2.9x (StockTitan 8-K summary)”; “watch the organic vs. acquired split and leverage (2.9x net at Q1).”

surprises.description: KNF amended its Term Loan B to add $400 million at a lower rate, a financing development the preview did not anticipate. The facts provided do not quantify the interest savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company amended its Term Loan B to add $400 million at a lower rate.”

in_line: Ready-mix volume growth was 15%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of mid-teens ready-mix volume growth.
Q2 revenue growth was 13%, close to the preview’s approximately 12% year-over-year consensus growth estimate.

surprises.description: Twilio reported $1.5 billion of revenue, up 22% reported and 17% organically, well above the roughly $1.42 billion consensus and the 10%-11% Q2 organic-growth guide. Organic growth also exceeded the preview’s 13% upside marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached a record $1.5 billion, up 22% year-over-year reported and 17% organically, marking another quarter of organic growth acceleration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus ~$1.42B”; “Organic rev growth +10% to +11%”; and “Organic growth ≥13% vs. 10–11% guide.”

surprises.description: The full-year organic-growth outlook was raised to 13%-13.5%, well beyond the preview’s expected raise to roughly 11%-12% and above its 11.5% bull-case threshold. Reported-growth guidance was also raised to 18%-18.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Twilio raised full-year organic revenue growth guidance to 13%-13.5% from 9.5%-10.5% previously, and reported growth to 18%-18.5% from 14%-15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The functional whisper is … a FY organic raise to ~11–12%”; “Bulls need FY organic taken to ≥11.5%.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP operating income reached a record $285 million, beating the preview’s roughly $255 million consensus and the company’s $250-$260 million guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record non-GAAP income from operations of $285 million (up 29% YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op income … $250–260M” and “Consensus ~$255M.”

surprises.description: Twilio generated record free cash flow of $353 million and raised its full-year FCF guide to $1.135-$1.155 billion, above the prior $1.08-$1.10 billion range. The preview had highlighted that Q1’s $132 million FCF left substantial weighting for the rest of the year, but gave no Q2 FCF consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record free cash flow of $353 million”; “free cash flow guidance also raised to $1.135-$1.155 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$132M FCF in Q1 against a $1.08–1.10B FY target means heavy 2H weighting”; FY FCF target was “$1.08–1.10B.”

surprises.description: The reported gross margin fell to 49.1% as $71 million of U.S. carrier pass-through fees weighed on it, while those fees contributed about 10 points to messaging growth and 5 points to DBNE. This made the headline mix look weaker, though underlying messaging still grew about 18%, underlying DBNE improved, and margins would have risen year over year excluding the fees.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Incremental U.S. carrier pass-through fees of $71 million pressured non-GAAP gross margin to 49.1% (down 160 bps YoY), though margins would have risen 60 bps YoY excluding these fees”; messaging grew “28% (about 18% excluding roughly 10 points from carrier pass-through fees)”; “roughly 5 points” of DBNE came from carrier fees.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin (50% in Q1)”; “Watch gross profit growth vs. revenue growth”; and “Bear is any sign that the Q1 acceleration was A2P fee pass-through and acquisition arithmetic rather than underlying demand.”

surprises.description: Self-serve revenue grew over 30%, above the preview’s roughly 25% expectation, while total software add-ons grew over 25% and Verify accelerated to over 30%. The preview identified software attachment as an important watch item but did not give a specific Verify growth forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Self-serve revenue grew over 30%”; “total software add-ons grew over 25%”; “Verify accelerated to over 30% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Look for … AI/software attach”; “self-serve and ISV channels each +25%.”

in_line: DBNE rose to 116%, meeting the preview’s 115%+ confirmation threshold; the call also said underlying DBNE continued to improve about 1 point quarter over quarter.
Voice growth accelerated above 20% and branded calling had triple-digit growth, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of voice growth above 20% and triple-digit branded-calling growth.
ISV revenue grew over 25%, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of about 25% ISV-channel growth.

surprises.description: The preview built Q2 core revenue at about $6.2 million, roughly flat with Q1; MaxCyte reported $6.5 million. That was a modest sequential improvement and a beat against the preview’s core estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core revenue fell 21% year-over-year to $6.5 million” and total revenue “exceeded management's expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 core revenue” estimated at “~$6.2M”; management guided Q2 core “≈ Q1 ($6.2M).”

surprises.description: Total revenue came in at $7.3 million, above the preview’s roughly $7.0 million build, although still within its $6.8–7.4 million base-case range. The gap was small and does not change the fact that the preview anticipated a year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $7.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 build was “~$7.0M”; its base-case range was “$6.8–7.4M.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses were higher than the preview’s $14–15 million estimate, at $15.8 million. The year-over-year reduction and restructuring savings were expected, but the reported quarterly cost was above the estimated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses fell 25% year-over-year to $15.8 million (from $21.2 million), reflecting full run-rate benefits of 2025 restructuring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 operating expenses estimated at “$14–15M” on a “Post-restructuring run-rate.”

surprises.description: MaxCyte said five partner programs could potentially reach commercial launch in the next couple of years, including as early as 2027. The preview discussed the existing commercial program and partner pipeline but did not flag this number or near-term launch timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Five partner programs positioned for potential commercial launch in the next couple of years, including as early as 2027.”

in_line: SPL program-related revenue was $0.8 million, essentially matching the preview’s estimate of about $0.8 million, driven predominantly by Casgevy royalties; the preview expected roughly $0.75 million of royalties.
Q2 gross margin was 77%, within the preview’s 76–79% estimate.
Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $30–32 million, as the preview’s base case expected; it also anticipated modest H2 growth.
Cash and investments were $141.9 million, within the preview’s Q2 estimate of $140–143 million.

The preview expected a qualitative discussion of the Genentech agreement and no Q2 revenue from it. The call described the partnership but did not disclose its economics or raise the full-year guidance.

The preview cited Vertex’s Q2 Casgevy revenue of about $76 million and expected continued patient initiations; the call reported approximately $76 million and over 100 initiations for a third consecutive quarter.

surprises.description: BuzzFeed announced a company-wide headcount reduction of about 35%, targeting roughly $30 million in annualized savings, with $6.5–$8.5 million of one-time costs through year-end. The preview discussed possible cost actions but did not anticipate a reduction on this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “reduced headcount by approximately 35% across the entire company,” expected to yield “roughly $30 million in annualized savings” at a “one-time cost of $6.5–$8.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “cost actions” as part of Allen’s strategic plan, but gave no expected scale or cost.

surprises.description: Content revenue, which the preview identified as the only growing revenue line in Q1, declined by $700,000 in Q2. That marks a reversal of the recent growth signal, although the preview did not provide a Q2 content forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue declines included “content ($700K).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “content +69% to $7.5M” in Q1 2026; the preview called content “the only growing line” in Q1.

surprises.description: BuzzFeed disclosed a sales-representation agreement with Allen Media Group to pursue advertising across premium TV, streaming, and local broadcast, while retaining control of pricing, packaging, and inventory. The preview anticipated possible integration with Allen Media interests but did not describe this agreement.
surprises.fact_evidence: BuzzFeed “entered a sales representation agreement with Allen Media Group to expand ad monetization across premium TV, streaming, and local broadcast,” while “retaining full control over pricing, packaging, and inventory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “integration with Allen Media interests” as something to watch, but did not mention a sales agreement.

surprises.description: The company said its primary engagement metric, time spent, was down 11% year over year to 62.3 million hours, despite a sequential increase from Q1. The preview did not flag this metric or give an expected direction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Time spent, the primary engagement metric, declined 11% year-over-year to 62.3 million hours,” while rising “1.7 million hours sequentially from Q1.”

surprises.description: BuzzFeed said it aims to become a free streaming service and a “super app,” a specific strategic ambition not laid out in the preview’s discussion of Allen’s plans.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is “aiming to become a free streaming service and ‘super app.’”

surprises.description: BuzzFeed paid down $20 million of its term loan, leaving $25 million of principal and about $5 million of net debt, with more than $2 million in expected annual interest savings. The preview anticipated that proceeds would partly go toward debt reduction, but did not specify this amount or resulting balance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “paid down $20 million against its term loan,” cutting principal to “$25 million (roughly $5 million net debt),” and expected to save “more than $2 million in annual interest expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the quarter had added Allen investment proceeds and that “management said proceeds partly paid down debt,” and flagged an updated “cash/debt picture” to watch.

in_line: BuzzFeed continued to withhold quarterly guidance, consistent with the preview’s account that guidance had been paused since the March 2026 report.

The completion of Byron Allen’s investment and his role as Chairman and CEO, with Jonah Peretti moving to lead BuzzFeed AI, were consistent with the preview’s description of the completed investment and leadership transition.

surprises.description: Q2 organic growth was 3%, slightly above the 2–3% guidance range, and revenue of $711 million exceeded both the $704.5 million consensus and the top of the company’s $699–707 million range. The preview’s base case was an in-line quarter at $703–709 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma organic growth was 3% in Q2, coming in slightly above the high end of guidance, with total revenue of $711 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (pro forma) Consensus $704.5M”; company guide “$699–707M”; base case “$703–709M (organic 2–3%).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.41 greatly exceeded the preview’s $1.23 consensus. Much of the upside came from $16 million in one-time tariff refunds and a lower 16% tax rate that reverses in Q4, so the beat was substantially helped by temporary items.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma adjusted EPS was $1.41, well above guidance, with roughly half the upside from $16 million in one-time tariff refunds and about one-third from a lower 16% tax rate that reverses in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS Consensus $1.23.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY26 organic growth guidance to 4–5% from 3–4% and adjusted EPS guidance to $5.30–$5.40 from $5.20–$5.30. This was stronger than the preview’s base case of reaffirming or narrowing guidance to the high end, and the new EPS range is above the $5.25 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year organic growth guidance was raised to 4%-5% from the prior 3%-4%, and adjusted EPS guidance was raised $0.10 to $5.30-$5.40.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 organic 3–4%”; “FY26 adj. EPS Consensus $5.25” and company guide “$5.20–5.30”; base case: “FY guide reaffirmed or narrowed to the high end.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted operating margin was 29.3% versus the roughly 27% expectation, and it still exceeded that level excluding tariff refunds. FY26 margin guidance also rose to 28.7% from 28.4%, better than the preview’s expected 2H margin ramp without a guide increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margins were 29.3% in the quarter, and even excluding tariff refunds, margins exceeded the 27% guidance assumption; full-year margin guidance was lifted 30 basis points to 28.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted operating margin was expected at “~27%”; FY26 adjusted operating margin guide was “28.4%.” The preview called the 2H margin ramp the “highest importance” watch item.

surprises.description: Diagnostics organic growth reached 11%, well above the preview’s description of the segment as a growth engine based on Q1 growth of 4%. Reproductive health grew double digits and immunodiagnostics grew high single digits even excluding the Genomics England contract.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Diagnostics segment grew 11% organically, with reproductive health up double digits and immunodiagnostics up high single digits, remaining strong even excluding the Genomics England sequencing contract.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diagnostics (Q1: $349M, +4% organic). Expected to remain the growth engine”; the preview also highlighted the Genomics England partnership in Reproductive Health and expected “Immunodiagnostics ex-China stability.”

surprises.description: Life Sciences declined 3% organically, rather than sustaining the growth implied by the preview’s Q1 +3% result and expectations for continued pharma/biotech strength and mid-single-digit instrument growth. Signals software fell about 20% on difficult comparisons, although ARR grew in the mid-20s and management expects a return to double-digit growth in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Life Sciences segment declined 3% organically, dragged down by an approximate 20% decline in Signals software due to difficult comps, though software ARR grew in the mid-20s and management expects a return to double-digit growth in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Life Sciences (Q1: $362M, +3% organic). Pharma/biotech ran low-double-digit organic in Q1”; the preview asked whether that would hold and said to watch “instrument growth (guided mid-single-digit).”

surprises.description: Instrument demand was stronger than the preview’s call for order and backlog color: the company entered Q3 with its strongest instrument backlog in 3–4 years, while Opera Phenix OptIQ orders were outpacing production capacity. Management also upgraded full-year platform growth guidance from low to mid-single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Company entered Q3 with its strongest instrument backlog in 3-4 years, driven by high-content screening (Opera Phenix OptIQ) order velocity outpacing production capacity, prompting an upgrade of full-year platform growth guidance from low to mid-single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for order/backlog color and instrument book-to-bill to substantiate” the second-half acceleration.

surprises.description: Management reported emerging demand from nontraditional, AI-focused customers building AI-driven drug-discovery platforms. The preview discussed Signals and AI as a narrative and a possible software-ARR topic, but this customer-demand signal was new; management said it was too early to quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management signaled emerging demand from nontraditional AI-focused customers building AI-driven drug discovery platforms, but said it remains too early to quantify the magnitude of this opportunity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called software/AI a “multiple story, not an estimate story” and said to watch for any attempt to quantify software ARR or attach.

surprises.description: The call reported $184 million of free cash flow, 117% conversion of adjusted net income, and a completed €500 million note retirement, with gross leverage expected below 3x and net leverage approaching 2x by year-end. The preview had emphasized share repurchases as the primary capital-allocation use instead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $184 million (117% conversion of adjusted net income), and after retiring a EUR 500 million note in July, the company expects gross leverage below 3x and net leverage approaching 2x by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$86M repurchased in Q1; buyback is the stated primary use of capital. Pace matters for the EPS bridge.”

in_line: The China immunodiagnostics divestiture advanced from an LOI to a definitive agreement on expected terms, with closing timing still around 2H27: the preview specifically identified LOI-to-definitive conversion and the expected 2H27 close as watch items.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted diluted EPS was $3.19, above the $3.06 consensus and the $3.06 top of Marriott’s own guide. The beat was about 4% versus consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted diluted EPS rose 20% year-over-year to $3.19.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $3.06”; company guide “$2.99–$3.06.”

surprises.description: Global RevPAR rose 3.4%, well above the prior 1.5%–2.5% guide. U.S. and Canada RevPAR was especially strong at 5%, above the preview’s 4.5% bull-line threshold, while international RevPAR declined slightly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global RevPAR rose 3.4% in Q2, with U.S. and Canada up 5% (the highest quarterly increase in 13 quarters) and luxury RevPAR up over 9%, while international RevPAR declined slightly.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The company’s worldwide RevPAR guide was “+1.5% to +2.5%”; the scorecard’s U.S. & Canada bull line was “≥+4.5%.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $1.59 billion, above the prior $1.525–$1.550 billion guide, exceeding its upper end by about 3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 13% to $1.59 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guide — adj. EBITDA “$1,525M–$1,550M.”

surprises.description: Gross fee revenues reached $1.58 billion, above the prior $1.538–$1.553 billion guide, even though the preview identified Middle East-sensitive incentive management fees as a potential source of weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total gross fee revenues up 13% to $1.58 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guide — gross fee revenues “$1,538M–$1,553M”; the preview also said incentive management fees were modeled “−3.8% YoY.”

surprises.description: Marriott’s estimate of the Middle East conflict’s full-year RevPAR drag improved to about 100 basis points from the prior 100–125 basis-point assumption. The region’s Q2 RevPAR still fell 43%, but that was less severe than the preview’s roughly 50% Q2 decline assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Middle East RevPAR fell 43% in Q2 due to regional conflict, and the full-year drag on global RevPAR is now estimated at ~100 basis points (improved from prior 100-125 bps).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 guide assumed “100–125 bps off full-year global RevPAR” and that Zacks’ model assumed “roughly a 50% Middle East RevPAR decline in Q2.”

surprises.description: Full-year net rooms growth is trending toward the low end of the prior 4.5%–5.0% range because Middle East construction delays are limiting additions. That is weaker than the preview’s cited upside case of a pipeline above 620,000 rooms, though the pipeline itself grew and conversions remained strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net rooms growth is now trending toward the low end of the prior 4.5%-5% range, primarily due to Middle East construction delays.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the FY net-rooms guide as “+4.5–5.0%” and its scorecard’s bull line as “pipeline >620k rooms.”

surprises.description: Marriott announced new long-term co-branded card agreements with JPMorgan Chase and American Express, a catalyst the preview said had not yet been announced and was excluded from guidance. The deals are expected to add about $30 million in partial-year 2026 fees and $100–$125 million to co-brand card fees by 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New long-term co-branded credit card agreements with JPMorgan Chase and American Express are expected to add ~$30 million in incremental 2026 fees (partial year) and $100-$125 million to co-brand card fees by full-year 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The U.S. co-brand card renegotiation is explicitly excluded from guidance and no new agreement had been announced”; the scorecard called a signed, quantified deal the bull line.

surprises.description: Marriott raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to $5.97–$6.03 billion from $5.88–$5.97 billion, and now expects adjusted EPS growth of 16%–18%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA is guided to $5.97-$6.03 billion (up 11-12%) with adjusted diluted EPS growth of 16-18%, aided by share count reduction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 guide: adjusted EBITDA “$5,880–5,970M” and adjusted EPS “$11.38–11.63.”

surprises.description: A new guest-satisfaction incentive will reimburse up to 50 basis points of gross room revenue, paid by Marriott rather than the system fund and recorded in owned/leased/other expenses. The preview did not flag this new company-borne cost.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marriott is launching a new ITR guest-satisfaction incentive of up to 50 basis points of gross room revenue fee reimbursement, paid by Marriott (not the system fund) and hitting the owned/leased/other expense line.”

surprises.description: Marriott raised 2026 investment-spending guidance to $1.25–$1.35 billion, including substantial contract-acquisition and technology-transformation spending; the preview did not flag an increase in planned investment spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2026 investment spending guidance was raised to $1.25-$1.35 billion (contract acquisition costs ~40-45%, tech transformation ~25%).”

surprises.description: Owned/leased net revenue guidance was cut to $175–$185 million, partly because of a $27 million litigation accrual. The preview did not identify this cut or litigation accrual as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Owned/leased net revenue was cut to $175-$185 million partly due to a $27 million litigation accrual.”

surprises.description: The global pipeline reached a record roughly 629,000 rooms, exceeding the preview’s 620,000-room upside threshold; Marriott also reported record first-half signings and strong conversion contributions to signings and openings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The global pipeline grew nearly 7% year-over-year to a record ~629,000 rooms, with over 279,000 rooms under construction and record first-half signings, of which conversions made up 34% of signings and 40% of openings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s net-rooms bull line was “pipeline >620k rooms.”

in_line: Marriott raised full-year global RevPAR guidance to 3%–3.5%, in line with the preview’s stated expectation of a raise toward 3%–3.5%.
The company expects to return over $4.5 billion to shareholders, consistent with the preview’s expectation of more than $4.4 billion.
Q4 headwinds, including no World Cup benefit, fit the preview’s expectation that Q4 would be weaker than the full year and its concern about second-half guidance.

surprises.description: Cerence’s adjusted EBITDA was $13.5 million, above the top of the preview’s $8–12 million guidance range. The beat was supported by favorable margin mix and lower operating expenses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $13.5 million” and was “above the high end of the $8-12 million guidance range,” driven by “favorable margin mix and lower operating expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: $8–12M.”

surprises.description: Cerence raised FY26 free cash flow guidance to $76–82 million from $66–76 million, while the preview had cited the lower range. Q3 itself generated $20 million of free cash flow, for which the preview had no estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year fiscal 2026 free cash flow guidance to $76-82 million from the prior $66-76 million, generating $20 million in free cash flow in Q3.”

surprises.description: Variable license revenue fell 15% as Cerence’s vehicle production declined 8%, substantially more than the roughly 2% decline in global light-vehicle production. The preview anticipated flat-to-down global volumes but did not flag this degree of company-specific production weakness or the unfavorable OEM and regional mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Variable license revenue fell 15% year-over-year to $29.1 million” as “Cerence's vehicle production dropped 8% versus a roughly 2% decline in global light vehicle production, reflecting unfavorable OEM and regional mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cerence needs price to offset flat-to-down global volumes.”

surprises.description: The Board authorized Cerence’s first share repurchase program, for up to $30 million over 12 months. This was not anticipated in the preview, which instead emphasized continued debt reduction as part of the equity story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized Cerence's first-ever share repurchase program of up to $30 million over the next 12 months, funded from cash on hand and free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Continued deleveraging is a real part of the equity story at a ~$417M cap.”

surprises.description: Cerence reported about 100,000 XUI-powered cars already on the road and projected a couple million by FY27, with significantly higher price per unit than current products. The preview expected an FY27 XUI ramp but did not provide this scale or price-per-unit outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 100,000 XUI-powered cars on the road,” with management “expecting a couple million XUI vehicles by fiscal 2027 at significantly higher price-per-unit than current products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has been explicit that xUI revenue is immaterial in FY26 and inflects in FY27”; the preview also noted a claim of “PPUs that exceed our current run rate.”

surprises.description: Cerence secured its first customer for a Microsoft-developed mobile work agent with a global premium automaker, extending its opportunity beyond XUI programs. The preview did not anticipate this non-XUI customer or product.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Secured its first customer for a Microsoft-developed mobile work agent with a global premium automaker, expanding its addressable market beyond XUI programs.”

surprises.description: The fixed license revenue recognized in Q3 was $12.5 million, above the preview’s approximately $10 million assumption. The expected deal did land, but at a higher amount than the preview indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 guidance reflects “the absence of the $12.5 million fixed license revenue recognized in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FQ3 guidance explicitly assumed a deal not yet closed” of “~$10M of fixed license revenue.”

surprises.description: Non-automotive revenue is expected to grow faster than automotive revenue in FY27. The preview discussed core growth and XUI but did not forecast this relative growth pattern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-automotive revenue (forecast at $7-9 million for FY26) expected to grow faster than automotive.”

in_line: Q3 revenue was approximately $70 million, within the $68–72 million guidance range and close to the preview’s approximately $70.1 million consensus estimate.
Recurring connected services grew 20% year over year to $15.5 million, broadly in line with the preview’s focus on sustained growth after citing 21% growth to $15.3 million in Q2.
The expected additional XUI close materialized as a new Stellantis deal; the preview said management expected “at least one more” close by FQ3.

Q4 revenue guidance of $61–65 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1–5 million are broadly in line with the preview’s implied Q4 revenue of about $63 million and EBITDA of about $3 million. The sequential decline was expected, though the call attributed it to the Q3 fixed-license item and seasonality.

FY27 high-single to low-double-digit revenue growth is consistent with the preview’s description of the core business as roughly an 8%-growth franchise. Excluding upside from ongoing IP monetization efforts is also consistent with the preview’s expectation of no near-term litigation revenue.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $173.5 million, below the preview’s $175–179 million estimate, and the 49.7% margin was about 110 basis points below its ~50.8% estimate. The margin slipped below 50%, although EBITDA remained above the preview’s <$172 million bear-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to $173.5 million (49.7% margin)” from $203.2 million (53.3% margin).
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … My est. $175–179M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin … ~50.8%.”

surprises.description: Management provided no update on the MBI transaction and declined to answer questions about financing at either Cable One or MBI. The preview expected at least a noncommittal discussion of the MBI decision and pro forma leverage, so the lack of any financing clarity left more uncertainty than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management provided no update on the MBI transaction and explicitly declined to answer questions about financing efforts at either Cable One or MBI.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Non-committal; ‘evaluating alternatives.’ PF leverage confirmed ~4.5–4.7x”; the preview also said the MBI exchange-offer decision was the most important call question.

surprises.description: Digital and direct channels had already grown to roughly 35% of sales, from less than 10% a year earlier, with door-to-door contribution more than doubling. The preview did not anticipate or discuss this channel-mix progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital and direct sales channels grew from less than 10% of sales a year ago to roughly 35% in Q2, with door-to-door contribution more than doubling.”

in_line: Revenue of $348.9 million was essentially in line with the preview’s ~$349 million estimate and within the pre-announced $346–352 million range.
Residential broadband losses of 17,000 were within the expected 16,000–18,000 range, and the reported 6.6% year-over-year subscriber decline matched the preview’s derived estimate.
CapEx of $74 million matched the preview’s guidance-midpoint estimate.
Fixed-wireless overlap remained a little over 80% of the footprint, broadly in line with the preview’s estimate that about 80% faced FWA competition.
The preview cautioned that GAAP EPS was likely to be dominated by impairments and one-offs; the reported noncash impairment and fair-value adjustments were consistent with that warning.

surprises.description: Brinker’s FY27 adjusted EPS guide of $12.60–$13.40 is above the preview’s base expectation of $11.90–$12.30 and above the $12.15–$12.60 range implied by the long-term algorithm. Even the low end reaches the algorithm’s upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 guidance calls for… adjusted diluted EPS of $12.60-13.40.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 EPS guide $11.90–12.30” in the base case; the long-term algorithm “implies $12.15–12.60.”
