surprises.description: Reported revenue was far below the preview’s estimate, at $187 million versus roughly $310–320 million, because exiting the rail contracts produced a negative $136 million revenue adjustment. The adjustment related to contracts previously booked at zero margin, and underlying revenue grew year over year, so the headline gap did not represent an equivalent deterioration in underlying activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total reported Q2 revenue was $187 million, reflecting a negative $136 million adjustment from exiting the two rail contracts (previously booked at zero margin), though underlying revenue grew year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $310–320M”; consensus revenue “$311.3M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA beat the preview’s $29–32 million estimate, reaching $34 million. Harsco Environmental was the main driver, with $46 million of segment adjusted EBITDA versus the preview’s $38–40 million estimate, indicating stronger profitability than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose over 20% year-over-year to $34 million (up 22%), exceeding company expectations and driven primarily by Harsco Environmental”; Harsco Environmental adjusted EBITDA “rose 15% to $46 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$29–32M”; HE Adj. EBITDA “$38–40M.”

surprises.description: The company reported roughly $400 million of cash, far above the preview’s inferred opening cash of about $90 million, though only $100 million counted in the covenant calculation. Net debt was about $290 million and covenant net leverage was 1.9x, making the cash position more substantial than expected but less available for covenant purposes than the headline balance suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enviri ended the quarter with net debt of approximately $290 million and a net leverage ratio of 1.9x, counting only $100 million of its roughly $400 million cash balance in the covenant calculation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described opening cash of “~$90M” as inferred and said the liability appeared funded from “the ~$90M opening cash plus the undrawn $152M revolver.”

surprises.description: Unusual P&L items totaled $247 million, exceeding the roughly $208 million of rail-contract charges disclosed before the release; the facts also confirm the charges were recorded in Q2, a timing question the preview had left open. The provided facts do not detail the additional items beyond the previously disclosed impairment and contract-exit liability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded $247 million of unusual P&L items, including $75 million in noncash impairment charges and a $133 million liability for contract exit obligations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had announced “a ~$208M rail charge” and that whether it would hit Q2 or Q3 was “genuinely open.”

surprises.description: The call quantified a substantial cash benefit from exiting the Deutsche Bahn and Network Rail contracts: they had consumed about $40 million of cash in 2025 and were expected to consume a similar amount in 2026. The preview focused on the exit liability and its payment schedule, but did not highlight the avoided recurring cash drain.
surprises.fact_evidence: The contracts “consumed roughly $40 million of cash in 2025 and were expected to consume a similar amount in 2026,” and Enviri “exited” them, “significantly derisking the rail business.”

surprises.description: Enviri disclosed restructuring that will eliminate about 300 positions and is expected to add more than $15 million of annual margin at full run rate, a cost-saving plan not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restructuring actions eliminating approximately 300 positions are expected to deliver over $15 million in annual margin uplift on a full run-rate basis once completed.”

surprises.description: Management set an additional longer-term target of meaningful earnings and cash-flow growth beginning in 2027. The preview centered on 2026 guidance and did not identify this 2027 outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management [is] targeting meaningful earnings and cash flow growth beginning in 2027.”

in_line: Full-year guidance was maintained at the preview’s expected ranges: Harsco Environmental adjusted EBITDA of $170–180 million and a Rail adjusted EBITDA loss of $19–26 million. The preview’s base case expected reaffirmation, and Rail’s $5 million adjusted EBITDA loss was within its estimated $5–8 million loss range.
Harsco Environmental revenue was $266 million, close to the preview’s $258–265 million estimate and consistent with its expectation for revenue comparable to 2025.

Rail adjusted revenue was $58 million, at the top of the preview’s $50–58 million range; its multi-decade-low original equipment demand and aftermarket growth broadly matched the preview’s discussion of the Rail business.

surprises.description: The preview described RCC as Trevi’s most crowded competitive area, but after GSK terminated its RCC program, management said Trevi is essentially alone across all three chronic-cough indications. That is a meaningful improvement in the competitive picture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Following a competitor's recent RCC program termination (GSK), Trevi believes it is now essentially alone across all three of its chronic cough indications, positioning it as a potential first-in-class therapy.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “RCC is also the largest commercial prize and the most crowded competitively.”

surprises.description: The runway remains into 2030, but management specified that it covers the IPF-related cough program through potential FDA approval—not commercial launch costs or a Phase III RCC trial. That qualification leaves those expenses outside the stated funding runway, unlike the preview’s framing of the April raise as potentially sufficient through approval.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The cash runway funds the IPF-related chronic cough program through potential FDA approval, but explicitly excludes commercial launch costs and any Phase III RCC trial.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The market is watching whether the April raise really was the last one before approval.”

surprises.description: The LAKE sample-size re-estimation could increase the trial by as much as 50%, a potential expansion the preview did not quantify. Management characterized any increase as routine rather than a negative signal, tempering the concern but not removing the possibility of a larger trial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management indicated the LAKE trial could be upsized by up to 50% following the SSRE, but framed any increase as a routine statistical exercise rather than a negative signal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “what triggers an expansion” and whether “an expansion should be read as a negative signal,” but did not specify a possible expansion of up to 50%.

surprises.description: The non-IPF ILD FDA process remains unresolved: Trevi has requested a meeting and expects to learn within the month whether it is granted, rather than reporting completed protocol alignment. The preview specifically sought confirmation that the meeting occurred and that the H2 2026 plan was intact, so this leaves a key execution question open.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trevi submitted an FDA meeting request for its non-IPF-ILD chronic cough program and expects to learn within the month whether the meeting is granted, with alignment anticipated in 2H 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side wants explicit confirmation the meeting occurred and H2 2026 initiation is intact”; the preview also described a meeting “that includes protocol review.”

surprises.description: Management described a focused RCC commercial approach: target about 1 million treatment-resistant U.S. patients and use specialty pricing rather than pursue the broader market, partly to avoid cannibalizing IPF/ILD revenue. The preview did not flag this market-segmentation strategy.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company targets a treatment-resistant RCC population of approximately 1 million U.S. patients, pursuing specialty pricing rather than the broad market to avoid cannibalizing IPF/ILD revenue.”

surprises.description: Trevi said it would not wait for OCEAN-1’s readout before releasing OCEAN-2 top-line results, and expects OCEAN-1 to be largely enrolled by the time OCEAN-2 reports. This adds an explicit commitment to preserving the earlier OCEAN-2 data timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated it will not hold OCEAN-2 top-line data (expected 2H 2027) until OCEAN-1 reads out (1H 2028), and expects OCEAN-1 to be largely enrolled by the time OCEAN-2 reports.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called OCEAN-2 “the smaller, faster trial” that “reads out first” and flagged any change to its H2 2027 top-line timing.

surprises.description: Trevi reported that its unbranded awareness campaign has already reached more than 17,000 pulmonologists, a commercial-awareness metric the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's unbranded awareness campaign has reached more than 17,000 unique pulmonologists so far.”

surprises.description: All six of Trevi’s ATS 2026 submissions were selected for presentations or posters, an unexpected positive update on scientific visibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All six of its ATS 2026 submissions were selected for presentations or posters.”

in_line: OCEAN-1 Phase III was initiated in Q2, as the preview’s key execution check expected; the LAKE Phase IIb RCC trial also began in Q2, consistent with the preview’s stated Q2 initiation plan.
The company reiterated cash runway into 2030 without changing prior guidance, matching the preview’s central funding expectation.
The LAKE SSRE remains expected in Q4 2026, consistent with the preview’s timing expectation.
OCEAN-2 remains planned for a 2H 2027 top-line readout, with OCEAN-1 still expected to read out in 1H 2028.

surprises.description: Amylyx had $250.8 million in cash and marketable securities at quarter-end, above the preview’s $240–245 million estimate. It also reiterated runway into 2028 through potential approval and launch milestones.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 2026 with $250.8 million in cash and marketable securities” and said this provides “anticipated runway into 2028 through key milestones including potential FDA approval and commercial launch in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash & investments (6/30) … My Estimate: ~$240–245M”; the preview also expected runway “into 2028.”

surprises.description: SG&A was materially higher than the preview’s expected $18–19 million, reaching $21.9 million. Amylyx attributed the increase to commercial investment and a one-time legal charge, so the elevated spend was partly nonrecurring but still above the preview’s stated >$21 million bear-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A increasing to $21.9 million (from $15.6 million) due to a one-time legal charge and commercial investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SG&A of $18–19M reads as on-plan; >$21M with no offsetting narrative reads as spending ahead of a coin-flip readout.”

surprises.description: R&D came in well below the preview’s modeled $28.5 million, at $23.8 million, as PSP spending fell. This more than offset the higher SG&A in the total operating-expense figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D fell to $23.8 million (from $27.2 million) on reduced PSP spending.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “R&D … ~$28.5M.”

surprises.description: Total operating expenses were slightly below the preview’s modeled $46–48 million range, despite rising year over year. The result reflects the lower R&D spend offsetting the SG&A overrun.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total operating expenses rose 7% year-over-year to $45.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled total operating expenses of “~$46–48M.”

surprises.description: Amylyx gave a more specific readout window than the preview’s general Q3 expectation, saying Lucidity top-line data are expected in late August or early September. The database is still blinded and unlocked, so the timing remains an expectation rather than a completed analysis milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amylyx expects top-line data … in late August or early September 2026,” with the last participant having completed their final visit, “though the database remains blinded and unlocked.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said topline was guided to “Q3 2026” and described “September” as plausible, while a named month or data-day would be a narrowing.

surprises.description: Amylyx described a robust trial-design basis for the upcoming readout that the preview did not discuss: Lucidity is powered to detect a 35% treatment effect even while allowing for a placebo response as high as 50%, and the company cited a larger reduction in the prior Phase 2 endpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Lucidity trial is powered at least 90% to detect a 35% treatment effect versus placebo,” tolerating “up to a 50% placebo response,” while prior Phase 2 showed “a 55% reduction” in the level 2/level 3 composite endpoint.

surprises.description: Amylyx said that a label limited to Roux-en-Y gastric bypass patients could require an additional confirmatory study for sleeve gastrectomy patients. Management characterized that study as efficient and not overly burdensome, but it is a potential extra regulatory step not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “If FDA restricts the label to Roux-en-Y gastric bypass patients,” the company believes “an additional confirmatory study for sleeve gastrectomy patients would be efficient and not overly burdensome.”

surprises.description: A PBH-specific ICD-10 code is set to take effect on October 1, 2026, a market-access development the preview did not mention. Management qualified its significance by saying the code is not required for reimbursement and patients can already be identified through claims analysis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A PBH-specific ICD-10 code will become effective October 1, 2026,” but “it is not required for reimbursement” and patients “can already be identified via claims analysis.”

surprises.description: Amylyx entered a second Gubra research collaboration for peptide candidates targeting another undisclosed rare endocrine disease, adding a pipeline program beyond the collaboration already discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amylyx entered a second research collaboration with Gubra in July to develop peptide candidates for another undisclosed rare endocrine disease.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview mentioned the existing Gubra collaboration for AMX-318, but not a second collaboration.

surprises.description: The call reported week-96 Wolfram syndrome data showing stabilization or improvement, whereas the preview flagged the timing of the data but did not anticipate or state an outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AMX-0035 for Wolfram syndrome (week 96 data showing stabilization/improvement).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “AMX0035 Wolfram Week 96 HELIOS data timing.”

surprises.description: Management said there are no PBH competitors with a comparable profile, a favorable competitive-positioning claim not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported no competitors with a comparable profile in PBH.”

in_line: Lucidity remained on track for Q3 2026, consistent with the preview’s central timing expectation.
The company reiterated runway into 2028, as the preview expected.
AMX-318 remains in IND-enabling studies with a 2027 IND filing target, consistent with the preview’s expectation that its IND was on track for 2027.
Amylyx cited an estimated U.S. PBH population of approximately 160,000, consistent with the preview’s stated 160,000 eligible-patient estimate.

The company said it is preparing NDA sections ahead of Lucidity’s outcome, consistent with the preview’s discussion of pre-writing NDA sections; the call did not provide the weeks-to-submission estimate the preview sought.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $3.3 billion came in above the preview’s $3.21–$3.23 billion consensus range, and year-over-year growth was 12% versus the preview’s 8.8% estimate. The reported growth included an approximately 170-basis-point benefit from foreign exchange.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $3.3 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with an approximate 170 basis point benefit from foreign exchange rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $3.23B (+8.8% YoY)” and “Revenue | ~$3.21B.”

surprises.description: Vertex raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $13.1–$13.2 billion, above the preview’s cited prior range of $12.95–$13.1 billion. The increase was modest, and the expectation of at least $500 million from non-CF products was maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vertex raised full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to $13.1-13.2 billion, while maintaining expectations of $500 million or greater from non-CF products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue guidance context: company had guided to $12.95B–$13.1B (8–9% growth); watch for reaffirmation/updates.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $4.73, below the preview’s $4.85 consensus, with 5% year-over-year growth versus the preview’s 7.3% estimate. SG&A rose sharply, while R&D was nearly flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $4.73, representing only 5% growth versus prior year, as SG&A rose 45% year-over-year to $520 million while R&D grew just 1% to $889 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (non-GAAP) | $4.85 (+7.3% YoY).”

surprises.description: CASGEVY accelerated substantially: revenue rose roughly 75% sequentially and more than 150% year over year, with more infusions in the first half of 2026 than in all of 2025. The preview highlighted sequential variability after a prior-quarter decline but did not indicate an increase of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CASGEVY delivered $76 million in Q2 revenue, up roughly 75% sequentially and over 150% year-over-year, with more infusions in H1 2026 than in all of 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CASGEVY: Sequential variability expected” and “CASGEVY quarter-over-quarter patient-infusion trend after a sequential decline noted in the prior quarter.”

surprises.description: JOURNAVX gross-to-net normalization was pushed out to the first half of 2027 because use of the patient support program was heavier than forecast amid restricted coverage. Of the approximately 260 million covered lives, only 180 million have unrestricted access, with about 80 million facing restrictions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vertex now expects JOURNAVX gross-to-net to normalize in the first half of 2027 (later than prior expectations) due to heavier-than-forecast use of the patient support program amid restricted coverage”; “only 180 million have unrestricted access, with ~80 million subject to restrictions like quantity limits or prior authorizations.”

surprises.description: The FDA accepted Vertex’s povetacicept BLA for IgAN, with Phase III results cited showing substantial reductions in proteinuria, hematuria, and Gd-IgA1. The preview noted the expected November decision and that commentary would be watched, but did not anticipate this filing-acceptance milestone or provide these data.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA accepted the BLA for povetacicept in IgAN with a November 30, 2026 PDUFA date, backed by RAINIER Phase III data showing 52% proteinuria reduction and 70%+ reductions in hematuria and Gd-IgA1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Povetacicept (IgA nephropathy) — FDA decision expected November 30, 2026; any pre-decision commentary will be watched.”

surprises.description: The FDA cleared the IND for VX-017, a universal-donor islet cell therapy for type 1 diabetes, and Vertex said this could double the addressable market. The preview did not flag this program or milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA cleared the IND for VX-017, a universal-donor (blood type O) islet cell therapy for type 1 diabetes, which Vertex expects to double its addressable market from about 60,000 to about 120,000 patients.”

in_line: JOURNAVX showed sequential improvement and rising prescription activity, consistent with the preview’s expectation of improving sequential performance and prescription volumes; Q2 revenue was $50 million, up about 70% sequentially, and monthly scripts rose from about 50,000 in January to about 100,000 in June.
Povetacicept’s November 30, 2026 PDUFA date matched the FDA decision timing cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.3 million, about 16% below the $1.54 million consensus estimate; first-half revenue of $2.7 million was also below the roughly $2.92 million implied by the preview. That leaves a larger H2 revenue ramp needed to reach the preview’s cited full-year guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $1.3 million”; “First half 2026 revenue reached $2.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $1.54M”; “In-line H1 (~$2.92M) leaves $3.5–3.67M in H2 to hit guidance/consensus.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin came in below the preview’s roughly 68% expectation, at 64%. The margin was still substantially higher than a year earlier, but it missed the level the preview identified as important.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin expanded to 64% from 43% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~68% (est.)”; the preview also flagged “Gross margin ≥68%, trending to 70%+.”

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was much wider than expected: net loss was $4.1 million, or $12.35 per share, versus the preview’s implied $2.9–3.0 million loss and split-adjusted EPS estimate of -$8.40. The call attributed part of the gap to $0.9 million of non-cash convertible-note amortization interest expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $4.1 million ($12.35 per share) from $2.8 million, partly driven by $0.9 million of non-cash interest expense from convertible note amortization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (post-split basis) -$8.40”; “Implied net loss ~$2.9–3.0M.”

surprises.description: Management reported a record case-value month in July, an encouraging commercial signal beyond the preview’s discussion of surgeon training and the challenge of converting trained users into repeat cases. The call did not quantify the record or its effect on revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reported a record case value month in July.”

surprises.description: The July 2 FDA clearance had been noted in the preview, but the reported change from disposable to reusable instruments—and the expected reduction in per-procedure costs and boost to margins starting in Q3—was a more specific favorable economic benefit than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “On July 2, the company received FDA 510(k) clearance for the Catamaran SI joint fusion system, reclassifying certain instruments from disposable to reusable, which is expected to reduce per-procedure costs and boost margins beginning in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Catamaran received updated 510(k) clearance July 2.”

in_line: Quarter-end cash was $1.7 million, within the preview’s expected $1.5–2.5 million range, and the $4.2 million July offering had been flagged as closing after quarter-end.
Q2 operating expenses were $4.2 million, matching the preview’s cited Q1 baseline and remaining below its approximately $4.4 million concern threshold.

Training activity at the Tampa facility increased, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the facility was ramping; the call reported first-half training events up 98% versus the second half of 2025.
The July Catamaran 510(k) clearance and further product-development activity were broadly consistent with the preview’s discussion of the clearance and expected 2026 launches.

surprises.description: FIGS reported Q2 revenue of $196.6 million, well above the $186.17 million consensus and above the preview’s inferred $190 million-plus whisper. Revenue growth was 29%, versus the low-20% outlook and the preview’s expected 22% consensus growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net revenues grew 29% year-over-year to $196.6 million,” beating the company’s “low-20% growth outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” revenue was “$186.17M” with “+22.0%” implied growth; the preview also inferred a “$190M+” whisper.

surprises.description: FIGS raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to approximately 20%, a bigger increase than the preview’s expected base-case raise to 15–17% and above even its 17–19% bull-case range. The company projects about 20% growth in Q3 and 10% in Q4, rather than the roughly 8% H2 growth implied by the prior full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 net revenue growth guidance was raised to approximately 20% from the prior 14%-16%, with Q3 growth projected at ~20% and Q4 growth decelerating to ~10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated a raise “to 15–17%”; its bull case called for “FY guide → 17–19%.” It calculated that the prior guide implied H2 growth of “roughly +8%.”

surprises.description: The preview expected gross margin around 66–66.5% and said the roughly $20 million IEEPA refund was not included in guidance. FIGS instead reported 75.2% gross margin after recovering $20.5 million in refunds, with $15.4 million of the refunds adding 780 basis points to the quarter’s margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin [was] up 820 basis points to 75.2%, of which 780 basis points came from a $15.4 million refund benefit”; the company “recovered $20.5 million in IEEPA tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at “~66–66.5%” and described the “~$20M duty drawback / IEEPA refund option” as “explicitly not embedded in guidance.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 18.6%, far above the preview’s roughly 13.5% estimate, while diluted EPS of $0.15 was more than twice the $0.07 consensus. The preview had expected only a modest margin improvement from the prior-year 12.9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin (excluding prior-year tariff refunds) surged to 18.6% from 12.9% a year ago, and diluted EPS rose to $0.15 from $0.04.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adj. EBITDA margin” at “~13.5%” and “EPS (GAAP diluted)” at “$0.07.”

surprises.description: AOV was $127, above the preview’s $124 watch level, and net revenue per active customer reached a new high. Active-customer growth itself was close to the preview’s threshold rather than a major deviation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AOV increased 9% to a record $127, and net revenues per active customer hit an all-time high of $229, surpassing the COVID-era peak of $227.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether “AOV ≥$124” and whether active-customer growth held at double digits.

surprises.description: International revenue grew 67%, accelerating from the 50% growth cited in the preview, and more than 50 points of growth came from existing comparison markets. That provided stronger evidence of growth beyond the newest market openings than the preview had described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International net revenues grew 67% to $37.9 million with over 50 points of growth from existing comp markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “+50% in Q1'26” and said to “watch for the first evidence of the 2025 cohort monetizing.”

surprises.description: U.S. Customs blocked imports from FIGS’ Jordan supplier, requiring the company to move production to other partners and use airfreight. The preview did not flag this disruption, although management said it was largely mitigated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Customs issued a withhold release order blocking imports from the company's Jordan supplier, prompting a shift of production to other partners and use of airfreight, though management says the disruption is largely mitigated.”

surprises.description: Non-scrubwear grew 40%, its strongest pace in nearly four years, and reached 18% of revenue. The preview did not discuss this category or signal this degree of growth outside scrubwear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-scrubwear surged 40% (highest in nearly four years) to reach 18% of revenue.”

surprises.description: The board authorized another $100 million for repurchases, bringing remaining program capacity to $119 million; the preview had not identified a new buyback authorization as a catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized an additional $100 million to the share repurchase program (bringing capacity to $119 million) after buying back $24 million in Q2.”

surprises.description: FIGS acquired V Coterie to enter pins and jewelry, an expansion not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired V Coterie to expand into pins and jewelry.”

surprises.description: FIGS added Bupa Dental Care as a TEAMS client, with plans to outfit nearly 400 U.K. dental centers; the preview did not mention this customer win.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] onboarded a TEAMS client, Bupa Dental Care, to outfit nearly 400 U.K. dental centers.”

surprises.description: Inventory fell 12% to $119.6 million, with further double-digit declines expected in Q3. The preview did not set an inventory expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory fell 12% to $119.6 million with continued double-digit declines expected in Q3.”

in_line: Active customers grew 13%, consistent with the preview’s watch point of maintaining double-digit growth and its threshold of at least 12%.
The footprint remained at 85 markets, matching the preview’s stated current market count.
The preview anticipated a substantial growth slowdown against the tough Q4 comparison; FIGS still projected Q4 growth to decelerate to about 10%.

surprises.description: COP reported adjusted EPS of $3.24, above the preview’s published estimates of $2.88–$2.96. That is a clear consensus beat, though it was below the preview’s own $3.30–$3.45 scenario build before accounting for the Qatar equity-earnings drag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2… delivered $3.24 in adjusted EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS: $2.96” (Zacks), “$2.89–$2.90” (Street composite), and “$2.88” (Benzinga); the preview’s independent build was “roughly $3.30–3.45 before the Qatar equity-earnings drag.”

surprises.description: Q2 production was 2.248 million boe/d, beating both the 2.19–2.22 million boe/d guidance range and the 2.212 million boe/d consensus estimate. The record Permian output of 920,000 boe/d helped drive the outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 production reached 2,248,000 boe/d, above the high end of guidance, driven by a record Permian output of 920,000 boe/d.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 production: 2.19–2.22 MMBOED” and “Total production: 2,212 MBOED.”

surprises.description: Cash generation exceeded the preview’s implied base expectations: CFO was $7.2 billion versus an estimated $6.5–$7.0 billion, and free cash flow was $4.2 billion, above the preview’s $3.5 billion bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$7.2 billion of cash flow from operations, and $4.2 billion of free cash flow after $3 billion of CapEx.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said CFO “could approach $6.5–7.0B” and its bull scenario specified “FCF >$3.5B.”

surprises.description: COP raised Q2 shareholder distributions to $3 billion and doubled buybacks to $2 billion. That exceeded the preview’s base-case expectation of $1.0–$1.25 billion in buybacks, although the preview’s bull case had anticipated at least $1.5 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 shareholder distributions rose to $3 billion, including a doubling of buybacks to $2 billion plus $1 billion in dividends.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “buyback $1.0–1.25B”; its bull tell was “buyback stepped up to ≥$1.5B.”

surprises.description: The Q3 production outlook assumes a Qatar ramp, addressing the preview’s concern that Qatar might not return to guidance after force majeure. The guidance is 2.290–2.320 million boe/d, with Qatar and Lower 48 growth offsetting the effect of asset sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 production guidance of 2,290,000–2,320,000 boe/d assumes a Qatar ramp and Lower 48 growth, offsetting a 15,000 boe/d impact from July noncore asset sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called inability to restore Qatar volumes “the most likely source of a negative reaction” and said “folding Qatar back in” would be the “cleanest bull trigger.”

surprises.description: Management gave a more favorable long-term cost and investment trajectory: it said free-cash-flow breakeven falls from the mid-$40s WTI today to the low-$30s by 2029 as Willow comes online and capital spending declines. The preview expected the $7 billion 2029 FCF target to be reaffirmed, but did not provide this breakeven outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed the $7 billion free cash flow inflection by 2029, with free cash flow breakeven falling from mid-$40s WTI today to low-$30s by 2029 as Willow comes online and CapEx (past its peak) declines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Company still guiding to a $7B FCF inflection by 2029” and flagged the “capex trajectory” as a key item to watch.

surprises.description: The commercial LNG portfolio reached 12 MTPA after two new 1 MTPA offtake deals, above the preview’s stated 10 MTPA Port Arthur offtake level. Management also quantified a potential cash-flow sensitivity for part of the portfolio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The commercial LNG portfolio grew to 12 MTPA via two new 1 MTPA offtake deals (Indonesia and U.S. Gulf Coast), with management estimating roughly $200 million of cash flow per $1/MMBtu of margin on 5 MTPA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Port Arthur LNG Phase 1 commercial offtake built to 10 mtpa.”

surprises.description: Management framed the new Middle East activity as relatively contained and largely self-funding: it cited roughly $30/bbl cost of supply and a $300–$500 million cost for the Kirkuk acquisition. This gave investors more reassuring capital framing than the preview’s unresolved question about commitments against a roughly $25 billion gross redevelopment program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New Middle East entries in Iraq (Kirkuk) and Syria feature ~$30/bbl cost of supply and are expected to be largely self-funding, with the Kirkuk acquisition costing $300–500 million at an expected year-end close.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “total redevelopment cost estimated near $25B” and said the buy-side wanted management to address the Iraq capital question, including whether the entry was funded within the existing envelope.

surprises.description: COP said it had achieved its $5 billion disposition target ahead of schedule, including $1.7 billion of noncore Lower 48 sales in July. The preview did not anticipate this early completion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The $5 billion disposition target was achieved ahead of schedule, including $1.7 billion of noncore Lower 48 asset sales in July.”

surprises.description: CEO Ryan Lance announced he will retire effective September 1 after 14 years, with Andy O'Brien taking over as President and CEO and Konnie Haynes-Welsh becoming CFO. The preview did not flag a leadership transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Ryan Lance will retire effective September 1 after 14 years, with CFO/Strategy head Andy O'Brien becoming President and CEO and Konnie Haynes-Welsh joining as the new CFO.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the 45% of CFO shareholder-return target for the full year, as the preview expected.
Management reaffirmed the $7 billion free-cash-flow inflection by 2029, which the preview had already identified as the company’s target.

surprises.description: Tyson lowered full-year adjusted operating income guidance to $2.1–$2.3 billion from the prior $2.2–$2.4 billion range. The cut was driven primarily by a worse expected beef loss, now $500–$650 million rather than $350–$500 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tyson cut its full-year adjusted operating income guidance to $2.1-$2.3 billion, driven primarily by a worse full-year beef loss now expected between $500 million and $650 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year adjusted operating income guidance raised to $2.2–$2.4 billion” and “Beef segment full-year adjusted operating loss guided to $350–500 million.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.99, below the preview’s headline consensus of $1.03, although it was within the preview’s alternative $1.00–$1.01 estimate range. Year-over-year EPS growth was 9%, less than the preview’s expected 11–13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.99, up 9% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $1.03” and “Adjusted EPS (alt.): $1.00–$1.01”; the preview’s bottom line expected “~$1.00–$1.03, +11–13%.”

surprises.description: Sales were $13.9 billion and essentially flat, below the preview’s $14.1 billion estimate and its expected 1.8% growth. Higher average selling prices offset lower volume, but did not produce the expected sales growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total company sales were essentially flat at $13.9 billion as a 3.4% higher average sales price offset a 2.8% volume decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $14.1 billion” and “+1.8%.”

surprises.description: Prepared Foods operating income was down slightly as higher commodity costs outpaced pricing, whereas the preview expected branded-portfolio momentum, innovation, and distribution gains to support growth. Management nevertheless raised the segment’s full-year guidance midpoint, so the quarterly weakness did not translate into a lower outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prepared Foods operating income was $321 million (12.6% margin), down slightly as roughly $30 million of higher commodity costs outpaced pricing that continues to catch up”; management “raised the Prepared Foods full-year operating income guidance midpoint to a range of $1.3-$1.35 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Prepared Foods: Branded portfolio momentum, innovation, and distribution expansion expected to support growth.”

surprises.description: Management raised the Prepared Foods full-year operating income guidance midpoint to a $1.3–$1.35 billion range, a more favorable outlook than the preview’s expectation of segment growth alone specified. The preview did not provide a segment guidance estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised the Prepared Foods full-year operating income guidance midpoint to a range of $1.3-$1.35 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Prepared Foods: Branded portfolio momentum, innovation, and distribution expansion expected to support growth.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that roughly three-quarters of Chicken operating income now comes from a demand-committed model rather than commodity spot markets. The preview expected Chicken to remain the earnings engine but did not flag this degree of demand-committed coverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “About three-quarters of chicken operating income now runs on a demand-committed model rather than commodity spot markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Chicken: Expected to stay the primary earnings engine — steady demand plus gains in live production, yield, and labor productivity.”

surprises.description: Tyson described a new competitive big-bird genetics line with a substantial rollout and said it is expected to boost both genetics and domestic Chicken results. The preview discussed Chicken productivity gains generally but did not anticipate this specific initiative or its expected contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new competitive big-bird genetics line will represent about 75% of big-bird harvest by year-end 2025 with the remainder in fiscal 2027, expected to boost both the genetics and domestic chicken P&Ls.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Chicken gains in “live production, yield, and labor productivity.”

surprises.description: The call reported substantial cash generation and debt reduction alongside shareholder returns, offering a more constructive update on the balance-sheet concern flagged in the preview. The preview noted elevated debt and questions about dividend sustainability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $4 billion in liquidity, net leverage of 2.1x, reduced gross debt by about $800 million, generated $913 million free cash flow year-to-date, and returned $652 million to shareholders plus another $49 million in buybacks since quarter-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Elevated debt levels and questions around dividend sustainability” as a valuation risk.

in_line: Chicken remained the primary earnings engine: it delivered $488 million of operating income and an 11.2% margin, with income up $40 million year over year, consistent with the preview’s expectation of steady Chicken strength.
Beef remained a material drag amid tight cattle supply and margin pressure, consistent with the preview’s expectation of persistent Beef pressure.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $257.5 million, well above the preview’s roughly $244–246 million estimate and the company’s flat-sequential framing. The reported quarter was about 5% above that expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $257.5 million, up 6.6% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue relatively flat sequentially” → ~$244.7M”; estimate “$244–246M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $155.8 million, above the preview’s $150–153 million estimate and above its level for de-risking the year. The dollar result was a clear beat even though the margin was below the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $155.8 million … the strongest absolute-dollar performance in 13 quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … $150–153M”; “Above $153M de-risks the year.”

surprises.description: The 60.5% adjusted EBITDA margin came in below the preview’s expected 61–62.5%. That is a modest shortfall against the stated margin range, despite the stronger EBITDA dollars.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $155.8 million at a 60.5% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$150–153M (61.5–62.5% margin)”; the preview also said a “61% print is on plan.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.0–$1.02 billion and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $610–$620 million, rather than reaffirming the existing ranges as the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year revenue guidance by two points to $1.0–$1.02 billion (4–6% growth) and lifted adjusted EBITDA guidance to $610–$620 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue guide … reaffirm expected”; “FY26 Adj. EBITDA guide … Reaffirm”; catalyst: “FY26 Adj. EBITDA guide reaffirmed at $605–615M.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was far above the preview’s $25–40 million base-case range and its $30 million watch level. The $54.6 million result was also the highest quarterly level in 15 quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Levered free cash flow reached $54.6 million (up 49%), the highest quarterly level in 15 quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “FCF … $25–40M”; catalyst checklist: “Q2 FCF ≥$30M.”

surprises.description: The strong cash result also led management to raise full-year free cash flow guidance by $5 million to $5–15 million, rather than reaffirming the preview’s expected $0–10 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prompting a $5 million raise to full-year free cash flow guidance to $5–$15 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 FCF guide … $0–$10M”; “Reaffirm — the fragile line.”

surprises.description: First-half bookings were about $74 million, implying roughly $30 million in Q2 after the preview’s cited $44.1 million Q1 result—above its expected $20–24 million for the quarter. First-half bookings had already surpassed all of 2025, while management remained on track for the $100 million full-year target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half bookings totaled roughly $74 million of ACV, already surpassing the full-year 2025 total of $67 million and up 150% year-over-year, keeping the company on track for its $100 million full-year target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ACV bookings … $20–24M”; “Anything ≥$20M keeps the ‘Vision 2030’ … narrative alive.”

surprises.description: The preview expected claims intelligence to grow from its Q1 pace of 8.4% while warning that PSAV volume declines could challenge the mix story. On the call, claims intelligence grew nearly 14% and total P-SAVE revenue reached its highest level in almost four years, driving much of the beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Claims intelligence revenue grew nearly 14% and total P-SAVE revenue hit $220 million, its highest level in almost four years, driving much of the quarterly beat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 showed Claims Intelligence +8.4% offsetting PSAV volume declines”; the preview flagged the risk that “PSAV volume erosion accelerates.”

surprises.description: Management described a longer path from current bookings to their full revenue contribution: most current bookings are expected to benefit 2027 and 2028 results. That makes the preview’s expectation of 3–5% second-half growth as bookings convert less clearly supported by near-term bookings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New bookings typically take two to four quarters to generate first revenue and another four quarters to fully annualize, meaning most current bookings will primarily benefit 2027 and 2028 results.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “3%–5% growth for the second half” as “ACV bookings convert (6–12 month lag).”

surprises.description: The TPA vertical was the largest contributor to Q2 bookings and is expected to account for about 30% of new bookings this year, a specific source of growth that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The TPA vertical was the largest contributor to Q2 bookings and is expected to represent about 30% of total new bookings this year, second only to the payer segment.”

surprises.description: Management cited an NSA arbitration win rate about eight percentage points above the industry and said nearly half of IDR submissions are ineligible. This provided specific support for AI-driven efficiency gains that was not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of litigation and operational risks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's NSA arbitration outcomes outperform the industry by roughly 8 percentage points, and analysis indicates nearly half of all IDR submissions are ineligible, supporting AI-driven efficiency gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified DOJ/MDL exposure as a key debate and said quantified exposure or a litigation reserve could be a material negative.

in_line: The full-year ACV bookings target remained consistent with the preview’s $80–100 million range: management said the company was on track for $100 million.

surprises.description: Talen said it now expects 2027 adjusted EBITDA to exceed its previously announced approximately $2.6 billion, rather than merely meeting that level. The preview described ~$2.6 billion as the implied benchmark and a result approaching it as validation, so exceeding it is a positive upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Talen now expects to exceed its previously announced pro forma 2027 EBITDA of approximately $2.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2027 EBITDA framing vs. the ~$2.6B implied by 6.6x on Cornerstone — validates or breaks the $36+/share 2027 AFCF bridge.”

surprises.description: The pre-buyback free-cash-flow-per-share outlook came in below the preview’s base case: $34 for 2027 versus $36+ expected, and $40 for 2028 versus $41+. However, the company’s $48-per-share 2028 forecast including buybacks (with potential to exceed $50) is substantially above the preview’s stated base-case figures, making the overall outlook mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its free cash flow per share outlook to $34 (2027 base) and $40 (2028 base) before buybacks”; including buybacks, “2028 free cash flow of $48 per share,” with “potential to exceed $50 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted FCF/share trajectory vs. the $36+ (2027) / $41+ (2028) base case.”

surprises.description: Talen’s referenced 2028 spark-spread assumptions were materially higher than at its July 2025 Investor Day: PPL spreads were up 28% and PJM West Hub spreads up 27%. The preview did not flag this improvement in its expected setup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2028 PPL spark spreads up 28% and West Hub sparks up 27% versus July 2025 Investor Day pricing.”

surprises.description: The PPL zone’s power-price discount to PJM West Hub had widened to about $20/MWh from a historical roughly $9/MWh, an adverse basis development that the preview did not identify. Talen said each $1 of basis improvement would translate to roughly $1 of adjusted free cash flow per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The PPL zone's power price discount to PJM West Hub widened from a historical ~$9/MWh to ~$20/MWh due to transmission outages, with each $1 of basis improvement translating to roughly $1 of adjusted free cash flow per share.”

surprises.description: Talen described a substantial potential increase in long-term contracted margin as the AWS campus ramps: from 10% to 35% by 2028–2030, potentially reaching 60% if another ~2 GW of contracts are executed. The preview highlighted AWS and the data-center pipeline but did not anticipate this specific contracted-margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “As the AWS campus ramps to full build-out between 2028 and 2030, long-term contracted margin is projected to rise from 10% to 35%, with potential to reach 60% if an additional ~2 gigawatts of contracts are executed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On the Q1 call management flagged 1+ GW of long-term PPA opportunities” and “a signed contract is the single largest upside catalyst available tonight.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $374 million, close to the preview’s approximately $370 million estimate and within its $340–400 million range; the preview also said the year-over-year increase would be a setup rather than an upside surprise.

The 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint was $2.125 billion, close to the preview’s approximately $2.1 billion expected midpoint; the preview anticipated the guidance reset after Cornerstone closed.

surprises.description: Q2 AFFO was $0.35 per share, above the preview’s modeled $0.30–$0.33 live band and its roughly $0.31 estimate. It also exceeded the preview’s $0.34 bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 AFFO came in at $0.35 per share,” and it was the “fourth consecutive quarter of meeting or exceeding analyst consensus.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat $0.30–$0.33 as the live band”; the bull case listed “$0.34+.”

surprises.description: Physical occupancy rose sharply both sequentially and year over year, rather than following the preview’s expected flat-to-down seasonal pattern. The preview had described Q2 occupancy as roughly flat year over year and still down sequentially in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Physical occupancy rose over 200 basis points sequentially and nearly 300 basis points year-over-year, defying the typical flat-to-down Q1-to-Q2 seasonal pattern.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Occupancy roughly flat YoY, still down sequentially on normal seasonality”; the preview also noted Q1 physical occupancy was “flat YoY.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year AFFO guidance instead of merely maintaining it, lifting the midpoint by $0.04 even after absorbing an estimated $0.05 of EQT JV dilution. The preview’s base case was a reaffirmed guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year AFFO guidance to $1.26-$1.32 per share, a $0.04 midpoint increase, after absorbing an estimated $0.05 of dilution from the EQT joint venture.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 AFFO guidance action. Maintained = base case.” The preview gave existing guidance of “$1.20–$1.30.”

surprises.description: The newly reported same-store operating outlook is substantially below the prior ranges: same-store NOI is now guided to $660–$695 million versus $735–$785 million, and core EBITDA’s upper bound is lower. Same-store revenue guidance also falls by about $230 million, explicitly due to the JV; the preview anticipated a possible guidance split but did not give these lower ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported same-store revenue guidance was lowered by ~$230 million to $2.03-$2.09 billion due to the JV, while same-store NOI is now guided to $660-$695 million and core EBITDA to $570-$600 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior FY26 guidance listed “SS revenue (CC) $2.20–2.27B,” “SS NOI (CC) $735–785M,” and “Core EBITDA $570–620M.” The preview said to “watch whether they now split guidance pre/post-JV-close.”

surprises.description: The gap between physical and economic occupancy narrowed by 240 basis points to 860 basis points, a newly reported improvement the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The gap between physical and economic occupancy narrowed 240 basis points to 860 basis points, which management views as a healthier, more sustainable long-term level.”

surprises.description: Interest expense guidance is now $155–$160 million, below the prior $170–$180 million range. The preview anticipated the debt paydown but did not forecast this lower expense range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interest expense of $155-$160 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior FY26 guidance listed “interest expense $170–180M.”

surprises.description: Fixed-commitment storage revenue was 58%, one percentage point below the preview’s watch threshold of at least 59%. The fact that all top 25 customers use fixed commitments provides a counterpoint, but the reported share missed that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fixed-commitment storage revenue held steady at 58%, with all top 25 customers (over 50% of total revenue) using the fixed-commitment structure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Fixed-commitment revenue held at 59% of rent & storage in Q1; … Watch … whether the fixed-commit share holds ≥59%.”

surprises.description: The noncash impairment charge was slightly below the preview’s already-disclosed expected range: $298.8 million versus $305–$320 million. The facilities are listed for sale, consistent with the preview’s expectation that they would be held for sale in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A noncash impairment charge of $298.8 million was recorded in Q2 tied to winding down the Lancaster and Plainville automated facilities, which are now listed for sale.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “pre-announced $305–320M non-cash impairment” would hit Q2 and expected the facilities to be “held-for-sale in Q3.”

in_line: The EQT JV received regulatory approval and remained on track to close in Q3, with about $1.1 billion of proceeds going to debt repayment—consistent with the preview’s expected clearance, Q3 close, and approximate net cash proceeds and deleveraging.

surprises.description: The FDA review picture was cleaner than the preview could confirm: the call reported no efficacy-related significant issues for either NDA, no planned advisory committee meetings, and a completed BIMO inspection with no findings or Form 483. The preview expected no AdCom but specifically wanted inspection confirmation, so the clean inspection result adds reassurance.
surprises.fact_evidence: For both ulixacaltamide and relutrigine, the FDA completed mid-cycle communications, identified no efficacy-related significant issues, and stated it does not plan to hold advisory committee meetings; the BIMO inspection concluded with no findings and no Form 483 issued.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked for “confirmation that no AdCom is planned” and asked whether there had been “an inspection”; it noted no safety or manufacturing issues had been cited.

surprises.description: Vormatrigine moved from a paused program awaiting a decision to planned redesigned POWER2 and POWER3 trials restarting by Q4 2025. The preview identified a POWER2 restart as the upside case, but its baseline expected only a decision by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: POWER1 missed its primary endpoint but hit a key secondary endpoint on the proportion of patients achieving at least 50% seizure reduction, prompting redesigned POWER2 and POWER3 trials to restart by Q4 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said POWER2 enrollment was “paused,” expected a “decision by year-end” in its base case, and described a restart as the bull case.

surprises.description: The relutrigine PDUFA date differs sharply from the preview: the call facts state December 27, 2025, rather than December 27, 2026. That would be a one-year acceleration, but the stated date is already past relative to the release, so the timing update is internally inconsistent.
surprises.fact_evidence: Relutrigine is “carrying a new PDUFA date of December 27, 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave relutrigine’s PDUFA date as “Dec 27, 2026.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating expenses came in below the preview’s estimates for both major lines: R&D was $69.4 million versus an expected $74–78 million, and G&A was $27.5 million versus an expected $32–36 million. This was a lower expense level than anticipated, even though management expects G&A to accelerate in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 operating expenses were $96.9 million, including $69.4 million of R&D and $27.5 million of G&A; G&A is expected to accelerate in the second half to fund launches.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “R&D expense” at “$74–78M” and “G&A expense” at “$32–36M.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed an early tolerability issue affecting about one in five ulixacaltamide patients and is seeking label titration instructions to improve persistence. The preview focused on launch readiness and the label process but did not flag this potential adoption or persistence issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: About 20% of patients experienced early tolerability issues that resolve with continued use, and Praxis is seeking a titration approach in the label to improve persistence.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “launch readiness and PDUFA integrity” and possible “label discussion,” but did not mention early tolerability issues.

surprises.description: EMERALD had more scale and broader coverage than the preview’s recruitment-complete description conveyed: it over-enrolled to about 200 patients across more than 50 genetic etiologies, with high baseline seizure counts. Management also positioned it as a basis for a potential 2027 supplemental NDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: EMERALD over-enrolled with approximately 200 patients spanning more than 50 genetic etiologies, a median baseline of over 50 countable seizures per 28 days, and could support a potential supplemental NDA in 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said EMERALD recruitment was complete and guided topline for Q4 2026.

surprises.description: The call added potential pediatric review vouchers for relutrigine and elsunersen, an additional possible source of value not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Both relutrigine and elsunersen are eligible for pediatric review vouchers.

in_line: Ulixacaltamide remained on the expected January approval timeline; the preview gave a January 29, 2027 PDUFA target.
The company reaffirmed runway into 2028, consistent with the preview’s baseline expectation.
POWER1’s primary-endpoint miss and achievement of a 50% responder secondary endpoint were already known and described in the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $972 million, above the preview’s $950.9–951.4 million consensus and above the $963 million top of company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 organic revenue grew 10% to $972 million, beating the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus $950.9–951.4M”; “Q2'26 Company Guide $938–963M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS came in at $0.86, beating the preview’s $0.80 consensus and exceeding the guidance midpoint by $0.06.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $0.86, beating the guidance midpoint by $0.06.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” consensus “$0.80”; company guide “$0.78–0.82.”

surprises.description: Trimble raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance more decisively than the preview’s baseline expectation of a raise roughly sized to the quarter’s beat: the revenue midpoint rose to $3.925 billion and EPS guidance to $3.65, both above the preview’s bull-case thresholds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance, lifting the revenue midpoint by $50 million to $3.925 billion (~9% growth) and EPS by $0.10 to $3.65 (~17% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a raise only by the size of the Q2 beat will read as conservative-but-fine”; its bull case called for revenue raised to “≥$3.90B and EPS to ≥$3.60.”

surprises.description: Field Systems’ ARR outlook was cut because Trimble is replacing a low-margin white-label product, creating a sizable headwind that the preview had not identified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Field Systems ARR guidance was cut to high-single-digit/low-double-digit growth due to replacing a low-margin white-label field data processing product, creating a 400-500 bps ARR headwind ($16-20M) for the segment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Field Systems as having 12% ARR growth and flagged tariff and hardware exposure, but did not anticipate a product replacement or an ARR-guidance cut.

surprises.description: Trimble said it now expects to reach its 30% EBITDA margin target in 2026, a full year ahead of the 2027 timing cited at Investor Day.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects to reach its 30% EBITDA margin target a full year early in 2026, versus the prior 2027 Investor Day goal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “progress toward the 2027 Investor Day targets” and highlighted the H2 margin ramp as a risk to the EPS guide.

surprises.description: The company authorized another $1 billion of repurchases, beyond the $608 million of authorization the preview said remained after Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a new $1 billion share repurchase authorization and has bought back nearly $1.2 billion in stock since the start of 2025, with leverage at just 1.1x versus a 2.5x long-term target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “$608M authorization remaining after Q1” and noted that buyback pace mattered, but did not anticipate a new $1 billion authorization.

in_line: Organic ARR grew 12% to a record $2.509 billion: this was within the preview’s 12–14% FY growth guide and just above its estimated $2.48–2.50 billion range, though it did not reach the preview’s ≥13% upside catalyst.
AECO ARR growth of 14% matched the preview’s stated 14% Q1 growth and its expectation that AECO remain a key growth engine.

Trimble’s Goldman Sachs-advised T&L strategic review was broadly in line with the preview’s call for a strategic update or confirmation of the reported sale process; the call provided no predetermined outcome or timeline.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating profit and EPS came in above expectations even though organic sales were about 100 basis points below internal expectations. A $45 million tariff refund—about half of what KMB paid in North America—helped produce the earnings upside; the preview had treated the $2.01 EPS consensus as demanding and expected organic growth around 2.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 organic sales came in roughly 100 basis points below internal expectations”; “received a $45 million tariff refund in Q2 … which drove adjusted operating profit and EPS above expectations despite the organic sales miss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS attributable to KMB $2.01”; “Organic sales growth ~+2.5%”; the preview called $2.01 “a demanding number.”

surprises.description: KMB lowered its full-year outlook, contrary to the preview’s base case that FY26 guidance would be reaffirmed. The stated reasons included the China disruption, the distribution-center fire, and North American retailer inventory reductions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year outlook due to discrete one-off items including the China disruption, an L.A. distribution center fire … and North American retailer inventory reductions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “FY26 reaffirmed with no change to the shape”; it also highlighted whether FY26 attributable EPS would be “reaffirmed at ~flat, or hedged.”

surprises.description: A social-media safety-claims disruption in China diaper products created an unanticipated second-half headwind: about 200 basis points to sales, roughly $70 million of operating profit and $0.16 of EPS, split between Q3 and Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A China diaper business disruption from social media safety claims (only impacting the final 2 weeks of June) is expected to be a ~200 basis point top-line headwind in the second half, roughly $70 million in operating profit and about $0.16 of EPS, split evenly across Q3 and Q4.”

surprises.description: The L.A. distribution-center fire’s reported financial hit was smaller than the preview’s estimate: about $22 million versus roughly $50 million of operating profit, although the reported 80-basis-point Q2 headwind was in the preview’s expected 70–80-basis-point range for organic growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An L.A. distribution center fire (~$22 million/80 bps Q2 headwind).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected the fire to be “~70–80bps off Q2 organic growth” and “~$50M off operating profit.”

surprises.description: North American shipments were notably weaker than underlying consumption, with retailer inventory reductions adding pressure. The preview focused on North America’s sales and profit debate and modeled organic growth near category growth, but did not anticipate shipments running 170 basis points behind consumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North American consumer shipments lagged consumption by about 170 basis points in Q2, with shipments down 1.4% versus consumption growth of only 0.3%”; the outlook reduction also cited “North American retailer inventory reductions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “organic in line with category growth”; its key debate was whether North America profit would stop going backwards.

surprises.description: Category growth weakened more than the preview’s roughly 2.5% growth assumption: North American weighted category growth slowed to 1.9%, while global trailing-12-month growth slipped to about 2%. Management also cited increasing pressure on lower-income consumers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Weighted category growth in North America moderated sequentially from 3.7% last quarter to 1.9%, with global trailing-12-month category growth slipping from ~2.5% to ~2% amid increasing pressure on lower-income consumers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “organic sales growth ~+2.5% (category growth ~2.5%)” and FY26 organic growth “in line to ahead of category growth (~2.5% LTM).”

surprises.description: KMB unveiled a proprietary alternative natural-fiber program, including acquired land and a pilot facility beginning construction, that was not part of the preview’s discussion. The company says it is intended to improve margins and reduce forest-fiber cost volatility, with investment already included in results and outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kimberly-Clark unveiled a proprietary alternative natural fiber program (with land already acquired and a pilot facility breaking ground) aimed at improving margins and reducing forest fiber cost volatility, with investments already embedded in current results and outlook.”

in_line: KMB delivered 6.4% gross productivity, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of a third consecutive year of roughly 6% productivity.

Management expects to fully offset second-half inflation and keep full-year price-net-of-cost inflation roughly neutral, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q2 cost pressure would be mitigated in the second half.
The Kenvue acquisition is expected to close in Q4, within the preview’s anticipated 2H26 closing window.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $152.5 million, well above both the roughly $129 million implied by management’s flat-sequential guide and the $136.6 million consensus. Instead of staying near Q1’s level, sales rose 18.6% sequentially, making the year-over-year decline smaller than the preview’s 29% consensus decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales were $152.5 million,” up “18.6% sequentially from Q1's $128 million,” exceeding the company's prior expectation of flat sequential revenue; sales were down 21% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue ($136.6M) sits ~6% above management's own ‘flat sequentially’ guide (~$129M)”; the consensus table projected revenue down 29% year-over-year.

surprises.description: Gross margin recovered much more sharply than the preview’s flat-or-slightly-better guide and 23% base case suggested: it reached 27.1%, above even the preview’s 24%+ recovery threshold. EBITDA margin also improved substantially sequentially, although it remained below the year-ago level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved approximately 420 basis points sequentially to 27.1% from 22.9%,” driven by Wisconsin operational improvements. EBITDA margin improved 670 basis points sequentially to 16.9%, versus 17.8% a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided gross margin “flat or slightly better” for Q2, set a 23.0% base case, and said “24%+” would give the recovery narrative its first real datapoint.

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $0.73 substantially exceeded the preview’s $0.32 consensus estimate. It was still below the preview’s roughly $0.95 adjusted prior-year comparison, but the year-over-year decline was much less severe than the preview’s clean-comp estimate of about 66%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income was $16.9 million ($0.73 per diluted share), down from $51.2 million ($2.22) a year ago,” with the prior-year result including a “$29.2 million ($1.27 per share) tax benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 diluted EPS consensus of “$0.32” and estimated prior-year “clean” operating EPS of “~$0.95,” implying a roughly 66% decline.

surprises.description: Cash generation was much stronger than the preview’s expectation of a working-capital build ahead of the second-half ramp: operating cash flow reached $56.6 million and the company used cash to reduce debt by about $38.8 million during the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow surged to $56.6 million in Q2” versus $20.2 million a year earlier, enabling “a total debt reduction of approximately $38.8 million”; quarter-end cash was $70.1 million and total debt about $72.6 million, down from $103.4 million at March 31.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$95M drawn against $45.1M cash” and said “A working-capital build ahead of the H2 ramp is expected and fine.”

in_line: Management said second-half 2026 sales should exceed first-half sales and be roughly in line with second-half 2025, consistent with the preview’s expectation that management would reaffirm H2 sales approximately in line with H2 2025.
Oil and gas demand remained soft with no significant improvement expected for the rest of the year, consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued near-term weakness.
No quantified backlog or data-center commitment was reported; the preview described the base case as an unquantified reaffirmation and treated quantified visibility as a potential bull surprise.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was expected to be about $1.06, but Innospec reported $1.27—roughly 20% above consensus, despite being essentially flat year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS essentially flat at $1.27 versus $1.26 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $1.06.”

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to be about $462.35 million, but came in at $491.4 million, about 6% above consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenues rose 12% year-over-year to $491.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $462.35M.”

surprises.description: Oilfield Services substantially outperformed the preview’s estimates: revenue was $115.4 million versus $105 million expected, and operating income was $8.7 million versus $6.5 million expected. The preview anticipated only a gradual improvement and management’s cautious stance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oilfield Services was the standout with revenue up 14% to $115.4 million and operating income up 40% to $8.7 million,” with gross margin up 2.7 points to 32.3%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Oilfield Services” Q2’26E “Rev / OI” of “$105M / $6.5M”; management was described as “cautiously optimistic.”

surprises.description: Performance Chemicals beat the preview’s model, with revenue of $190.3 million versus $178 million expected and operating income of $16.4 million versus $15.5 million expected. Price/mix and currency more than offset a 2% volume decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Performance Chemicals revenue grew 9% to $190.3 million, with an 8% positive price/mix and 3% favorable currency offsetting a 2% volume decline, driving 15% operating income growth to $16.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Performance Chemicals Q2’26E “Rev / OI” of “$178M / $15.5M.”

surprises.description: Fuel Specialties revenue exceeded the $180 million estimate, reaching $185.7 million on 7% volume growth. That stronger top line came with the expected margin pressure, however, and operating-income growth was limited to 3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fuel Specialties revenue rose 12% to $185.7 million on 7% volume growth, but gross margin fell 1.5 points to 36.6% on weaker sales mix, limiting operating income growth to just 3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Fuel Specialties Q2’26E revenue of “$180M”; the preview also flagged “some gross margin compression” and operating income “a little lighter than Q1.”

surprises.description: Management said Fuel Specialties margins would likely face further sequential pressure in Q3 before potentially stabilizing, indicating that the raw-material pricing lag is likely to persist into Q3 rather than clearly reverse sooner.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fuel Specialties margins will likely face further sequential pressure in Q3 due to the pricing lag against cost inflation before potentially stabilizing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified whether the raw-material lag “reverses in Q3 or extends” as the key question, and asked whether pricing had “caught up” or the lag would “persist into H2.”

surprises.description: The preview described the North Carolina plants as repaired, but management said repairs were only about 60% complete and expected to finish by the end of Q4. The eventual efficiency gains are meaningful—more than 10% additional capacity next year without extra CapEx—but arrive later than the preview’s recovery framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The North Carolina Performance Chemicals plant repairs are about 60% complete, expected to finish by end of Q4, with efficiency gains projected to add north of 10% capacity for next year without additional CapEx.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the “NC plants” as “repaired” and said the backlog was “largely worked through.”

surprises.description: Oilfield demand and expansion prospects sounded stronger than the preview’s cautious framing: existing DRA capacity was nearly sold out, management was discussing another expansion, and it cited strong Middle East demand tied to East-West pipeline shipments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DRA capacity added is nearly sold out with strong Middle East demand tied to East-West pipeline shipments, and management is discussing a further DRA expansion,” alongside new technologies and potential Mexico opportunities within roughly six months.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said DRA capacity was “maxed out in Q2 and Q4,” described management as “cautiously optimistic,” and cited heavy-crude opportunities in Argentina, Venezuela, and Mexico.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA fell short of the preview’s modeled range: $50.1 million versus an estimate of roughly $52–54 million, even as revenue and adjusted EPS beat consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA edged up only modestly to $50.1 million from $49.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (my est.): ~$52–54M.”

in_line: Performance Chemicals operating income improved sequentially from $10.7 million in Q1 to $16.4 million in Q2, consistent with the preview’s expected Q2 recovery, though the preview had modeled a slightly lower $15.5 million.
Fuel Specialties operating income was lighter than Q1 as previewed: it grew 3% year over year from $35.4 million, implying about $36.5 million, below Q1’s $37.8 million.
The buyback remained modest: Innospec repurchased just over 87,000 shares for $6.4 million, close to the $6.2 million used in Q1 rather than an acceleration.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case put Q2 gross margin at 9–12%, but KSCP reported about 7% ($0.7 million). Gross margin was positive for a second consecutive quarter, but it came in below that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin turned positive at $0.7 million (~7% of revenue), the second consecutive positive gross margin quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... Gross Margin 9–12%”; the preview also said to watch whether Q1’s 7.7% margin was “a trend or a one-quarter artifact.”

surprises.description: The preview derived Q2 EPS of about -$0.60, while KSCP reported a loss of $0.79 per share. That is a larger loss per share than the already caveated estimate, even though the reported loss per share improved year over year because of a larger share count.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $14.1 million ($0.79 per share) ... though loss per share improved due to a larger share count.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 EPS | ~-$0.60 (derived, not published)” and “Base: ... -$0.60 to -$0.70.”

surprises.description: The preview expected K7’s limited release by late summer 2026; KSCP instead said initial deployments remain on track for Q4. That puts the stated deployment milestone later than the preview anticipated.
