surprises.description: Ramaco disclosed a plan to grow total production above 6 million tons from about 4 million currently, with low-vol coal reaching half the slate, new Maven sections adding roughly 600,000 tons, and a rail loadout lowering transport costs on that coal by about $20 per ton. The preview focused on possible volume trims and did not describe this growth plan or its logistics savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: The strategy targets “over 6 million tons (from ~4 million currently) with low vol rising to 50% of the slate,” including Maven sections adding “~600,000 tons” and a rail loadout “cutting transport costs ~$20/ton on that coal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 production guidance of “3.7 – 4.1M tons” and identified reaffirmation or a trim as the volume catalyst; it did not describe the longer-term Maven expansion or rail savings.

surprises.description: Ramaco ended Q2 with more than 1 million tons of coal inventory, valued at about $100 million, which it is holding for better prices. The preview discussed the committed book and floating-price exposure but did not anticipate this volume being held back for later sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: Ramaco ended Q2 with “roughly 1 million tons of coal inventory (~$100 million) being held to sell at better prices as markets improve.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said 3.5Mt, or “~90% of planned production,” was committed and highlighted the 1.4Mt index-linked tranche as the market-exposed volume.

in_line: The Brook Mine’s headline potential economics were broadly consistent with the preview’s already-released Hatch figures: the call cited a potential NPV up to $8 billion and average adjusted EBITDA up to $1.3 billion. The preview had reported an expanded-case NPV of about $8 billion and annual EBITDA of about $1.3 billion.
The approximately 75% share of Brook Mine revenue tied to non-rare-earth critical minerals such as gallium, germanium, and silica was already highlighted in the preview.

The FY26 capex increase was modest and in the direction the preview expected: guidance rose from about $90 million to $92–97 million, while the preview said the stale $90 million figure “should go up.”

Diesel and high-end cost pressure were flagged in the preview; the call quantified diesel at an average of $4.64 per gallon in Q2, adding about $3 per ton, and said Q3 costs should trend toward the high end of guidance.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case expected Q2 revenue around $318M, with consensus at $318.8M and the buy-side whisper at $325–330M. WEST reported about $306M, roughly 4% below consensus and further below the whisper.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 net sales rose 8.8% to ~$306 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales $318.8M”; “buy-side whisper at ~$325–330M revenue”; “My base case: revenue $318M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected free cash flow to remain negative in Q2 and identified H2 2026 as the target for becoming FCF-positive. WEST instead generated $20.2M of Q2 free cash flow and was positive for the first half, a quarter ahead of schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company turned free cash flow positive a quarter ahead of schedule, generating $20.2 million in free cash flow in Q2 and positive free cash flow for the first half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management promised FCF-positive in H2 2026”; the base case anticipated “FCF still negative but improving.”

surprises.description: The preview expected lower coffee prices to provide a gross-margin tailwind. Instead, Q2 gross profit declined year over year, with Conway depreciation and amortization and a negative mark-to-market impact outweighing that expectation; first-half gross profit was nevertheless higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross profit fell $3.6 million year-over-year to $37.7 million due to $4.1 million in incremental Conway depreciation/amortization and a $2 million negative mark-to-market impact, though first-half gross profit rose 19%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Lower C-price is a gross-margin tailwind and a working-capital release.”

surprises.description: Beverage Solutions EBITDA came in above the preview’s expected clean level of at least $20M. The reported $22.2M also just exceeded the preview’s bull-case threshold of more than $22M.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Beverage Solutions net sales grew nearly 17% year-over-year, driving segment adjusted EBITDA up 13% to $22.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Look for clean BevSol EBITDA ≥$20M”; the bull case called for “clean BevSol EBITDA >$22M.”

surprises.description: Management described a pipeline of eight new products expected to launch over the next 24 months, with growth positioned to come without additional CapEx or new sales wins. The preview discussed existing-asset capacity and customer opportunities, but did not flag this specific product-launch pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has eight new products expected to launch over the next 24 months” and is “positioning for growth without additional CapEx or new sales wins.”

in_line: Q2 consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $21.3M, within the preview’s $20–22M base-case range, though below its $22–23M buy-side whisper; the preview’s central estimate was about $21M.
Management reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $90–100M without raising it, as the preview’s base case expected.
Secured net leverage was 3.36x, within the preview’s expected 3.2–3.4x range and below the tightened 4.00x covenant.
The 2026 CapEx outlook of about $30M matched the preview’s stated expectation of roughly $30M.
Full replacement of the lost single-serve customer volume remained targeted by the end of 2027, matching the preview’s timeline.

surprises.description: The preview expected a net loss of $11–15 million and EPS of $(0.48)–$(0.65), partly anticipating a warrant-related mark-to-market loss. Veru instead reported a $7 million net loss and EPS of $(0.30), a materially smaller loss than forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 net loss narrowed to $7 million ($0.30 per diluted share) from $7.3 million ($0.50 per diluted share) in the prior period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss (GAAP) … My estimate: $11–15M”; “EPS … $(0.48) – $(0.65)”; the preview also said the net loss and EPS “can look materially worse” because of a warrant mark-to-market loss.

surprises.description: Cash at June 30 was $23.9 million, above the preview’s $20–22 million estimate and its stated $23 million threshold for a genuine positive. The balance was supported by $23.3 million in net public-offering proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash rose to $23.9 million as of June 30, 2026”; the balance was “bolstered by $23.3 million in net proceeds from a public offering.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “$20–22M” cash and said “above $23M is a genuine positive.”

surprises.description: Veru disclosed that Novo Nordisk’s supply agreement gives Novo a right of first negotiation on enobosarm combined with any Novo GLP-1 product. The preview characterized the arrangement as a supply deal, not an economic partnership, and treated broader business-development terms as unlikely.
surprises.fact_evidence: Novo “provides Wegovy free of charge and receives a right of first negotiation on enobosarm combined with any Novo GLP-1 product.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called it a “clinical supply agreement” and “a supply deal, not an economic partnership”; it said broader partnership or licensing discussion was the highest-torque possibility and that “absence of comment is the base case.”

surprises.description: G&A expense was $3.4 million, below the preview’s $3.8–4.2 million estimate. Veru attributed the decline to lower share-based compensation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “G&A fell to $3.4 million from $5 million on lower share-based compensation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated G&A of “$3.8–4.2M.”

in_line: R&D expense was $4.4 million, within the preview’s $4.0–4.8 million estimate; the preview expected an increase as PLATEAU ramped up.
Management retained the expected cash-runway language: current cash is expected to fund operations “beyond the interim analysis,” consistent with the preview’s key runway expectation.

PLATEAU’s 239 patients and completed enrollment were consistent with the preview’s expectation of full enrollment above the approximately 200-patient target; the Q1 2027 interim analysis and Q4 2027 final-data timing also matched the preview.
The patent notice extending protection to at least October 3, 2044, and the basic Novo Wegovy supply arrangement were already flagged in the preview.

surprises.description: Ring raised full-year 2026 capital spending guidance to $158–$178 million, far above the preview’s $115 million expectation. Management said $80–$100 million is planned for the second half, including accelerated infrastructure investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 capital spending guidance was increased to $158-$178 million, with $80-$100 million planned for the second half to accelerate development infrastructure investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY capex $115M” and said the market wanted “debt paydown, not a rig.”

surprises.description: Oil realizations were better than the preview’s estimate: Ring realized about $95.45 per barrel versus the preview’s roughly $92 estimate. The preview had identified realizations below $88 as a warning sign, so the reported price was materially stronger than its modeled level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Realized oil pricing rose 38% to approximately $95.45 per barrel.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Realized oil ~$92” and said “Anything below $88 signals differential blowout.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $104.7 million, below the preview’s $108 million base estimate, although above its cited $93.3 million consensus. The result therefore beat the published consensus but fell short of the preview’s own expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue of roughly $104.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Revenue | $93.3M” consensus and “My Q2'26E | $108M.”

surprises.description: Ring’s initial 2027 outlook paired roughly 10% volume growth with a capital budget whose midpoint is about 10% below the revised 2026 midpoint. That gives a more constructive growth-and-spending outlook than the preview’s concern about an activity increase that could undermine debt reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Initial 2027 guidance projects BOE volumes of 21,500-23,500/day (midpoint growth ~10% over 2026) with capital spending of $135-$165 million, a ~10% midpoint reduction versus 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether management would “hold the line on discipline” and said “The buy-side wants debt paydown, not a rig.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a substantial potential cost benefit from its infrastructure work and longer laterals: at least $7.5 million of savings across the planned 20–30 wells in 2027. The preview did not anticipate this specific efficiency target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Infrastructure investments and longer laterals are expected to cut future drilling and completion costs by at least $7.5 million across the planned 20-30 wells in 2027.”

surprises.description: Ring lowered its second-half LOE guidance to a $10.00–$10.60 per BOE range, below the preview’s cited $10.55 company guide and its $10.40 estimate. The midpoint of the new range is $10.30 per BOE.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowering LOE guidance to $10.00-$10.60 per BOE (midpoint down ~2%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “LOE/Boe | $10.55 (co. guide)” and estimated “$10.40.”

surprises.description: The call indicated that the hedge book would leave more exposure to market prices than the preview’s stated coverage assumptions, especially for gas, and that 2027 coverage would loosen further. That increases upside participation but also leaves more commodity-price exposure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For the remainder of 2026, ~70% of oil … and ~62% of natural gas … is hedged”; “hedged exposure loosens to ~60-64% in 2027, providing more upside participation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “~72% of 2026 oil” hedged and “73% covered” for gas, and flagged possible “hedge restructuring.”

in_line: Q2 oil sales were within guidance, and total BOE sales of 19,990/day were close to the preview’s 20,200/day expectation.
Natural gas remained under pressure from the Waha/Permian pricing environment, as the preview had warned; the call reported a negative $8.14/Mcf differential to NYMEX.

The equity proceeds were used to reduce debt, consistent with the preview’s account that the approximately $65 million raise had funded the previously announced reduction in debt to about $360 million.

surprises.description: Q2 SaaS growth was 4.2%, below the preview's stated +8% catalyst threshold and short of the pace it said was needed to support the full-year double-digit target. That makes the reaffirmed target harder to reconcile with the quarter's growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 SaaS revenue grew 4.2% year-over-year to $1.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SaaS growth ≥ +8% YoY — below this, the FY26 double-digit commitment is dead on arrival”; the preview also said Q2–Q4 must average roughly “+13% YoY” after a flat Q1.

surprises.description: Despite Q2 SaaS growth falling well below the preview's threshold, management reaffirmed double-digit SaaS growth for fiscal 2026 rather than softening or withdrawing the target as the preview's base case anticipated. The reaffirmation came without quantified second-half detail in the supplied facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed guidance for double-digit year-over-year SaaS growth for fiscal 2026, unchanged from prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected the guide to be “softened to ‘year-over-year growth’”; the preview described reaffirmation as the bull case, “with specifics.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses were materially above the preview's estimated clean run-rate, reaching $3.7 million rather than roughly $3.23 million. The increase included higher variable compensation, added engineering staff, and more share-based compensation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating expenses rose 14.7% to $3.7 million,” including a “24.4% jump in G&A” and “roughly $229,000 more share-based compensation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1's $3.66M included ~$430K of CEO transition costs and that “the clean run-rate is ~$3.23M”; Q2 materially above that would indicate spending into growth and push profitability out.

surprises.description: Profitability was weaker than the preview's base case: the net loss was $1.1 million, or $0.24 per share, versus the base-case estimate of a $0.14 loss per share. Adjusted EBITDA was also more negative than the base case, though less negative than the preview's bear-case estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $1.1 million ($0.24 loss per share)” and “adjusted EBITDA swung to a loss of $331,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base case estimated GAAP EPS of “$(0.14)” and adjusted EBITDA of “$(0.15)M”; its bear case estimated EPS of “$(0.22)” and adjusted EBITDA of “$(0.50)M.”

surprises.description: Professional services revenue slipped to $1.8 million from $1.85 million in Q1, rather than clearly stabilizing as the preview was watching for. The company also reported reduced scanning activity and a lower backlog, but said it had since taken orders to refill that backlog, a potentially positive offset not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Professional services revenue fell 5.8% to $1.8 million” due to “reduced scanning project activity and lower backlog,” though the company “has since taken orders to refill that backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for watching “Professional services sequential direction” and said “sequential stabilization here is the difference between a base and bear print.”

in_line: Consolidated gross margin was 66.4%, meeting the preview's marker of a recovery toward 66%+ from Q1's 63.5%, even though the reported Q2 margin declined 162 basis points year over year.
Cash ended the quarter at $1.7 million with no debt, at the upper end of the preview's expected $1.5–$1.7 million cash range after another quarter of roughly $400–500K burn.

surprises.description: Revenue was $23.3 million, about 5.3% below the $24.6 million consensus and down 5% year over year, rather than roughly flat. The shortfall was larger than the preview’s bear-case revenue range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 5% year-over-year to $23.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $24.60M” with “Implied YoY 0.0%”; the preview also described the functional bar as “revenue $24.4–24.7M (any YoY growth at all).”

surprises.description: Management withdrew the prior Q4 breakeven net-income guidance and is now targeting only a return to positive free cash flow in Q4. That is a clear retreat from the unqualified breakeven reaffirmation the preview identified as critical.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management withdrew its prior guidance for Q4 breakeven net income, now targeting only a return to positive free cash flow in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 2026 breakeven and 2027 profitability, reaffirmed or hedged”; the preview called an “unqualified reaffirmation” important.

surprises.description: The reported loss of $0.12 per share narrowly beat the $0.13 consensus loss, but was materially worse than the preview’s functional buy-side bar of a loss no wider than $0.08. The headline result was therefore a slight consensus beat, not the stronger loss performance that bar implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $3.0 million (-$0.12 per share) from a $1.8 million loss (-$0.07 per share) a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS $(0.13)” consensus; the preview’s functional buy-side bar was “loss no wider than ~$(0.08).”

surprises.description: Management also walked back earlier expectations of double-digit Q4 revenue growth. The preview anticipated a Q4 uptick, but this update removes the earlier double-digit growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “walking back earlier expectations of double-digit Q4 revenue growth.”

surprises.description: Cash fell to $5.3 million, far below the preview’s expectation of cash near $13 million. Management attributed the decline to a $2.4 million seasonal renewal impact, lower revenue, and higher marketing costs, while noting the $10 million credit line is fully available.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash fell to $5.3 million as of June 30, 2026, pressured by a $2.4 million seasonal renewal impact, lower revenue and higher marketing costs, with a fully available $10 million line of credit as backup.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A tenth consecutive positive FCF quarter with cash near $13M keeps the dilution question closed.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 85.3%, about 70 basis points below the preview’s roughly 86% model and down 140 basis points year over year, twice the decline the preview modeled. Management attributed the pressure to lower revenue against a relatively fixed content-cost base.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 85.3% from 86.7% a year ago due to lower revenue against a relatively fixed content cost base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin n/a (model ~86%)”; the preview estimated “-70bps” year over year.

surprises.description: A major advertising partner’s algorithm change caused a CPA spike in April and May and pressured results, an issue not anticipated in the preview. Management said the problem has since been corrected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A CPA spike in April and May, driven by an algorithm change at a major advertising partner, pressured results, though management states the issue has since been corrected.”

surprises.description: Gaia reported more than $3 million in annualized cost savings executed or identified since late February, with the full benefit expected by year-end. That gives a more specific and substantial cost-savings update than the preview’s general expectation of cost discipline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has executed or identified over $3 million in annualized cost savings since starting its spend review in late February, with full benefit expected by year-end”; G&A fell to “$1.5 million from $2.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “EPS beats $(0.13) comfortably because of cost discipline,” but did not give a savings figure.

surprises.description: Management quantified direct-member economics as lifetime value above $500 against an $85 acquisition cost, roughly a 6:1 ratio. The preview noted the $85 CAC and the shift toward direct memberships, but did not provide this LTV figure or ratio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct members carry a lifetime value of over $500 against an $85 customer acquisition cost, roughly a 6:1 ratio that underpins the strategy to sacrifice lower-quality revenue.”

in_line: Management said it remains on track for Q4 2026 targets of a 20% improvement in churn reduction and ARPU growth, broadly matching the preview’s stated Q4 targets of about 20% lower churn and 20–25% higher ARPU.
Management expects Q3 to mark the revenue bottom, followed by sequential growth in Q4, consistent with the preview’s expectation that revenue would be soft in the near term and uptick into Q4.

The revenue decline was attributed to pulling back from lower-value international regions and third-party acquisition channels, consistent with the preview’s discussion of intentionally shedding lower-value third-party subscribers and accepting near-term revenue pressure.

surprises.description: Horace Mann reported Q2 core EPS of $1.17, well above the preview's $0.91 consensus estimate and its base-case range of $0.95–$1.02. The result also rose more than 10% year over year, versus the preview's expectation of a 14% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 core earnings of $1.17 per share, up more than 10% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Core EPS **$0.91**” consensus; base-case scenario: “Core EPS **$0.95–$1.02**”; consensus Y/Y: “**-14%**.”

surprises.description: Management raised 2026 core EPS guidance to $4.60–$4.90, above the prior $4.20–$4.50 range and even above the preview's bull-case range of $4.40–$4.60. The increase was attributed entirely to operating performance, not acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 core EPS guidance to a range of $4.60 to $4.90,” attributing the increase “entirely to strong operating performance rather than acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … Core EPS **$4.20–$4.50**”; bull scenario expected guidance “raised or narrowed to **$4.40–$4.60**.”

surprises.description: The P&C combined ratio improved to 89.6%, substantially better than the preview's estimated 97–99%. Favorable weather, lower catastrophe losses, and $7 million of favorable prior-year reserve development contributed to the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Property & Casualty combined ratio improved 7 points to 89.6%,” aided by “favorable weather, lower catastrophe losses, and $7 million in favorable prior-year reserve development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “P&C combined ratio ~97–99% (est.).”

surprises.description: The company cut its full-year catastrophe loss assumption to about $75 million from about $90 million. The preview expected the existing $90 million load and noted a benign national catastrophe backdrop, but management also cautioned that favorable weather is not expected to continue in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year catastrophe loss assumptions were cut from approximately $90 million to $75 million based on favorable first-half experience,” while management “does not expect the favorable weather to continue into the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cat load **~$90M**.”

surprises.description: Full-year net investment income guidance was lowered to $465–$475 million, below the preview's $485–$495 million range. The weakness was in alternative strategies, despite new fixed-income yields reaching 5.85%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net investment income guidance was lowered to $465-$475 million due to weaker returns on alternative strategies … sensitive to higher-for-longer rates,” while “core fixed income new money yields reached 5.85%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NII **$485–495M** pre-tax”; the preview also said weak alternative returns could force a reduction to the NII guide.

surprises.description: Individual Supplemental & Group Benefits sales surged 44%, while Life sales grew 20%. The preview highlighted prior sales momentum in these businesses but did not anticipate these Q2 growth rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Individual Supplemental & Group Benefits sales surged 44% and Life sales grew 20%.”

surprises.description: Management raised its blended benefit-ratio assumption for Individual Supplemental & Group Benefits to about 42%, citing growth in paid family and medical leave, which has higher benefit ratios. Lower expense ratios partly offset that pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its Individual Supplemental & Group Benefits blended benefit ratio assumption to approximately 42%,” driven by paid family and medical leave “which carries higher benefit ratios offset by lower expense ratios.”

in_line: Revenue increased 8% year over year, broadly matching the preview's approximately 7.5% growth expectation.
P&C core earnings of $26 million were at the upper end of the preview's $20–$26 million base-case range, even though the combined ratio was much better than its estimate.
The expected roughly 100 basis points of acquisition-related ROE accretion was consistent with the preview's estimate of about 100 basis points.

surprises.description: RMR said it is on pace to generate more than $40 million in incentive fees in calendar 2026, up from $23.6 million in 2025. The preview expected incentive fees again but did not anticipate this much higher total; DHC is expected to provide about 75% of it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “On pace to generate over $40 million in incentive fees for calendar year 2026, up from $23.6 million earned for calendar year 2025, with DHC representing about 75% of the projected total.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CY2026 incentive-fee tracking commentary for DHC/ILPT”; the preview noted RMR was “on track to earn incentive fees again this year” but gave no projected total.

surprises.description: Recurring service revenue reached $45.5 million, above the preview’s roughly $44 million expectation. However, RMR expects it to be roughly flat around $45 million next quarter, below the preview’s stated buy-side aspiration of at least $46 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring service revenues rose approximately $3.5 million sequentially to $45.5 million, but are expected to remain flat at roughly $45 million next quarter as Greenwich acquisition fees roll off.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Recurring service revenue (~$44M guided) is the signal”; for Q4, “Buy-side wants … recurring service revenue ≥$46M.”

surprises.description: RMR’s Q4 distributable-earnings guidance of $0.48–$0.50 per share falls below the preview’s expected $0.50–$0.53 range, with only the top of the company’s range reaching the bottom of that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RMR guided to Q4 … distributable earnings of $0.48–0.50 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “FQ4 DE guided $0.50–0.53 on full-quarter OPI”; the catalyst checklist said buy-side wanted “DE guided ≥$0.52.”

surprises.description: RMR recorded a $19 million net non-cash impairment tied to OPI’s bankruptcy emergence, an adverse one-off the preview did not flag despite discussing the emergence and new fee arrangements. The 2% equity in the new OPI entity partly offsets the charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded a $19 million net non-cash impairment charge tied to OPI's bankruptcy emergence, partially offset by receiving 2% equity in the new OPI entity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed OPI’s June 17 emergence and the “2% OPI equity grant,” but did not mention an impairment charge.

surprises.description: Management described global real estate fundraising in the first half as having fallen to a nine-year low. The preview already warned that Middle East conflict was disrupting fundraising and reducing 2026 deployment, but did not indicate fundraising had reached such a low level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global real estate fundraising in the first half of the calendar year hit a nine-year low amid Middle East conflict headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Middle East conflict had “disrupted fundraising, with 2026 capital deployment down ~50% y/y.”

surprises.description: Management put a specific figure on RMR’s valuation discount, saying its shares trade at just over 5 times EBITDA from its evergreen management contracts versus a 16.5-times average for peers. The preview discussed the share price and valuation setup but did not include this comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated RMR shares trade at just over 5x the EBITDA from its 20 evergreen management contracts versus a 16.5x average multiple for peers, signaling a significant valuation discount.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the stock’s price and the analyst price target but did not state a comparable-company multiple or this specific valuation gap.

in_line: Q3 distributable earnings of $0.48 per share and adjusted EBITDA of $19.7 million met company guidance of $0.48–$0.50 and $19–$21 million, respectively.
The initial five-year OPI management agreement and $14 million annual business management fee for the first two years were in line with the preview’s description of the post-bankruptcy fee reset.
The Greenwich, Connecticut JV’s roughly $350 million size and approximately $750,000 in annual management fees matched the preview’s expectations.
Private capital AUM above $12 billion was consistent with the preview’s roughly $12 billion figure.
Liquidity above $130 million was broadly consistent with the preview’s approximately $133 million liquidity figure and its stated buffer of more than $100 million.

surprises.description: LEGH shipped 113 workforce homes in Q2, far below the preview’s assumption of roughly 300 units and its expectation that at least half of a 600-unit backlog would ship. The call described a 380-unit contract, with 267 units still to deliver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company began delivering on its 380-unit workforce housing contract, shipping 113 units this quarter” and has “a remaining backlog of 267 units.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said ‘at least half’ ships in Q2”; consensus was “effectively modeling ~300 workforce units.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $0.99, well above the preview’s $0.68 consensus estimate. The reported low tax rate was a favorable contributor, though the call also expects that rate to rise in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS reached $0.99 versus $0.60 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS $0.68” Q2’26 consensus.

surprises.description: Revenue reached $66.3 million, exceeding the preview’s $59.9 million consensus by $6.4 million, or about 11%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total net revenue rose 32.3% year-over-year to $66.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue $59.9M” Q2’26 consensus.

surprises.description: Product sales were $53.8 million, above the preview’s roughly $48 million operational estimate, despite the much lower-than-expected workforce shipment count. The call also reported higher revenue per unit as the mix shifted toward higher-value homes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product sales increased 40% to $53.8 million,” with “net revenue per unit rising to roughly $74,900 from $68,100 on a shift toward higher-value homes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s operational estimate was “~$11.5M interest income + ~$48M product sales.”

surprises.description: The effective tax rate was unusually low in Q2, but management expects it to move toward 21% in the second half. The preview did not flag the Section 45L credit’s expiration or the resulting tax-rate change, making this a near-term earnings benefit with a second-half headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The effective tax rate fell to 11.2% from 17.3% due to the Section 45L energy-efficient home credit and reversal of uncertain tax positions,” and management expects it “to move toward the 21% statutory rate in the second half since the credit terminated June 30.”

surprises.description: Cash and operating cash generation were stronger than the preview’s liquidity snapshot suggested: cash was $29 million versus the preview’s $14.1 million figure, and first-half operating cash flow more than doubled year over year. The preview had already noted the workforce-order advance, so that deposit itself was not new.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow more than doubled to $24.4 million in the first half from $11 million a year ago”; cash was “$29 million (up from $8.5 million at year-end),” with a $10.7 million rise in customer deposits including a $7.1 million nonrefundable workforce-order advance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “$14.1M cash and a near-undrawn $50M revolver” and noted “$7.1M booked in Q1.”

in_line: Loan interest income was about as expected: the preview implied approximately $11.5 million, and the call reported $11.5 million.

The bridge-note outcome broadly matched the preview’s expectation of a negotiated partial repayment and renewal-style resolution: the borrower made a partial paydown and received forbearance terms, with management expecting no loss.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $3.1 million, roughly flat with Q1 and about 11% below the preview’s $3.47 million consensus. The preview said consensus implied 13% sequential growth, so the reported quarter was weaker than that growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 217% year-over-year to approximately $3.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2'26 Consensus | ~$3.47M (+254% YoY, +13% QoQ)”

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was substantially worse than expected: GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.53 versus the preview’s $0.21 loss estimate. The reported net loss was $2.9 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP net loss was $2.9 million, or $0.53 per share.”

surprises.description: First-half gross margin was 19%, far below the preview’s roughly 36% expectation. Tooling costs persisted in Q2 despite the preview saying the U.S. manufacturer tooling investment would conclude then; management also cited costly alternative sourcing and absorbing costs to protect customers. Management expects sequential recovery in Q3 and Q4, with price increases and overseas manufacturing, and reaffirmed a long-term target above 40%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half gross margin fell to 19%” with Q2 margins compressed by “one-time U.S. contract manufacturer retooling costs, higher-cost alternative component sourcing amid AI-driven supply shortages, and a deliberate choice to absorb costs to protect key customers.” Management “expects sequential margin recovery in Q3 and Q4” and reaffirmed “40%-plus gross margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~36% (unguided)” and “Management said US contract-manufacturer tooling investment would conclude in Q2.”

surprises.description: The national retailer rollout appears much further along than the preview’s last disclosed count: management said the roughly 4,700-store deployment is about 90% complete, versus about 1,500 locations previously installed. The planned warehouse expansion also adds a sizable next phase, targeting roughly 550 sites in early 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The largest deployment with a leading national retailer targeting ~4,700 U.S. stores is now roughly 90% complete,” with expansion into “~50 membership warehouse locations planned to scale to ~550 sites in early 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Last disclosed: ~1,500 of ~4,700 planned US locations at the retailer” and “Watch whether the retailer install pace implies completion on schedule.”

surprises.description: The Fortune 10 e-commerce/cloud deployment has broadened beyond the 14 international installations last reported, with multiple markets and five active use cases. The preview had cited a target of about 35 facilities in 2026, but the call facts do not provide an updated facility count or confirm that target.
surprises.fact_evidence: The customer “has expanded beyond the 14 international installations reported in Q1 to multiple international markets with five distinct use cases in active but not-yet-fully-scaled deployment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “14+ international installs at the e-commerce/grocery customer, targeting ~35 facilities in 2026.”

surprises.description: A federal agency proof of concept was a top-five customer and generated meaningful Q2 revenue, with potential to expand to as many as 500 sites. The preview did not flag this customer or deployment, so this adds an unanticipated source of current and potential revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A federal government agency proof of concept generated meaningful Q2 revenue (a top-five customer) and could span up to 500 sites over two to three years, with ~15 sites planned over the remainder of this year.”

surprises.description: Management reported a faster enterprise sales cycle and much larger pipeline opportunities, neither of which the preview highlighted. This is a favorable change in the company’s stated commercial momentum, though it does not quantify conversions or revenue from the pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The enterprise sales cycle has shortened to six-to-nine months from 18-to-24 months two years ago,” and “individual pipeline opportunities are now many multiples larger than a year ago.”

surprises.description: Revenue concentration improved substantially from the prior year: five customers represented about 74% of Q2 revenue, compared with two customers representing about 94% a year earlier. The preview had flagged customer concentration as a key issue but did not anticipate this degree of diversification.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Five customers made up ~74% of Q2 revenue, versus two customers representing ~94% a year earlier, reflecting broader commercial diversification.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Customer concentration. Fugazi flagged 99% of accounts receivable in three customers. Any 10-Q disclosure change here cuts both ways.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed no additional ATM usage or equity financing plans for the year, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would honor its stated no-ATM pledge.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.15, far above the preview’s $0.30 consensus and also well above its own $0.55–$0.75 guidance-based estimate. The gap was large even allowing for the preview’s warning that consensus was a weak anchor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $9.1 million or $1.15 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus ($0.30 adj EPS)”; the preview’s guidance-based estimate was “adj. EPS ≈ $0.55–0.75.”

surprises.description: Reported adjusted EBITDA of $35.6 million exceeded the preview’s $27–$29 million estimate, but a $7.2 million duty-related benefit explains much of the difference: excluding it, EBITDA was $28.4 million, close to expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased approximately 33% year-over-year to $35.6 million”; “excluding a $7.2 million duty-related benefit, adjusted EBITDA was $28.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “adj. EBITDA ≈ $27–29M” and set a bogey of “≥$27M.”

surprises.description: Net sales came in above the $793.7 million consensus, although they were essentially at the preview’s $815 million bull-case figure. The beat was positive but not a major departure from the range the preview considered plausible.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose over 4% year-over-year to $814 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $793.7M” consensus; the bull scenario projected “$815M.”

surprises.description: The reported volume trends in multifamily and national accounts were stronger than the preview’s expectation of slightly lower overall daily sales and its concern about weak housing indicators: multifamily volumes rose 11% and national-account volumes rose 2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multifamily volumes grew 11% and national account volumes rose 2% year-over-year, reflecting share gains amid declining housing starts and weak repair and remodel activity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management guidance was “down slightly” year over year; the preview’s volume bogey was “Flat to -3% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Total gross margin was materially above the preview’s roughly 15.3%–15.6% expectation. Excluding the duty benefit, it was still 16.3%, so the outperformance was not limited to the one-off benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total gross margin expanded to 17.2% from 15.3% a year ago, or 16.3% excluding the duty benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at “~15.3–15.6%” and modeled “Total GP ≈ $124M (15.6%).”

surprises.description: Specialty gross margin exceeded the top of the company’s Q2 guidance on the reported figure; even excluding the duty item, 18.7% was slightly above the 18.5% top of the guided range. The underlying beat was therefore positive but modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty gross margin was 20% (18.7% excluding the duty item) versus 18.5% last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 specialty gross-margin guidance was “17.5% – 18.5%”; the preview’s bogey was “≥18.0% (mid-guide).”

surprises.description: Structural gross margin reached 10.9%, above both the top of Q2 guidance and the preview’s 10.0% bogey. Management also said the Q2 strength should not persist into Q3, guiding to 8.5%–9.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Structural gross margin jumped to 10.9% from 8.2% a year ago on higher lumber pricing and volumes, but management expects Q3 structural margin to normalize to 8.5%-9.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 structural guidance was “9.5% – 10.5%”; the preview’s Q2 bogey was “≥10.0%” and its bull scenario expected structural margin to “capture[] the lumber upcycle at 10.5%.”

surprises.description: The call identified nearly $25 million of quarterly sales and $2.7 million of adjusted EBITDA from Tesaro/Cesero, a named acquisition contribution not discussed in the preview, which instead focused on Disdero’s contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Tesaro acquisition, closed in Q4 2025, contributed nearly $25 million of net sales and $2.7 million of adjusted EBITDA in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed Disdero: “Q2 FY2026 is the third full quarter of contribution” and referred to “Disdero annualiz[ing].”

surprises.description: The new Trex distribution partnership was not part of the preview’s catalyst discussion. Its potential contribution is delayed: meaningful P&L impact is expected to build in 2027, with upfront working-capital and hiring needs during the ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BlueLinx signed a new Trex distribution partnership covering 11 markets, though meaningful P&L contribution is expected to build in 2027 as the ramp-up requires upfront working capital and hiring investments.”

in_line: Q3 specialty gross-margin guidance of 18%–19% broadly held the range the preview was watching: it overlaps the preview’s expected 17.5%–18.5% band.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $11.2 million versus the preview’s $9.9 million estimate, and the 42% margin came in well above the expected 37–38% range. The expected sequential margin step-down did not occur.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 48% to a record $11.2 million,” with adjusted EBITDA margin “expanding by 7 percentage points to a record 42%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $9.9M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin 37–38%”; “A sequential drop to 37–38% is management doing what they said.”

surprises.description: Revenue reached $26.7 million, above the preview’s $26.3 million estimate and the cited consensus range of $25.6–26.1 million. Growth was 23%, faster than the preview’s roughly 20% expectation for the clean year-over-year comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $26.7 million, up 23% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.50, materially above the preview’s estimate of about $0.37. The preview cautioned that the headline consensus EPS mixed accounting bases, so the clearest comparison is against its adjusted estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income rose 58% to $7.2 million, yielding record adjusted EPS of $0.50 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (dil.) … Q2'26E (ours) ~$0.37”; the preview cautioned that “a mechanical ‘beat/miss’ print from the wires is close to meaningless here.”

surprises.description: Operating cash generation exceeded the preview’s estimate: cash flow from operations was $10.6 million versus about $8.5 million expected, and free cash flow was $7.2 million. The preview did not provide a free-cash-flow estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash flow from operations increased 42% to a record $10.6 million and free cash flow rose 50% to $7.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating cash flow … Q2'26E (ours) ~$8.5M.”

surprises.description: IDI added 447 billable customers, above the preview’s expected run rate of roughly 380 adds per quarter and its base-case range of 380–420. The total of 10,869 also exceeded the preview’s estimate of about 10,800.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added a record 447 new IDI billable customers in the quarter (up from 400 in Q1), ending with 10,869 total IDI customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “IDI billable customers … Q2'26E (ours) ~10,800”; “~+380/qtr run rate”; base case “Adds in line at ~380–420.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 86%, above the preview’s expected 84–85% range. This was a further margin improvement beyond the already anticipated high gross margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin hit a record 86%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin … Q2'26E (ours) 84–85%.”

surprises.description: FOREWARN added fewer users than expected: 25,493 versus the preview’s estimate of about 27,700, leaving total users at 443,173 versus roughly 445,000 expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FOREWARN added 25,493 users to reach 443,173 total users.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FOREWARN users … Q2'26E (ours) ~445,000”; the preview cited Q1 additions of “~27.7k.”

surprises.description: Gross revenue retention slipped to 95%, down 2 points. The preview raised churn as a risk to watch but did not forecast a decline in retention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross revenue retention slipped 2 points to 95%.”

surprises.description: The company continued repurchasing shares at a pace similar to Q1 rather than visibly deprioritizing the buyback after the offering. It repurchased 74,500 shares, compared with 73,250 in Q1, leaving $15.5 million under the program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$15.5 million remains under the buyback program after repurchasing 74,500 shares at an average $41.87.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “whether the $15.6M buyback authorization is now deprioritized” and said the company bought “73,250 shares at $41.90 in Q1.”

in_line: The offering’s stated uses—working capital, general corporate purposes, and potential strategic acquisitions—matched the preview’s expectation of broadly framed proceeds rather than a disclosed acquisition pipeline.
Management reaffirmed full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance in the high 30s, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the margin framework would remain in the mid-to-high 30s.
The home-healthcare expansion was already flagged in the preview as a July 20 launch and a major new FOREWARN vertical; the call’s launch and stated target market were consistent with that setup.

surprises.description: Yelp reported adjusted EBITDA of $91 million, far above the preview’s roughly $73 million consensus and the company’s $70–75 million guidance range. The 24% margin was also well above the preview’s implied Q2 margin of about 19.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined 9% to $91 million (24% margin), the latter beating guidance by $16 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA ~$73M (guide midpoint)” and “Adj. EBITDA margin ~19.8% (implied at midpoints)”; company guidance was “$70M – $75M.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $376 million, about $9 million above the preview’s consensus and $8 million above the high end of Yelp’s outlook. The preview noted that Yelp often beats revenue estimates, but this quarter’s result still exceeded both reference points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue rose just 1% year-over-year to $376 million, though it came in $8 million above the high end of the company's outlook range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus net revenue was “$366.7M”; company guidance was “$363M – $368M.”

surprises.description: Paying advertising locations declined only 1% year over year to 510,000, much better than the preview’s 485,000 Q1 baseline and its focus on whether the decline would stabilize around that level or improve only modestly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paying advertising locations declined only 1% year-over-year to 510,000, an improvement over Q1, with services locations staying flat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1 as “485,000, -6% y/y” and said “stabilization at ~485K or better” was the key bull datapoint; it also said buy-side wanted “≤-5%.”

surprises.description: Ad clicks fell 5%, substantially less than the preview’s Q1 decline of 10% and its concern that clicks could worsen. Services clicks also edged up rather than turning negative, as the preview specifically warned to watch for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ad clicks fell 5% year-over-year driven by RR&O category weakness, partially offset by a slight services increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 clicks of “-10% y/y” and said to scrutinize whether “Services clicks are now also negative.”

surprises.description: CPC growth slowed sharply: it rose just 1%, versus 8% in Q1. That is weaker than the preview’s expected price support for ad revenue, even though click declines were milder than feared.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average CPC rose 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 CPC growth of “+8% y/y” and described the flat-revenue story as relying on “price” offsetting volume declines.

surprises.description: RR&O ad revenue declined 10%, a smaller decline than the preview’s 11% Q1 rate and less severe than the preview’s warning scenarios of a decline past 12–13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RR&O ad revenue declined 10% year-over-year to $102 million, reflecting a challenging local business environment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited RR&O revenue of “$99M, -11%” and flagged a decline “past -12%” as a risk; its bear scenario was “past -13%.”

surprises.description: Services ad revenue was flat year over year rather than continuing the 1% growth reported in Q1, a small deterioration in the segment the preview expected to hold up the total.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Services ad revenue was flat year-over-year at $241 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Services ad revenue of “$234M, +1%” and said Services would need to “accelerate to hold the total.”

surprises.description: Hatch’s annual run-rate revenue grew 59%, below the preview’s stated need for growth to remain above 70% and slower than the 92% growth cited for March. The reported adjustment period following an aggressive team expansion adds a near-term execution concern not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hatch annual run rate revenue grew 59% year-over-year to $35 million in June, though an aggressive team expansion caused an adjustment period in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Hatch at “a $34M annual run rate in March, +92% y/y” and said the buy-side “needs Hatch growth to stay >70%.”

surprises.description: Yelp disclosed that buybacks have been paused to pay down its revolving credit facility, with resumption not expected until 2027. The preview anticipated a possible slowdown in repurchases, but not a pause tied to debt repayment or such a long delay before restarting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $15 million of shares in Q2 at $24.92 and ~$25 million in Q3 (~$200 million total for the year), but has paused buybacks to pay down its revolving credit facility with resumption expected in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Watch for a slowdown in repurchase intensity,” and noted that a “step-down in buyback” would remove the main EPS support.

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $70–75 million implies a margin of roughly 19–21% on the guided revenue range, below the preview’s implied 22.8% average H2 margin needed to reach the FY midpoint. Yelp attributed the outlook to increased spending on AI, Hatch, and consumer marketing, rather than the opex discipline the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Third quarter guidance calls for revenue of $365-370 million and adjusted EBITDA of only $70-75 million, reflecting increased investment spending on AI, Hatch, and consumer marketing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY midpoint required “~$168M for H2 on ~$737M of revenue — a 22.8% margin,” and described “opex discipline” as real.

surprises.description: Yelp Host reached a 2.4 million-call annual run rate and added an OpenTable integration, 16 languages, and food-ordering functionality. The preview discussed other-revenue growth and Yelp’s AI products but did not anticipate these Host usage and product milestones.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Yelp Host reached an annual run rate of 2.4 million calls handled in July, more than tripling from January, and added OpenTable integration, 16 new languages, and food ordering functionality.”

in_line: Other revenue was $33 million, within the preview’s stated target range of at least $32–33 million for Q2.
Revenue growth remained roughly flat year over year, consistent with the preview’s consensus expectation of roughly flat growth.
Management’s description of a challenging local-business environment was consistent with the preview’s expectation that the Q1 macro-caution message might continue.

surprises.description: The preview put Q3 consolidated revenue at $228–243 million, with even its bull case starting at $245 million. Lattice guided to $245–265 million, and its standalone FPGA guide of $210–230 million was also above the preview’s $195–205 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 combined revenue guidance is $245-265 million (midpoint $255 million), including $33-37 million of AMI”; “The standalone FPGA business is guided to $210-230 million for Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consolidated Q3 guide: ~$228–243M”; “Lattice standalone: $195–205M”; bull scenario: “≥$245M.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue substantially exceeded the preview’s consensus range and the high end of company guidance: $201 million versus consensus of about $185 million and guidance topping out at $195 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $201 million … exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” revenue: “$185.1–185.5M”; company guide: “$175–195M.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS came in well above the preview’s $0.44 consensus, at $0.53.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $0.53.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” non-GAAP EPS: “$0.44.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was higher than the preview’s roughly 70% expectation, reaching 71.7%; operating margin also expanded to 38.3%, alongside strong operating leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 71.7%, up 170 basis points sequentially … with operating margin expanding 390 basis points to 38.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin consensus: “~70%.”

surprises.description: The company said the combined business would exceed a $1 billion annualized run rate a quarter ahead of plan, earlier than the preview’s year-end 2026 run-rate milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 guidance “put[s] Lattice at over $1 billion annualized run rate a quarter ahead of plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified the “$1B annual run rate by year-end 2026” as a milestone to reaffirm and said it “needs Q4 ≈ $250M+ to hold.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that assembly and packaging constraints and rising costs are pressuring margins until expected normalization in Q4. The preview focused on Q3 gross margin of 71–73% and AMI’s expected gross-margin accretion, but did not flag these supply and cost pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industry-wide assembly/packaging supply constraints and rising costs are pressuring margins until expected normalization in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q3 gross-margin marker was “71–73%” and noted management said AMI is “GM-accretive.”

surprises.description: The call clarified that AMI becomes meaningfully accretive to EPS starting in Q4, once a low-margin hardware pass-through business is exited, rather than contributing meaningfully to EPS immediately. That timing is less favorable than the prior immediate-accretion claim highlighted in the preview, though the preview itself modeled the stub quarter as potentially EPS-neutral to dilutive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AMI becoming meaningfully accretive to EPS starting in Q4 once a low-margin hardware pass-through business is fully exited.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had called the deal “immediately accretive to … non-GAAP EPS,” while also estimating the stub quarter could be “EPS-neutral-to-dilutive.”

surprises.description: Backlog visibility reached the end of 2027, with management describing 2027 as essentially fully booked. The preview expected bookings to extend well into 2027, so this was stronger than the stated durability marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog visibility extends through the end of 2027, with 2027 described as essentially fully booked.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that bookings extended “well into 2027” and called for the company to “reaffirm or extend” that outlook.

in_line: AMI’s Q3 revenue contribution was in line with the preview’s estimate: the preview estimated about $33–38 million net, and the call guided to $33–37 million.

surprises.description: Rocket guided Q3 adjusted revenue to $2.5–$2.7 billion, below the preview’s expected $2.7–$2.9 billion range and the buy-side midpoint of at least $2.75 billion. Management also said the Q3 mortgage market is expected to shrink sequentially, a contraction the industry has not seen since 2022.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 adjusted revenue to $2.5–$2.7 billion, expecting the Q3 mortgage market to shrink sequentially—something the industry has not seen since 2022.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … Q3 guide reiterated at $2.7–2.9B”; “the buy-side wants a midpoint ≥$2.75B.”

surprises.description: Mortgage rates rose further than the preview’s cited July readings: the 30-year fixed rate reached 6.8%, the highest in over a year, and was pressuring both purchase and refinance activity. That is a worse rate backdrop than the preview’s 6.55% Freddie Mac and 6.65% MBA readings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 30-year fixed rate rose to 6.8% in recent weeks, 50 basis points above the first-half average and the highest level in over a year, pressuring both purchase and refinance activity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Freddie Mac 30-yr hit 6.55% on July 16”; “the MBA survey rate hit 6.65%.”

surprises.description: Rocket added roughly $100 million of annualized Mr. Cooper savings beyond the original $400 million target, with the additional savings expected in H1 2027. The preview expected the $400 million goal by year-end, but did not anticipate a higher total target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its Mr. Cooper expense synergy target, identifying an additional ~$100 million in annualized savings (to be realized in H1 2027) beyond the original $400 million goal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$400M by end-2026”; “Mr. Cooper synergy confirmation ($100M incremental in Q2, $400M by YE26).”

surprises.description: Rocket reported record purchase and refinance market shares—6.2% and 14.3%, respectively—while the preview anticipated share gains but did not flag record levels. The reported gains were especially notable against the tougher rate environment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rocket hit record market share of 6.2% in purchase … and 14.3% in refinance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management repeats ‘share gains’ and ‘operating leverage’”; the preview’s base case described “repeat share gains.”

surprises.description: Existing servicing clients made up 57% of refinance closings, above the preview’s 54% Q1 benchmark, and did so at near-zero acquisition cost. The call also said Mr. Cooper recapture rates reached a record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Existing servicing clients accounted for 57% of refinance closed volume (up from 54% in Q1) at near-zero acquisition cost, with Mr. Cooper recapture rates hitting a record.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Recapture hit an all-time-high 54% of refi closings in Q1.”

surprises.description: Redfin integration produced double year-over-year mortgage leads in June and 45% year-over-year growth in direct-to-consumer purchase volume. The 47% attach rate improved on the preview’s roughly 45% Q1 figure, though it remained below the 50% target the preview identified as a potential upside milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Redfin integration drove mortgage leads to double year-over-year in June, a 47% mortgage attach rate (approaching the 50% target), and 45% year-over-year growth in direct-to-consumer purchase volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1: attach ~45% with ‘line of sight to 50%’”; “a 50% attach print would be a genuine positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.16, a penny below the $0.17 consensus estimate. It was still within the preview’s $0.15–$0.17 whisper range and the $0.16–$0.18 base scenario, so the shortfall was limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS $0.17”; the preview also gave a “whisper” of “$0.15–$0.17.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted revenue was $2.8 billion, near the $2.82 billion consensus and the midpoint of the $2.70–$2.90 billion company guide.
The original Mr. Cooper synergy schedule remained on track: $100 million was realized in Q2 and the original $400 million goal remained on track by year-end, as the preview expected.

The preview highlighted servicing as a potential hedge to origination softness; the call’s description of more than 70% of revenue as recurring or less rate-sensitive and $1 billion of servicing cash flow was consistent with that theme.

surprises.description: Eton reported Q2 revenue of $37.6 million, far above the preview’s roughly $27 million working consensus. The preview’s bull case was only $29–31 million, so the result substantially exceeded even that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $37.6 million, up 99% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working consensus I'd trade against: ~$27M revenue”; bull scenario: “Revenue $29–31M.”

surprises.description: Eton raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to more than $145 million, well above the prior floor of more than $120 million and the preview’s approximately $121 million consensus. This was a much larger raise than the preview’s bull-case example of guidance above $125 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to exceed $145 million, up from the prior guidance of more than $120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus FY26 of ~$121M”; the preview said a raise to “>$125M” would be the bull trigger.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $16.2 million, about twice the preview’s roughly $8.1 million “on track” estimate, with a 43% margin versus the preview’s approximately 29–30% base/on-track range. The result was much stronger than the preview’s bull-case EBITDA estimate of $9–10 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $16.2 million (43% of revenue) versus $3.6 million (16%) a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On ~$27M of revenue, ~$8.1M of adj. EBITDA is the ‘on track’ number”; the bull case estimated “$9–10M (~32%).”

surprises.description: Eton raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA margin target to more than 35%, rather than merely preserving the prior target above 30% that the preview viewed as a key credibility test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was raised to exceed 35% from prior guidance of over 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY26 guidance: … adj. EBITDA margin >30%”; the preview said the key test was whether “the >30% guide survives.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP diluted EPS came in at $0.43, almost three times the preview’s $0.148 consensus; GAAP diluted EPS was also $0.35 despite the preview anticipating that GAAP EPS would be materially lower and potentially generate an apparent miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income was $11.6 million ($0.35 per diluted share) versus a prior-year net loss of $2.6 million, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.43 compared to $0.03.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (non-GAAP basis) $0.148”; “Expect at least one headline calling this an ‘EPS miss’ regardless of the underlying result.”

surprises.description: Hemangiol was already a primary driver of Q2 revenue growth, whereas the preview’s base case assumed its contribution would be immaterial and the bull case expected only about $3–4 million. The preview had described Q2 as a limited-contribution period after the May 1 relaunch.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue growth was “driven primarily by the Hemangiol relaunch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base is DESMODA + legacy portfolio … doing the work with HEMANGEOL immaterial”; the bull case expected “roughly $3–4M in the quarter.”

surprises.description: About 95% of Hemangiol’s roughly 8,000 patients had transitioned to Eaton’s single-pharmacy model by the end of June, ahead of the three-to-four-month timeline. The preview highlighted the enrollment ramp as important but did not anticipate this speed or give a comparable patient-transition figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 95% of Hemangiol's roughly 8,000 patients were transitioned to Eaton's single-pharmacy Eaton Cares model by end of June, well ahead of the expected three-to-four-month timeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether Eton gives any HEMANGEOL-specific revenue or patient-start numbers”; management had said it “could be our largest product” in 2027.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin was 73%, above the preview’s base expectation of roughly 68–70% and even above its bull-case threshold of 72%+. The preview had identified Hemangiol mix and gross-to-net as a major margin risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 73% … with full-year adjusted gross margin expected to exceed 70%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “adj. GM ~68–70%”; the bull case expected “adj. GM back to 72%+.”

surprises.description: The preview described ASN-001 as optionality and noted the planned bridging study, but the call disclosed that this is the only remaining development requirement: a 24-patient, 29-day FDA-reviewed study costing about $4 million, after a Phase 3 trial had already shown efficacy versus placebo. That provides more specific and apparently limited remaining development work than the preview laid out.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The only remaining ASN-001 development requirement is a 24-patient, 29-day FDA-reviewed bioavailability bridging study costing approximately $4 million over the next 12 months, following an already-completed Phase 3 trial showing efficacy versus placebo.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “ASN-001 … bridging study, NDA 2H27, launch 2028” and said to “treat as optionality only.”

surprises.description: Management said ASN-001 could address a patient population two to three times larger than Hemangiol’s and expects it to become Eton’s largest product. The preview had noted the possible largest-product status but had not specified this larger patient-population comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Newly licensed ASN-001 … could address a patient population two-to-three times larger than Hemangiol and is expected to become Eaton's largest product.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said ASN-001 “could be our largest product” but did not give a patient-population comparison.

surprises.description: Eton ended the quarter with $26.8 million in cash after prepaying $3 million of debt and plans to accelerate repayment of the remaining credit facility over the next 6–12 months. That contrasts with the preview’s concern that financing needs and a possible equity raise were live risks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $26.8 million in cash after a $3 million debt prepayment, and plans to accelerate repayment of its remaining credit facility over the next 6 to 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Balance sheet / financing risk” and said “an equity raise is a live risk.”

surprises.description: Management raised the long-term outlook to more than a $200 million annualized run rate exiting 2027 and a 50% adjusted EBITDA margin by 2028. The run-rate target is above the preview’s $186.93 million FY27 revenue consensus, while the 50% margin target was not in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised long-term targets, now expecting to exceed the $200 million annualized run rate exiting 2027, a 50% adjusted EBITDA margin by 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY27 Revenue / EPS $186.93M / $2.18”; it did not state a 50% adjusted EBITDA margin target.

surprises.description: Eton set a goal of achieving or exceeding $500 million in annual revenue by 2030 with ASN-001 included. The preview had mentioned a $500 million-plus peak-sales ambition, but not this more specific annual-revenue target or its inclusion of ASN-001.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “to achieve or exceed $500 million in annual revenue by 2030 with ASN-001 included.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to a “100 products / $500M+ peak sales by 2030” ambition.

in_line: ASN-001’s planned NDA filing in the second half of 2027 and potential 2028 launch remained consistent with the preview’s stated timeline.
The full-year adjusted gross margin outlook remained above 70%, as in the prior guidance cited in the preview.

surprises.description: CECO was expected to report a combined backlog of about $1.3–1.5 billion, but it ended the quarter at a record $1.82 billion. Record orders of $799 million and a pipeline above $8.5 billion added substantially stronger demand visibility than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 orders of $799 million, up 191% year-over-year,” with book-to-bill of approximately 2.8x; “quarter-ending backlog reached a record $1.82 billion,” up 76% sequentially; “sales pipeline exceeds $8.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Combined backlog should print ~$1.3–1.5B. Below $1.25B is a problem.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $40.2 million, above the preview’s modeled $34–36 million, and the 14.1% margin showed a mid-teens margin quarter sooner and more strongly than the preview’s questioned H2 margin ramp implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 73% to $40.2 million with margins expanding ~150 basis points to 14.1%, marking CECO’s first quarter with mid-teens EBITDA margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$34–36M (my est.)”; the preview called the H2 margin step-up “the stretch” and said legacy CECO had to add “~500bps of EBITDA margin in the back half.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow was strongly positive rather than remaining negative as the preview’s base case anticipated, with quarterly conversion already exceeding the full-year conversion threshold. This was a substantial improvement from Q1’s negative FCF.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted free cash flow rebounded to ~$53 million (132% of adjusted EBITDA).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “FCF still negative but improving,” and warned that “a second negative FCF quarter with an unchanged FY conversion target strains credibility.”

surprises.description: CECO raised the low ends of both full-year ranges instead of merely reaffirming the existing guidance. The high ends stayed unchanged, so the increase was an improvement to the floor rather than a raise toward or above the high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CECO raised its full-year 2026 outlook to revenue of $1.3–1.375 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $200–225 million, both with higher low ends.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guidance was “Revenue $1.275–1.375B” and “Adj. EBITDA $195–225M”; the preview said reaffirmation was the base case and that a raise “toward/above high end” was a bull scenario.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in modestly above the preview’s soft expected range and the approximately $279 million implied consensus, though not at the preview’s $290 million bull-scenario level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $285 million (up 54% YoY), including one month of Thermon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$279M” implied consensus and modeled “~$268–272M”; it said to treat “a $265–280M print as effectively in-line.”

surprises.description: Thermon synergy capture was quantified as running ahead of the preview’s implied in-year pace: CECO had already captured about $13 million of annualized synergies after only 60 days, although management did not raise the $40 million target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Captured ~$13 million of annualized net adjusted EBITDA synergies from Thermon in just 60 days,” about one-third of the $40 million target; management expected $17–20 million captured by year one and about $5 million realized in 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the $40 million target over three years as “on-or-ahead” and its guide cross-check implied “~$10M of in-year synergy capture.”

surprises.description: SG&A improved sharply as a share of revenue, and management indicated the lower rate was not expected to reverse. The preview did not flag this level of cost improvement or sustainability as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A improved ~400 basis points to 22.4% of revenue, with management not expecting the rate to drift back up.”

in_line: Q2 included only one month of Thermon, as the preview expected.
The full-year guidance high ends remained at $1.375 billion of revenue and $225 million of adjusted EBITDA; the change was an increase to the low ends.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $13.8 million, above the preview's $11.4–12.0 million working range. The company attributed the increase to higher Suboxone manufacturing revenue and Zevra royalties, partly offset by lower Ondif revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 38% year-over-year to $13.8 million from $10 million, driven by higher Suboxone manufacturing revenue and Zevra royalties, partially offset by lower Ondif revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working range | Rev $11.4–12.0M”; consensus revenue was “$11.65M.”

surprises.description: Reported net loss and EPS were materially worse than the preview's expected range because of an $11.7 million debt-extinguishment loss. Excluding that one-time charge, the net loss was $11.2 million, but the call did not provide an adjusted EPS figure for comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recognized a one-time $11.7 million loss on debt extinguishment… widening Q2 net loss to $22.9 million ($0.18/share)…; excluding the one-time item, net loss was $11.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's working EPS range was “$(0.10)–$(0.12)” and its consensus estimate was “$(0.10).”

surprises.description: The adjusted EBITDA loss was only $5.2 million, below the preview's expected $8–10 million loss. The preview specifically warned that a materially smaller loss could signal slower-than-planned launch hiring; the call facts do not say whether hiring was delayed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $5.2 million from $9.3 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q2 adj. EBITDA loss of $8–10M is on plan; a loss materially smaller than that is arguably a negative signal that launch hiring has slipped.”

surprises.description: Management is pushing for a possible two-month Class 1 review, a faster path than the preview's expected six-month Class 2 base case. This remains an aspiration rather than a confirmed FDA classification; management still guides to six months as the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guides to a standard 6-month FDA review as the base case but is pushing for a potential 2-month Class 1 review given the succinct, focused resubmission package.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management expects a Class 2 resubmission (6-month review) and has said it will request expedited handling.”

surprises.description: The call added that Anaphylm showed no statistical difference between clinician- and self-administration in the PK study, a reassuring result not specifically covered in the preview. The preview had focused on the top-of-tongue arm as a potential labeling issue, but this new comparison does not establish FDA agreement on labeling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The PK study showed no statistical difference between clinician-administered and self-administered Anaphylm.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the full HF report and labeling as an open issue: “That delta is a live labeling-negotiation item.”

in_line: Management remained on track to resubmit the Anaphylm NDA before the end of Q3 2026, as the preview expected; the preview had also identified Q3 timing as the target.
