surprises.description: Q2 gas realization was only $1.12/Mcf, far below the preview’s estimated $1.90–$2.10/Mcf; gas sales were also just $9.6 million. The reported realization makes the weak Waha basis a more severe drag than the preview estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Waha basis weakness pushed Q2 gas realization to just $1.12/MCF, the weakest on record, with gas sales of only $9.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GRNT realized gas … ~$1.90–2.10 (est.).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.09 beat the $0.06 consensus estimate, although it was below the preview’s $0.11–$0.19 scenario outcomes. The adjusted result was much lower than GAAP EPS because of hedge and one-time impacts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was only $11.1 million ($0.09 per diluted share), reflecting large hedge and one-time impacts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.06” consensus; the base scenario estimated “~$0.11.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was $0.23, below the preview’s illustrative expectation of a potentially large $0.30–$0.50 print from a hedge mark reversal, even though it rose from $0.19 a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income was $30 million ($0.23 per diluted share, up from $0.19 a year ago).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GRNT could print a large positive GAAP EPS (plausibly $0.30–0.50).”

surprises.description: Management said Q2 marked the bottom for gas sales and expects Q3 sales above $30 million, with an even higher level in Q4 as takeaway improves and basis firms. That sharp second-half recovery outlook was not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q3 gas sales north of $30 million (from $9.6M in Q2) and even higher in Q4 as takeaway improves and basis firms.”

surprises.description: Management supplied a more specific 2027 cash-flow and operating plan than the preview’s general expectation of sustainable FCF: a 10% FCF yield, 1.25x dividend coverage, about 1.25x leverage, and high-single-digit production growth at $65 oil.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2027 free cash flow inflection targeting a 10% free cash flow yield, 1.25x dividend coverage, ~1.25x leverage, and high-single-digit production growth at $65 oil.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a strategic pivot “targeting sustainable FCF in 2027” and asked for a “specific bridge.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a sizable contingency to cut development spending by 40–50% if oil stays below about $65, while still expecting exit production near 40,000 BOE/day and directing over 75% of 2027 capital to operated partnerships. The preview did not lay out this downside spending flexibility or allocation detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management can flex the development budget down 40-50% if oil holds below ~$65, staying below the $250M maintenance capital level, while expecting exit production approaching 40,000 BOE/day with over 75% of 2027 capital going into operated partnerships.”

surprises.description: Granite Ridge reported 27 asset transactions for about $28 million, adding 21.9 net undeveloped locations, and said it is replacing inventory at roughly twice the development rate with five to six years of runway. The preview had not anticipated this inventory addition or replacement pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “During Q2 the company closed 27 transactions for ~$28 million (including ~$11M future carry), adding 21.9 net undeveloped locations, and is replacing inventory at roughly a 2-to-1 rate versus development, giving five to six years of runway.”

surprises.description: Grey Rock plans to distribute Granite Ridge shares to LPs over the next six to nine months, reducing its ownership below 50% and ending controlled-company status. The preview did not flag the change, which management says will increase float and liquidity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Grey Rock intends to distribute Granite Ridge shares to LPs over the next six to nine months, pushing its ownership below 50% and ending Granite Ridge's controlled-company status, increasing float and liquidity.”

in_line: Q2 oil mix was 51%, within the preview’s expected 50–52% range.
Management continued to frame 2027 as the free-cash-flow inflection year, consistent with the preview’s stated strategic goal.

surprises.description: QuickLogic reported Q2 revenue of $5.5 million, below both the $6.0 million consensus and the $6.0 million guidance midpoint; the preview’s buy-side bar was higher still, around $6.5–$6.6 million. The company attributed the shortfall to a delayed contract extension.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $5.5 million … but landed below the guidance midpoint due to a delayed contract extension.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $6.0M” consensus and “$6.0M ±10%” company guide; the preview says the buy-side was “almost certainly anchored to the high end of guidance (~$6.5–6.6M).”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue is guided flat at $5.5 million, well below the preview’s expected $6.5–$7.0 million base case and its $7.0 million key threshold. This indicates a weaker near-term revenue trajectory than investors were led to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue is guided flat at $5.5 million (±10%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … Q3 guided $6.5–7.0M”; the catalyst checklist says “Q3 revenue guide ≥ $7.0M.”

surprises.description: The commercial Intel 18A ASIC award that the preview treated as likely soon and a key Q3 catalyst has been pushed out to 2027. The preview explicitly identified a second delay as a bear catalyst, so this is a notable reversal of the anticipated timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A commercial Intel 18A ASIC design” was “pushed out to 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview calls the award “the cleanest bull catalyst,” says the base case had the award “expected shortly,” and lists an “Intel 18A multimillion-dollar commercial award booked in Q3.”

surprises.description: QuickLogic narrowed its FY2026 revenue-growth outlook to 70%–80%, below the 85% growth implied by the $25.5 million consensus forecast. The new range is also more restrained than the preview’s base case, which expected the prior broad range to be reiterated unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “QuickLogic narrowed its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to 70%-80%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists “FY2026 revenue: $25.5M” and “+85%” y/y, and its base case expected the “FY range [to be] reiterated unchanged.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin reached 46.8%, above the preview’s roughly 42% consensus and above its 45% bull-case threshold. This was a stronger quarter-level margin result than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin rose to 46.8% in Q2 2026 from 31% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists “Non-GAAP gross margin: ~42%” consensus and says the bull case required “GM ≥45%.”

surprises.description: Despite the Q2 margin beat, full-year gross margin is now modeled at approximately 51%, below the preview’s 57% model. That leaves a less favorable full-year margin outlook than the preview had assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 gross margin modeled at approximately 51%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says “FY non-GAAP GM was modeled at ~57% on the Q1 call.”

surprises.description: Cash is substantially higher than the preview’s roughly $5 million reference point, but QuickLogic raised $9.8 million through its ATM program, a large issuance relative to the preview’s prior $3.2 million Q1 raise. The stronger liquidity position therefore came with more dilution than the preview’s neutral cash scenario contemplated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net cash grew to $13.5 million (excluding a $5 million credit line drawdown) from $3.8 million at year-end 2025, aided by $9.8 million raised through the ATM program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cites “$6.05M cash” and says cash “at or above ~$5M without heavy issuance = neutral”; it also warns that “any large ATM usage in the quarter” would be a tell on H2 confidence.

surprises.description: Management newly tied a significant percentage of Q4 revenue to the U.S. government contract, whose total ceiling is $89 million. The preview discussed the DIB contract and defense conversion but did not flag this degree of Q4 dependence on one government contract.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's Q4 growth story hinges heavily on its U.S. government contract, which carries an $89 million total ceiling and is expected to contribute a significant percentage of total Q4 revenue.”

surprises.description: Management put a specific $8–$10 million figure on second-half eFPGA-related revenue, including government NRE work, and said several IP contracts are signed with others in late-stage negotiation. The preview focused on the H2 revenue hurdle and IP-mix dependency but did not anticipate this quantified revenue contribution or contract status.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects second-half eFPGA-related revenue (including government NRE work) of approximately $8-10 million, with several IP contracts already signed and others in late-stage negotiation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says FY consensus “requires ~ $14.4M in H2” and that H2 margin depends on “IP/royalty mix vs. services,” but gives no eFPGA revenue estimate.

surprises.description: QuickLogic disclosed two additional late-stage customer opportunities—one spanning automotive, industrial automation, and robotics, and an international LEO satellite ASIC—and said a second-ever eFPGA IP architectural license is possible late this year. The preview did not identify these opportunities, adding potential pipeline beyond its highlighted Intel and defense debates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two new customer contracts are in late-stage negotiation—one targeting automotive, industrial automation, and robotics, and an international LEO satellite ASIC—while a second-ever eFPGA IP architectural license is possible late this year.”

surprises.description: A newly funded small-package qualification for defense customers could open a multi-million-dollar opportunity starting in 2027. The preview expected defense evaluations and possible FY2027 revenue, but did not anticipate that this specific qualification had received funding or carried a multi-million-dollar opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A newly funded small-package qualification for defense customers could open a multi-million-dollar opportunity starting in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says “Eval kits are still scheduled for late 2026 — i.e., revenue is FY2027,” and calls for watching “dollar-value design wins vs. more pipeline language.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed non-GAAP profitability and positive cash flow in the second half of 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation of H2 profitability.
Full-year mature product revenue is expected to be flat with 2025, consistent with the preview’s expectation that mature product revenue would remain flat.

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 40.6%, well above the preview’s roughly 37.5% base case and even its approximately 39.5% bull-case level. The preview said a print above 38% would show cost inflation had been absorbed, and the reported margin expansion was attributed to efficiencies across all three segments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit grew 9% year-over-year to $2.7 million, with gross margin expanding to 40.6% from 37.5%, driven by cost efficiencies across all three business segments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” gross margin: “~37.5%”; “Bull” gross margin: “~39.5%”; “A print above 38% is the single cleanest evidence that cost inflation has been absorbed.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased about 65,000 shares in Q2, compared with 24,469 in Q1, indicating a sharp acceleration in the quarterly pace. The preview identified acceleration as a possible support but did not anticipate this reported Q2 volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately 65,000 shares in Q2 and nearly 89,500 shares year-to-date.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The company bought 24,469 shares for $293K in Q1”; “an accelerated pace is a real, if unglamorous, support.”

surprises.description: Whole Foods’ adoption of RaiseWell was already known, but the call disclosed that participating ranchers had enrolled more than 270,000 cattle. The preview was watching for a revenue figure or another retailer, not an enrollment count of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Whole Foods Market adopted the new RaiseWell Certified program for its beef supply, resulting in more than 270,000 head of cattle now enrolled by participating ranchers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for any dollar-quantification or a second named retailer”; Whole Foods had adopted the program in February.

surprises.description: After roughly three years without a transaction, management said it was renewing its focus on M&A and planned to file a shelf registration within the next year. The preview did not flag this strategic shift, though management said no deals were imminent.
surprises.fact_evidence: “After a roughly three-year pause since its last transaction, management is renewing its focus on M&A and plans to file a shelf registration within the next year, though no deals are imminent.”

surprises.description: The preview characterized the stock’s anomalous 52-week high as likely a thin-tape spike. Management’s call commentary added that the stock had spiked above $20 on two occasions in the first half and that the company could not explain the moves despite working with NASDAQ market surveillance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The stock traded above $20 per share on two occasions in the first half of 2026 (May and July), a spike the company could not explain despite working with NASDAQ market surveillance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “52-week range | $9.15 – $22.15 *(high looks anomalous vs. both MAs — likely a thin-tape spike; verify on your own terminal before using)*.”

in_line: Total revenue of $6.6 million and verification and certification revenue of $5.4 million were in line with the preview’s $6.4–$6.6 million base revenue range and approximately $5.4 million V&C threshold.

Net income of $413,000, or $0.08 per share, was within the preview’s $0.08–$0.10 base EPS range. The preview also anticipated a roughly $240,000 year-over-year digital-asset valuation swing, consistent with the call’s reported negative swing from those non-cash changes.
The flagship Beef business remained pressured by fewer cattle moving through the system and record-high beef prices, consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued cattle-cycle headwinds.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $1.603 billion, well above the preview’s derived $1.42–$1.47 billion range. The result cleared even the preview’s $1.50 billion bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached a record $1.603 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$1.42–1.47B”; the preview’s bull case was “$1.50B+.”

surprises.description: Marketing businesses exceeded expectations by about $250 million in the first half, much of it in Q2. That was a larger contribution than the preview’s anticipated Q2 tailwind, though management expects minimal marketing gains in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marketing businesses outperformed expectations by approximately $250 million in the first half, much of it in Q2,” while management “assumes minimal marketing gains in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called negative-priced Permian gas “a real Q2 tailwind,” but described the base case as “solid but not spectacular marketing.”

surprises.description: LPG export loadings averaged a record 14.8 million barrels per month—roughly 487,000 barrels per day—above the preview’s 435,100-barrel-per-day consensus and its expected record threshold of more than 440,000.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LPG export loadings averaging a record 14.8 million barrels per month.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “LPG export volumes: 435.1 MBbl/d” and said a “genuine record implies >440 MBbl/d.”

surprises.description: Permian inlet volumes reached 7.2 Bcf/d, above the preview’s derived 6.9–7.0 Bcf/d expectation. The company added 450 MMcf/d sequentially despite ongoing shut-ins, versus the preview’s cited run rate of about 250 MMcf/d above the Q1 average.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Permian volumes hit 7.2 Bcf/d, up 7% sequentially and 14% year-over-year, adding 450 MMcf/d quarter-over-quarter despite ongoing shut-ins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~6.9–7.0 Bcf/d” and said volumes were running “~250 MMcf/d above the Q1 average.”

surprises.description: Fractionation and NGL transportation volumes both exceeded the preview’s estimates: fractionation was 1.2 million barrels per day versus 1.166 million, and transportation was 1.1 million versus about 1.05 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record downstream volumes included NGL transportation of 1.1 million bpd [and] fractionation of 1.2 million bpd.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “NGL fractionation: 1,166.1 MBbl/d” and “NGL pipeline transport: ~1.05 MMBbl/d.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased about $80 million of stock, up from the $55 million Q1 buyback the preview cited. This was a step-up in repurchases, although smaller than an unspecified larger buyback that the preview identified as a possible confidence signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased roughly $80 million of stock at an average price of $259.93.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 buybacks were “only $55M” and that “a step-up in repurchases at ~$260 would be a genuine confidence signal.”

surprises.description: Pro forma leverage was about 3.4x, below the preview’s 3.6x figure, and available liquidity was $3.2 billion versus $3.1 billion cited ahead of the release.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma consolidated leverage was approximately 3.4x with $3.2 billion of available liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Leverage 3.6x pro forma” and “liquidity $3.1B.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s expectation that Targa could monetize negative-priced Permian gas, management said the company remained largely below fee floors and expected to stay below them in aggregate in Q3; Waha price improvements were primarily benefiting producers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has five Permian processing plants under construction and remains largely below fee floors, expecting to stay below them in aggregate in Q3, with Waha price improvements primarily benefiting producers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Targa with firm takeaway can monetize negative-priced Permian gas aggressively.”

in_line: Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA was expected toward the upper half of the $5.7–$5.9 billion range; management now expects the result toward the top end of that same range, without reporting a new range.
The $1.25 quarterly dividend was expected to hold and was unchanged.
Net growth capital of approximately $4.5 billion and maintenance capital of $250 million matched the preview’s expectations.
Speedway and the LPG export expansion remained on track for Q3 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated timeline.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.55 beat the preview’s $0.53–$0.54 consensus estimates, though it remained within the preview’s expected $0.53–$0.55 base-case range. The beat was positive but modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose 8% year-over-year to $0.55, landing at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “MarketBeat preview | $0.53”; “Investing.com earnings page | $0.54”; the preview’s base case was “Adj. EPS $0.53–$0.55.”

surprises.description: Net sales of $935 million came in slightly below the preview’s roughly $939 million consensus estimate, although sales were within management’s $932–$942 million guidance range and comparable sales were flat as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 net sales totaled $935 million with flat comparable sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “MarketBeat preview | … Revenue | ~$939.3M”; the preview also described consensus as “~$939M.”

surprises.description: BSG comparable sales weakened to a 2.1% decline, rather than showing a return to growth after the previous quarter’s 0.3% decline. That was a disappointing outcome on one of the preview’s central open questions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BSG comparable sales declined 2.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Does BSG return to growth?”; the preview noted that BSG comps were “-0.3%” in Q2 FY26.

surprises.description: BSG’s operating margin slipped 20 basis points to 12.3%, reversing direction from the prior quarter’s 90-basis-point expansion even though gross margin expanded. This undercut the preview’s description of BSG margin as carrying the segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Segment operating margin declining 20 basis points to 12.3% despite gross margin expanding 70 basis points to 40.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported “BSG segment operating margin 12.4%, +90 bps” in Q2 and said “BSG margin (12.4%, +90 bps in Q2) is carrying the segment.”

surprises.description: Care sales declined in both segments, including a 5% decline at BSG, rather than continuing the stabilization the preview described. Care fell 6% at Sally as well.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Care declined 6% at Sally and 5% at BSG amid consumer choicefulness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had reported that “the care category stabilized after three flat quarters.”

surprises.description: The call supplied a positive Sally Ignited update that the preview had not anticipated: the remodel program was on track to reach 80 locations by the end of September, and those locations were outperforming the fleet on sales growth. The company also plans to extend fragrance, nails, and skin categories into fiscal 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Sally Ignited remodel initiative is on track to reach 80 locations by end of September with sales growth outperforming the fleet, and the company plans to expand fragrance, nails, and skin categories into fiscal 2027.”

in_line: Comparable sales were flat, matching the preview’s Q3 guidance of approximately flat.

Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was narrowed to $2.04–$2.08 from $2.02–$2.10, leaving the midpoint unchanged at $2.06; comparable-sales guidance of approximately 0.5% matched the midpoint of the prior flat-to-+1% range.
Fuel for Growth remained on track for approximately $45 million in FY26 savings and roughly $120 million in cumulative three-year run-rate savings, as the preview expected.
Gross margin continued to expand, consistent with the preview’s expectation that margin would support the EPS outlook.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was approximately $8.4 million, well above the preview’s $7.56–$7.64 million consensus range. That is about 19% year-over-year growth, versus the preview’s implied expectation of roughly 7–8% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 19.2% year-over-year to approximately $8.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $7.56M – $7.64M” and “Implied Y/Y | +7% to +8%.”

surprises.description: Direct Patient Services grew about 40% in Q2, materially faster than the preview’s base-case expectation of 20–28% growth. It also became the company’s primary growth driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct Patient Services segment revenue jumped ~40% year-over-year to $4.9 million in Q2 … becoming the primary growth driver.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case called for “DPS +20–28%” and flagged deceleration below about 20% as a concern.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $1.3 million, below the preview’s $1.5–$1.8 million base-case range and the prior-year quarter’s $1.7 million. Revenue substantially beat expectations, but EBITDA did not keep pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to ~$1.3 million in Q2 from $1.7 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case forecast “Adj. EBITDA $1.5–1.8M”; its bear case was below $1.2 million.

surprises.description: Cash rose to $6.8 million, with $4.4 million generated from operations in the first half. This was stronger than the preview’s base-case cash range of $4.5–$5.5 million and exceeded its identified $6 million upside threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating activities generated $4.4 million of cash in the first six months, boosting the cash balance over 80% to $6.8 million from $3.7 million at year-end 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “cash $4.5–5.5M”; it said “Above ~$6M” would lengthen the liquidity clock materially.

surprises.description: The call identified a $909,000 credit-loss allowance on Rhode Island receivables as a major driver of the net loss, an adverse receivables issue not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported net loss was driven largely by a $909,000 credit-loss allowance on Rhode Island receivables.”

surprises.description: The company reported $285,000 of legal and professional costs tied to the credit agreement amendment. The preview discussed the forbearance but did not anticipate this specific expense in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Net loss was driven] largely by … $285,000 in legal/professional costs tied to the credit agreement amendment.”

surprises.description: Debt owed is expected to decline from about $15.5 million to $13.3 million, and the loan maturity was extended to June 30, 2027. The preview focused on debt of roughly $17 million and the asset-sale obligation, so the stated debt reduction and extended maturity are favorable balance-sheet developments versus that framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The amendment] extend[s] loan maturity to June 30, 2027, with debt owed expected to fall from ~$15.5 million to ~$13.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “~$17M of debt” and highlighted the forbearance’s required asset-sale process.

surprises.description: Although the preview emphasized that the forbearance requires pursuing an asset sale, management said it was pursuing all options and expected to refinance rather than necessarily sell. That offers a less sale-centered outlook, but the stated requirement remains and no concrete sale-process progress was provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The forbearance agreement reportedly requires the company to pursue a sale of all or part of ASHS's assets, though management stated it is pursuing all options and expects to refinance rather than necessarily sell.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the agreement “requires the company to pursue a sale of all or a portion of its assets” and made disclosure about the “mandated asset-sale process” a key issue to watch.

surprises.description: The Executive Chairman’s newly formed company also purchased additional AMS shares from a private investor. The preview noted the related-party $2 million financing but did not flag this separate share purchase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Executive Chairman's newly formed company … purchased additional company shares from a private investor.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the $2.0 million related-party note and its warrant, but did not mention a purchase of existing shares from a private investor.

surprises.description: The company disclosed a recent CFO transition to Interim CFO Alexis Wallace, which the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[A] recent CFO transition to Interim CFO Alexis Wallace.”

in_line: The $2 million subordinated financing from the Executive Chairman’s newly formed company was already disclosed in the preview as a July 22 related-party note.
The announced Rhode Island development plans and Guadalajara growth initiative broadly align with the preview’s cited Rhode Island site pipeline and Guadalajara project.

surprises.description: Adjusted net income was $0.48 per share, below the preview’s $0.51–$0.52 consensus and its $0.53 model estimate. The shortfall was also larger against the preview’s estimated $0.54–$0.56 whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income reached $60 million or $0.48 per share, up from $0.40 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ANI/share: $0.51–$0.52” consensus; “My Q1 FY27 est.” $0.53; functional whisper “$0.54–$0.56.”

surprises.description: Fee-related earnings came in at $106 million, above the preview’s $102 million model estimate and at the top of its roughly $100–$105 million expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fee-related earnings rose 30% year-over-year to $106 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Fee-related earnings (FRE) … My Q1 FY27 est. $102M”; preview also said consensus math implied “roughly $100–105M.”

surprises.description: Private Wealth subscriptions reached a record $2.8 billion, above the preview’s buy-side threshold of at least $2.4 billion and its $2.2–$2.5 billion base case. SPRING contributed nearly $1.7 billion, and platform assets surpassed $21 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Private Wealth generated a record $2.8 billion of subscriptions, growing total platform assets past $21 billion … with SPRING alone contributing nearly $1.7 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said buy-side needs “≥$2.4B gross subs”; its base case was “PW subs $2.2–2.5B.”

surprises.description: Company-wide inflows were especially strong: nearly $40 billion over the trailing 12 months, the best 12-month period ever, with quarterly inflows of $10 billion. The preview highlighted flow risks and thresholds but did not anticipate this record company-wide inflow figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross inflows totaled $10 billion for the quarter and nearly $40 billion over the trailing 12 months, the best 12-month period ever, split evenly between managed accounts and commingled funds.”

surprises.description: SPRING returned 23% net in the first half of the calendar year, a stronger update than the preview’s cited +11% YTD through April and potentially reassuring on the portfolio-mark concern it flagged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SPRING delivered 23% net returns in the first half of the calendar year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited SPRING as “+11% YTD through April” and flagged AI/software marks as a potential narrative resetter.

surprises.description: Management reported a $116 million GAAP net loss attributable to StepStone, or $1.41 per share, due to the fair-value change in the Private Wealth profits interest buy-in. The preview discussed GAAP revenue volatility but did not flag a loss of this size tied to this item.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A GAAP net loss attributable to the company of $116 million or $1.41 per share, driven by the change in fair value of the Private Wealth profits interest buy-in.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that GAAP revenue “includes unrealized carried interest” and that a GAAP ‘beat’ or ‘miss’ headline was “close to meaningless,” but gave no expectation for a profits-interest-related GAAP loss.

surprises.description: The dividend rose 18% to $0.33 per share from the $0.28 quarterly base the preview described, a larger payout than that stated base expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its quarterly dividend by 18% from $0.28 to $0.33 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “base is $0.28/qtr” and described the remainder of the trailing dividend as supplemental and carry-dependent.

surprises.description: Repurchases had reached $30 million of the $100 million authorization, with more than 710,000 shares bought at an average $41.87. That is a more substantial pace than the preview’s concern that only $9 million had been executed in March and that a passive buyback could signal a lack of conviction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased $30 million of its $100 million authorization, buying over 710,000 shares at an average price of $41.87.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “only $9M executed in March” and warned that “a passive buyback will be read as a lack of conviction.”

surprises.description: Management plans to buy in the Private Wealth profits interest as soon as contractually able, with up to 75% funded in equity and the balance in cash. The equity mix includes shares tradable immediately and shares locked up over three years; this transaction and funding structure were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to buy in the Private Wealth profits interest as soon as contractually able, funding up to 75% in equity (30% tradable immediately, remainder locked up over 3 years) with the balance in cash while maintaining its A+ investment-grade rating.”

surprises.description: Management flagged a $1.5 billion managed-account expiration next quarter, creating a specific near-term flow risk not identified in the preview’s flow discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged a $1.5 billion managed account expiration next quarter.”

surprises.description: The commingled fee rate is expected to remain relatively flat because PE secondaries funds carry a lower fee structure, with growth resuming only once those funds are fully raised. This is a less favorable fee-growth timing detail than the preview’s emphasis on UFEC activation turning on fees and the possibility of pulled-forward flagship activation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A lower fee structure on PE secondaries funds will keep the commingled fee rate relatively flat before resuming growth once fully raised.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said activation of flagged undeployed capital “turns on management fees,” and its bull case included “UFEC activations pulled forward.”

surprises.description: More than 70% of net accrued carry was tied to programs older than five years and described as ready to harvest, a favorable maturity profile beyond the preview’s estimate of the carry balance and its general focus on whether carry would convert into realizations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net accrued carry reached $935 million, up 19% year-over-year, with over 70% tied to programs older than five years and ready to harvest.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated net accrued carry at “~$936M” and said to watch whether accrued carry was “still building or starting to convert.”

surprises.description: Management warned that SPRING’s public positions could add performance volatility as lockups expire and positions are exited; the SpaceX holding had already fallen from its peak to a mid-teens share of NAV. The preview flagged software and venture marks as a possible issue but did not anticipate this specific position-level volatility and exit commentary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The SpaceX position in SPRING has declined from its peak to a mid-teens percentage of NAV, and management expects public positions to introduce performance volatility as lockups expire and positions are exited.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “AI/software mark commentary” and noted SPRING’s venture/growth exposure, but gave no specific expectation about SpaceX or lockup-related volatility.

in_line: FRE margin was 39%, within the preview’s 38–39% base-case range and close to its 38.5% model estimate.
Net accrued carry was $935 million, essentially in line with the preview’s estimate of approximately $936 million.

surprises.description: Chegg reported Q2 revenue of $51.8 million, above the preview’s $49.8 million consensus and the company’s $49–50 million guide, as well as the preview’s $50 million-plus functional whisper. The beat was real but relatively modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 total revenue was $51.8 million, exceeding company expectations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Total net revenue: $49.8M consensus; company guide $49–50M. The functional whisper is revenue $50M+.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA came in well above the expected $5–6 million guide and the preview’s $6 million-plus whisper, at $9.1 million and a 17% margin. This was a substantial beat against the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA for Q2 was $9.1 million (17% margin).
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA: company guide $5–6M (~11% margin); the functional whisper is adjusted EBITDA ≥$6M.

surprises.description: Chegg is pivoting toward an employability platform for internships and jobs, which the preview did not identify as the company’s strategic direction. More than 10,000 students have used the beta, but rollout is just beginning and continues through 2027, so the opportunity is not yet proven.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is pivoting strategically toward an 'employability' platform to help students find internships and jobs, targeting what management believes is a larger TAM than its academic business. More than 10,000 students have used the beta; rollout begins in Q3 and continues through 2027.

surprises.description: Chegg is ending separate revenue guidance for Academic Services and Skilling as the businesses integrate. That removes visibility into the segment trends the preview treated as central, including Skilling’s growth and the pace of Academic Services’ decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is discontinuing separate revenue guidance for Academic Services and Skilling, instead guiding on total revenue and adjusted EBITDA as the businesses integrate.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave a Chegg Skilling revenue guide of $17.5–18.0M and an implied Academic Services range of about $31.5–32.5M; it identified Skilling growth and the Academic Services decay slope as key metrics to watch.

surprises.description: Cash generation and liquidity were stronger than the preview’s runway framing suggested: Q2 free cash flow was $6.4 million despite $14.4 million of severance payments, and quarter-end cash and investments were $72.3 million. After the expected $33.9 million debt repayment, that implies about $38.4 million of cash, above the preview’s rough $30–35 million post-repayment estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Free cash flow was $6.4 million in Q2 and $9.5 million in the first half, despite $14.4 million in severance payments from prior restructuring. The company ended the quarter with $72.3 million in cash and investments.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated roughly $30–35M of post-repayment cash against the business’s quarterly EBITDA needs.

surprises.description: Chegg repurchased $1.7 million of stock in Q2, a capital-allocation action the preview did not anticipate while emphasizing the upcoming convertible repayment and cash runway. The amount was small, and the call also noted that $120.7 million remained on the buyback authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: Chegg repurchased $1.7 million of stock in Q2 and has $120.7 million remaining on its buyback authorization.

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $43–44 million was within the preview’s expected range of roughly $43–46 million.
The company expects to fully repay its convertible debt in Q3, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the September notes would be repaid in full from cash on hand.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1–2 million is sharply lower than Q2, but remains positive, matching the preview’s stated Q3 floor of positive EBITDA.

surprises.description: Q2 continuing-operations sales were $66.7 million, above the preview model’s $62–65 million range. The preview warned that published consensus was unreliable, so this is a modest beat against its own model rather than a clean consensus comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales from continuing operations were roughly flat year-over-year at $66.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$62–65M” in the preview’s model.

surprises.description: The company raised full-year potash production guidance to 290–300,000 tons from the previously stated 270–285,000 tons, exceeding the preview’s expectation that production was tracking toward the upper end of the old range. Management said the increase reflected sustainable recovery and throughput improvements, not tons pulled forward from 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year production guidance for…potash (to 290-300,000 tons)…driven by sustainable mill recovery and throughput improvements rather than pulling tons forward from 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year potash production guide 270–285k tons, tracking ‘upper end’ as of May.”

surprises.description: Management also raised full-year Trio production guidance to 295–305,000 tons. The preview did not provide a full-year Trio production expectation or anticipate this increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year production guidance for…Trio (to 295-305,000 tons).”

surprises.description: Trio’s cost of goods sold per ton reached its lowest level since Q4 2019, providing a stronger indication of durable cost improvement than the preview’s base case of roughly $230 per ton. The preview had identified a rebound toward $240 or more as a risk and sub-$230 as the more favorable outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trio delivered its lowest cost of goods sold per ton since Q4 2019.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Trio COGS ~$230” in its base case and said a move “back toward $240+” could signal Q1’s performance was not structural.

surprises.description: Q3 Trio pricing guidance of $400–410 per ton was above the $390–400 level the preview used as its comparison point for Q3/H2 pricing. Management also said Trio pricing was expected to trend up on low-chloride and sulfate value.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance…Trio sales of 30-40,000 tons at $400-410 per ton, with Trio pricing expected to trend up on low-chloride and sulfate value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist compared Q3 pricing with “$390–400 Trio” and said buyers wanted “flat-to-up.”

surprises.description: The $5 million Pecos Water Rights accrual was an unanticipated charge that reduced reported continuing-operations net income and diluted EPS. The preview’s EPS estimates focused on adjusted EPS and did not flag this accrual.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income from continuing operations improved to $2.4 million ($0.18 per diluted share), including a $5 million accrual related to the Pecos Water Rights matter.”

surprises.description: Although the $50 million authorization was already known, the preview looked for Q2 buyback execution as a read on capital allocation. Management instead said buybacks were expected to begin in Q3, meaning the anticipated Q2 execution had not begun.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Buybacks expected to begin in Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked “How many shares were retired in Q2” and said “> $15M executed” would be a strong signal; it also identified “near-zero” execution as a concern.

surprises.description: Full-year capital expenditure guidance moved to approximately $40 million, at the low end of the preview’s $40–50 million expectation. The reduction reflected deferral of the AMAX project and lower Wendover Primary Pond 8 costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance was reduced to approximately $40 million, reflecting deferral of the AMAX project and reduced costs for Wendover's primary pond 8.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex guide $40–50M including Wendover Primary Pond 8.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was $185 million, above the preview’s approximate $170 million cash expectation based on the South Ranch proceeds. The company also reported no revolver borrowings and $149.8 million of revolver availability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ending the quarter with $185 million cash, no revolver borrowings, and $149.8 million of revolver availability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash was $99.3M at 3/31 plus $70M South Ranch proceeds (closed April 1) ≈ $170M.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $17.5 million, within the preview model’s $16–18 million range.

Potash Q2 volume of 59,000 tons was within the preview’s 50–60,000-ton guidance range, and its $391 per-ton realized price was essentially in line with the expected $380–390 range. The sales decline was consistent with the preview’s expectation of lower potash volumes.
Q3 potash pricing guidance of $380–390 per ton met the preview’s key threshold of at least $380 per ton.
The South Ranch sale generated $68.9 million net, close to the preview’s approximately $70 million proceeds expectation.

surprises.description: Veeco reported Q2 revenue of $193 million, above the $180.1 million consensus and the $190 million top of its guidance range. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.33 beat the $0.26 consensus and $0.32 guidance ceiling, while non-GAAP operating income of $23 million was also well above the preview’s $1–10 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $193 million with non-GAAP operating income of $23 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.33, exceeding guidance and Street expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” was $180.1M revenue and $0.26 non-GAAP EPS; Q2 guidance was $170M–$190M revenue, $0.20–$0.32 EPS, and $1M–$10M operating income.

surprises.description: Veeco raised its FY2026 revenue outlook to $780–810 million from $740–800 million. That is better than the preview’s expected range, including a higher low end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Veeco raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $780-810 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reiterated 5/5/26): Revenue $740M–$800M.”

surprises.description: Despite raising revenue guidance, Veeco cut FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $1.36–1.61 from $1.50–1.85. Management attributed the reduction to growth investments, which add about $10 million of operating expenses and reduce full-year gross margin by roughly 75 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered non-GAAP EPS guidance to $1.36-1.61 due to growth investments”; the investments “will add approximately $10 million of incremental operating expenses and reduce full-year 2026 gross margin by roughly 75 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reiterated 5/5/26): ... Non-GAAP EPS $1.50–$1.85”; the preview said the key issue was whether the range was “reaffirmed / narrowed to lower half / cut.”

surprises.description: Veeco’s Q3 revenue outlook has a $210 million midpoint, above the preview’s $200 million threshold to keep the FY outlook intact and at the level it said would validate the upper half of expectations. The preview’s base case was a $195–205 million midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects revenue of $200-220 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Needs ≥$200M midpoint to keep FY intact; ≥$210M to validate the upper half”; base case: “$195–205M mid.”

surprises.description: Q3 EPS guidance of $0.35–0.49 is below the preview’s estimated $0.55–0.72 quarterly EPS run rate needed in H2 to meet the original FY2026 EPS range. The annual EPS outlook was cut as well, but the Q3 range itself falls short of that earlier required run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance ... diluted EPS of $0.35-0.49.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated an “Implied H2 run-rate/qtr” of “~$0.55 – $0.72” to meet the FY2026 guide.

surprises.description: Veeco guided Q3 gross margin to 41–42%, above the preview’s expectation that management would need to move gross margin toward 40% or higher in H2. This contrasts with the separately disclosed full-year margin reduction from growth investments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects ... gross margin of 41-42%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management needs to walk the Street to 40%+ in H2”; the preview also said the H2 EPS ramp required gross margin to move “toward 40%+.”

surprises.description: Veeco disclosed $200 million of Q2 orders for advanced-packaging wet-processing and lithography systems, primarily for 2027 delivery. The preview watched for order acceleration and a possible same-day order announcement, but did not anticipate this specific order amount or advanced-packaging demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured $200 million in advanced packaging orders for wet processing and lithography systems during Q2, primarily for delivery in 2027.”

surprises.description: Veeco plans to more than double advanced-packaging and silicon-photonics capacity during 2027, using internal production and Southeast Asian outsourcing partners. The preview discussed the opportunity and order book but did not flag a capacity expansion of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to more than double advanced packaging and silicon photonics capacity during 2027 through internal production and Southeast Asian outsourcing partners.”

surprises.description: Veeco said compound-semiconductor revenue is expected to approximately double in 2026 versus 2025, an end-market outlook not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Compound semiconductor revenue is expected to approximately double in 2026 versus 2025.”

in_line: Data storage revenue is expected to double year over year, matching the preview’s expectation that data storage would “double in 2026 vs. 2025.”
Semiconductor revenue was 68% of Q2 revenue, close to the preview’s approximate semiconductor mix of 69%.

The Axcelis merger remains targeted for a second-half 2026 close with China antitrust the remaining approval, consistent with the preview’s expectation that only China SAMR clearance remained and that management would reiterate a second-half close target.

The Tier 1 logic customer’s evaluation completion and follow-on order for a second nanosecond annealing system align with the preview’s discussion of a follow-on NSA order and its expectation of eval-to-order conversions.

surprises.description: Spire reported an adjusted continuing-operations loss of $0.26 per share, slightly worse than the preview’s $0.24 loss consensus. The gap was $0.02 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted Q3 FY2026 loss from continuing operations improved to $0.26 per share ($15 million).”

surprises.description: The divestitures produced a substantial after-tax sale gain and reported discontinued-operations earnings, an accounting boost the preview did not quantify even though it discussed the asset sales. This was separate from the adjusted continuing-operations loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Spire recorded $253.8 million in earnings from discontinued operations, including an after-tax gain on sale of $254.6 million from divesting Spire Marketing and Spire Storage.”

surprises.description: Spire disclosed FFO-to-debt of 13% during the transition year, below the 14%–15% target, and said it expects to reach that target by the end of 2028. The preview flagged the target but did not specify a current 13% level or that timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FFO-to-debt currently stands at 13% during the transition year, with a 14%-15% target expected to be reached by end of 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch bridge balance, FFO/debt against the lowered 14–15% target.”

surprises.description: O&M expense rose by about $4 million, primarily because of higher bad debt, a cost pressure the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “O&M expense rose about $4 million primarily due to higher bad debt.”

surprises.description: Corporate/other losses widened to $12 million from $3 million, with higher corporate and interest costs contributing. The preview anticipated higher interest expense from Tennessee, but did not flag the wider corporate/other loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Corporate/other losses widened to $12 million from $3 million on higher corporate and interest costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Interest expense stepped up hard — Q2 net interest was $62.6M, +38.2% y/y, before Tennessee debt was fully carried.”

surprises.description: Ahead of the Alabama RSE hearings, intervenors recommended 8%–9% ROEs, below both the company’s requested 10.5% and 10.75% adjusting-point ROEs and the current 9.9% allowed ROE. This introduced a specific downside to the rate-setting debate that the preview did not describe.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Alabama RSE renewal hearings on August 6-7 will decide requested adjusting-point ROEs of 10.5% for Spire Alabama and 10.75% for Spire Gulf, with intervenors recommending 8%-9% versus the current 9.9% allowed.”

surprises.description: Spire Tennessee filed its first annual review mechanism, seeking a $14 million revenue increase and new rates effective October 1, 2026. The preview focused on Tennessee’s first-full-quarter economics and financing costs but did not identify this rate filing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Spire Tennessee filed its first annual review mechanism seeking a $14 million revenue increase based on a 9.8% ROE and $1.5 billion rate base, with new rates expected effective October 1, 2026.”

in_line: Spire reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.90–$4.10, as the preview’s base case expected.
Spire reaffirmed FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $5.40–$5.60 and the 5%–7% long-term EPS growth target, matching the preview’s central guidance debate.
The $11.2 billion 10-year capital plan and roughly $800 million of FY2026 capex were consistent with the preview’s stated plan.

surprises.description: PSEG reported Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.86, well above the preview’s roughly $0.79–$0.80 consensus range (and the $0.83 alternate estimate).
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 non-GAAP operating earnings of $0.86 per share,” compared with $0.77 in Q2 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus looks for non-GAAP EPS of roughly $0.79–$0.80”; alternate estimates were $0.794 and $0.83.

surprises.description: PSE&G plans to file a base-rate update by year-end 2026, advancing the filing from the previously required 2029 deadline. The preview mentioned favorable distribution-rate trends but did not flag this much earlier filing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PSE&G plans to file to update base rates by year-end 2026, pulling forward from the previously required 2029 deadline,” citing regulatory lag and distribution rate-base additions.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “favorable electric/gas base distribution rates” but gave no expectation of an accelerated rate case.

surprises.description: PSEG disclosed that a PJM transmission cost-allocation change will provide customer benefits of about $33 million through 2026 and an expected annual benefit of about $65 million thereafter; the preview did not identify this benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: The change effective June 1, 2026 “will deliver roughly $33 million in customer benefit through year-end 2026” and an “expected prospective annual benefit of approximately $65 million.”

surprises.description: PSEG identified a prospective earnings headwind from the potential loss of the RTO transmission incentive, beginning in 2027, which the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Potential elimination of the 50 basis point RTO transmission incentive represents an annual headwind of about $40 million net income (roughly $0.08 per share) effective January 2027,” with no 2026 impact.

surprises.description: PSEG said it can fund its five-year capital program without new equity issuance or asset sales, an important funding assurance not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The “$24 billion to $28 billion five-year capital investment program” can be funded “without issuing new equity or selling assets.”

surprises.description: PSEG Nuclear cleared 3,600 MW in the latest PJM capacity auction at the $325/MW-day collar ceiling, below the prior $333 and far below the stated uncapped price of $555. The preview did not discuss the auction outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: PSEG Nuclear cleared “approximately 3,600 megawatts” at “$325 per megawatt day (the collar ceiling),” versus the prior $333 and an uncapped price that “would have been $555.”

surprises.description: PSEG said higher realized prices and generation more than offset the absence of expired zero-emission certificates, a favorable nuclear earnings offset not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The absence of expired zero emission certificates was more than offset by higher realized prices and generation”; nuclear generation was 7.8 TWh at a 92% capacity factor.

surprises.description: PSE&G disclosed a planned residential gas-bill reduction and a $166 million customer refund. The preview had highlighted affordability pressure, but did not anticipate these specific customer-relief actions; no earnings effect was stated.
surprises.fact_evidence: PSE&G “filed to lower residential gas bills by more than 5% beginning October 1” and is refunding “roughly $166 million of zero emission certificates over 12 months to customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Affordability pressure on New Jersey bills remains a political overhang.”

in_line: PSEG reaffirmed FY2026 non-GAAP operating earnings guidance of $4.28–$4.40 per share, matching the range the preview said had already been reaffirmed.

surprises.description: Ziff Davis’s adjusted diluted EPS was $1.03, well above the preview’s $0.807 consensus. The company attributed the growth primarily to buybacks, so the per-share result beat expectations even though the underlying revenue and EBITDA were roughly on plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 13.2% year-over-year to $1.03, driven primarily by the significant share count reduction from buyback activity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $0.807”

surprises.description: Technology & Shopping improved much more than the preview’s base case: revenue declined 5%, versus the preview’s expected decline of roughly 9–11%, and adjusted EBITDA grew more than 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tech & Shopping revenue declined 5% year-over-year, a marked improvement from the 13% drop in Q1 and 18% drop in Q4, while its adjusted EBITDA rose more than 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “T&S ~−9 to −11%”; the preview also said “Better than −8% is a genuine positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Buybacks were substantial: Ziff Davis spent more than $200 million in the first seven months of 2026 and reduced shares outstanding by nearly 11%, including $121.5 million of repurchases in Q2. That is more aggressive than the preview’s base case of buybacks continuing at the existing pace, though it had identified a large capital return as a possible bull-case outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company deployed over $200 million to buy back 4.5 million shares in the first seven months of 2026, reducing shares outstanding by nearly 11%, and repurchased $121.5 million of stock during Q2 alone.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “buyback continues at existing pace, no new authorization”; the bull case called for a “large capital return announced.”

surprises.description: Health and Wellness weakened despite the preview noting that MedPage bookings were improving: revenue fell nearly 5% and adjusted EBITDA dropped nearly 10%. Management also cited pharma clients cutting HCP advertising and shifting to lower-cost AI platforms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Health and Wellness revenues fell nearly 5% and adjusted EBITDA dropped nearly 10% as large pharma clients reduced HCP advertising spend at MedPage and shifted to lower-cost AI-based platforms.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q1 baseline showed Health & Wellness revenue “+0.2%” and stated “MedPage bookings improving.”

surprises.description: The outlook did not reaffirm the H2 revenue growth thesis the preview highlighted: management instead expects revenue to keep declining in Q3 and Q4, although the decline should ease in Q4. Q3 margins are expected to improve modestly, while Q4 margins are expected to be slightly lower year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 revenue to decline low-to-mid single digits year-over-year with modest margin improvement, and expects Q4 to show a lower rate of revenue decline with adjusted EBITDA margin slightly down year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “H2 revenue growth reaffirmation” as a key metric and cited the prior outlook for “YoY growth in H2” in Technology & Shopping.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a notable internal AI productivity gain that the preview had not anticipated: the share of code authored by AI roughly doubled in one quarter, enabling more code output with fewer engineers, with an ambitious target for year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The share of code authored by AI roughly doubled in one quarter, enabling 24% more code shipped in Q2 versus Q1 on lower engineering headcount, with a target of nearly all code being AI-authored by end of 2026.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $286.7 million, close to the preview’s $286.10 million consensus and its expected year-over-year decline of about 2.7%.
Adjusted EBITDA was $76.8 million with a 26.8% margin, broadly in line with the preview’s estimates of about $77 million and a 27.0% margin.

surprises.description: CPSS’s Q2 originations were far above the preview’s ~$600–640 million estimate: the company reported $758 million, up 75% year over year. The preview said anything below $560 million would suggest March’s run rate had not held, but reported volume substantially exceeded even the estimate’s upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 loan originations surged to $758 million, up 75% from $433 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New contract purchases … ~ $600–640M”; “Anything under $560M says March was a pull-forward.”

surprises.description: Credit losses were materially better than the preview’s expected range: net charge-offs were 7.28%, below the preview’s 8.5–8.9% base case and below its ~8.5% thesis-intact threshold. This was also a year-over-year improvement rather than the modest deterioration the base case allowed for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net charge-offs declined to 7.28% from 7.45%” year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … NCO … 8.5–8.9%”; “NCOs at or below ~8.5% with the bad vintages shrinking = thesis intact.”

surprises.description: Revenue exceeded the preview’s estimate by $4.4 million, or about 4%, and grew 11% year over year versus the preview’s modeled 6.6% growth. The revenue beat was positive but smaller than the originations outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue increased 11% to $121.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … My Q2'26 Base Est. ~ $117M (+6.6% YoY).”

surprises.description: The preview worried that the expanded sales force could weigh on expenses before volume arrived, but reported expense trends showed leverage instead: core operating expenses grew more slowly than revenue and the expense-to-managed-portfolio ratio improved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core operating expenses grew only 3% over six months while revenue grew 8%, improving the expense-to-managed-portfolio ratio to 4.6% from 4.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If Q2 opex runs above ~$110M without a commensurate origination beat, the market will read the growth as bought rather than earned.”

surprises.description: Recoveries improved further rather than reversing: the reported 33.3% rate was above the preview’s Q1 reference of 31.1%. The stronger recovery rate also accompanied the better-than-expected net charge-off result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recovery rates rose to 33.3% from 30.4% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Recoveries improved to 31.1% from 27.7% in Q1. If that reverses, gross charge-offs flow straight through.”

surprises.description: The growth was not accompanied by a higher approval rate: applications rose sharply while approvals stayed near 51%. That addresses the preview’s concern that rapid dealer and sales-force expansion might be buying growth through looser credit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Applications received climbed 42% to 1.1 million, while the approval rate held steady at roughly 51%, indicating growth was achieved without loosening credit standards.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bear” case required that “the growth is real but is being bought with looser credit”; the preview also called for evidence that dealer and rep expansion converted.

surprises.description: Delinquency improved year over year but rose from Q1’s 11.58% to 12.16%, so the leading indicator did not continue its prior sequential improvement. The increase was not paired with rising charge-offs, however, and the year-over-year rate remained better.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total delinquency over 30 days improved to 12.16% from 13.14% a year earlier.” The preview reported Q1 at 11.58%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Delinquency >30 days. Improved to 11.58% from 12.35% YoY in Q1”; “DQ turning back up alongside rising NCOs is the genuinely bad combination.”

surprises.description: The fair-value portfolio reached $4.2 billion, slightly above the preview’s estimated $4.10–4.15 billion managed portfolio. The gap was modest, and the reported 11.3% yield was in line with the preview’s Q1 run-rate assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The fair value portfolio reached $4.2 billion (18% higher year-over-year), yielding 11.3% net of credit losses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Managed portfolio (AUM) … ~$4.10–4.15B”; “Q1 run-rate interest yield of 11.3% of average portfolio.”

in_line: Diluted EPS of $0.27 matched the preview’s ~$0.27 base estimate and fell within its $0.26–0.28 base-case range.
Pretax income of $9 million and net income of $6.2 million matched the preview’s respective ~$9.0 million and ~$6.2 million estimates.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $54 million, far above the preview’s $5–12 million expectation. But about $45 million came from favorable payer settlements and prior-year development, leaving underlying adjusted EBITDA at about $9 million—within the expected range—so the headline beat was largely nonrecurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $54 million”; “approximately $45 million reflected favorable payer settlements ($41 million, affecting only medical claims expense, not revenue) and prior year development, leaving underlying adjusted EBITDA of only about $9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: ~$5–12M.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $80–110 million, midpoint $95 million, versus the preview’s cited $20–60 million range. The midpoint is a substantial increase, although the call facts imply only about $15 million of additional underlying EBITDA in the back half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $80 million to $110 million with a midpoint of $95 million, implying roughly $15 million of additional underlying EBITDA in the back half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance is $20–60M”; the preview said a raise was the bull trigger and that a Q2 print above about $12 million would force one.

surprises.description: MA medical cost trend was 1.8% below the full-year 2025 baseline, better than the preview’s expectation that P3 would hold a roughly flat trend. That is a favorable result against the preview’s near-flat benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MA medical cost trend for the first half of 2026 ran 1.8% below the full-year 2025 baseline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “P3 claimed a roughly flat Q1 MA trend”; the preview asked whether P3 could “hold near-flat trend.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $386 million modestly exceeded the $377.95 million consensus estimate, though it was below the preview’s $390 million-plus bull-case threshold. Growth came despite a smaller at-risk membership base, as per-member funding improved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue rose to $386 million from $356 million a year earlier, driven by an approximately 15% year-over-year improvement in per-member funding despite the lower membership base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $377.95M”; the bull scenario cited “$390M+.”

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter at only $21 million, down from the preview’s reported Q1 cash balance of $25.5 million and consistent with a tight liquidity position. The preview flagged liquidity and cash burn as a key issue, but the call facts give no update on the remaining preferred commitment or the cash-versus-PIK dividend election.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with only $21 million in cash and equivalents, underscoring a tight liquidity position.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$25.5M cash at Q1”; “Watch the remaining ~$40M, operating cash burn, and critically whether preferred dividends are PIK'd or paid in cash.”

surprises.description: The Nebraska expansion will remain services-only through 2027, with full risk not assumed until 2028. That sets a later timeline for converting those lives to at-risk economics than the preview’s conversion watch might have led investors to look for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Nebraska expansion remains a services-only arrangement through 2027, with full risk not assumed until 2028, reflecting a deliberate glidepath approach to geographic growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether the ~29K management-services lives … begin converting to at-risk economics.”

surprises.description: Point-of-care technology deployment had reached more than 65,000 lives, about 110% of the original year-end goal, and providers closed nearly 90% of care gaps where the tool was used. The reported reach exceeded the company’s stated goal, although the tool opened in only about half of eligible visits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Point-of-care technology deployment reached over 65,000 lives (roughly 110% of the original year-end goal), with providers closing nearly 90% of care gaps where the tool is used, though it opens in only about half of eligible visits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Original year-end goal” (as described on the call).

in_line: Underlying Q2 adjusted EBITDA of about $9 million was within the preview’s expected $5–12 million range, despite the much higher reported result.
At-risk membership of approximately 105,000 was within the preview’s expected range of about 103,000–107,000.

surprises.description: ECG was expected to generate about $1.10–$1.12 billion of revenue, but reported $1.23 billion, including 30% organic growth. The result was also far above the published $1.0796 billion consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $1.23 billion, up 34% year-over-year, with 30% organic growth excluding the SE&M acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “the functional whisper is ~$1.18–1.22 EPS on ~$1.10–1.12B revenue”; published revenue consensus was “$1.0796B.”

surprises.description: Backlog was expected to clear $3.8 billion, with the base case at $3.8–$3.9 billion; instead it reached $4.55 billion. The increase was especially strong in E&M, and roughly 80% of backlog is expected to convert within 12 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog grew 53% year-over-year to $4.55 billion, driven by E&M backlog up 62%, with roughly 80% expected to convert within 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch: does total backlog clear $3.8B?” The base scenario expected “$3.8–3.9B”; the bull scenario expected “>$4.0B.”

surprises.description: The EBITDA result substantially exceeded the preview’s roughly $92–$95 million implied range, while consolidated margin reached 10.4%, above the preview’s 8.6% base and 9.1% bull assumptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EBITDA rose 53% to a record $128.6 million, with EBITDA margin expanding 130 basis points to 10.4% from 9.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: EBITDA was “~$92–95M implied”; the base scenario forecast “~$95M (8.6%)” and the bull scenario “~$103M (9.1%).”

surprises.description: The preview expected E&M margins to drift toward roughly 8%–8.5% after Q1’s timing-driven result. Instead, Q2 E&M margin rose to 10.8%, a much stronger result than the key margin debate anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The E&M segment posted revenue of $1.01 billion (up 42%, or 37% organically) and EBITDA up 72% with margin expanding 190 basis points to 10.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had framed Q1’s 9.0% margin as “timing-driven,” with “~8% core margins for the balance of 2026”; the preview said the base case had E&M margin “drifts to ~8.5%.”

surprises.description: The full-year guide was raised much more than the preview’s base case anticipated: the new revenue range starts above the prior guide’s high end, and the EBITDA range is well above both the prior guide and the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $4.5–4.7 billion and EBITDA of $410–425 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guide was “revenue $4.3–4.4B, EBITDA $345–360M”; the preview’s bull case expected a raise to “~$4.45–4.55B / $365–380M,” while its base case expected guidance to be “narrowed/nudged, not meaningfully raised.”

in_line: Second-half EBITDA margins of around 8.5% indicate a fade from first-half levels, consistent with the preview’s expectation that elevated Q1 margins would revert toward core levels.
Epsilon Industries remained excluded from current guidance, as the preview stated it was “not in current guidance” and identified inclusion in the guide as something to watch.

The strong first-half cash flow came with a favorable working-capital timing benefit, consistent with the preview’s warning that cash conversion was timing-affected and that an outsized cash-flow result would be low quality.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $2.37 versus the preview’s $1.84 consensus estimate, a substantially larger beat than the preview’s roughly in-line base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS increased 48% to $2.37.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | Consensus | $1.84”; the preview’s “Base case” was “adj. EPS ~$1.85.”

surprises.description: Total revenue of $64 million came in above the preview’s $61.4 million consensus and approximately $62 million base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 34% to $64 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Consensus | $61.4M”; “Base case: Revenue ~$62M.”

surprises.description: Royalty revenue was $48 million, below the preview’s estimated $50–52 million. That also fell short of the preview’s $55 million level that it said would meaningfully de-risk the full-year guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 royalty revenue grew 32% year-over-year to $48 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Royalty revenue ~$50–52M (my est.)”; “Q2 royalty ≥ $55M meaningfully de-risks the guide.”

surprises.description: Ligand raised the low end of adjusted EPS guidance by $0.50 to $9.00 while keeping the $9.50 upper end, partially meeting the preview’s expectation for a guidance raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ligand raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance low end to $9.00 (from below), maintaining the $9.50 upper end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the bull trigger” was “a raise to the upper half (or a lift of the royalty range)” and that investors wanted “a raise to the upper half.”

surprises.description: Despite the EPS guidance increase, Ligand left its $225–250 million royalty range unchanged. The preview said investors wanted that range lifted after XOMA closed and Filspari reported strong growth, and described a reaffirmation as conservative-to-disappointing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed royalty revenue guidance of $225-250 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side wants the royalty range lifted now that XOMA has closed and Filspari printed +96%”; “a reaffirm will read as conservative-to-disappointing.”

surprises.description: Management said a $100–125 million annual investment pace is needed for perpetual growth, below the preview’s $150–250 million annual deployment framing. The lower stated capital requirement supports growth with less deployment, though it also implies a different pace of deal activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ligand retains approximately $700 million of deployable capital, with a target investment pace of $100-125 million annually needed for perpetual growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether management would repeat “the ~$300M 2027 operating cash flow / $150–250M annual deployment framing.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted a 17% decline in Amgen’s Kyprolis sales, an unexpected offset to the strong growth in Filspari and Ohtuvayre that the preview emphasized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amgen's Kyprolis declining 17% to $314 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview emphasized Filspari’s “+96%” growth and Ohtuvayre’s $204 million sales, while listing Kyprolis only among products in its residual royalty estimate.

surprises.description: Management described up to seven pivotal trial readouts over the next 18 months, creating a more catalyst-rich outlook than the preview discussed, while cautioning that not all readouts would be positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ligand faces one of its most catalyst-rich periods with up to 7 pivotal trial readouts over the next 18 months, though management cautioned not all will be positive.”

surprises.description: Mirum’s volixibat PSC timeline slipped after the FDA recommended a Phase III study at the pre-NDA meeting, an adverse development not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mirum's volixibat PSC timeline slipped after the FDA recommended a Phase III study at the pre-NDA meeting.”

in_line: Filspari and Ohtuvayre partner sales were broadly in line with the preview’s figures: it modeled Filspari at about $141 million and Ohtuvayre at $204 million.
XOMA’s expected adjusted EPS contribution matched the preview’s stated expectation: roughly $0.50 in H2 2026 and $1.50 in 2027.
The preview anticipated “approaching 100%” XOMA synergy capture; management said integration would capture “virtually all” anticipated cost synergies.
The preview referenced approximately $300 million of expected 2027 operating cash flow, consistent with the call’s expectation of $300 million in 2027.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.77, well above the preview’s $0.62–$0.65 consensus range and even its highlighted $0.65 estimate. That is a substantially larger beat than the preview’s base-case EPS range of $0.66–$0.69.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$0.77 of non-GAAP EPS,” up 24% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” consensus: “$0.62–$0.65”; the preview says “Use $0.65 as the number that matters.” Its base scenario gives “$0.66–$0.69.”
