surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $57.7 million, above the preview’s $52–$54 million estimate, while the 20.8% margin expanded about 115 basis points year-over-year. That margin expansion was stronger than the preview’s concern that faster EnergyHub growth could dilute margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 15.7% year-over-year to $57.7 million,” with “adjusted EBITDA margin of 20.8%, up about 115 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was estimated at “~$52–54M”; the preview also says faster EnergyHub growth is “dilutive to blended margin” and flags a “+30bps adj. EBITDA margin in 2026” bridge.

surprises.description: SaaS and license revenue was $188.8 million, about $3.2 million above the guidance midpoint and roughly $3.2 million above the preview’s consensus estimate. The beat was modest rather than the $5.6 million beat the company delivered in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 SaaS and license revenue reached $188.8 million” and “beating the guidance midpoint by approximately $3.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists SaaS and license revenue consensus of “~$185.6M” and company guidance of “$185.5–185.7M.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year total revenue outlook and increased the hardware outlook by $15 million, a better outcome than the preview’s hardware-risk framing. The preview highlighted expected H2 tariff pass-through reductions and the risk that memory-cost price increases could hurt volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lifted total revenue guidance to $1.079-1.089 billion, including a $15 million increase in the hardware outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s prior FY26 total revenue guidance was “$1.0595–1.0705B”; it warned that tariff pass-through fees “drop ~$5M/quarter in H2” and described hardware as the line “where the quarter breaks.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance rose by about $6.5 million at the midpoint, rather than merely being held as the preview’s base case expected. The new range also exceeds the preview’s bull-case reference to a raise toward $220 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised by approximately $6.5 million at the midpoint to $221-223 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists prior guidance of “$215–216M” and says “FY EBITDA reaffirmed” in its base case, while its bull case says “FY EBITDA raised toward $220M.”

surprises.description: The combined commercial, EnergyHub, and international initiatives grew faster than the preview’s expected 25–30% range and contributed about 900 basis points to Q2 growth. This is a stronger reported growth contribution than the preview’s trajectory implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: The initiatives “now represent about 35% of revenue and grew over 30% year-over-year, contributing roughly 900 basis points to Q2 growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview describes the “growth initiatives” bucket as “compounding 25–30%.”

surprises.description: Q3 SaaS and license guidance implies growth of about 8.3%, a deceleration from Q2’s 11.1% growth and below the roughly 9.4% full-year growth implied by the raised guidance. The preview did not give a Q3 growth estimate, but it emphasized the need for H2 growth to support its expected full-year guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 SaaS/license guidance implies decelerating growth of about 8.3% at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says H1 at guidance implies “$383M in H2 against a $750M FY midpoint” and identifies SaaS as “the metronome.”

surprises.description: The newly launched Fire Communicator already had nearly 1,000 units deployed, with roughly twice the ARPU of a typical residential account. The preview mentioned the launch as a commercial-market proof point but did not anticipate this deployment or ARPU detail; the slightly lower hardware margins temper the upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Fire Communicator “targets an addressable market of 4-5 million fire panels,” has “roughly 2x the ARPU of a typical residential account at slightly lower hardware margins,” and “already has nearly 1,000 units deployed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview names the “new commercial fire communicator” as a “commercial-TAM expansion proof point.”

surprises.description: Q2 repurchases increased to $25 million from the $20 million deployed in Q1, indicating a faster pace than the prior quarter. The preview specifically identified an accelerated Q2 pace as a possible confidence signal, though it did not set a dollar expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “repurchased 570,000 shares for $25 million in Q2 under its $150 million authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says “$20M (428K shares) in Q1” and that “An accelerated Q2 pace … would be a confidence signal.”

in_line: Full-year SaaS and license guidance of $754–754.4 million fell within the preview’s expected $752–755 million range and exceeded its $753 million checklist threshold.
Revenue retention remained in the 95% range, meeting the preview’s expectation of at least 95%.

surprises.description: Ideal Power reported a long-term supply agreement with an automotive-qualified high-volume wafer foundry outside China and said it had achieved functional first silicon. The preview did not flag either milestone, so this adds concrete manufacturing progress beyond the expected funnel and prototype updates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Entered a long-term supply agreement with an automotive-qualified high-volume wafer foundry in Asia (not China)” and “achieved functional first silicon.”

surprises.description: The sales funnel grew to over $400 million from about $300 million at the mid-May call, exceeding the preview’s threshold of more than $300 million. The preview also hoped for a first production order, but the call facts report funnel growth rather than one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's sales funnel grew to over $400 million in total revenue opportunity, up from about $300 million at its mid-May call.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The funnel “was $300M” and the bogey was “>$300M, ideally with a first PO.”

surprises.description: The company reported co-developing an intelligent SSCB prototype for evaluation by a U.S. hyperscaler’s NVIDIA Rubin Ultra systems, a more concrete step than the preview’s existing LOI-stage description. However, the preview’s hoped-for named partner or firm agreement was not reported; this remains an evaluation prototype.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Co-developing an intelligent SSCB prototype for evaluation by a U.S. hyperscaler for NVIDIA Rubin Ultra 800-volt DC data center systems,” targeting delivery by end of Q4 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Data-center LOI conversion” and “LOI → definitive agreement is the upgrade”; the bogey was a “Named partner or firm agreement.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating expenses were $3.6 million, below the preview’s $3.9–$4.1 million estimate. This is a favorable expense result against the stated estimate, even though expenses rose year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses rose to $3.6 million from $3.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Opex estimate: “$3.9 – $4.1M.”

surprises.description: Q2 net loss was $3.4 million, narrower than the preview’s $3.7–$3.9 million estimate. The loss still widened from the prior-year quarter, but came in better than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $3.4 million in Q2 2026 from $3.0 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net loss estimate: “–$3.7 to –$3.9M.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for automotive reliability and qualification testing to be complete or complete within weeks. Instead, management said it plans to begin industrial JEDEC qualification this quarter and is prioritizing that work over automotive qualification, leaving the expected automotive milestone unconfirmed and shifting the near-term qualification focus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plans to begin industrial JEDEC qualification this quarter with completion in Q4 2026, prioritizing it over automotive qualification.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Automotive reliability/qualification testing was guided for “this summer”; the bogey was “Complete or complete-within-weeks.”

surprises.description: The lead Asia customer is expected to receive initial low-volume orders to support Q4 prototype builds. The preview expected the Q4 prototype timing to hold, but did not flag these supporting orders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “B-TRAN-enabled SSCB prototypes for the lead Asia customer's 800-volt AI data center and energy grid customers are expected in Q4 2026, along with initial low-volume orders to support prototype builds.”

in_line: Q2 cash burn was $2.5 million, within the preview’s $2.5–$2.7 million expected range.
Full-year 2026 cash-burn guidance of $10.3–$10.5 million remained within the preview’s expected $10–$10.5 million range.
Q2-end cash of $41.3 million was close to the preview’s estimate of about $41.5 million.
The lead Asia customer’s SSCB prototype timing remained Q4 2026, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: FIS cut full-year adjusted revenue growth guidance to 4.5%–5.0%, below the preview’s cited prior range of 5.1%–5.7%. This was a clear reversal from the preview’s base case of an unchanged guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted revenue growth guidance was lowered to 4.5%-5% from 5.1%-5.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the base case as “FY26 guide reaffirmed unchanged” and said the bull case needed “a raise or narrowed-to-the-high-end guide.”

surprises.description: Capital Markets guidance fell to 3%–3.5%, below the preview’s 3%–4% range, with management attributing the shortfall to internal execution rather than the market conditions highlighted in the preview. Slower recurring revenue and lower professional-services revenue drove the cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital Markets guidance was cut by 225 basis points to 3%-3.5% revenue growth,” including “a 120 bps hit from lower professional services plus slower recurring revenue”; the miss was “attributed to internal execution rather than market conditions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Capital Markets guidance of “+3.0%–4.0%” and discussed Q1 lending softness tied to “macro volatility.”

surprises.description: The UBS/Credit Suisse client attrition creates an additional 2026 Capital Markets headwind that the preview did not identify: it is expected to reduce segment revenue growth by about one percentage point, concentrated in trading and asset services.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The UBS/Credit Suisse client attrition is reducing 2026 Capital Markets revenue growth by approximately 1 percentage point, concentrated in trading and asset services.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow was substantially stronger than the preview’s $2.05–$2.15 billion full-year guide: it more than tripled year over year in Q2, and FIS raised the full-year range by $100 million to $2.15–$2.25 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow more than tripled year-over-year to $525 million,” prompting management to “raise full-year FCF guidance by $100 million to a range of $2.15-$2.25 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “FY26 FCF (ex-Worldpay tax) … $2.05–$2.15B” and described a reaffirmation or better as important.

surprises.description: Banking Solutions modestly exceeded its previewed growth range, with 6.1% pro forma growth versus the 5.5%–6.0% outlook. EBITDA growth and margin expansion were also strong, though the call facts do not provide a recurring-versus-nonrecurring revenue split.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Banking Solutions grew 6.1% pro forma (Banking +5.6%, Payments +6.4%) with adjusted EBITDA up 10.6% and margins expanding 178 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Banking guidance of “+5.5%–6.0%.”

surprises.description: Q2 margin expansion slightly exceeded the top of the expected range, reaching 113 basis points against a 75–110 basis-point outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Margins expanding 113 basis points, ahead of the 75-110 bps outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 sequential margin expansion was guided at “+75–110bps.”

surprises.description: FIS disclosed that it is evaluating strategic alternatives for select lower-growth Capital Markets products, an option not raised in the preview; management also cautioned that integrated costs and tax leakage could complicate asset sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is evaluating strategic alternatives for select lower-growth, non-core products within Capital Markets,” while noting that “asset sales are complicated by integrated cost structures and tax leakage.”

surprises.description: The Total Issuing portfolio showed encouraging retention and commercial traction: contracted coverage rose to 72%, large-bank win rates exceeded 85%, and ACV sold to joint clients grew 35%. The preview flagged acquired-book attrition and ACV conversion as issues to watch but gave no expected levels for these metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “72% of the Total Issuing portfolio is now under contract through 2029 or beyond (up from 65%),” the win rate was “above 85%” on large U.S. bank opportunities, and joint-client ACV “grew 35% year-over-year in the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “attrition in the acquired book” and called recurring ACV a “leading indicator.”

surprises.description: Total Issuing cost savings were reported as tracking near the high end of the stated target, providing a positive integration update; the preview flagged synergy realization as important but did not give an expected savings pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$13 million of cost savings captured year-to-date, tracking near the high end of the $30-$40 million target,” with “over $150 million in EBITDA benefit by 2028” reiterated.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “commentary on synergy realization” was a direct input to 2027 numbers.

in_line: Q2 pro forma revenue growth was 5.3%, within the previewed 4.9%–5.5% guide and close to its approximately 5.2% expectation; reported revenue of $3.4 billion was also close to the $3.384 billion consensus.
The full-year Banking outlook was reiterated, as the preview anticipated Banking growth around 5.5%–6.0%.
Total Issuing growth was described as in line with overall Payments growth of approximately 6%.
Full-year margin expansion guidance of 85–105 basis points was described as broadly in line with the prior outlook, and the preview also expected a broadly unchanged margin outlook.
FIS reaffirmed its path to more than $3 billion of free cash flow by 2028, a target the preview had already highlighted.

The $270 million returned to shareholders was primarily dividends; the preview noted the prior quarter’s dividend-heavy return and said a meaningful buyback authorization would be a signal to watch, not an expected outcome.

surprises.description: Revenue was $47.9 million, below the preview’s $51 million estimate and its $50–52 million buy-side whisper range. The preview already warned that stale consensus was likely too high, but the reported result also fell short of the lower expectations it considered more relevant.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $47.9 million,” roughly flat year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Our estimates: Revenue $51.0M”; the preview also characterized the buy-side whisper as “~$50–52M revenue.”

surprises.description: Gross margin substantially exceeded the preview’s 23.5% base estimate and even its 25.5% bull case. A one-time IEPA tariff refund contributed 230 basis points, but margin excluding that contribution was still about 26.6%, above both estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin expanded 500 basis points to 28.9%, though 230 basis points came from a one-time $1.1 million net refund of IEPA tariffs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Our estimates: … gross margin 23.5%”; the bull scenario projected “25.5%.”

surprises.description: Profitability was stronger than the preview’s base case: GAAP EPS was $0.15 versus the preview’s $0.05 estimate, and adjusted EBITDA was $6.1 million versus an estimated $4.0–4.5 million. EPS was nevertheless below the preview’s cited $0.19 consensus, making the result mixed against the different expectations it laid out.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP EPS rose to $0.15 per share ($2.5 million net income)”; “Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $6.1 million (12.8% of sales).” Operating income was $3.4 million, “despite $0.9 million in one-time litigation and consulting costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “EPS (GAAP) $0.19” consensus, but estimated “EPS $0.05” and adjusted EBITDA of “~$4.0–4.5M.”

surprises.description: The quarter-end backlog was slightly above the preview’s threshold, but the more notable upside was the post-quarter acceleration: management said it had grown to nearly $130 million in July. The preview expected backlog to hold at least $110 million at quarter-end, but did not anticipate this further increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total backlog reached a company-record $117.5 million”; “backlog grew to nearly $130 million in July following strong order pull-through.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s ideal outcome was “backlog held ≥$110M,” and it described the Q2 base case as “backlog roughly flat.”

surprises.description: Management put a concrete savings range and timing on two Newark gross-margin initiatives, including a second benefit expected in mid-Q3. The preview discussed gradual margin recovery but did not anticipate these quantified savings or timing details.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two gross margin improvement initiatives at Newark are expected to generate annual savings of approximately $600,000 to $800,000, with the second benefit materializing in mid-Q3.”

surprises.description: Ultralife disclosed that water-based drone programs are expected to begin contributing meaningful revenue in Q4, with production starting in early 2027. The preview discussed recently launched products generally but gave no expectation for these programs or their timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water-based drone programs are expected to add meaningful revenue starting in Q4 and production in early 2027.”

surprises.description: The company reported that it had already shipped more than $2 million of conformal battery orders in 2026 and expected the remaining backlog of over $7 million to ship before year-end. The preview noted conformal battery orders in backlog, but did not specify this shipment progress or year-end conversion timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company shipped over $2 million of conformal battery orders in 2026 with a remaining backlog exceeding $7 million expected to fully ship before year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “>$8M of conformal wearable battery orders” in backlog.

surprises.description: Communications Systems revenue of $3.8 million came in slightly below the preview’s roughly $4 million base expectation and remained below the $5–6 million level it said would validate a fuller recovery. However, the segment’s gross margin rose to 36.3%, a strong improvement not specifically projected in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The communication systems segment grew revenue 39.3% to $3.8 million with gross margin improving to 36.3% from 28.4%, driven by order timing and favorable mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario put Communications Systems at “~$4M”; it said “a return toward $5–6M/quarter” would validate the recovery priority.

surprises.description: One-time costs were below the level the preview identified as a warning sign: the quarter included $0.9 million of litigation and consulting costs, rather than the $1.5 million or more that might suggest another unusually burdened quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: Operating income increased to $3.4 million “despite $0.9 million in one-time litigation and consulting costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “if Q2 carries another $1.5M+ of ‘one-time’ ERP/integration/brand costs, the market will stop treating them as one-time.”

in_line: Quarter-end backlog remained above the preview’s $110 million threshold, at $117.5 million versus $115.1 million at the end of Q1.

surprises.description: Astec lowered its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $160M–$175M from $170M–$190M, rather than maintaining or narrowing the prior range. Management attributed the cut primarily to asphalt plant deliveries shifting into Q4 2026 and Q1 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Astec cut its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance from $170M-$190M to $160M-$175M, driven primarily by asphalt plant deliveries shifting to Q4 2026 and Q1 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA guide: $170–190M (reaffirmed at Q1).” The preview described a cut as the bear case and said investors wanted a narrow to the upper half or at least a bridge for the H2 ramp.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.94, below the preview’s $1.05 consensus estimate by $0.11, although it was close to the preview author’s own $0.95 forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.94 versus $0.90 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (adj.): $1.05.” The preview author’s own estimate was $0.95.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA and margin fell short of the preview’s expected profitability recovery: EBITDA was $42.6M versus an estimated $44–47M, and the 10.4% margin was below the roughly 11.0% estimate and the preview’s 10.5–11% validation threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record adjusted EBITDA of $42.6 million (up 26%).” “Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 10.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$44–47M (est., not formally polled)” and “Adj. EBITDA margin: ~11.0% (est.).” The preview said the margin “Needs to be ≥10.5–11% to validate the guide.”

surprises.description: Infrastructure Solutions margin moved in the opposite direction from the recovery the preview was looking for: it compressed 130 basis points, with management citing a mix shift toward lower-margin mobile paving equipment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Infrastructure Solutions net sales grew 11.6% to $228.3 million but margin compressed 130 basis points due to an unfavorable mix shift toward lower-margin mobile paving equipment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “a return toward 17–18%” and said a recovery to “17%+” would signal the thesis was intact.

surprises.description: Q2 sales slightly exceeded the published consensus estimate: $408.1M was $2.6M, or about 0.6%, above the $405.5M estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 23.6% year-over-year to $408.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales: $405.5M.”

surprises.description: Management reported that July was among Astec’s strongest booking months for asphalt plants and parts, a constructive update against the preview’s concern that customers might defer orders around the highway-funding deadline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management noted “July was among its strongest bookings months for asphalt plants and parts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “customer order deferral risk” and said that an admission of customers “deferring ahead of reauthorization” would be a concern.

surprises.description: The call gave new, mixed detail on highway funding: the proposed Build America 250 Act would raise core highway funding and the guaranteed formula-funded share, but management said only a continuing resolution appeared likely near-term. The preview had flagged reauthorization timing as uncertain but did not anticipate these proposal details.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The proposed Build America 250 Act carries a smaller $580 billion headline but raises core highway funding ~7% ($351B to $376B) and lifts guaranteed formula-funded share from 87% to 90%, though only a continuing resolution appears likely near-term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted the “Surface Transportation Bill” expiration on September 30, 2026, and called for a read on reauthorization timing and customer order deferral risk.

in_line: The second-half profit weighting was heavily back-loaded, with roughly one-third of adjusted EBITDA expected in Q3 and two-thirds in Q4; the preview had already described the H2 ramp as a key concern and Q4 as the swing quarter.

surprises.description: Underlying earnings fell well short of the preview’s realistic bar: adjusted EPS was $0.15 versus an estimated $0.40–$0.50, and adjusted EBITDA was $3.4 million versus the preview’s $5.5 million estimate. The weakness came despite the preview’s expectation of a partial recovery as the quarter progressed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the bargain purchase gain, adjusted net income from continuing operations dropped to $0.9 million ($0.15/diluted share) from $3.5 million ($0.57) a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA fell approximately 49% to $3.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Assume the real buy-side bar is materially lower — roughly $64–67M revenue and $0.40–0.50 adj. EPS.” The preview’s estimates were “adj. EPS $0.42” and “adj. EBITDA $5.5M.”

surprises.description: Sales were weaker than the preview’s realistic estimate, falling 11.9% year over year rather than landing around $64–67 million. Shipments declined across truck mirrors, returnable transport packaging, and latch/handle assemblies, so the expected RTP inflection was not evident in the reported results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales from continuing operations fell 11.9% year-over-year to $61.8 million from $70.2 million,” driven by lower shipments of truck mirror assemblies, returnable transport packaging, and latch/handle assemblies.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Assume the real buy-side bar is materially lower — roughly $64–67M revenue.” The preview also flagged “RTP volume inflection” and noted program launches management had flagged for Q2–Q3.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 20.8%, below the preview’s 21.5% estimate, and the below-margin Big 3 contract runoff was still weighing on the quarter rather than being largely behind the company by quarter-end. Tariff costs also remained a headwind, although margin improved sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 20.8% ($12.8M) from 23.3% ($16.4M) year-over-year due to lower volume, the below-margin Big 3 contract runoff, and ~$1.9 million of China tariff costs, though it improved roughly 60 basis points sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “gross margin 21.5%” and said management’s damage was “largely behind us by the end of the second quarter.” It described 21.5–23% as needed for the bull case.

surprises.description: Backlog far exceeded the preview’s roughly flat base-case expectation: it reached $126.2 million, up 45% year over year, versus an anticipated $80–84 million. About $19 million came from the newly acquired aerospace businesses, but legacy business also contributed to the increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog surged 45% year-over-year to $126.2 million from $87.1 million, with roughly $19 million from the new aerospace book and the balance from legacy business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “backlog roughly flat $80–84M”; its bull case called for backlog above $88 million.

surprises.description: Eastern completed a $7.85 million acquisition of Crown Precision and Sun Gear, entering aerospace and defense manufacturing—an actual deal rather than merely the possible tuck-in M&A mentioned in the preview. The businesses contributed $1.7 million of sales for one month and are expected to generate about $20 million in annual revenue, but currently have near-breakeven gross margins and are expected to weigh about 120 basis points on overall margin near term.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired California-based Crown Precision and Sun Gear for $7.85 million, funded by borrowings, marking its entry into aerospace and defense precision manufacturing effective June 1.” The businesses “contributed $1.7 million in sales during the one month of ownership,” are expected to run at “roughly $20 million in combined annual revenue,” and “currently operate near breakeven gross margins”; the acquisition is expected to weigh “~120 basis points on overall gross margin near-term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “tuck-in M&A” among possible strategic/capital-allocation news, but did not anticipate this acquisition or its near-term margin effects.

surprises.description: The reported $5.6 million of GAAP net income included a $6.5 million noncash bargain-purchase gain, making the headline profit much stronger than the underlying adjusted result. The preview’s earnings bar was based on adjusted EPS, so this accounting gain was not part of the expected operating performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income from continuing operations rose to $5.6 million ($0.94/diluted share) from $2.0 million ($0.33) a year ago, but this was inflated by a $6.5 million one-time noncash bargain purchase gain from the acquisitions.”

surprises.description: The company borrowed to fund the acquisition rather than showing the deleveraging the preview highlighted: long-term debt was $41.7 million and revolver availability was $59 million, versus the preview’s cited $33 million of debt and $67 million of availability. Cash generation was notably stronger, however, with first-half operating cash flow of $12 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: The acquisition was “funded by borrowings.” The company ended the quarter with “$15.1 million cash, $41.7 million long-term debt, and $59 million available under its $100 million revolving credit facility”; cash from operations was “$12 million in the first six months versus $1.9 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Deleveraging and cash,” citing “LT debt ~$33M” and “$67M available on the $100M Citizens revolver,” and said Schroeder called deleveraging “a clear priority.”

in_line: Management expected the second half to be more favorable; the call said it expects a “significantly stronger second half” driven by recovering heavy-truck build rates benefiting Velvac and Eberhard.
The company paid the expected $0.11-per-share quarterly dividend; the preview specifically anticipated the 344th consecutive dividend.
The company continued share repurchases, broadly consistent with the preview’s discussion of buybacks, though the preview only raised acceleration as a possibility.

surprises.description: ADTRAN's gross margin was 40.7%, below the preview's base-case expectation of roughly 41–42% and well below the 42–43% level it identified as a healthier outcome. Management attributed the decline to supply constraints that limited shipments of higher-margin products.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin declined to 40.7%, down from 43% in Q1 2026 and 41.4% a year ago, driven by supply constraints limiting shipments of higher-margin products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If GM held near 42–43%, this is an opex/absorption story that self-corrects; if GM printed 40% or below, memory/freight is structural.” The base scenario also expected “GM ~41–42%.”

surprises.description: The preview treated the delayed project as potentially recapturable in H2, but management said it did not expect a Q3 rebound in the delayed customer's Access & Aggregation orders. That makes near-term recovery less likely than the preview's base-case H2 framing suggested, though it does not establish that the project is lost.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $275-295 million and non-GAAP operating margin of 1.5-5.5%, with no expected rebound in the delayed customer's Access & Aggregation orders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “‘Delay’ implies H2 recapture. Watch for an explicit dollar quantification and a re-booking timeline.” The base scenario expected the project to be “expected to recover in H2.”

surprises.description: Enterprise, government and cloud revenue grew 47% year over year, while hyperscaler revenue surged 97%. The preview anticipated hyperscaler momentum but did not quantify growth of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue from enterprise, government and cloud customers grew 47% year-over-year and 19% sequentially, reaching 25% of total company revenue.” “Hyperscaler revenue surged 97% year-over-year, driven by data center interconnect.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Optical / hyperscaler momentum” was identified as an offsetting bull leg, with the preview watching for “backlog commentary on hyperscalers”; no growth rate was given.

surprises.description: Management disclosed that reaching its 10% operating-margin target requires roughly $310–320 million of revenue at 42–43% gross margin. The preview highlighted the margin collapse and Q3 margin bridge but did not provide this revenue hurdle, which shows the target depends on materially higher revenue and gross margin than the Q3 guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimates reaching its 10% operating margin target requires revenue of roughly $310-320 million at 42-43% gross margin.”

surprises.description: ADTRAN generated positive Q2 free cash flow despite the preview's concern about cash burn, although cash still declined during the quarter. The cash-flow result was better than the preview's bear-case scenario of continued cash burn, but the lower cash balance tempers the improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was $8.7 million and operating cash flow was $25.9 million, while cash declined to $79.2 million from $88.3 million at March 31, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's bear scenario included “cash burn continues,” and it flagged “Free cash flow, inventory, and the new facility” as key items to watch.

surprises.description: The refinancing was already known to have closed, but the call added that it reduced borrowing costs by 200 basis points and extended the facility's maturity to 2031—favorable financing details the preview did not specify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a refinancing of its credit facility led by JPMorgan, reducing borrowing costs by 200 basis points and extending maturity to 2031.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said ADTRAN had closed a “$350M JPMorgan-led senior secured facility” and listed its interest spread and covenants, but did not state the 200-basis-point reduction or 2031 maturity.

in_line: Q2 revenue of $281.1 million was within the pre-announced $280–282 million range and essentially matched the preview's cited post-cut consensus of $281.2 million.
Q2 non-GAAP operating margin of 3.8% was within the pre-announced 3.5–4.0% range.
Q3 revenue guidance of $275–295 million and non-GAAP operating-margin guidance of 1.5–5.5% matched the guidance already reported in the preview.
Optical Networking Solutions remained a strong growth engine, consistent with the preview's expectation of optical strength and continued momentum.

surprises.description: Ironwood reported Q2 LINZESS U.S. net sales of $582.3 million, far above the preview’s estimate of about $288 million. The reported figure is more than double the expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LINZESS delivered Q2 2026 U.S. net sales of $582.3 million, up 14% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2 2026E” LINZESS U.S. net sales: “$288M”; the preview also cited a guidance-implied bar of “~$288–292M.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year LINZESS sales outlook to $1.15–1.2 billion, above the preview’s cited prior guidance range of $1.125–1.175 billion. This is a positive, though relatively modest, increase to the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ironwood raised full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting LINZESS U.S. net sales of $1.15-1.2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether FY26 guidance of “$1.125–1.175B is reaffirmed, raised, or narrowed,” and its base case assumed “FY guidance maintained not raised.”

surprises.description: Ironwood raised full-year revenue guidance to $460–485 million, while the preview cited prior guidance of $450–475 million and described maintaining guidance as its base case. The new range is also above the cited $460.1 million FY consensus at the midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $460-485 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue guidance math of “$450–475M” and FY26 revenue consensus of “$460.1M”; its base case expected “FY guidance maintained not raised.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to greater than $310 million, above the preview’s cited prior guide of more than $300 million. The increase is positive, though below the preview’s bull-case threshold of more than $325 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance to greater than $310 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “>300M of guided FY26 adjusted EBITDA” and its bull scenario called for EBITDA “to >$325M.”

surprises.description: Q2 LINZESS prescription demand grew 4%, one percentage point below the preview’s 5% reference for demand. The company nevertheless raised its full-year demand-growth expectation from low-single-digit to mid-single-digit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LINZESS TRx volume grew 4% year-over-year in Q2 and 5% year-to-date, prompting a raise in full-year demand growth expectations from low-single-digit to mid-single-digit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified demand growth “vs. +5%” as a key metric and described its base case as “demand ~4–5%.”

surprises.description: Q2 total revenue was $113 million, slightly below the preview’s $114.8 million consensus and its own $115 million estimate. The shortfall was small relative to the preview’s stated $114–123 million reasonable Q2 band.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 delivered … $113 million in total revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed total revenue consensus of “$114.8M,” a company-model estimate of “$115M,” and a “honest Q2 revenue band at $114–123M.”

surprises.description: Q2 GAAP net income was $51.3 million, above the preview’s roughly $46 million estimate. The preview cautioned that EPS comparisons were unreliable, so this is a modest upside versus its own net-income model rather than a clean consensus beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 delivered $51.3 million in GAAP net income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 model estimated “~$46M” in GAAP net income and warned that EPS estimates mixed GAAP and adjusted conventions.

surprises.description: The STARS-EXTEND update provided encouraging long-term patient outcomes that the preview did not discuss: more than one in five patients had achieved enteral autonomy, and roughly 90% of STARS patients rolled over into the extension study.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In the STARS-EXTEND long-term extension study, more than 1 in 5 patients achieved enteral autonomy as of January, with roughly 90% of STARS patients rolling over into the extension.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that the original STARS trial’s delivered dose was 3.5 mg rather than the intended 5 mg, and that STARS II will use the 3.5 mg dose with a redesigned delivery kit to prevent dosing errors. The preview did not flag this prior dosing issue or the resulting trial-design detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “STARS II uses a 3.5 mg dose to match the actual delivered dose in the original STARS trial (intended to be 5 mg), with an improved delivery kit developed after root cause analysis to prevent prior dosing errors.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $83 million, matching the preview’s estimate of $83 million.

The company repaid the $200 million convertible notes at maturity in June, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the June convert would be repaid from cash; its year-end gross-debt and leverage outlook was also consistent with the preview’s less-than-$300-million debt and below-1x leverage target.
STARS II was initiated and actively recruiting, as the preview expected for the trial.

surprises.description: GENK delivered much stronger CPG progress than the preview’s still-unproven, forward-looking framing suggested: management reported 341% sequential revenue growth, more than $2 million of June sales, and placement in nearly 2,000 retail doors. It raised the next-12-month run-rate target to $35–$40 million from the prior $20 million-plus target, excluding a prepared-meals opportunity that buyers say could double frozen-product sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The CPG division's revenue grew 341% sequentially from Q1,” June was “the biggest month at over $2 million in revenue,” products were in “nearly 2,000 retail doors nationwide,” and management raised the forward 12-month CPG run rate to “$35 million-$40 million” from the “prior $20 million+ run rate target.” The guidance excludes fresh prepared/cooked meals, which buyers indicate could generate double the sales of frozen products.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said CPG projections were “promised ‘by end of Q2 2026’” and that “First hard numbers on revenue, margin, and door count matter more than the restaurant P&L.” It described the three-year framing as “$100M+ revenue at high-teens EBITDA margin — completely unproven.”

surprises.description: GENK disclosed a nonbinding offer to sell its U.S. restaurant operations and related leases for approximately $100 million while retaining all of its CPG business—an unexpected potential separation of the restaurant and CPG businesses. The letter is nonbinding, so the transaction is not assured.
surprises.fact_evidence: GEN received a “nonbinding letter of intent” from a nationwide restaurant operator to acquire “only its U.S. restaurant operations and related leases” at approximately “$100 million,” while GEN retains “100% of its CPG business.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the $215–$225 million FY2026 revenue range rather than trimming it to the low end, as the preview’s base case expected. That is a better outcome than the preview’s central forecast, though reaffirmation was also identified as a possible outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GEN reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $215 million-$225 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “FY guide trimmed to low end”; it also framed “$215–225M reaffirmed vs. cut” as the guidance decision to watch.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was slightly above the preview’s own $54.5 million estimate and above Q1, returning to year-over-year growth, although it still missed the $57.2 million consensus that the preview expected it to miss. This is a modest improvement over the preview’s base forecast, not a consensus beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue rose just 1.2% year-over-year to $55.7 million,” after a 6% decline in Q1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave “Consensus of $57.2M revenue” but said “My base” was “$54.5M,” with a likely range of “$54–55.5M”; it also forecast $53–55M after applying the prior-year seasonal step-down to Q1 revenue.

surprises.description: Restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA margin recovered to 11.3%, above the preview’s 10.5% estimate and its 10% credibility threshold for the H2 margin target. However, it remained below the preview’s roughly 13% consensus-implied margin, so the comparison is mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA was “$6.3 million (11.3% of revenue)” versus 7.4% in Q1 and 7.9% in Q4 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base estimate was “10.5%,” and it said Q2 “needs to print 10%+” for the H2 guide to be credible; its consensus-implied margin was “~13%.”

surprises.description: The expected Q2 easing in food-cost pressure did not appear: COGS rose to 39.1% of revenue rather than recapturing costs from Q1. Most of the reported food-cost increase was tied to the new CPG business, with the remainder attributed to commodity inflation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost of goods sold jumped over 5 percentage points to 39.1% of revenue”; 81% of the $3.2 million food-cost increase was attributable to CPG and the rest to commodity inflation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management reported commodity pressure had “eased considerably” during Q2 and identified “a 200–300bps COGS recapture” as the most likely source of upside.

surprises.description: The company’s stated development pace was more restrained than the preview’s cited guidance of 5–7 new restaurants: GEN expects development to remain near maintenance levels while completing its fifth and final restaurant transfer in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: GEN expects to “complete its fifth and final restaurant transfer in Q3 while keeping development near maintenance levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company guidance of “5–7 new restaurants” for FY26.

surprises.description: The reported Class A loss per share was worse than both the preview’s base estimate and consensus, despite the preview’s warning that this metric was a low-signal measure for GENK.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net loss widened to “$4.6 million (negative $0.14 per share)” from a $1.7 million net loss a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed EPS consensus of “$(0.08)” and its own estimate of “$(0.11).”

surprises.description: The CPG inventory build required a substantial line-of-credit draw and raised total debt to $24 million. The preview expected borrowing to fund CPG, but did not quantify a draw of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt rose to $24 million from $14.6 million at year-end,” driven by an “$11 million net line-of-credit draw to fund CPG inventory build.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “expects to draw on credit to fund CPG,” and highlighted Q1-end cash of $4.4 million and $4.5 million drawn on the revolver.

in_line: Q2 revenue remained below the $57.2 million consensus, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the quarter would miss the stale consensus estimate.
The preview expected management to publish CPG projections by the end of Q2; the call delivered specific run-rate guidance and sales and distribution figures.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating EPS was $8.89, far above the $6.51 consensus estimate. Even subtracting the $0.83-per-share benefit from onetime/other items leaves about $8.06 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: RGA reported $8.89 per share after tax; onetime/other items contributed $0.83 per share.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted operating EPS consensus: $6.51.

surprises.description: A material $71 million of onetime/other items boosted the quarter, although management said they were nonrecurring and expected to net closer to zero over time. The preview cautioned that some revenue lines were lumpy, but did not anticipate this specific earnings benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Onetime/other items contributed a material $71 million ($0.83 per share) benefit this quarter,” and management characterized it as “nonrecurring” and expected it “to net closer to zero over time.”

surprises.description: TTM adjusted operating ROE rose to 18.4%, above the preview’s 16.2% starting point and even the preview’s bull-case threshold of 16.5%. The 13%–15% target was not reported as having been reset.
surprises.fact_evidence: TTM adjusted operating ROE was 18.4%, “tracking above the 13%-15% intermediate-term target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said ROE was “Running 16.2% at Q1” and its bull case specified “TTM ROE ≥16.5%.”

surprises.description: In-force deployment was only $158 million in Q2 and nearly $500 million year to date, leaving RGA below the pace needed for roughly $1.5 billion annually. That fell well short of the preview’s bull-case Q2 deployment threshold, though the preview already expected deployment to remain below the annual pace in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: RGA deployed “$158 million this quarter” and “nearly $500 million year-to-date,” below the roughly $1.5 billion annual deployment pace previously discussed.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 deployment of $338 million against an annual need of about $1.5 billion, said the buy-side wanted to see Q2 deployment and pipeline conversion, and set “Q2 deployment ≥$600M” as a bull-case condition.

surprises.description: Variable investment income was substantially ahead of plan: the Q2 annualized return was 15%, and the year-to-date return was 11%, both above the 7% planned return for 2026. Management said this increased confidence in meeting or exceeding the target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Variable investment income delivered a “15% annualized return in Q2 and 11% year-to-date,” “well above the 7% planned return for 2026,” raising confidence of meeting or exceeding the target.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “7% planned return for 2026.”

surprises.description: Economic claims were favorable rather than roughly neutral, despite the preview noting that two consecutive favorable quarters raised the chance of mean reversion. The favorable experience included a $14 million current-period earnings benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: Economic claims were “$31 million favorable to expectations,” with a “$14 million current-period earnings benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described an “implicit neutral bar” for claims and said two consecutive favorable quarters raised “the odds of mean reversion.”

surprises.description: The cumulative pool of favorable economic claims not yet fully reflected in earnings was $375 million, $32 million above the $343 million cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cumulative economic claims favorability since 2023 totaled “$375 million not yet fully reflected in earnings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$343M cumulative unrecognized favorable economic claims” since 2023.

surprises.description: Buybacks did not accelerate: RGA repurchased $50 million of shares, the same amount as in Q1, despite the preview flagging acceleration toward the stated payout target as a key issue. The $111 million total shareholder return also included $61 million of dividends.
surprises.fact_evidence: RGA returned $111 million to shareholders, including “$50 million buybacks and $61 million dividends.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Buyback acceleration toward the 20–30% payout target” and noted that “$50M/quarter is light.”

surprises.description: RGA announced a 5.4% dividend increase for Q3, an increase not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of capital returns.
surprises.fact_evidence: RGA “announced a 5.4% dividend increase for Q3.”

in_line: RGA still plans $400 million of debt reduction in 2026, consistent with the preview’s note that $400 million was earmarked for debt reduction; the call specified that the payment is planned for September.

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS was $2.96, well above the preview’s $2.31 consensus, and FY26 adjusted EPS reached $4.57 versus the preview’s $3.75–$4.00 full-year guide. Record Q4 operating and EBITDA margins accompanied the earnings beat, largely because of favorable raw-material timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EPS reached a record $2.96” and “Q4 adjusted EBITDA and operating margins hit records of 46.8% and 41.5%”; FY26 adjusted EPS was $4.57. The margin results were “driven largely by ~$252 million favorable timing of raw material pricing versus cost.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $2.31”; the preview’s FY26 guide reconciliation showed “$3.75–4.00.”

surprises.description: FY27 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.15–$5.15 has a $4.65 midpoint, below the roughly $5.40–$5.50 NTM EPS embedded in published estimates. The range also implies little growth from FY26’s $4.57 despite the very strong Q4 result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance projects…adjusted EPS of $4.15–$5.15 (midpoint $4.65, roughly flat versus FY26's $4.57).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The 6.6x forward multiple implies NTM consensus EPS near $5.40–$5.50”; the preview also called FY27 guidance the “entire trade.”

surprises.description: The FY27 free-cash-flow outlook is weaker than the preview’s base case: management expects free cash flow of only about 20% of adjusted net income, rather than the preview’s 60–80% base-case conversion. The FY26 cash result itself was close to the preview’s expected roughly negative $90 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 free operating cash flow was negative $79 million” and “FY27 free cash flow expected at only ~20% of adjusted net income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “FY27 FOCF conversion 60–80%”; it estimated FY26 FOCF at “roughly -$90M for the year.”

surprises.description: Management gave a concrete FY27 Q4 EBITDA margin reference point of only the mid-teens for a “clean” FY28 starting base, underscoring how far normalized margins could sit below Q4’s record 46.8%. The preview anticipated normalization in FY27 H2 and asked for a clean underlying margin, but did not forecast this specific mid-teens endpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to a Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin in the mid-teens as a ‘clean’ jump-off point for modeling FY28, implying normalized earnings materially below the reported peak levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the timing benefit would be “normalizing in H2” and called for “a clean, ex-timing underlying margin for Q4.”

surprises.description: Higher debt is expected to add about $0.25 of EPS expense in FY27, an earnings headwind the preview did not identify in its guidance framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects a ~$0.25 EPS headwind from higher interest expense in FY27 due to increased debt.”

surprises.description: The energy outlook improved sharply: Q4 energy sales surged, and the FY27 U.S. land-rig outlook shifted from a decline to growth. The preview had noted strong prior-quarter energy growth but did not anticipate this upward revision to the rig outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The energy end market surged in Q4 (up 101% overall, +135% in infrastructure), and U.S. land rig count outlook was revised upward from a mid-single-digit decline to high-single-digit growth for FY27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q3 “Energy +28%” and flagged whether volume growth was durable, but did not give a more positive FY27 rig-count outlook.

surprises.description: The end of Bolivia’s preferential exchange program created an additional currency headwind that was not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 23% Bolivia FX headwind after the government ended its preferential exchange program.”

in_line: The FY26 free-operating-cash-flow shortfall was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of roughly negative $90 million; the reported result was negative $79 million.

The timing benefit was expected to be concentrated in Q1 and to fade through FY27: the preview said the bulk would land in Q1 and normalize in H2, while management said Q1 included about $2.25 per share and the benefit would be substantially behind the company by the start of Q3.
The $110 million restructuring-savings target by the end of FY27 matched the preview’s stated target.
